DoR text supplied by owner 2026-08-04 from the session handoff; permanent committed home is the portal wave doc (in authoring by YELLOW). Titles quote that text VERBATIM. Where an item references work already merged, the doneness lives in state, evidence and notes - never by editing the quoted text.

=== STANDING RULE ADDED 2026-08-21 BY STRATEGY RULING: ERROR VISIBILITY. ===

ERROR VISIBILITY IS PROVEN ONLY BY AN OBSERVED EVENT ARRIVING IN SENTRY FROM
PRODUCTION. NO GATE ON THIS BOARD MAY BE COUNTED AS PROVING IT UNTIL THAT
OBSERVATION LANDS.

IT IS A RULE ON THE GATE AND NOT A TENTH CONDITION, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION TO
THE DISPATCH RATHER THAN A CHOICE. The dispatch asked for a condition to be
added. The nine conditions are PINNED: validate-board.mjs holds
LAUNCH_GATE_DENOMINATOR = 9 and refuses any other count, because PORTAL-REHYDRATE
section 6 maps PG1-PG9 ONE-TO-ONE to the nine portal Definition of Ready items
and their titles quote the DoR verbatim. A tenth condition would break that
mapping and would require a DoR change, which is not this terminal's to make.
So the rule is recorded where it binds every condition instead of becoming one.

WHY THE RULE EXISTS. On 2026-08-21 the owner opened the Sentry project and found
the ONBOARDING screen - step 2, Verify, never completed. ZERO EVENTS HAD EVER
ARRIVED, through months of deployments and through a page that threw on EVERY
REQUEST for a day. Every piece of wiring was correct throughout: Sentry.init on
all three runtimes, onRequestError exported, withSentryConfig wrapping the build,
every name in .env.example.

NONE OF THAT WAS EVIDENCE. Sentry.init({ dsn: undefined }) accepts the call and
discards every event in silence - no warning, no throw, and captureException
still returns an id. A code review could have confirmed that wiring forever and
learned nothing about whether anything arrives.

HOW IT IS SATISFIED, AND THE ONLY WAY: the owner opens /admin/sentry-check on the
DEPLOYED site, presses the button, and FINDS OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY in Sentry.
Tracked on LE-sentry-capture-unverified, which closes on that observation and on
nothing else - not on the DSN being set, not on a green build, not on that page
existing.

PG7 IS THE CONDITION THAT COMES CLOSEST AND IT DOES NOT PROVE THIS. Its subject
is whether a missing variable degrades silently; whether the reporter RECEIVES
anything is a different question. PG7 carries the contradiction found the same
day in its own note and stays PASS by ruling.

rulings.title: Owner ruling: patient confirm-from-SMS is deferred post-launch
rulings.ruling: Patient confirm-from-SMS is deferred post-launch. No short-link scheme is built pre-launch. Counsel's confirm-only token row stays enforced server-side. For launch the confirm action is delivered by the 48h email channel only. Next session verifies whether the approved email body already carries the confirm link; if it does not, that gap returns to Ivan as a JP re-approval question, never as a silent wording change.
rulings.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-04:

"Patient confirm-from-SMS is deferred post-launch. No short-link scheme is built pre-launch. Counsel's confirm-only token row stays enforced server-side. For launch the confirm action is delivered by the 48h email channel only. Next session verifies whether the approved email body already carries the confirm link; if it does not, that gap returns to Ivan as a JP re-approval question, never as a silent wording change."

WHY THIS RULING EXISTS. The token is too long for a single SMS segment, so apps/web/lib/reminders/dispatch.ts sends the 24h SMS with the clinic phone number and NO LINK. Counsel's per-offset matrix (docs/rgpd-token-flow.md section 5) gives that offset confirm-only, and W13-01 enforces it inside the signature - a confirm-scoped token refuses cancel before any database contact. So the RULE is built and unit-tested; only its DELIVERY channel is absent.

NEXT SESSION'S CHECK, and it is a real one: read the approved 48h email body in apps/web/lib/reminders/notification-registry.ts and confirm it actually renders the rescheduleLink. All ten bodies are approved:true / approvedBy JP (#766). If the confirm link is NOT in the approved wording, adding it CHANGES AN APPROVED CLINICAL BODY, which re-opens JP's approval. That returns to Ivan as a question. It is never edited quietly.

VERIFICATION DONE 2026-08-05, AND THE GAP IS REAL. This ruling instructed: 'Next session verifies whether the approved email body already carries the confirm link; if it does not, that gap returns to Ivan as a JP re-approval question, never as a silent wording change.' It has been verified against committed code, and the answer is nuanced enough that both halves matter.

THE MECHANISM CARRIES CONFIRM. apps/web/lib/reminders/dispatch.ts:219 signs the 48h email link with scope 'confirm_cancel' (and :446 likewise), the scope travels INSIDE the signature (link-token.ts:29-42), and the landing page derives its offered actions from that scope, rendering both a confirm and a cancel CTA (apps/web/app/r/[token]/page.tsx:54-61). So a patient who opens the 48h email link IS offered confirm. Counsel's per-offset matrix is satisfied by the code.

THE WORDING DOES NOT. The approved pt-PT 48h body (apps/web/lib/reminders/templates.ts:56-65) reads 'Para remarcar ou cancelar: {{reschedule_link}}' - reschedule or cancel. It never mentions confirming. The EN body says the same ('To reschedule or cancel'). So the confirm action is available but UNDISCOVERABLE: a patient reading that line has no reason to click in order to confirm.

WHY THIS MATTERS AT LAUNCH RATHER THAN LATER. This ruling makes the 48h email the ONLY delivery channel for confirm pre-launch, because the token is too long for a single SMS segment and no short-link scheme is being built. If the only channel that can deliver confirm never tells the patient it can, then confirm effectively does not ship, even though every line of it is built and tested.

NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Changing the body is a copy change to one of the ten bodies JP approved blanket on 2026-08-03, and any change re-opens the clinical review and enters the registry approved:false. The ruling itself forbids the silent edit in as many words. So it goes back as a question, and the card is blocked on Ivan to carry it to JP. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT if JP wants the smallest possible change: amend the 48h line only, to name confirming alongside remarcar/cancelar, leaving the 24h bodies untouched - the 24h SMS is confirm-only by counsel's matrix and carries no link at all.

ANSWERED 2026-08-05. JP approved amending the SINGLE 48h line, relayed by Ivan. The line becomes 'Para confirmar, remarcar ou cancelar'. NO OTHER BODY CHANGE - the other nine approved bodies are untouched, and the 24h bodies keep their existing wording because the 24h SMS is confirm-only by counsel's matrix and carries no link at all.

UNBLOCKED from Ivan's column: the decision is made, so what remains is the edit itself. Patient-visible, so WF-03 applies and the rendered body goes into VERIFY-QUEUE rather than closing on a green gate.

CLOSED 2026-08-05 on the owner's screenshot. The gap this ruling existed to find - confirm built and enforced server-side but never mentioned to the patient in the only channel that could deliver it - is closed.

rulings.title: Owner ruling R4: patient linkage is phone-match at OTP claim time, and it REFUSES on anything but exactly one match
rulings.ruling: R4 - linkage mechanism (Q4): phone-match at OTP claim time, per Decision D. If EXACTLY ONE live patient row (deleted_at null, merged_into_id null, auth_user_id null) carries the proven phone, link it. Zero matches, multiple matches, or any candidate already linked: REFUSE with a clear pt-PT message directing the patient to the clinic. Card the staff-assisted activation path as post-launch. Mis-linking a medical record is the failure class the refusal exists to prevent.
rulings.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R4, answering Q4):

"R4 - linkage mechanism (Q4): phone-match at OTP claim time, per Decision D. If EXACTLY ONE live patient row (deleted_at null, merged_into_id null, auth_user_id null) carries the proven phone, link it. Zero matches, multiple matches, or any candidate already linked: REFUSE with a clear pt-PT message directing the patient to the clinic. Card the staff-assisted activation path as post-launch. Mis-linking a medical record is the failure class the refusal exists to prevent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. Decision D (WAVE-13.md section 1.4) makes patient login a 6-digit SMS OTP, phone only. It does not say how a proven phone number becomes a link to a patient row. Without that, LOOP 3 cannot build the claim step.

THE PREDICATE IS EXACT, and every clause of it is load-bearing. A candidate row must have deleted_at null (not soft-deleted), merged_into_id null (not the losing side of a patient merge), and auth_user_id null (not already claimed by someone). EXACTLY ONE such row must carry the proven phone. Any other count refuses. So does any candidate that is already linked - a phone reaching an already-claimed row is either a shared number or a re-registration, and neither is safe to resolve automatically.

IT IS DELIBERATELY FAIL-CLOSED AND WILL REFUSE REAL PATIENTS. Shared household numbers, a clinic row holding the wrong phone, a patient with two rows: all refuse. That is the trade the owner made explicitly, and the reason is on the ruling - mis-linking a medical record hands one patient another patient's clinical history. A refused login is an inconvenience and a phone call. A mis-link is a data breach with two named patients in it.

REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE BUILD: the refusal copy is pt-PT, in packages/i18n, and directs the patient to contact the clinic. It must NOT tell the patient which predicate failed - 'no row found' versus 'several rows found' versus 'already claimed' are three different disclosures about who else exists in the database, so the refusal is generic, exactly as the token rejection is generic under counsel's section 3. Refusal-style tests per the Decision B precedent: zero-match refuses, multi-match refuses, already-linked refuses, and the single live match links.

FOLLOW-ON CARDED: LE-staff-assisted-activation, post-launch, for the patients this legitimately locks out.

If the confirmation covers all four, the card closes whole. If it covers fewer, close what it covers and say which remain - never flip past the evidence, which is the rule PG3 was held under for a day.

RELATED: INC-04, the prod DB password exposure the owner accepted on 2026-08-02 with a commitment to rotate everything once the work was done. This confirmation appears to be that sweep landing.

=== HARD DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-08-07: SECURITY DEFINER OWNERSHIP. ===

The rotation this ruling closes on is scoped as "rotate the exposed credentials".
There is a second-order effect nobody has recorded, and it is the reason this
appears here rather than only on its own card.

ROTATING A PASSWORD IS SAFE. Same role, new secret, no effect on function
ownership. That is the expected case and nothing changes.

CHANGING THE ROLE IS NOT. Every SECURITY DEFINER function in production is owned
by whoever ran migrate, no migration pins it, and RLS is ENABLE not FORCE so that
ownership IS the RLS bypass the availability path depends on. If a rotation moves
the apply to a different principal - a new service account, a personal login
replaced by a shared one, a project migration - every function applied afterwards
inherits a different owner, the set splits in two, and NOTHING DETECTS IT. CI
structurally cannot: supabase db reset builds a database where one principal
creates everything.

SO THE ROTATION PLAN MUST RECORD WHICH PRINCIPAL APPLIES MIGRATIONS, BEFORE AND
AFTER. If it changes, ownership is pinned for all twelve functions in the same
change and verified by reading pg_proc.proowner, not inferred.

Mechanism and the full failure analysis: docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, section
"SECURITY DEFINER ownership is UNPINNED, and it is a rotation dependency". Card:
SEC-function-owner-unpinned, which holds the read-only query and gates any
migration on its result.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: the POST-01 / POST-02 deferral STANDS, and stopping to ask was correct
rulings.ruling: POST-01-drizzle-kit-migrate-silent-exit-1 and POST-02-e2e-shard2-intermittent-404 remain DEFERRED post-go-live. Do not build them. The committed `deferred` field is upheld against the dispatch that named them as buildable. The terminal that found the conflict and stopped to ask, rather than building or silently skipping, behaved CORRECTLY - that is the behaviour the field exists to produce, and it is not a halt to avoid next time.
governs: any future sweep dispatch that names a deferred card
rulings.notes:
IVAN WAS CONSULTED AND RETURNED IT TO STRATEGY as a decision that did not need him. Recorded as a STRATEGY ruling for that reason; attributing it to the owner would be a false provenance on a decision he explicitly declined to take.

=== WHAT THE CONFLICT WAS ===
Both cards carry a `deferred` field ruled 2026-08-27, ending: "Excluded from the self-merge sweep until go-live." Both notes end "BLOCKED ON GO-LIVE." The same day's dispatch said, in its buildable set: "the self-merge LE-* cards and POST-01 and POST-02."

So a committed machine-readable deferral and a live instruction pointed in opposite directions, on the same date.

=== WHY THE FIELD WINS, AND IT IS NOT A PREFERENCE FOR PAPER OVER PEOPLE ===
`deferred` exists for exactly one purpose, stated in validate-board.mjs's own comment: it is a FIELD and not a sentence in `notes` so that the out-of-scope predicate in PORTAL-REHYDRATE 4.11 can SEE it, because "a deferral matched out of prose fails OPEN - the check goes quiet and reports success" and "a later sweep would read the card as available and build the thing the owner deferred."

A field that yields to any dispatch that does not mention it is that same fail-open, one layer up. The whole value of the marker is that it survives a sweep written by somebody who did not re-read the card.

=== STOPPING TO ASK IS THE OUTCOME, NOT THE COST ===
This is the sentence a future session most needs, because the natural lesson to draw from a halt is "do not halt next time." The wrong outcomes here were: build them, which overrides a committed ruling on a terminal's own judgement; or skip them silently, which leaves the conflict alive for the next reader to hit fresh. Reporting the conflict verbatim, with the deferral text, and continuing with everything else, is the behaviour. It cost one paragraph in a report.

=== THE MERITS, WHICH POINT THE SAME WAY AND ARE THE WEAKER ARGUMENT ===
Recorded second on purpose: if the merits had pointed the other way the deferral would still stand, because a ruling is not re-litigated by the terminal it binds.
POST-01 needs a live non-prod Supabase project to reproduce a tool that prints nothing on stdout and stderr; check-pending-migrations.mjs already answers the question drizzle-kit was being asked, exits 0, and says how it knows.
POST-02 is an intermittent CI environment fault that a re-run clears, in no product code, and the cards themselves call chasing it open-ended.

=== WHEN THEY ACTIVATE ===
Go-live. Neither card is cancelled, neither is dismissed, and both keep their full diagnosis so whoever picks them up starts half-way. Removing the `deferred` field is the act that reopens them, and it is a deliberate edit rather than a side effect of a sweep.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: admins do NOT gain clinical_records:author - the Iniciar consulta tile is deliberately absent
rulings.ruling: Admins do not gain `clinical_records:author`. Admin stays an OVERSIGHT role, not a clinician, per CLAUDE.md's permission matrix and packages/auth/permissions.ts. The "Iniciar consulta" quick-access tile is therefore DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the admin dashboard and must not be added. If a particular person genuinely needs to record consultations, the answer is to grant that INDIVIDUAL a therapist role alongside admin - a person-level change and a JP question, and only that version is an owner decision.
rulings.notes:
IVAN WAS CONSULTED AND RETURNED IT TO STRATEGY as a decision that did not need him. Recorded as a STRATEGY ruling; the only part that IS an owner decision is named at the end and is not taken here.

=== THE OBSERVATION THAT PRODUCED IT ===
The owner reported that Inicio shows "Iniciar consulta" as a quick access for some roles and not for admin, and asked for it to be added for admin.

=== WHY THE TILE IS NOT THE FIX, RE-DERIVED FROM MAIN BEFORE ANY CHANGE ===
The tile is gated on `clinical_records:author` (apps/web/app/dashboard/page.tsx). The destination refuses the same capability at the route (apps/web/app/consultation/page.tsx redirects), and ALL FOUR server actions behind it return {ok:false, error:"forbidden"} on the identical check: startConsultationAction, signAudioUploadAction, fireConsultationWebhookAction and createStubPatientAction.

Admin does not hold the capability BY EXPLICIT DESIGN, and permissions.ts says so in its own words: "Admin: full operational control, but does NOT author/review/sign clinical records (oversight role, not clinician)... admin keeps read-only clinical access." CLAUDE.md's permission matrix agrees: Edit clinical records - Admin is read only.

So adding the tile alone ships a button that redirects on click. That is worse than an absent tile, because an absent affordance is a boundary and a broken one is a defect report.

=== WHY THE CAPABILITY IS NOT GRANTED EITHER ===
Granting admin `clinical_records:author` makes every admin a clinician. It contradicts two committed documents rather than one file, and it moves a line about who may write into a patient's clinical record - which is a clinical-governance question and not a UI one. The distinction the matrix draws is the whole shape of the role.

=== WHAT A FUTURE SESSION MUST NOT DO, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS RECORDED AT ALL ===
The absence looks exactly like an oversight. Five roles-worth of tiles are listed in one array in dashboard/page.tsx, five carry a capability, and the sixth's absence for one role is invisible unless you read the matrix. A future sweep tidying that array, or a future owner report of the same symptom, will produce the same one-line temptation.

IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. It is the matrix working. Do not add the tile, and do not add the capability to make the tile work.

=== THE ALTERNATIVE, IF THE NEED IS EVER REAL ===
Grant the INDIVIDUAL a therapist role alongside admin. That gives one named person the clinician capabilities without moving the role boundary for everybody, and it leaves the matrix intact.

THAT VERSION IS AN OWNER DECISION AND A JP QUESTION, and it is not taken here. It is person-level and clinical: who at this clinic may author a clinical record is JP's to answer, not engineering's and not strategy's. If the need arises, it opens as a card blocked on JP.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: a forced artifact republish is authorised when the render is a verified strict superset and the page has no save-back path
rulings.ruling: The 2026-08-27 board republish is authorised to use force. More generally: a force republish of a GENERATED artifact is legitimate when two things are established mechanically rather than assumed - (1) the new render's data is a verified strict SUPERSET of the live version's, and (2) the published page has NO save-back path, so nothing a viewer did can ever have reached the published HTML. Absent either, do not force; merge, or ask.
governs: every republish of the portal board artifact
rulings.notes:
IVAN WAS CONSULTED AND RETURNED IT TO STRATEGY as a decision that did not need him.

=== WHAT WAS BLOCKED ===
The publish interlock refused the republish because this session had not viewed the live version. That guard is generic and it is right by default: its job is to stop an unread newer version being overwritten by content built from memory.

=== WHY IT DOES NOT BIND A GENERATED MIRROR, AND THE TWO FACTS ARE MEASURED ===
BOARD-SPEC.md already settles the direction of the arrow: "The artifact is a RENDER of the JSON... If the artifact and the JSON disagree, the JSON wins and the artifact is re-rendered." The interlock protects content that originates IN the page. This page has none.

FACT 1, THE SUPERSET, established by diffing the two data islands rather than by eyeballing 1.7MB: identical card-id sets, identical ruling-id sets, and exactly two cards differing - RB-01-recuperacao-utentes and VERIFY-QUEUE - where the new render's notes are strictly longer and contain the live ones. Those are the two the session had just extended.

FACT 2, NO SAVE-BACK PATH, established from the saved page source: the artifact declares no save-back CAPABILITY, contains no publish call, and board-app.js writes viewer edits only to `localStorage`. A viewer's edits are per-browser by construction and cannot reach the published HTML. There is provably nothing to lose.

=== TEST THE DECLARATION, NOT A SUBSTRING. A TRAP THIS RULING CREATED FOR ITSELF. ===
The first version of this note named the capability's API symbol literally, and that text is inlined into the board's data island - so the moment this ruling was published, THE PAGE CONTAINED THE STRING IT SAYS THE PAGE DOES NOT CONTAIN. The publish returned a warning saying exactly that: a reference that is incidental text rather than authored code.

Harmless in itself, and a real trap for the next reader: a session checking fact 2 by grepping the page for the symbol would now get a hit on this sentence and refuse a force that is legitimate. So the check is on the artifact's CAPABILITY DECLARATION and on the absence of a publish CALL - what the page can DO - never on whether a string appears in it. The symbol is deliberately not written out again here.

IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY EDITED AWAY because it is a small instance of the failure this project keeps cataloguing: a check that reads the wrong surface and fails in the direction that looks like caution.

=== WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A ONE-OFF PERMISSION ===
The board is republished at every checkpoint, by a stateless terminal, forever. Without a written test the next session facing this interlock either forces it on vibes or stalls the owner's only status surface. The test above is the reusable part; the 2026-08-27 authorisation is the instance.

=== WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE ===
It is not a general licence to force. It does not apply to an artifact whose page CAN publish new versions of itself, nor to one whose live content was authored anywhere but the committed JSON. On either of those, the merge-then-publish path stands and the answer to a conflict is to re-read and merge.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: the /recuperacao therapist scope stays PRIMARY-PRACTITIONER-ONLY, and the dual-therapist cost is carded rather than built
rulings.ruling: The therapist scope on /recuperacao stands as built: `followupOwnPatientClause` reads `done.practitioner_id` only. A therapist who was the SECOND clinician on a dual-therapist session does not get that patient on their list. This is a KNOWN AND ACCEPTED COST, carded with its reasoning. Build no alternative. The card activates only if the clinic reports a real case.
rulings.notes:
IVAN WAS CONSULTED AND RETURNED IT TO STRATEGY as a decision that did not need him.

=== WHY PRIMARY-ONLY IS THE SCHEMA'S RULE AND NOT A SHORTCUT ===
packages/db/src/schema.ts states it on the column itself: the secondary participants are "de-emphasized LINKED DISPLAY data" with "PRIMARY-ONLY SEMANTICS everywhere - availability, the Servico/Localizacao auto-selects, analytics money attribution, the AI-recording primary pair + idempotency key, and the Estado/lifecycle axes ALL stay on the primary pair." `followupPractitionerSql` - the expression that renders the practitioner NAME on this very page - reads the primary for the same reason.

So scoping on the primary keeps the page consistent with every other axis in the product, and the alternative would make this one screen the exception.

=== THE PROPERTY THAT WOULD BREAK IF IT CHANGED ALONE ===
The scope clause and the displayed practitioner are THE SAME SUBQUERY SHAPE - same completed set, same ORDER BY starts_at DESC LIMIT 1 - so the row the scope admits is by construction the row whose clinician the page names. Scoping on either practitioner column while the screen still names only the primary would show a therapist a patient whose visible clinician is somebody else. That is the more confusing of the two failures, and it is why the display column must move in the same commit if this is ever revisited.

=== WHY NOTHING IS BUILT NOW ===
The cost is theoretical until somebody feels it. Massagem 4 Maos and Sessao Familia are the dual-participant services; whether a secondary therapist on one of those ever wants that patient on their recuperacao list is a question about how the clinic actually works, and nobody has asked it. Building both halves - the clause and the display column - against a case nobody has reported is speculative work on a live patient-data surface.

=== WHAT ACTIVATES IT ===
A real report from the clinic: a therapist saying a patient they treated is missing from their list, traced to a dual-therapist session where they were the secondary. Not a hypothetical, and not a code review. The card carries the whole shape so that report costs an hour rather than a re-derivation.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: ad-hoc work is CARDED BEFORE EXECUTION, and strategy does not dispatch uncarded work
rulings.ruling: Ad-hoc work is carded before execution. If a dispatch names work that has no card, the terminal creates the card FIRST, with the dispatch quoted as its origin, and then executes. Strategy does not dispatch uncarded work. A card created after the fact is valid remediation and is NOT re-done.
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. The 2026-08-27 dispatch named three builds - the therapist scope, the admin tile and the sidebar icons - and none of them had a card. BLUE opened PRs #1055 and #1056 and shipped them, then found at closure time that the cards it was asked to close did not exist, and created them retroactively as shipped with the PR and the owner's observation as evidence.

CLAUDE.md already said it: "Never start work that has no ticket. If the owner gives an ad-hoc instruction, create the ticket first, then execute." The rule was not missing; it was not followed.

=== THE MISS ORIGINATED IN THE DISPATCH, NOT IN THE TERMINAL, AND THAT HALF IS THE POINT OF WRITING IT DOWN ===
A dispatch that names work without a card puts the terminal in a position where the FIRST thing it must do is disobey the order it was given - stop, card, then build. That is a correct thing to ask of a terminal and a bad thing to rely on, because a dispatch reads as authority and the card rule reads as bookkeeping. So the obligation is stated on BOTH sides: the terminal cards first, AND strategy stops shipping dispatches that require it to.

=== THE COST, WHICH WAS SMALL AND NOT ZERO ===
RB-01's sitting script had to carry those steps because no card existed to carry them; the closure dispatch asked to close cards that were not there; and for four days the board did not show that two shipped features existed. The board is the ledger - work that never enters it is work nobody can find later.

=== RETROACTIVE CARDING IS VALID REMEDIATION AND IS NOT RE-DONE ===
Ratified. A card written at close, carrying the PR and the owner's quoted observation, records the same facts a card written at open would have. Re-running the work to give it a card that preceded it would be theatre. What retroactive carding CANNOT recover is the interval - the days when the board was wrong - and that is the cost the rule exists to avoid, not the card itself.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: a write path whose failure UI can be destroyed by navigation must be observable ON THE SERVER
rulings.ruling: A write path whose failure UI can be destroyed by navigation must be observable on the server. Client-side alerting is NOT sufficient evidence of loudness when the document may not survive the request.
governs: any write issued from a click that also navigates
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. #1063 fixed the contact mark by making the write survive the navigation (a keepalive fetch) and by making failure LOUD - role=alert on the row, above the contact history, with 401 given its own message.

THE SECOND HALF WAS ONLY HALF TRUE, AND THE GAP IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN THEORETICAL. Of the three channel anchors, ONE opens a new browsing context and TWO navigate the current document:
  WhatsApp: href="https://wa.me/..." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" - a NEW context; the current document survives and the alert is reachable.
  SMS:      href="sms:+351..." with NO target - the CURRENT document.
  Email:    href="mailto:..." with NO target - the CURRENT document.
So on two channels of three, the document that would render the alert may be gone before there is anything to render. The alert is unreachable in exactly the failure case that matters, and the page would look identical to the silent version it replaced.

=== WHY THE ANSWER IS THE SERVER AND NOT MORE CLIENT CODE ===
Every client-side remedy has the same shape as the defect: it needs the document to still be there. sessionStorage set before the navigation and read on the next load is a state machine across a page transition that may never come back; a beacon reporting the failure needs the failure to be observed first, which is the thing that cannot be guaranteed.
The server ALREADY has the request - keepalive delivered it - so it already knows the outcome. Capturing there costs nothing and depends on nothing surviving.

=== IT IS A RULE ABOUT A CLASS, NOT ABOUT THIS ROUTE ===
The class is: a write issued from a click that also navigates. Every one of them has a failure the user may never see, so every one of them owes a server-side trace. The contact mark is the first member and the reason the rule exists; the next one must not have to rediscover it.

=== WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY ===
It does not retire the client alert. On the channel where the document DOES survive, the person who can act on the failure is the one looking at the screen, and telling them is worth more than a line in an issue tracker they will never open. Both, not either.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: on a board-file conflict, RECOMPUTE the counts and as_of from the merged file - never keep the local ones
rulings.ruling: On a docs/board/portal-board.json or docs/board/HANDOVER-STATE.md conflict, never keep local counts or `as_of`. Recompute both from the MERGED file. A locally correct count describes a board that no longer exists.
governs: every rebase by BLUE or PURPLE
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. Two terminals share this repository and both write the board. Three of BLUE's PRs have now conflicted on it, every time on the same two things: `as_of`, and the counts headline in HANDOVER-STATE.md.

=== WHY 'KEEP MINE' IS ALWAYS WRONG HERE, EVEN THOUGH IT IS ALWAYS TEMPTING ===
A conflict on a count is not two opinions about one number. Each side computed a TRUE number for a different board: 164 shipped was true of the board before the other lane's card landed, and 165 was true after. Keeping either is keeping a fact about a file that no longer exists.

The failure is quiet in the worst way: the number is plausible, it is off by exactly one, and the only reader who would notice is the owner counting cards on his screen - which is precisely how the handover count guard came to be written in the first place.

=== RECOMPUTE MEANS FROM THE FILE, NOT FROM ARITHMETIC ===
Not "mine plus theirs". Resolve the JSON, then DERIVE the counts by reading it - the same filter render-board.mjs applies, external_agenda excluded - and write those. `scripts/handover-counts-match-the-render.test.mjs` then agrees by construction rather than by luck, and it is the check that catches a resolution done by hand.

`as_of` takes the LATER timestamp, and it is not a tiebreak: it is a claim about when the board was last true, and the merged board is newer than either side.

=== IT APPLIES TO BOTH LANES ===
Recorded as a rule rather than as BLUE's habit, because the conflict has two sides and only one of them has hit it so far.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: a reclaim, recovery or re-link candidate set is built from POSITIVE PROVENANCE, never from the absence of a record
rulings.ruling: A candidate set for any reclaim, recovery or re-link path is built from positive provenance, never from the absence of a record. Absence is shared by the thing being recovered and by principals that must never be recoverable. Acceptance for such a path must include a negative arm that FAILS when the naive absence predicate is substituted, and the arm must be PROVEN to fail rather than assumed to, because an ordering accident can leave a weaker arm green against the same defect.
governs: any reclaim, recovery, re-link or undelete path
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. LE-staff-delete-leaves-auth-user, 2026-08-28. Deleting a
staff member leaves the Supabase auth identity behind, so the address is held
forever and the same person can never be re-invited. The obvious fix is to
reclaim the orphan on re-invite, and the obvious way to find it is:

  "an auth user holds this email and NO public.users row references it,
   therefore it is an orphan."

THAT PREDICATE IS THE DEFECT, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE ONE IT FIXES.

=== ABSENCE IS SHARED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE RULING ===
A portal patient has an auth identity and no public.users row. schema.ts states
it on the column: "A patient is a DISTINCT principal from a staff users row:
there is no users row for a patient." So the naive predicate classifies EVERY
PATIENT WITH A PORTAL LOGIN as a reclaimable orphan.

An admin could invite staff using a patient's address, have the password reset
onto that identity, insert a staff row keyed to it, and take over the patient's
portal login - locking a patient out of their own clinical record. A PRIVILEGE
ESCALATION CREATED BY THE FIX, on the surface with the most sensitive data on the
platform.

AND THE SET IS OPEN AT THE OTHER END TOO. Any future table that links an auth
identity re-opens the hole silently, and the failure is invisible until somebody
cannot sign in. A predicate maintained as a list of exclusions is a predicate
that is wrong the moment somebody adds a table and does not think of it.

=== POSITIVE PROVENANCE IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION ===
The shipped shape asks the opposite question: WHICH IDENTITIES DID THIS TENANT
CREATE AS STAFF AND THEN DELETE? That set is enumerable without guessing -
deleteStaffMember writes an audit row that SURVIVES the delete, which is the same
reason the delete refuses an account with any activity. A patient's identity is
never in it. Another tenant's live user is never in it. A future auth-linked
table cannot put anything in it. Nothing has to be remembered or excluded.

THE RULE GENERALISES BEYOND AUTH. Any path that says "restore the thing that is
missing" is choosing between "what is absent" and "what we recorded doing", and
only the second describes the thing it means.

=== THE NEGATIVE ARM MUST BE PROVEN TO FAIL, NOT ASSUMED TO ===
And this half was learned rather than reasoned. The suite for that card carried
TWO tests refusing a patient's identity. When the naive predicate was substituted
to check the guard bites, ONLY ONE OF THEM REDDENED:

  x REFUSES a patient's login when NO staff deletion matches at all
    AssertionError: expected '9522bfeb-3cd2-41e2-9825-ddcbcd57ac88' to be null
    Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)

The other - "REFUSES a PATIENT's login holding the same address" - STAYED GREEN
under the broken predicate, because the legitimate staff candidate happened to
sort first and was returned before the patient's was reached. A reader would have
called it the security test. It was an ordering accident.

SO A SINGLE "the dangerous principal is refused" TEST CAN BE GREEN AGAINST THE
EXACT DEFECT IT NAMES. The arm that counts is the one with every decoy removed,
and the only way to know which one that is, is to substitute the naive predicate
and watch. Asserting that a guard would fail is not evidence that it does.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: {name} is the FIRST WHITESPACE-DELIMITED TOKEN, accepted by the owner, and not to be re-raised as a defect
rulings.ruling: The {name} token in patient-facing message templates is the first whitespace-delimited token of the name field. The owner accepted this on 2026-08-28 for compound Portuguese given names - Maria Joao rendered as Maria. This is settled and is NOT to be re-raised as a defect. Any future change to full-name rendering is a DATA question about how the name is stored on the ficha before it is a template question.
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. RB-01's step C put the recovery message on a real screen for
the first time, and the template review going to Rodica needed the behaviour
stated rather than assumed. `followupMessage` resolves {name} as
`patientName.trim().split(/\s+/)[0]`, so a patient registered as "Maria Joao
Silva" is greeted "Bom dia Maria".

IT WAS RAISED AS A QUESTION, NOT FIXED, AND THAT WAS THE RIGHT ORDER. Whether
"Bom dia Maria" is acceptable for a patient called Maria Joao is a question about
how the clinic speaks to people. It is not derivable from the repository, and
guessing it is what standing rule 15 forbids. The owner answered: acceptable.

=== WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A NOTE ===
The behaviour LOOKS like a defect to anybody who meets it cold. "Only the first
word of a compound given name is used" reads as a truncation bug, and it will be
found again - by a sweep, by a new terminal, or by whoever next reads
deep-links.ts. Without this record the natural response is a fix, and the fix
would change how patients are addressed on the strength of a terminal's taste.

=== THE ORDER OF THE QUESTION, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE PART ===
If the clinic ever does want the full given name, THAT IS A DATA QUESTION FIRST.
Nothing in a stored full name distinguishes a second given name from a first
surname - "Maria Joao Silva" is three tokens and the record does not say which
are given. No template change can decide it, and a heuristic that guessed would
address some patients by half a surname.

So the sequence is: decide how the name is captured on the ficha, then decide
what the template renders. A change made in the other order is a change made
without the fact it depends on.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE ===
It settles {name} in PATIENT-FACING TEMPLATES. It says nothing about how a name
is displayed on a staff screen, printed on a document, or matched during import -
each of those has its own reasons and none of them is bound by this.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: migration authorship transfers to BLUE for migration 0068 only, under apply-before-merge
rulings.ruling: The LV import being complete, migration authorship transfers to BLUE for migration 0068 ONLY. Apply-before-merge doctrine binds: the migration is applied to production from the prod-apply worktree BEFORE the PR merges, and proof of apply is PASTED JOURNAL OUTPUT, never self-assertion. After 0068 merges, migration authorship freezes again until strategy releases it.
governs: migration authorship in the platform lane
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. The platform lane has never owned migration authoring. That boundary existed because the import pipeline was live and two terminals writing migrations against a database mid-import is how a numbering collision becomes a production incident. The LV import is complete, so the reason is spent - for one migration.

WHY IT IS SCOPED TO 0068 AND NOT OPENED GENERALLY. The defect PERF-01 names is measured, its fix is one additive CREATE INDEX, and it was confirmed by production Sentry hours before this ruling. That is a specific warrant, not a general one. A general release of migration authorship is a separate decision and this ruling deliberately does not make it. The freeze resumes the moment 0068 merges.

APPLY BEFORE MERGE, AND WHY THE PROOF SHAPE IS NAMED. The doctrine is not new; what this ruling adds is that the evidence is pasted journal output and a production EXPLAIN ANALYZE, never a terminal's own claim that it ran something. The project has a recorded history of apply steps that silently no-opped - db:migrate against the wrong checkout being the known one - and a self-assertion cannot distinguish that from success.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. No other migration. No schema change beyond the index. No data write. No CONCURRENTLY judgement call is delegated either: the clinic is closed today and a plain sub-second build was authorised explicitly.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: every task in the 2026-08-30 dispatch may merge today; from Monday 08:00 the platform lane freezes except live-day defects
rulings.ruling: SR-12 amends SR-10. Every task in the 2026-08-30 dispatch may merge today. From Monday 2026-09-01 08:00 the platform lane FREEZES, except for defects observed on the live clinic day, which merge under the SR-10 standard.
rulings.notes:
SR-10 IS NOT PRESENT IN THIS BOARD FILE, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS NOT IN `governs`. This ruling was dispatched as an amendment to SR-10, and a governs entry naming it was written first and then REMOVED, because the reconciler correctly reported it as a governs-ghost: SR-10 is neither a card nor a ruling here. A search of origin/main at 831a4772 finds no SR-10 in portal-board.json, in any doc, or in any open PR; the recorded rulings run WF-02..WF-16 and SR-01..SR-09. SR-10 appears to have been dispatched to a terminal and never written to the board. Listing it would have made the board assert the existence of a record it does not hold.

SO SR-12 STATES THE STANDARD IT INHERITS RATHER THAN POINTING AT AN ABSENT RECORD. As relayed in dispatch, the SR-10 standard is: a terminal may self-merge its own work when the required checks are green. The four required checks on main today are, verbatim from branch protection: "Lint + typecheck + test", "DB-gated tests (RLS isolation, seeded DB)", "Playwright E2E (seeded DB)", "Validate spec + drift check".

A CAUTION THAT IS PART OF THE STANDARD, not commentary on it: a docs-only PR skips two of those in seconds. Green on a docs-only PR is a SKIP, not a proof, and must not be read as one.

IF STRATEGY HOLDS A DIFFERENT SR-10 TEXT, this note is the place to correct it, and SR-12 should be re-issued naming the real wording. It is written this way so the next terminal inherits a standard it can actually read instead of a dangling reference.

THE FREEZE IS THE OPERATIVE HALF. From Monday 08:00 the lane is closed. "A defect observed on the live clinic day" means somebody at the clinic saw it happen, not a terminal's own finding, not a Sentry issue nobody has felt, and not work this dispatch chose to defer.

rulings.title: Owner ruling: the booking confirmation sends for portal appointments only, and only at ACCEPTANCE
rulings.ruling: The booking confirmation sends for portal-originated appointments only, and only at the moment reception ACCEPTS the pedido, never at request time. Q-W14-02 is thereby answered and closed. The single-letter n and s classifications stand as shipped.
rulings.notes:
WHAT IT RESOLVES. Decision A (2026-08-31) scoped the confirmation to portal-originated appointments, and the collision reported back was that JP ruled 2026-08-06 that ALL twelve bookable services are request-mode with zero auto-confirmed - so every portal booking is a pedido, and the approved body opens "A sua marcacao esta confirmada". Sending at request time would have asserted a confirmation the clinic had not made.

THE RULING TAKES THE RECOMMENDED DEFAULT and needs no new copy: at acceptance the appointment genuinely IS confirmed, so the body JP approved on 2026-08-03 is true when it arrives.

IT ALSO CLOSES A WIDER DEFECT THAT WAS NOT ABOUT COPY. apps/api emits no background event of any kind, so a portal-booked appointment received NO reminders either - not before acceptance and not after. The acceptance emit fixes both with one call and no new dependency or environment variable.

THE CLASSIFIER VOCABULARY IS RATIFIED AS SHIPPED. BLUE reported that `n` and `s` are one keystroke from each other and that a stray `n` cancels an appointment; the owner has read that and let it stand. The risk is pinned by a test rather than argued away.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: migration authorship opens to BLUE for migration 0069 only, the reminders inbound review queue table
rulings.ruling: Migration authorship opens to BLUE for migration 0069 only, the reminders inbound review queue table. Apply-before-merge doctrine binds exactly as 0068: applied from the prod-apply worktree, target ref verified first, journal proof 68 to 69 pasted, then merge. Authorship freezes again on merge.
rulings.notes:
WHAT PRODUCED IT. SR-11 released authorship for 0068 and re-froze it on merge, which left the inbound reply path finished except for the one part that needed a table: somewhere to keep the message text a human has to read. #1083 shipped with that gap stated rather than worked around, and Q-W14-05 recorded it.

EXECUTED AS RULED. Target ref verified in the prod-apply worktree BEFORE the apply (detached on the feature branch, never main - the failure mode where db:migrate silently no-ops); journal read at 68 before and 69 after; table, RLS, three policies, six constraints, four indexes and the grant set all read back from production, with the `patient` role holding no grant at all.

WHAT IT DOES NOT OPEN. Q-W14-01's `reminder_email_enabled` default flip is a DIFFERENT migration and remains blocked - it needs a JP product decision AND a further strategy release. One number was released, and one number was used.

rulings.title: Owner ruling: JP approves the three reply acknowledgements, the 24h reply instruction, and the reversal of the 48h email default
rulings.ruling: JP has approved, verbally to the owner on 2026-09-01, all three open items. A: the three reply acknowledgements, packet sections 12 to 14. B: adding the reply instruction line to the 24h SMS. C: reversing the 48h email default - the reminder goes to every patient with a registered email, the portal opt-out toggle remains. Q-W14-01 is answered and closes.
rulings.notes:
A - APPROVED AS WRITTEN. The three bodies shipped `approved: false` on 2026-08-31 and NOT A WORD CHANGED before approval. That is the case for registering unapproved copy rather than leaving it unwritten: what JP approved was the exact string that sends, already proven GSM-7 and single-segment, so approval required no follow-up work.

B - COSTS THE FEE VARIANT ITS SEGMENT MARGIN, reported rather than absorbed. The 24h body goes 99 -> 148 chars, leaving 12; the fee line is 53. Variant B no longer fits one segment and renderSms THROWS rather than splitting - the loud failure fee-notice.ts always said it wanted. Nothing is at risk today (flag unarmed, entry unapproved, counsel unsigned), but the fee decision now carries that price. NOTHING APPROVED WAS TRIMMED to make room.

C - THE BACKFILL COULD NOT PRESERVE AN OPT-OUT, and JP ruled knowing it. `false` means both 'opted out' and 'never chose'; the portal PATCH writes no audit row; SR-08 forbids building a set from an absence. 1,930 patients with a registered email were re-enabled, including anyone who had deliberately switched it off. The portal toggle is the mitigation; the provenance gap is carded, not closed.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: migration authorship opens for migration 0070 only, the email reminder default reversal and backfill
rulings.ruling: Migration authorship opens for migration 0070 only, the email reminder default reversal and backfill. Apply-before-merge binds exactly as 0068 and 0069: prod-apply worktree, target ref verified, journal proof 69 to 70 pasted, then merge, authorship freezes on merge.
rulings.notes:
THE THIRD SINGLE-NUMBER RELEASE IN THE SAME PATTERN (SR-11 for 0068, SR-14 for 0069, SR-15 for 0070). Executed as ruled: target ref verified in the prod-apply worktree BEFORE the apply, detached on the feature branch and never main; journal read at 69 before and 70 after; the default, the row counts and the invariants all read back from production rather than asserted.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER: 8,404 patients; 1,930 with a registered email, all of whom were switched on; 6,474 without an email, untouched; zero patients with an email left off; the SMS default unchanged. This is the widest-reaching migration the lane has applied - it changes what 1,930 real people receive - which is why the counts are on the card rather than in a log.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling: the fourth staleness shape is recorded - a card falsified by another committed file's prose trips neither reconciler rule. Card the design, do not build it
rulings.ruling: A card whose prose is contradicted by another committed file's prose is invisible to `reconcile-board.mjs`: its stale-card rule keys on the PRs a card cites and its gate-claim rule on the gate a card claims, and such a card does neither. This is recorded as the FOURTH staleness shape. The design is to be carded. It is NOT to be built without a further ruling on which candidate.
rulings.notes:
A GREEN RECONCILER IS READ AS A TRUE BOARD, which is what makes this expensive rather than untidy. It exited 0 on INC-16 throughout, and the boot report that quoted it was accurate and useless.

BUILDING IS WITHHELD ON PURPOSE. The obvious fix - extract factual claims from card prose and from docs, diff them - is natural-language contradiction detection, and its failure mode is to go quiet when the extractor stops matching. That is the shape this project has been burned by three times (an empty PROD_REFS behind a working-looking comment; a gate-bearing test that skipped; a load-test guard naming a retired ref). A rule that looks mechanical and is not would make the board MORE trusted and no more true.

THIS ONE KEPT ITS DISPATCHED NUMBER. Its two siblings in the same dispatch did not: they were dispatched as SR-14 and SR-15, which were already taken, and are recorded as SR-17 and SR-18. SR-16 was free.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling (dispatched as SR-14): the import RAN. INC-16 resolves against the committed artefacts, and five cards carried a false status
rulings.ruling: The production client-data import HAS happened. INC-16 is resolved against the second column: the owner confirms go-live and reports a production dashboard showing a 153.3 MB database, which 33 staff-training patients cannot produce. LAUNCH-01, LAUNCH-03-client-data-migration, MIG-05-prod-import-path, MIG-06-import-guards and MIG-07-test-patient-cleanup carry a FALSE status and are corrected to shipped by evidence. Nothing is re-run: the PERF-01 measurements were sized against the real database and the ranking stands.
rulings.notes:
NUMBER COLLISION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED SILENTLY. This ruling was DISPATCHED AS "SR-14" on 2026-09-01. That number was already taken on this board by the migration-authorship ruling of 2026-08-31 (migration authorship for 0069 only), so it is recorded here as SR-17 and the dispatched label is written down so a reader searching for the dispatch text finds this entry.

THE EXISTING RULING WAS NOT OVERWRITTEN. PORTAL-REHYDRATE rule 7 already carries this exact disease one register over: "a migration number is taken at BUILD time from whatever is free, never reserved in advance in a deferred card's notes, which is how the same number was double-booked twice." A ruling register has the same property and had no such rule; the strategy terminal numbered from its own count, not from the board's.

THE EVIDENCE IS RELAYED, NOT TERMINAL-VERIFIED, AND EVERY CARD IT TOUCHES SAYS SO. Standing rule 1 forbids this lane reading production at all, read-only included, so no terminal can ever discharge these cards; the dashboard figure arrives as pasted plain text under SR-18 or not at all. Recording an owner reading AS an owner reading is the honest form. Recording it as a proof would be the same error INC-16 exists for, in the other direction.

THE HALT WAS CORRECT AND SO WAS THE MEASUREMENT. PERF-01 stopped before Phase 2, which is why the contradiction cost a dispatch rather than a wrong fix, and its shim was seeded to the shape the PERF-01 card had recorded FROM production - so this ruling confirms the premise those numbers already assumed rather than invalidating them.

rulings.title: Strategy ruling (dispatched as SR-15): production observability reads are owner-only, and the PERF-01 dispatch asking for them was an instruction error
rulings.ruling: Sentry, pg_stat_statements, the Supabase pooler dashboard and Vercel function metrics are OWNER-ONLY reads. No terminal points anything at production, in any environment it did not create locally. Dashboard numbers arrive as pasted plain text or not at all. The PERF-01 dispatch's items 1 to 4 instructed a terminal to read them and were an instruction error on strategy's side, not a terminal failure.
rulings.notes:
NUMBER COLLISION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED SILENTLY. This ruling was DISPATCHED AS "SR-15" on 2026-09-01. That number was already taken on this board by the migration-authorship ruling of 2026-09-01 (migration authorship for 0070 only), so it is recorded here as SR-18 and the dispatched label is written down so a reader searching for the dispatch text finds this entry.

THE EXISTING RULING WAS NOT OVERWRITTEN. PORTAL-REHYDRATE rule 7 already carries this exact disease one register over: "a migration number is taken at BUILD time from whatever is free, never reserved in advance in a deferred card's notes, which is how the same number was double-booked twice." A ruling register has the same property and had no such rule; the strategy terminal numbered from its own count, not from the board's.

IT CHANGES NOTHING ABOUT STANDING RULE 1, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING. Rule 1 already said this. What this ruling adds is that a DISPATCH asking for a prod read does not override it: the terminal that received PERF-01 was right to refuse items 1 to 4 and report them blocked with the owner-run statements written out, rather than reasoning that an explicit instruction outranked a committed rule.

PORTAL-REHYDRATE §4.9 records the same conflict from the other side, where a booting terminal chose the committed rule over an explicit dispatch and flagged it. This makes that the answer rather than a judgement call each terminal has to make alone.

cards.title: LOOP 3 - patient AUTH, 6-digit SMS OTP

evidence.ref:
ACCEPTANCE OBSERVED BY THE OWNER, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-18. This was the ONE check skipped at the 2026-08-17 sitting, and it has now been run from the standalone checklist at docs/board/W13-03-ACCEPTANCE-CHECKLIST.md.

STEPS 1, 2, 3 AND 5 OBSERVED EXACT.
  1. The portal opens on "Entrar com o seu telemovel" and a single phone field. No email field, no password field, no "Recuperar acesso" link.
  2. A number submitted reaches the code screen, the number shown above the field, with the notice "Se o numero estiver registado, enviamos um codigo por SMS."
  3. Below that card: "Nao recebeu o codigo?" and all three lines - no mobile on record, a landline, a shared number - each ending in "Contacte a clinica". All three show together, always, which is what stops the screen becoming a patient-list oracle.
  5. /auth/reset-password returns the portal's not-found page.

STEP 4 WAS NOT RUN, AND IS RECORDED AS NOT RUN RATHER THAN AS A PASS. It needs a real six-digit code and OTP_LIVE_SEND is off, so it belongs to the supervised LAUNCH-01 canary, which now carries it explicitly. The checklist says so in its own words and PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 is the reason: an unrun check that reads as a green one is the collapse this project has already paid for twice.

WHY THE CARD CLOSES ANYWAY, ruled by the owner 2026-08-18: step 4 is not blocked on this card's work, it is blocked on an environment flag that only LAUNCH-01 may arm. Holding W13-03 open for it would park a finished loop behind a launch-day action and hide four real observations behind one unrunnable one. THE ROUTES. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request answers 204 for ANY well-formed number, known or not, and never queries the patient table at all - so membership cannot leak even through the timing of a lookup that is never performed. The only distinguishable outcomes are 400 (malformed input, which tells the caller about their own typing) and 429. Two independent limits, per client key AND per phone hash, because either alone is bypassable: one by rotating the number, the other by rotating the source. The phone limit is applied AFTER normalization, so '912345678' and '+351912345678' cannot be spent as two budgets against one handset.

POST /verify returns ONE 401 with ONE body for all five failure modes. Tested by deep-equality across them, not by both being falsy. It reaches the patient table only AFTER the code verifies - WF-07's claim time - and a test asserts linkage is never called when the code fails.

WF-07 LINKAGE. All four predicates are in the SQL rather than applied afterwards in JS, so a later edit cannot silently widen the candidate set by dropping a filter. LIMIT 2, not LIMIT 1, and that is the load-bearing detail: LIMIT 1 returns the same single row for one match and for five, silently turning an ambiguous match into a confident mis-link.

THE COST IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a patient whose number sits on two rows sees exactly the same screen as someone who mistyped a digit, and cannot be told why. WF-07 accepted that. The alternative confirms to any caller that a number is in this clinic's files, and how many times.

DEGRADATION COPY. The generic otp_refused stays generic and is tested against leaking any predicate.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is one thing: THE SESSION MINT. verify returns the resolved patientId and NOTHING else - no cookie, no token, asserted by test. What it is: the CLAIM is one transaction - verifyCode proves the code, WF-07 linkage resolves the patient, store.consume spends the code, and the trusted device is issued, all on one connection, committing together or not at all (0054 coupling).

THREE CONTRACT CHANGES THIS FORCED, each with a reason that is not cosmetic. (1) OtpStore.consume now RETURNS A BOOLEAN. The consumed_at IS NULL guard stopped the race loser WRITING but nothing stopped it GRANTING - both requests would have claimed one code. (2) verifyCode NO LONGER CONSUMES; it returns codeId and the caller spends inside its own transaction. Consuming inside verifyCode put the spend outside the caller transaction, which is exactly the split 0054 exists to prevent. (3) both stores and the linkage read now take the caller db handle, defaulting to getDbAdmin, so they can be enrolled in that transaction.

NEW ROUTE, POST /api/v1/auth/otp/trusted, which is the isTrusted() check that had to exist somewhere for the 30-day window to be more than a stored fact. === THE SCREENS ARE BUILT 2026-08-06 (branch portal/W13-03-login-screens, 119742f). PG1 STILL FAILS, BY DESIGN: it is a WF-03 gate and closes on Ivan's deployed screen. ===

WHAT WAS BUILT: /auth/login is now a phone screen then a code screen, both posting to a server action that calls the API server-to-server and stores the session with writePortalSession. The trusted-device check runs on load, and only when the browser actually holds a device cookie, so a first-time visitor pays no round trip.

A PREMISE CORRECTION, and it is load-bearing rather than pedantic. W13-03b's card says the device token "belongs to the browser, and the portal has no use for it". The first half is true; the second cannot be. The API plants __Host-ojp_device on ITS OWN host, and under Option B the only caller of that route is the PORTAL SERVER. A Set-Cookie on a server-to-server fetch lands in the portal's response object and is discarded, so the browser never saw it: the 30-day device row was being written at every login and read by nobody. The portal now copies the token into its own first-party cookie and forwards it back as the Cookie header the API's readDeviceToken parses. A copy, not an interpretation - nothing in the portal decodes anything. apps/portal/lib/auth/device.ts, and otp.test.ts asserts the copy happens.

THREE MORE DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE LOGIN USELESS, each found by following the patient PAST the button:
1. proxy.ts asked Supabase for a session. An OTP patient has none by construction (WF-07 refuses a patient row already linked to an auth user), so every patient who logged in was redirected straight back to the login screen.
2. app/page.tsx did the same at the root URL, which is the URL a patient types.
3. account/actions.ts built its Authorization header from the Supabase cookie only, so "editar dados" would have answered 401 for every OTP patient.
All three now read the portal session.

AND LOGOUT: it called supabase.auth.signOut(), which cannot clear an httpOnly portal cookie. It now clears the session AND the trusted device, because a sign-out that leaves a 30-day credential on a shared handset is exactly what a patient signs out to prevent.

THE PASSWORD DOOR IS SHUT, which is Decision D's "no session minted from any other artefact" rather than tidying: /auth/reset-password, /auth/activate and /auth/callback each minted a Supabase session for a patient. They survived the 2026-08-05 magic-link removal only because deleting them then would have left the portal with no login at all - the condition these screens end. All three deleted; the dead "change password" row on the account screen went with them; the guard test INVERTED (it asserted signInWithPassword was present, it now asserts its absence) and additionally asserts the three files are gone and nothing links to them.

THE THREE DEGRADATION COPIES (LOOP 3 step 8) render as STANDING GUIDANCE on the code screen, never as a diagnosis. The API answers ONE 401 for six failure modes so the screen cannot become a patient-list oracle; branching to one of the three would have rebuilt that oracle inside the portal. All three are shown together, always.

E2E HAD TO CHANGE AND IT GOT BETTER. The portal patient signed in with an email and a password, which no longer exist. It now presents a SEEDED TRUSTED DEVICE and lets the ordinary on-load check mint the session: no test-only code in the app, and it exercises the path a returning patient takes every day. The OTP code itself is unreadable to a test by construction - the transport is off outside production and the sink holds the code in the API process's memory - and reading it would have needed the back door this loop exists to remove.

FOUR NEW pt-PT STRINGS were needed and are additive only: otp_invalid_phone, otp_unavailable, otp_help_title, otp_trusted_checking. The eleven the dispatch named all existed.

STILL OPEN ON THIS CARD: the owner merge its gate requires, PORTAL_TENANT_ID (card W13-03c), and the deployed-screen evidence, which WF-03 batches to the acceptance session.

MERGED 2026-08-06 as #828 (6596d15). NOT CLOSED: WF-03 makes the owner's deployed screen the closing evidence, so this card stays in flight until the acceptance session. Two things still stand between the merge and a patient logging in: PORTAL_TENANT_ID (card W13-03c) and OTP_LIVE_SEND, which stays off until LAUNCH-01 arms it.

ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN CI, worth recording because the mistake was mine and it was a reasoning error rather than a typo. The e2e planted the trusted-device cookie with addCookies against an http url and every shard died at the setup: 'Protocol error (Storage.setCookies): Invalid cookie fields', 58 tests never ran. TWO DIFFERENT RULES LOOK LIKE ONE HERE. The Chrome DevTools Protocol validates the URL's SCHEME before storing a Secure cookie and refuses http://localhost outright; the BROWSER separately treats localhost as trustworthy and both accepts and sends Secure cookies there, which is why the portal's own cookies work in dev. I read the second as if it governed the first. Fixed by storing against the https origin - cookies are scoped by host, not scheme - and VERIFIED against a real Chromium before pushing: http rejected, https accepted, and the cookie then arrived on a plain http request. The same probe confirmed the other half nobody had checked: a __Host- Secure cookie set by Set-Cookie from an http://localhost RESPONSE is accepted, captured by storageState, and replayed by a restored context. That is what the portal server does on every login.

THE RULE IS NOW ONE PURE PREDICATE, isServiceBookableByPatient, so each of its three clauses can be SHOWN load-bearing rather than asserted to be. The refusal test is three layers: the predicate exhaustively (including the row that is both internal_only and patient_bookable, which is reachable and is what an admin mis-click produces); that the columns are actually SELECTED, which is the one version of this bug a unit test cannot see, because an unselected column arrives undefined, undefined is falsy, and the check then passes for every row while CI stays green; and that both write paths still resolve through the guarded function. THE DoD's OWN DEMONSTRATION, PASTED. With the internalOnly clause removed: 3 failed | 13 passed - REFUSES an internal_only service; refuses when internal_only is combined with patient_bookable; every clause is load-bearing, that last reporting [false, false, true] where [false, false, false] was expected. THE PEDIDO EMIT, COMPLETE (c475f56). A portal booking now emits appointment_request, not booked. THE FINDING BEHIND IT: three places already told the truth - the patient is shown 'a aguardar confirmacao pela recepcao', confirmation_state defaults to pending, and reception is who confirms. The NOTIFICATION was the only place still calling it a finished booking, so the one item in reception's centre that needed their action was the item that looked like it did not. booked keeps its meaning and loses its caller: it is the kind for a booking confirmed on arrival, which is what JP's post-launch graduation produces. NO MIGRATION WAS NEEDED, and that is a finding rather than luck. Request-mode does not need a new entity: the portal booking path ALREADY creates an appointment awaiting reception confirmation and already tells the patient so. The pedido is that row plus the correct notification.

1. THE RECEPTION CONFIRM SURFACE. Reception now receives an appointment_request in the notification centre; what they do not have is a screen that lists pedidos awaiting confirmation and a control that confirms one. === CORRECTION 2026-08-06, MINE, BEFORE IT WAS BUILT ON. THE CONFIRM AXIS IS THE WRONG AXIS. ===

WHAT I WROTE THREE TIMES - on this card, in #829's body, and to the owner: 'no migration is needed, appointment_confirmation_state has existed since 0024 and is orthogonal to appointment_status by design.' The no-migration half is right. The rest is wrong, and it would have produced a real defect.

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SAYS, re-derived rather than remembered. apps/web/lib/scheduling/estado.ts:8-20 defines the two axes: lifecycle appointment_status, and confirmation appointment_confirmation_state. The confirmation axis answers 'DID THE PATIENT REPLY TO THE REMINDER' - it is written by the Twilio inbound webhook, and appointment-drawer.tsx:1188-1192 shows it READ-ONLY with the comment 'never edited here (BACKLOG specs a display only, no edit control)... shown separately so the two are never visually or semantically conflated.'

SO RECEPTION ACCEPTING A PEDIDO IS NOT THAT AXIS. It is the LIFECYCLE axis: status scheduled -> confirmed. Writing the confirmation axis for a reception action would record 'the patient confirmed' when no patient did, which is the same class of collision as record_status vs ai_review_state (CLAUDE.md rule 4), and it would corrupt the reminder-reply data the clinic reads.

THE CORRECTED DESIGN, and it still needs no migration:
  QUEUE: derive it from the notification rows. staff_notifications of kind appointment_request already exist per R1, already fan out to reception plus both therapists per R2, and already carry appointment_id. Join to appointments and keep the ones still status=scheduled. THIS IS THE ONLY WAY TO IDENTIFY A PORTAL PEDIDO: there is no provenance column, and packages/db/tests/appointments-created-by-provenance.test.ts proved (7/7 against live Postgres) that created_by CANNOT identify portal rows. Do not add a column for it - the notification IS the provenance record.
  CONFIRM: set status = confirmed. That already renders as 'Confirmada' through deriveEstado, and reception can already do it by hand through the Estado selector in the drawer, so the control is a shortcut for an action the product already supports, not a new state.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: no migration, the in-flight slot stays with LOOP 5.

=== THE CONFIRM SURFACE IS BUILT, AND THE OPTION-B RULING LANDED WITH IT (2026-08-06). ===

JP ruled option B on W13-04a: an unconfirmed pedido does NOT hold the slot. That ruling amended this card's next action mid-build. Of its four binding consequences, three shipped and one is halted on an owner decision - see W13-04a-availability-exclusion, which carries the full recon and the recommendation.

SHIPPED. listPendingRequests(ctx) in apps/web/lib/notifications/centre.ts: staff_notifications of kind appointment_request, INNER joined to appointments, kept at status=scheduled. The queue renders as the FIRST section of /notificacoes, above the log, because it is the only part of that page carrying work. confirmAppointmentRequest in apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts, a distinct action rather than updateAppointment(id,{status:confirmed}), because the ruling makes the re-check mandatory: same transaction as the status write, behind the same slot lock every other write path takes, excludeIds set to the pedido itself so its own row cannot block its own confirmation. On conflict nothing is written, the pedido stays scheduled and stays in the queue, and reception is told in pt-PT which appointment took the slot.

DECLINING IS CANCELLING, and no new status was invented. A declined pedido leaves the queue through the same status predicate that removes a confirmed one. There is no declined value on the lifecycle axis and adding one would have been a migration nobody asked for.

THE AXIS CORRECTION HELD THROUGH THE BUILD. The action writes status only. Two tests assert it: a behavioural one over every set() payload, and a source read of the function body, because a behavioural test can only prove the path it happened to take.

PATIENT COPY, the ruling's point 3. Verified rather than assumed: the old wording did not promise the slot outright, but it called a pedido a marcacao and said nothing about the time being provisional, which reads as a reservation. Now "Pedido recebido", and both pending strings state the time is only reserved once confirmed. Patient-visible, so WF-03 applies and it closes on Ivan's deployed screen at the acceptance session.

EVIDENCE. lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, test 8/8 tasks (web 1756 passed), build 4/4. pedido-confirm.test.ts 11/11 with the conflict guard PROVEN load-bearing - replacing if (blocking.length > 0) with if (false) fails exactly the two no-write-on-conflict cases and nothing else. pending-requests.test.ts 11/11. pedido-queue.db.test.ts is DB-gated and SKIPPED locally with no DATABASE_URL; its seven cases including the RLS negative control are proven by the CI run, not by the local one, and this note says so rather than counting them.

=== PRESELECTION SHIPPED (step 5), 2026-08-06. TWO PIECES LEFT. ===

=== FIRST CI RUN, 2026-08-06. ONE REAL FAILURE, TWO INFRASTRUCTURE ONES. THE ARTIFACT WAS READ FIRST. ===

DB-GATED: MINE, AND REAL, BUT NOT AN ASSERTION. 602/602 tests passed, including all seven of pedido-queue.db.test.ts. The suite failed in afterAll: delete from tenants was refused by staff_notifications_tenant_id_fkey. Re-derived at the source rather than guessed - 0055 line 96 declares tenant_id as a PLAIN FK and line 97 declares recipient_user_id ON DELETE CASCADE, and the migration header says so in words: recipient_user_id DOES cascade, and that is the one place. appointments.tenant_id DOES cascade (schema.ts), which is why every other suite deletes a tenant cleanly - and why this one did not: it is the first to persist staff_notifications rows outside a rolled-back transaction. Teardown now deletes them first.

E2E SHARDS 2 AND 3: NOT MINE, and the log says so rather than my inferring it. Both died in "Set up job" with "Failed to resolve action download info. Error: Service Unavailable" then "Internal Server Error", after two retries. No test executed and no playwright-report artifact exists to read, which is itself the evidence: a shard that fails a test produces one. Shard 1 ran the full suite and PASSED in 6m52s on the same commit. The aggregate gate reports the shard result as "abandoned", which is what a job that never started produces.

THE DOCTRINE HELD: the artifact was read before anything was blamed. The runner really was the cause here, and it is recorded with the exact error text so the next reader does not have to take my word for it.

=== STEP 7 SHIPPED, 2026-08-06. THE E2E IS THE LAST BUILDABLE PIECE. ===

patient_bookable is now staff-maintainable from Admin > Servicos, modelled on how is_bookable is surfaced for therapists (0046, the Equipa checkbox): same capability, same audit shape, same not_found. 0057 backfilled the column and JP's real set was then applied to production BY HAND; without a screen every future change is another hand-run statement against production.

ITS OWN CONTROL, NEVER FOLDED INTO ARCHIVE. active answers "does the clinic offer this at all"; patient_bookable answers "may a patient book it themselves". One control for both would make archiving the only way off the portal, and archiving also removes the service from the STAFF agenda. Two forms, asserted as two.

THE AUDIT NAMES THE DIRECTION: service.patient_bookable_on / _off rather than one service.update carrying a payload, so who opened a service to patients is answerable from the trail without diffing rows.

THE MIS-CLICK IS HANDLED WHERE BOOKING HAPPENS. This screen CAN set patient_bookable on a row that is also internal_only - that is reachable and is exactly what a mis-click produces. The refusal stays in isServiceBookableByPatient (active AND patient_bookable AND NOT internal_only), whose every clause already has a test proving it load-bearing. Turning this on grants nothing on its own.

services-patient-bookable.test.ts 9/9. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, test 8/8 tasks (web 193 files), build 4/4.

REMAINING ON THIS CARD, now two items: the availability exclusion (HALTED on the owner, W13-04a-availability-exclusion) and the e2e for preselection and request-mode. The e2e is buildable but cannot be PROVEN while GitHub Actions is in partial_outage - see the CI note above.

=== THE EXCLUSION IS SEQUENCED OUT OF THIS CARD (strategy ruling, 2026-08-06). ===

W13-04a-availability-exclusion is ruled to run AFTER LOOP 5, as the wave's final migration. It is no longer blocked on a person and it is no longer this card's to finish. What remains ON THIS CARD is the e2e for preselection and request-mode - one item.

The interim behaviour is ruled and is the safe side: a pedido HOLDS the slot until the exclusion ships. Everything option B required that does NOT depend on the exclusion is already merged into #830 - the transactional confirm re-check, the pt-PT conflict copy, the patient wording - and all of it is correct under both behaviours.

=== THE E2E GAP I CARDED DID NOT EXIST. MY GREP WAS WRONG. 2026-08-07. ===

I recorded that the positive preselection case could not be e2e-covered because "seed-e2e.mjs creates no appointments". THAT IS FALSE, and the reason is worth more than the correction: the grep behind it searched apps/web/e2e/seed-e2e.mjs, A PATH THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The file is apps/web/e2e/seed/seed-e2e.mjs. ugrep printed "No such file or directory" and I read the empty result as evidence of absence.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: ensureDeclaracaoAppointment (seed-e2e.mjs:322-337) gives Maria Silva a COMPLETED Osteopatia appointment dated 2022-03-15, and fixtures.ts:238 says "Maria Silva's patient row doubles as the portal test patient". So the portal patient has EXACTLY the history Decision C preselects from, and the positive case is not merely coverable - it is the fixture's DEFAULT state.

HOW IT SURFACED, and it is the good news: CI failed on my own assertion that the badge was ABSENT. Expected 0, received 1. The badge was there because preselection WORKS - priorCompletedServiceId found the completed Osteopatia, and Osteopatia is patient_bookable after the seed fix. A test written on a false premise was corrected by the system it was testing.

THE TEST NOW ASSERTS THE WHOLE RULE instead of half of it: the badge appears exactly once, it is on the RIGHT row (a badge on the wrong service would satisfy a bare count), the OTHER bookable service is still offered, the step is not skipped, and every row is enabled. That last-but-one is the Decision C invariant and the one that fails the moment preselection becomes a filter.

THE LESSON, third time this pattern has cost this project: a grep that returns nothing because it searched the wrong place reads identically to a grep that returns nothing because the thing is not there. Check the path resolves before believing an empty result.

=== MERGED 2026-08-07 AS #830 (0987ee7). ===

Green took four CI rounds once Actions recovered, and every one of the four found something real rather than flaking:
