cards.title: A hardcoded mint date plus a 12h TTL turned main red at midnight UTC - fixed, kept as the pattern

evidence.ref: FIXED in #830 (0987ee7), commit f3392d9. apps/api/lib/auth/patient-session.test.ts beforeEach now pins the clock with vi.useFakeTimers() plus vi.setSystemTime(NOW), verified present on main at line 56. 18/18 green, and the Lint+typecheck+test job went from fail to pass on the very next CI run.

cards.notes:
CARDED AFTER THE FACT, 2026-08-07, and it is ALREADY FIXED. The fix rode in #830 rather than waiting for its own PR, because it was the thing BLOCKING #830 and leaving main red overnight to keep a change tidy would have been the wrong trade. Recording the reconciliation rather than re-doing the work.

WHAT HAPPENED. patient-session.test.ts mints every token at a hardcoded NOW of 2026-08-06T10:00:00Z and then VERIFIES it. Verification checks exp against the REAL clock and PATIENT_SESSION_TTL_MS is 12h, so the token expired at 06T22:00Z. CI ran at 07T00:12Z. Two hours too late.

IT WENT RED WITH NO CODE CHANGE ON ANY BRANCH, on the feature branch AND on main at the same moment. git show origin/main carried the identical hardcoded date. A pre-existing LOOP 3 defect that simply reached its detonation date.

THE FIX: beforeEach pins the clock for the whole file. The expiry tests in that same file already did exactly this themselves and were never affected, so the fix only extends the idiom the file had already chosen. Whether a token round-trips is now a question about the code and never about the calendar.

WHY THE CARD SURVIVES THE FIX. The PATTERN is what matters. A test that mints at a FIXED instant and verifies against the REAL clock is a bomb with a fuse as long as the TTL: it passes for months, then fails at a date boundary with no diff to blame, and the first instinct is to hunt the most recent change, which is exactly the wrong place. Anyone adding a signed, expiring artefact to a test should pin the clock in the same commit.

NO OTHER INSTANCE FOUND, but the search was not exhaustive and I am saying so rather than implying coverage. The reminder-token suites and the OTP suites both mint expiring artefacts and are the first places to look if this recurs.

cards.title: Hydration mismatch on the patient profile notes list - toLocaleString differs server vs client

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19 in PR #953, squashed to 111a2cc.

THREE CALL SITES, NOT ONE. The card named notes-list.tsx:139; the same bare `toLocaleString("pt-PT")` also formatted the appointment instant and the edited-at stamp. Fixing only the named line would have left two live copies of the identical defect in the same component.

Europe/Lisbon explicitly - the zone this product displays in per CLAUDE.md, and the one the notification centre already uses. UTC would have removed the mismatch too and shown a Lisbon clinic a time nobody in the building recognises.

THE SOURCE GUARD FAILED ON ITS OWN DOC COMMENT FIRST, and that is the part worth keeping. The comment quotes the defective call to describe it, and a raw text scan cannot tell a description from a call - criterion F at the tooling level, the THIRD instance in one day after the import-vs-JSX assertion and RECON-02's first draft. It now strips comments the way audit-override-trace.test.ts already does, asserts its vacuous-pass guard on the STRIPPED body, and records why stripping is safe here when criterion C warns it is not always.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-07 in an E2E WebServer log while chasing an unrelated failure. Located precisely rather than guessed at, and NOT attributed to the change that happened to be under test.

apps/web/app/patients/[id]/notes-list.tsx:139 renders new Date(note.createdAt).toLocaleString("pt-PT"). The server formats in the Node/ICU timezone and the browser formats in the viewer's, so the two strings differ and React logs "Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client".

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SAID HONESTLY: it is a console error, not a test failure. Every patients.spec.ts test around it passes, and React recovers by re-rendering on the client. What it costs is a real error in the log that trains people to ignore errors in the log.

PRE-EXISTING. Nothing in W13-04 touches this file. It surfaced only because an E2E log was being read line by line for a different reason.

FIX SHAPE, matching how this repo already solves it elsewhere: format on ONE side only. apps/web/app/notificacoes/page.tsx formats server-side with an explicit timeZone: "Europe/Lisbon" and passes strings down, and UpdatePasswordClient uses useSyncExternalStore for the browser locale without a hydration mismatch. Either pattern works here; the second is right if the note timestamp should follow the viewer.

CLOSES ON: the warning absent from a clean E2E run of patients.spec.ts.

BELL VERDICT: REAL, AND FIXED. The owner's report was verified against the code before anything was touched, and all three authoring-time findings held. The bell was a span with aria-hidden=true, no href and no handler, in packages/ui UserAreaCluster.tsx:2,41-48, decorative by design per its own doc comment. apps/web/components/app-shell.tsx:77-88 wrapped the WHOLE cluster in a Link to /perfil. No committed test expressed that invariant before, which is how a decorative element could drift inside a link and stay there.

THE MIGRATION QUESTION FROM THE LAST CHECKPOINT IS ANSWERED BY RECON, and the answer is YES. cards.title: The loud-at-boot sweep covered the notification path only, not every portal var

evidence.ref:
THE PORTAL WALK IS DONE, 2026-08-20, and it found one real silent degradation. Derived from origin/main at a7b4aa6.

THE WALK, COMPLETE: NINE process.env reads in apps/portal across FIVE variables, enumerated rather than sampled (apps/portal/{app,lib,proxy.ts}, excluding tests and .next).
  NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL   3 reads - ONE SILENT, now fixed. See below.
  NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY  2 reads - loud, via the library throw.
  NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL        2 reads (one is a comment) - already owned by lib/api/base.ts and loud. Correctly left alone.
  PORTAL_TENANT_ID           2 reads - both THROW when unset, naming the variable. Loud. Correctly left alone; the duplication is LE-portal-tenant-id-two-readers, a separate card.

THE ONE DEFECT, and it is PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3's FIRST INSTANCE VERBATIM. apps/portal/app/portal/account/actions.ts:27 read `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL ?? ''`, fed it to `new URL()`, and caught the throw with a bare `catch { return null }`. FOUR DISTINCT CAUSES RETURNED THE SAME NULL: (1) the variable absent, (2) set but not a URL, (3) no session cookie, (4) cookie unparseable. apiAuthHeader reads null as "this patient is not signed in" and sends the request with NO Authorization header, so the API answers 401 and the account screen says the edit failed - with nothing anywhere naming the variable. Causes 1 and 2 are deployment faults; 3 and 4 are ordinary. The screen could not tell them apart.

THE FIX IS THE PATTERN THIS CARD'S OWN EARLIER ENTRY ESTABLISHED. New apps/portal/lib/supabase/env.ts is the ONE owner: supabaseUrl(), supabaseAnonKey(), supabaseAuthCookieName(), each logging loudly ONCE PER PROCESS and naming the VARIABLE, never the value. The null return is UNCHANGED, exactly as lib/api/base.ts keeps its callers' shape - what changed is that the two deployment causes now log and the two ordinary ones stay silent, because logging the ordinary ones would bury the ones somebody can act on. All three call sites route through it.

THE TWO CLIENT FACTORIES WERE ALREADY LOUD AND STAY SO. @supabase/ssr throws "Your project's URL and API key are required to create a Supabase client!" on a falsy value - VERIFIED in the installed package (createBrowserClient.js:19), not assumed. They route through the owner only so the log names WHICH variable before the library's generic message, and so the source guard can see them.

9 TESTS in apps/portal/lib/supabase/env.test.ts, every rule in BOTH directions, plus a source-level guard that no module re-derives the reads. TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each with its substitution count asserted: reintroducing a raw read outside the owner turns the guard red (1 of 9); disabling all three log sites turns 6 of 9 red. Both restored and re-run 9/9. Full suite green: portal 249, web 2292, api 613, db 262, admin 10.

THE GUARD CAUGHT ITSELF FIRST, and it is worth recording. Run over raw source it went red on the account action - matching the COMMENT that describes the pre-fix shape. That is the class #962 and #965 removed from five other guards; comments are stripped before the assertion, same helper, and the vacuous-pass guard on the file count is kept.

BOTH NAMED RESIDUALS ARE RESOLVED. REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM was verified and its real defect fixed in this card's 2026-08-04 entry (apps/web's only boot assertion sat on an Inngest route the invite path never touches). FALLBACK 6 no longer exists: apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts is GONE from main, deleted under owner ruling WF-08 (R5), and sendPatientActivation survives only inside comments and test prose. The card said fallback 6 closes when W13-03 rules on that function; the function was removed instead, which closes it more completely.

NOT AN OWNER-VISIBLE BUILD, so it is NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. On a correctly configured deployment - which production is - nothing a patient or a staff member sees changes. The new behaviour is only reachable by removing a variable, which is what the tests do.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20. THE REMAINING SCOPE WAS WALKED AND IT WAS NOT EMPTY. ===

The 2026-08-19 open_on_purpose narrowed this card to one thing: walk every remaining portal env var surface beyond the notification and invite paths. That walk is done - nine reads, five variables, enumerated not sampled - and it found ONE real silent degradation, of the same class the card was opened for and in a module nobody had looked at.

WHY THE ACCOUNT SCREEN WAS THE PLACE IT SURVIVED: the notification and invite sweeps followed SEND paths. This read is on a READ path, in a server action, deriving a cookie NAME. It is not a call to anything and it does not look like a degradation site, which is exactly why walking the surface beats walking the paths.

WHAT A DEPLOYMENT WITH THE VARIABLE MISSING DID: a signed-in patient looked signed OUT to the account screen, every profile edit went out with no Authorization header, the API answered 401, and the screen reported a failed edit. That is the SAME SYMPTOM the comment at the top of apiAuthHeader records having already been fixed once from a different cause - the fix is now guarded against arriving from this one.

BOTH NAMED RESIDUALS RESOLVED, one of them by deletion rather than by ruling: activation.ts is gone from main under WF-08 (R5), so fallback 6 has no code to be dead in.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

Closes PG7. Provisional id; see W13-03 (seeded as PW-01). The pattern to copy already exists: #763 made the notification path fail at boot rather than at the patient, guarded by apps/web/lib/reminders/loud-env.test.ts. Two named residuals: fallback 6 (apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117, PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL silently omitted) is deliberately LEFT as dead code and closes when W13-03 (seeded as PW-01) rules on that function; and REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM must be listed in boot validation for BOTH apps now that it powers staff invites as well as reminders - verify it, do not assume it. Env var NAMES only in any output, never values. Do not re-litigate the two benign cases recorded in docs/notifications-work-notes.md (the TWILIO either-or, and PATIENT_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL defaulting to SMS by owner ruling). RE-CUT 2026-08-04. WAVE-13.md has no ENVIRONMENT loop, because its coverage map rules PG7 already closed on main by #763. So this stops being a build loop and becomes the honest residual: the posture is right and enforced by loud-env.test.ts, but 'every var' in the DoR text is the whole portal surface and only the notification path was walked. Kept as a loose end so the PG7 pass cannot quietly absorb it. Fallback 6 (activation.ts:117) closes with W13-03's ruling on sendPatientActivation.

--- WORKED 2026-08-04, CARD STAYS OPEN ---
The card said 'REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM must be listed in boot validation for BOTH apps - verify it, do not assume it'. Verified by walking the path, and the real defect sat next door to the one described.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: apps/web's only boot assertion was in app/api/inngest/route.ts, which is loaded for Inngest-driven work. Staff invites are not Inngest-driven - lib/admin/staff.ts -> lib/invites/email.ts -> sendEmail in lib/reminders/clients.ts - a chain that never touches that route. So arming INVITES_LIVE_SEND with REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM or RESEND_API_KEY absent booted clean, providerConfigured() returned false, and every invite silently degraded to the temporary-password hand-off: no email, no error, no boot signal. The owner would have seen invites 'working' while nothing was ever sent. Exactly the fails-at-the-user-not-at-boot class #763 removed from the reminder path, surviving on the invite path because the sweep followed the reminder path only - which is what this card exists to record.

VERIFIED AND CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE: apps/api asserts on REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND alone, and that is right rather than an omission. apps/api has no invite path at all ('the only body this app can send is patient activation'), so INVITES_LIVE_SEND would be meaningless there. Adding it would have looked like symmetry and meant nothing. The card's 'BOTH apps' framing is therefore superseded: the gap was two send paths inside ONE app, not two apps.

STILL OPEN, and why this card is not shipped: the DoR's 'every var' is the whole portal surface and only the notification path has now been walked twice. Fallback 6 (activation.ts:117) still closes with W13-03's ruling on sendPatientActivation, which is blocked behind LOOP 1.

PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-05 by WF-08 (R5). This card's first named residual - fallback 6, apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117, PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL silently omitted - was deliberately LEFT because the code was dead and the card said it closes when the ruling on sendPatientActivation lands. That ruling has landed and it is DELETE. So the residual retires with the function rather than being fixed. When W13-03 merges the deletion, come back here and check whether PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL and PATIENT_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL are left unreferenced, and strike them from the fallback inventory in docs/notifications-work-notes.md if so. The card's OTHER open half is unchanged: 'every var' is the whole portal surface and only the notification path has been walked.

FALLBACK 6 IS RETIRED, NOT FIXED, 2026-08-05. This card predicted it: 'fallback 6 (apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117, PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL silently omitted) is deliberately LEFT as dead code and closes when W13-03 rules on that function.' W13-03 ruled DELETE (WF-08), the module is gone, and a repo-wide search for PATIENT_ACTIVATION across apps/ and packages/ now returns NOTHING. Both PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL and PATIENT_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL are unreferenced by any code path, so the fallback inventory row retired with the function rather than being repaired.

ONE ORPHAN LEFT DELIBERATELY: the i18n key patientActivation.smsBody still exists in both strings.pt.json and strings.en.json with no code reference. Kept rather than swept because LE-staff-assisted-activation is a real post-launch card and that pt-PT wording is already written; deleting it would mean re-authoring patient copy later. Recorded so it reads as a decision rather than as something missed.

THE CARD'S OTHER HALF IS UNCHANGED: the DoR's 'every var' is the whole portal surface, and only the notification and invite paths have been walked.

=== THE FULL WALK, 2026-08-07, PR #843. ===

EVERY process.env READ ACROSS ALL FOUR APPS, enumerated rather than sampled:
apps/web 40 vars, apps/api 14, apps/portal 4, apps/admin 4.

WHAT IS ALREADY CORRECT, checked rather than assumed:
  PORTAL_TENANT_ID - requestOtp returns 'unavailable', never a refusal and never
  a build failure, with a test asserting the distinction PG7 exists for.
  PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET - 503 with the variable NAME logged, deliberately not a
  module-scope throw (that failed `next build`, and a build is not a boot).
  STAFF_INVITE_REDIRECT_URL - made loud in #837 the same day.
  The notification path - assertNotificationEnv, #763, guarded by loud-env.test.ts.

THE ONE REAL DEFECT, and it was next door to where the card pointed:
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? '' copied into THREE portal modules
(lib/api/client.ts, lib/auth/otp.ts, app/portal/account/actions.ts).

WHY THE EMPTY STRING IS THE WORST POSSIBLE DEFAULT HERE: fetch('' + '/api/v1/...')
is not a failed call. It is a RELATIVE request to the PORTAL's own origin, which
has no such route. So a missing variable produced a 404 AT THE PATIENT rather
than an error at boot - the dashboard rendered, the request looked like it went
somewhere, and the failure surfaced as "could not load" to a person who could do
nothing about it. Exactly the shape #763 removed from the reschedule link.

FIXED as one owner with a loud log (name only, once per process - a per-request
log on a dead deployment buries the first occurrence), plus a source-level test
that no module re-derives the pattern.

[STRUCK 2026-08-19. The paragraph here read: "STILL OPEN, unchanged: fallback 6
(apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117) is dead code awaiting the
sendPatientActivation ruling." IT WAS STALE AND IT CONTRADICTED THIS CARD'S OWN
EARLIER ENTRY, which already recorded "FALLBACK 6 IS RETIRED, NOT FIXED,

DOES NOT EXIST, and PATIENT_ACTIVATION returns zero matches across apps/ and
packages/ source. The residual retired with the function, as the 2026-08-05 entry
said. Struck rather than deleted so the contradiction stays visible - a card that
disagreed with itself for two weeks is the finding, not the typo.]

=== SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-19 BY STRATEGY RULING. THIS IS NOW THE WHOLE CARD. ===
WALK EVERY REMAINING PORTAL ENV VAR SURFACE BEYOND THE NOTIFICATION AND INVITE
PATHS ALREADY WALKED. Nothing else is outstanding on this card: the named
residual is retired (struck above), the full four-app enumeration was done in
#843, and the one real defect it found (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? '' in three portal
modules) is fixed and guarded.

WHAT "REMAINING" MEANS, so the next session does not re-walk what is done: the
notification path (assertNotificationEnv, #763, guarded by loud-env.test.ts) and
the invite path (the 2026-08-04 finding, apps/web's boot assertion living only in
the Inngest route) are BOTH walked and closed. The DoR's phrase is "every var",
and the portal surface is larger than those two paths.

ENV VAR NAMES ONLY IN ANY OUTPUT, NEVER VALUES - standing rule 3, and it applies
to the deliverable as well as to the working notes.

cards.notes:
=== SILENT APPEND 2026-08-18: one question for JP, not for counsel and not for the security rep. ===
Appended here per this card's own rule. It is a PRODUCT question about who sees which patients' names, raised by engineering during SEC-01 and ACCEPTED AS REPORTED by the owner on 2026-08-18: nothing was changed, and nothing should be changed until JP answers. It is recorded here so JP receives it with the rest rather than as a separate interruption.

SHOULD RECEPTION'S PEDIDO QUEUE BE LOCATION-FILTERED?

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY, re-derived from the source rather than remembered.
`resolveRecipients` (apps/api/lib/notifications/centre.ts) selects EVERY active user whose role slug is `reception`, filtered by tenant and by nothing else. There is no location predicate in that query. So a pedido raised at Linda-a-Velha notifies the receptionist at Castelo Branco, and `listPendingRequests` then shows it to them with the PATIENT'S NAME and the appointment time.

WHY THIS IS NOT A DEFECT AND WAS NOT TREATED AS ONE. It is the direct consequence of D4, JP's own ruling of 2026-08-11, which made `staff_notifications` a PER-RECIPIENT INBOX: migration 0055 pins every read to `recipient_user_id = auth.uid()`, there is no supervisor view, and the owner correctly receives nothing. The reasoning recorded with that ruling was that a patient-initiated change concerns ALL of reception. Engineering did not touch it, because reading a narrower intent into a stakeholder ruling on its own judgement is exactly the decision the standing rules reserve.

WHY IT IS BEING ASKED NOW. PL-09 scoped reception's ORDINARY reads - appointments, patients, and as of 2026-08-18 the guest queue - to the locations they are assigned to. The pedido queue is now the one reception surface that is NOT location-scoped. That may be exactly right, and it may simply be the place the PL-09 sweep did not reach. The two possibilities look identical from the code, which is why it needs a person rather than an inference.

THE ARGUMENT FOR LEAVING IT TENANT-WIDE: a pedido is an unanswered request from a patient who is waiting. If the receptionist for that clinic is away, ill or off-shift, a location filter means NOBODY sees it and the patient waits indefinitely. Cross-cover is a real front-desk practice and the current behaviour supports it without anyone configuring anything.

THE ARGUMENT FOR FILTERING IT: a receptionist at one clinic reads the names of patients at another clinic they otherwise cannot see at all. PL-09 exists because the clinic wanted that boundary, and a boundary that holds on four surfaces and not the fifth is the kind that erodes - the same sentence this card already carries about the guest-queue service name, and it is not a coincidence that both are about one rule holding unevenly.

A MIDDLE OPTION, so JP is not forced to choose between cover and confidentiality: scope the queue to the viewer's locations by default and show other locations' pedidos only once they have gone unanswered for some period. Engineering does not recommend it unprompted - it adds a timer to a surface that currently has none, and the extra machinery only earns its place if JP says both concerns are real.

WHAT IS NOT BEING ASKED: nobody proposes changing D4 itself. The per-recipient inbox, the absence of a supervisor view, and the owner receiving nothing all stand whatever JP answers. The question is only WHICH receptionists are recipients.

IF JP SAYS FILTER IT, that is a card, not a config change: the fan-out is a server-side write that resolves recipients from roles, so location scoping has to happen where the recipients are chosen, and the unassigned-staffer fallback (PL-09 and STAFF-02 both treat no-assignment as unrestricted) has to be decided with it or a new receptionist silently receives nothing on their first day.

=== SILENT APPEND 2026-08-18: one question for COUNSEL, not for the security rep. ===
Appended here per this card's own rule. It is the first item on this card that is

MAY RECEPTION'S GUEST QUEUE DISPLAY THE SERVICE A GUEST REQUESTED?

THE GUARD THAT FORBIDS IT TODAY. lib/notifications/centre.test.ts refuses the
string "serviceName" anywhere in the /notificacoes page source, enforced over the
WHOLE FILE rather than over the notification list alone. PG4 is a launch gate and
the sibling payload-minimization test is annotated "counsel requires this
maintained". When the guest queue row tried to show the requested service, the
suite went red and THE FIELD WAS REMOVED - the guard was not touched.

THE ARGUMENT FOR ALLOWING IT, stated so counsel can rule on the real question
rather than on a summary: PG4's rule exists so a notification about an existing
PATIENT does not disclose what treatment they are having. A guest is different in
kind. They chose the service themselves, minutes earlier, on a public form. They
have no clinical record for it to be about, and they are not yet a patient. What
reception loses without it is triage: they must open each request to see what was
asked for.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, which is why engineering did not act: the moment a guest is
converted, that same string is attached to a person who now HAS a record, and the
queue is a staff screen where both kinds of row sit together. A rule that holds
for one row type and not the neighbouring one is the kind that erodes.

WHAT IS NOT BEING ASKED: nobody proposes weakening the guard for patient
notifications. The question is whether guest rows are inside PG4's intent at all.

WHY IT IS COUNSEL AND NOT THE OWNER ALONE: the guard's own annotation names
counsel as its source. Reading intent into a counsel-derived guard on
engineering's judgement is the decision the standing rules reserve, and this card
exists because that reading was refused rather than taken.

Appended here per this card's own rule rather than opening cards. Neither returns

1. SUPABASE DEFAULT PRIVILEGES GRANT BROADLY AT TABLE CREATION, TENANT-WIDE.
   MEASURED ON ONE TABLE, GENERAL IN CAUSE. Migration 0063 created
   public.guest_booking_requests and granted NOTHING. A production read on
   2026-08-17 found authenticated holding SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT,
   REFERENCES, TRIGGER and TRUNCATE on it, and service_role holding all
   privileges. Nobody wrote those grants: they come from the project's DEFAULT
   PRIVILEGES, applied at CREATE TABLE.

   WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE ENGAGEMENT. Every table in this project has an ACL that
   is partly authored and partly inherited, and the inherited part is invisible
   in the migration files - the only place engineering ever looks. RLS is what
   actually guards the rows, and it holds here, so this is not an exposure
   finding. It is a CONFIGURATION finding: the default privilege configuration
   should be reviewed as a whole, and preferably narrowed, rather than corrected
   one table at a time after the fact. A future table that ships without RLS
   would inherit those privileges too, and nothing in the migration set would
   show it.

   read-only script that produced the finding and can be pointed at any table;
   card GUEST-07-migration-0065-guest-acl is the per-table correction; card
   INC-11-guest-requests-no-grant carries the full output.

2. DEPARTED-COLLABORATOR ACCESS SWEEP ACROSS THE VENDORS.

=== APPENDED 2026-08-13 FOR THE CYBERSECURITY ENGAGEMENT: THE OTP CODE HASH IS
    INVERTIBLE BY ANYONE WITH DATABASE READ ACCESS. MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. ===

APPENDED RATHER THAN CARDED, PER THIS CARD'S OWN PROTOCOL. The dispatch said
"card for the cybersecurity rep"; this card's standing ruling says a security or
legal finding APPENDS HERE and never opens a new card. The ruling wins and the
deviation is reported rather than taken silently.

=== THE FACT ===
patient_otp_codes.code_hash is sha256(sha256(e164) || ':' || code).
Both hashes are UNSALTED and DETERMINISTIC, by documented design
(apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts). The code is 6 digits, so the space is 10^6.

I INVERTED IT. Not as an argument - as a measurement, taken 2026-08-13 while
building the OTP e2e coverage:
    recovering a known code   222ms
    worst case (999999)       305ms
in plain Node on a laptop, no GPU, no precomputation. The e2e spec
apps/web/e2e/portal-otp-login.spec.ts does exactly this on every CI run to read
the code it was issued.

=== WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN ===
IT IS NOT A BREAK OF THE DESIGN. A 6-digit code has a 10^6 space by definition
and the hash was never what protects it. otp.ts says so itself about the phone
hash: it "is a confirmation oracle rather than a secret". The protections are
stated in the same file and all three hold:
    the table is SERVICE-ROLE ONLY (migration 0056, RLS with no policies)
    FIVE attempts per code, then it is dead
    FIVE MINUTES of life
So the exposure is bounded to whoever can read that table, during the five
minutes a code is live.

WHAT IT MEANS IS THAT THE TABLE IS A LIVE-CREDENTIAL STORE, NOT A HASH STORE.
The usual reason to hash a secret at rest is that a database read does not yield
the secret. HERE IT DOES, in a third of a second. Anyone with read access to
patient_otp_codes - a leaked service-role key, a backup, a support export, a
replica, a subpoenaed dump - can log in as any patient whose code is currently
live, and the five-attempt cap does not apply because they are not guessing.

=== WHY IT IS FOR THE CYBERSECURITY REP AND NOT FOR A BUILD QUEUE ===
Every mitigation is a TRADE, not a fix, and none is an engineering call:
    a SECRET PEPPER outside the database would make the hash non-invertible from
      a dump alone, and moves the problem to key custody and rotation;
    a LONGER CODE shrinks the space advantage and costs patient usability on the
      exact login Decision D chose for accessibility reasons;
    SHORTER EXPIRY narrows the window and increases legitimate failures on slow
      SMS delivery.
Choosing among those is a risk decision with a patient-experience cost, which is
the engagement's to make with the owner. Building one now would be guessing.

=== WHAT THE ENGAGEMENT SHOULD BE HANDED ===
    this note, with the 222ms / 305ms measurement;
    apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts, which states the design and its trade-offs openly;
    migration 0056, which is what actually bounds the exposure;
    apps/web/e2e/portal-otp-login.spec.ts, which is a working demonstration.

AND ONE HONEST NOTE ABOUT PROVENANCE: this was not found by attacking the system.
It was found while looking for a way to give Decision D's login its first e2e
coverage without adding a back door. The inversion IS the coverage mechanism, and
it needs no production change - which is itself the observation worth passing on.

The slot is FREE and it is this card's. Re-derived rather than assumed: main ends at 0057_services_patient_bookable, journal idx 56, 57 .sql files in packages/db/migrations and 57 in supabase/migrations, and nothing anywhere holds an unapplied migration.

NUMBER RE-DERIVED AT AUTHORING, never pre-assigned. 0058 is what is free TODAY; that is a reading, not a reservation, and it is re-taken when the migration is actually written.

=== READ-ONLY RECON 2026-08-06, GREENLIT AND COMMITTING NOTHING. AUTHORING-READY EXCEPT FOR ONE OWNER FORK. ===

1. THE FICHA SURFACE, AND THE CONFIRMATIONS BLOCK ALREADY EXISTS. apps/web/lib/clinical/consent.ts is the Ficha Medica consent model (SPEC-ficha-medica.md 5.14 / 7). Two items, CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS = [treatment, rgpd], rendered by apps/web/app/clinical/[id]/SignatureConsent.tsx and wired from RecordForm.tsx:236-240.

2. THE UI PATTERN THE CARD ASKS FOR IS ALREADY BUILT, and matches its wording exactly. Each item is an EXPLICIT TERNARY - granted, denied, or unset - and consent.ts:13-16 states the rule the card restates as "never pre-checked": the UI NEVER renders a bare unchecked box; unset shows a "por decidir" chip and the clinician toggles to an affirmative check or an affirmative X. So the terms item is a THIRD entry in that block, not a new widget.

3. THE PREMISE THAT IT CARRIES A MIGRATION SURVIVES RECON, BUT NOT FOR THE REASON THE CARD IMPLIES, and this is the finding that matters. The existing consent block is MIGRATION-FREE ON PURPOSE: it lives in clinical_records.data jsonb under the reserved key _consent (consent.ts:40), because an underscore-prefixed key cannot collide with a template field or the twelve AI ingestion keys, and validateRecordData only checks required template fields so the extra key rides along untouched. A THIRD ITEM IN THAT BLOCK WOULD NEED NO MIGRATION AT ALL.
   What forces storage is the word PER PATIENT. _consent is per RECORD. The card requires patient_id, accepted_at, terms_version, recorded_by, and the gate must answer "has THIS PATIENT accepted" without scanning every clinical record they own. That question cannot be answered from a jsonb key on a record set.

4. THE OWNER FORK, and it decides the migration shape rather than whether there is one. Does the acceptance need HISTORY?
   A. LATEST ONLY: three columns on patients (terms_accepted_at, terms_version, terms_recorded_by). Smallest migration, one row per patient, trivially indexed, and the patients table already carries exactly this kind of per-patient scalar - activatedAt, nifExempt, the four contraindication booleans, reminderSmsEnabled. Re-accepting a new terms_version OVERWRITES the old one.
   B. FULL HISTORY: a patient_terms_acceptances table, one row per acceptance, so "which version did they accept and when" is answerable for every version. Bigger migration, an RLS policy and an isolation test of its own per CLAUDE.md rule 2 and the repo RLS rule.
   RECOMMENDED: B. The card says this flow is THE SOLE LEGAL PATH to the fee line ever shipping, and JP confirmed no existing signed document contains the fee rule. A legal basis that OVERWRITES its own history cannot answer "what did this patient agree to in March" after the terms change - which is the one question that matters if the fee is ever disputed. A prevents that answer permanently and cannot be migrated back into afterwards, because the overwritten rows are gone.

5. WHAT DOES NOT NEED DECIDING. REMINDERS_FEE_NOTICE_ENABLED stays SPECIFIED NOT BUILT, default OFF - the card is explicit and the packet says so, because claiming a protection that does not exist is the pattern the notification lane spent a session removing. The gate is per-patient acceptance AND the global flag, never the flag alone.

6. STILL TO READ BEFORE AUTHORING, and it is small: SignatureConsent.tsx render loop (the file path contains bracket characters that broke a shell read this session - open it with a tool, not a glob), the i18n keys clinical.consent.<item>.label/.body so the terms item follows the same key shape, and whether writeConsentState has a caller that assumes exactly two keys.

NOTHING WAS COMMITTED BY THIS RECON. The migration slot is untouched and is still this card's, with W13-04a-availability-exclusion sequenced after it.

=== STORAGE RULED 2026-08-06: OPTION B, FULL HISTORY. THE FORK IS CLOSED. ===

patient_terms_acceptances, one row per acceptance, its own RLS policy and an isolation test in the same PR per CLAUDE.md rule 2 and the repo RLS rule. Rationale as ruled: this is the sole legal path to the fee line, terms change over time, only append-only history answers what a patient agreed to at a given DATE, and option A is not upgradeable to B after the fact because the overwritten values are gone.

MIGRATION: slug only, number DERIVED AT AUTHORING, never reserved here. Full post-0057 apply-block doctrine - worktree path verified against the filesystem before the block is issued, a COMMITTED checker naming exactly what the migration created (a TABLE, so check-migration-tables.mjs, never a one-off), evidence written in the SAME TURN the output arrives. Apply before merge. Ivan runs the block after strategy validates it.

=== RECON CLOSED 2026-08-06. THE THREE OUTSTANDING ITEMS ARE READ, AND ONE OF THEM IS A TRAP. ===

1. THE RENDER LOOP IS GENERIC. SignatureConsent.tsx:313 is CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS.map((key) => ...). A third key renders automatically with no component change.

2. THE i18n SHAPE IS TYPE-ENFORCED. CONSENT_ITEM_STRINGS is Record<ConsentItemKey, ConsentItemStrings> (consent.ts:94) keyed clinical.consent.<item>.label and .body. Adding a key to ConsentItemKey without adding its strings is a COMPILE error, so that site cannot be forgotten.

3. NO CALLER ASSUMES EXACTLY TWO KEYS IN A WAY THAT BREAKS SILENTLY. RecordForm.tsx:113 spreads readConsentState(d) and sets one key by variable - fully key-agnostic. emptyConsentState() hardcodes both keys but ConsentState is Record<ConsentItemKey, ConsentDecision>, so omitting a third is again a compile error. Every addition site is forced by the type system.

*** AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS IS DANGEROUS. THE TRAP, NAMED SO THE AUTHORING SESSION DOES NOT WALK INTO IT: ***
Adding "terms" to CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS makes everything COMPILE AND RENDER CORRECTLY, and it will be WRONG. The render loop picks it up, the type system is satisfied, the checkbox appears in the right place with the right ternary - and RecordForm.tsx:113 then writes it into data._consent, which is PER CLINICAL RECORD. The card requires PER PATIENT. The result would be an acceptance that exists on one record and not on the patient, a fee gate that answers the wrong question, and NOTHING IN CI WOULD FAIL. There is no test that could catch it, because every existing test asserts the per-record behaviour that is correct for treatment and rgpd.

SO THE TERMS ITEM IS NOT A THIRD ConsentItemKey. It renders IN that block for the user, and persists through a SEPARATE path to patient_terms_acceptances. The authoring PR must keep CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS at two and add the terms row beside the map rather than inside it, or add a test that asserts _consent never contains a terms key. Preferably both.

NOTHING WAS COMMITTED BY THIS RECON. Authoring opens the moment #830 merges.

The migration half of LOOP 5 is complete and proven. What CI actually proved, beyond a green tick: the RLS suite ran against a real Postgres and confirmed tenant isolation both ways, recorded_by pinned to auth.uid(), UPDATE and DELETE both refused, the blank-version CHECK, the table gate being exactly SELECT plus INSERT for authenticated and nothing at all for patient, and a negative control proving RLS was actually on rather than everything being refused.

TWO GRANT MISTAKES WERE CAUGHT BY TESTS, NOT BY REVIEW, and both are worth remembering. First, the migration granted NOTHING - a new table does not inherit 0003 blanket grant - which made both append-only assertions pass for the wrong reason while the table was unusable. The positive control caught it. Second, the comment claimed the REVOKE was insurance against a FUTURE blanket grant; it is load-bearing TODAY, because Supabase default privileges hand authenticated UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE at CREATE time. Delete that REVOKE and the table silently stops being append-only.

ONE FLAKE, EVIDENCED NOT SHRUGGED AT. nif-required.spec.ts timed out on all three retries at 0df8668 and passed at a4de096, with a diff between those commits of comment-only SQL plus one db test - no app code, no seed, no spec. docs/notifications-approval-packet.md "Variante A / Variante B" are both the 24h

THE SEGMENT HALT CONDITION FIRED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE REPORT.

evidence.ref: #777 MERGED 2026-08-04T15:25:07Z, branch board/LE-darkmode-ink-token, squashed to 0158af7 on origin/main. docs/board/board.css only. Light mode is byte-identical (the token resolves to #ffffff). color-scheme is now restated in both [data-theme] blocks, so UA surfaces (scrollbars, native selects, date pickers) follow the viewer's toggle instead of the OS. Verified against the RENDERED output, since render-board.mjs inlines the CSS: 0 hardcoded #fff, 0 leftover #170a12, 4 --on-accent declarations, 4 --stakeholder declarations, 7 consumption sites, 2 color-scheme restatements.

cards.notes:
Found during the board-parity work and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED there, because both defects are visible changes to the platform board's dark mode and fixing them inside a byte-parity ticket would make the diff unreviewable: a reviewer could no longer tell an intended generalisation from an unrelated colour edit. Two defects. (1) `color-scheme: light dark` is declared only on `:root` (board.css:22) and never restated per [data-theme], so scrollbars, native select popups and date pickers follow the OS rather than the viewer's toggle. (2) Hard-coded #fff on light dark-mode fills, seven sites: board.css:216 .btn.primary (on dark --brand #45b9a7), board.css:287 .pips button.pass (for system-dark viewers who never touched the toggle - the #170a12 patch at board.css:286 is scoped to :root[data-theme="dark"] only), and the five .segrow.status button[aria-pressed="true"] fills at board.css:461-465 (shipped, blocked, in_flight, halted, todo). The fix is one theme-driven ink token used in all seven places, the same job --brand-ink already does for brand-tinted surfaces. Also worth folding in while there: two person-coupled sites that survived the parity work untouched because the additive-only rule forbade editing an existing declaration - board.css:323 colours the rodica_batch lane RAIL with var(--rodica), so on this board the STAKEHOLDER FEEDBACK lane wears a person's colour for a person who is not on it, and board.css:395 colours the `stakeholder` gate badge the same way, which five cards on this board carry. Neither is wrong-looking today; both are a token whose name has outlived its meaning.

--- CLOSED 2026-08-04 (#777) ---
The card's line citations for the two person-coupled sites were WRONG and were re-derived rather than transcribed: board.css:323 and :395 as written, 325 and 399 in fact. The seven #fff citations were correct.

Both were fixed with ONE token each rather than seven patches. --on-accent is deliberately not --ink: --ink is text on paper, --on-accent is text on a filled accent, and the two move in OPPOSITE directions between themes, which is why a single literal could never be right in both. --stakeholder carries the identical value to --rodica in both themes, so the role/person split is a rename by indirection with zero visual change; --rodica stays for the two sites that really do mean the person.

The deleted :root[data-theme="dark"] .pips button.pass patch was itself the shape of the bug: it fixed the gate pip only for viewers who had touched the toggle and left every system-dark viewer on 2.41:1.

ONE FINDING DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: light-mode --todo (#a86f10) with white ink is 4.25:1 and already failed 4.5:1 before this PR. Fixing it means changing a light-mode palette VALUE, which is a visible redesign rather than a tokenisation - and silently altering the light palette inside a dark-mode ticket is the same mistake this card was created to avoid. Flagged, not folded in.

cards.title: Shard the Playwright e2e gate across three runners, required check name held stable

evidence.ref: #774 MERGED 2026-08-04 (5fc88a2). MEASURED, not estimated, on run 30942125889 - the first run where all three shards completed on one commit with the isolation defect fixed: shard 1 6m43s, shard 2 6m58s, shard 3 7m10s, aggregate gate 3s. Wall clock ~7m13s, and the number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average. Against the same day's unsharded runs on real code changes (12m30s, 13m00s, 13m22s, 13m57s, 14m08s) that is roughly a 45% cut. The split is now even - 27s between fastest and slowest - where before the fix it ran 6m27s to 13m22s because shard 3 was spending 6.3 minutes on doomed retries, which is exactly why no figure was quoted earlier. Required check name held: 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' reported and passed as the aggregate, and branch protection needed NO change - the hard constraint on the whole design.

cards.notes:
Not a Wave 13 loop. Infrastructure that pays back across every PR of the wave, dispatched by the owner before LOOP 1.

THE CONSTRAINT: branch protection pins three contexts by exact string, and a check context IS a job name. Sharding the existing job in place would have renamed its checks to 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB) (1)' and friends; the required context would never report again and every PR would hang forever on a check that no longer exists. So the work moved to a job named 'E2E shard' and a new aggregate job inherits the exact old name, runs no tests, and fails unless all three shards succeeded. NO REPOSITORY SETTINGS CHANGE IS NEEDED - which was the stated fallback condition.

Workflow file and matrix only: zero test-file edits, zero playwright.config.ts edits, retries untouched (no --retries flag on pull_request, so the config's CI ? 2 : 0 still governs).

VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED: setup runs in every shard. Pinned Playwright 1.60.0, runner/index.js:2443-2465 - the shard filter iterates rootSuite.suites, which holds top-level projects only, and dependency projects are prepended afterwards from the UNFILTERED suite. That is also why the invocation now passes --project=chromium alone: naming setup explicitly promotes it to top-level and puts its tests INTO the shard filter, the one arrangement where a shard could receive no setup tests.

THE RED PATH IS PROVEN, and not by a contrived test. A deliberate forced-failure run was planned; it turned out to be unnecessary because attempt 1 produced the exact scenario that needed proving: shard 3 genuinely failed while shards 1 and 2 passed, and the required check 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' went RED in 4 seconds. That is the partial-failure case - one leg red, two green - which is the one that matters and the one a designed-to-work argument could not have settled. `if: always()` plus a strict 'success' comparison behaved exactly as intended. Skipped is deliberately NOT accepted as success; this repo has already been bitten by a green that was really a skip.



--- CORRECTION AND DIAGNOSIS, 2026-08-04. THE EARLIER CHECKPOINT WAS WRONG. ---
Board checkpoint 01 (#776, merged) recorded that the cross-file-dependency hypothesis was CHECKED AND REFUTED. That was WRONG, and it was wrong because the check was too narrow: it asked who else REFERENCES the fixture constant AI_REVIEW_DRAFT, when the question that mattered was who else MUTATES the shared review queue. Correcting it here rather than leaving a merged board claim standing.

THE REAL CAUSE, proven rather than hypothesised. e2e/clinical.spec.ts:169-188 HARD-DELETES AI_DELETE_DRAFT, which fixtures.ts defines as a SECOND draft belonging to the SAME patient, Joao Pereira. e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts:36-39 finds its queue row by getByRole("row").filter({hasText: patientName}).first().
Unsharded, clinical.spec.ts runs BEFORE revisao-consulta.spec.ts (file order, c before r), so by the time revisao-consulta reads the queue there is exactly ONE Joao Pereira row and .first() is unambiguous.
Sharded, the local listing puts clinical.spec.ts in SHARD 1 and revisao-consulta.spec.ts in SHARD 3. AI_DELETE_DRAFT is therefore never deleted in shard 3, two Joao Pereira rows sit in the queue, and .first() selects the wrong one - whose Assumir never becomes clickable. Hence a 120s locator.click timeout, three times, 6.3 of the 10.4 minutes, which is also why shard 3 was the long pole.

THIS IS A LATENT TEST-ISOLATION DEFECT THAT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. revisao-consulta.spec.ts has always depended on another spec file having run first. Any change to file order would trigger it.

PARKED per the owner ceiling of one working session. The enabling fix is one line in a TEST file - scope the row by data-record-id, exactly as clinical.spec.ts:173 already does, instead of hasText + .first() - and this PR was dispatched with zero test-file edits, so it does not belong here.

UNBLOCK CONDITION, exact: authorise the one-line test-isolation fix to e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts as its own PR. Once that is on main, #774 needs no change of its own - re-run its checks and all three shards should go green.
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: authorise it. The defect is real independently of sharding and the fix makes the test say what it means.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN AND SURVIVES THE PARK: the required-check name held stable (three new E2E shard (N) contexts appeared, Playwright E2E (seeded DB) kept reporting, branch protection untouched); setup ran in all three shards; and the RED PATH works - one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds.
WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: the wall-clock win. Shards 1 and 2 came in at 7m27s and 6m27s against the 13m21s baseline, but shard 3 spent 6.3 minutes on three doomed retries, so no honest speed figure exists until the test is fixed. The number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-04, and the park was the right call ---
Parking it rather than merging on a red run is what produced the correct diagnosis. Merging it green-by-retry would have shipped the shard split on top of a live test-isolation defect and left the next person to find it.

The red path was proven twice over: once by accident on attempt 1 (one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds), and the planned deliberate forced-failure run was never needed.

--- OWNER RULING 2026-08-05: THE SPEC DRIFT CHECK BECOMES REQUIRED. ---
Ivan is making the branch-protection change dashboard-side; no repo change is needed and none was made. THE EXACT CONTEXT STRING GITHUB LISTS IS THE JOB NAME, NOT THE WORKFLOW NAME, which is the same trap this card was created by: the workflow is named "OpenAPI drift" (.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml:1) and the job is named "Validate spec + drift check" (:19). The string to tick is "Validate spec + drift check". If it is absent from the list, it is because GitHub only offers contexts it has SEEN report on the default branch in the last week - the workflow is path-filtered (apps/api/app/api, apps/web/app/api/v1, docs/api/openapi.yaml, scripts/check-openapi-drift.mjs, its own file), so it does not run on PRs that touch none of those. cards.title: Address the review-queue row by record id, not by patient name

evidence.ref: #785 MERGED 2026-08-04 (0b32eed). Owner-authorised. revisao-consulta.spec.ts now passes in 8.3s with no retry, where in shard 3 it was timing out at 120s three times over. Two files: the spec's locator, plus data-record-id on the review queue's desktop <tr> and mobile <li>.

cards.notes:
A LATENT DEFECT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. fixtures.ts seeds TWO drafts for the same patient (AI_REVIEW_DRAFT and AI_DELETE_DRAFT, both Joao Pereira). revisao-consulta.spec.ts found its row by patient NAME and took .first(), which was only ever correct because clinical.spec.ts runs earlier in file order (c before r) and hard-deletes the second one at clinical.spec.ts:169-188. So the spec silently depended on ANOTHER SPEC FILE having run. Renaming a spec, or adding one that sorts between them, would have broken it with no sharding involved.

WIDER THAN A TEST EDIT, and flagged as such at the time: the queue row carried only a React `key`, which never reaches the DOM, so there was nothing addressable. data-record-id was added to the markup, mirroring the attribute the patient Registos tab already uses - which is how clinical.spec.ts:173 targets that very record. Inert: no behaviour, no styling, no data beyond an id already in that row's own links.

SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION IN BETWEEN, recorded because the lesson is the useful part: putting the attribute on BOTH layouts and then writing an unqualified [data-record-id=...] locator matched two elements - the queue renders desktop table AND mobile list into the DOM at all times, hidden by CSS - and Playwright strict mode refused it. The hook was right; the selector was ambiguous. Qualifying it to tr[...] fixed it. It shipped because an e2e locator change was made without running e2e, the same shape of miss as running a filtered test suite instead of the root gates.

cards.title: Portal deployment failure: every apps/api call from the portal is failing

evidence.ref: CLOSED 2026-08-05 on the DEPLOYED portal per WF-03. Ivan screenshots of osteojp-portal.vercel.app/portal/dashboard: "Ola, ZZ" with the greeting populated and the appointments card rendering, and /portal/appointments rendering "Nao tem consultas marcadas" - the LOADED-AND-EMPTY state, not the PL-34 error state. That distinction is the proof: before PL-34 both a real empty list and a failed fetch rendered identically.

cards.notes:
ROOT CAUSE, TWO LAYERS, BOTH PROVEN AND BOTH FIXED.

LAYER 1 - ZERO PATIENT LINKAGE. All 21 prod patients had auth_user_id NULL. The access-token hook (public.custom_access_token_hook, 0010_patient_identity_layer.sql:204-221) resolves a patient by p.auth_user_id = v_user_id; on a miss it stamps NO claims and still returns the event, so a perfectly signed token is issued carrying nothing. parsePatientPrincipal (packages/auth/patient.ts:50-56) then rejects it and every patient route 401s. No error, no log, nothing observable - which is why it survived.

LAYER 2 - STAFF IDENTITY PREEMPTION. Ivan was testing as owner staff accounts (info@a-and-i-automation.com, then ivanbong333@gmail.com, the latter proven staff role_slug=owner by the 0b check BEFORE any write). The hook checks the staff branch FIRST; a staff identity can never receive patient claims. Correct design, wrong test identity. The portal shell admits any valid session and role enforcement happens at the api, which is why login appeared to succeed while every data call 401ed.

THE FIX: a dedicated non-staff identity linked to a dedicated ZZ TESTE patient row. No real patient record was touched - linking a real patient to Ivan's login would have handed him another person's clinical data, which is the boundary this entire wave exists to defend.

BUILD HALF, closed earlier the same incident: the deployed osteojp-api was serving a stale build - /api/v1/patient/profile 404ed while /api/health answered. A no-cache rebuild of the SAME commit (1131f2d) flipped it to a correct 401. Cause confirmed, no code change.

FALSE TRAILS KILLED ALONG THE WAY, recorded so they are not re-walked: root-directory config (verified correct), deployment protection (api root page renders openly), split-brain Supabase projects (anon key identical across all three Vercel projects), stale build (production current at 1131f2d), path mismatch (both route files exist at the composed paths), middleware 404 (updateSession only ever returns NextResponse.next), and the two health-URL 404s which were CHAT GUESSES at paths that never existed - the real path is /api/health.

THE CHECK THAT PAID FOR ITSELF: step 0b, the staff-exclusion predicate, ran BEFORE any write and caught ivanbong333@gmail.com as owner staff. Without it the fix would have been applied to an identity that could never work, and the failure would have looked identical.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WAVE, carded against LOOP 3: no patient portal login can ever have worked against prod, because provisionPatientAuthUser (activation.ts:65-95) is the ONLY code that ever wrote auth_user_id and it is registered approved:false and slated for deletion. LOOP 3 must SUPPLY the linkage mechanism, not merely replace activation.

cards.notes:

THE BLOCKER. THE THREE PIECES:
1. A test-file CONVENTION for apps/web tests needing a live database - they must SKIP cleanly when DATABASE_URL is unset, or ci.yml (which has no database) goes red. packages/db/tests/rls-harness.ts already models this with `const live = Boolean(url)` and `live ? describe : describe.skip`.

THEN the three DoD lines land: action and consumption commit or roll back TOGETHER with a forced failure between them; a cancel token issued at 48h and redeemed at 30h before start refused with the pt-PT telephone copy; a refusal writes an audit row. Plus the partial line - that a consumed token's response is byte-identical to a forged token's.

And once for real: the suite's FIRST CI execution went red on a fixture bug (a JS Date bound as a timestamptz through the raw sql template, which the driver rejects; drizzle's typed insert builder converts it, a raw template does not). All seven cases failed identically at seedAppointment, so nothing about redeemActionToken had been exercised - and the guard could not have hidden that. evidence.ref:

THE HYPOTHESIS ON THIS CARD WAS RIGHT, AND THE MECHANISM WAS EXACTLY AS PREDICTED. The card said: apps/api/lib/notify/clients.ts records that the verified Resend identity lives on send.osteojp.pt and a root-domain sender is REJECTED; Supabase Auth SMTP is a separate sender configuration the app code never touches, so if its sender is wrong it fails the same way.    WHAT WOULD BE A DEFECT: no section at all; the section BELOW the pedido queue;

   THE POPULATED ARM CANNOT BE RUN AND IS NOT BEING ASKED FOR. A row appears only

=== ITEM 3 ADDED 2026-08-20. THE QUEUE IS AT THREE, WHICH IS THE WF-09 TRIGGER. ===
3. THE AGENDA SAYS HOW OLD IT IS (LE-agenda-does-not-learn-of-portal-bookings).
   Open /agenda as reception, or as yourself, on a desktop screen.
   EXPECTED, in the toolbar at the top right, next to "Nova marcacao":
     - a chip reading "Atualizado as HH:MM", showing the time the page was read.
     - beside it a button "Atualizar" with a circular-arrow icon.
   THEN THE PART THAT IS THE ACTUAL TEST, and it takes about a minute:
     note the time on the chip, WAIT until the clock has moved on a minute or two,
     then press Atualizar. THE CHIP MUST MOVE TO THE NEW TIME. A chip that keeps
     showing the old time means the refresh is not re-reading; a chip that shows
     the CURRENT clock time WITHOUT pressing anything is the worse failure and the
     one this build exists to avoid - it would mean the screen is reading its own
     clock rather than reporting when the data arrived, and it would look freshest
     exactly when it was stalest.
   WHAT WOULD BE A DEFECT: no chip; no button; the chip in English; the chip in a
   12-hour format (it must be 24h, matching the times down the left of the grid);
   or the chip changing on its own without a refresh.

   WHY IT IS THERE, in one line, because you will reasonably ask what it fixes: an
   agenda left open at reception does NOT learn about a booking made through the
   patient portal until somebody navigates or reloads. That has not changed and is
   not a double-booking risk - the database refuses the second booking regardless.
   What changed is that the screen no longer implies it is live when it is not.

   NOT ASKED FOR, and said so it is not attempted: making the agenda update ITSELF
   is a separate build (polling) that was deliberately not done. If reception finds
   the lag costly in practice, that is the next step and it is on the card.

=== ITEM 4 ADDED 2026-08-20 (RB-03). THE QUEUE IS AT FOUR. ===
4. A MANUAL TIME OUTSIDE THE THERAPIST'S HOURS IS NOW REFUSED.
   BOTH ARMS. The second is what tells you the fix did not break booking.

   ARM 1, THE REFUSAL. Open /agenda, Nova marcacao. Pick a therapist who HAS
   hours set in Horarios - Catarina is the reported example, ending at 13:00.
   TYPE a time outside them, 17:00, into the time field rather than picking a
   slot. Save.
   EXPECTED: it REFUSES, and the message NAMES her hours that day - something
   like 'Fora do horario do terapeuta nesse dia. Horario nesse dia: 08:00-13:00.'
   followed by a line saying to change the disponibilidade in Horarios first.
   WHAT WOULD BE A DEFECT: it saves; or it refuses WITHOUT naming the hours; or
   it offers 'Guardar mesmo assim' and that button then saves it anyway. That
   last one is the important one - the override is not supposed to reach this
   refusal, and if it does, the bug is back with one extra click in front of it.

   ARM 2, THE ORDINARY PATH STILL WORKS. Same drawer, same therapist. This time
   PICK a slot from the disponibilidade panel instead of typing, and save.
   EXPECTED: it saves normally, with no message and no change from before.
   WHY THIS ARM EXISTS: a fix that refused everything would pass arm 1
   perfectly and stop the clinic booking. Arm 1 alone cannot tell them apart.

   ARM 3, ONE MINUTE, AND IT IS THE ONE WITH THE WORST FAILURE MODE. Pick a
   therapist who has NO hours set in Horarios at all. Type any time. Save.
   EXPECTED: it SAVES. Availability is opt-in - a therapist nobody has
   configured hours for stays bookable at any hour, exactly as today.
   IF IT REFUSES, STOP AND SAY SO: that would mean any therapist without hours
   set has become unbookable, which is a bigger problem than the one this fixes.

   ALSO WORTH KNOWING, and it is a question rather than a check: there is now
   NO way to book a one-off exception outside a therapist's hours. Extending
   the disponibilidade in Horarios is the intended answer. If the clinic needs
   a real exception path, say so at the sitting and it gets carded.

=== ITEM 5 ADDED 2026-08-20 (landline ruling). THE QUEUE IS AT FIVE. ===
5. PATIENTS WHOSE REMINDER CANNOT REACH THEM.
   Open /notificacoes as reception, or as yourself.
   EXPECTED: a section headed 'Pacientes sem SMS possivel', BELOW the two
   request queues and ABOVE the notification log. Beneath the heading, a line
   saying these patients have a marcacao coming up, the number on file is a
   fixo which cannot receive SMS, they will not get their lembrete, and to ask
   for a telemovel.

   THE LIKELY RESULT IS AN EMPTY BOX and that is not a failure. It lists
   patients who have BOTH a landline on file AND an appointment still to come.
   If the clinic has none right now, expect 'Nenhum paciente nesta situacao.'
   and beneath it 'Todos os pacientes com marcacao proxima tem um numero que
   recebe SMS.'

   IF YOU WANT TO SEE IT POPULATED, and it is worth one minute: open any
   patient with a future marcacao, change their telefone to a Lisbon fixed
   line - 212 345 678 - save, and reload /notificacoes. They should appear,
   with the number AS YOU TYPED IT (not reformatted) and the date of their
   next marcacao. PUT THE REAL NUMBER BACK afterwards.

   WHAT WOULD BE A DEFECT: no section; the section listing a patient with a
   MOBILE; the same patient listed more than once when they have several
   upcoming marcacoes; the number shown reformatted to +351212345678 rather
   than as stored (reception reads it back to a person); or English text.

   THE OTHER HALF OF THIS RULING IS INVISIBLE BY DESIGN. Reminders to those
   numbers are no longer sent, so nothing on any screen changes for them - the
   only observable difference is a smaller Twilio bill. There is nothing to
   check for it, and that is why this item is only about the list.

=== QUEUED 2026-08-20: RB-01 AND RB-02. Both merged, both green, neither seen. ===

RB-01 - RECUPERACAO DE UTENTES (#998, merged 308399a). Sign in as owner, admin or reception.

  A. GO TO /recuperacao. It is also in the sidebar as "Recuperacao", between Marcacoes and Faturacao.
     EXPECTED: a page titled "Recuperacao de utentes" with either a list of patients or the empty message.
     BOTH ARMS COUNT AS AN OBSERVATION AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT FACTS. If everyone has rebooked the
     honest answer is "Ninguem para contactar." plus a second line explaining why. WHAT WOULD BE
     WRONG is a blank area with no message at all: that is the page failing to load, and it looks
     almost identical. Say which of the two you saw.

  B. IF THERE ARE ROWS, pick one and read it. EXPECTED: the patient's name, the date of their last
     consultation, the therapist who saw them, and their telephone number AS IT IS STORED - not
     reformatted into +351.

  C. THE BUTTONS. A patient with a mobile shows WhatsApp and SMS; a patient with an email shows Email;
     a patient with a FIXED LINE shows NEITHER WhatsApp NOR SMS and instead says so in words.
     PRESS WhatsApp ON ONE PATIENT. EXPECTED: WhatsApp opens with a message already written, addressed
     to that patient by FIRST NAME and naming the date they were last seen. NOTHING IS SENT until you
     press send inside WhatsApp. You can edit every word first.
     THE COPY IS A DRAFT AND IT IS YOURS TO CHANGE. It has not been approved by anyone.

  D. GO BACK TO /recuperacao. EXPECTED: under that patient, a line saying "WhatsApp contactado por
     <your name> em <date and time>". READ THE NOTE UNDER THE LIST: it says the mark records that
     somebody OPENED the contact, not that a message was sent or delivered. Tell us if that sentence
     is not clear enough, because the whole point is that nobody mistakes the mark for a delivery.

  E. ADIAR. Press Adiar on a patient and choose 4 semanas. EXPECTED: they leave the list immediately
     and appear in the "Adiados" section below, with the date they come back and your name.
     Then press "Trazer de volta". EXPECTED: they return to the main list.

  F. THERAPIST CHECK, and this is the one that matters most. Sign in as a THERAPIST.
     EXPECTED: NO "Recuperacao" entry in the sidebar, and typing /recuperacao in the address bar
     sends them to the dashboard. A therapist must never see this list - it is every patient's
     telephone number in one place.

RB-02 - PACOTES (#999, merged 325c2e6).

  G. THE OBSERVATION THAT MATTERS MOST, DO IT FIRST. Open a patient who ALREADY has a pacote,
     Consultas tab. EXPECTED: the number reads EXACTLY what it read before today. The migration
     proved this arithmetically on the live database; you looking at a real pacote is the acceptance.
     IF ANY EXISTING PACOTE READS A DIFFERENT NUMBER, STOP AND SAY SO IMMEDIATELY.

  H. THE CONSUMIR AND RESTAURAR BUTTONS ARE GONE from that panel. That is deliberate, not a
     regression. A falta is now recorded by marking the marcacao as "Faltou", which spends the
     session by itself - the button existed to do that by hand, and it could be pressed for a
     patient with no marcacao at all, which is why the number could never be checked against the diary.
     READ THE LINE UNDER THE LIST explaining where the sessions are counted from.

  I. BOOK A PACOTE SESSION. Nova marcacao, pick a patient with a pacote, choose the Pacote.
     EXPECTED: a banner showing the sessions left BEFORE you save. Save it, then reopen the patient.
     EXPECTED: the number has gone down by one.

  J. CANCEL THAT MARCACAO. EXPECTED: the session comes BACK. A cancelled marcacao does not spend a
     session; a falta does.

  K. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-21, BEFORE THE SITTING, BECAUSE IT WAS WRONG. Do not look for it.
     This step said a pacote could now book several marcacoes at once through the repeticao
     control. IT CANNOT, and nothing about that is visible on your screen. "Agendar lote" is
     HIDDEN whenever a Pacote is selected - it has been since W8-01c and this batch did not

     control that is not there.
     WHAT IS TRUE: booking a pacote still books ONE marcacao, and that one is now linked, which
     is what steps G to J check. The rest is written up on the card and carded as RB-02b.

=== QUEUED 2026-08-21: RB-02b. Merged, green, not seen. ===

RB-02b - A PACOTE BOOKS N MARCACOES, EVERY SLOT HAND-PICKED. This is the half of
RB-02 that step K wrongly said was already there. Sign in as owner, admin or reception.

  L. THE SECTION APPEARS. Nova marcacao, pick a patient who HAS a pacote, choose the Pacote.
     EXPECTED: below the sessions banner, a box with "Quantas sessoes marcar agora" and a number
     ALREADY FILLED IN with the sessions the pacote has left. Beside it a line saying how many are
     available and that you may book fewer.
     WHAT WOULD BE WRONG: no box at all; or the number blank; or a number LARGER than the balance
     the banner just showed you. Those two numbers must agree - they come from the same query, and
     if they disagree, say so and stop.
     ALSO WRONG, AND WORTH LOOKING FOR DELIBERATELY: any weekday picker, any "a cada N semanas",
     any "Gerar datas" button. There is meant to be NO way to impose a rhythm here. If you see one,
     the pacote path has been wired to the lote by mistake.

  M. THE SLOT LIST. Set the number to 3.
     EXPECTED: three numbered rows appear. ROW 1 already carries the date and time you picked in the
     form above. ROWS 2 AND 3 ARE EMPTY, and that is deliberate - the system does not choose the
     spacing, you do.
     WHAT WOULD BE WRONG: rows 2 and 3 pre-filled with dates a week apart, or any other pattern.
     That would be the system deciding a cadence for a patient, which is the thing this design
     refuses to do.

  N. IT REFUSES AN INCOMPLETE LIST. Leave row 3 empty and press Guardar.
     EXPECTED: it refuses with a message saying a session is missing its date or hora, and NOTHING
     is booked. Check the agenda afterwards to confirm nothing appeared.
     WHAT WOULD BE WRONG: it books rows 1 and 2 and drops row 3 silently. That is the failure this
     whole card is careful about - a partial success that looks like a whole one.

  O. IT BOOKS THEM. Fill rows 2 and 3 with real free slots, then Guardar.
     EXPECTED: three marcacoes appear in the agenda, all for that patient, all with the PACOTE'S
     service, on the three dates you chose. Then open the patient's ficha, Consultas tab.
     EXPECTED: the pacote balance has gone down by THREE.
     WHAT WOULD BE WRONG: the balance going down by one; or the marcacoes carrying a different
     service from the pacote's.

  P. THE REFUSAL, AND IT IS THE ARM THAT MATTERS MOST. Pick a patient whose pacote has only a FEW
     sessions left - use the one from step O, which now has three fewer. Try to set the number
     HIGHER than what is left.
     EXPECTED: the box will not let you type more than the balance. Then, to test the server rather
     than the form, book the pacote down to its last session and try to book 2.
     EXPECTED: it REFUSES, and the message names the problem: the pacote does not have enough
     sessions, with a suggestion to book fewer or register a new pacote.
     WHAT WOULD BE WRONG, AND THIS IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: it books SOME of them and reports success.
     If you ever see a batch partly booked with no message saying so, stop and say so - the whole
     design turns on refusing rather than truncating.

  Q. A BUSY SLOT IS DIFFERENT FROM A REFUSAL, and both must still work. Book 2 sessions where one of
     the two slots is a time the therapist is NOT available - outside their horario that day, or
     already taken.
     EXPECTED: the free one is booked, and a dialog lists the busy one with a suggested nearby time.
     The balance goes down by ONE, not two.
     WHY BOTH ARMS: step P is "you asked for more than you have" and this is "one of the times you
     picked is not free". They are different problems with different answers, and a system that
     conflated them would either refuse a whole batch over one busy slot or quietly drop sessions.

=== RE-RUN 2026-08-21 AFTER INC-12. RB-01 AND RB-02b STEP L. ===

CLOSED AT THE SITTING AND NOT TO BE RE-RUN: RB-02 steps G-J, item 4 all three arms, item 5. Their cards carry the Observed lines.

evidence.ref:
SR-17 (dispatched as SR-14), strategy ruling 2026-09-01. THE IMPORT RAN.

RELAYED FROM THE OWNER, NOT VERIFIED BY A TERMINAL, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT: standing rule 1 forbids this lane reading production at all, so this card cannot ever carry a terminal-run proof. The owner confirms go-live and reports the production dashboard showing a 153.3 MB database. Thirty-three staff-training patients do not produce 153.3 MB.

IT AGREES WITH THREE COMMITTED ARTEFACTS THAT WERE ALREADY ON MAIN, which is what made INC-16 a contradiction rather than a question. 0068's header records Sentry statement timeouts on production and 41,000 appointments; the PERF-01 card records a production EXPLAIN at 227.163 ms cold / 170.734 ms warm over 188 rows and dual=0; PERF-06 records 8,400 patients and 41,429 appointments; PHASE-2-PERF.md TASK 4 calls the import complete.

THE BOARD WAS THE WRONG SIDE. This card carried `todo` while the work behind it had happened, and it told four dispatches that production was empty.

cards.notes:
CREATED 2026-08-05 by WF-12 (R9), which requires a launch-day sequence card and puts the arming of both live-send flags on it. This card is the sequence. It executes on launch day, not before, and every step is owner-terminal: env changes are cloud writes and PURPLE performs none of them.

PRECONDITION FOR THE WHOLE SEQUENCE, per WF-10 (R7): a patient can use every planned portal feature start to end. Not a gate count, a behavioural condition on the deployed app.

SEQUENCE:

1. REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND stays FALSE through all acceptance testing. It is armed here and nowhere earlier. Env var NAME only; PURPLE never sees or sets the value.
2. FIRST SEND IS SUPERVISED AND CANARY-STYLE: one known recipient, watched, before any volume follows.
3. WATCH FOR THE SUPPRESSION LOG LINE on that first send. The suppression path has never run end to end (LE-suppression-observation) and this is the first moment it can be observed. Record what was seen on that card.
4. INVITES_LIVE_SEND is armed in the same session, not earlier (LE-invites-live-send, answered HOLD by WF-12). Note it governs a NON-Inngest path - lib/admin/staff.ts -> lib/invites/email.ts -> sendEmail in lib/reminders/clients.ts - which before #778 degraded silently with no boot signal. It now fails loudly at boot, so a misconfiguration surfaces immediately rather than as invites that appear to work and send nothing.
5. Verify the first real invite actually sent, rather than falling back to the temporary-password hand-off.

TEST THAT MUST STILL PASS BEFORE ARMING: 'sends NOTHING with live send off, even though all 10 are approved'. If that test is red, do not arm anything.

STEP 0 ADDED 2026-08-05, ahead of everything below: JP'S FORMAL PACKET SIGN-OFF (LAUNCH-02-jp-packet-signoff). Do not arm REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND without it. Confirmed absent when this was carded - the sequence had no JP step at all, arming both flags with no clinical gate above them.

NOTE ON THE TEST NAMED AT THE FOOT OF THIS CARD ('sends NOTHING with live send off, even though all 10 are approved'): its wording was always literally true and the PACKET disagreed with it, claiming all ten were approved:false. The packet was wrong and is now corrected. The test is unchanged and still load-bearing.

=== 2026-08-18: TWO ADDITIONS, BOTH FROM TODAY'S INCIDENT AND SITTING ===

FIRST, A PRE-ARMING CHECK IS NOW PART OF THIS CARD, and it is not advice. ARMING ANY LIVE-SEND FLAG REQUIRES ITS SECRETS TO BE PRESENT FIRST. On 2026-08-18 REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND=true reached production with REMINDERS_LINK_SECRET absent. assertNotificationEnv ran at MODULE EVALUATION, threw NotificationEnvError, and took down two things that have nothing to do with reminders: /admin/staff and the ENTIRE /api/inngest route. The owner armed the flag himself, set it back to false and redeployed, and /admin/staff renders again. There was no committed-source arming to hunt for.

THE ORDER IS THEREFORE: set every variable the stream needs, redeploy, confirm the app is up, and only then set the flag to "true". Names only, never values, and never in a terminal's context.

The code no longer punishes getting that order wrong with an outage - the guard is lazy from 2026-08-18 and an armed-but-incomplete config now fails THE SEND with the same error instead of an unrelated module load. That is a blast-radius fix, NOT a licence to arm first: an armed flag with a missing secret still means every send in that stream throws.

SECOND, THIS CARD NOW OWNS W13-03 STEP 4. W13-03 closed on the 2026-08-18 sitting with steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 observed exact and step 4 recorded as NOT RUN. Step 4 is: on the code screen, type six WRONG digits, and expect ONE red banner reading "Nao foi possivel entrar..." that NEVER names which of the six failure modes occurred. It needs a real code screen reached with OTP_LIVE_SEND armed, which only this card may do. Run it during the canary and record the result here.

THE WORDING IS THE TEST, not the colour of the banner: the API answers ONE 401 for six distinct failure modes so a caller cannot learn whether a number belongs to a real patient. A banner naming which one went wrong would rebuild that oracle inside the portal.

=== 2026-08-18: A THIRD SUPERVISED ITEM. THE STORAGE ROUND-TRIP. ===
Assigned here by owner ruling when the live half of
storage-signed-url.integration.test.ts was DELETED rather than wired into CI
(ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep). Running it in a runner needs
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in CI, which widens the credential surface two weeks
before a planned rotation.

IT LANDS HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE OTP CANARY DOES: a check that needs a
live secret belongs in a session with a human, not in a runner.

WHAT TO RUN: attach a file to a clinical record, confirm it uploads, then
re-open the record and download it back. EXPECTED: the file returns
byte-identical, and the object key is namespaced under the tenant id - the
prefix the server uses to refuse forged paths.

WHAT IS STILL COVERED WITHOUT IT, so nobody reads this as a hole: the path
derivation itself - tenant prefix, record nesting, filename sanitisation and
the forged-path refusal - is pure, still tested, and runs on every PR. What
the deleted half proved and this replaces is the NETWORK round-trip against a
real bucket.

=== HARD PRECONDITION ADDED 2026-08-21: ERROR VISIBILITY. ===

DO NOT ARM ANY LIVE SEND UNTIL AN ERROR RAISED IN PRODUCTION HAS BEEN OBSERVED ARRIVING IN SENTRY. Tracked on LE-sentry-capture-unverified; satisfied by the owner pressing the button on /admin/sentry-check on the DEPLOYED site and finding OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY.

WHY IT SITS ON THIS CARD RATHER THAN ONLY ON THE GATE. This is the card that turns on real SMS and email to real patients. On 2026-08-21 it was established by observation that ZERO events have ever reached Sentry - so today, arming the sends would put messages in front of patients with NO error reporting of any kind behind them. A page that threw on every request for a day was found by the owner opening it, not by any instrument.

IT IS A PRECONDITION, NOT A GATE CONDITION, because the nine gate conditions are pinned one-to-one to the Definition of Ready and a tenth cannot be added without a DoR change. The standing rule is recorded on launch_gate.source_note; this is where it bites.

=== THE ERROR-VISIBILITY PRECONDITION IS SATISFIED, 2026-08-22. ===

The hard precondition added 2026-08-21 read: "DO NOT ARM ANY LIVE SEND UNTIL AN
ERROR RAISED IN PRODUCTION HAS BEEN OBSERVED ARRIVING IN SENTRY... satisfied by
the owner pressing the button on /admin/sentry-check on the DEPLOYED site and
finding OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY."

THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT WAS DONE AND EXACTLY WHAT WAS FOUND. Sentry's own issue list
for osteojp-web shows "OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY 2026-08-24T14:48:41.512Z -
deliberate t...", Unhandled, GET /admin/sentry-check, 1 event. Recorded in full
on LE-sentry-capture-unverified, which is now shipped.

THE PRECONDITION IS LIFTED. It does not unblock this card - LAUNCH-01 is
owner_authorizo and remains so, and the other supervised items on it are
untouched. What changes is that arming a live send would no longer put messages
in front of patients with no error reporting behind them, which was the specific
condition this precondition existed to prevent.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and this matters on launch day rather than in
principle: an event ARRIVING is not a person being TOLD. Alerting is a separate
gap, named on the Sentry card's own (a) branch and not carded. On a supervised
launch that is acceptable because a human is watching by design; it would not be
acceptable as the steady state afterwards.

STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-01 UNDER SR-17 (dispatched as SR-14), from "todo". It was false. See INC-16 for the contradiction that surfaced it and for why the reconciler could not.

THE RECOMMENDATION ON THIS CARD WAS TO WAIT FOR LOOP 3. LOOP 3 LANDED (#828), so the wait is over and the residual set is now known rather than predicted.
