cards.notes:
=== STATE AS OF THE 2026-08-20 RULING: SENT. AWAITING THE AMOSTRA. NOT WAITING ON IVAN. ===

CADERNO v1.1 WAS SENT TO EDUARDO AT FISIOZERO ON 2026-08-18. This card no longer waits on Ivan forwarding anything, and every sentence below that reads that way is history, marked as such where it appears.

WHAT IT WAITS ON NOW IS THE AMOSTRA. Section 8 of the document asks the vendor for a sample of 20 to 50 patients in the delivery format, ahead of the single full extraction. Until that sample arrives there is nothing to build the adapter against and nothing to decide.

IT STAYS ON THE ENGINEERING BOARD AND IS NOT FLAGGED external_agenda, ruled 2026-08-20: it is PROCUREMENT WORK FOR LAUNCH-03, not legal family. docs/board/EXTERNAL-AGENDA.md had already reached the same conclusion for the same reason, and its entry is corrected in the same commit as this note. THE FLAG IS WRITTEN BY ABSENCE, not by the value false: docs/board/validate-board.mjs rejects external_agenda: false outright, on the reasoning that a field meaning 'not external' spread across 180 cards makes the ABSENCE of the field stop meaning anything.

ONE THING THE REPOSITORY CANNOT CONFIRM, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED OVER: the copy committed here is v1.0, dated 2026-08-06, at docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md. v1.1 is what was sent, and it is NOT in the repository - so nothing committed can tell a future reader what the vendor actually received, or how v1.1 differs. The file stays frozen per the 2026-08-06 instruction; supplying v1.1 is the owner's to do, and it is worth doing before the delivery is validated against a specification the repo does not hold.

STATUS STAYS halted WITH blocked_on null, deliberately. This board's blocked_on vocabulary is ivan | jp | lawyer | infra | null and the vendor is none of them. halted with blocked_on null is what keeps a waiting-on-an-outsider card out of the people lane and out of the next-card picker, the same deviation END-legal-sweep carries and for the same reason.
AUTHORED 2026-08-06. The document exists and is at docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md.

WHY IT EXISTS. The vendor asked the clinic to specify exactly which data, which fields and which format. Answering that specifies the CONTRACT the import is built against: the adapter is then written to OUR spec rather than to a guess at his export, and a delivery that deviates is a non-compliant deliverable rather than a surprise discovered on the clinic's last day.

THE FIELD LIST IS DERIVED, NOT REMEMBERED. Every column in the spec traces to a committed shape:
  pacientes.csv <- MigrationPatient (types.ts:39-57). sourceId and fullName required; dateOfBirth, sex, nif, email, phone, address, postalCode, city, notes nullable BECAUSE the target columns are; locationKeys is the clinic association.
  marcacoes.csv <- MigrationAppointment (types.ts:60-78). sourceId, patientSourceId, practitionerKey, locationKey, startsAt, endsAt and status all required, because validate.ts:46-55 rejects the row without them and the target columns are NOT NULL. serviceKey optional, matching the target.
  episodios.csv <- MigrationClinicalEpisode + MigrationClinicalRecord, deliberately merged into ONE vendor-facing file. The vendor plausibly has no episode concept, and demanding two files for a distinction their schema may not draw is how a spec becomes unquotable. The spec says exactly what to do in that case: one line per clinical record, id_episodio = the record id, estado = fechado.
  documentos.csv <- MigrationAttachment (types.ts:123-131). fileName and the ZIP path are required; mimeType and sizeBytes are optional because the clinic can derive both from the file itself.

THE STABLE PATIENT IDENTIFIER IS THE SPEC'S SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING REQUIREMENT, and it is written as such. Migration 0014's unique key is (tenant_id, source_system, entity_type, source_id), and the whole cross-record resolution in upsert.ts runs through it. Without a consistent id_paciente across all four CSVs the delivery is not reconstructable and has no value, which is why it has its own section rather than a row in a table.

CONSTRAINTS EXPRESSED THAT COME FROM THE PIPELINE, not from convention: no filtering (validate.ts accepts missing NIF and DOB, so there is no reason to drop those patients); duplicates exported as separate rows (mergeImportedPatient exists precisely to fix them AFTER import, and merge_patients() from 0005 does the repointing); cancelled and no_show exported (both are appointment_status values); the clinical signature explicitly NOT requested, because MigrationClinicalRecord.status admits only draft and locked - a signature attests a review in THIS system.

THE ONE THING ASKED FOR THAT THE DISPATCH DID NOT LIST: a 20-to-50 patient SAMPLE, framed as a request distinct from the full pull so it does not read as an attempt to reopen the one-shot condition. If it arrives, the adapter is written against the real format instead of this specification's best reading of it. If it is refused, nothing is lost and the rehearsal runs on synthetic data built from this same document.

FIELDS FLAGGED AS PLAUSIBLY UNSUPPLIABLE, each with a fallback, in section 8 of the document: appointment end time (fall back to duracao_minutos), the episode concept (one row per record), NIF/DOB/sex (leave empty, the platform allows it), mime type and size (derived), the timezone of stored instants (declare it in the manifest), appointment state (declare the vocabulary), and the clinical signature (not requested at all).

SEQUENCING, and this is why the card is high priority while the migration itself is not launch-blocking. THE SPEC GOES OUT EARLY so the vendor quote and JP's fee approval run in PARALLEL with the build. The real pull stays at the very end, on the clinic's named last day, after the platform and portal are fully validated. The rehearsal in between runs against SYNTHETIC data generated from this same document, which is what makes the one-shot pull meet a proven pipeline. A delivery that deviates from the spec is a non-compliant deliverable and goes back to the vendor: the one case where re-delivery does not violate the one-shot condition.

WHAT IS STILL NOT BUILT, and is not in scope here: the FisiozeroSource adapter itself (packages/db/src/migration/source.ts is an interface with no implementation, deliberately), the synthetic generator, and the attachment byte-copy into Supabase Storage. The 1,660 lines behind the seam - staging, upsert, validate, batch-validate, reconciliation, health - are already on main against migration_staging_rows from 0014.

=== UNDER OWNER REVIEW 2026-08-06. THE DOCUMENT IS FROZEN. ===

One correction is pending on the LOCATIONS line. Instruction, binding: DO NOT MODIFY docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md until that correction arrives. Not a wording pass, not a typo fix, not a re-render. The next edit to that file is the owner's correction and nothing else.

The document was published for review at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/faefe7e7-978b-4300-82f7-37b4b9663cce so it could be read and forwarded without waiting on #830 to merge. Sending it was never gated on the merge: it is a document, and forwarding it is an email. The board card saying blocked_on ivan meant, AT THE TIME, waiting for Ivan to SEND it, which was ambiguous enough to read as waiting for a merge - recorded here so the next reader does not repeat the misreading. THAT BLOCK IS GONE: the document was sent on 2026-08-18. See the head of this card.

=== OWNER CORRECTION APPLIED 2026-08-06. MONTEMOR-O-NOVO DOES NOT EXIST. THE DOCUMENT IS UNFROZEN AND READY TO SEND. ===

The clinic has EXACTLY TWO locations: Linda-a-Velha and Castelo Branco. The emitente line named a third. Fixed, and the whole document was grepped: zero occurrences remain.

THE STATED CAUSE IS WRONG, AND CORRECTING IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TYPO. The relay recorded this as "a location introduced into a vendor-facing binding document without any source in repo, board, or ruling". There IS a source, and it is the most authoritative file in the repo:
  CLAUDE.md:4 - "Unified clinic platform for OsteoJP (Linda-a-Velha, Castelo Branco, Montemor-o-Novo)." CLAUDE.md is loaded into EVERY session and its instructions are declared to override default behaviour.
  README.md:3 - the same sentence.
  docs/architecture.md:13 and :202 - three locations, one marked "(opening)".
  docs/jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md:49-56 - a JP ruling ABOUT Montemor-o-Novo: configured as a third clinic, not yet open, to appear with a "Coming soon" notice or be hidden.
  47 committed files in total mention it, including the cutover runbook, launch comms, the QA load-test record and two PDF templates carrying a TODO for its address.

SO THE FAILURE WAS NOT INVENTION. It was TRANSCRIPTION FROM COMMITTED GROUND TRUTH THAT IS ITSELF WRONG. That distinction is the whole lesson: the rule "state only facts traceable to committed ground truth" was FOLLOWED here and still produced a wrong vendor-facing document, because the ground truth is stale. Recording the cause as invention would leave 47 files intact to seed the same error into the next document, the next session and the next vendor email.

WHAT I FIXED, and the boundary is deliberate: the caderno, plus the six Supabase auth email footers written in this same session, which are PATIENT- AND STAFF-FACING and would have mailed a nonexistent clinic to real people. supabase-email-templates.test.ts now pins it - 40/40, with an explicit assertion that no template contains "Montemor", so a future edit copying the stale line out of CLAUDE.md fails instead of shipping.

WHAT I DID NOT FIX, and it needs an owner decision rather than my initiative: the other 45 files. Correcting them touches a committed JP RULING (jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md), the architecture doc, the cutover runbook and historical QA records. Rewriting a recorded ruling is not a typo fix. RECOMMENDED, in order: correct CLAUDE.md:4 and README.md:3 FIRST and on their own, because CLAUDE.md is loaded every session and is therefore the one that keeps reproducing the error; then decide separately whether the JP ruling is superseded (Montemor abandoned) or historical (recorded as it was). Carded as LE-montemor-ground-truth.

=== DEFERRED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-06. DO NOT RE-RAISE. ===

The caderno is sent to the vendor AT THE VERY END of the project, not now. The document stays FROZEN as corrected and is not edited again.

THE COST IS ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A SURPRISE: a late send puts the vendor QUOTE, JP's FEE APPROVAL and the EXTRACTION PREP on the end-phase critical path, in series rather than in parallel with the build. The original sequencing note on this card argued the opposite. That argument is superseded, not forgotten.

LANE DEVIATION as on END-legal-sweep: deferred-by-decision does not exist in the pinned lane set, so this is status HALTED with home_lane loose_ends and blocked_on null - not todo, not blocked, out of the people lane, skipped by the next-card picker.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the corrected document is at docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/faefe7e7-978b-4300-82f7-37b4b9663cce, and it is ready to send whenever the end phase arrives.

=== SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20: THE 2026-08-06 DEFERRAL DID NOT HOLD, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. ===

The block above rules that the caderno goes to the vendor AT THE VERY END of the project, not then. It went on 2026-08-18. The ruling is SUPERSEDED BY THE EVENT, not forgotten, and the cost it named is moot in the direction that helps: the vendor quote and the extraction prep now run in PARALLEL with the build, which is what the ORIGINAL 2026-08-06 sequencing note argued for before the deferral overrode it.

Written down because the alternative is a card carrying two live rulings that contradict each other, with the next reader picking whichever one they read first.

=== v1.1 COMMITTED 2026-08-21, OWNER RULING B. THE GAP IS CLOSED. ===

WHAT GOVERNS VALIDATION: docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao-v1.1.docx. The vendor's delivery is checked field by field against v1.1. v1.0 is NOT the specification any more; it is the historical record, unchanged, under its standing no-edit instruction from 2026-08-06.

THIS CLOSES THE GAP THIS CARD HAS CARRIED SINCE 2026-08-20, which was recorded then as "nothing committed can tell a future reader what the vendor actually received". It can now.

FILE-NAME MISMATCH WITH THE DISPATCH, NAMED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER: the dispatch said docs/caderno-encargos-exportacao-v1.1.pdf. What was actually on disk was docs/caderno-encargos-exportacao-osteojp-v1.1 (1).docx - a WORD file, a different name, and a browser "(1)" duplicate suffix. It is a valid .docx with an internal timestamp of 2026-08-18, which is the send date, so it is the right document; only the description was wrong. Committed as docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao-v1.1.docx, beside v1.0, with the correct extension and no download suffix.

AND BECAUSE IT IS A .docx RATHER THAN A .pdf, IT IS DIFFABLE. The text extracts cleanly from word/document.xml, so what changed between the two versions is on the record below rather than being a thing nobody can check.

WHAT CHANGED, v1.0 -> v1.1. Same ten sections, same structure. Substantive differences:

  1. VERSION AND DATE. v1.1, 2026-08-18, and it says so in the header: "Versão: 1.1 (substitui a versão 1.0)".

  2. A REAL ERROR IN v1.0 IS FIXED. v1.0 said "Entrega composta por DUAS partes" and then listed THREE (Parte A, Parte B, Parte C). v1.1 says "três partes". A binding vendor document that miscounted its own deliverables.

  3. VOLUME NARROWED: "cerca de 10.000 pacientes" becomes "entre 8.000 e 10.000 pacientes". A range the vendor can quote against rather than a single round number.

  4. NEW - METODO DE EXTRACAO: the extraction method is explicitly the vendor's choice (direct database export, internal tools, other); the DELIVERY FORMAT stays binding. This removes an argument before it happens.

  5. NEW - DIA DA EXTRACAO, and it is much tighter. v1.0: "no dia acordado como último dia de utilização". v1.1: a FRIDAY agreed between the parties, AFTER the clinic closes, over that day's FROZEN data, and from that moment the clinic enters no more data.

  6. NEW - MANUTENCAO DE ACESSO, and this is the most commercially significant addition. The clinic keeps read-only access to the old platform until the final delivery PASSES the section 7 acceptance criteria, and cutting access before acceptance is "não admissível". v1.0 had no such protection: the clinic could have lost access to its own history while holding a non-conforming delivery.

  7. NON-CONFORMING DELIVERY now explicitly carries the access condition through the correction period.

  8. AMOSTRA now explicitly includes THE MANIFEST as well as documents, and is worded against "a extração única" rather than "o ponto 1".

  9. NEW COLUMNS IN pacientes.csv: numero paciente (the patient number visible in the current platform, if distinct from the id), seguro saude and numero apolice (insurer and policy, semicolon-separated in matching order). Multiple telephone numbers are now specified as semicolon-separated with the principal one first.

  10. WORDING HARDENED throughout: "o fornecedor DEVE declarar" becomes "o fornecedor DECLARA". Obligations stated as facts rather than as expectations.

WHAT IS UNCHANGED: the four CSV files and their purpose, the stable-identifier requirement that section 4.0 calls the single most load-bearing element, the ZIP and manifest structure, the acceptance criteria, the no-filtering completeness rule, and the data-protection section.

cards.title: Montemor-o-Novo was a pure error - purge it from every live surface, annotate history

evidence.ref: COMPLETE. #831 (98ca808) fixed CLAUDE.md and README.md; the document sweep landed in #830 (0987ee7); the CODE AND SEED half is #838 MERGED 2026-08-07, squashed to 1c63940. Verified by grep on main: no file under apps/, packages/ or supabase/ names Montemor except as an annotation recording the ruling, plus location-cleanup.ts (the script that ARCHIVES the row) and the id it needs. Also corrected a false factual claim found while sweeping: twilio-proof.test.ts measured the worst-case SMS fill against a 15-char name that is not a clinic and is longer than any real one.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 by grepping the repo after the owner corrected the caderno. The clinic has EXACTLY TWO locations, Linda-a-Velha and Castelo Branco. Montemor-o-Novo does not exist.

IT IS NAMED IN 47 COMMITTED FILES, and two of them are the files every session is told to trust:
  CLAUDE.md:4 - "Unified clinic platform for OsteoJP (Linda-a-Velha, Castelo Branco, Montemor-o-Novo)." This file is loaded into EVERY session and declares that its instructions override default behaviour. It is the single highest-leverage wrong fact in the repo.
  README.md:3 - the same sentence, the first thing a new contributor reads.
  docs/architecture.md:13, :202, :560 - three locations, one "(opening)", plus an open item for its opening date and contacts.
  docs/jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md:49-56 - a JP RULING about it: configured as a third clinic, not yet open, to appear with a "Coming soon" notice or be hidden from booking entirely.
  docs/cutover-runbook.md:81, docs/launch-comms.md:83 - launch-day checklists that send staff to a clinic that does not exist.
  docs/pdf-templates/invoice-fatura-recibo.html:492 and declaration-tratamento.html:316 - commented-out footer blocks with a TODO for its address, on documents that are printed for patients.
  docs/qa-performance-loadtest-2026-06-20.md:24 and qa-seed-appointments-2026-06-19.md:65 - historical QA records asserting 3 locations and 24 appointments there.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT A TYPO. It already produced one wrong VENDOR-FACING binding document and six PATIENT-FACING email footers in a single session, by a terminal that was following the rule - state only what is traceable to committed ground truth. The rule held; the ground truth is stale. Until CLAUDE.md is corrected, every future session starts by being told the wrong thing, and the next document repeats it.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED ON IVAN RATHER THAN JUST FIXED. Three of these are not typo fixes and are not mine to decide:
  1. jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md records a RULING. Rewriting a recorded ruling to match present reality destroys the record of what was decided and when. The question is whether Montemor was ABANDONED (the ruling is superseded and should be annotated, not deleted) or never existed (the ruling was made on a false premise, which is a different and worse finding).
  2. The QA records are HISTORICAL measurements. They say what was measured then. Editing them makes past evidence lie.
  3. The PDF templates carry a TODO for its address. Deleting the TODO is right if it is abandoned; nobody should guess.

RECOMMENDED, in this order, because the first is cheap and stops the bleeding:
  A. Correct CLAUDE.md:4 and README.md:3 ALONE, in one small PR. Two lines. This is the one that keeps reproducing the error, because CLAUDE.md is loaded every session.
  B. Correct docs/architecture.md and the two launch checklists - forward-looking operational docs that would send a person somewhere.
  C. Owner decides on the JP ruling and the QA records: annotate as superseded, or leave as history with a dated note. Never silently rewrite either.

ALREADY FIXED, in the branch that found it: the caderno (vendor-facing) and the six Supabase auth email footers (patient- and staff-facing). supabase-email-templates.test.ts asserts no template contains "Montemor", so the stale line cannot be copied back out of CLAUDE.md without failing CI.

=== OWNER RULING 2026-08-06: PURE ERROR. NEVER A PLAN, NEVER REAL. ===

Unblocked: the question this card was waiting on is answered. Montemor-o-Novo never existed as a real or planned OsteoJP location.

DONE IN THIS BRANCH (documents only, no behaviour):
  ANNOTATED, not rewritten: docs/jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md entry 5 now carries a RECORDED IN ERROR block pointing at this ruling, with the original text preserved verbatim beneath it. A ruling is a record of what was asked; deleting it would make the history lie in the other direction.
  PURGED: docs/architecture.md (x3, including the open item for its opening date), docs/cutover-runbook.md, docs/launch-comms.md, docs/brand-voice.md, docs/handoff-brief.md, docs/pdf-templates/SPEC.md and README.md, and the TODO plus commented address block in ALL FOUR pdf templates.
  CORRECTED COMMENTS: apps/web/lib/clinical/report/location-contacts.ts and .../declaracao/signature-stamp-asset.ts both said the third location was absent because it was OPENING. That framing is the error restated. 23/23 tests still green.
  ALREADY DONE EARLIER: the caderno and the six auth email footers, with a guard test pinning it.

THE SWEEP FOUND MORE THAN THE 47 FILES FIRST REPORTED, and this is the correction to my own earlier count. The first grep was scoped to a file-extension list that missed a fourth PDF template (declaration-presenca.html) and docs/pdf-templates/SPEC.md, which itself said the placeholder was in ALL FOUR templates while I had found three. A count derived from a filtered grep is a count of what the filter allowed.

STILL NAMING IT, and DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED HERE:
  CODE AND SEEDS, which need CI and belong in the CLAUDE.md PR after #830: packages/db/seed/dev-reference.ts:85 (seeds an actual Montemor LOCATION ROW), packages/db/seed/dev-ids.ts:13 (LOC_MTN), packages/db/seed/availability-dev.ts, packages/db/seed/location-cleanup.ts, packages/ui/stories/Select.stories.tsx:31, scripts/perf-seed-loadtest.mjs, scripts/twilio-smoke.mjs, and several test files that assert on it.
  CLAUDE.md:4 and README.md:3 - approved, own PR, after #830 merges per the loop rule.
  HISTORICAL, RULED UNTOUCHED: docs/qa-performance-loadtest-2026-06-20.md, docs/qa-seed-appointments-2026-06-19.md, and the wave/session/design records that describe what was true then.

NO PATIENT-FACING EXPOSURE, verified rather than assumed. location-contacts.ts and signature-stamp-asset.ts named it ONLY in comments explaining its absence - no third-location contact block was ever printed on a clinical report, declaration or invoice. The only place it materialises as data is the DEV seed, which reaches no patient.

=== THE TWO-LINE PR IS OPEN AS #831, 2026-08-07, sequenced after #830 merged as ruled. ===

STILL OPEN AFTER #831: the code and seeds. packages/db/seed/dev-reference.ts:85 materialises an actual Montemor LOCATION ROW, plus dev-ids.ts LOC_MTN, availability-dev.ts, location-cleanup.ts, packages/ui/stories/Select.stories.tsx and two scripts. Those need CI and a little care - the dev seed is shared - so they are their own change, not a rider on a two-line docs PR.

=== CODE AND SEED SWEEP, 2026-08-07, PR #838. THE CARD CLOSES. ===

FIVE OF THE SIX ITEMS THE DISPATCH LISTED WERE ALREADY DONE, and checking rather
than transcribing is what found that. architecture.md, cutover-runbook.md,
launch-comms.md, both PDF templates and the jp-decisions annotation all have ZERO
hits on a live grep - they landed in #830. Only the code and seed half was owed,
which is what this PR does.

WHAT MATERIALISED THE LOCATION AND IS NOW GONE: dev-reference.ts seeded an actual
locations row for it. That row is deleted. availability-dev.ts gave two
therapists schedules there, working-hours-real.ts made it therapist 4's primary
location, appointments-dev.ts booked into it, and a packages/ui story offered it
in a Select. All retargeted to Castelo Branco.

TWO SEED TESTS ASSERTED THREE CLINICS and are now correct at two. That is the
good kind of failure: the seed changed and a test pinning the old shape caught
it, rather than the seed and its test drifting apart quietly.

WHAT DELIBERATELY STAYS, and each has a reason written at the line:
  location-cleanup.ts names it because it is the script that ARCHIVES it, and a
  dev database seeded before today still holds the row. Deleting the reference
  would remove the only thing that can clean up the mistake.
  dev-ids.ts keeps LOC_MTN for that one caller, now with a header saying nothing
  may ever CREATE it again.
  supabase-email-templates.test.ts asserts the string is ABSENT. That is a guard,
  not a residue.
  Historical documents - the QA records, the handoffs, docs/recon, the wave loop
  files, docs/design - are untouched, on the same principle the jp-decisions
  annotation established: a record of what was believed at the time is not a
  statement of fact, and rewriting it destroys the history.

A FALSE FACTUAL CLAIM FOUND WHILE SWEEPING, and it is the find worth keeping.
twilio-proof.test.ts declared "Montemor-o-Novo is the longest of the three real
clinics" and used it as the worst-case SMS fill. BOTH halves were wrong: there
are two clinics, and at 15 characters that name is one LONGER than any real one,
so every SMS segment budget in that suite was measured against a fill that cannot
occur. Conservative, so no assertion was wrong - but the label was a claim about
production that was false, and the real longest is "Castelo Branco" at 14, which
is what templates.ts:125 already said. reminders-e2e.smoke.test.ts carried the
same fixture. Both corrected.

cards.title: merge-on-green.sh hardcoded the required-check list, so it would have merged on a partial picture

evidence.ref: #824 merged 2026-08-06 (3fdd1b6) - merge-on-green.sh now reads the required-check set from branch protection instead of a hardcoded list, refuses any PR that is not OPEN, and RE-READS the PR state after merging rather than trusting the exit code. Distinct exit codes: 0 merged, 1 red or refused, 2 timed out, 3 bad usage. .claude/commands/ship.md updated to match.

cards.notes:
SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS W13-CI-03, found the same day and one layer down. Branch protection owns the list of what gates a merge; anything that keeps its own copy eventually disagrees with it.

WHAT WAS WRONG. scripts/merge-on-green.sh, which /ship drives, carried a literal set of THREE contexts: Lint + typecheck + test, DB-gated tests, Playwright E2E. The owner made a FOURTH required on 2026-08-06 (Validate spec + drift check). The script could not know: it would have declared GREEN while that check was still pending, fired a merge GitHub then refused, and - had the check gone on to fail - reported a green that was never true.

NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS LANE. The script predates the wave (#311, session 13). What changed under it was the required set. It is fixed here because this lane found it and because the ruling that exposed it landed here.

THE FIX: the required contexts are read from the branch-protection API on every run, and if that read fails the script REFUSES rather than falling back to a guessed list - guessing is precisely what broke it. A context that has not reported at all counts as PENDING, never as green, which is the distinction the old version lost and the one that matters when a required check is path-filtered and never runs.

TWO MORE THINGS FIXED WHILE IN THERE. GH_TOKEN is no longer demanded: gh is already authenticated in the shells this runs in and honours GH_TOKEN by itself, so requiring it only produced a failure mode where a usable session was refused. And exit codes are now distinct - 0 merged, 1 red or refused, 2 timed out, 3 bad usage - so a caller can branch on them instead of on 0-or-not.

A DEFECT IN MY OWN REWRITE, CAUGHT IN TESTING AND WORTH RECORDING. The first version had no state guard, and gh pr merge on an ALREADY-MERGED PR prints "was already merged" and EXITS 0 - so the script announced MERGED for a merge it had not performed. A false green in the tool whose only job is to tell green from not-green. Two guards now: it refuses any PR that is not OPEN, and after merging it RE-READS the PR state rather than trusting the exit code of the call that was supposed to change it. Same doctrine as verifying a migration against the database instead of trusting "applied successfully!".

.claude/commands/ship.md updated to match: no GH_TOKEN step, and the exit-code table documented.

CLOSED 2026-08-06. PR #824 merged at 3fdd1b6.

cards.title: The session cookie is host-scoped to the API and the portal has no way to carry it

evidence.ref: #826 merged 2026-08-06 (2c0c708) - the mint routes return the session token in the RESPONSE BODY and the portal server writes its own first-party cookie via writePortalSession. Tests prove the body token and the cookie token are the same credential, the device token is absent from the body, and neither mint route redirects or builds a query string (constraint 3, no token in a URL).

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 WHILE STARTING THE LOGIN SCREENS. HALT, not improvised. The ruling settled WHAT the session is; it did not settle HOW the portal carries it, and the portal existing architecture has no slot for it.

THE MISMATCH, re-derived from committed code:
1. The API sets __Host-ojp_session. The __Host- prefix means HOST-ONLY, no Domain attribute - the browser scopes it to api.osteojp.pt and nothing else. That prefix is load-bearing and I would not drop it.
2. apps/portal/lib/api/client.ts:96-110 calls the API SERVER-TO-SERVER with an Authorization: Bearer header built from the portal own Supabase session. Its comment says it deliberately avoids forwarding cookies at all: "the fragility of manually forwarding the Cookie header string (encoding edge cases, SameSite restrictions, cookie-path scoping)".
3. There is NO credentialed browser-to-API call anywhere in the portal: a search for credentials: across apps/portal returns zero hits, and no client component reads NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. Every API call is made by the portal SERVER.
4. An OTP patient has no Supabase session, so the Bearer the portal knows how to build does not exist for them.

CONSEQUENCE: the portal server cannot read a cookie scoped to another host, and the browser never calls the API directly. The session works - it is minted, signed, verified and tested - and nothing in the portal can present it.

OPTIONS, with what each costs:
(a) BROWSER CALLS THE API DIRECTLY for patient routes, credentials: include. Cost: the API needs CORS with Allow-Credentials and a pinned origin, which it has today for nothing; and the portal gains a second, different call pattern beside the server-side one.
(b) PORTAL OWNS THE COOKIE, API ONLY SIGNS AND VERIFIES. The API verify/trusted return the session token in the RESPONSE BODY; the portal server-side login action calls them, sets its OWN __Host- cookie on the PORTAL host, and forwards the token as Authorization: Bearer on every later call - the pattern that already exists. The API Bearer path tries verifyPatientSession before the Supabase verifier. Cost: the token appears in a response body. That is smaller than it looks: the only caller is the portal SERVER, so an XSS on the portal origin still cannot see that response, and a patient calling verify directly with their own code receives their own credential, which is not a leak.
(c) SHARE THE COOKIE ACROSS SUBDOMAINS with Domain=.osteojp.pt. Cost: drops the __Host- prefix and broadcasts a patient credential to every subdomain in the estate including the staff platform. NOT RECOMMENDED, listed so nobody proposes it later believing it was missed.

RECOMMENDED: (b). It keeps the __Host- prefix, keeps the secret in the osteojp-api project alone (the portal relays, never verifies), reuses the portal existing Bearer path so no new call pattern appears, and needs no CORS surface. It is also the only option that leaves the XSS argument intact where it matters.

NOTHING IS BUILT ON THIS UNTIL IT IS RULED. The session module, both routes, the cookie helpers and the principal path are merged and correct under every option; only the transport differs.

=== RULED 2026-08-06: OPTION B. Portal owns the cookie, API only signs and verifies. UNBLOCKED. ===

CONSTRAINTS AS RULED, all three load-bearing:
1. THE PORTAL TREATS THE TOKEN AS OPAQUE. It wraps it in its own __Host- cookie on the portal host and forwards it as Bearer. It NEVER parses, decodes or trusts the contents locally. The API remains the single verifier, forever. Asserted by a test in the WF-08 style: no JWT decode or verify symbol is reachable in the portal against this token.
2. PORTAL COOKIE: __Host- prefix, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, path scoping per the prefix rules. Lifetimes MIRROR the ruled artefact - 12h session, 30-day trusted device, device-refresh semantics unchanged from #825.
3. THE TOKEN TRAVELS ONLY IN THE BODY of the server-to-server response. Never in a redirect URL, never in a query string. Both are logged by proxies, kept in browser history and leaked by Referer.

BUILT 2026-08-06. All three ruled constraints implemented and asserted.

API SIDE: verify and trusted now return sessionToken IN THE BODY alongside the cookie, for the portal SERVER. The Bearer path in getPatientPrincipal tries verifyPatientSession BEFORE the Supabase verifier - neither kind can be mistaken for the other, since ours is rejected by the Supabase verifier on signature and a Supabase token is rejected by ours on issuer, so trying both is not weaker than trying one.

PORTAL SIDE: apps/portal/lib/auth/session.ts owns __Host-ojp_session on the PORTAL host - httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax, path /, maxAge 12h mirroring the ruled artefact. apiHeaders() now prefers it over the Supabase session, because an OTP patient has no Supabase session at all.

CONSTRAINT 1 (OPACITY) IS ASSERTED BY A SOURCE SCAN, WF-08 style, in apps/portal/lib/auth/session-opacity.test.ts: no jwtVerify, decodeJwt, decodeProtectedHeader, SignJWT, jwt.verify, jwt.decode, jsonwebtoken or createRemoteJWKSet anywhere in the portal; the session module contains no base64 decode, no JWT split and no reference to exp/payload/claims; and the client forwards the token verbatim with no slicing. A behavioural test could only prove the paths someone remembered to call - the scan proves absence across the app. 11 assertions, green.

WHY OPACITY IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN TIDY: the signing secret lives in osteojp-api and nowhere else, so the portal COULD NOT verify honestly even if it tried. A portal that checked a token it cannot verify would be reading the attacker own claims and believing them - the exact defect behind SEC-W1-patient-jwt-verify, where apps/api decoded a token and trusted the payload.

CONSTRAINT 3 (NO URL) IS ALSO ASSERTED, replacing the now-obsolete no-token-in-body test: neither mint route may contain a redirect() call or build a query string. A body is bounded to the portal server; a URL is written to proxy logs, kept in browser history and leaked through Referer.

THE BODY TOKEN AND THE COOKIE TOKEN ARE PROVEN IDENTICAL by test - one credential carried two ways, not two live sessions per login. And the DEVICE token is proven absent from the body: it belongs to the browser, and the portal has no use for it.

CLOSED 2026-08-06. PR #826 merged at 2c0c708. This is what unblocks the W13-03 login screens: the portal now has a supported way to carry a session, so the screen after the code entry has somewhere to put it.

cards.title: Signing out drops the device COOKIE but cannot revoke the device ROW - there is no endpoint

evidence.ref:
OWNER A4 OBSERVATION ON THE DEPLOYED PORTAL, 2026-08-19, per WF-03: signed out via Conta / "Terminar sessao", confirmed the "Terminar sessao?" dialog, closed the tab, reopened the portal URL, and landed on the phone screen ("Entrar com o seu telemovel") rather than the dashboard. The device row is revoked, not merely the cookie dropped: landing on the dashboard would have been the cookie-only sign-out this card exists to end. docs/board/OBSERVE-SWEEP.md row A4, `Observed:` line filled with this result; row F3 answered "closed on that observation".

THE ENDPOINT IS OBSERVED WORKING, and it is the one #843 built. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/revoke, merged 2026-08-07 as PR #843, merge commit 45f05c4, re-derived from origin/main this session: apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/revoke/route.ts exists, and apps/portal/app/portal/account/actions.ts:106 signOutAction calls it BEFORE clearDeviceToken (that order is load-bearing - the revoke needs the token). 8 DB-gated assertions in apps/api/lib/auth/otp-revoke.db.test.ts, including the card's DoD verbatim: a revoked row is refused by /otp/trusted.

PG1 ITEM 15 IS COVERED BY THIS SAME OBSERVATION - one click, two records, which is why the two were never worth costing separately.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20 ON THE OWNER'S 2026-08-19 OBSERVATION. ===

The build half merged 2026-08-07 (#843). The observation half was run by the
owner on 2026-08-19: sign out, reopen, phone screen. Evidence field carries it.

READ THE NOTE BELOW IT AS HISTORY, NOT AS STATE. It says "A4 WAS NOT RUN ON
2026-08-12. THIS CARD DOES NOT CLOSE TONIGHT", and it was correct on the day it
was written. It is left in place because it is the only contemporaneous record
that the 2026-08-12 A4 claim on PG1 was false, and deleting it would delete the
evidence that the correction was needed.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

A4 WAS NOT RUN ON 2026-08-12. THIS CARD DOES NOT CLOSE TONIGHT.

The owner ran A3's second half believing it was A4. OBSERVE-SWEEP.md A4 is this
card's observation as well as PG1 item 15 - one click covers both - so both are
still outstanding. The owner is running A4 now; when it comes back clean this
card closes and PG1 item 15 is observed.

Nothing about the CODE changed: #843 is merged and the endpoint exists. This is
an observation gap, not a build gap.

--- prior notes below ---

FOUND IN W13-03, 2026-08-06, while making sign-out actually sign a patient out.

WHAT IS TRUE NOW: signOutAction clears the portal session cookie AND the trusted-device cookie, so the token is gone from that browser and unrecoverable - that browser can never present it again. The bound is real and it is what a patient on a shared handset needs.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE: the ROW in patient_trusted_devices survives its full 30 days with revoked_at still null. The schema was built for revocation (the column exists, and its comment says 'revoked on the 4th stays an answerable question') but nothing writes it, because there is no API route to write it and the portal must not touch the database directly.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: the token only exists in one browser, so a dropped cookie is effectively a revocation for every practical case. The gap is the case where the value was captured before sign-out - a shoulder-surfed device cookie is not a realistic attack, but 'we cannot revoke' is the wrong answer to have when someone reports a lost phone.

DoD: a POST route on apps/api that revokes the CALLER's device row (authenticated by the device cookie itself, so it needs no patient id), called by signOutAction, plus a test that a revoked row is refused by /otp/trusted.

=== BUILT 2026-08-07, PR #843. ===

THE STORE ALREADY HAD revoke(). It has existed since 0056 with a comment saying
"revoked on the 4th stays an answerable question", and its ONLY callers were
tests. The gap was the route and the wiring, exactly as the card said.

THREE DESIGN POINTS, each a deliberate refusal of something simpler:
  NO BODY AND NO PATIENT ID. The device cookie IS the authentication - whoever
  holds it may revoke it, and holding it is the only thing that could authorise
  revoking it. A patient id would be a caller-supplied value needing
  reconciliation against the device row, and the two can disagree. Same argument
  that kept the phone number out of /otp/trusted.
  ALWAYS 204, for an unknown, expired, already-revoked or absent token. The
  honest outcome is identical, and distinguishing them would make this an ORACLE
  for whether a given device token is live - the enumeration surface /otp/trusted
  was built not to be. A 401 for a missing cookie would also make sign-out noisy
  for a patient who never trusted the browser.
  NO PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET ASSERTION. The route mints nothing, so that variable
  is irrelevant to it. Asserting it would make a REVOCATION fail on a
  misconfiguration that cannot affect the revocation - the wrong direction for a
  security control.

ORDER IN signOutAction IS LOAD-BEARING and commented as such: the revoke needs
the token, so it runs BEFORE clearDeviceToken. A tidy-looking reorder would turn
this back into a cookie-only sign-out.

BEST-EFFORT BY CHOICE. If the API is unreachable the cookies still clear and the
patient IS signed out of this browser. Failing the sign-out because a revocation
could not be recorded would leave them signed IN, which is strictly worse.

cards.title: nif-required.spec.ts flakes under load - second occurrence, now with a controlled comparison

evidence.ref:

cards.notes:
OBSERVED 2026-08-06 on run 31105176063, shard 2 of #829: 'an existing NIF cannot be edited back to empty' timed out at 120s, three times counting both retries. Recorded because it is the kind of thing that gets written off as flake and then costs an afternoon later.

WHAT THE ARTIFACT SHOWED, and it is not what the summary suggested. The click did not time out on a slow element: the PAGE WAS A 404. The snapshot is Next's own 'This page could not be found', so getByLabel(/^NIF/i) was waiting for a field that was never going to exist.

WHY THAT IS ODD RATHER THAN ORDINARY: createPatient asserts the URL becomes /patients/{uuid} within 15s BEFORE it returns, and that assertion passed. So a patient WAS created, a real uuid came back, and the app was demonstrably working at that instant - and then the edit route for that same uuid answered 404.

WHAT RULES OUT THE BRANCH: apps/web application code is identical across the failing run and both parent runs. W13-03 touched only e2e harness files in that app and the merge changed nothing under apps/web/app; W13-04 is apps/api, which the staff platform does not import. The same test passed in 6.0s and 6.4s on the two parents and in 4.8s on a re-run of the identical commit.

WHAT IS LEFT: a Next DEV-SERVER 404 (the snapshot carries the Dev Tools button) with hydration errors in the same window, on a runner hosting three Next servers plus Supabase. Plausible, and NOT PROVEN - a single green re-run never proves the absence of a race, which is why this is a card and not a conclusion.

IF IT RECURS: do not re-run. Capture whether the patient row exists in the database at the moment of the 404, which separates 'the row is not there' from 'the route did not compile'. Those have different fixes and guessing between them is how the last four CI causes were called wrong.

=== SECOND OCCURRENCE 2026-08-07, and this time the code path was PROVEN unchanged rather than assumed. ===

SYMPTOM, different from the first: nif-required.spec.ts:129 timed out clicking getByLabel(/^NIF/i), 120s, on all three Playwright retries. The first occurrence was a 404 on /patients/[id]/edit. Same spec, same under-load character, different surface.

THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, which is what makes this a flake claim rather than a guess. Shard 2 PASSED at a4de096 and FAILED 3/3 at 0df8668 on the same PR. git diff between those two commits touches exactly three files: 0058_patient_terms_acceptances.sql in both mirrored trees, and patient-terms-acceptances-rls.test.ts. Filtering the SQL diff to non-comment lines returns NOTHING - the change was comment-only. No app code, no seed, no e2e spec.
So the spec ran identical application code against identical fixture data, and flipped. That is a flake with evidence behind it.

LOAD IS THE COMMON FACTOR IN BOTH OCCURRENCES. Shard 2 took 13m10s on the failing run against roughly 7m for shards 1 and 3 - the three 120s timeouts plus retries account for most of it, but it was the slow shard before the retries began. The first occurrence was also recorded as happening under load.

A HYDRATION MISMATCH FIRES IN THE SAME WINDOW, three times, seconds before each timeout. It is LE-notes-list-hydration-mismatch (notes-list.tsx:139, toLocaleString server vs client) on the patient profile page. NOT CLAIMED AS THE CAUSE - the two are correlated in the log and nothing more, and this project has paid for causal claims made on correlation. But a hydration failure can leave a client tree unattached, and a form field that never becomes interactive is exactly this symptom, so it is the first hypothesis to test if there is a third occurrence.

ACTION TAKEN: job re-run, which is legitimate here only BECAUSE the diff proved the code path unchanged. Re-running to make a red go away without that proof is how a real defect gets buried.

=== DIAGNOSTIC CAPTURED, 2026-08-07, PR #843. NOT FIXED, BY INSTRUCTION. ===

The card says: do not re-run, capture whether the patient row exists at the
moment of the 404, because "the row is not there" and "the route did not
compile" have different fixes and guessing between them is how the last four CI
causes were called wrong. That is what shipped.

THE HARNESS CANNOT QUERY POSTGRES AND DOES NOT NEED TO. The DETAIL route
/patients/{id} reads the same row from the same database as the edit route. At
the instant of the 404:
  detail 200 -> THE ROW EXISTS, so the EDIT ROUTE is the problem (dev-server
  compile or chunk serving, which the Dev Tools button in the first artefact

  detail 404 -> THE ROW IS NOT VISIBLE, so it is a data or transaction problem.

The verdict, both statuses and the patient id are ATTACHED to the Playwright
report and thrown, so it survives the runner and is readable from the artefact
without re-deriving anything. A pass is silent. There is NO retry and NO fix.

cards.title: JP ruled: an unconfirmed pedido does NOT hold the slot (option B)

evidence.ref: JP ruling 2026-08-06, verbatim choice: "o horario fica livre ate a rececao confirmar". Option B, over the recommended default and over the behaviour as built. He accepted the stated trade-off: reception's confirm can fail when another booking takes the slot first. Recorded in the dispatch of 2026-08-06 and carried into code as the mandatory transactional re-check in confirmAppointmentRequest (apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts) and the patient-facing copy change in packages/i18n/src/portal/strings.pt.json. The QUESTION is closed; the availability half it created is carded separately as W13-04a-availability-exclusion.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 while designing the reception confirm surface. NOT A BLOCKER for that surface, which is correct under either answer, and carded so it is ruled rather than absorbed.

WHAT HAPPENS TODAY. A portal booking calls bookAppointment, which picks a conflict-free therapist and WRITES THE APPOINTMENT immediately, status=scheduled. The patient is told it awaits confirmation, reception is notified, and the appointment already occupies that therapist's calendar. Nothing is auto-CONFIRMED, so JP's ruling as recorded ('zero auto-confirmed') IS satisfied - the lifecycle stays scheduled until reception acts.

THE QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS: should an unconfirmed pedido OCCUPY THE SLOT while it waits?
  HOLDING IT (today) means two patients cannot request the same slot, and reception's confirm is a formality that never fails. The cost is that a pedido reception never gets to blocks the calendar, and a patient who requests and is refused has still denied that slot to everyone meanwhile.
  NOT HOLDING IT means a pedido is a request against an open calendar, several patients may request the same slot, and reception's confirm can FAIL on a conflict - which needs its own refusal path and its own pt-PT copy.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT IF NO ANSWER ARRIVES: keep holding it. It is what is built, it cannot double-book, and the failure mode it creates (a stale pedido blocking a slot) is visible to reception in the queue and fixable by cancelling. The alternative introduces a conflict path on the confirm action, which is new failure surface at launch. A STARTING POINT FOR JP, NOT A RULING.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: at launch every bookable service is request-mode and the clinic is small, so a stale pedido is a phone call, not an outage.

=== RULED 2026-08-06. OPTION B. THE QUESTION IS CLOSED. ===

JP chose NOT HOLDING IT, against the recommended default recorded above. His words: "o horario fica livre ate a rececao confirmar". He was told the cost and took it: a confirm can fail on a conflict, and that needs its own refusal path and its own pt-PT copy.

WHAT THAT MAKES BINDING, in the order it has to be built:
  1. Availability, staff AND portal, must exclude an unconfirmed pedido. NOT BUILT - it needs a migration and the slot is LOOP 5's. See W13-04a-availability-exclusion.
  2. The confirm action re-checks availability in the same transaction as the status write. BUILT.
  3. Patient copy must not promise the slot. BUILT.
  4. Both therapists of a dual-therapist service are covered by the exclusion, per R2. FOLLOWS FROM 1, so it is unbuilt with it.

THE CARD IS CLOSED AS A QUESTION, NOT AS WORK. Closing it while item 1 is unbuilt is deliberate: the thing this card asked for was a RULING, and the ruling exists. Leaving it open would hide the build behind a question that is no longer being asked.

cards.title: Option B availability exclusion - the FINAL migration, sequenced after LOOP 5

evidence.ref: MIGRATION 0059 APPLIED AND PROVEN 2026-08-07, owner-run, FIRST ATTEMPT. Evidence at docs/migration-apply-0059.md section 9. Pre-check: pending 1, PENDING 0059_pedido_does_not_block_slot when=1786700000000 against last-applied 1786600000000, forward. Checker: is_unconfirmed_pedido EXISTS, appointment_conflicts EXISTS and its INSTALLED BODY contains the token (the 0052 body does not), 2 of 2 passed. #836 MERGED after the apply in the ruled order, squashed to be0e1d4. All three occupancy sites landed together. Next free migration number is 0060; nothing in the repo holds an unapplied migration. This was the wave's final planned migration.

cards.notes:
HALT, LOUD, 2026-08-06. The dispatch said to halt if the clean mechanism for JP's option B needs a schema change. It does. This card is that halt, and it is the ONLY thing on W13-04 that is stopped - everything else in the ruling was built and merged in the same session.

WHAT OPTION B REQUIRES: whatever availability computation staff booking and portal booking read must exclude an unconfirmed pedido. RECON, READ-ONLY, WITH FILE EVIDENCE. There are exactly THREE places that answer "is this slot occupied", and they were found by grepping the occupancy predicate rather than trusted from a note:
  1. apps/api/lib/appointments/store.ts:150 apptOverlapExists. ONE fragment, feeding listOpenSlots (the patient slot sweep), listAvailableTherapists, the createBooking guard and hasWindowConflict. APP LAYER, no migration.
  2. apps/web/lib/scheduling/day-availability.ts:51 NON_BLOCKING. The staff free-interval display, shared by the new-appointment panel, the batch engine and multi-therapist conflict reporting. APP LAYER, no migration.
  3. public.appointment_conflicts(), defined in packages/db/migrations/0052_conflicts_no_show_releases_slot.sql:49. The staff HARD BLOCK on save, reached through apps/web/lib/scheduling/conflict.ts findConflicts. A SECURITY DEFINER SQL FUNCTION. Changing it is a migration.

WHY THERE IS NO APP-LAYER ESCAPE FROM (3), and both alternatives were checked rather than dismissed:
  POST-FILTER THE FUNCTION'S OUTPUT in apps/web/lib/scheduling/conflict.ts. It would need to ask, per returned id, "is this an unconfirmed pedido", and the only provenance is a staff_notifications row whose SELECT policy (0055) is pinned to recipient_user_id = auth.uid(). A caller who is not a recipient - an admin, a therapist who is not on the appointment - would classify every pedido as a normal booking. The pedido would then block THEM and not reception, inconsistently and invisibly. apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts:34 also forbids getDbAdmin in this module by name, so there is no sanctioned way to read past RLS here.
  USE created_by IS NULL as the portal marker. Refused on evidence: packages/db/tests/appointments-created-by-provenance.test.ts proves 7/7 against live Postgres that 0049's WITH CHECK is a DISJUNCTION, so a staff principal satisfying another branch may insert a null created_by and the database accepts it. Keying the exclusion on it would put staff rows into the does-not-block set, which is a double-booking generator.
  MOVE THE PEDIDO OUT OF appointments until confirmed. Also a migration, and a bigger one: staff_notifications.appointment_id is NOT NULL with an FK, and the row carries no service, location or practitioner, so a pedido could not be stored at all without new columns or a new table. It would also undo what #829 shipped.

THE OWNER DECISION, and it is his because the rule is his: a SECOND migration in flight repo-wide, or LOOP 5 waits. One migration in flight is not a lane rule, it is a repo rule, and the slot belongs to LOOP 5 (terms acceptance). Two options, and a recommendation:

cards.notes:
THE PATTERN, which is why this is a card and not two unrelated entries in a log.
drizzle-kit migrate prints "migrations applied successfully" when it applies
NOTHING. The message answers "did the command run", never "did the schema
change". Twice now a migration has been reported applied when it had not run, and
BOTH times the checkout, the connection and the SQL file were fine, or looked it.

0049, 2026-07-30: the prod-apply worktree sat on main, because git checkout
<branch> is rejected in that worktree and the fallback went unnoticed. The
migration was not in the tree. Caught afterwards, by the owner asking for schema
evidence.

0058, 2026-08-07: the journal `when` for 0058 was LOWER than 0057's. Drizzle's
pending test is lastDbMigration.created_at < folderMillis
(drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:62), so a backwards timestamp reads as
already-applied and the entry is skipped. Caught afterwards, by
check-migration-tables.mjs.

WHY THE 0058 MECHANISM IS NOT A TYPO ANYONE WOULD SPOT. This repo's journal
`when` values are a SYNTHETIC series stepping +100000000, already years ahead of
wall-clock time. A hand-appended entry using a real Date.now() produces a value
BELOW its predecessor. 1786093200000 looks like a perfectly ordinary millisecond
timestamp, because it is one. It is just smaller than the line above it.

THE CHECK THAT WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME. check-journal.mjs asserted file count,
idx contiguity and filename order. All three reconciled while the migration was
unappliable. None of them looked at `when`. A green check on an adjacent property
reads exactly like a green check on the property you cared about, and that is the
transferable half of this incident.

THE RULE: a command's own success message is never evidence that its side effect
occurred. Verify the side effect from a different source, and in BOTH directions -
before, that the work is pending; after, that the object exists. The 0049 lesson
was recorded as "check the schema afterwards", and that half ALONE still cost a
full owner round-trip on 0058, because an after-check reports the failure once
the owner's terminal session is already over.

cards.title: Every SECURITY DEFINER function is owned by whoever ran migrate, and nothing pins or checks it

evidence.ref: MIGRATION 0060 APPLIED AND PROVEN 2026-08-07, owner-run, FIRST ATTEMPT, detached at 1ea8697. Evidence at docs/migration-apply-0060.md section 10. EXECUTION PROVEN BY THE PENDING COUNT MOVING 1 -> 0, which is the only line in the output that could: four of the six would have printed on a run that did nothing, because 0060 is a no-op. Ownership 13/13 postgres before AND after, identical, which is the second finding - a difference would have meant the migration was not a no-op and pinning was an unauthorised ownership MOVE. #844 merged after the apply in the ruled order. Next free number 0061; nothing holds an unapplied migration.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-07 answering a SECURITY DEFINER interrogation on the freshly applied
0059. The question asked for the owning role. THE ANSWER IS THAT NOTHING SAYS.

THE MECHANISM. Postgres gives a SECURITY DEFINER function the privileges of its
OWNER, and the owner is whoever ran the CREATE unless an explicit
ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO says otherwise. NO MIGRATION IN THIS REPO CONTAINS
ONE - verified by grep across all 59, zero hits for OWNER TO. So every such
function in production is owned by the principal in the env file used at apply
time.

THAT OWNERSHIP IS NOT INCIDENTAL. IT IS THE MECHANISM THE PLATFORM DEPENDS ON.
RLS on these tables is ENABLE, not FORCE, so a table's owner BYPASSES RLS BY
OWNERSHIP. Three load-bearing behaviours rest on it:
  jwt_tenant_id() / jwt_patient_id() are readable by the patient role, which has
  no grant on the auth schema;
  appointment_conflicts() reports a conflict a caller could not otherwise see
  past location RLS - a conflict must block even when the row is invisible to
  you;
  is_unconfirmed_pedido() answers for the patient role, which has NO GRANT AT
  ALL on staff_notifications.

TWELVE DISTINCT FUNCTIONS ACROSS NINE MIGRATIONS: assign_patient_number,
clinical_admin_sees_patient, clinical_therapist_sees_patient,
custom_access_token_hook, is_unconfirmed_pedido, jwt_patient_id, jwt_tenant_id,
location_in_viewer_scope, merge_patients, patient_appt_at_viewer_location,
patient_appt_treated_by_viewer, viewer_has_location_assignment. 37 occurrences
across 0002, 0005, 0010, 0012, 0045, 0047, 0048, 0052, 0059.

THE SILENT-FAILURE MODE, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS HIGH AND NOT LOW.
If the applying principal changes, every SECURITY DEFINER function created after
that point inherits a DIFFERENT owner. Functions created earlier keep the old
one, so the set silently splits in two. NOTHING DETECTS IT:
  drizzle-kit migrate succeeds - ownership is not its concern;
  check-migration-functions.mjs reports EXISTS and a live body, both TRUE;
  check-journal.mjs reconciles - counts and timestamps are unaffected;
  CI passes, and CI STRUCTURALLY CANNOT REPRODUCE IT: supabase db reset builds a
  fresh database where one principal creates everything, so the split cannot
  exist there.

The production symptom is a WRONG ANSWER, not an error: fewer rows, or false
where true is correct, because the new owner does not bypass the RLS the old one
did. For appointment_conflicts that means A CONFLICT IS NOT REPORTED, which is a
double booking.

Same shape as INC-07 and as the stale-mirror incident: every green check stays
green while the property that matters has changed.

WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED IN THIS TURN, and this is deliberate rather than
timid. Pinning ownership means naming a role, and NOBODY HAS READ THE CURRENT
OWNER FROM PRODUCTION. Authoring ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO <guess> would either
no-op or MOVE ownership away from the role the whole availability path depends
on - the failure this card exists to prevent, caused by the fix for it. No
migration is authored until the read comes back. NOTHING MAY OCCUPY MIGRATION
NUMBER 0060 until then.

WHAT IS NEEDED FROM IVAN: one READ-ONLY query, run in his own shell against
production, output pasted back. It reads pg_catalog only, touches no patient
table, and writes nothing:

  select p.proname,
         pg_get_userbyid(p.proowner) as owner,
         p.prosecdef as security_definer
  from pg_proc p
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
  where n.nspname = 'public' and p.prosecdef
  order by owner, p.proname;

WHAT THE ANSWER DECIDES. If all twelve share ONE owner, the exposure is latent
and the fix is a pin plus a CI assertion, authored against the real name. If they
DO NOT all share one owner, the split has ALREADY happened and this becomes an
incident with a live behavioural consequence to hunt.

WIRED AS A HARD DEPENDENCY of the pre-launch credential rotation:
docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, section "SECURITY DEFINER ownership is UNPINNED,
and it is a rotation dependency". Rotating a PASSWORD is safe - same role, new
secret. Changing the ROLE is what triggers this, and a rotation that moves the
apply to a new service account would do exactly that.

=== THE READ RETURNED. THIRTEEN, NOT TWELVE. 2026-08-07. ===

MY GREP WAS WRONG AND PRODUCTION WAS RIGHT. I reported twelve functions;
production has THIRTEEN. THE MISSING ONE IS appointment_conflicts - the function
at the centre of the entire 0059 work, and the one whose wrong answer is a double
booking.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, measured rather than guessed: the grep read SIX lines of
context above each SECURITY DEFINER marker (grep -B6). appointment_conflicts has
a six-parameter list plus a RETURNS TABLE block, so its CREATE line sits
EIGHTEEN lines above its SECURITY DEFINER line. A FIXED-SIZE CONTEXT WINDOW IS
THE BUG. Two other definitions have gaps of 39 and 127 lines and were caught only
because they carry a second, closer marker - so the same grep was already lucky
twice.

A PINNING MIGRATION BUILT ON THE TWELVE-ITEM LIST WOULD HAVE LEFT THE MOST
IMPORTANT FUNCTION UNPINNED WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS. Same failure class as the
backwards journal timestamp and the superseded mirror: an artefact that
reconciles on everything except the property that matters.

A SECOND ERROR CAUGHT BEFORE THE APPLY, by checking each signature against its
CREATE rather than writing them from the name list: merge_patients takes THREE
uuid parameters (p_source_id, p_target_id, p_actor_id DEFAULT NULL), not two. A
two-argument ALTER would have failed mid-migration with "function does not
exist". A DEFAULT does not change a function's identity, so the argument list is
all three types.

THE CHECKER ASSERTS TWO THINGS, and the second is the one people forget. Owner is
obvious. COUNT is not: an owner-only check passes happily on a FOURTEENTH
function that arrived correctly owned, which is exactly how an unreviewed
SECURITY DEFINER function enters the schema. Both negative arms are proven -
a fabricated wrong owner fails with the function named, and a count of twelve
fails while every remaining owner is correct.

CI CAN ONLY CATCH HALF, and the workflow says so rather than implying otherwise:
supabase db reset builds a database where ONE principal creates everything, so an
owner SPLIT cannot exist there and CI cannot detect it. What CI DOES catch is the
count. The owner half is enforced where it is enforceable - against production,
by the same script, twice per apply block.

=== APPLY BLOCK CORRECTED 2026-08-07 BEFORE IT REACHED IVAN. ===

THE FIRST DRAFT COULD NOT PROVE THE MIGRATION RAN. It checked ownership before
and after, and the pre-check for pending 1 - but 0060 is a NO-OP, so its correct
end state is identical to its correct start state. Every state check would pass
whether migrate executed or not, and drizzle prints success on a no-op. The block
would have produced a receipt.

FIXED: check-pending-migrations.mjs 0 AFTER migrate. The pending count moving
from exactly 1 to exactly 0 is the ONLY thing in the block that proves execution,
because only a tracking row written into drizzle.__drizzle_migrations can move
it. The block now states which of its six outputs is the proof and which are not.

ALSO PINNED THE SHA, not the branch: git checkout --detach 1ea8697. A push to the
branch between validation and apply would otherwise silently change what runs.

=== APPLIED AND PROVEN 2026-08-07. THE CARD CLOSES. ===

The block was correct as validated and ran first time. Evidence at
docs/migration-apply-0060.md section 10.

WHAT THIS CARD LEAVES BEHIND, beyond the pin itself:
  ownership is now a REPO FACT (0060) rather than an accident of who ran migrate;
  check-security-definer-owner.mjs enforces owner AND count, in CI (count only -
  supabase db reset cannot reproduce an owner split, and db-tests.yml says so)
  and against production in every future apply block (both halves);
  docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md carries the rotation rule in one sentence:
  rotating the postgres password is safe, same role and new secret; introducing a
  separate migration role is what splits ownership, and that failure is silent.

AND THE APPLY-BLOCK DOCTRINE GAINED ITS LAST PIECE from this migration. 0060's
first draft could not prove a no-op had run. That produced the standing rule that
every apply block now starts NOT VALIDATED - STRATEGY REVIEW REQUIRED - DO NOT
RUN, written into the runbook and into PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md section 4 item 9 so it
survives a rehydrate.

cards.notes:
PRODUCTION FACT, 2026-08-09. Two portal pedidos created against osteojp-api at 09:02:52 and 09:04:08 both logged "[notifications] patient-change NOT DELIVERED (stub consumer, centre not built yet)". A LEFT JOIN to staff_notifications returned null for both. A GET at 09:03:39 logged "consumer registered" BETWEEN them, which is what made the shape legible.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both owner-observed on production. (1) Neither pedido appeared in reception's queue at /notificacoes. (2) A staff Nova marcacao for the same therapist at the same time was REFUSED with "Conflito de terapeuta", because migration 0059 keys is_unconfirmed_pedido on a staff_notifications row with kind appointment_request and there was none. JP's PEDIDO SLOT option-B ruling was silently INVERTED in production. 0059 is correct; it cannot see a pedido that left no trace.

NOT A COLD-START RACE, and that mattered: the obvious reading was that the POST beat instrumentation. It did not. The 09:04:08 POST hit the stub a full minute AFTER registration succeeded, because registration mutated a module copy the booking path does not share.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT, which is the part worth keeping. Every suite that emitted called setPatientChangeConsumer first, so every suite tested a REGISTERED module. Nothing tested an UNREGISTERED one - and that was the only state production was ever in on that path. The new guard emits from a fresh module copy with no registration call, which is the defect's actual shape.

DOCTRINE THIS ADDS: a module-level singleton mutated from a boot hook is not wiring, it is a hope about bundling. If correctness depends on a swap, the thing that needs the value must be able to resolve it ITSELF.

=== SHIPPED 2026-08-11 AS #862 (56d54ce). ===

The card's own reading was right and is worth preserving: THE DELIVERY HALF WAS
ALREADY PROVEN, and only the entry point was missing. Recon confirmed it before
building - resetPasswordForEmail had ZERO call sites in the whole repo, and its
only occurrence was on the ban list at apps/api/lib/auth/no-session-minting.ts
test:44, which scans API_ROOT = apps/api and enforces Decision D on the PATIENT
side only. It does not bind apps/web, and no equivalent ban exists there.

TWO DECISIONS RECORDED IN THE CODE, NOT ONLY IN THE PR, so the next session does
not undo them:

  THE SUPABASE CALL RUNS IN THE BROWSER, NOT IN A SERVER ACTION. It looks less
  consistent with login/actions.ts and it is correct. This route triggers an
  email send from an UNAUTHENTICATED caller and apps/web has no rate limiter of
  its own (SEC-r-token-no-rate-limit is LOOP 6's port), so Supabase's own
  throttle on /recover is the only control there is - and it keys on the CALLER.
  A server action makes every request arrive from one server IP, bucketing an
  abuser's flood together with a real staff member's reset, so one abuser could
  deny recovery to the whole clinic on the day someone is locked out. The
  reasoning is in ForgotPasswordClient.tsx under a DO NOT SIMPLIFY header.

  ONE SCREEN FOR EVERY OUTCOME. Success and every failure render the same
  confirmation, because the staff email list is the clinic's roster and a form
  that answers differently for a known address publishes it. Same oracle the
  patient OTP path refuses to become. The cost is accepted rather than hidden: a
  rate-limited staff member sees 'check your email' and no mail arrives, and
  cannot be told which happened. The failure is still not SILENT (PG7) - it is
  logged by transport message only, and the collapser is never given the address,
  so it cannot leak what it never sees (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

THE NOTE ABOUT THE SUPABASE TRANSPORT WAS CORRECT and was verified before
building rather than after: the send goes through Supabase's own SMTP, not our
notify gate, so INVITES_LIVE_SEND does not gate it and no approval-registry entry

cards.title: Duplicate pedido rows in the queue - the stated premise is DISPROVED by the code; needs one owner-run read

evidence.ref:
OWNER-RUN READ-ONLY QUERY on production, 2026-08-11, against appointment 1863b4f5-dde1-45bf-bf97-ffcc0cce6e27. Eight rows, TWO DISTINCT KINDS, thirteen minutes apart:
  4 rows kind=appointment_request, occurred_at 2026-08-09 15:09:15.868+00
  4 rows kind=cancelled,            occurred_at 2026-08-09 15:22:42.271+00
Both groups address the SAME four recipients (54e3cd08, f6d111c2, 4750c272, 251d5d69). occurred_at is IDENTICAL within each group, which is the 0055 unique index doing exactly its job.

WHAT IT PROVES: the patient created a pedido and cancelled it. Both emits fanned out correctly to four recipients. THERE IS NO DUPLICATION AND THERE NEVER WAS. Re-verifiable by re-running the query in the card notes.

cards.notes:
REPORTED: one pedido produced SEVEN staff_notifications rows of kind appointment_request, with Raquel Monteiro, Tamara Tabarra and Carlos Barrelas each receiving TWO.

HALTED RATHER THAN BUILT, because the code disproves the stated mechanism and building a dedupe on a wrong premise would hide the real cause.

WHAT THE CODE PROVES. resolveRecipients ALREADY DEDUPES: it accumulates reception rows and practitioner rows into a Set<string> and returns [...set] (apps/api/lib/notifications/centre.ts, the recipients Set). The reception query cannot fan out either - innerJoin on roles is one role per user. So ONE emit can produce AT MOST ONE ROW PER RECIPIENT. Duplicates within a single appointment_id cannot come from a single emit, and cannot come from a missing dedupe, because the dedupe is there.

SO EITHER THE EMIT FIRED TWICE, OR THE SEVEN IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE.

The second reading is very plausible and must be excluded FIRST. 16 rows for TWO pedidos is 8 each. If the tenant has 7 reception-role users plus 1 practitioner, 8 rows per pedido is CORRECT FAN-OUT, and "Raquel, Tamara and Carlos each received two" is each of them receiving ONE ROW PER PEDIDO - which is right, not a bug. Counting across both pedidos would look exactly like duplication.

IF IT IS A REAL DOUBLE EMIT, the dedupe index cannot stop it: 0055's unique index is (recipient_user_id, appointment_id, kind, occurred_at) and occurred_at comes from a per-request a per-request Date, so two emits carry different instants and both persist. One candidate worth checking then: the portal confirm button has loading={pending} but NO disabled prop (BookingFlow.tsx:327), unlike the step-3 button at :276 which does carry disabled.

WHAT IS NEEDED: one read-only query from Ivan, grouping by appointment_id and recipient_user_id. If every (appointment, recipient) count is 1 there is NO duplication and the finding becomes "why are Raquel, Tamara and Carlos reception-role", which is a data question. If any count is 2 it is a genuine double emit and the button guard is the first suspect.

=== ROOT-CAUSE READ 2026-08-11, PURPLE, CODE ONLY, NO PROD TOUCH ===

ALL THREE PROPOSED MECHANISMS ARE REFUTED, and the refutation is structural rather than probabilistic.

THE DEDUPE KEY IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. 0055:145-147 is UNIQUE(recipient_user_id, appointment_id, kind, occurred_at) and centre.ts:145 writes through onConflictDoNothing(). occurred_at is NOT a per-write clock: it is e.occurredAt, carried on the event, stamped once by the caller at booking.ts:411 as now.toISOString() where now is a parameter of bookAppointment (booking.ts:339). So TWO ROWS FOR ONE (recipient, appointment, kind) REQUIRE TWO DISTINCT occurredAt VALUES, which requires two separate executions of bookAppointment carrying two different now.

(1) DOUBLE POST FROM THE CONFIRM STEP - REFUTED TWICE OVER. confirmAppointmentRequest (apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts:1021) does NOT emit at all; the staff app never calls emitPatientChange, it only READS staff_notifications and inner-joins on kind=appointment_request (actions.ts:1052-55). No confirm can write a notification row. Separately, a double POST to the portal BOOKING route would run store.createBooking twice and mint TWO appointment ids, so it cannot produce eight rows on ONE id.

(2) INNGEST AT-LEAST-ONCE REPLAY - REFUTED. emitPatientChange (patient-change.ts:204-215) is a plain inline await in the request, post-commit. No step wrapper, no queue, no retry. INC-06 corroborates: the stub logged at request time.

(3) TURBOPACK DOUBLE MODULE COPY - REFUTED BY THE DEDUPE, and this is the subtle one worth keeping. Even if two copies of the module each resolved a consumer and both ran, both receive THE SAME event object and therefore the SAME e.occurredAt. The unique index collapses the second write to zero rows. Module duplication yields ONE row, not two. It was the INC-06 mechanism because that was a NOT-DELIVERED bug; it cannot be a DOUBLE-delivered bug.

SO THE WHOLE-WRITE-TWICE HYPOTHESIS IS STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE ON THE CREATE PATH, and the most likely reading is that these are NOT DUPLICATES AT ALL - the same misreading D3 was already halted on once.

THE LIKELY BENIGN EXPLANATION: two rows per (recipient, appointment) pair with DIFFERENT kind. There are four kinds (patient-change.ts:46-49): booked, cancelled, rescheduled, appointment_request. The only emit sites in the codebase are the three PATIENT paths in booking.ts - create :403, cancel :441, reschedule :548. So an appointment the patient created AND then cancelled or rescheduled through the portal legitimately carries TWO rows per recipient, and that is correct behaviour, not duplication. Appointment 1863b4f5 having 2 per pair while 1b5979db and 37e049b5 have 1 per pair fits exactly: one of the three was acted on afterwards, the other two were not.

THE DISPATCHED SQL WAS INSUFFICIENT AND WAS WIDENED. A block returning only created_at CANNOT distinguish these hypotheses, because both produce rows at different instants. kind and occurred_at are the discriminating columns and the corrected block selects them. If the 8 rows show TWO DISTINCT kinds, D3 closes as not-a-defect. If they show ONE kind with two occurred_at values, there is a real double execution and the next question is the route layer, not the notification layer.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-11. NOT A DEFECT. ===

THE QUERY SETTLED IT. Four rows kind=appointment_request at occurred_at 15:09:15.868, then four rows kind=cancelled at 15:22:42.271, same four recipients both times, thirteen minutes apart. A patient created a pedido and cancelled it. Correct fan-out on both emits.

BOTH OF D3 PREMISES WERE WRONG, and the second was not PURPLE’s. The FIRST premise (one pedido produced seven rows, so resolveRecipients must be missing a dedupe) was disproved by the code: the dedupe is there and the reception join cannot fan out. The SECOND premise (fan-out is 4 per pedido and one appointment has 2 rows per pair, so the whole write executed twice) was STRATEGY’S, supplied with the production counts, and it was wrong the same way the first was: it counted rows across two DIFFERENT KINDS and read the total as duplication. Both times the number was real and the interpretation was not.

CORRECTED READING RULE, recorded because the previous version of it was unsound. PURPLE wrote: “one kind with two occurred_at means a real double execution.” THAT IS FALSE AS STATED. A patient who reschedules twice produces exactly that signature legitimately - two events, two occurred_at, same kind, full fan-out each time. THE RULE HOLDS ONLY WHEN THE REPEATED KIND CANNOT RECUR. Of the four kinds (patient-change.ts:46-49), appointment_request is the ONLY non-recurring one, because an appointment is created exactly once; booked, cancelled and rescheduled can all legitimately repeat against one appointment id. So the sound rule is: TWO ROWS SHARING (recipient, appointment, kind=appointment_request) WITH DIFFERENT occurred_at IS THE ONLY SIGNATURE THAT EVIDENCES A DOUBLE EXECUTION. Anything else needs the event history before it means anything.

THE LESSON THAT GENERALISES: a raw row count over a table with a kind column is not a duplication measurement. Group by kind and occurred_at before concluding anything. This is the second time this card was opened on a count read without its discriminator.
