cards.title: OTP request endpoint was an unauthenticated SMS pump - global send ceiling and landline rejection SHIPPED; bot challenge not in scope

evidence.ref: #865 MERGED. Closes directions (a) GLOBAL SEND CEILING and (b) LANDLINE REJECTION, which is exactly what this card said it closes on: 'THE CARD CLOSES ON CODE ... each with a guard proven red against the pre-fix sha. Not on a console setting.' Direction (c), the bot challenge, is deliberately NOT in scope and is not carded as done. FIVE NEGATIVE ARMS, each firing exactly the assertions it should: ceiling deleted -> 8 failed; landline check deleted -> 5 failed; ceiling key made caller-derived -> 8 failed; ceiling moved before validation -> exactly 1 failed (the ordering test); geographic regex broken -> 3 failed. All reverted, 70/70 green after. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, test api 485 passed (+23) and web 1953 passed, build 4/4. NO MIGRATION: rate_limit_counters (0056, applied 2026-08-05) is a generic key/value fixed-window counter, so the ceiling is two more keys against a table that already exists. Re-verifiable without asking anyone: read apps/api/lib/rate-limit/limiter.ts (RULES.otpGlobalHour, RULES.otpGlobalDay, OTP_GLOBAL_HOUR_KEY, OTP_GLOBAL_DAY_KEY) and apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts, and observe the ceiling is checked after every validation gate and keyed on a constant.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-11 BY CODE READ, NOT BY EXERCISING THE ENDPOINT. No prod touch, no request issued. VERDICT: EXPOSED.

THE FINDING. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request accepts any well-formed Portuguese number from any caller and, when OTP_LIVE_SEND is armed, dispatches a real Twilio SMS to it. There is NO patient lookup and therefore NO refusal branch for a number matching zero patients.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS, apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts:
  :36-41  rate limit per client key
  :43-54  parse body, require phone and tenantId
  :58-59  normalizePhonePT, 400 if malformed
  :64-69  rate limit per phone hash
  :71-74  requestCode - ISSUE AND SEND
  :77     204 always
The route states the absence itself at :20-22: 'AND IT NEVER LOOKS THE PHONE UP. There is no patient query on this path at all.'
apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts:245 is the send, unconditional. :216-220 states the intent: 'A code is issued for any well-formed number; an unknown number simply receives an SMS that helps nobody.'
apps/api/lib/auth/otp-transport.ts:171-172 - resolveOtpTransport returns the real Twilio adapter if and only if OTP_LIVE_SEND === 'true', else a sink. THE FLAG IS THE ENTIRE CONTROL.

BLAST RADIUS. PT_SUBSCRIBER at apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts:19 is /^[29]\d{8}$/ - first digit 2 or 9 plus eight digits = 200,000,000 accepted inputs. RULES.otpRequest at apps/api/lib/rate-limit/limiter.ts:184 is {limit: 3, windowMs: 3600000}. The per-phone limit caps harassment of ONE handset at 3/hour and does NOT bound spend: an attacker rotating numbers never approaches it. The per-client limit keys on the first x-forwarded-for hop (limiter.ts:117-119), so a proxy pool yields 3 sends per IP per hour with no global ceiling. Route is public: apps/api/proxy.ts:5 confirms authorization is per-route via requirePatient, which this pre-auth route cannot and does not call.

THE MULTI-PATIENT QUESTION DOES NOT ARISE HERE. The exactly-one-row rule lives in resolvePatientByProvenPhone at CLAIM time (apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.test.ts:40). A number matching 0, 1 or 5 patients is treated identically at request: SMS sent. The refusal happens at verify, after the message has left.

THIS IS DELIBERATE DESIGN, NOT A BUG, and that is why it is an owner decision rather than a fix. The trade is documented at apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts:7-13: a lookup-then-refuse endpoint would be a patient-list oracle for anyone with a phone book, and this clinic's patient list is itself sensitive. The engineering is sound. What is unsound is arming the flag on a public origin and leaving it.

OWNER ACTION REQUIRED: confirm whether OTP_LIVE_SEND is currently 'true' on osteojp-api Production, and disarm it if so. PURPLE performs no cloud writes and cannot read the value. Governed by docs/rulings/R9a-otp-live-send-not-separable.md.

DESIGN DIRECTION, SET BY STRATEGY 2026-08-11. NOT IMPLEMENTED THIS DISPATCH. The fix MUST preserve enumeration resistance. A lookup-then-refuse design is REJECTED OUTRIGHT: it converts the endpoint into the patient-list oracle the current design exists to avoid.
  (a) GLOBAL SEND CEILING, highest value per unit of work. A tenant-wide cap on OTP sends per rolling hour and per rolling day, independent of the existing per-IP and per-phone rules. Once tripped every caller receives the SAME generic response, so no enumeration signal is added. This bounds spend ABSOLUTELY, which neither existing limit does.
  (b) REJECT LANDLINES. phone.ts:19 accepts the 2 prefix, which is geographic and cannot receive SMS. Rejecting it removes roughly half the accepted input space AND supplies the enforcement point PG1's own DoR requires for the landline degradation case, which today has none. Leaks nothing: prefix ranges are public numbering-plan facts, not patient data.
  (c) INVISIBLE BOT CHALLENGE on the request route, ONLY if (a) and (b) prove insufficient. Weigh against accessibility for elderly patients before proposing it.

TEST DEBT, RECORDED: there is NO test file for this route. ls apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/ returns route.ts alone. The send-for-unknown-number behaviour is currently UNASSERTED, which is how a deliberate trade became an unreviewed one. Any fix ships with a guard proven RED against the pre-fix sha.

HOME_LANE IS in_flight, NOT incidents, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The lane derivation puts an in_flight card that is blocked on a person into BLOCKED ON PEOPLE, under the owner column, which starts the answer-latency clock. This card is not an incident RECORD, it is active work whose next step is an owner decision (is the flag armed, and disarm it), followed by build directions (a), (b) and (c). Filing it under incidents would leave the most urgent item on the board out of the column the owner reads for what he owes.

THE PLAN ALREADY RULED THIS, AND THE RULING IS COMMITTED. docs/acceptance-session-wave-13.md:1161-1165, section 11 'Disarm - a named step, and not optional': 'OTP_LIVE_SEND IS DISARMED AT THE END OF THIS SESSION. R9 authorises supervised canaries, not a standing arm. "Left armed" is NOT permitted merely because it was written down - writing it down is a note, not a decision.' The voided amendment proposed exactly the standing arm that paragraph refuses.

WHY THE EXPOSURE IS LIVE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL, and this is the load-bearing fact: item 25 is the disarm step and it carries two blanks in the committed file, `Disarmed at: ______` and `Redeploy Ready at: ______`. BOTH ARE UNFILLED. The sittings ran 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09; no results file existed until 2026-08-11. There is NO COMMITTED RECORD THAT THE DISARM WAS EVER PERFORMED. Absent a filled-in item 25, the flag must be treated as ARMED. The plan even anticipated the failure mode: 'STOP if the redeploy errors. The flag is still armed until one succeeds.' A save without a successful redeploy does not disarm a running deployment.

=== OWNER INTERIM MITIGATION 2026-08-11. NOT A FIX. THE CARD STAYS OPEN AT HIGHEST PRIORITY. ===

Completed by the owner and recorded here as reported, not verified by PURPLE (all four are cloud-console state, which PURPLE does not read):
  1. OTP_LIVE_SEND set to false on osteojp-api Production, REDEPLOYED WITH BUILD CACHE UNTICKED. This is the control that matters: with the flag off, resolveOtpTransport (otp-transport.ts:171-172) returns the in-process sink and nothing leaves the process.
  2. Twilio auto-recharge OFF, with a spend trigger set. Bounds the financial blast radius if the flag is ever armed again.
  3. Twilio geo permissions restricted to Portugal. Narrows the destination space but does NOT narrow it below the ~200M PT numbers the endpoint already accepts, so it does not touch this defect.
  4. Lurdes Cruz credential rotated again.

WHY THIS IS MITIGATION AND NOT A FIX, stated plainly so no future session closes this card on it. THE CODE IS UNCHANGED. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request is still unauthenticated, still performs no patient lookup (route.ts:20-22), and still sends unconditionally (otp.ts:245) across ~200,000,000 accepted inputs (phone.ts:19). Every one of the four items above is REVERSIBLE FROM A CONSOLE BY ONE PERSON IN ONE MINUTE, and item 1 is exactly the toggle that R9a permits a supervised sitting to flip. The next sitting that arms the flag re-opens the full exposure unless directions (a) and (b) have shipped by then.

THE CARD CLOSES ON CODE: a tenant-wide send ceiling (direction a) and landline rejection (direction b), each with a guard proven red against the pre-fix sha. Not on a console setting.

=== SHIPPED 2026-08-11 (#865). DIRECTIONS (a) AND (b). ===

OWNER CONTEXT RULING, and it changes how this card should be read by anyone
reviewing it later: the platform is NOT in live use and no real patient numbers
are on it, so this was a PRE-LAUNCH BUILD ITEM and not a live incident. It was
built properly rather than rushed.

FORK 1, THE CEILING KEY. RULED: a process-wide CONSTANT key, not the supplied
tenantId. A spend ceiling must hold when the attacker controls the input, and a
constant needs no trust in the body at all.
  THE BYPASS THAT RULING CLOSES, recorded because it is not obvious: keying on
  tenantId looks tenant-correct. tenantId arrives in the body of an
  UNAUTHENTICATED endpoint and is not validated before the limit is checked, so
  a rotating attacker gets a fresh bucket for free. They would not have SPENT
  anything - the FK on patient_otp_codes.tenant_id throws before the send - but
  they would have kept the REAL tenant's counter at zero while probing. A
  ceiling that reads healthy during an attack is worse than no ceiling.
  A per-tenant inner bound was authorised ONLY if it cost nothing extra. It
  costs an extra database round trip per request, so it was NOT added, and the
  outer global bound is the requirement that shipped.

THE ORDERING IS ITSELF A CONTROL, and it is the part most likely to be undone
by a later tidy-up. The ceiling is checked LAST, after every validation gate.
Checked first, a malformed body or a landline would SPEND global budget, and an
attacker could exhaust the clinic's daily allowance with garbage that costs them
nothing and us nothing in SMS - denying login to every real patient without
buying a single message. A test asserts the ceiling keys are NOT reached on a
refused request, and moving the block earlier fails exactly that one test.

FIXED WINDOW, NOT ROLLING. The dispatch said rolling; the store implements a
fixed window (limiter.ts header, durable-store.ts). The code and its comment say
fixed rather than promising what the store does not do: a burst spanning a
boundary can spend up to two windows. That is accepted and it still bounds spend
ABSOLUTELY, which neither pre-existing limit did at all.

FORK 2, THE LANDLINE. RULED: reject at the OTP REQUEST ROUTE only. Neither
apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts nor its declared-canonical mirror
apps/web/lib/reminders/phone.ts is touched. normalizePhonePT has FIVE live call
sites across TWO apps, two of them on launch-critical reminder dispatch, so a
one-character edit to PT_SUBSCRIBER would have changed reminder behaviour as a
side effect. That question is real and is carded separately as
LE-reminders-landline-dispatch, NOT built.
  The predicate lives in apps/api/lib/auth/otp-sms-capability.ts, which is
  AMBER-owned by the file table. normalizePhonePT still decides what a
  well-formed PT number IS; the new module decides whether we are willing to
  SEND to one. Two questions, two modules, and the second cannot drift into the
  first.

PG1 GATE READING, RULED: PG1 does NOT require the landline-specific message to
fire to the patient. The three standing bullets at
apps/portal/app/auth/login/LoginOtp.tsx:169 are deliberate anti-oracle design
and are not weakened to satisfy a gate note. PG1's clause needs an ENFORCEMENT
POINT and the rejection supplies it. Consequence: apps/portal was NOT touched
and needed no ownership ruling.
  The refusal therefore reuses invalid_input rather than naming itself. A
  distinct code would be SAFE to disclose - the numbering plan is a public fact
  and says nothing about our records - but it would still be a new
  distinguishable outcome on the endpoint whose whole design is to have as few
  as possible, and with the portal ruled not to branch it buys nothing.

THE ORACLE IS NOT REINTRODUCED, asserted rather than claimed. Lookup-then-refuse
stays rejected. The route still never queries the patient table, still answers
204 for any sendable number known or unknown, and the ceiling never looks at the

=== OWNER RULING 2026-08-12: THE FLAG STAYS ARMED FOR SUPERVISED SITTINGS.
    THIS CLOSES THE QUESTION. STOP RE-ASKING IT. ===

Three facts, and together they remove the risk rather than accepting it:

  THE PLATFORM IS NOT IN LIVE USE. The only number present on it is the
  owner's own. There is no patient who can be reached by an accidental send,
  because there is no patient on the system.

  A SWEEP IS A SUPERVISED SITTING, which is precisely the condition R9 permits
  arming under. The flag being on during an observation the owner is running,

cards.title: apps/web now HAS a rate limiter: the module is extracted to @osteojp/rate-limit and consumed by both apps, and the public /r/[token] redeem POST is limited. Adoption across the rest of the apps/web surface is carded separately

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-13. The card named two shapes - PORT into apps/web, or SHARED
PACKAGE. IT IS A SHARED PACKAGE, and the reason is not tidiness.

A PORT WOULD HAVE MEANT TWO COPIES OF A SECURITY CONTROL. RULES is a set of
numbers saying how hard to throttle; two copies drift and the drift is SILENT -
nobody would know which app enforced what until an incident asked. This week
already paid twice for duplicated logic: the phone normalisation needed a whole
parity suite to stay honest across two languages, and a duplicated e2e traversal
cost a 12m33s shard. NEITHER OF THOSE WAS A SECURITY BOUNDARY. This is.

NOTHING IN apps/api MOVED. packages/rate-limit holds the code; apps/api's
limiter.ts and durable-store.ts are one-line re-export shims, so every existing
import - INCLUDING THE OTP ROUTES THAT CARRY PG1 - resolves exactly as before.
The extraction changed no call site on a gate-bearing path. The shims contain no
logic and so cannot drift.

ONE NEW FUNCTION, AND IT EXISTS TO PREVENT A SECOND IDENTITY. clientKeyFromHeaders
takes anything with .get(name). A Next SERVER ACTION never receives a Request -
it gets headers() - so without it the only way to limit this action would have
been a second key-derivation, and two ways of deciding "who is this caller" is
exactly the drift the package was created to stop. clientKey(req, ...) now
delegates to it, so the route-handler and server-action paths cannot disagree.

NO MIGRATION. rate_limit_counters already exists from 0056, which is what made
this an afternoon rather than an owner-gated change. 0063 is still free.

RULES.tokenRedeem: 10 per minute, matching booking, because each one that gets
through MUTATES AN APPOINTMENT. KEYED ON IP, NOT ON THE TOKEN: keying on the
token would hand an attacker a fresh budget per token, which is exactly the
traffic worth refusing, and a token is a credential rather than a bucket key.

THE LIMITED PATH TAKES THE SAME ?r=refused REDIRECT AS EVERY OTHER REFUSAL, and
that is counsel section 3 rather than a shortcut. This surface renders ONE
generic outcome for bad, expired, forged, unknown and already-spent tokens. A
distinguishable "you are rate limited" would be a NEW SIGNAL on the one page
designed to emit none, and it would confirm to a prober that their earlier
attempts registered.

NINE TESTS, and the one that matters counts DATABASE CALLS rather than statuses.
A test asserting only the redirect flag would pass against an implementation that
limited AFTER redeeming, which is no control at all. Also asserted: the key is
the IP and never contains the token; a cancel is refused exactly as a confirm;
and MALFORMED SUBMISSIONS DO NOT SPEND BUDGET - checked before the limiter, the
same ordering apps/api's OTP route settled on, so an attacker cannot exhaust a
real patient's allowance with garbage that never reaches a query and deny them
the link in their own SMS.
NEGATIVE ARM RUN AND OBSERVED: with the limit removed, FIVE of the nine go red.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, because the card is emphatic about it. The token is 128 bits
and is not brute-forceable at any rate; a GET performs nothing, since opening a
link renders and only the POST mutates. This is DEFENCE IN DEPTH and a cost
control. The real exposure closed is an unauthenticated endpoint on the
patient-facing domain doing database work per request with nothing bounding how
often.

THE REST OF apps/web IS NOT LIMITED, and that is stated rather than implied. The
staff surface is authenticated, which bounds abuse to authenticated users, and
the card itself says the public route is where it began to matter. The seam now
exists for every other route to adopt in one import. Carded as
SEC-web-surface-limiter-adoption.

Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11 including the new package, unit green
including 9 new, build 4/4.

cards.notes:
BROADENED 2026-08-11 BY STRATEGY. The original title named one route; the finding is surface-wide.

THE FINDING AT ITS REAL SIZE. There is NO rate limiter anywhere in apps/web. A repo-wide search across apps/web/lib and apps/web/app for a rate-limit module returns ZERO files. The limiter (RULES, clientKey, checkDurableRateLimit, tooManyRequests) exists ONLY in apps/api/lib/rate-limit/, and apps/web does not import it. So this is not one route lacking a limiter; it is an entire application with no limiting concept, and /r/[token] is simply the first patient-facing route on that surface where it began to matter.

WHAT IT COVERS: every server action and route handler in apps/web, which is the STAFF platform plus the public token landing page. The staff surface is authenticated, which bounds abuse to authenticated users. /r/[token] is PUBLIC and unauthenticated.

WHY IT SURFACED NOW: Task B (R11) puts the confirm link in every 24h reminder SMS AND truncates the token to 22 chars. Truncation plus no rate limit is a materially different risk from truncation alone.

STATED SO IT IS NOT OVER-READ: 128 bits is not brute-forceable regardless of rate limiting, and GET is inert - opening a link performs nothing, the action runs only from the confirmation POST (page.tsx:18-20). This is DEFENCE IN DEPTH and an abuse and cost control, not a live hole. The real exposure is cost and noise: an unlimited endpoint that hits the database per request, on the patient-facing domain.

THE FIX IS ARCHITECTURAL, NOT LOCAL, which is why this is not a quick win. apps/web has nothing to reuse, so it is either a PORT of apps/api/lib/rate-limit/ or a SHARED PACKAGE consumed by both apps. That is a real design choice with a durable-store dependency. NO MIGRATION either way - the durable store already exists.

CARRY INTO LOOP 6 AS A SURFACE-WIDE ROW, alongside SEC-otp-unauthenticated-sms-pump. LOOP 6 enumerates the patient-facing surface and names an enforcement point per row; no limiter exists in this application is an enforcement-point answer for every apps/web row at once, and the matrix should say so rather than repeat it per route.

DO NOT BUILD THIS DISPATCH, per instruction. Ordering recommendation stands: ship with or before the Task B link, never after.

cards.title: 24h SMS confirm link - CLOSED WON'T-DO 2026-08-11. R11 dropped: the 22-char token it needs cannot exist statelessly

evidence.ref: OWNER RULING 2026-08-11: R11 IS DROPPED, option 2 of the five in docs/rulings/R11-24h-sms-carries-the-link-not-the-phone.md. The 24h SMS keeps the clinic phone CTA. NO code change, NO template edit, NO token change, NO migration. THIS IS A WON'T-DO CLOSE, and status=shipped is the enum's only terminal value - nothing shipped, and nobody should read it as the link having landed (same treatment as D1-pedido-versus-pedido-stacking, closed by ruling with no code change). RE-VERIFIABLE WITHOUT ASKING ANYONE, and this is the arithmetic the ruling rests on: apps/web/lib/reminders/link-token.ts:95-107 emits base64url(payload) + '.' + base64url(HMAC). Sign a token with two real uuids and measure it: 202 chars, of which 158 is payload and 43 is signature. packages/db/migrations/0054_patient_audit_log_and_token_consumption.sql:187-189 states the same independently ('around 183 characters and containing a dot'). R11's own table assumes a 47-char link, which is the 25-char base plus a 22-char TOKEN - so the whole token, not the signature. 22 base64url chars carry 132 bits; the payload they would replace is two uuids (256 bits) plus an expiry plus a scope. It is not tight, it is impossible.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED WON'T-DO 2026-08-11 BY OWNER RULING. R11 IS DROPPED. ===

The ruling is option 2 of the five in R11: the 24h SMS keeps the clinic phone
CTA and does not carry the confirm link. No code change, no template edit, no
token change, no migration. The 48h email keeps its link and is unaffected.

TWO REASONS, AND THE SECOND IS THE BINDING ONE:
  a. The 22-character token R11 needs is not tight, it is IMPOSSIBLE. 132 bits
     against 256 bits of uuid payload alone.
  b. The only design that produces R11's numbers takes a migration, and 0061 is
     RESERVED for the scheduling EXCLUDE constraint on the double booking. R11
     does not outrank it.
Option 3 (short domain) was never sufficient and option 4 (two segments) weakens
a guard protecting every template. Neither is revisited.

=== THE RECORDED SHORTFALL WAS CONDITIONAL ON A TOKEN THAT CANNOT BE ISSUED. ===

WITHDRAWN FIGURE: 'SHORTFALL: 25 CHARACTERS, and only when the fee notice is
armed.' That line is not wrong arithmetic - AMBER re-measured it from the
committed signer on 2026-08-11 and reproduced every figure in the old table
exactly (99, 153, 131, 185, 53, margin 7, margin 29, over by 25), which is what
validates the re-measurement. What is wrong is its PRECONDITION: the 185 and the
over-by-25 occur only with a 47-char link, and a 47-char link requires a 22-char
token, and that token cannot exist statelessly.

THE TRUE FIGURES, worst case Castelo Branco plus the longest phone
(twilio-proof.test.ts:97-98), measured from the committed signer and templates:
  24h base today                      99   fits, margin 61
  24h base + fee notice              153   fits, margin 7
  fee notice alone                    53
  token today                        202   (payload 158 + '.' + signature 43)
  link today                         227
  24h + FULL link, fee OFF           311   OVER BY 151
  24h + link with SIGNATURE cut to 22 290   OVER BY 130
  24h + link with a 22-CHAR TOKEN    131   fits, margin 29  <- the impossible one
  24h + 22-char-token link + fee     185   OVER BY 25       <- the withdrawn figure

SO THE TWO READINGS OF 'TRUNCATE THE HMAC TOKEN TO 22 CHARACTERS' BOTH FAIL.
Truncating the SIGNATURE to 22 keeps the design intact and leaves the message 130
over. Truncating the WHOLE TOKEN to 22 produces R11's arithmetic and destroys the
payload.

WHY THE PAYLOAD CANNOT LEAVE THE TOKEN. link-token.ts:12-16 states it as a
deliberate design decision, not an accident: tenant_id is carried INSIDE the
signed token 'rather than discovering it from the appointment id' so that 'the
public route can enter tenant-scoped RLS context directly from a value WE signed,
with no global/cross-tenant lookup (hard architecture rule #3)'. The same comment
already names the cost: 'The cost is a longer token - fine for email, which is
why the SMS reminder points to the phone instead of this link.' R11 proposed to
reverse a trade whose own comment had already predicted this outcome.

AND action_token_consumptions CANNOT SERVE AS THE STORE. Checked rather than
assumed: 0054 writes it at REDEMPTION, its primary key is token_hash under a
CHECK (~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'), it carries no exp and no scope column, and it has an
append-only trigger. Pre-inserting at issue time would make every token read as
already spent. A short-code table is therefore a NEW table, which is a migration,
which is what reason (b) forbids.

THE SEARCH WAS DONE BEFORE THE HALT, so 'impossible' is a measurement and not a
shrug. The most aggressive stateless packing available - raw 16-byte uuids rather
than hex-with-dashes, a 4-byte epoch, a 1-byte scope, HMAC truncated to 128 bits,
no JSON - gives 53 bytes and a 71-char token KEEPING tenant_id, which is 180
chars and 20 over with the fee OFF. DROPPING tenant_id gives 37 bytes and a
50-char token, 159 chars and margin 1 with the fee OFF, and 213 chars and 53 over
the moment the fee line arms. The only variant that fits anything violates hard
architecture rule #3, and it still dies when the fee notice is armed.

=== HIGH VALUE, AND THE REASON THIS CARD IS WORTH READING AFTER IT CLOSED: ===

characters and FITS ONE GSM-7 SEGMENT, with 7 characters of margin. No shortening
of anything is required for the fee line to ship.

THAT MARGIN IS PINNED BY EXACT-EQUALITY ASSERTIONS, not by an upper bound:
apps/web/lib/reminders/fee-notice.test.ts:173-183 asserts base.length toBe(99),
SMS_SEGMENT_LIMIT - base.length toBe(61), withFee.length toBe(153), and
SMS_SEGMENT_LIMIT - withFee.length toBe(7). An exact equality fails on a copy
edit in EITHER direction, so the margin cannot be spent silently and cannot be
gained silently either.

and that shortfall existed only to make room for the confirm link. With R11

TIMING: THE BACKFILL RUNS AFTER LAUNCH-03, NEVER BEFORE. The reason is simple and it is why this sat mis-prioritised: THE PATIENTS WHOSE HOME CLINIC MATTERS DO NOT EXIST IN THE DATABASE YET. Roughly ten thousand real patients arrive from the vendor at LAUNCH-03 carrying their own visit history, and that is the moment the derivation has inputs. Backfilling the current test rows has no value at all - it would derive a home clinic for a handful of fixtures and prove nothing about the rule.

THE RULE WHEN IT RUNS: MOST-FREQUENT location, tie-break MOST-RECENT. primaryLocationId stays STAFF-EDITABLE in the ficha as an override, so a wrong derivation is correctable by reception without an engineer.

Decision C's SERVICE preselection uses priorCompletedServiceId (booking.ts:521), most-recent-completed, and that precedent DOES NOT TRANSFER. Recency is a good signal for a repeated SERVICE and a weak one for a PLACE: A SINGLE VISIT TO THE OTHER CLINIC WHILE TRAVELLING MUST NOT RELOCATE A PATIENT. Most-frequent is stable against that; the most-recent tie-break only decides genuine fifty-fifty cases, where recency is the best remaining signal.

Null renders the clinic choice unpreselected, which is correct Decision C behaviour and is the ONLY path that runs until this card does. RAISED 2026-08-11 by the external AI partner's sub-processor audit of our Sentry
configuration. Owner-dispatched as a one-off, no wave dependency.

THE AUDIT'S CONCLUSION IS RIGHT. ITS STATED MECHANISM IS WRONG, AND THE
DIFFERENCE CHANGES HOW URGENT THIS IS.

What the audit claimed: the Sentry Node SDK enables the localVariables
integration BY DEFAULT, so in-scope variables are attached to stack frames, so
the clinical payload is leaving for Sentry today.

What the installed SDK actually does (@sentry/node-core 10.54.0, re-derived from
node_modules, not from memory):
  - localVariablesIntegration() IS in the default list, build/cjs/sdk/index.js:46.
  - It is INERT unless includeLocalVariables is true. Its own setup() returns
    before installing the debugger hook, at
    build/cjs/integrations/local-variables/local-variables-sync.js:190-193.
  - We have never set that option. So no frame.vars are populated today and
    nothing has leaked through this path. REGISTERED IS NOT ARMED.

WHAT IS TRUE, AND IS WHY THIS SHIPPED ANYWAY. Nothing in the repo pinned any of
it. Before this card there was no beforeSend, no scrubber and no integration
override anywhere - verified by grep for beforeSend|localVariables|sendDefaultPii
across the whole repo, zero hits outside node_modules. The exposure is one
config line away, from us or from an SDK default change.

THE EXPOSED PATH IS REAL. apps/web/lib/clinical/review.ts:223-224 calls
projectAiPayloadOntoFichaFields on row.data and throws ClinicalError inside the
same transaction closure (line 242 among others). row.data holds the AI
partner's full clinical payload under _aiIngestionRaw, written at
apps/web/lib/ingestion/store.ts:91. A frame-locals capture on that throw is a
patient's clinical record in Sentry, which CLAUDE.md rule 7 forbids without
qualification.

WHAT SHIPPED - three config files plus one tested module:
  1. sendDefaultPii: false stated EXPLICITLY on all three Sentry.init calls
     (sentry.server.config.ts, sentry.edge.config.ts, instrumentation-client.ts).
     It already defaults to false. The point is that a future SDK default change
     cannot flip it silently.
  2. Server config only: includeLocalVariables: false AND the LocalVariables
     integration filtered out of the defaults. Two readings of "disable it" -
     the gate the integration reads, and the integration that reads the gate.
  3. Server config only: beforeSend: stripFrameVars. A SECOND layer that does
     not depend on 2. Total by design - no allowlist, no in_app check, no
     condition - because an allowlist is a list of things someone remembered,
     and this payload's shape is defined by an external partner's contract.
  4. The scrubber lives at apps/web/lib/observability/sentry-scrub.ts, not
     inline in the config, for a reason worth recording: importing the config to
     test it would run Sentry.init as a side effect. Its test had to live under
     lib/ for a second reason - apps/web/vitest.config.ts collects only lib/**,
     app/** and components/**, so a test placed beside the root config would
     have been SILENTLY NEVER RUN. That is the exact trap W13-01 and W13-02 each
     hit and each widened the include glob to escape.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: tracesSampleRate unchanged, no integration added,
review.ts unchanged. The edge runtime gets sendDefaultPii only - LocalVariables
is a Node-inspector mechanism and has no edge equivalent.

GATES, all four green locally before the PR: pnpm lint 0 errors (12 pre-existing
warnings, none in the new files), pnpm typecheck 10/10 tasks, pnpm test 1921
passed across 200 files, pnpm build 4/4 tasks. The new test is proven
LOAD-BEARING by mutation, not by passing: deleting the single "delete
frame.vars" line fails 3 of its 6 assertions.

cards.title: The ficha projection treats an explicit null as a filled value, and the partner's strict schema is about to send nulls for every unfilled field

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-11 in PR #859, squashed to 652d1bd. Verified an ancestor of origin/main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 652d1bd origin/main` exits 0). STATUS SET 2026-08-18 ON THE OWNER'S RULING, seven days late.

=== THE CARD WAS FALSE, AND IT IS THE FIFTH IN THE FAMILY WITH A NEW VARIANT. ===
The session that BUILT this wrote the full narrative into the card's notes - 'WHAT SHIPPED, two guards', 'GATES, all four green', the mutation proof for both guards - and then never set `status` or `evidence`. So the card read `in_flight` with `evidence: null` while the work sat on main.

WHAT MAKES IT A NEW VARIANT, and it is the part worth keeping: the previous four carried a false `todo` while CITING PRs, so the reconciler's pr-state rules could see them. This one CITES NOTHING. `citedPrs()` reads `evidence.ref` and only that - deliberately, because notes narrate and name adjacent PRs while evidence.ref is the only field whose PR numbers are a CLAIM. With evidence null the function returns [] and every PR rule hits `if (cited.length === 0) continue`. The card claims no gate either, so gate-claim is silent too. IT WAS INVISIBLE TO EVERY RULE.

The reconciler's own header predicted this shape: 'a check that only compares cited PR numbers against merge state would have stayed silent on them forever.' The new evidence-null rule authorised 2026-08-18 closes it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON main, re-derived before this flip rather than taken from the card's own notes: apps/web/lib/clinical/ficha-medica.ts carries BOTH guards with their documented asymmetry - the presence guard skips undefined, null and whitespace-only strings; the clobber guard treats ONLY undefined and null at a field path as unset, so an empty string a reviewer deliberately left is never refilled. ficha-medica.test.ts carries 28 tests including a dedicated 'null and empty-value hardening' block.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-11 by the owner. AMBER lane, isolated card, no loop dependency.

THE COLLISION, WHICH IS A CONTRACT DISAGREEMENT AND NOT A BUG ON EITHER SIDE.
The external AI partner is moving extraction to a STRICT JSON schema. A strict
schema declares every property required and expresses an unfilled one as null.
Our standing contract says the opposite: omit unfilled fields, never send nulls.
Both positions are internally coherent and they cannot both hold on the wire.

THE FIX IS ON OUR SIDE, and it is worth having even if the partner never
changes anything. projectAiPayloadOntoFichaFields guarded on
`value === undefined` only, so an explicit null was a PRESENT value: it was
pushed to `projected`, written to the ficha field path, and the field then
rendered as filled-with-null rather than empty-and-editable. Same for an empty
or whitespace-only string.

WHAT SHIPPED, two guards that are DELIBERATELY NOT SYMMETRIC:

  1. PRESENCE (the incoming side). Skip when the raw value is undefined, null,
     or a string that is empty or whitespace-only. Skipped keys push to
     `absent` exactly as an omitted key always did - no new code path, no new
     return shape.

  2. CLOBBER (the existing side). Treat undefined AND null at a field path as
     unset and therefore writable. An EMPTY STRING IS NOT UNSET. A reviewer who
     deliberately cleared a field left "" behind, and refilling it from the raw
     payload would silently undo a clinical decision.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT AND IT WILL LOOK LIKE A BUG TO THE NEXT READER.
Blank arriving FROM the AI is noise; blank sitting AT a field path is a human
who meant it. Both the code comment and the doc comment say so explicitly,
because the obvious "cleanup" is to unify the two guards and that would be a
data-loss change.

NOT TOUCHED, as instructed: FICHA_MEDICA_AI_KEYS, readFichaKeyPath,
writeFichaKeyPath, review.ts, and the ingestion path. Verified no ripple:
review.ts:223 destructures only `data` from the result and ignores
`projected`/`absent`, so tightening what counts as present changes nothing
downstream.

ONE PRE-EXISTING DOC DEFECT FIXED IN PASSING: the function's @returns described
the third return field as `missing`. It has always been named `absent`.

GATES, all four green: pnpm lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, test 1930 passed
across 200 web files (was 1921; +9 new), build 4/4. BOTH guards proven
LOAD-BEARING BY MUTATION, not by passing: reverting the presence guard to
undefined-only fails 4 of the new tests; making the clobber guard also treat ""
as unset fails the asymmetry test specifically.

NO MIGRATION. Pure function, no schema change.

cards.title: A key the partner sends that maps to no ficha field is silently discarded - including, once, an alarm-symptom answer

evidence.ref:
BUILD HALF DONE 2026-08-19. PR #951 MERGED, squashed to 6e1f231.

THE ALLOWLIST IS DERIVED WITH split(".")[0], which is the trap the card named: FICHA_MEDICA_AI_KEYS holds twelve DOTTED PATHS and only seven distinct top-level keys, so comparing against the twelve would flag `systems_review` - the most important container in the payload - as drift on every record. The negative arm restores exactly that mistake and fails the two tests that describe it.

ONE LEVEL DEEP into systems_review per the card's recommendation, reported dotted. ANNOTATES, NEVER BLOCKS. KEY NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES (rule 7), asserted.

IT RENDERS ON THE REVIEWER'S SCREEN rather than as a third return field. `projected` and `absent` have been returned all along and read by nobody; a third ignored field would have been one more invisible signal - the same defect one layer up.

NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL PAYLOAD. The card says the first step should be to pull one; no terminal may read production, so this was built from the contract in code. The owner-reported instance (two unmapped keys, one an alarm symptom) is recorded as reported.

cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-11 BY OWNER INSTRUCTION, EXPLICITLY NOT IMPLEMENTED IN THE SAME
DISPATCH AS AI-01. Do not fold it into that PR.

THE DEFECT. projectAiPayloadOntoFichaFields walks FICHA_MEDICA_AI_KEYS and
copies what it finds. It never looks the other way. A key the partner puts in
`_aiIngestionRaw` that maps to no ficha field is stored verbatim under
`_aiIngestionRaw` (so it is not lost) and reaches NO field, NO editor surface
and NO reviewer's eye. It is invisible, not absent, and those are different.

WHY IT IS PRIORITY HIGH RATHER THAN HOUSEKEEPING. Owner-reported: the partner
produced a payload in which two keys sat physically in the payload while never
reaching a ficha field, AND ONE OF THEM WAS AN ALARM-SYMPTOM ANSWER. Not
verified against a stored payload by this session - recorded as reported, and
the first implementation step should be to pull a real payload and confirm the
shape before building anything.

WHAT TO SURFACE. Top-level keys of `_aiIngestionRaw` that are NOT in the
allowlist, NOT `template`, and NOT underscore-prefixed.

  THE ALLOWLIST IS SEVEN KEYS, NOT TWELVE, AND THIS IS THE TRAP IN THIS CARD.
  FICHA_MEDICA_AI_KEYS holds twelve DOTTED PATHS, six of which live under
  `systems_review.*`. The distinct TOP-LEVEL keys are seven:
  consultation_reason, relief_aggravation, clinical_history, systems_review,
  treatment_objectives, treatment_plan, observations.
  Comparing top-level payload keys against the twelve dotted paths would flag
  `systems_review` - the single most important container in the payload - as
  unknown drift on every single record. Derive the allowlist as
  `new Set(FICHA_MEDICA_AI_KEYS.map(k => k.split(".")[0]))`, never hand-write
  it, so it cannot drift from the contract it is checking.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP, none of them decided here:
  - Does drift extend INTO `systems_review`? An unknown nested leaf has the
    same invisibility problem and the same clinical weight. Recommended: yes,
    one level deep, same rule.
  - Where does it surface? The claim-time return value is the cheap answer, but
    `projected`/`absent` are currently ignored by review.ts:223, so a third
    return field would be ignored too. It needs a consumer, or it is another
    invisible signal.
  - Does it block the claim or annotate it? Recommended: ANNOTATE, never block.
    A claim that fails because the partner added a key is a worse outage than a
    key that goes unread.
  - PII: an unknown key's VALUE is clinical content. Whatever surfaces it must
    not log the value (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Surface the KEY NAME, never the value.
    See SEC-sentry-frame-vars for the same rule applied to Sentry frames.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. Sits on top of AI-01 cleanly but does not require it.
cards.open_on_purpose:

cards.title: The Supabase email-template guard passes on a COMMENT - the two templates #837 changed are the two it no longer guards

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19. THE FIRST CARD IN THIS SWEEP WHOSE DIAGNOSIS HELD UP EXACTLY AS WRITTEN, which is worth saying because the three before it did not. Re-derived from main at d8275a8 before building: reset-password.html:10 and invite.html:10 each carry ONE occurrence of ConfirmationURL and in each it is inside the warning comment; both files interpolate TokenHash twice; REQUIRED_VARIABLE still mapped both to ConfirmationURL; and the assertion read the raw bytes.

RED BEFORE GREEN, per the card's own instruction and standing rule 11.
  RED: comment strip in place, mapping UNCHANGED -> 2 failed | 50 passed. The two failures are exactly reset-password.html and invite.html, named in the output. Nothing else moved.
  GREEN: mapping corrected to TokenHash for those two -> 52 passed.
A fix that only ever ran green would have repeated the mistake it corrects.

THE STRIP IS SCOPED TO ONE ASSERTION ON PURPOSE. The suite's other checks are about PROSE - stock English, brand teal, clinic names, malformed entities - and a comment cannot satisfy those in a way that matters. Stripping the whole file would have been a bigger change with no argument behind it.

ONE ARM BEYOND THE CARD'S SPEC, added deliberately and flagged rather than slipped in. The corrected mapping catches a REVERT: delete the TokenHash link, put ConfirmationURL back, and the presence assertion fails. It does NOT catch a template carrying BOTH - a well-meaning "fallback" ConfirmationURL added beside the working link keeps TokenHash present and sails through. That is the exact shape the files' own comment forbids and the card names as the risk ("the property a future simplification would undo"), and nothing enforced it. A FORBIDDEN_VARIABLE arm now refuses ConfirmationURL and RedirectTo in the BODY of those two templates. A presence assertion proves the mechanism EXISTS; only the refusal proves the wrong shape is REFUSED.

NEGATIVE CONTROL FOR THE NEW ARM, run separately: injecting one body-level ConfirmationURL into reset-password.html fails exactly that assertion with the intended message (1 failed | 57 passed). The template was restored byte-for-byte afterwards and git diff on supabase/ is empty.

THE TEMPLATES WERE NOT EDITED, which the card required in capitals. Only apps/web/lib/auth/supabase-email-templates.test.ts changed.

Gates: pnpm lint 0 errors, pnpm typecheck 11/11, pnpm test 232 files / 8 tasks, pnpm build 4/4. Suite 58 passed.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-11 BY AMBER during LE-staff-no-forgot-password recon, from a
code read. Not found by a failing test - the test is green, and that is the
defect. CARDED, NOT FIXED: it needs a ticket, and this is it.

THE GUARD. apps/web/lib/auth/supabase-email-templates.test.ts:24-34 declares
REQUIRED_VARIABLE, mapping each Supabase Auth template to the GoTrue variable
it MUST interpolate, and :98-102 asserts read(f) contains that string. Five of
the six are mapped to {{ .ConfirmationURL }}.

WHAT #837 CHANGED. LE-auth-recovery-deadend moved reset-password.html and
invite.html OFF {{ .ConfirmationURL }} and onto
?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=recovery|invite pointing at our own inert
landing page. That variable is now ABSENT from both files as an interpolation.

WHY THE TEST STILL PASSES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE FINDING. The assertion reads the
raw file with readFileSync and DOES NOT STRIP COMMENTS. The literal string
{{ .ConfirmationURL }} survives in both files inside the HTML comment that warns
against using it - reset-password.html:10 and invite.html:10, verbatim: 'Do not
"simplify" to {{ .ConfirmationURL }} or {{ .RedirectTo }} - both reintroduce a
fixed bug.' grep -c ConfirmationURL returns 1 for each file, and in each the
single hit is that warning.

SO THE TWO TEMPLATES WHOSE SHAPE ACTUALLY CHANGED ARE THE TWO THE GUARD NO
LONGER GUARDS. It would pass on a reset-password.html that had been reverted to
the old spend-on-GET shape, or to Supabase stock structure, for as long as the
warning comment survived the edit - and a reverting edit is exactly the edit
that would delete the interpolation and keep the comment.

SEVERITY IS MEDIUM, SAID HONESTLY. Nothing is broken in production today: both
committed templates are correct, and the OTHER assertions in that suite (pt-PT
lang, no stock English, brand teal, two clinics, no emoji, well-formed entities)
still bite, because they assert on prose that no comment carries. What is lost
is the one assertion that pins the LINK SHAPE, which is the property #837
existed to fix and the property a future 'simplification' would undo.

stripped and the mapping still pointing at {{ .ConfirmationURL }}, the suite must

DO NOT EDIT THE TEMPLATES. They are correct. The test is what is wrong.

cards.title: A SKIP INSIDE A PASSING SHARD IS A GUARD THAT CANNOT FAIL, and it is invisible without instrumentation - 39 suites can do it today. Plus the 123 counted assertions

evidence.ref:
docs/recon/ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep-counts.md, which now carries the counts (2026-08-11, from 56d54ce) AND the triage of all three categories plus fixtures (2026-08-19, read against d8275a8 / 5a8197f / 9bc69e0).

123 SUSPECTS RESOLVED TO ONE REAL DEFECT.
  (A) self-mocking, 24 hits  -> ZERO. 14 are the card's own excluded side-effect sinks; 5 mock ../auth/context, which is MANDATORY here; the other 5 were read individually and all drive their mock as an INPUT.
  (B) unstripped comments, 25 hits -> ONE real, fixed as LE-vacuous-template-guard, plus FIVE hardened pre-emptively in #965. 9 of the 25 parse JSON and could never have been defects.
  (C) no negative arm, 74 hits -> ZERO. 43 are E2E specs, 17 have modules with no refusal path, 4 were candidates and all four refuse via error codes and discriminated results the detector cannot see.
  FIXTURES -> the known instance is CLOSED and the class is now UNCONSTRUCTIBLE in the database: the fixture is fixed, 0061's EXCLUDE constraint is real, and packages/db/tests/no-double-confirmed.test.ts tests the constraint itself.

THE ONE LESSON ALL FOUR PRODUCED, and it is worth more than the number: a SHAPE-MATCH CANNOT DISTINGUISH DOING THE SUSPICIOUS THING FROM BEING ABOUT THE SUSPICIOUS THING. migration-syntax's subject IS the comment delimiters; double-booked-surface's subject IS the forbidden state; a driven mock is an INPUT, not an answer; and this codebase's refusals are error codes rather than booleans. Four categories, four different mechanical reasons, one mistake underneath. THE HEADER'S OWN WARNING - "every hit needs a human read before it is called vacuous" - was load-bearing rather than cautious boilerplate.

WHAT THIS CARD DOES NOT CLOSE, carded rather than absorbed: ACC-visibility-assertions-unswept (the population that passes falsely as its ORDINARY behaviour, never swept) and ACC-fixture-forbidden-state-sweep (the invariant set beyond double-confirmed is not enumerated). Closing this card on a claim to have covered those would be the exact defect it exists to remove.

cards.notes:
################################################################
# BOTH SWEEP FINDINGS RESOLVED 2026-08-18, BY OWNER RULING.
################################################################

=== THE STORAGE SUITE: OPTION B, DELETE THE LIVE HALF ===
Owner ruling. storage-signed-url.integration.test.ts keeps its three pure
path-derivation tests, which need no network and run on every PR. The gated
upload-sign-download round-trip is GONE.

THE REASONING, recorded because it is a trade rather than a cleanup:
  A SUITE THAT HAS NEVER RUN IS NOT PROTECTION, and one that LOOKS like
  protection is worse than none - it is the exact currency this card exists to
  remove. This one had never run since it was written.
  WIRING IT UP WOULD HAVE COST MORE THAN IT PAID. It needs
  SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY available to a CI job, which widens the credential
  surface TWO WEEKS BEFORE A PLANNED ROTATION. Spending credential surface to
  buy back a test nobody has missed is the wrong direction at the wrong moment.

THE COVERAGE IS REASSIGNED, NOT ABANDONED. The live round-trip is a supervised
sitting item on LAUNCH-01, where a real credential is already in the room and
under supervision. That is the same shape as the OTP canary: a check that needs
a live secret belongs in a session with a human, not in a runner.

The deletion is documented IN THE FILE, at length, including why it was never
run and why the workflow's own glob fix did not catch it. A deleted suite that
leaves no trace is how the same gap gets rebuilt.

=== THE REQUIRED LIST IS NOW DERIVED. RECON-02. ===
assert-rls-executed.mjs gains a SECOND pass that inverts the question. The
18-entry allowlist stays and still hard-requires what it names; the new pass
asks whether ANYTHING in the three DB-gated reports failed to run, so every
suite is in scope the moment it appears in a report.

WHAT THE ALLOWLIST DID AND DID NOT COVER, since deleting it would have been
wrong: if DATABASE_URL vanished, all 48 suites would skip together and the 18
would redden the job, so the ENV failure mode was always covered. What was not
covered is an UNLISTED suite being renamed, deleted, or gaining a second skip
condition while the other 17 still pass. Eight DB-gated suites were unlisted,
including guest-match.db.test.ts.

IT MEASURES THE REPORT, NOT THE SOURCE, and that is the load-bearing choice.
The obvious implementation greps the tree for `skipIf(` and requires every
match. IT WAS TRIED FIRST AND IT IMMEDIATELY MATCHED A DOC COMMENT - the very
comment written to explain the deleted suite above. That is criterion F at the
tooling level: matching a MENTION rather than a USE, the same shape as the
assertion that matched an import instead of the JSX element. The vitest JSON
report cannot make that mistake, because a test either ran or it did not.

THE SWEEP NEARLY COMMITTED ITS OWN DEFECT TWICE IN ONE PASS - once in the
38-unguarded miscount corrected below, and once here. Both times the error was
measuring a PROXY (a list, a text match) instead of the THING (whether suites
run). That is worth more than either fix.

VERIFIED BY DRY RUN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, per the atomic condition rule F set:

  "@deprecated This option is ignored. locator.isVisible() does not wait for the
   element to become visible and returns immediately."

So the probe answered from whatever the DOM held at that instant. Every reading
that said "absent" came back FASTER THAN A PAGE CAN PAINT:

  run 31635017752   391ms   absent
  run 31641934973   ~400ms  absent to reception AND to the owner
  run 31649767622   443ms   absent   (attempt 1)
  run 31649767622  1683ms   PRESENT  (attempt 2, same commit, same seed)
  run 31651759598   548ms   PRESENT  (attempt 1, with a probe that waits)

THE PRODUCT WAS CORRECT THROUGHOUT. The row was always there.

=== WHY IT COST SO MUCH ===
THE THREE "INDEPENDENT SURFACES" WERE ONE BROKEN INSTRUMENT CALLED THREE TIMES.
Reception, the owner viewer and the patient's own appointment list all reported
no row, and their agreement was read as corroboration. It was one probe, three
times. That apparent corroboration is what made a TEST defect look like a PRODUCT

be CANCELLED, and a launch gate held open across five sessions.

=== THE RULE THIS ADDS, AND IT GENERALISES PAST PLAYWRIGHT ===
A DEPRECATED OPTION THAT IS SILENTLY IGNORED TURNS A WAITING PROBE INTO A RACE.
PIN AND CHECK THE API SURFACE OF ANY TOOL AN ASSERTION DEPENDS ON.

Read the installed types, not the tutorial and not memory. isVisible({timeout})
reads at the call site EXACTLY like a check that waits, and the call site is what
gets reviewed. Nothing in the diff, the lint or the type-check was wrong.

string|null, test.skip(), .catch(() => {}) and ?? e.kind were all written BY THIS

would never have found it. That is why the rule is about the tool's API surface
rather than about our own conventions.

becameVisible() in apps/web/e2e/sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts: waitFor({state:

=== CRITERION C ADDED 2026-08-12, FROM LOOP 7. THE FIRST TWO CAME FROM LOOP 6's
    CITATION AUDIT; THIS ONE CAME FROM AN ASSERTION I WROTE AND THEN CAUGHT. ===

CRITERION C - AN ASSERTION OVER STRIPPED SOURCE MUST BE PROVEN TO SURVIVE
STRIPPING.

Comment-stripping is what makes a structural test real: without it, a file that
merely DISCUSSES a guard passes. But the same `strip()` that removes comments
also blanks STRING AND TEMPLATE LITERALS - and in this codebase template literals
are exactly where SQL lives.

THE CONCRETE CASE. sync-single-source.test.ts asserted that the patient slot route
contains no query of its own, as `expect(src).not.toMatch(/select ... from/i)`
over the STRIPPED source. It was UNFALSIFIABLE. The negative arm inserted a real
`getDbAdmin().execute(\`select id from appointments\`)` into the route and the
assertion DID NOT REDDEN, because strip() had already blanked the template literal
the SQL was written in. It was rewritten to match query-builder CALL SHAPES -
`db.execute(`, `getDbAdmin(`, `sql\``, `.from(` - which are identifiers and
survive stripping. Both arms then reddened.

HOW TO TRIAGE ON IT: for every assertion that runs over transformed source, ask
what the transform REMOVES, and check the assertion is not looking for exactly
that. The three transforms in this repo's structural tests each have a blind spot:
  strip comments      -> blind to anything only stated in prose (intended)
  blank literals      -> BLIND TO SQL, URLs, i18n keys, error strings
  line-level comment  -> blind to a construct hidden inside a block comment
An assertion whose subject lives in a blanked region cannot fail. It is the purest
form of the guard that cannot fail, because it looks MORE rigorous than the naive
version.

AND THE GENERAL LESSON, which is the reason all three criteria exist: THIS WAS
CAUGHT ONLY BY RUNNING THE ARM. Reading the assertion back did not reveal it, and
it was written by the same session that had just audited 22 citations for exactly
this class of defect. A negative arm is not paperwork; it is the only thing that
distinguishes an assertion from a sentence.
