EVERY GATE THIS PROJECT HAS PASSED RESTS ON THIS SUITE, and the number of assertions in it that cannot fail was unknown until now. It is now bounded.

DETECTION IS MECHANICAL AND THE COUNTS ARE AN UPPER BOUND ON SUSPICION, NOT PROVEN DEFECTS. Each category is a regex-level proxy for the SHAPE that produced the three known cases. Category (A) in particular has known false positives: stubbing a pure side-effect module such as ./audit is legitimate and matches the same pattern. Every hit needs a human read before it is called vacuous. Saying so here is the difference between a finding and a scare number.

TWO CI DEFECTS COUNTED SEPARATELY, both shipped in #861, and both the LIMIT CASE of the class - a suite that cannot run cannot fail:
  1. .github/workflows/db-tests.yml ran the apps/web DB step against redeem.db.test.ts BY EXPLICIT PATH. pedido-confirm.db.test.ts would have been committed, reviewed, merged and NEVER EXECUTED. Now globs .db.test.ts.
  2. .github/scripts/assert-rls-executed.mjs did not hard-require pedido-confirm.db.test.ts, so a silent skip would have reported green. Now hard-required.

RECOMMENDED TRIAGE ORDER, BY BLAST RADIUS. This is a recommendation, not work performed:
  FIRST - the (A) hits on paths that gate CLINICAL or SCHEDULING writes: pedido-confirm.test.ts, records.hard-delete.test.ts, actions.hard-delete.test.ts, patients/actions.hard-delete.test.ts. A vacuous guard on a delete or a booking is the one that costs a patient something.
  SECOND - the (B) hits that assert on TEMPLATES or MIGRATIONS: supabase-email-templates, private-notes-template-guard, migration-syntax, journal-sync. These are the ones where the asserted string can live in a comment, which is precisely how case 2 above passed.
  THIRD - the (C) hits, largest by count and lowest by severity. Many are legitimately positive-only (a token or palette snapshot has no meaningful negative arm). Triage by whether the module under test has a REFUSAL path at all; if it does and the file has no negative arm, that is the real hit.
  NOT A PRIORITY - (A) hits whose mocked module is purely a side-effect sink (./audit, ./analytics, ./reminders). Mocking those is how the suite stays unit-level.

DO NOT BULK-FIX. A sweep that rewrites 123 files at once cannot be reviewed, and the failure mode of this class is precisely a change nobody could check. Triage in the order above, in small PRs, each proving its guard RED against the pre-fix sha.

=== THE STRONGEST SINGLE EXAMPLE THIS SWEEP HAS, AND A CONSTRAINT FOUND IT
    RATHER THAN THE SWEEP. 2026-08-12. ===

packages/db/tests/appointment-note-present-capture.test.ts seeded TWO CONFIRMED
APPOINTMENTS ON ONE THERAPIST AT ONE IDENTICAL WINDOW - the exact state the
system exists to prevent, sitting in a fixture, for months. Every assertion in
that suite passed against it. Nothing noticed, because nothing was looking.

WHY IT BELONGS TO THIS CARD AND NOT ONLY TO INC-08. A guard that cannot fail
and a fixture that constructs the forbidden state are the same defect wearing
different clothes: in both cases a test is GREEN over a condition it was
supposed to be sensitive to. The 123 instances counted here are assertions that
cannot go red. This is the mirror image - a SETUP that should never have been
constructible, and which every downstream assertion then agreed with.

IT WAS FOUND BY 0061's EXCLUDE CONSTRAINT ON ITS FIRST CI RUN, not by a review,
not by this sweep, and not by any of the 385 test files. That is the
transferable lesson and it is uncomfortable: THE SWEEP LOOKS AT ASSERTIONS, AND
THIS DEFECT WAS IN THE FIXTURE. A sweep scoped to expect() calls would have
walked straight past it.

SECOND INSTANCE, SAME RUN: pedido-does-not-block.db.test.ts confirmed a second
pedido onto an already-confirmed window under a comment reading TWO CONFIRMS
STILL CANNOT BOTH SUCCEED. The comment was right and the fixture contradicted
it. It was rewritten to assert the database refusal, which is the same claim one
layer down and no longer contingent on a caller choosing to look.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE SWEEP'S SCOPE WHEN IT RUNS: fixtures are in scope, not
just assertions. The question to ask of every seed block is 'could production
ever contain this?' - and where the answer is no, the fixture is either wrong or
it is documenting a hole nobody has closed.

=== CATEGORY (B) TRIAGED 2026-08-19. THE SECOND TRANCHE IS CLEAN TOO. Full grid in docs/recon/ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep-counts.md. ===
THE RECOMMENDED SECOND TRANCHE NAMED FOUR FILES AND THREE OF THEM COULD NEVER HAVE BEEN DEFECTS. private-notes-template-guard and journal-sync both JSON.parse what they read, and JSON HAS NO COMMENTS. migration-syntax is INVERTED - its subject IS the comment delimiters, it counts /* against */ to prove they balance, so stripping would destroy the property it measures, and it already carries a vacuous-pass guard. The fourth, supabase-email-templates, is the real one and is owned by LE-vacuous-template-guard, now shipped.

WHY THE REGEX OVER-COUNTS, as three conditions rather than one. The detector asks only whether a file reads text and asserts without stripping. THE DEFECT NEEDS THREE THINGS AT ONCE: the read must be TEXT and not JSON.parse; the assertion must be a PRESENCE assertion, because an absence assertion FAILS LOUDLY when a comment matches and that is the safe direction; and the format must have comments the asserted string could plausibly sit in. migration-syntax adds a fourth case the conditions miss - a suite whose SUBJECT is the comments.

THE GRID: 9 of 25 parse JSON and are unreachable; 2 already strip; 4 have no presence assertion; 10 remain as candidates, of which supabase-email-templates is now fixed. A CANDIDATE IS NOT A DEFECT and the nine remaining are listed in the recon doc rather than counted as findings. The three packages/ui tokens*.test.ts suites are the strongest group, because a comment mentioning a hex code in a CSS file is entirely plausible - a claim about where to look, not a finding.

BOTH RECOMMENDED STARTING POINTS WERE ALREADY SAFE. The FIRST tranche was re-derived earlier the same day and found clean; the SECOND is clean for the reasons above. Ten unnamed candidates sat outside the recommendation. The COUNTING was sound; the ORDERING was a guess about severity the reads did not support, and it is the second such guess this sweep has produced. THE CARD STAYS OPEN: categories (A) and (C) are untouched, fixtures are in scope per the 2026-08-12 note, and nine (B) candidates remain unread.

=== (A) AND (C) TRIAGED 2026-08-19. BOTH COME OUT AT ZERO. Full grid and reasoning in docs/recon/ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep-counts.md. ===

(A) SELF-MOCKING, 24 HITS, ZERO DEFECTS. 14 are the side-effect sinks this card's own notes already exclude. 5 mock ../auth/context, which is MANDATORY here rather than optional - it opens the DB scope, so a unit test that does NOT mock it opens a real connection, which is precisely the defect ACC-preselection-spec-flaky found when a stub scoped to one describe block let two suites connect for real. FAILING to self-mock is the bug there. The remaining 5 were read one by one and all drive their mock as an INPUT.

THE CRITERION IS RESTATED, and this is the part worth keeping: "mocks a module it also imports" is not the defect, it is the normal shape of a unit test. THE DEFECT IS MOCKING THE MODULE WHOSE BEHAVIOUR THE ASSERTION IS ABOUT, WITHOUT DRIVING IT. A driven mock is the test's INPUT; a vacuous one is the test's ANSWER.

THE FOUNDING CASE'S REMEDY WAS ADDITIVE, WHICH THIS CARD DID NOT RECORD. pedido-confirm.test.ts:42 is cited as instance 1 of the whole class. It was never changed and never needed to be: pedido-confirm.db.test.ts exists, its header names that exact vi.mock("./conflict") as the reason it was written, and it runs the REAL findConflictsForWindow against public.appointment_conflicts() over 8 tests including two simultaneous confirms racing for one slot. The unit test proves orchestration; the DB suite proves the query. Both are correct.

(C) NO NEGATIVE ARM, 74 HITS, ZERO DEFECTS. 43 are E2E specs with no colocated module under test, 17 have modules with no refusal path to assert against, 10 are not colocated, and 4 were real candidates. All four read clean, for ONE shared reason.

THE DETECTOR'S NEGATIVE-ARM VOCABULARY ASSUMES REFUSALS ARE BOOLEANS OR THROWS - .not., rejects., toThrow, toBe(false), toBe(0), toHaveLength(0), toBeNull, toBeUndefined. THIS CODEBASE EXPRESSES REFUSALS AS ERROR CODES AND DISCRIMINATED RESULT OBJECTS: toBe("invalid_slug"), toEqual({ ok: false }), toEqual({ ok: false, error: "unknown_therapy" }). That is the BETTER style and one this repo argues for explicitly - sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts documents choosing a discriminated result over string | null after four distinct failures all returned the same null. SO THE SUITES THAT REFUSE MOST CAREFULLY ARE EXACTLY THE ONES THE DETECTOR CANNOT SEE REFUSING.

TWO DEFECTS IN THE TRIAGE ITSELF, recorded rather than quietly fixed. The E2E specs were inflating (C) from 4 to 14: deriving "the module under test" by stripping .test. from the filename matches NOTHING on a *.spec.ts, so the path came back unchanged, the file existed, and each spec was scanned AGAINST ITSELF. And the refusal-detector matched a COMMENT - invoicexpress/profile.ts's only hit is line 41, inside a doc comment reading "rejects issuing without one". Criterion F, in the instrument, third instance in one session.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS CARD, and it is now small and concrete: NINE (B) CANDIDATES UNREAD - base.test.ts, consent-terms-axis, declaracao-pdf, approval-packet, fee-notice, pedido-confirm, and the three packages/ui tokens* suites, which are the strongest group because a comment mentioning a hex code in a CSS file is entirely plausible. Plus FIXTURES, which the 2026-08-12 note added to scope and which no category covers: the sweep looks at ASSERTIONS, and appointment-note-present-capture.test.ts seeded two confirmed appointments on one therapist at one window - a SETUP that should never have been constructible, found by 0061's exclude constraint rather than by any of the 385 test files. PRIORITY DROPPED HIGH -> MEDIUM: the alarming number is gone and what is left is a reading task, not a hunt.

=== THE (B) TAIL READ AND CLOSED 2026-08-19. FIVE SUITES HARDENED, NONE WAS VACUOUS YET. ===
All nine remaining (B) candidates were read. FIVE carried a PRESENCE assertion on a raw text body that a comment could satisfy, and all five are now stripped. FOUR needed nothing: base.test.ts and consent-terms-axis.test.ts carry no toContain presence assertion at all, pedido-confirm.test.ts's source scan is an ABSENCE assertion (the safe direction), and approval-packet.test.ts reads a docs markdown packet whose asserted strings are section headings and flag names rather than anything a comment would carry.

NOT ONE OF THE FIVE WAS ACTUALLY VACUOUS TODAY, and that was checked rather than assumed before anything changed: across the three packages/ui tokens suites, 55 asserted literals were tested against the comment-stripped theme.css and ZERO were satisfied only by a comment. THIS REMOVES THE CLASS RATHER THAN FIXING AN INSTANCE, which is the honest description.

THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS IN theme.css ITSELF and is why this was worth doing rather than noting: line 307 reads "SPEC 3.1 lists #6E7A89, but that is 4.37:1 on white ..." - a REJECTED value, recorded in a comment, deliberately absent from every declaration. Assert that hex and the guard passes on the rejection notice. The tokens suites assert bare hexes; the two sets do not currently overlap, and the reason they do not is coincidence rather than design.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each moving a real thing into a comment and proving the stripped guard fails where the raw one passed:
  theme.css - #45B9A7 removed from all 4 declarations, left in one comment. Raw css contains it (old assertion PASSES); stripped does not (new assertion FAILS). Demonstrated both directions, not just the failure.
  dispatch.ts - the shouldRenderFeeNotice( call renamed, the name left in a comment. The guard fails naming dispatch.ts. NOTE the comment three lines above that assertion in the test itself says "it must call shouldRenderFeeNotice" - the defect was reachable from the file's own prose.
  declaracao-pdf.ts - model.responsavel renamed in both real uses, left in a comment reading "always use model.responsavel, never a hardcoded name" - exactly the comment a fix like this leaves behind.
All three production files were restored byte-for-byte; git status shows only test files modified.

ABSENCE ASSERTIONS DELIBERATELY STAY ON THE RAW BODY, and this is the one design decision in the change. A comment naming a superseded hex SHOULD make .not.toContain fail: that is the direction it is safe to be wrong in, and moving those to the stripped body would quietly narrow what they refuse.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS CARD: FIXTURES ONLY. All three categories are now read - (A) 24 hits zero defects, (B) 25 hits one real and fixed plus five hardened, (C) 74 hits zero defects. The fixture question is the one no category covers and it has the worst instance this project has had: appointment-note-present-capture.test.ts seeded TWO CONFIRMED APPOINTMENTS on one therapist at one identical window, the exact state the system exists to prevent, and it was found by 0061's exclude constraint rather than by any of the 385 test files. The question to ask of every seed block is "could production ever contain this?".

cards.title: OTP request answers 500 for an unknown tenantId where it answers 204 for a known one, and the route header claims it cannot

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test (api 57 files pass / 5 skipped), pnpm build.

THE CARD'S PRIMARY PREMISE IS FALSE ON main, AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS REF. The card, written 2026-08-11, says the route answers 500 for an unknown tenantId. IT DOES NOT. `store.create` runs inside `requestCode` inside the try/catch that SEC-otp-unassigned-prefix-500 added on 2026-08-13 for an unrelated reason (an unroutable 9x prefix), so the foreign-key violation on patient_otp_codes.tenant_id is caught and the route answers 204 like everything else. Re-derived by reading route.ts, otp.ts and otp-store.ts on main at 06f4c29, not inferred.

THE CARD'S RECOMMENDED OPTION 1 IS THEREFORE MOOT TOO. It recommended narrowing the header's completeness claim to say what was true. The claim - 'the only distinguishable outcomes are a malformed number (400) and rate limiting (429)' - is true again as written, because the third outcome the card found no longer exists.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY STILL WRONG, and it is smaller and real: NOTHING HELD THE 204 THERE. The behaviour was correct by coincidence - one card's fix covering another card's defect, with no test naming the second case. A revert of that try/catch, or a refactor that moved the store write out of requestCode, would have restored the 500 silently.

AND THE LOG LINE WAS FALSE ON THE BRANCH IT NOW COVERS. The catch said 'The code row was already written and is now live-but-undelivered until its TTL expires' UNCONDITIONALLY. That is true of a failed SEND and it is the OPPOSITE of the truth when the WRITE is what failed: there is no row, because writing it is what threw. A log line on a failure path is a VERDICT PATH - it is read only when something has already gone wrong, by somebody who cannot see the code, and it is the only account they get - so it was sending that person to look for a row that does not exist. Section 1.3, one layer out from the product.

WHAT SHIPPED, three files:
  apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts - a new `OtpCodeNotStored` error class, and requestCode's store.create wrapped so a write failure is nameable by the caller. The driver's own error rides along as `cause`, so the class ADDS a fact rather than replacing a diagnostic. Discriminated by CLASS, never message text, for the reason OtpTransportMisconfigured already gives in place: a string match fails OPEN the day somebody rewords the prose.
  apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts - the catch branches, and the header records that its completeness claim HAS been false once, so the next person to add a branch knows the comment is load-bearing and must be re-read rather than merely preserved.
  the two test files below.

NEITHER BRANCH CHANGES A RESPONSE. Both failures still answer 204 and both are asserted byte-identical to a success - status, body and headers. What is discriminated is the LOG, never the caller's view, so nothing here adds a distinguishable outcome to the endpoint whose whole design is to have as few as possible.

THE CARD'S 'DO NOT FIX IT BY VALIDATING tenantId AGAINST THE TENANTS TABLE' WAS HONOURED and the reasoning is now in the route header rather than only on the card: a lookup keyed on caller-supplied input would contradict the route's own stated property that it performs none, and it would turn tenant existence from an accidental oracle into a deliberate one.

SIX NEW ASSERTIONS IN send-failure.test.ts (14 total in the file, all pass): the write failure answers 204 and not 500 - the regression guard for the card's original finding, which nothing held before; byte-identical to a success; the log says CODE ROW NOT WRITTEN and NOTHING WAS SENT and does NOT match /live-but-undelivered until its TTL/; the driver's PostgresError and the constraint name survive into the log; no phone, no national part, no tenant is logged; and the class discrimination, with a plain Error carrying the constraint name asserted NOT instanceof.

TWO NEW ASSERTIONS IN otp.test.ts, PLUS ONE CORRECTED (20 total, all pass). The corrected one is worth naming: 'does not send when the store write fails' asserted .rejects.toThrow('db down') and the wrapper changed the message, so it went red and was updated to assert the CLASS. The two new ones pull in opposite directions - a failing write must be OtpCodeNotStored with the original error on `cause`, and a failing SEND must NOT be, because that row DID get written. The second is the half that catches a fix which works by labelling everything: if both arrived as OtpCodeNotStored the route would print 'no row exists' over a row that is live and undelivered, the same false sentence pointing the other way.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each restored from the git index and the baseline re-run green afterwards (34/34):
  the log stops branching -> 2 red, both on the write arm.
  requestCode stops naming the write failure -> 2 red in otp.test.ts.
  the route's catch re-throws instead of absorbing, which is the pre-2026-08-13 behaviour -> 9 red, INCLUDING 'answers 204 when the code row cannot be written, not 500'. That is the card's own finding, proven reproducible.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. Nothing on any screen changes; the only observable difference is what a log line says when something has already failed.

SEVERITY UNCHANGED AND STILL LOW, restated so nobody reads this as a security fix: discovering a tenant uuid this way meant guessing 122 bits. No data was exposed and no patient membership leaked. What was wrong was a claim, and now a second claim.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20. THE 500 WAS ALREADY GONE; WHAT SHIPPED IS THE THING THAT KEEPS IT GONE, AND A LOG LINE THAT STOPPED LYING. ===

READ THE EVIDENCE REF FIRST: this card's primary premise was FALSE on main by
the time it was picked up. The 500 it reports was closed on 2026-08-13 by
SEC-otp-unassigned-prefix-500, incidentally, and neither card noticed.

TWO THINGS WERE LEFT AND BOTH ARE NOW BUILT. Nothing held the 204 there - the
behaviour was correct by coincidence, and a revert would have restored the 500
silently. And the catch absorbing the FK violation described it with a sentence
written about a different failure, telling a reader that a code row exists when
writing that row is exactly what failed.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

FOUND 2026-08-11 BY AMBER during the SEC-otp-unauthenticated-sms-pump recon,
from a code read. CARDED, NOT FIXED, on the owner's instruction.

THE FINDING. apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts takes tenantId from
the request body and validates only that it is a non-empty string (:52-54). It
is then passed to requestCode, which inserts a patient_otp_codes row BEFORE the
send (apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts, 'Send AFTER the row exists'). That column
carries REFERENCES tenants(id) (migration 0056:95), so a tenantId that is not a
real tenant raises an FK violation. Nothing on the route catches it, so the
request answers 500 where a real tenantId answers 204.

WHAT IS WRONG IS THE ROUTE HEADER'S CLAIM, not primarily the behaviour. The
header states: 'The only distinguishable outcomes are a malformed number (400,
which reveals nothing about anyone) and rate limiting (429, which an unknown
number hits identically).' There is a third: 500 versus 204, and it
distinguishes a real tenant from a fabricated one.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SAID HONESTLY. This is NOT a practical oracle. Discovering
a tenant uuid this way means guessing a v4 uuid, which is 122 bits of search -
not a shortcut to anything. Nobody's data is exposed and no patient membership
leaks: the tenant set is not the patient set. What is actually wrong is that a
header making a completeness claim about an endpoint's observable outcomes is
the kind of sentence a future reader RELIES ON, and it is not true as written.

SECOND, SMALLER ISSUE ON THE SAME PATH: an unhandled FK violation is a 500 with
a stack, on a public unauthenticated route. It is a database error surfacing as
an application crash rather than a refusal. Nothing leaks (the handler returns
Next's generic 500) but it is noise in Sentry attributable to any caller who
posts a wrong uuid.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and the choice is a real one rather than obvious:
  1. NARROW THE CLAIM. Edit the header to say what is true: three outcomes, and
     why the third does not matter. Cheapest, and honest. Leaves the 500.
  2. CATCH AND FLATTEN. Wrap the requestCode call so an FK violation returns the
     same 204 as everything else. Makes the header true as written. Costs a
     swallowed error - and a swallowed error on a send path is exactly the
     silent-degradation shape PG7 exists to refuse, so it would need a loud log
     naming the variable and nothing else.
RECOMMENDED: 1, plus a log line. The behaviour is not the defect; the claim is.

DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY VALIDATING tenantId AGAINST THE TENANTS TABLE. That adds a
database lookup keyed on caller-supplied input to the endpoint whose entire
design is that it performs NO lookup - route.ts:20-22, 'AND IT NEVER LOOKS THE
PHONE UP. There is no patient query on this path at all.' It would also make
tenant existence a fast, cheap, deliberate oracle rather than an accidental one.

CLOSES ON: either the header narrowed to a true statement, or the outcome
flattened with a loud log. Exit codes pasted, not described.

cards.title: Should the reminder SMS path also refuse landlines? The OTP route now does; the shared normalizer deliberately still does not

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN ON DEPLOYED SCREENS 2026-08-21, VERIFY item 5. The 'Pacientes sem SMS possivel' section is present on /notificacoes with its explanatory line. Merged #994. NOTE ON WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE: the observable half is the LIST. The other half - reminders to landlines no longer being sent - is invisible by design and its only external evidence is a smaller Twilio bill; it is covered by test, not by eye, and was never asked of the sitting.

cards.notes:
=== RULED AND BUILT 2026-08-20. BOTH HALVES. ===

Owner ruled option 2: skip-and-surface. Status is in_flight rather than
shipped because the surface half is a new section on reception's screen and
WF-03 applies. VERIFY-QUEUE item 5.

THE DRIFT GUARD THIS CARD ASKED FOR SHIPPED EARLIER THE SAME DAY (#981) and
is untouched: the two phone.ts copies still agree. This card adds a SECOND,
smaller duplication - the +3512 prefix in SQL - and guards it the same way,
in both directions, rather than leaving a comment.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

=== SPLIT 2026-08-20. THE GUARD IS BUILT; THE RULING IS OWED. ===

BLOCKED ON IVAN, and home_lane moved to in_flight so it lands in his column
and starts the answer-latency clock. The question is written out in full, with
a recommended default, at docs/QUESTIONS.md > Q-LE-REMINDERS-LANDLINE-1.
RECOMMENDED: option 2, skip the send AND surface it to staff. Reasoning on the
question, not here, so there is one copy of it.

THE HALF THAT NEEDED NO RULING IS DONE. The card itself said a drift check
between the two phone.ts copies would be cheap and did not exist. It exists
now, and it takes no position on the ruling - it asserts the two copies AGREE,
whatever they agree on, so that when the answer lands a change to one that
misses the other cannot ship green.

NOTHING ABOUT THE SEND BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. Landline reminders still go to
Twilio and are still billed.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

RAISED 2026-08-11 BY AMBER as the explicit consequence of the owner's fork-2
ruling on SEC-otp-unauthenticated-sms-pump. CARDED, NOT BUILT, by instruction.

WHAT SHIPPED AND WHAT DID NOT. #865 rejects Portuguese geographic numbers (the
2 prefix, which cannot receive SMS) at the OTP REQUEST ROUTE ONLY, through a
new predicate at apps/api/lib/auth/otp-sms-capability.ts. It deliberately did
NOT edit PT_SUBSCRIBER at apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts:19 or its mirror.

WHY THE SHARED NORMALIZER WAS LEFT ALONE, which is the whole of this card:
normalizePhonePT has FIVE live call sites across TWO apps -
  apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts:58
  apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/verify/route.ts:118
  apps/api/lib/notify/clients.ts:133
  apps/web/lib/reminders/dispatch.ts:160
  apps/web/lib/reminders/clients.ts:203
and the last two are the LAUNCH-CRITICAL reminder send path. Additionally
apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts:7 declares apps/web/lib/reminders/phone.ts the
CANONICAL copy and itself a mirror, so editing one silently diverges them and
editing both changes reminder behaviour as a side effect of a security fix.

THE ACTUAL QUESTION, which is a product question and not an engineering one:
when a patient's stored phone is a landline, what SHOULD the 48h/24h reminder
do? Today dispatch.ts:160 normalizes it successfully, hands it to Twilio, and
Twilio bills for a message nobody can receive. The options:
  1. SKIP IT, logging the structured warning dispatch.ts:162-164 already emits
     for an invalid phone (ids only, never the number). Stops paying for
     undeliverable messages. Costs: the clinic loses a reminder it currently
     believes it is sending, silently, unless someone reads the log.
  2. SKIP IT AND SURFACE IT to staff, so reception can ask the patient for a
     mobile. More work, and the right answer if the clinic wants the data
     cleaned rather than the sends suppressed.
  3. LEAVE IT. The spend is bounded by the appointment count, not by an
     attacker, which is the whole difference from the OTP case.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT, stated so nobody promotes it on the security card's
coat-tails: the OTP exposure was unbounded because an UNAUTHENTICATED stranger
chose the numbers. Here the numbers come from the clinic's own patient records
and the volume is bounded by real appointments. This is a data-quality and
small-waste question, not an abuse surface.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE BUILDING: whichever way it goes, the two phone.ts copies
must move TOGETHER or the mirror comment at phone.ts:7 becomes false. A drift
check between them would be a cheap guard and none exists today.

CLOSES ON: an owner or JP ruling on the three options, then the code and a
guard proven red if the ruling is 1 or 2, or this card closed won't-do if 3.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-21 ON THE OWNER'S SCREEN. ===

OBSERVED: the 'Pacientes sem SMS possivel' section is on /notificacoes and reads correctly.

WHAT THAT CLOSES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT, stated so a later reader does not count it as more than it is: the LIST is observed. The suppression itself - a landline reminder no longer being sent - changes nothing on any screen, so there was nothing to observe and nothing was claimed. It is covered by unit test and by the parity test between the SQL filter and isSmsCapablePT.

=== 0061 PROVEN ON A DEPLOYED SCREEN 2026-08-12. B2.3. ===

The constraint was applied to production on 2026-08-12 and its journal recorded. THIS
IS THE SEPARATE THING: it has now been OBSERVED DOING ITS JOB, by the owner, on
the deployed build.

WHAT HE DID: opened the pending pedido at T-B 22/08/2026 11:00 in the agenda
drawer, set Estado to Confirmada over an existing CONFIRMED row on the same
therapist and window, clicked Guardar, got the conflict warning, and then clicked

WHAT HAPPENED: THE WRITE WAS STILL REFUSED, at the database, with the pt-PT
message. The pedido stayed Pendente.

WHY THIS IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE ON THIS CARD. "Guardar mesmo assim" submits
allowConflict: true, and updateAppointment HONOURS it (actions.ts:867-873) - the
application conflict check is SKIPPED BY OPERATOR CHOICE. So this observation
bypasses every application guard and lands on the constraint alone. Before 0061
that path produced a double booking; that is the owner's ruling being overridden
by a button, and it is one of the three mechanisms that produced this incident.
NOW THE DATABASE REFUSES AN OPERATOR WHO INSISTED. That is the ruling
"the override is OVERRULED AT THE DATABASE" observed rather than asserted.

It is also the ONLY row on the entire observation sweep that could not have been
run before tonight's apply. Everything else was runnable for days.

--- prior notes below ---

CLOSED 2026-08-12. THE FULL CHAIN IS RECORDED BELOW SO THE NEXT SESSION DOES NOT
REOPEN IT. Read this section before re-reading the forensic history that follows
it; the history is kept because the wrong turns are instructive, not because the
question is still open.

=== THE MECHANISM, END TO END. THIS IS THE ANSWER. ===
Three independent failures composed into one confirmed production double booking:

  1. `updateAppointment` ran NO CONFLICT CHECK AT ALL on a status-only patch. A
     patch that moved a row INTO the blocking set went through unexamined.
  2. The agenda drawer offered ALL FIVE statuses, unguarded, as a plain select.
     Every illegal transition was one click away.
  3. `isLegalEstadoTransition` existed but was NEVER ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE. The
     lifecycle map was advisory.

WHAT THE OWNER ACTUALLY DID, which is the step every prior reconstruction was
missing: while testing, Ivan moved a CONFIRMED pedido BACK TO `scheduled`. That
transition is illegal under the lifecycle map and was enforced nowhere, and it
returned the row to the does-not-block set - so the window read as free. Both
rows were then flipped to `confirmed` by unchecked status patches. The
constraint that should have stopped it did not exist, and the two application
checks that should have stopped it were on paths nobody took.

=== BOTH STRATEGY HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG. RECORDED SO NEITHER IS RETRIED. ===
- `is_unconfirmed_pedido` keys on `status = 'scheduled'` PLUS a request row. It
  does NOT key on `confirmation_state`. Any reasoning that ran through
  `confirmation_state` was reasoning about a column the predicate never reads.
- THE CONFIRM PATH WAS NEVER AT FAULT, and the GREEN diagnostic that exercised it
  RETURNED A CORRECT RESULT. The pedido was confirmed 68 seconds before the staff
  appointment existed, so there was nothing on that window to conflict with.
  GREEN tested the one path that was not involved and reported accurately. That
  is not a criticism of the diagnostic; it is why the diagnostic was run.

=== THE FIXES, ALL THREE ON main ===
  #869  merged 2026-08-11 (1b24682) - SERVER-SIDE ENFORCEMENT. Every status
        patch goes through isLegalEstadoTransition, and updateAppointment
        conflict-checks any transition moving a row INTO the blocking set,
        behind the slot lock, reading pedidos through is_unconfirmed_pedido
        rather than a staff_notifications join (0055 pins that table's SELECT to
        the recipient, so a non-recipient caller would see no row and skip the
        very check it needs). Negative arms proven by deletion: removing the
        legality check reddens 3 tests, removing the conflict check reddens 4.
  #873  THE AUDIT TRAIL. A deliberate override was forensically invisible -
        allowConflict was never written to audit metadata by any path, and
        updateAppointment recorded only {changed, scope} with no from/to status.
        Two of the three paths in this incident left no evidence of how.
  0061  THE STATE-LEVEL CONSTRAINT. An EXCLUDE keyed on STATE, not on PATH:
        no two `confirmed` appointments may overlap for one practitioner.
        Applied to production 2026-08-12, #870 merged as 225edfc.

WHY A CONSTRAINT AND NOT A FOURTH APPLICATION CHECK. Three paths produced this in
ninety seconds. Patching the paths you found is the vacuous-guard failure mode
this project has counted 123 instances of: you fix three and the fourth is
written next month. A constraint cannot be bypassed by a path nobody thought of.

=== THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN A GREEN CI RUN ===
- The section 3 pre-check returned ZERO ROWS ON PRODUCTION. The live clinic diary
  held no confirmed overlap at apply time, so the constraint took cleanly.
- 0061 CAUGHT TWO LATENT DOUBLE BOOKINGS ALREADY IN THE REPO, including a
  FIXTURE THAT EVERY EXISTING TEST AGREED WITH. The constraint found defects the
  entire test suite was built around. That is the argument for state-level
  enforcement, made by the enforcement itself.

=== DO NOT REOPEN THIS CARD ===
Reopen only on a NEW production overlap observed after 2026-08-12. If that
happens it is a NEW incident with a new id, because the constraint makes the old
mechanism impossible: a second confirmed overlapping row now raises 23P01 at the
database. What is still OPEN and belongs elsewhere: acceptance item 18 half two
(the owner observing a confirm being REFUSED on a deployed build) is a PG2
observation, not this card.

--- HISTORY BELOW THIS LINE. Kept for the wrong turns, not for the question. ---

REAL DEFECT, CONFIRMED BY FORENSIC AUDIT READ 2026-08-11. Not a report, not a
hypothesis. Two rows, ONE practitioner, overlapping window, both reaching
`confirmed`.

=== THE PRACTITIONER MATCH KILLS THE "TWO THERAPISTS" READING ===
Both rows carry practitioner 8ac3b349 (ZZ TESTE THERAPIST), location LV. The
earlier hypothesis that this was two different therapists on one room is DEAD.

=== THE CORRECTED TIMELINE, FROM audit_log, UTC ===
This REPLACES the sequence every prior document recorded. The order is the
REVERSE of what was written down.

  16:58:37  pedido 78c695b5  portal_request_confirm, scheduled -> confirmed
  16:59:18  pedido           status changed
  16:59:45  staff  9ad688eb  CREATED as scheduled, at 09:00 UTC
  16:59:55  staff            RESCHEDULED to 10:00 UTC, onto the pedido window
  17:00:01  staff            status changed, ends at confirmed
  17:00:14  pedido           status changed
  17:02:16  pedido           cancelled

=== THE CONFIRM PATH IS EXONERATED, WITH EVIDENCE ===
The pedido was confirmed 68 SECONDS BEFORE THE STAFF APPOINTMENT EXISTED. At
16:58:37 there was nothing on that window to conflict with, so
confirmAppointmentRequest could not have failed and its transactional re-check
(actions.ts:1072-1090) was never the thing under test. The GREEN diagnostic that
exercised the confirm path returned a correct result; it tested the one path that
was never involved. That is why the diagnostic was run, not a criticism of it.

=== TASK 1 CODE READ, 2026-08-11. THREE PATHS, ALL ON origin/main b4317fc ===

(a) STAFF RESCHEDULE - apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts:842. CHECKS.
    :894 gated on `!input.allowConflict`; :897 findConflictsForWindow ->
    conflict.ts:198-206 -> the SQL appointment_conflicts() plus
    findScheduleConflicts; :906 blockingConflicts drops ONLY `availability`
    (conflict-core.ts:13-14), so a therapist overlap still blocks.

(b) PLAIN STATUS CHANGE - apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts:681
    (updateAppointment). DOES NOT CHECK CONFLICTS AT ALL. The only conflict
    branch is :730, `if (!opts?.allowConflict && "room" in set && newRoom)`. A
    status-only patch never enters it: the drawer builds `patch` by field-diff
    (appointment-drawer.tsx:617-621), so `"room" in set` is false unless the room
    actually changed. Its audit write at :787-794 emits action
    `appointment.update` with `metadata: { changed, scope }` where
    `changed = Object.keys(set) = ["status"]` - the exact signature in the
    timeline above.

(c) STAFF CREATE - apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts:304. CHECKS. :380 gated on
    `!input.allowConflict`, :381 collectConflicts per occurrence, same
    classifier.

=== is_unconfirmed_pedido, EXACT, 0059_pedido_does_not_block_slot.sql:132-148 ===
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.appointments a
    JOIN public.staff_notifications n ON n.appointment_id = a.id
    WHERE a.id = p_appointment
      AND a.tenant_id = public.jwt_tenant_id()
      AND a.status = 'scheduled'
      AND n.kind = 'appointment_request'
  )

IT KEYS ON `status` PLUS THE PRESENCE OF AN appointment_request ROW.
`confirmation_state` APPEARS NOWHERE IN 0059.

THE QUESTION ASKED, ANSWERED: NO. After portal_request_confirm the row is
`confirmed`, so is_unconfirmed_pedido returns FALSE and the row blocks again. A
confirmed pedido is NOT permanently invisible to conflict checks. The
`confirmation_state = pending` observed on the surviving row is inert here -
nothing on the conflict path reads that axis. That hypothesis is dead too.

=== THE INVERSE MECHANISM, WHICH *IS* LIVE AND FITS THE TIMELINE ===
is_unconfirmed_pedido returns TRUE for ANY row at status 'scheduled' carrying an
appointment_request row, and NOTHING PINS THAT STATUS ONE-WAY:
  - the agenda drawer's Estado selector offers all five statuses unconditionally
    (appointment-drawer.tsx:112-118);
  - isLegalEstadoTransition, which forbids confirmed -> scheduled
    (estado-transitions.ts:34), is imported ONLY by
    apps/web/app/patients/[id]/appointments-list.tsx:312. The drawer does not
    import it;
  - the server does not enforce it. estado-transitions.ts:27-28 says so in its
    own words: "the server itself is unchanged (no new lifecycle rule authored
    there)".
So confirmed -> scheduled is ONE CLICK in the agenda drawer, server-accepted,
WITH ZERO CONFLICT CHECKING, and it returns the row to the does-not-block set.
The two bare "status changed" rows on the pedido (16:59:18, 17:00:14) sit exactly
where that move would sit.

=== TWO FORENSIC BLIND SPOTS. BOTH MATTER FOR WHAT WE MAY CONCLUDE ===

BLIND SPOT 1 - "allowConflict is absent from the reschedule audit metadata" is
VACUOUS EVIDENCE. allowConflict is NEVER written to audit metadata by ANY path in
actions.ts. Reschedule writes {practitionerId, locationId, startsAt, endsAt,
scope} (:953-959). Create writes :495-506. Update writes :792. None carry it. Its
absence is a property of the SCHEMA, not a fact about the call. "Guardar mesmo
assim" is FORENSICALLY INVISIBLE and that hypothesis remains fully live.

BLIND SPOT 2 - the status transitions cannot be read from the audit either.
updateAppointment records {changed, scope} only: no from_status, no to_status.
Only confirmAppointmentRequest records those (:1108-1117). "17:00:01 staff status
changed, ends at confirmed" is an INFERENCE from the surviving row, not a reading
of the log.

NET: at least three code paths can produce the double-booked state, and two of
them leave no evidence of how. That is the argument for the fix below.

=== ACCEPTED FIX DIRECTION: KEY ON STATE, NOT PATH ===
A btree_gist EXCLUDE constraint over
  (tenant_id, practitioner_id, tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at))
  WHERE status = 'confirmed'
Rationale: at least three code paths can produce the state, two of them
unobservably, and patching them individually is the vacuous-guard failure mode
ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep just counted 123 instances of. A database constraint
cannot be bypassed by a path nobody thought of, by a "Save anyway" click, or by a
status edit that no guard is watching.

D1 IS PRESERVED BY THE PARTIAL PREDICATE. Pending pedidos carry status
'scheduled' - confirmed against the tree, not taken from the dispatch:
0059:145 keys the helper on 'scheduled', and apps/web/lib/notifications/centre.ts:96
declares `const PENDING_STATUS = "scheduled"`. So `WHERE status = 'confirmed'`
leaves stacked pendings legal, exactly as D1 requires.

WHAT THE CONSTRAINT DOES NOT COVER, recorded rather than hidden. It forbids two
CONFIRMED overlaps only. Two `scheduled` staff bookings on one window stay legal
at the database layer, so the application check REMAINS LOAD-BEARING and this is a
backstop, not a replacement. Claiming otherwise would be the same overreach this
card exists to correct.

=== WHY NOTHING IS BUILT THIS DISPATCH ===
The constraint is a MIGRATION and needs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS
btree_gist`. Migration 0061 is RESERVED AND UNAUTHORED and is authored only after
AMBER's OTP PR merges (PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.1, rule 8). This card therefore takes
0062 or later, at BUILD time per rule 7, and it CANNOT START until the 0061 slot
clears. It also needs a pre-check for EXISTING violating pairs: an EXCLUDE
constraint fails to create if the table already contains a conflicting pair, and
the surviving row from this very incident may be one.

=== SOLVED 2026-08-11. THE OWNER SUPPLIED THE MISSING STEP. ===

Ivan confirmed from memory that he changed appointment statuses in the agenda
while testing whether a conflict would show. That is the trigger, and it closes
the timeline with ZERO unexplained steps:

  16:58:37  pedido confirmed -> it now BLOCKS
  16:59:18  flipped back down. status `scheduled` + an appointment_request row =
            is_unconfirmed_pedido TRUE = does NOT block. Illegal under the
            Estado map, and enforced nowhere on the server.
  16:59:55  the staff reschedule onto 10:00 saw nothing, and was CORRECT given
            what the predicate could see.
  17:00:01  and 17:00:14 - both rows flipped to confirmed by a plain status
            patch. That path ran no conflict check at all.

BOTH OF THE DISPATCH'S HYPOTHESES ARE DEAD and the code read is the finding:
  - "two therapists" died on the practitioner match (8ac3b349 on both rows);
  - "is_unconfirmed_pedido keys on confirmation_state" died on 0059:132-148,
    which keys on `status = 'scheduled'` plus the presence of an
    appointment_request row. confirmation_state appears nowhere in 0059, so a
    confirmed pedido blocks again rather than going permanently invisible.

WHAT IS BUILT (#869, merged): the Estado map enforced server-side, and a conflict
check on any status transition INTO the blocking set.
WHAT IS HELD (#870, apply-before-merge): the EXCLUDE constraint, plus the pt-PT
message so the refusal reaches the agenda instead of a 500 during the clinic
demo.

=== THE CONSTRAINT PROVED ITSELF IN CI BEFORE IT REACHED PRODUCTION. ===
#870 went RED on the DB gate at first push, with 23P01 on
appointments_no_double_confirmed. NOT a problem with the constraint - it caught
TWO PRE-EXISTING FIXTURES that were creating the exact state it forbids:

  packages/db/tests/appointment-note-present-capture.test.ts seeded TWO
  confirmed appointments on ONE therapist at the IDENTICAL window. A literal
  double booking, sitting in a fixture, unrelated to what that suite measures -
  it simply needed two appointments. Moved an hour apart.

  packages/db/tests/pedido-does-not-block.db.test.ts confirmed a second pedido
  onto an already-confirmed window, under a comment reading TWO CONFIRMS STILL
  CANNOT BOTH SUCCEED. 0061 now enforces exactly that, so the old body died at
  the UPDATE before its assertion ran.

THE SECOND TEST WAS REWRITTEN, NOT RELAXED, and the claim got STRONGER. Its old
proof depended on the APPLICATION choosing to look: the second confirm would SEE
the first in a conflict query. The database now refuses it outright, so the test
asserts the refusal. The original claim - a confirmed pedido occupies its slot -
is KEPT as its own case on a clean window, because the constraint proves
coexistence is impossible but says NOTHING about whether appointment_conflicts
REPORTS the pedido. That is 0059 job, and a regression there would stop the app
warning anyone before the database refused them - turning a clean pt-PT message
back into a raw error during the clinic demo.

WHY THIS IS EVIDENCE AND NOT AN ANECDOTE. The argument for keying on STATE was
that paths nobody thought of would keep producing it. Within one CI run the
constraint found two such producers that had been in the repo for months and
that every existing test agreed with.

#870 IS NOW FULLY GREEN (all four required checks; DB-gated a real 2m43s run;
packages/db 51 -> 53 files passing) AND IS HELD FOR THE OWNER APPLY. The
skip-guard passing is the proof no-double-confirmed.test.ts actually executed.

=== OWNER PRE-CHECK, RUN 2026-08-12. ZERO ROWS. ===
Reported by the owner from his own shell, recorded as HIS observation rather
than as a claim of this lane. Three facts, and the middle one is what makes the
zero mean something:

  DATA SANITY   0 rows with a null or inverted ends_at. The overlap predicate
                would silently skip a row whose range is backwards, so a dirty
                diary could have produced a false zero.
  PRIVILEGE     running_as postgres, 29 appointments visible. RLS did not
                filter the read, so the zero is over the WHOLE table and not
                over one tenant's slice.
  PRE-CHECK     ZERO ROWS. No existing overlapping confirmed pair on any
                practitioner.

THE PRIVILEGE LINE IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN EASY TO SKIP. A pre-check
run under a role that RLS filters returns zero for a table it cannot see, and
that zero is indistinguishable from a clean diary. He checked; it is clean.

CONSEQUENCE: ADD CONSTRAINT will not be refused for existing data. The apply is
unblocked on that axis. #870 STILL DOES NOT MERGE until the journal is pasted
back - rule 9, apply before merge.

29 APPOINTMENTS IS ALSO A FINDING, and it is the reason for the new LAUNCH-03
pre-import clause: 0061 is being added to a near-empty table, so it proves
nothing about the ~10k rows arriving at LAUNCH-03.

cards.title: Item 20 / PG4: the staff app emits ZERO patient-change events, so a therapist confirming a pedido makes it vanish from reception's queue with no record - HALTED on a contract ruling

evidence.ref: #870 MERGED 2026-08-12, squashed to 225edfc on origin/main, after migration 0061 was applied to production (journal proof on INC-08-double-booking-state-not-path and at docs/migration-apply-0061.md section 10). This card's own DoD was "Closes when 0061 applies and #870 merges"; both are now true. Shipped: PatientChangeKind grows by one (`confirmed`), staff_notifications gains actor_user_id (nullable, ON DELETE SET NULL), 0055's kind CHECK rewritten from four values to five, and apps/web gains emitConfirmedNotification wired post-commit into confirmAppointmentRequest. The fan-out EXCLUDES THE ACTOR. 6 tests including a source arm on the actor exclusion, because the mocked db cannot see a WHERE clause. cards.notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-12. The migration applied, #870 merged as 225edfc, and this card's
stated closing condition is met exactly.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated first because it is the thing most likely to be
misread next session: IT DOES NOT MOVE PG4. PG4 closes on acceptance item 20
observed and RECORDED in docs/acceptance-session-wave-13-results.md - the owner
opening /notificacoes on a deployed build and seeing it populated, with no
service name and no clinical content. This card removes the reason the
observation was impossible (nothing was ever written to observe); it does not
substitute for the observation. Flipping PG4 on this merge would be the exact
error WF-03 exists to prevent, and PG4 was already corrected down from pass once
on 2026-08-11 for it.

--- HISTORY BELOW THIS LINE ---

RAISED 2026-08-11 FROM THE TASK 2 CODE READ. HALTED BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN,
under the dispatch's own instruction: "If the contract needs EXTENDING, HALT."
IT NEEDS EXTENDING, IN TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, AND ONE OF THEM IS A MIGRATION.

=== THE PREMISE HOLDS. RE-DERIVED FROM THE TREE, NOT TRANSCRIBED ===
emitPatientChange has exactly THREE call sites repo-wide, all in
apps/api/lib/appointments/booking.ts: :576 create, :614 cancel, :721 reschedule.
(The dispatch cited :403/:441/:548 and ACC-therapist-queue-unobserved cited
:408/:446/:553; both are stale line numbers for the same three sites. The SITES
are right, the NUMBERS have moved.) The staff app - apps/web - has ZERO emit
calls. Confirmed by repo-wide grep excluding tests.

=== WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS, WHICH IS WORSE THAN "RECEPTION IS BLIND" ===
Reception's queue is a LIVE QUERY ON STATE, not a message list:
apps/web/lib/notifications/centre.ts:151-155 selects
`kind = 'appointment_request' AND appointments.status = 'scheduled'`. So when a
therapist confirms a pedido, status leaves 'scheduled' and THE ROW SILENTLY
DISAPPEARS FROM RECEPTION'S QUEUE. Reception cannot distinguish:
  - a pedido a therapist just confirmed,
  - a pedido reception themselves confirmed,
  - a pedido that was cancelled,
  - a pedido that was never there.
No notification is written for the confirm, so the log half of /notificacoes
carries nothing either. centre.ts:118-121 documents the decline case collapsing
into the same predicate on purpose; the CONFIRM-BY-SOMEONE-ELSE case was not
considered.

=== HALT REASON 1: THERE IS NO KIND FOR "CONFIRMED", AND ADDING ONE IS A
    MIGRATION ===
PatientChangeKind is `booked | cancelled | rescheduled | appointment_request`
(patient-change.ts:45-49). None of them means "a pedido was accepted". Using
`appointment_request` for a confirm would be a semantic lie AND would collide
with 0059, which reads that exact kind as the portal-provenance record.
The vocabulary is PINNED IN THE DATABASE:
  0055_staff_notifications.sql:106-107
  CONSTRAINT "staff_notifications_kind_check"
    CHECK ("kind" IN ('booked','cancelled','rescheduled','appointment_request'))
and 0055:83-86 states the intent outright: "A fifth kind requires a migration,
which is the point: the contract in patient-change.ts calls itself FIXED, and a
CHECK constraint is how the database says the same thing."
So the confirm arm - the exact case in the dispatch - needs BOTH an owner ruling
(WF-04 precedent: growing the kind set is an owner ruling) AND a migration.
0061 is reserved and unauthored. Two stop conditions at once.

=== HALT REASON 2: THE THREE "SAFE" ARMS ARE NOT SAFE EITHER ===
Staff create / cancel / reschedule DO map onto existing kinds. Emitting them
anyway is still a contract extension, because THE EVENT HAS NO ACTOR FIELD
(patient-change.ts:81-93) and the type's own header says "All four are
patient-initiated writes, never staff ones" (:30). A staff-emitted `booked` row
is INDISTINGUISHABLE in the database from a patient-emitted one, so reception's
queue would stop meaning "a patient did something that needs you" and start
meaning "something happened", including things reception did themselves thirty
seconds ago. Adding an actor field is explicitly OUTSIDE WF-04's scope limit:
"It does not license changing the existing field set."
Shipping the three noisy arms while the one signal arm (confirm) is unbuildable
is the worst available outcome, so nothing was built.

=== WHAT IVAN IS BEING ASKED TO RULE. Recommended default first ===
RECOMMENDED: extend the contract by ONE kind, `confirmed`, plus ONE nullable
`actor_user_id` column, and instrument the staff CONFIRM path only. That is one
migration, one emit site, and it closes the actual defect. The other three staff
paths stay silent until someone asks for them - reception is already looking at
the agenda for those.
ALTERNATIVE A: confirm-kind only, no actor field. Cheaper migration; reception
still cannot see WHO confirmed.
ALTERNATIVE B: rule the defect out of scope for launch. Defensible - reception
can read the agenda - but the queue then silently lies about pedidos in a way no
screen explains.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE, STATED PLAINLY ===
PG4 closes on acceptance item 20 and item 20 alone
(ACC-13-results-uncommitted, corrected gate map). This card is item 20's code
half. PG4 CANNOT PASS UNTIL THIS RULING LANDS AND THE WORK SHIPS. The dispatch's
Wave 13 closure explicitly excepts item 20, so no gate credit is taken.

=== RULED AND BUILT 2026-08-11. THE HALT IS LIFTED. ===
The owner ruled: ONE kind (`confirmed`), CONFIRM PATH ONLY.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE RULING'S ARITHMETIC, recorded because the board should not
carry a wrong number. The dispatch described this as "2 kinds to 3, not the 2 to
4 that WF-04 reserves for the owner". The contract on main was already at FOUR
kinds (booked, cancelled, rescheduled, appointment_request) - WF-04 ratified the
2->4 growth back in R1. This change is 4 -> 5. The RULING is unaffected: the
owner ruled explicitly on adding one kind and on folding the column into 0061,
so it is settled either way. Only the count was wrong.

WHY THE ACTOR COLUMN IS REAL AND NOT A PAYLOAD FIELD, since the dispatch left
that open: staff_notifications had no actor column at all, and a `confirmed`
row without one says an acceptance happened but not by whom - to an audience
that includes the person who did it. Folded into 0061 as instructed rather than
authored as 0062.

CARRIED FORWARD, NOT DROPPED: staff cancel, reschedule and no-show still emit
nothing. See LE-staff-transitions-emit-nothing.
