cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-11 BY AMBER when PR #865 went red on a job its diff could not
touch: that PR changes five files, all under apps/api, plus the board. The
failing suite is apps/web. The artifact was read BEFORE anything was blamed,
per the e2e/CI debugging doctrine, and the runner was NOT the cause.

THE MECHANISM, and all three ingredients are needed:
  1. ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE/ENABLE TRIGGER changes GLOBAL table state. It is
     not session-scoped and not transaction-local to the connection that ran
     it. Every connection to that database sees the change.
  2. TWO apps/web DB-gated suites now toggle the SAME trigger:
       apps/web/lib/reminders/redeem.db.test.ts (afterEach, :98-100)
       apps/web/lib/scheduling/pedido-confirm.db.test.ts
     A third, packages/db/tests/patient-audit-append-only.test.ts, toggles it
     too but runs in a different vitest invocation.
  3. VITEST RUNS TEST FILES IN PARALLEL BY DEFAULT and apps/web/vitest.config.ts
     sets no fileParallelism override.
So suite B's teardown can re-ENABLE the trigger in the window between suite A
disabling it and suite A's DELETE. A's delete is then refused, and the suite
that fails is whichever one lost the race - which is why it moves around.

WHY IT APPEARED NOW, dated rather than guessed. Both halves landed today:
  .github/workflows/db-tests.yml changed the apps/web step from an explicit
  path list naming redeem.db.test.ts to a GLOB. That change was correct and its
  own comment says why - pedido-confirm.db.test.ts 'would have been added to the
  repo, passed review, and NEVER RUN'. It is not the defect; it is what made
  the second suite execute at all.
  pedido-confirm.db.test.ts gained the patient_audit_log toggle in 5103c24
  (#861), the double-booking diagnostic.
Before those two, only one suite in that invocation touched the trigger and
there was nothing to race.

IMPACT, AND WHY IT IS HIGH RATHER THAN AN ANNOYANCE. This blocks BOTH LANES
intermittently, on a REQUIRED check (branch protection lists 'DB-gated tests
(RLS isolation, seeded DB)'). Worse than the delay: it trains the reflex this
project has already paid for twice - re-run until green. A flake on a required
check is how a real failure eventually gets re-run away. #865 merged on a
re-run green and its report says so explicitly rather than quietly.

FIX OPTIONS, and the choice is real:
  1. fileParallelism: false in apps/web/vitest.config.ts, or a sequential
     shard for .db.test.ts. Smallest change, removes the race by removing the
     concurrency. Costs wall-clock on every DB run, including the suites that
     never touch a trigger.
  2. STOP TOGGLING THE TRIGGER. Both teardowns disable an append-only guard so
     they can DELETE, which is fighting the very property 0054 exists to
     enforce. Deleting the TENANT with a cascade, or truncating in a
     transaction that rolls back, or simply leaving audit rows behind and
     scoping every assertion by tenant_id, all avoid the global toggle
     entirely. Most work, and it is the only option that removes the shared
     mutable state rather than serialising access to it.
  3. A per-file advisory lock (pg_advisory_lock) around the toggle. Correct and
     cheap, and it keeps the parallelism. Adds a concept to two test files.
RECOMMENDED: 2 for redeem.db.test.ts and pedido-confirm.db.test.ts, with 1 as
the immediate stopgap if the queue needs unblocking today. A test that has to
disable a production integrity guard to clean up after itself is a smell
independent of the race.

OWNERSHIP. Both files are apps/web; pedido-confirm.db.test.ts is PURPLE's
double-booking work and apps/web/vitest.config.ts is in neither lane's table.
AMBER found it and is NOT fixing it across that boundary. Raised for the owner
to assign.

CLOSES ON: the DB-gated job green on ten consecutive runs of an unchanged sha,
or the global toggle removed from both suites. One green run proves nothing
that can race - that is this project's own recorded doctrine and it is exactly
what this card is about.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-11 AS #868 (1bc28db). ===
AMBER's diagnosis was correct in every particular and is preserved above. The fix
took option 2, and the card's own DoD is now met by its deterministic half: the
global toggle is GONE from both suites, which is stronger than "ten consecutive
greens" because it removes the shared mutable state rather than sampling it.

ONE THING WORTH KEEPING FROM THE FIX. The guard's first draft failed on the two
files it had just fixed. Their new teardown comments explain the ban using the
same words the ban is written in, and a scanner that cannot tell prose from code
is the unstripped-comment vacuous-guard class in its inverted form: there it
passes on a comment, here it failed on one. The guard now strips comments before
it scans, and tests the stripper - including the arm proving stripping does not
disarm the guard.

cards.title: "Guardar mesmo assim" leaves NO trace - allowConflict is never written to audit metadata by any path, so a deliberate override cannot be reconstructed after an incident

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-12 in PR #873, squashed to 444c9b1. Verified an ancestor of origin/main. STATUS SET 2026-08-19, seven days late, after this card was picked as the next thing to BUILD and turned out to be already built.

RE-DERIVED FROM main BEFORE FLIPPING, per standing rule 4, and every one of the card's three scope items is present:
  1. `allowConflict` is written at ALL THREE audit sites in apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts - create, update and reschedule - and always as `!!`, so it is a boolean on every row and never omitted when false. That last detail is the whole point: the card exists because an ABSENT field was read as evidence the override had not been used, when it was a property of the schema.
  2. `fromStatus`/`toStatus` on update, guarded `...(patch.status ? ... : {})` so it is BOTH ENDS OR NEITHER. A `to` with no `from` is the shape that made the INC-08 timeline an inference rather than a reading. They are absent from create (which has no prior status) and from reschedule (which does not change status), which is the correct reading of the scope rather than a gap.
  3. The source-level guard the card asked for: apps/web/lib/scheduling/audit-override-trace.test.ts, 10 tests passing. It splits actions.ts per exported action and asserts that a path READING allowConflict RECORDS it - and it carries its own vacuous-pass guard (asserting the split found more than six actions, and naming three by hand) so the scan cannot silently pass over nothing.

=== SIXTH IN THE FAMILY, AND A THIRD DISTINCT SHAPE ===
  The first four carried a false `todo` while CITING PRs - visible to the reconciler's pr-state rules once those existed.
  AI-01 carried a false `in_flight` with evidence NULL and its notes claiming completion - invisible to the PR rules, which is what rule F was built for.
  THIS ONE CARRIES A FALSE `todo`, evidence null, no cited PR, no gate claim, no named consumer, AND NO COMPLETION CLAIM IN ITS NOTES. Its notes read 'SCOPE WHEN BUILT:' - correct future tense for a card nobody had started. Nothing textual distinguishes it from a genuine todo. Rule F excludes `todo` deliberately (a plan may be written in the past tense before anyone starts) and would not have fired here even if it did not, because none of its phrases appear.

WHAT ACTUALLY DISTINGUISHES IT IS SEMANTIC: the defect the card DESCRIBES no longer exists. That is not cheaply checkable by any rule, and the obvious candidate was measured and rejected - see the card's notes.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-11 FROM THE INC-08 CODE READ, and accepted by the owner as
"the more important half" of that finding.

THE FINDING, re-derived from the tree rather than remembered. NO path in
apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts writes `allowConflict` into audit metadata:
  reschedule  writes { practitionerId, locationId, startsAt, endsAt, scope }
  create      writes { patientId, practitionerId, locationId, serviceId, packId,
                       status, startsAt, seriesId, occurrence, count }
  update      writes { changed, scope }
Only confirmAppointmentRequest records anything about WHY, and only as
`via: "portal_request_confirm"`.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A GAP IN A REPORT. "Guardar mesmo assim" is a
deliberate, permitted override of a safety check. It is the single most
consequential discretionary act the scheduling UI offers, and it is
INDISTINGUISHABLE IN THE RECORD from a save that had no conflict to override.

IT ALREADY COST A DIAGNOSIS. During INC-08 the absence of allowConflict from the
reschedule audit row was read as evidence that the override had NOT been used.
It is not evidence of anything: the field is never written by any path, so its
absence is a property of the SCHEMA. The hypothesis stayed alive for a full
dispatch on the strength of a fact that could not have been otherwise.

A SECOND BLIND SPOT IN THE SAME PLACE, worth fixing together: updateAppointment
records { changed, scope } with NO from_status and NO to_status. Every plain
status change in the audit log is therefore "the status changed" and nothing
more. The end states in the INC-08 timeline are INFERENCES from the surviving
row, not readings of the log.

SCOPE WHEN BUILT: add `allow_conflict` (boolean) and `from_status`/`to_status`
to the audit metadata of create, update and reschedule. Metadata is jsonb, so
this is an app-layer change with NO migration. Add a source-level guard that
every conflict-overridable path records the flag, or the next path to be written
will forget it.

WHY IT IS high AND NOT medium: this is the observability that makes the NEXT
incident diagnosable. INC-08 took three dispatches and two dead hypotheses, and
two of the three implicated paths still cannot be reconstructed from the trail.

=== 2026-08-19: THE CARD WAS FALSE. PICKED AS NEXT-TO-BUILD, FOUND ALREADY BUILT. ===

Shipped 2026-08-12 in #873 (444c9b1). Full verification on the evidence ref.

A CANDIDATE RULE WAS TESTED AND REJECTED, and the measurement is worth more than the rule would have been. The hypothesis: a card whose ID IS CITED IN COMMITTED SOURCE has been built, because nobody writes a card id into a source comment before doing the work. This card is cited in actions.ts and in audit-override-trace.test.ts, so it would have been caught.

MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE TREE: 57 card ids are cited in committed source, and FIFTEEN of those cards are still `todo`. Spot-reading them, most are CORRECT PRACTICE - a comment saying 'this is a known gap, carded as X' is exactly what a good source comment does, and the card genuinely is open. LE-no-show-notification-kind in centre.ts, ACC-immediate-isvisible-probes in a spec, LE-guest-convert-abandoned-booking in guest-convert.ts - all correct.

SO THE RULE WOULD REDDEN CORRECT BEHAVIOUR ON FOURTEEN CARDS TO CATCH ONE. That is the fastest way to get a guard switched off, and the card that authorised rule F said the same thing in the same words. NOT BUILT.

THE HONEST CONCLUSION: this shape is not cheaply detectable today. What distinguishes a false todo from a real one is whether the defect it describes still exists, which needs a reader who understands the card. The mitigation that actually works is the one that caught it here - RE-DERIVE FROM main BEFORE BUILDING, every time, which standing rule 4 already requires and which cost about four minutes on this card.

cards.title: Staff CANCEL and RESCHEDULE now emit notifications. No-show is SPLIT OFF because it has no kind and would need a migration

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-13. Two of the three arms, exactly as this card said to split them.

NO MIGRATION, VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE CARD.
0061:248 rewrites staff_notifications_kind_check to
  ('booked','cancelled','rescheduled','appointment_request','confirmed')
so 'cancelled' and 'rescheduled' were already permitted and simply never emitted.
NO-SHOW HAS NO KIND, so it needs a migration and an owner ruling under the WF-04
precedent - and a migration beyond 0062 is a STOP CONDITION on this dispatch.
Split off as LE-no-show-notification-kind. 0063 is still free.

=== THE REFACTOR IS THE POINT, NOT THE TWO EMITS ===
The obvious move was to copy emitConfirmedNotification twice. THREE COPIES OF A
RECIPIENT RULE IS THREE PLACES FOR THE ACTOR EXCLUSION TO GO MISSING, and this
card's own last line says the exclusion is the part to copy - without it staff are
notified of their own clicks and the queue gets noisier rather than truer.
So there is ONE emitStaffTransitionNotification parameterised by kind, and three
thin wrappers over it. The confirm path's behaviour is unchanged.

THE SOURCE-TEXT GUARD WENT RED ON THAT REFACTOR, WHICH IS WHAT IT WAS FOR.
confirm-fanout.test.ts asserts on SOURCE that the actor exclusion appears twice,
because a mocked db cannot see a WHERE clause. After the move,
emitConfirmedNotification contained no query at all and the slice it reads was
empty of them. Repointed at the shared function, and a SECOND assertion added:
all three wrappers must DELEGATE and must not contain ne(users.id themselves.
Without that, a later change could give one kind its own copy while the exclusion
assertion stayed green - the exact drift the consolidation exists to prevent.
NEGATIVE ARM RUN: adding a stray ne(users.id, ...) to the cancel wrapper turns it
red.

=== A DESIGN FLAW THE EXISTING TESTS EXPOSED, AND IT WAS WORTH FIXING PROPERLY ===
The fan-out needs the patient and BOTH practitioners, which resolveSeries does not
select, so a new read runs INSIDE the caller's transaction - it must, because it
needs the PRE-UPDATE instants and must be RLS-scoped. Three audit tests went red
with a TypeError from their db mock, and that surfaced the real problem: AN
UNHANDLED THROW THERE WOULD ROLL BACK THE CANCELLATION ITSELF. A staff member's
clinical action failing because the notification centre could not be told about
it is the wrong trade.
The read now catches, logs loudly, and returns []. THAT IS NOT THE SECTION 1.3
FALLBACK and the code says why: 1.3 governs VERDICT paths, the verdict here - did
the cancel succeed - is untouched, and 1.3's own wording is that a fallback is
right where the cost of stopping exceeds the cost of being wrong.

=== RESCHEDULE IS THE ONLY KIND WHOSE TWO INSTANTS DIFFER ===
Which is the entire reason staff_notifications carries previous/new. The old
value is read BEFORE the update and carried to the emit; re-reading afterwards
would report that it moved from where it now is - true, useless, and invisible on
the screen. Asserted, including that the two are NOT equal.

NINE NEW TESTS in staff-transition-fanout.test.ts, with two anti-vacuous guards:
a confirm still writes a row, and zero recipients writes nothing and reports
delivered:false. The recipient rule and actor exclusion stay asserted once, in
confirm-fanout.test.ts, because there is now only one place they live.

Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, unit 2022 passed in web, build 4/4.

cards.notes:
CARDED, NOT BUILT, BY EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION 2026-08-11. Recorded so it is not
silently forgotten, which is the whole reason this card exists rather than a
sentence in a PR body.

WHAT SHIPPED. 0061 adds ONE kind, `confirmed`, and instruments ONE path:
confirmAppointmentRequest. The owner's ruling was deliberately narrow because
that path is the one with a demonstrated defect - a therapist accepting a pedido
made it VANISH from reception's live queue with nothing written anywhere.

WHAT DID NOT. A staff member cancelling, rescheduling or marking a no-show still
emits nothing. Reception sees those on the agenda, which is why this is a gap
rather than an incident, but the asymmetry is now IN THE CODE and a reader will
reasonably assume the fan-out is complete.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE. The kinds `cancelled` and `rescheduled` ALREADY EXIST in
the CHECK constraint (0055, unchanged by 0061) and already carry the right
previous/new instants, so the cancel and reschedule arms need NO migration -
only emit calls in cancelAppointment and rescheduleAppointment plus the
recipient rule already written in apps/web/lib/notifications/centre.ts.
NO-SHOW HAS NO KIND and would need one, so it needs a migration and therefore an
owner ruling under the WF-04 precedent. Split the card if the first two are
wanted before the third.

THE ACTOR EXCLUSION IS THE PART TO COPY, not the emit. emitConfirmedNotification
excludes the acting user from its own fan-out; without that, staff would be
notified of their own clicks and the queue would get noisier rather than truer.

cards.title: On a docs-only diff three of the four REQUIRED checks finish in 4-7s as path-filter skips - "all required checks green" is weaker than it reads

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build. pnpm test:scripts 99 pass, 0 skipped (was 96; +3 from this card).

RE-DERIVED FROM main AT 375a297 AND THE OBSERVATION HOLDS, with one correction to the card. The card names three short-circuiting required checks and it is right about all three, but only TWO of them were silent: .github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml ALREADY emits `::notice::` on its skip path and has since it was written. db-tests.yml and e2e.yml did not. So the fix was to bring two workflows into line with a precedent the third already set, not to invent a mechanism.

THE FOUR REQUIRED CONTEXTS WERE READ FROM LIVE BRANCH PROTECTION rather than taken from the card: `gh api repos/happygamer1919-tech/OsteoJP/branches/main/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'` returns exactly DB-gated tests (RLS isolation, seeded DB), Lint + typecheck + test, Playwright E2E (seeded DB), Validate spec + drift check. The card's list was correct.

WHAT SHIPPED, three files:
  .github/workflows/db-tests.yml and e2e.yml - the docs-only skip step now emits a `::notice::` annotation and writes a GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY block saying, in as many words, that the check is green because it is REQUIRED and must report, not because anything was verified.
  scripts/required-checks-are-honest.test.mjs - the guard, in the required check via pnpm test:scripts.

THE GUARD ASSERTS TWO THINGS, both facts a PR can break:
  every required branch-protection context still has a job declaring that EXACT name. A rename does not look like a failure - the context simply never reports, so every open PR sits waiting on a check that will never arrive, with nothing red to point at.
  every step that short-circuits such a job on a docs-only diff emits a workflow annotation on that path.

IT DOES NOT ASSERT THAT A CHECK RUNS, and cannot: whether a given PR's diff is docs-only is a property of that PR. What it makes impossible is a SILENT abstention.

THE CARD'S OWN 'IF EVER FIXED' SHAPE IS NOT AVAILABLE, and this is the finding worth carrying forward rather than re-attempting. The card proposes 'a distinct neutral/skipped conclusion rather than pass'. GitHub Actions has no supported way for a normal job to finish NEUTRAL - exit code 78 was removed - so the only route to a non-pass conclusion is a job-level `if:` skip, which changes how branch protection sees the context. That is the one experiment on this repo that can block EVERY OPEN PR AT ONCE if the assumption about skipped-equals-satisfied is wrong, and it is not a terminal's to run. NOT ATTEMPTED, deliberately, and recorded here so the next reader does not treat it as an oversight.

TEXT SCANNING, NOT YAML PARSING, and that is a constraint rather than a preference: this repo has no YAML parser at the root and standing rule 13 forbids adding a dependency to get one. The scan finds a step by its `- name:` line and reads to the next one at the same indent, which is how these files are written. Said in the file rather than left for a reader to discover.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each restored from the git index, baseline 3/3 green after:
  the db-tests annotation removed -> the abstention assertion red, naming the offending step.
  the DB-gated job renamed -> the branch-protection assertion red, with the message explaining that the context would never report.
  the short-circuit condition changed so the DETECTOR stops matching -> the VACUITY assertion red at 'found 0'. That third one is the important one: without it the guard would go green over workflows that abstain in total silence, passing for the exact reason it exists to prevent.

THE SKIP PATH ITSELF IS NOT EXERCISED BY THIS PR, said plainly rather than implied. This PR touches .github/ and scripts/, so it is NOT docs-only and the new echo lines never execute in its own run. What was verified instead: both workflow files parse as valid YAML (ruby -ryaml YAML.load_file, OK on both), and the guard is green. The annotation will first be OBSERVABLE on the next docs-only PR.

OBSERVED 2026-08-20, AND THIS CLOSES THE ONE THING THAT PR COULD NOT PROVE. #983 was the next docs-only PR. `gh api repos/happygamer1919-tech/OsteoJP/check-runs/96482344671/annotations` returns, against a GREEN required check:
  notice: DB tests DID NOT RUN - Docs-only PR. This required check reports green WITHOUT having run the RLS suites. It is an abstention, not a proof.
The E2E shards carry their own equivalent. That is an OBSERVATION of the annotation attached to the check itself, not an inference from the workflow source, and it is the evidence #982 was missing.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. Nothing on any product screen changes; the surface is a GitHub check page.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20. THE ABSTENTION IS NOW ANNOUNCED, AND A GUARD KEEPS IT ANNOUNCED. ===

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS CARD, both from re-deriving it on main:
  openapi-drift.yml was ALREADY emitting a ::notice:: on its skip. Only two of
  the three named checks were silent.
  the card's proposed fix - a neutral conclusion instead of pass - is NOT
  available in GitHub Actions for a required check, and the route that looks
  like it would work is the one change here that can block every open PR at
  once. Not attempted. Reasoning in the evidence ref.

'Not this wave' on this card dates from 2026-08-11 and the wave it refers to
is closed at 9/9. The 2026-08-20 self-merge sweep is a later instruction and
the 4.11 predicate, re-run this session, returns this card as IN scope. Said
out loud because the two sentences look like they disagree.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

NOTED, NOT CHASED, by instruction 2026-08-11. Recorded on the board so the next
session reading a green docs-only PR knows what that green means.

THE OBSERVATION, measured rather than assumed. On #866 and #867 (both docs-only)
the four REQUIRED checks reported:
  DB-gated tests (RLS isolation, seeded DB)   pass   7s
  Playwright E2E (seeded DB)                  pass   4s
  Validate spec + drift check                 pass   5s
  Lint + typecheck + test                     pass   ~2m20s
Only the last one actually exercised anything. The other three short-circuit on
a "Detect whether code files changed" step (.github/workflows/db-tests.yml:70)
and report success without running.

WHY THAT IS CORRECT AND STILL WORTH KNOWING. Skipping a database suite for a
diff that cannot touch the database is right, and the alternative is a slow gate
everyone learns to ignore. The hazard is purely in how the RESULT READS: a
reviewer, or a session, sees four green required checks and infers four proofs.
On a docs-only PR it is one proof and three abstentions.

CONTRAST, so the distinction is concrete. #868 changed test files, and its
DB-gated check ran for 2m32s - a real execution. The duration IS the tell.

IF EVER FIXED: the honest shape is a distinct neutral/skipped conclusion rather
than `pass`, so the difference is visible without reading durations. Not this
wave.

cards.title: FEASIBILITY ONLY: can the validator or the reconciler cross-check a gate's evidence against OBSERVE-SWEEP.md's Observed lines? A blank slot must outrank a pass

evidence.ref:
RECON DELIVERED IN THE CARD'S NOTES, which is where the card asked for it. Derived from origin/main at 2322658: docs/board/OBSERVE-SWEEP.md and docs/board/portal-board.json, both read this session. NO CODE, per the card's own instruction.

THE HEADLINE: RECOMMEND SHAPE 1 (structured `observations: [{doc,row}]`), CONDITIONED on keying it to `evidence.kind == "screenshot"` so it is CLOSED rather than optional - an optional field fails open and would reproduce this defect wearing a schema. Shapes 2 and 3 are disqualified with measured numbers rather than by argument.

THE FIVE MEASUREMENTS, each re-runnable:
  25 rows, 27 `Observed:` slots, 1 filled (A4). The card's 26-of-27 is exact.
  THE ROW-TO-SLOT MAPPING IS NOT 1:1 - A3 HAS THREE SLOTS. The card did not know this and it is the blocker: the rule's central predicate is undefined for one row in 25 until the file states a contract.
  the naive label regex yields 11 hits over 3 gates, of which the TRUE false positives are 4 (all PG8, read in place and traced to a LATENCY TABLE), not the 7 a path-anchoring rule would imply.
  shape 2 therefore trades 4 false positives for 3 FALSE NEGATIVES: PG2's B2.1/B2.2/B2.3 are genuine (the sweep's own B2.2 heading says 'the row that moves PG2') and PG2 names the file only in its notes, as a bare filename. Silence where it should speak is the section 1.3 shape and is worse than the noise removed.
  shape 3's premise is FALSE: the sweep declares a gate mapping for exactly ONE gate (line 215, PG1). 8 of 25 rows mention a PG in their block and that is noise - A4's block alone mentions three, because a block runs to the next heading and swallows the section prose.

A FOURTH SHAPE THE CARD DOES NOT LIST WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED: anchoring on a sweep mention ANYWHERE in the gate (evidence or notes, path or bare filename) scores ZERO false positives and ZERO false negatives on main today. It is still not recommended, and the reason is the recon's whole point: it is correct by accident of prose, a measurement rather than a contract.

BACK-FILL COST MEASURED AT FOUR GATES, not two: PG1, PG2, PG3, PG4 all carry `evidence.kind == "screenshot"`. PG3 and PG4 cite no sweep row at all despite being observation-backed - PG4's write is row C2 by the sweep's own heading and PG4's evidence never says so.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS SPECIFIED, including the one usually forgotten: with every slot FILLED, removing the `observations` array must STILL go red - otherwise the rule passes on a fully-observed file for the wrong reason and goes green forever the day somebody drops the field.

SCOPE BOUNDARY RE-CHECKED AND IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A NOTE: both validators are shared with the platform board, and the proposed key (`evidence.kind`) exists there too. Whoever builds this runs BOTH validators before and after and pastes both exit codes.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. Read-only recon; no product surface exists to look at.

cards.notes:
=== RECON DELIVERED 2026-08-20. RECOMMENDED SHAPE: 1, WITH ONE CONDITION AND ONE BLOCKER. NO CODE, AS INSTRUCTED. ===

EVERY NUMBER BELOW WAS MEASURED AGAINST main AT 2322658 THIS SESSION. Nothing is carried from the card.

--- WHAT THE FILE ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE ---

25 rows (`### <LABEL> · <title>`), 27 `Observed:` slots under a row, 1 of 27 FILLED (A4). The card said 26 of 27 blank and it is exactly right.

BUT THE ROW-TO-SLOT MAPPING IS NOT 1:1, AND THE CARD DID NOT KNOW THIS. 24 rows have exactly one slot; A3 HAS THREE. So 'the row's Observed line' is undefined for A3, and any rule keyed on it must either pick one or require all of them. That is a contract the file does not currently carry, and it is the BLOCKER named below.

A 28th `Observed:` occurrence exists at line 23 and is PROSE inside a blockquote describing this very incident. Any scanner must anchor on rows rather than on the string, or it will count a sentence about the defect as a slot.

--- SHAPE 2, ANCHORED PROSE MATCH: DISQUALIFIED, AND NOW WITH THE NUMBER ---

THE NAIVE LABEL REGEX OVER GATE EVIDENCE PRODUCES 11 HITS ACROSS 3 GATES: PG1 [A4,A1,A2,A3], PG2 [B2.2,B2.1,B2.3], PG8 [B6,A1,A2,A4].

THE TRUE FALSE-POSITIVE COUNT IS 4, NOT 7, and the correction matters. PG8's four hits are FALSE - read in place, they come from a LATENCY TABLE ('A5+A6+A7 lock, conflict re-check, insert + commit 1317ms', 'B6+B7 portal learns and renders 552ms', and a sentence 'A1, A2 AND A4 CARRY NO SEPARATE NUMBER'). PG2's three are GENUINE: the sweep's own B2.2 heading reads 'This is the row that moves PG2.'

SO ANCHORING ON THE PATH, WHICH IS WHAT SHAPE 2 PROPOSES, TRADES 4 FALSE POSITIVES FOR 3 FALSE NEGATIVES. Only PG1 cites `docs/board/OBSERVE-SWEEP.md` in its evidence; PG2 names the file only in its NOTES and only as the bare filename. A rule anchored on the path is SILENT on PG2's three genuine rows. Under section 1.3 that is worse than the noise it removes: a rule that abstains where it should speak reports the benign case, and the benign case is what the board already shows.

--- SHAPE 2b, WHICH THE CARD DOES NOT LIST AND WHICH MEASURES BEST TODAY ---

ANCHOR ON A SWEEP MENTION ANYWHERE IN THE GATE - evidence OR notes, path OR bare filename - then label-match within that gate's evidence. Measured: 7 labels checked (PG1's 4, PG2's 3), 4 ignored (PG8's). ZERO false positives and ZERO false negatives against main today.

IT IS STILL NOT RECOMMENDED, and the reason is the whole point of this recon. It is correct today by accident of prose: a gate that is observation-backed and never happens to name the file is unchecked, and a gate that mentions the file in passing acquires a rule nobody intended. It is a measurement, not a contract. Recorded because a future reader will propose it and should see that it was priced.

--- SHAPE 3, FILE-SIDE ONLY: ITS PREMISE IS FALSE ---

IT REQUIRES THE SWEEP TO DECLARE ITS OWN GATE MAPPING. IT DOES NOT. Exactly ONE explicit declaration exists in the whole file: line 215, '→ A1, A2, A3, A4 all clean ⇒ PG1 PASSES.' Eight of the nine gates have none.

8 OF 25 ROWS MENTION A `PG` SOMEWHERE IN THEIR BLOCK, and that number is noise rather than a mapping: A4's block alone mentions PG1, PG2 AND PG4, because a block runs to the next heading and swallows the section prose that follows it. The genuine per-row declarations are written three different ways ('this is PG4's write', 'the row that moves PG2', '⇒ PG1 PASSES'), which is the prose-marker failure mode PORTAL-REHYDRATE 4.11 already names: it stops matching the day somebody rewords a sentence, and it FAILS OPEN.

Shape 3 WOULD have caught the instance this card comes from, and only because PG1 is the one gate with an explicit line. That is not coverage; it is one lucky row.

--- RECOMMENDED: SHAPE 1, STRUCTURED CITATION, WITH ONE CONDITION ---

THE CONDITION IS WHAT MAKES IT WORTH BUILDING: AN OPTIONAL FIELD FAILS OPEN. `observations: [{doc, row}]` as a purely optional array is checked only when present, so a gate that omits it passes unchecked - which is the defect this card exists to close, wearing a schema.

MAKE IT CLOSED BY KEYING ON THE EVIDENCE KIND. Measured on main: FOUR gates carry `evidence.kind == "screenshot"` - PG1, PG2, PG3, PG4 - and the other five carry pr, sha256, e2e. The rule then reads: A GATE WHOSE EVIDENCE IS `screenshot` MUST CARRY A NON-EMPTY `observations` ARRAY, EVERY CITED ROW MUST EXIST IN THE NAMED DOC, AND EVERY SLOT UNDER A CITED ROW MUST BE NON-BLANK. No prose is parsed, so the false-positive count is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION, and there is no gate the rule can silently skip.

BACK-FILL COST, MEASURED: FOUR gates, not two. PG1 and PG2 cite rows in prose already and are mechanical. PG3 AND PG4 CITE NO SWEEP ROW AT ALL despite being screenshot-backed - PG4's write is row C2 by the sweep's own heading and PG4's evidence never says so. Establishing what those two observed is real work and is the honest price of the rule, not an oversight to be waved through.

--- THE BLOCKER, WHICH MUST BE FIXED BEFORE ANY OF THIS SHIPS ---

A3'S THREE SLOTS. Until `OBSERVE-SWEEP.md` carries a stated contract - one slot per row, or 'every slot under a row must be filled' - the rule's central predicate is undefined for one of the 25 rows, and an undefined predicate on a verdict path resolves to whichever branch the implementer happened to write. Fixing the file is cheaper than teaching the rule to guess, and it is a DOC change with no code.

--- THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, per LEARNINGS entry 5 ---

THREE CONTROLS, and the third is the one that is usually forgotten:

  1. BLANK A4's slot on a scratch copy of the sweep, leave PG1 `pass`. THE RULE MUST GO RED. This reproduces the exact instance: seven days of a gate passing while its own observation slot was empty.

  2. Point a gate's `observations` at a row label that does NOT exist in the doc. THE RULE MUST GO RED - a citation to nothing is not a citation, and this is what catches a typo'd label silently satisfying the check.

  3. FILL EVERY SLOT IN THE FILE, then REMOVE the `observations` array from a screenshot-backed gate. THE RULE MUST STILL GO RED. Without this control the rule passes on a fully-observed file for the wrong reason - because there is nothing left to be blank - and would go green forever on the day somebody drops the field.

--- SCOPE BOUNDARY, RE-CHECKED ---

`validate-board.mjs` and `reconcile-board.mjs` are shared by BOTH boards. The rule keys on `launch_gate.conditions[].evidence.kind`, which the platform board also has, so it MUST be additive: no `observations` array means the rule does not fire unless the kind is `screenshot`, and the platform board's own gates would come into scope the moment one of them is screenshot-backed. THAT IS A FINDING, NOT A DETAIL - whoever builds this must run both validators before and after and paste both exit codes, or the portal board's new rule silently becomes the platform board's new rule.

--- WHAT THIS RECON DOES NOT ANSWER ---

Whether the rule is WORTH the four-gate back-fill is a judgement about how often this failure recurs, and one instance is one data point. The recon's answer is that shape 1 is the only one of the four that is a CONTRACT rather than a measurement; whether to spend it is the owner's call, and this card does not spend it.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

CARDED 2026-08-20 OUT OF LEARNINGS.md ENTRY 6. READ-ONLY RECON. NO BUILD ON THIS CARD UNTIL THE FEASIBILITY ANSWER IS WRITTEN DOWN.

THE INSTANCE IT COMES FROM. PG1's evidence field claimed "ITEM 15 / A4 PASS" dated 2026-08-12. A4 was not run that day; the owner ran A3's second half believing it was A4, and the genuine observation happened 2026-08-19. For seven days the gate passed on a false line while TWO committed documents disagreed with it: PG1's own notes field, which recorded "A4 NOT RUN" verbatim on the day, and docs/board/OBSERVE-SWEEP.md, whose A4 `Observed:` box was BLANK in a file that says at the top "a blank is not a pass". Nothing mechanical reads either.

THE RULE TO TEST FOR FEASIBILITY, stated as the prevention in LEARNINGS.md entry 6:
  (a) a gate's evidence must cite the observation document's FILLED line, not the document and not the row label;
  (b) any gate citing an observation whose `Observed:` slot is blank is UNPROVEN regardless of its verdict - a blank slot outranks a pass.

WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN, DERIVED FROM main THIS SESSION, so the recon does not start from zero:
  * OBSERVE-SWEEP.md carries 27 `Observed:` lines. Before this session ALL 27 were blank (`grep -c "Observed: \`_"` returned 27 of 27). A4 is now filled, so the count is 26 of 27. A rule that fires on "gate cites a blank row" is therefore checking a file that is almost entirely blank, and the answer to "what does it fire on today" is part of the feasibility question, not an afterthought.
  * Rows are `### A4 · <title>` headings and the slot is a fenced-backtick line beginning `Observed:`. Both are mechanically parseable as they stand; neither is a stable contract, and pinning them is part of the work if this proceeds.
  * THE NAIVE FORM DOES NOT WORK, and this is the finding that makes this a recon card rather than a build card. Extracting row labels with a regex over evidence prose produces FALSE POSITIVES: PG8's evidence names hops `A1`, `A2`, `A4`, `A5`-`A9`, `B6`, `B7` from a LATENCY TABLE that has nothing to do with the sweep, and PG4's names `D4` from an unrelated sentence. Of the nine gates, only PG1 cites `docs/board/OBSERVE-SWEEP.md` by path in its evidence; PG2 mentions the file only in its notes. The reconciler's own doctrine (reconcile-board.mjs, the comment above rule A) says a rule needing exemptions on the day it ships is a rule that does not work, so a bare label regex is disqualified before it is written.

THE THREE CANDIDATE SHAPES the recon should price, and it should recommend one or recommend none:
  1. STRUCTURED CITATION. Give gate evidence an optional `observations: [{doc, row}]` array and check THAT against the file. Exact, no prose parsing, and it costs a schema change plus a back-fill of the gates that already cite rows in prose.
  2. ANCHORED PROSE MATCH. Fire only when the evidence names the file by path, and then only on labels appearing within that citation's own line or block. Cheap, no schema change, and it misses PG2 (which cites the sweep in notes only) - a rule that is silent where it should speak, which is the §1.3 shape and must be weighed as such rather than waved through as "partial coverage".
  3. FILE-SIDE ONLY. Ignore gate evidence entirely; assert that every row the sweep marks as feeding a gate has a non-blank `Observed:` line before that gate may read `pass`. Inverts the direction, needs the sweep to declare its own gate mapping, and would have caught this instance.

DELIVERABLE OF THE RECON: a written answer in the card's notes naming the recommended shape, the false-positive count it would produce against main TODAY, and the negative control that would prove the rule red - per LEARNINGS.md entry 5, a control that changes nothing and reports a pass is worse than no control. NO CODE THIS RUN.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: docs/board/validate-board.mjs and docs/board/reconcile-board.mjs are shared by BOTH boards (portal and prelaunch). Anything proposed here is additive or it does not ship - a non-gate card, and the platform board, must stay valid untouched.

cards.title: CLEARED BY THE OWNER: the 21 untracked scripts are out of the production-credentialled worktree. git status there returns zero paths

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-15, cleared by the owner during the 0063 apply sitting on
2026-08-14 as a pre-flight step. Recorded at docs/migration-apply-0063.md section
3.1.

THE ARITHMETIC RECONCILES EXACTLY, which matters because this card's own
inventory had already corrected one count and said the count is the thing
somebody will check:
  20 archived (19 .mjs, 1 .ts) to /Users/ivan/osteojp-archive/prod-apply-strays-20260814,
     directory structure preserved
   1 removed without archive: packages/db/scripts/ficha-v5-only/osteopathy-v5.json,
     the sole file in that directory, untracked scratch - recorded rather than
     left as a silent discrepancy
  21 total, matching the inventory on this card line for line.

RE-DERIVED FROM THE MACHINE 2026-08-15, not transcribed from the report:
git -C .../osteojp-prod-apply status --porcelain --untracked-files=all returns
ZERO paths, HEAD reads 4b7fbc8, and the archive directory holds 20 files.

WHAT THE HAZARD WAS, so the closure is read for what it is: that tree is the ONLY
one whose shell holds production credentials, and after the allexport line every
one of those files was a single node <path> away from the live database. Roughly
half were writers. One carried a dead AUTORIZO in its filename, still reading as
authorised fifteen days after the single sitting it was authorised for. Three
were purge scripts whose WHERE clauses asserted a July schema that nine
migrations had since moved.

CORRECTED 2026-08-15, SAME DAY, BY STRATEGY. This evidence first read "the apply
protocol has no step that READS git status in that worktree". THAT IS WRONG. The
pre-flight block strategy validates before every apply OPENS with
`git status --short` (must print nothing) and `git cat-file -t <sha>` (must print
commit), and that pre-flight is exactly what caught these 21 files before the
0063 apply. The step existed; this terminal inferred its absence from the strays
having accumulated, which is reasoning from a symptom to a missing control that
was in fact present and working.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING, and it is a different defect: the pre-flight lived
ONLY in strategy's paste discipline and was committed nowhere. Correct, followed,
and one forgotten paste from not existing - the same failure mode as a ruling
that lives in chat. NOW COMMITTED at docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, section
"THE PRE-FLIGHT", with both expected outputs, both STOP conditions, and the rule
that strategy re-verifies the pin as the LAST action before the owner runs
anything (0061 and 0062 both proved that a moved sha which still RESOLVES is
worse than one that errors).

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-12 BY PURPLE, ON THE OWNER'S INSTRUCTION TO CARD IT RATHER THAN FIX
IT. NOTHING HAS BEEN DELETED, MOVED OR EDITED. Deleting files outside a scratch
directory is owner-confirmable under rule 12, and every one of these is outside
one.

=== THE EXACT INVENTORY, re-derived, not transcribed ===
`git -C /Users/ivan/Documents/Projects/GitHub/osteojp-prod-apply status
--porcelain --untracked-files=all` returns 21 untracked paths: 19 `.mjs`, 1
`.ts`, 1 `.json`. The dispatch said "22 .mjs files"; the true figure is 19
`.mjs` among 21 files. Correcting it because the disposition below is a
file-by-file decision and the count is the thing someone will check.

  AT packages/db/ (4)
    cyan-verify-jp-role-owner-READONLY-20260728.mjs
    green-jp-role-admin-to-owner-AUTORIZO-20260728.mjs
    green-pl06-readonly-blockers-and-idmap-20260728.mjs
    inc02-purge-teste-cb-lv-20260728.mjs
  AT packages/db/ (4 more, the 005x verifiers)
    verify-0050.mjs  verify-0051.mjs  verify-0052.mjs  verify-prod-apply.mjs
  AT packages/db/scripts/ (13)
    canary-cleanup-20260724.mjs
    canary-create-20260724.mjs
    create-diversos-20260724.mjs
    enumerate-dash-services-b1-20260724.mjs
    ficha-v5-only/osteopathy-v5.json
    purge-w12-incident-synthetic-20260724.mjs
    purge-w12-incident-synthetic-20260724-v2.mjs
    roster-w12-40-upsert-20260724.mjs
    seed-ficha-v5-only-20260724.ts
    seed-therapist-colours-20260727.mjs
    slot-granularity-both-60-20260724.mjs
    verify-prod-final-0042-purge-20260724.mjs
    verify-prod-final-0042-purge-v2-20260724.mjs

By intent, read from the names: 1 AUTORIZO, 3 purge, 2 seed/upsert, 1 create,
2 canary create/cleanup, 1 slot-granularity write, 8 verify/enumerate/READONLY.
Roughly half are writers.

=== WHY THIS IS A STANDING HAZARD AND NOT UNTIDINESS ===
1. THIS IS THE ONE TREE WITH PRODUCTION CREDENTIALS IN ITS SHELL. Every apply
   block runs `set -o allexport; source ~/osteojp-secrets/new-prod.env`. After
   that line, in that window, EVERY ONE OF THESE FILES IS ONE `node <path>`
   AWAY FROM PRODUCTION. Nothing else in the estate has that property; the
   PURPLE and AMBER trees never hold prod credentials.
2. THE AUTORIZO FILE CARRIES A DEAD AUTHORISATION IN ITS FILENAME.
   `green-jp-role-admin-to-owner-AUTORIZO-20260728.mjs` was authorised once, for
   one run, on 2026-07-28. The name still reads as authorised fifteen days later
   and will still read that way next year. An authorisation that does not expire
   with the sitting is a trap for whoever reads the directory next.
3. THE PURGE SCRIPTS ARE DESTRUCTIVE BY NAME AND WERE WRITTEN FOR A DATABASE
   STATE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. `inc02-purge-teste-cb-lv` and the two
   `purge-w12-incident-synthetic` scripts targeted specific rows in a July
   database. Nine migrations have landed since. Their WHERE clauses are
   assertions about a schema that has moved.
4. THE NOISE HIDES THE NEXT REAL FILE. `git status` in the apply worktree
   already prints 21 untracked paths. A 22nd, pasted in during a future sitting,
   does not stand out - and the apply protocol has no step that reads status.
5. RULE 7 SAYS THAT TREE IS FOR APPLYING. docs/migration-apply-0061.md:151 states
   it verbatim: "the prod-apply worktree is for applying, not for building." A
   script library is neither.

=== PROPOSED DISPOSITION, for the owner to accept, amend or refuse ===
RECOMMENDED - option A, and it is one command the OWNER runs, not PURPLE:
  MOVE the whole set, unchanged, to a dated archive OUTSIDE every worktree, e.g.
  ~/osteojp-archive/prod-scripts-20260812/, preserving relative paths. Nothing is
  read, nothing is deleted, nothing is judged, and every script stays recoverable
  by date. The apply tree goes to a clean `git status`, which restores property 4
  above at zero cost. THEN add one line to the apply runbook's pre-flight: the
  apply worktree must report a clean status before the credentials are sourced.
  Cheapest, reversible, and it removes the credential-adjacency for all 21 at
  once rather than triaging 21 files one at a time.

  Option B - triage first, archive second. Read all 21, promote the genuinely
  reusable read-only verifiers (verify-prod-apply.mjs looks like a permanent
  tool) into tracked `packages/db/scripts/` under review, archive the rest.
  Better end state, but it needs a reading session per file and it leaves the
  hazard live until that session happens. Worth doing AFTER A, never instead.

  Option C - delete. NOT RECOMMENDED and NOT PROPOSED as a default. These are the
  only record of several one-time production operations, and the audit value
  outlives the execution risk once they are out of the credentialed tree.

WHY THE GATE IS owner_authorizo: option A moves files outside a scratch
directory, which rule 12 makes owner-confirmable. PURPLE will not run it.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-15: POINT 4 ABOVE IS WRONG IN ITS LAST CLAUSE ===
Point 4 ends "and the apply protocol has no step that reads status". It does have
one, and it always did: the validated pre-flight opens with `git status --short`,
which must print nothing. That step is what caught these 21 files. The rest of
point 4 stands - noise does hide the next real file, which is why the STOP
condition is ANY line rather than any line that looks dangerous.

The real gap was that the pre-flight was uncommitted, living only in strategy's
paste discipline. It is now a committed section of
docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md. Left in place rather than rewritten, because
what a terminal believed on 2026-08-12 is part of why this card was written the
way it was.

cards.title: FIXED: a failed SMS send was a fourth distinguishable outcome on the endpoint designed to have three, arriving by uncaught exception. The route now absorbs any transport failure and still answers 204, and re-throws a MISCONFIGURED transport by class

evidence.ref:
FIXED 2026-08-13. Fix (a) from this card, taken on its own merits.

WHAT CHANGED, TWO FILES:
  request/route.ts - the unwrapped await requestCode(...) is wrapped. Any
    transport failure is caught, logged loudly, and the route still answers 204.
  otp-transport.ts - a new exported class OtpTransportMisconfigured, thrown where
    a plain Error was thrown when OTP_LIVE_SEND is armed with no credentials.

THE PREFIX IS THE SYMPTOM AND THE FIX IS NOT ABOUT IT. Every provider-side
failure fell through the same crack into the same 500 - suspended account,
exhausted balance, destination-country permission never enabled, Twilio's own
rate limiting. Catching at the route closes all of them at once. The tests are
written about THE TRANSPORT THROWING, never about a particular number, because a
test pinned to +351900000000 would pass while the next failure mode walked
through.

THE MISCONFIGURED CASE IS DISCRIMINATED BY CLASS, NEVER BY MESSAGE TEXT, and
that choice is load-bearing. A .includes("not configured") match couples the
route to prose anyone may reword AND IT FAILS OPEN: reword the message and a
total outage - the flag armed with no credentials, failing for EVERY patient -
starts being swallowed as a per-number delivery failure. A class survives
rewording and instanceof is checkable by the compiler. There is a test asserting
a plain Error carrying the same words is still absorbed.

EIGHT TESTS, apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/send-failure.test.ts:
  TWO ANTI-VACUOUS GUARDS - a permitted request really reaches requestCode, and
    the harness can actually make it throw. Without the second, the regression
    test would pass against a route with no try/catch at all.
  204 INSTEAD OF 500 when the transport throws - the regression guard.
  INDISTINGUISHABLE BYTE FOR BYTE from a successful send: same status, same body,
    same headers. A status-code assertion alone is not the property - a 204 with
    a different body or an extra header is still an oracle and would read as
    fixed in every status check.
  THE LOG CARRIES NO PHONE, NO NATIONAL NUMBER, NO TENANT, and asserts each
    absence separately (PII rule 7; the tenant identifies the clinic).
  THE LOG SAYS THE CODE ROW SURVIVES - requestCode writes the row BEFORE sending
    so a delivered code always has a record behind it, therefore a throwing send
    leaves a live undelivered row until its TTL. Bounded by the 3/hour per-phone
    limit, so not an exhaustion vector, but somebody reading that table later
    needs the sentence.
  MISCONFIGURED IS RE-THROWN rather than answered 204.
  CLASS NOT STRING - a plain Error with the same words is not an instance.

NEGATIVE ARM, RUN AND OBSERVED: with the try/catch removed, FOUR of the eight go
red - the 204, the byte-for-byte comparison, the log assertion and the code-row
assertion. Restored and re-run green.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, deliberately. It does not give an undeliverable number its
own pt-PT copy. That is fix (b) on this card, it is a PRODUCT question about
whether to add a distinguishable outcome, and the card says it does not gate (a).
A patient on an unroutable number now sees otp_sent - "if the number is
registered, we sent a code" - which is honest about what the server did and stops
telling them THE SERVICE is broken when the truth is about their number. The
three standing degradation bullets on the login screen already cover the case
without branching.

Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, unit 57 passed across the three otp route
suites and the full suite green, build 4/4.

cards.notes:
DISCRIMINATOR RESOLVED 2026-08-12. See evidence. The three-way ambiguity this card
described - unroutable-prefix 500, PORTAL_TENANT_ID unset, or the portal unable to
reach the API - is closed in favour of the first, by the owner logging in with his
own number at B0.1. Cost: nothing, because he was logging in anyway.

STATUS UNCHANGED OTHERWISE: still todo, still not built, still moves no gate. The
significant finding remains the fourth distinguishable outcome arriving by
exception, not the deliverability oracle.

--- prior notes below ---

=== OWNERSHIP AND GRADING, SET BY THE OWNER 2026-08-12 ===

OWNERSHIP: AMBER IS STOOD DOWN AND SINGLE-LANE IS IN FORCE, so
apps/api/lib/auth/otp* passes to PURPLE FOR THIS CARD ONLY. It reverts with the
lane if AMBER is stood back up. NOT TO BE BUILT TONIGHT: it moves no gate, and
LOOP 6 does.

=== THE SIGNIFICANT FINDING IS NOT THE ORACLE. THE OWNER RULED THIS EXPLICITLY,
    AND THE CARD IS RE-HEADED TO SAY SO. ===

The deliverability oracle is the LESSER half and stays graded LOW: what separates
an unassigned block from a real number is whether a CARRIER can route it, which
is a public fact from the numbering plan, and the endpoint still never queries
the patient table.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS IS THE SHAPE OF THE FAILURE:

  A 500 IS A FOURTH DISTINGUISHABLE OUTCOME ON AN ENDPOINT DESIGNED TO HAVE
  THREE, AND IT ARRIVES BY EXCEPTION RATHER THAN BY DECISION.

The route's own header states the design: 204 always, 400 for a malformed
number, 429 for rate limiting, and nothing else, because every additional
distinguishable outcome is a signal an attacker can read. The 500 was not
designed, argued for, or written down. It exists because
`await deps.transport.send(...)` at apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts:245 and
`await requestCode(...)` at request/route.ts:139 are both unwrapped, and
apps/api has no middleware.ts to catch what they throw.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOLLOW, AND BOTH ARE WORSE THAN THE ORACLE:

1. EVERY FUTURE TWILIO FAILURE MODE FALLS THROUGH THE SAME CRACK. Today the 500
   correlates with carrier routability. Nothing holds it there. A suspended
   account, an exhausted balance, a destination-country geo-permission that was
   never enabled, Twilio's own rate limiting - each becomes the identical 500
   through the identical unhandled rejection. Whatever the 500 currently
   discloses, it will disclose something else the first time the provider fails
   for a different reason, and no one will be watching.

2. IT TELLS A PATIENT THE SERVICE IS BROKEN WHEN THE TRUTH IS THEIR NUMBER
   CANNOT RECEIVE SMS. "Nao e possivel entrar neste momento. Tente novamente mais
   tarde ou contacte a clinica" invites a patient to wait and retry something
   that will never work. The honest answer already exists one case over:
   otp_landline says "O numero associado a sua ficha nao recebe SMS." The
   geographic case got copy; the unassigned case falls through to a service-fault
   message. That is a PG7 mis-attribution, on the patient's side of the screen.

3. THE CODE ROW SURVIVES THE FAILED SEND. requestCode writes the OTP row at :235
   and sends at :245, in that order deliberately ("Send AFTER the row exists", so
   a delivered code always has a record behind it). A THROWING SEND LEAVES A
   LIVE, UNUSED CODE ROW WITH NO DELIVERY. Bounded by the 3/hour per-phone limit
   and the TTL, so it is not an exhaustion vector - but it is a write that
   outlives the operation that justified it, and it will not be obvious to
   whoever next reads that table wondering why codes exist that nobody received.

=== SO THE FIX IS (a), AND ITS MERIT IS INDEPENDENT OF THIS NUMBER ===
Catch the transport throw at the route and still answer 204, logging loudly by
NAME (PG7, never the phone or the code). That restores the three-outcome design
and closes all four future Twilio failure modes at once, rather than the one
prefix that happened to be typed. It must not swallow the deliberate
configured-wrong throw the transport raises when OTP_LIVE_SEND is armed without
credentials - that one is meant to be loud.
Whether an unassigned prefix ALSO deserves its own pt-PT copy is a separate
product question and does not gate (a).

--- the original code-read investigation follows, unchanged ---

RAISED 2026-08-12 FROM THE OWNER'S A3 OBSERVATION. INVESTIGATED BY CODE READ ONLY.
NOTHING FIXED, NOTHING EDITED IN apps/. The dispatch said card and do not fix.

LANE: this is AMBER's. PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md section 1.2 assigns
`apps/api/lib/auth/otp*` to AMBER, and the fix lives there. PURPLE traced it and
wrote it down; PURPLE does not build it.

=== WHAT THE OWNER SAW ===
On A3, typing `900000000` and clicking "Enviar código" produced:
  "Nao e possivel entrar neste momento. Tente novamente mais tarde ou contacte
   a clinica."
The sweep predicted the "Código de 6 dígitos" screen. The prediction was wrong.

=== THE MECHANISM, TRACED END TO END THROUGH COMMITTED CODE ===
The string is `portal.auth.otp_unavailable`
(packages/i18n/src/portal/strings.pt.json:88). It has exactly two emitters, and
the CLICK identifies which: "Enviar código" is the SEND path, so it is
apps/portal/app/auth/login/actions.ts:71, reached when `requestOtp` returns
`'unavailable'`.

`requestOtp` (apps/portal/lib/auth/otp.ts) returns `'unavailable'` in exactly
three cases: PORTAL_TENANT_ID unset (:56 throws), the fetch to the API throws
(:96), or the API answered anything that is not 204 / 400 / 429 (:104).

THE FIRST TWO ARE NUMBER-INDEPENDENT. They would fail identically for the
owner's own mobile. Only the third can depend on which number was typed.

THE THIRD, WALKED FORWARD THROUGH THE API ROUTE
(apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts):
  - `normalizePhonePT` ACCEPTS `900000000` -> `+351900000000`. phone.ts:19 is
    `/^[29]\d{8}$/`; it does not enforce prefix assignment.
  - `isSmsCapablePT` ACCEPTS IT TOO, and this is the load-bearing step.
    otp-sms-capability.ts rejects `PT_GEOGRAPHIC_E164 = /^\+3512\d{8}$/` and
    nothing else. Its own comment states the choice out loud: "PREFIX-LEVEL
    ASSIGNMENT IS STILL NOT ENFORCED, deliberately... over-strictness here
    silently drops reachable patients." `90` is not an assigned mobile block,
    but it is not geographic either, so it passes.
  - Neither rate limit fires on a first request.
  - The route calls `requestCode(...)` at :139, UNWRAPPED.
  - `requestCode` (apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts:226-246) writes the code row, then
    at :245 calls `deps.transport.send(...)` - also UNWRAPPED.
  - `resolveOtpTransport()` returns the LIVE Twilio adapter, because
    OTP_LIVE_SEND is armed for this sweep by the owner's 2026-08-12 ruling.
  - Twilio cannot route an unassigned block. `client.messages.create` rejects.
  - Nothing catches it anywhere on the path. apps/api has no middleware.ts. The
    App Router turns an uncaught rejection in a route handler into a 500.
  - 500 is not 204, 400 or 429, so the portal maps it to `unavailable`.

=== THE TWO OTHER CANDIDATES ARE RULED OUT BY THE STRING ITSELF ===
  THE GLOBAL SEND CEILING (#865) IS NOT THIS. It returns 429 via
  `tooManyRequests` (limiter.ts:147-157), which the portal maps to
  `otp_rate_limited` - "Demasiadas tentativas. Aguarde alguns minutos e tente
  novamente." A DIFFERENT SENTENCE. The owner did not see it. Also arithmetic:
  the ceiling is 60/hour and 300/day (limiter.ts:229-230) and this sweep spends
  one.
  OTP_LIVE_SEND BEING OFF IS THE OPPOSITE OF THIS. With the flag off,
  `resolveOtpTransport` returns the test sink, which returns
  `{delivered: false}` and NEVER THROWS. The route would answer 204 and the
  owner would have reached the code screen - the sweep's original prediction.
  ARMING THE FLAG IS WHAT EXPOSED THIS. It was invisible behind the sink.

=== IS IT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REAL PATIENT NUMBER? YES. ===
An assigned, routable number (the test patient's, on a 9x block Twilio can
reach): Twilio accepts, nothing throws, route answers 204, portal shows the code
screen.
An unassigned block: 500, and the owner's banner.
THOSE ARE DIFFERENT SCREENS, SO THE ENDPOINT IS AN ORACLE FOR SOMETHING.

WHAT IT IS AN ORACLE FOR, AND THE GRADE:
  IT IS A DELIVERABILITY ORACLE. LOW severity.
  What separates the two outcomes is whether a CARRIER can route the number.
  That is a public fact: the Portuguese numbering plan is published by the
  regulator and says which blocks are assigned. Anyone can look it up for a
  number they typed themselves.
  IT IS NOT A PATIENT-LIST ORACLE, and the reason is structural rather than
  lucky: this endpoint never queries the patient table. The route header states
  it ("it never looks the phone up... WF-07 resolves the patient at CLAIM time,
  on verify") and `requestCode` bears it out - it writes a row keyed on
  `hashPhone`, and reads nothing. A REGISTERED and an UNREGISTERED routable
  number produce the IDENTICAL 204. The property PG1 item 3 exists to prove
  SURVIVES INTACT. The owner's "A3 PASS on the security property" is correct.

=== BUT THE 500 IS THE REAL FINDING, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE ORACLE ===
1. IT IS A FOURTH DISTINGUISHABLE OUTCOME ON THE ONE ENDPOINT WHOSE ENTIRE
   DESIGN IS TO HAVE AS FEW AS POSSIBLE, and it arrives by an uncaught
   exception rather than by a decision. Today it correlates with carrier
   routability. NOTHING KEEPS IT THERE. Every future Twilio-side failure -
   suspended account, exhausted balance, destination-country geo-permission not
   enabled, Twilio's own rate limit - falls through the same crack into the same
   500. The oracle is a symptom; the unwrapped `await` is the defect.
2. IT MIS-ATTRIBUTES THE FAULT TO THE PATIENT'S DETRIMENT, which is a PG7
   concern. A real patient who mistypes into an unassigned block is told THE
   SERVICE is unavailable and to try later. It will never work. The honest
   answer is the one `otp_landline` already gives for the geographic case:
   this number cannot receive SMS. The landline case has copy; the unassigned
   case falls through to a service-fault message.
3. THE CODE ROW SURVIVES THE FAILED SEND. `requestCode` creates the row at :235
   and sends at :245, in that order and deliberately so ("Send AFTER the row
   exists"). A throwing send leaves a live, unused code row behind. Bounded by
   the 3/hour per-phone limit and the TTL, so it is minor - but it is a write
   that outlives the operation that justified it.

=== WHAT PURPLE DID NOT DO, AND WHY THE FIX IS NOT OBVIOUS ===
NO CODE WAS CHANGED. The naive fix - tighten the prefix regex to the assigned
mobile blocks - IS THE ONE otp-sms-capability.ts ALREADY ARGUED AGAINST, in
writing, and reversing a written ruling is not PURPLE's call and not a code-read
deliverable. The defensible shapes, for AMBER to choose between:
  (a) CATCH THE TRANSPORT THROW AT THE ROUTE and still answer 204. Cheapest,
      restores the three-outcome design, and closes every future Twilio failure
      mode at once rather than this one number. Costs: a send failure becomes
      silent, so it MUST log loudly (names only, PG7) and it must not swallow the
      configured-wrong throw the transport raises deliberately.
  (b) CATCH IT AND RETURN A DEDICATED SIGNAL for undeliverable, reusing
      `invalid_input`/400 exactly as the landline case does. Honest to the
      patient, and safe under otp-sms-capability.ts's own published-numbering-plan
      argument - but it adds a distinguishable outcome on a live-send timing
      path, which is the thing the module was careful about.
  (c) BOTH: catch at the route (always), and decide separately whether an
      unassigned prefix deserves its own pt-PT copy.
RECOMMENDATION: (a) first and on its own merits, because the uncaught `await` is
a defect independent of this number. (b) is a product question about copy.

=== HOW TO CONFIRM THE MECHANISM AT ZERO COST, before anyone builds anything ===
DO NOT SPEND AN OTP REQUEST ON THIS. The portal logs the discriminator itself.
`logUnavailable` (apps/portal/lib/auth/otp.ts:63) writes one line per case:
  "[auth] otp/request: api answered 500"        -> the mechanism above, CONFIRMED
  "PORTAL_TENANT_ID is not set; ..."            -> environment, not this card
  a fetch/network message                       -> the portal cannot reach the API
Read the portal function log for 2026-08-12 at the time of the A3 click. One line
decides it. If it is either of the last two, THIS CARD IS WRONG and the finding
is an environment fault affecting every number.

cards.title: Three cards have now carried a false status because nothing reconciles merged PRs against the board - two caught 2026-08-11, a third (A2) caught 2026-08-12 only because a sweep happened to need the feature

evidence.ref:
CLOSED 2026-08-18 by docs/board/reconcile-board.mjs, wired into the REQUIRED
"Lint + typecheck + test" check as a step in the existing quality job. Not a new
job: a new job is a new check name and would not be in the required set, which is
the reason the "Test scripts" step beside it gives for the same choice.

THE FOURTH INSTANCE IS WHAT MADE IT URGENT, AND IT IS ON THIS CARD'S OWN TERMS.
This card's argument for high priority was that a stale card becomes a stale plan.
W13-06, W13-06a and W13-06b carried todo for six days after LOOP 6 shipped, and a
dispatch then named W13-06 as the next card to BUILD. Instance 3 idled a lane;
instance 4 dispatched work that was already done.

=== THE RULE THAT CATCHES THIS FAMILY NEEDS NO NETWORK, AND THAT IS THE FINDING ===
The three W13-06 cards CITED NO PR AT ALL. Every check built on "compare cited PR
numbers against merge state" - which is what this card asked for, and what I would
have written unprompted - would have stayed silent on them forever.

What gave them away was structural: three cards claiming to close PG6 while PG6
was already passing. So GATE-CLAIM is rule A, it is local, it runs even with no
GitHub access, and it is the rule with teeth. The PR-state rules are worth having
and they are not the ones that caught the expensive instance.

=== WHAT IT DOES ===
  A gate-claim   card says "Closes PGn", PGn passes, card is not shipped   local
  B shipped-unmerged  shipped on evidence.kind "pr", no cited PR merged    api
  C stale-card   unfinished card citing a MERGED PR (instances 1, 2, 3)    api
  D pr-missing   a citation pointing at a PR that does not exist           api

Exit 0 in sync, 1 on any mismatch, 2 if it could not ask - never 0 on a check it
did not perform. --offline runs rule A alone and says so in its output.

=== THE ESCAPE IS A FIELD, NEVER A PHRASE ===
A card may legitimately stay open after its PR merges: WF-03 closes a
staff-visible card on the owner's DEPLOYED SCREEN, not on green CI. That escape is
an explicit open_on_purpose: "<reason>" on the card. A prose marker matched out of
the notes would stop matching the day somebody rewords a sentence, and it would
fail OPEN - the check goes quiet and reports success, which is every defect
PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 lists. A missing field cannot be reworded.

Acknowledged cards are PRINTED IN FULL on every run rather than skipped, because
an exemption nobody sees is an exemption nobody revisits - which is how four cards
sat stale for a week.

=== FIRST FULL RUN, 2026-08-18, over 163 cards and 60 cited PRs ===
NINE mismatches across seven cards. Two were resolved as genuine deliberate holds
(W13-03 and LE-auth-recovery-deadend, both of which say so in their own words),
FOUR were reported to the owner unresolved rather than flipped by this terminal
(LE-env-sweep-scope, LE-portal-supabase-residue, LE-trusted-device-revoke,
LE-e2e-nif-edit-404 - all four carry a STALE-REF CORRECTION saying the work is on
main and state no reason to remain open), and ONE was a false positive in the
check itself, corrected on the spot: INC-11 shipped on kind "journal" - a
production read - while its prose named the still-open #917 where the failure was
first seen. Rule B now applies only to cards whose evidence IS a PR. A rule that
fires on narration teaches people to strip citations, which is worse than the
staleness it was written to catch.

=== ITS OWN PROOF ===
docs/board/reconcile-board.test.mjs, 18 assertions, in pnpm test:scripts and
therefore in the required check. Every rule is asserted in BOTH directions - the
state that must be flagged and the adjacent state that must not be - plus a
counterweight that a genuinely in-sync board produces nothing at all. A check's
failure mode is silence, and silence is indistinguishable from a board that is
in sync.

cards.notes:
=== A KNOWN BLIND SPOT, DEMONSTRATED 2026-08-20. THE CARD STAYS SHIPPED. ===

THE SEVENTH FALSE CARD (LE-portal-booking-home-clinic-preselect, finished by #855 and carrying "CARDED, NOT BUILT" for nine days) WAS NOT CAUGHT BY THE RECONCILER, AND COULD NOT HAVE BEEN. Its stale-card rule keys on the PRs a card CITES; that card cited none. Its gate-claim rule keys on the gate a card CLAIMS; that card claimed none. A card written BEFORE the work and never touched after trips neither rule, and reconcile-board.mjs’s own header already names this as the third shape of staleness.

WHY THIS IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN AS A DEFECT: this card closed on the reconciler existing and running in a REQUIRED check, which it does, and the rules it has are the right rules. What must not happen is a future reader concluding from "reconciler shipped, board clean" that false cards are SOLVED. They are not. A clean reconciler says nothing about a card that cites nothing - and that is the shape that has now cost a dispatch twice (the A2 instance and this one). The only instrument for it is the human rule at the top of PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md: re-derive every card from main before building it.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

CLOSED 2026-08-18. The card asked for the reconciliation nobody was doing; the
answer is docs/board/reconcile-board.mjs, running in the required CI check and
named as mandatory in PORTAL-REHYDRATE's boot sequence.

ONE THING THIS CARD ASSUMED THAT TURNED OUT TO BE WRONG, and it is the reason the
fix is not the fix it asked for: every instance on this card is a card whose
citation was stale, so the obvious check is "compare cited PRs against merge
state". The fourth instance cited NOTHING. A PR-comparison check would have missed
it entirely. The rule that catches it compares a card's own claim - "Closes PG6" -
against the gate's state, needs no network, and would have caught it on day one.

--- original card below, unedited ---

PRIORITY RAISED TO HIGH 2026-08-12 BY OWNER DIRECTION, and the reason is worth
keeping because it is not "three is more than two":

  AN UNRECONCILED BOARD MAKES EVERY PLAN BUILT ON IT UNSOUND, AND THIS ONE COST
  A LOOP OF HELD WORK.

Instances 1 and 2 were understatements - a card said a PR was open when it was
merged. Annoying, self-correcting on the next read. INSTANCE 3 WAS DIFFERENT IN
KIND: PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md built a SEQUENCING RULE on the false status, holding
LOOP 6 behind an A2 that had already shipped, and two dispatches then instructed
"DO NOT START A2" on the strength of it. The strategy layer carried the false
premise forward twice without checking the code. A stale card became a stale
plan, and the plan idled the loop lane.

That is the argument for high: the cost is not the wrong card, it is everything
downstream that reasons from it.

--- original card below ---

RAISED 2026-08-12. THE PATTERN, NOT THE THREE INSTANCES, IS THE CARD.

INSTANCE 1 and 2, caught 2026-08-11 during the gate reconciliation:
  LE-env-sweep-scope        recorded "#843 OPEN"; #843 merged 2026-08-07.
  LE-portal-supabase-residue recorded "#841 OPEN"; #841 merged 2026-08-07.
Both were four days stale and both were caught only because a human was
re-reading every card for a different reason.

INSTANCE 3, caught 2026-08-12:
  LE-portal-booking-therapist-step (A2) read todo / "CARDED, NOT BUILT" while
  #857 (5e45653) had shipped it. Caught ONLY because the observation sweep needed
  to know whether a patient can pick a therapist. Nobody was auditing.

WHY THIS ONE COST MORE THAN THE OTHER TWO. The first two were cards recording an
OPEN PR that was actually merged - the work was done and the board understated
it. A2 was different: PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md built a SEQUENCING RULE on top of the
false status ("A2 -> LOOP 6 -> LOOP 7 -> LOOP 8", with LOOP 6 explicitly held
because "a matrix built before A2 lands is wrong on arrival"). Two dispatches
then instructed "DO NOT START A2". A false card became a false plan, and the
plan held up the loop lane.

THE MECHANISM IS ABSENT, NOT BROKEN. Nothing in this repo compares
`gh pr list --state merged` against card evidence. The validator checks
INTERNAL consistency - lane derivation, evidence presence, the readiness count -
and it is good at that. It cannot check whether a card's claim about the WORLD is
true, and every one of these three failures was exactly that.

PROPOSED SHAPE, deliberately small:
  A script, docs/board/reconcile-prs.mjs, that for every card extracts `#\d+`
  from evidence.ref and notes, asks `gh pr view` for each PR's state and merge
  commit, and reports any card where a referenced PR is MERGED while the card
  reads todo/in_flight, or where the card claims OPEN and the PR is merged.
  REPORT ONLY, never auto-edit: the reason a card is behind may be that the last
  session's REPORT was wrong too, and silently flipping the card hides that from
  the owner. Rehydrate section 3 already makes this point about item 4.
  Run it at boot, alongside the validator, as part of the mandatory status
  report - which is where all three of these would have been caught on day one.

NOT PROPOSED: folding it into validate-board.mjs. That script is offline, pure and
fast, and is run before every board commit; adding network calls to `gh` would
make a commit gate depend on GitHub being reachable and on an auth token.
Separate script, separate invocation.

cards.notes:

RECEPCAO - one account, correctly RECEPTION-scoped.

broken fan-out, and a non-RECEPTION account with an empty queue is D4 working as

cards.title: PG9 cannot close without an automated a11y checker and this repo has none - LOOP 8's first DoD line needs a new third-party dependency, which rule 13 makes owner-confirmable

evidence.ref: RULED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-12: @axe-core/playwright, ruleset wcag22aa. The recommendation was accepted with its own rationale - the e2e harness is already Playwright, so this adds a LIBRARY rather than a second runner, a second config and a second CI job. PG9 IS UNBLOCKED and LOOP 8 may start. The dependency is added under rule 13 with this ruling as the authorisation; the install lands with LOOP 8's first PR, not before.

cards.notes:
RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-12. @axe-core/playwright, ruleset wcag22aa.

WHY THE CARD EXISTED AT ALL, recorded so the pattern repeats: LOOP 8's first
machine-verifiable DoD line requires "an automated a11y check ... with the tool
and ruleset named", and the repo had NO such tool - the only a11y dependency
anywhere was @storybook/addon-a11y, an authoring addon with no CI signal. So the
LAST GATE could not be closed without a new third-party dependency, which rule 13
makes owner-confirmable. Asking before LOOP 8 started cost one line in a dispatch.
Discovering it three days in would have cost the loop.

WHAT THE TOOL DOES NOT DO, carried forward so PG9 is not over-claimed: automated
a11y checking catches roughly a third to a half of WCAG failures. Contrast,
accessible names, landmarks and target size are machine-checkable. "Focus not
obscured" and "consistent help" largely are not. LOOP 8's per-screen audit table
is what covers the rest, and the DoD asks for BOTH - the tool alone is not the
gate.

--- prior notes below ---

RAISED 2026-08-12 FROM THE HANDOVER ANALYSIS. ASKED NOW RATHER THAN THREE DAYS INTO
LOOP 8, because it is a decision and not a task.

WAVE-13.md's LOOP 8 section 3, first machine-verifiable line: "An automated a11y
check passes on every portal screen, WITH THE TOOL AND RULESET NAMED."

THE REPO HAS NO SUCH TOOL. Re-derived against main @ a377f6a by searching every
package.json in the workspace: the only a11y-related dependency anywhere is
`@storybook/addon-a11y` in packages/ui. That is a Storybook AUTHORING addon. It
runs in the Storybook UI, it is not wired to any portal screen, and it produces
no CI signal. No axe, no @axe-core/playwright, no pa11y, no Lighthouse CI.

SO PG9 - THE LAST GATE - CANNOT BE CLOSED WITHOUT ADDING A DEPENDENCY, and rule
13 says no new third-party dependency without asking first.

RECOMMENDED: `@axe-core/playwright`, ruleset `wcag22aa`.
  WHY: the e2e harness is already Playwright, so it adds a library rather than a
  second runner, a second config and a second CI job. axe-core is the engine
  behind most other options anyway, so choosing a wrapper that is not Playwright's
  means running the same engine through more machinery. It asserts per-screen
  inside specs that already navigate those screens.
  WHAT IT COSTS: one devDependency in apps/web, and e2e runtime grows by roughly
  the number of portal screens times one axe scan.
  WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated so the gate is not over-claimed: automated a11y
  checking catches perhaps a third to a half of WCAG failures. Contrast, names,
  landmarks and target size are machine-checkable; "focus not obscured" and
  "consistent help" largely are not. LOOP 8's per-screen audit table is what
  covers the rest, and the DoD asks for both.

THE ALTERNATIVE, if the answer is no: PG9's first DoD line has to be renegotiated
