cards.title: The Nova marcação availability panel lists a PENDING pedido under "Ocupado", contradicting D1, Option B, and the pedido queue header on the same product

evidence.ref:
CLOSED 2026-08-13 AS ALREADY FIXED. NO CODE CHANGE WAS MADE OR NEEDED.
The fix is be0e1d4 (PR #836, merged 2026-08-07), the W13-04a / JP option B
change, which predates this card by five days.

=== RE-DERIVED FROM THE CODE ON 2026-08-13, NOT ACCEPTED FROM THE DISPATCH ===
The panel's whole chain was walked before this card was touched:
  apps/web/app/agenda/availability-panel.tsx:122 renders the "Ocupado:" label
    (packages/i18n key appointment.availabilityBooked) from day.booked
  <- getTherapistDayAvailability, the server action, which calls
  <- getTherapistAvailability in apps/web/lib/scheduling/day-availability.ts
  <- readBookedRows, whose predicate list ALREADY CARRIES, at line 113:
       sql`not public.is_unconfirmed_pedido(${appointments.id})`
THE PANEL DOES ROUTE THROUGH THE EXCLUSION. An unconfirmed pedido is not in
day.booked and cannot be printed under Ocupado.

THE CARD'S OWN "WHERE TO LOOK" HYPOTHESIS WAS HALF RIGHT, and recording which
half matters for the next reader. It predicted the panel "selects appointments by
'not cancelled' rather than by the blocking-status set". NON_BLOCKING =
["cancelled","no_show"] is indeed a not-cancelled list and it IS still there, but
the pedido exclusion sits immediately beside it as a second predicate. Reading
only the first line would have confirmed the hypothesis and produced a fix for a
bug that was not there.

=== THE TWO AXES, WHICH IS WHAT ACTUALLY EXPLAINS THE OBSERVATION ===
The board recorded a real screen. The screen was not wrong. TWO ORTHOGONAL
COLUMNS on the appointment carry the word "pending" and they answer different
questions (packages/db/src/schema.ts, and the comment at :50 says it in the
source: "ORTHOGONAL to appointment_status ... Never collapse the two"):

  status              appointment_status    scheduled | confirmed | completed |
                                            cancelled | no_show
                      WHERE THE APPOINTMENT IS IN ITS LIFECYCLE. This is the
                      axis occupancy is decided on.

  confirmation_state  appointment_confirmation_state
                                            pending | confirmed | declined
                      DID THE PATIENT ANSWER THE REMINDER. Added by 0024, and
                      it is NOT the pedido axis.

is_unconfirmed_pedido (0059, lines 139-148) reads the FIRST axis only:
    a.status = 'scheduled' AND n.kind = 'appointment_request'
It never looks at confirmation_state.

SO: once reception CONFIRMS a pedido the row becomes status = 'confirmed', the
predicate goes false, and the slot correctly reads Ocupado. Its
confirmation_state is STILL 'pending', because that column tracks the patient
answering a reminder and defaults to 'pending' on every appointment ever
created. REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND is false, so no patient has ever answered one, so
EVERY appointment in the system currently reads "pending" on that axis. A screen
showing "Confirmacao pendente" beside a slot marked Ocupado is both surfaces
telling the truth about different questions. The STAFF-01 report carries the same
pairing in its own header line: "Agendada / Confirmacao pendente".

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE ===
The two rulings the card cited are unaffected and still hold: D1
(pedido-versus-pedido stacking) and JP's option B (the slot is not reserved until
reception confirms). Both are ENFORCED by the same be0e1d4 predicate this close
rests on. The pedido queue header, "O horario so fica reservado depois de
confirmado", is accurate.

NO LABELLING CARD IS RAISED, per the owner's instruction. The card's open product
question, whether a pending pedido should appear as a distinct third state
("Pedido pendente") rather than be absent from the panel, is NOT answered here
and is not carded. It is a product choice with no defect behind it, and the
surfaces currently agree.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-12 FROM THE OWNER'S SWEEP. RULED NON-BLOCKING AND POST-HANDOVER BY HIM.

OBSERVED: the Nova marcação availability panel showed
  Ocupado 09:00-09:55, 11:00-11:55
where the 11:00 row was STILL A PENDING PEDIDO, not a confirmed appointment.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A DISPLAY PREFERENCE: TWO STAFF-VISIBLE SURFACES ON
THE SAME PRODUCT CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. The pedido queue header states, in
pt-PT, "O horário só fica reservado depois de confirmado." The availability panel
says that same slot is Ocupado. A receptionist reading both cannot act on either.

AND IT CONTRADICTS TWO RULINGS, not just a header:
  D1-pedido-versus-pedido-stacking - two pending pedidos may coexist on one
    window, because a pending pedido does not hold the slot.
  JP's OPTION B - the slot is not reserved until reception confirms.
Migration 0059 encodes it: `is_unconfirmed_pedido` keys on
`status = 'scheduled'` plus a request row, and 0061's EXCLUDE deliberately keys
on `status = 'confirmed'` ONLY, so the DATABASE agrees a pending pedido blocks
nothing. The panel is the one surface that disagrees.

WHY IT BLOCKS NOTHING, which is the owner's ruling and is correct: PL-11 makes
availability ADVISORY, never a hard block. The save in B2.1 went through over
this very panel. So the panel misinforms; it does not prevent. Nothing on the
launch gate depends on it.

WHERE TO LOOK when this is taken: the panel's occupancy query almost certainly
selects appointments by "not cancelled" rather than by the blocking-status set.
apps/api/lib/appointments/blocking-status.ts is the canonical predicate and
blocking-status.test.ts is its test; the fix is likely to route this panel through
it rather than to write a new condition. CHECK FIRST whether the panel is meant
to show pending pedidos in a DISTINCT style rather than as Ocupado - showing them
as a third state ("Pedido pendente") may be better product than hiding them,
since reception does want to know a request exists. THAT IS A PRODUCT QUESTION and
if the answer is not obvious from the surrounding surfaces, log it rather than
guess.

cards.title: An agenda left open at reception never learns of a portal booking - apps/api cannot revalidatePath into apps/web, so the hop has no push, no poll and no invalidation. Not a double-booking risk

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN ON THE DEPLOYED /agenda SCREEN, 2026-08-22, AS THE QUEUE STEP WAS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN: the chip MOVES when Atualizar is pressed, and does NOT advance on its own. Both halves, which is what the step required and what a frozen chip would fail. Build half: option (c), the freshness chip and refresh control, 8 assertions and three negative controls.

cards.notes:
=== BUILT 2026-08-20, OPTION (c). THE LAG IS UNCHANGED; THE SCREEN NO LONGER HIDES IT. ===

Status is in_flight rather than shipped because WF-03 applies: this is two new
controls in reception's agenda toolbar and it closes on the owner's screen.
VERIFY-QUEUE item 3, which puts that queue AT the WF-09 trigger of three.

WHAT A READER SHOULD NOT CONCLUDE: the agenda still does not learn about a
portal booking on its own. Options (a) polling and (b) an invalidation channel
are both unbuilt, deliberately, and (a) remains the honest next step if
reception finds the lag costly in practice. What changed is that the picture's
age is now visible instead of assumed.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

RAISED 2026-08-12 BY LOOP 7. IT IS HOP A9 OF docs/recon/W13-07-sync-trace.md, carded
separately on owner direction so PG8's trace records the FACT and this card owns
the FIX.

THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. A portal booking is
written by `apps/api`. The staff agenda is rendered by `apps/web`. They are
SEPARATE NEXT.JS DEPLOYMENTS on separate Vercel projects (osteojp-api,
osteojp-platform). `revalidatePath` invalidates the CALLING deployment's own
cache, so apps/api could not invalidate /agenda even if it called it - and it
never calls it, which is now asserted by
apps/api/lib/exposure/sync-single-source.test.ts.

WHAT IT MEANS IN THE CLINIC: an agenda open on a screen at reception does not
learn about a portal booking. It learns when someone navigates, reloads, or
triggers router.refresh() (agenda-view.tsx:322,337). The data is never STALE ON
READ - the agenda page is dynamic SSR and re-queries every request - but NOTHING
PROMPTS THE READ. Latency is therefore "however long until a human interacts",
which is unbounded.

IT IS NOT A DOUBLE-BOOKING RISK, and this is why it is medium rather than high.
The protection is the LOCK and the CONSTRAINT, not the render: two writers
contending for one window are serialised at the database and one is refused
(slot-lock-concurrency.test.ts:264,274), and since 0061 a second confirmed
overlap is refused outright. A stale screen cannot CREATE a double booking. It can
only show a receptionist an out-of-date picture - which is a real UX cost when
they are on the phone to a patient, and that is the whole of this card.

THE OTHER DIRECTION IS FINE: every portal API read is `cache: 'no-store'`, so a
staff booking is reflected on the portal's next read. Asserted in the same suite.

OPTIONS, none chosen, all cross-app so none is trivial:
  a. POLL the agenda on a visible-tab interval. Cheapest, honest, and bounded by
     the interval. Costs a query per interval per open agenda.
  b. A SHARED INVALIDATION CHANNEL - apps/api publishes, apps/web subscribes and
     calls router.refresh(). Correct, and it is new infrastructure.
  c. ACCEPT IT AND SAY SO ON THE SCREEN - a "last updated HH:MM" stamp with a
     refresh control, so the picture's age is visible rather than assumed.
     Smallest honest change and it removes the wrong belief rather than the lag.
RECOMMENDED: (c) first, because it is small and it stops the screen lying about
its own freshness, then (a) if reception still finds it costly. (b) is not worth
new infrastructure for a surface that cannot cause the harm it looks like it
could.

=== NOT OBSERVED AT THE 2026-08-22 SITTING. STAYS in_flight. ===

The freshness chip and the refresh control were NOT among the items the owner
confirmed. RECORDED AS NOT OBSERVED rather than left silent, because this card
sat in the same sitting as three that were, and a card that goes unmentioned in
a session report reads afterwards as one that failed.

IT WAS NOT RUN. It did not fail. Nothing about the build has changed and nothing
is owed on it but a pair of eyes.

THE OBSERVATION THIS NEEDS IS UNUSUALLY EASY TO GET WRONG, which is worth
restating before the next sitting rather than after it. The property is that the
stamp is the READ instant, not the render instant. A chip showing a plausible
recent time satisfies a casual look and would ALSO be satisfied by the exact
defect this card exists to prevent - a client-derived stamp that always reads
"now" and is therefore freshest precisely when the data is stalest.

THE STEP, AS THE QUEUE WROTE IT: THE CHIP MUST MOVE WHEN Atualizar IS PRESSED,
AND MUST NOT ADVANCE ON ITS OWN. Two halves, and the FIRST one is the primary
assertion.

[THIS PARAGRAPH REPLACED AN INVERTED RESTATEMENT. SEE THE CORRECTION BELOW.]

=== CLOSED ON OBSERVATION 2026-08-22. AND I HAD RESTATED THE STEP INVERTED. ===

OBSERVED: the chip MOVES when Atualizar is pressed, and does NOT advance on its
own. Confirmed by Ivan as the queue step was ORIGINALLY WRITTEN.

THE CORRECTION, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY EDITED. On 2026-08-24 this card
carried a restatement of the observation step that led with the negative half -
"THE CHIP MUST STILL SHOW THE ORIGINAL TIME... Then press the refresh control" -
and called that "THE STEP". The queue step is TWO halves and the PRIMARY one is
the positive: THE CHIP MUST MOVE WHEN Atualizar IS PRESSED. The paragraph above
has been corrected in place and this note says what it used to say, because a
silently edited instruction is worse than a wrong one.

WHY IT IS NOT A PEDANTIC CORRECTION: A CHIP FROZEN FOREVER SATISFIES THE
INVERTED VERSION PERFECTLY. "It still shows the original time" is exactly what a
stamp that never updates at all would do, and an observer following my wording
could have watched a completely broken control and passed it. The assertion I
led with is satisfied by the feature being absent - which is the vacuous-guard
family this project has now recorded four times, and the first time I have
written one into an OBSERVATION STEP rather than into a test.

THE TWO HALVES DO DIFFERENT WORK AND BOTH ARE NEEDED. "Moves on Atualizar" proves
the control is wired and the stamp is re-taken. "Does not advance on its own"
proves the stamp is the READ instant rather than a client-side new Date() that
re-evaluates on every render - the inversion that would make the screen most
confident about its freshness exactly when the data is stalest. Either alone
passes a broken build: the first passes a chip that also drifts, the second
passes a chip that is dead.

BOTH WERE OBSERVED. The card closes on the step as written, not as I restated it.

cards.title: 39 vitest suites can skip inside a passing required check with nothing reddening - three of them are cited as enforcement points on PG6 and PG8

cards.notes:
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-12. The three gate-cited suites were verified as EXECUTED and are now
hard-required. The remaining 36 are tracked on ACC-skippable-suites-unguarded.

--- original ---

COUNTED 2026-08-12 DURING THE PG8 SKIP INVESTIGATION. NOT FIXED, ON DISPATCH
INSTRUCTION - the number IS the deliverable, because it is the true size of the
problem that let PG8's direction A skip green twice.

THE COUNT, and the commands that produced it:
  grep -rl "skipIf|describe.skip|it.skip|test.skip" apps/ packages/ --include="*.test.ts"
    -> 52 skippable suites
  hard-required in .github/scripts/assert-rls-executed.mjs
    -> 14
  DIFFERENCE -> 39 SKIPPABLE AND GUARDED BY NOTHING
  e2e: 2 of 57 specs carry a skip; sync-portal-agenda is now guarded.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT HYGIENE. THREE of the 39 are cited as enforcement points
in this project's own gate documents:
  portal-booking-slot-parity.test.ts   PG8, "a booked window drops out of the
                                       offered list" (W13-07 trace section 4)
  slot-lock-concurrency.test.ts        PG8, the contention negative control
  otp-revoke.db.test.ts                PG6, MH-04 trusted-device revoke
A citation naming a suite that SKIPPED is worth exactly as much as a citation
naming the wrong suite, which is the defect the LOOP 6 audit spent a session on.
This is that defect one layer down.

THE FIX IS MECHANICAL AND THE PATTERN EXISTS TWICE OVER: extend
assert-rls-executed.mjs's SUITES list, and/or the new
assert-e2e-executed.mjs HARD_REQUIRED list. Both take an entry per suite with a
written reason, which is deliberate - the list records a DECISION that a suite is
gate-bearing, not an inventory of every test.

DO NOT ADD ALL 39. Most are not gate-bearing and hard-requiring them would make
the guard a maintenance tax that someone eventually disarms. START WITH THE THREE
ABOVE, because a gate document already claims them.

THE DEEPER QUESTION, worth one paragraph of thought before the mechanical fix:
these suites skip on `!live` (no DATABASE_URL). In the DB-gated CI job they DO
have a database, so the skip is a local-development affordance that happens to be
load-bearing in CI. An alternative to per-suite allowlisting is to make `live`
FAIL rather than skip whenever CI is set - one change, all 52 suites, no list to
maintain. That is the same shape as guard 1 on the sync spec and it is probably
the better answer. It is not done here because it would redden any suite that is
currently skipping for a legitimate reason in CI, and finding those is the work.

cards.title: 36 vitest suites can still skip inside a passing required check with nothing reddening - counted, not fixed. The rule from here: a suite cited as a gate enforcement point is hard-required at the moment it is cited

evidence.ref:
RESOLVED 2026-08-18 by RECON-02, PR #946 (squashed to 698c734), and RE-MEASURED 2026-08-19 before closing rather than assumed.

THE POPULATION IS EXACTLY TWO KINDS, counted file by file across apps/ and packages/:
  48 suites gate on `!live` (DATABASE_URL), in two spellings - `describe.skipIf(!live)` in packages/db and `const d = live ? describe : describe.skip` in the app-level .db.test.ts files. ALL 48 ARE NOW COVERED: db-tests.yml sets DATABASE_URL and runs them, and RECON-02's derived pass in assert-rls-executed.mjs reddens the job if ANY test in ANY of the three DB-gated reports did not run. Not a list - every suite is in scope the moment it appears in a report, so one added next month is covered on arrival.
  3 suites carry a bare `describe.skip`, all deliberate and all documented in place: the IfThenPay, InvoiceXpress and Stripe sandbox happy-paths. Each waits on owner-provisioned vendor credentials and each carries the same instruction - do NOT un-skip without the keys, the rule is do not hit the live sandbox.

SO THE CARD'S "36 SUITES CAN SKIP WITH NOTHING REDDENING" IS CLOSED. There is no suite left that skips inside a required check where a skip would be a lie about coverage.

=== THE MECHANISM IS NOT THE ONE THE 2026-08-12 RULING PRESCRIBED, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED ===
The ruling said: make `live` FAIL rather than skip when CI is set, one change over all the suites. RECON-02 instead reads the DB-gated job's vitest reports and reddens on any not-run test.

IT REACHES THE SAME GUARANTEE WITH LESS BLAST RADIUS. The ruling's mechanism keys on `process.env.CI`, which is set in ci.yml too - where DATABASE_URL is deliberately ABSENT and these suites are MEANT to skip. Applied literally it reddens ci.yml for all 48 on the first run, which the ruling itself anticipated ("EXPECT IT TO GO RED THE FIRST TIME"). The report-based check reddens only where a suite was actually supposed to run, so it needed no such event.

AND IT IS THE MORE HONEST INSTRUMENT, for the reason this card's own criterion F names. A source-level check matches TEXT: the first draft of RECON-02 grepped for skip markers and immediately matched a DOC COMMENT describing a deleted suite - a MENTION, not a USE. A vitest report cannot make that mistake, because a test either ran or it did not.

=== WHAT REMAINS UNCOVERED, STATED PLAINLY ===
ONE RESIDUAL, and it is a memory problem rather than a guard problem: when the vendor credentials finally arrive, nothing will remind anyone to un-skip those three sandbox suites. A guard cannot help - the suites are correctly skipped today and there is no signal to key on. Carded as LE-sandbox-suites-unskip-on-credentials so it is attached to the event that resolves it rather than buried in a closed card.

ONE CLASS NOT STRUCTURALLY CLOSED: a suite that NO job runs produces no report entry, so the derived pass cannot see it. That is the shape the storage suite had. The population is empty today - that suite was deleted on the owner's Option B ruling - but the class is real. Not built: closing it needs ci.yml to emit a JSON report and a whole-repo collection check, which is a change to a required workflow for a class with zero current members. Named here so a future session finds the reasoning rather than the gap.

cards.notes:
=== RULED 2026-08-12. THE STRUCTURAL FIX, NOT THE HAND-LIST. NOT RE-LITIGATED. ===

TAKE THE STRUCTURAL FIX: make \`live\` FAIL rather than skip when CI is set. ONE
change covering all 52 suites, no list to maintain.

THE REASON, in the ruling own words: HAND-LISTING 36 GUARANTEES A 37TH NEXT MONTH.
A list is a maintenance tax that decays silently, and a decayed guard is worse
than none because it reads as coverage. The three suites hard-required today were
found by accident, during an unrelated investigation - that is not a process.

SEQUENCING, ALSO RULED: IT RUNS AFTER PG9, NOT BEFORE. It will redden suites that
skip for legitimate reasons in CI, and finding those is real work. THAT WORK DOES
NOT SIT IN FRONT OF THE LAST GATE. Queued as build-bucket item (e), after INC-09
and the two SEC cards.

WHAT THE FIX LOOKS LIKE, so the next session does not redesign it: the suites
gate on \`const live = Boolean(process.env.DATABASE_URL)\` and then
\`describe.skipIf(!live)\`. In the DB-gated CI job a database IS present, so the
skip is a LOCAL-DEVELOPMENT AFFORDANCE that happens to be load-bearing in CI. The
change is a shared helper - a suite that would skip while \`process.env.CI\` is set
must instead FAIL, naming itself. Same shape as guard 1 on the sync spec, and
keyed on CI, which this repo does not set and therefore cannot silence.

EXPECT IT TO GO RED THE FIRST TIME AND BUDGET FOR THAT. Every suite that reddens
is either (a) a suite that should have been running and was not, which is the
find, or (b) a suite with a legitimate second gate, which needs that gate stated
in code rather than implied by a skip. Both outcomes are worth having; neither is
a reason to defer past this ruling.

THE THREE ALREADY HARD-REQUIRED STAY HARD-REQUIRED. This fix replaces the need to
EXTEND the list, not the list itself: an explicit entry still documents WHY a
suite is gate-bearing, which the structural fix cannot express.

--- original card below ---

deliverable, because they are the true size of the problem that let PG8 direction A
skip green on two consecutive runs.

  ANY SUITE CITED AS A GATE ENFORCEMENT POINT IS HARD-REQUIRED AT THE MOMENT IT
  IS CITED.

Not later, not when someone remembers. A citation naming a suite that SKIPPED is
worth exactly what a citation naming the WRONG suite is worth, and this project
spent a full session on the second kind during the LOOP 6 audit. This is that
defect one layer down: the pointer is right and the thing it points at never ran.

=== WHAT IS NO LONGER ON THIS LIST, AND WHY THAT MATTERS ===

cards.title: Criterion F sweep: assertions that match shared vocabulary rather than identity on a shared seeded database. 170 count assertions triaged; the at-risk shape is narrower than it first looked and the method matters more than the number

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19. Finding at docs/recon/ACC-identity-blind-assertions.md, fix in apps/web/e2e/therapist-blocks.spec.ts, guard in apps/web/lib/e2e-hygiene/identity-blind-assertions.test.ts (5 assertions, all five COLLECTED by the default vitest run - proven with `vitest list`, not assumed).

THE CARD'S THREE NAMED CANDIDATES ARE ALL FALSE, re-derived from main at f23a110.
  notes-unification.spec.ts:111, the card's "CLEAREST CASE FOUND", says "a shared patient". The patient is created fresh per run under a random name (`DuasModes ${uniq()}`, uniq = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8)) and the dropdown is patient-scoped by construction - appointment-selector.tsx:41 loads listPatientAppointmentsForNoteAction(patientId). No other spec can add an option because no other spec can name the patient.
  scheduling.spec.ts:277 counts date pickers inside a modal this test opened, one per row, generated by the "2" it typed eleven lines earlier.
  camera-to-ficha.spec.ts:128-158 counts buttons inside getByRole("group",{name:"Câmara"}), a control group in its own page.
The card's caution - "the honest number is smaller than the alarming one" - was right and still not conservative enough.

ONE REAL CASE FOUND THAT THE SWEEP DID NOT NAME: therapist-blocks.spec.ts:260-261 counted the BADGE LABEL. Three facts, each read from the file: TherapistBlocks.tsx:177 maps over `blocks` WHOLE so the modal lists every block unfiltered by date; THERAPIST_NAME is a shared fixture and agenda-blocked-time.spec.ts creates its own pontual block for that same therapist; and BOTH specs run a clearBlocks() that deletes every block that therapist has, not only their own.

WHY IT MATTERS THOUGH AN EXACT COUNT USUALLY FAILS LOUDLY, which is the objection that has to be answered rather than ignored: contamination normally pushes toHaveCount(1) to 2 and the test goes red, harmlessly. The case that is not harmless is the COMPENSATING ERROR - our save silently fails WHILE a foreign pontual block is present, the count is still 1, and the spec reports as created a block it never created. That is the card's own distinction: a skipped suite fails to prove, an identity-blind assertion proves something FALSE. It has not fired because playwright.config.ts sets workers:1 and fullyParallel:false, so the two specs never interleave. That is a scheduling accident, not a property.

THE FIX IS THE CARD'S OWN RULE: identify each row by its own RUN_DAY_BASE-derived date (RUN_DAY_BASE = 60 + Date.now()%300, randomised per run), then assert the badge INSIDE that row. Both halves are needed and prove different things - the row proves the block is ours, the badge proves it is the mode we asked for. The old assertion collapsed the two questions into one count and could answer neither.

NEGATIVE ARM RUN: restoring the two original lines fails exactly 2 of the guard's 5 assertions, and the guard carries an explicit NEGATIVE CONTROL that the forbidden regex really does match the old line - without it a typo would make the check pass for the wrong reason and go on passing.

A REPO-WIDE BASELINE LOCK ON PRESENCE COUNTS WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, recorded so it is not re-proposed as an oversight: it would put maintenance friction on 55 assertions across 15 files to guard the population that already fails loudly, while leaving the population in section 4 of the finding unguarded. Protection aimed at the wrong population is worse than none, because it reads as coverage.

Gates: pnpm lint 0 errors, pnpm typecheck 11/11, pnpm test 232 files / 2286 passed, pnpm build 4/4. Playwright still collects therapist-blocks.spec.ts (3 projects, verified with --list).

MERGED as PR #957, squashed to ace0dd7. THE E2E PROOF IS THE SPEC'S OWN LINE, not the green shard: run 32263942836, E2E shard (3), job 96112495496 ->
  ✓  70 [chromium] › e2e/therapist-blocks.spec.ts:146:5 › W5-12: both modes create time_off blocks; pontual excluded from availability; overlap warns not cancels (26.2s)
FIRST ATTEMPT, no retry marker, 74 passed in 4.0m. Cited this way deliberately: a green shard is not evidence a particular spec ran - that is the skip-guard lesson this workflow already carries - so the named line is the evidence and the shard colour is not.

THE FIRST RUN OF THIS PR'S SHARD 3 FAILED AND IT WAS NOT THIS CHANGE. Job 96103690200 ran 25m23s against a 7-11m baseline, which looked exactly like a regression this change had caused. It was not: the log names CI-supabase-cli-setup-flaky, "Start Supabase (lean stack)" burned 23 of the job's 25 minutes, Playwright started at 14:51:02Z and the job's timeout-minutes:25 budget expired 0.7s later. ZERO TESTS RAN. Read before acting on the suspicion, per the e2e doctrine; the second-order finding is carded as CI-shard-timeout-budget-defeats-flaky-retry.

cards.notes:
SWEPT 2026-08-12 AFTER PG8's DIRECTION A PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON. Counted and
classified; NOT fixed wholesale, because the honest number is smaller than the
alarming one and reporting the alarming one would be its own kind of false claim.

=== WHY THIS IS WORSE IN KIND THAN THE 39 SKIPPABLE SUITES ===
A SKIPPABLE SUITE FAILS TO PROVE. AN IDENTITY-BLIND ASSERTION PROVES SOMETHING
FALSE. The first leaves a gap; the second fills it with a wrong answer that reads
as a right one. Both are on this board; this is the one that produces green.

=== THE E2E SWEEP, WITH THE METHOD ===
  170  toHaveCount(N) assertions across apps/web/e2e
   66  identity- or run-scoped (PATIENTS./USERS./RUN_DAY/a fixture name in the
       locator). SAFE by construction.
   63  toHaveCount(0) - ABSENCE assertions. STRUCTURALLY SAFE UNDER CRITERION F,
       and this is the distinction that shrinks the number honestly: an unrelated
       row can only ADD, so contamination makes an absence assertion FAIL LOUDLY
       rather than pass falsely. It is the presence direction that is dangerous.
   41  presence counts on a non-identity locator - THE NOMINAL AT-RISK SET.

BUT THE 41 IS AN UPPER BOUND AND IS DOMINATED BY STATIC UI STRUCTURE, which no
data row can satisfy:
  - <option> counts in dropdowns fed by the seeded CATALOG (services, hours,
    Estado values) - clinical, marcacoes-service-filter, equipa-primary-service,
    declaracao, booking-service-preselection, marcacoes-tab-edit
  - SVG chart structure - data-marker, data-marker-shape, data-legend-type
  - UI affordances - camera button counts, :focus, badge counts
Several more are identity-scoped in fact and were missed by the grep pattern
(equipa-primary-service's card(page, "E2E Reception") names an account).

GENUINE CANDIDATES - a PRESENCE count over DATA ROWS another spec could add to:
  notes-unification.spec.ts:111  apptSelect.locator("option") toHaveCount(2)
    an appointment dropdown for a shared patient; another spec booking for that
    patient adds an option and the count moves. CLEAREST CASE FOUND.
  scheduling.spec.ts:277         triggers toHaveCount(2)
  camera-to-ficha.spec.ts:128-158 cameraButtons 2/3/2 - UI, but sequential and
    stateful, worth a read.
NONE OF THE THREE CARRIES A GATE ROW, so per the dispatch none is fixed here.

=== DB-GATED SUITES: LARGELY IMMUNE BY CONSTRUCTION ===
  45 of 53 build their fixtures with randomUUID() PER RUN, so every assertion is
  identity-scoped by construction and criterion F cannot bite.
  The 8 that do not are availability-dev-seed, form-templates-seed, journal-sync,
  migration-syntax, osteopathy-v3-mobilidade-seed, private-notes-template-guard,
  security-definer-owner, working-hours-real. EVERY ONE ASSERTS ABOUT A SHARED
  ARTEFACT ON PURPOSE - the journal, the migration set, a seeded template, an
  ownership catalog. Their subject IS the shared thing, so naming it is correct
  and not a criterion-F defect. NO ACTION.

=== THE RULE GOING FORWARD, which is worth more than the count ===
WHEN WRITING AN ASSERTION AGAINST THE SHARED SEEDED DATABASE, ASK: could a row
this test did not create satisfy it? If yes, add identity. A patient name, a
run-unique id, a RUN_DAY-derived date. Never a time, a status, a service name, a
date or a bare count alone.

AND PREFER ABSENCE WHERE THE PROPERTY ALLOWS IT. toHaveCount(0) fails on
contamination instead of passing on it, which is the safer direction to be wrong
in.

=== RE-DERIVED AND CLOSED 2026-08-19. THE TRIAGE ABOVE IS CORRECTED, NOT DELETED. ===
The three "GENUINE CANDIDATES" listed above are ALL FALSE. Each was re-read from main at f23a110 and the disproof is on the evidence and in docs/recon/ACC-identity-blind-assertions.md. The classification method and the counts stand; the three conclusions drawn from them do not. Left in place rather than edited out, because the card's own thesis is that the method matters more than the number, and a sweep that names three non-cases while missing a real one is the evidence for that thesis.

THE POPULATION WAS THE LIMITATION, and this is the finding with the longest reach. toHaveCount was swept because it is greppable, not because it is where the risk concentrates: an exact count SELF-CORRECTS, because a foreign row usually pushes it off the expected number and it fails. The population that passes falsely as its ORDINARY behaviour is unswept - toBeVisible() and toContainText() on a non-identity locator, which pass on ANY matching row and fail only when nothing matches. Contamination makes them MORE likely to pass, not less, which is the opposite of the direction the absence-assertion argument above relies on. Carded as ACC-visibility-assertions-unswept rather than estimated here, because guessing its size would be the alarming-number mistake this card explicitly refused to make.

cards.title: PG8's e2e: the pedido is invisible on the agenda to EVERY viewer including the owner, so it is not location scope. Two candidates remain: the row was never created, or the card renders in a shape the locator misses

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test (web 235 files pass), pnpm build. The e2e proof is the CI run on the PR, because Playwright is the only thing that exercises this.

THE CARD'S PREMISE IS FALSE ON main AND THIS IS THE FIRST THING A READER NEEDS. The card exists to diagnose a FAILING assertion - 'the pedido is invisible on the agenda to EVERY viewer including the owner' - and names two remaining candidates for the cause. THERE IS NO FAILURE. Read out of the E2E shard 3 log of run 32387760214 (PR #984, main at 12b1f47):

  [W13-07] A: booking day = segunda-feira, 24 de agosto de 2026 -> 2026-08-24
  [W13-07] A: visible to RECEPTION on 2026-08-24? true
  ✓ 66 [chromium] › sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts:344 › DIRECTION A: a portal booking APPEARS on the staff agenda (2.8s)

DIRECTION A PASSES, and has been passing on every PR merged this session. Candidate A (the row was never created) and candidate B (the card renders in a shape the locator misses) are both moot for the failure described, because the row is created and it is found. Observed, not inferred, and not reconciled silently.

A SECOND, SMALLER STALENESS ON THE SAME CARD: it says 'PG8 is halted permanently'. PG8 closed on the amended DoD on 2026-08-13 and reads `pass` on the board. The card's conclusion - that it is not on a gate's critical path - is still right, and more so.

WHAT WAS STILL TRUE, AND IT IS WHAT SHIPPED. The card's own last paragraph: 'the patient is the seeded Maria Silva ... a run-unique patient remains the durable fix and is blocked on the trusted-device storage state fixing the portal identity.' Pinning the DATE narrowed the collision from 'anyone called Maria Silva at 09:00' to 'the same patient at the same time on the same day'. SMALLER IS NOT ZERO, and this spec's entire history is two FALSE GREENS produced by exactly that kind of match.

THE DURABLE FIX DID NOT NEED THE BLOCKED THING. `apps/portal/app/portal/booking/actions.ts:31` redirects to `/portal/booking/pending?id=<appointment.id>`, so THE ID OF THE ROW THIS RUN CREATED IS ALREADY ON THE URL THE FLOW LANDS ON. No run-unique patient, no second auth path, no new endpoint, no database query from a browser test. The blocker the card records was real for the approach it had in mind and does not bind the property.

WHAT SHIPPED, two files:
  apps/web/app/agenda/agenda-grid.tsx - `data-appointment-id={appt.id}` on the agenda card. Every other handle on that card describes its SHAPE rather than WHICH ROW IT IS: `agenda-card-patient` is on every card, the patient name is shared vocabulary on a seeded database, and the time is POSITIONAL rather than rendered inside the card at all. Inert - nothing reads it back - and it discloses nothing the card was not already rendering to the same viewer.
  apps/web/e2e/sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts - the helper returns the id, and the verdict is now `[data-appointment-id=<id>]` being visible on the booked day.

THE NAME CHECK IS KEPT AND IS NOW SCOPED TO THAT ROW rather than to the page: `row.getByTestId('agenda-card-patient')` must contain the patient's first name. Same coverage as the old page-wide text probe, minus the cross-match - it asserts THIS card renders the patient, not that SOME card somewhere renders somebody with that name.

THE TIME AND NAME PROBES ARE NOW REPORTED, NOT ASSERTED, so a future failure arrives already diagnosed - the same move LE-e2e-nif-edit-404 made. The log line says whether the time text and the name text were present alongside the id verdict: id absent with both present means the identity attribute regressed; id absent with both absent means no row reached that day. The card's two candidates become a printed answer instead of a next investigation.

ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep CRITERION F IS THE FRAME AND IT IS NOW SATISFIED PROPERLY: a guard proves a test RAN; only run-scoped identity proves it tested the right SUBJECT. Two neighbours booking the same patient at the same time on the same day can no longer satisfy this assertion, because a uuid is not shared vocabulary.

A SEPARATE FINDING, CARDED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE: apps/web/e2e IS NOT TYPECHECKED BY ANY GATE. `apps/web/tsconfig.json:33` excludes `e2e`, there is no e2e tsconfig, and Playwright strips types without checking them. PROVEN rather than asserted: running tsc over the UNMODIFIED main copy of this spec reports 1 error (TS2339, `booked.isoDate` on an unnarrowed union at :437). That error is on main today and no gate sees it. Corrected in this PR because the line was being touched; the class is now LE-e2e-suite-not-typechecked.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. A DOM attribute nothing renders and an e2e assertion. No product surface changes.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20. THE FAILURE IT DIAGNOSES NO LONGER REPRODUCES; THE RESIDUAL IT NAMED IS NOW FIXED. ===

WHAT WAS LEFT was the sentence the card itself ends on: the assertion still

reception false, OWNER false. The owner has a null location scope

cards.title: apps/web/e2e is excluded from tsconfig and Playwright strips types without checking them, so no gate typechecks the e2e suite - main carries a type error today

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build. pnpm test:scripts 127 pass, 0 skipped (was 123).

THE COUNT THE CARD DEMANDED BEFORE ANY DECISION: TWO. The card required the number to be measured and reported before choosing between fixing the errors and landing the config with a documented list, because it was unknown - one file had been measured, not the suite. Measured on a branch: 2 errors, both in apps/web/e2e/scheduling.spec.ts, both TS18047 'possibly null'. Small enough that fixing and landing in one PR is the obvious answer, which is exactly what the count was for.

THE ERROR THE CARD ITSELF NAMED IS ALREADY GONE. It cited TS2339 on booked.isoDate at scheduling's sibling spec; #985 corrected that line while building LE-pg8-e2e-needs-run-scoped-patient. Re-derived rather than trusted.

BOTH REMAINING ERRORS ARE THE SAME SHAPE AND IT IS AN INSTRUCTIVE ONE: `expect(tBox).not.toBeNull()` followed by `tBox.y`. The expectation asserts at RUNTIME and narrows NOTHING for the compiler. They never crashed, because the bounding boxes are always there when the dialog is open - WHICH IS PRECISELY WHY NOTHING FOUND THEM. A type error that does not crash is invisible without a compiler. Fixed with a throw, which narrows and asserts at once and fails with the reason rather than with 'cannot read property y of null' two lines later.

playwright.config.ts CAME IN TOO, and it was excluded alongside e2e. Worth its own arm: the config decides WHICH specs run and on what, so a type error there is a suite that runs the wrong thing rather than a spec that fails.

THE OTHER APPS WERE CHECKED, which the card listed as unknown. apps/portal, apps/api and apps/admin have NO e2e directory and NO such exclusion. The gap was confined to apps/web.

A GUARD, BECAUSE THE EXCLUSION IS ONE LINE OF JSON AND RE-ADDING IT TURNS NOTHING RED. scripts/e2e-is-typechecked.test.mjs, in the required check. Four assertions: the scan is not vacuous (a guard about a directory that does not exist would go green the day somebody deleted the suite); e2e is not excluded; playwright.config.ts is not excluded; and THE INCLUDE GLOBS ACTUALLY REACH e2e - because an exclusion is not the only way to leave the suite unchecked, and narrowing `include` to app/** would do it just as effectively while the exclude array stayed clean.

THE GUARD'S OWN JSONC READER WAS WRONG TWICE, and both are the same lesson this repo has now met four times in one day. FIRST: a naive block-comment regex read the slash-star inside the path alias "@/*" as a comment opener and ate the middle of the file; JSON.parse failed at the alias. It FAILED LOUDLY rather than returning {} - which matters, because an empty object would have given `cfg.exclude ?? []` an empty array and the two exclusion assertions would have PASSED, a broken instrument reporting a clean result. SECOND: the comment written to explain that fix quoted the regex literally, and the close-comment inside the quote ENDED THE DOC BLOCK EARLY and broke the file. The prose now spells the tokens out. A shape-match counts the APPEARANCE of a token, not what the token means where it sits.

SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each restored from the git index:
  a deliberate type error in an e2e SPEC -> gate red.
  the same in a HELPER -> gate red.
  the same in playwright.config.ts, now included -> gate red.
  the exclusion RESTORED with that error still present -> gate reports ZERO errors. THE DEFECT, demonstrated: the error goes invisible and no check goes red.
  the exclusion re-added -> the guard's assertion 2 red, with the full explanation in the message.
  `include` narrowed to app/** with no exclusion at all -> assertion 4 red, which is the arm the first three would have missed.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. A tsconfig line, two narrowings in a test, and a guard.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20. THE COUNT WAS TWO, SO THEY WERE FIXED RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED. ===

The card required the error count to be measured and REPORTED before deciding
between fixing and landing a documented list. It is 2, both in one file, both
the same shape: expect(x).not.toBeNull() narrows nothing for the compiler.

THEY NEVER CRASHED, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING FOUND THEM. A type error that does
not crash is invisible without a compiler, and Playwright strips types without
checking them.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

FOUND 2026-08-20 while building LE-pg8-e2e-needs-run-scoped-patient. CARDED, NOT BUILT.

THE FINDING, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. `apps/web/tsconfig.json:33` reads
`"exclude": ["node_modules", "playwright.config.ts", "e2e"]`. There is no
tsconfig inside `apps/web/e2e`. Playwright transpiles TypeScript with esbuild,
which STRIPS types and does not check them. So `pnpm typecheck` - one of the
four repo gates - does not read a single line of the e2e suite, and neither
does anything else.

IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Running tsc over the UNMODIFIED main copy of
apps/web/e2e/sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts reports one error:
  e2e/sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts(437,29): error TS2339: Property 'isoDate' does
  not exist on type '... | { ok: false; why: "empty-calendar"; detail: string; }'
That line is on main and every gate is green over it. It happens to be
harmless at runtime because `test.skip` stops the test before the read - which
is precisely why it survived: a type error that does not crash is invisible
without a compiler.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN ORDINARY CODE. The e2e suite is where this
project's most expensive defects have been found and where its gate evidence
comes from. An assertion that reads a property the type says is absent is the
same family as the vacuous guards ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep counts: it can be
wrong about its own subject and still be green.

SCOPE, so nobody starts by turning it on blind: adding `e2e` to the typecheck
WILL surface existing errors, and the count is unknown - one file was measured,
not the suite. The first step is to count them, on a branch, and report the
number BEFORE deciding whether to fix them or to land the config with a
documented list. Turning it on and fixing whatever falls out in the same PR is
how a scoped change becomes an unbounded one.

APPS/PORTAL AND APPS/API WERE NOT CHECKED and may have the same gap. Part of
the count.

CLOSES ON: a typecheck that reads the e2e suites, with the error count before
and after pasted, and a negative control - a deliberate type error in a spec
must turn the gate red.

cards.title: The E2E job's Supabase steps failed intermittently three times on 2026-08-12. THE LOGS NAME TWO DIFFERENT CAUSES, not one: a release-CDN outage the action's own retries could not outlast, and a port collision. Both now retried, and a retry is announced rather than hidden

evidence.ref:
FIXED 2026-08-13. THE CARD SAID "it wants a log read before a change is chosen" AND THE
LOG READ CHANGED THE FIX. The card listed three guesses - a rate limit, a
transient download, a port collision - and recommended pinning the CLI version.
THE VERSION WAS ALREADY PINNED at v2.107.0, so that recommendation was already
true and was never the cause. Reading the three runs found TWO causes, not one.

CAUSE 1, occurrences 1 and 2, step "Set up Supabase CLI".
Run 31622714249, verbatim:
    Unexpected HTTP response: 503
    Waiting 17 seconds before trying again
    socket hang up
    Waiting 14 seconds before trying again
    ##[error]socket hang up
supabase/setup-cli ALREADY retries twice with backoff and still lost - the
release CDN was down for longer than its internal budget. Run 31635017752 failed
identically on shard 1.
FIX: continue-on-error on the action plus a fallback step that installs the SAME
pinned version straight from the GitHub release, with three attempts and its own
curl --retry backoff. No new vendor and no new action - it is the same artifact
the action fetches.
BOTH HALVES VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL RELEASE rather than assumed:
  HTTP 200 on the exact pinned asset URL, and
  tar -tzf shows the archive's first entry is 'supabase' at the root, which is
  what the install line takes.

CAUSE 2, occurrence 3, step "Start Supabase (lean stack)".
Run 31647425292, verbatim:
    failed to start docker container "supabase_db_OsteoJP": ... failed to bind
    host port for 0.0.0.0:54322:172.18.0.2:5432/tcp: address already in use
A PORT COLLISION, and nothing to do with a download. A half-started stack leaves
containers holding their published ports.
FIX: one retry, preceded by supabase stop --no-backup and a forced removal of
any leftover supabase_* containers.

THE DIAGNOSTIC RUNS BEFORE THE CLEANUP, DELIBERATELY. ss -ltnp names WHAT holds
the port and docker ps -a says whether a container is already there. Cleaning
up first would erase the evidence, which is how an intermittent failure becomes a
permanent one.

A RETRY THAT HIDES ITSELF WOULD MAKE THIS FLAKE UN-MEASURABLE. Both paths print
::warning:: when they fire, so a run that needed rescuing stays visible in the
checks UI instead of reading as clean. That matters here specifically: this flake
reached THREE occurrences before anyone counted them, and the card's own closing
line is that a step reddening at random trains people to re-run instead of read -
the reflex that lets a genuine red be dismissed.

AND NEITHER RETRY IS UNBOUNDED. Two attempts for the start, three for the
download, then a hard non-zero exit. Two failures in a row is not a flake.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this fix has not been observed rescuing a real occurrence,
because the flake is intermittent and cannot be summoned. What IS proven is that
the fallback's download and archive layout are correct against the live release,
and that the workflow parses. The first real occurrence after this is the test,
and it will announce itself in the checks UI by design.

cards.notes:
RAISED TO HIGH 2026-08-12 AFTER A THIRD OCCURRENCE, AND THE THIRD ONE COST
SOMETHING REAL.

THREE OCCURRENCES, THREE DIFFERENT RUNS, TWO DIFFERENT STEPS, TWO DIFFERENT
BRANCHES AND SHARDS:
  run 31622714249  shard 3  step 12  "Set up Supabase CLI"      failed
  run 31635017752  shard 1  step 12  "Set up Supabase CLI"      failed
  run 31647425292  shard 3  step 13  "Start Supabase (lean stack)"  failed
Every downstream step skips, and the shard is red for a reason that has nothing
to do with the change under test.

WHY IT IS NOW HIGH RATHER THAN MEDIUM. The third occurrence killed the
INC-10 diagnostic BEFORE PLAYWRIGHT RAN. That measurement had already taken two
runs to set up - one to add the log lines, one to remove a diagnostic that had
made the suite slow enough to be cancelled - and it is still unanswered because
the infrastructure never got as far as the test. AN UNRELIABLE STEP DOES NOT JUST
COST A RE-RUN; IT COSTS THE ANSWER YOU WERE MEASURING FOR.

IT ALSO CAUSED A SECOND DEFECT ALREADY. The E2E skip-guard was originally
`if: always()`, so on run 31622714249 it ran after Supabase failed, found no
Playwright report, and announced "E2E SKIP-GUARD RED" for a Supabase failure -
reporting the wrong cause. Fixed by gating it on the Playwright step's
conclusion, but the trigger was this flake.

AND THE REAL COST IS THE HABIT. This project's e2e doctrine is READ THE ARTIFACT
FIRST. A step that reddens at random trains people to re-run instead, which is
exactly the reflex that lets a genuine red be dismissed.

THE FIX, and it wants a log read before a change is chosen: pin the CLI version
and add a retry to both steps (supabase/setup-cli@v1 and the start step in
.github/workflows/e2e.yml). Check a red run's log first - a rate limit, a
transient download and a port collision want different fixes, and guessing here
would be the same error this board keeps recording.

cards.title: FIXED: the booking confirmation screen now READS the patient's own appointment before claiming a pedido was received, and fails closed when it cannot verify one

evidence.ref:
FIXED 2026-08-13. All four steps of this card's own fix taken, in one PR.

1. IT CARRIES THE ID - already did, via /portal/booking/pending?id=...
2. IT READS IT, through getMyAppointments(), which is RLS SELF-SCOPED. That
   property is why it is the right read: a wrong or invented id returns NOTHING
   rather than somebody else's row, so the screen became truthful without
   becoming a way to probe whether an arbitrary appointment id exists.
   NO NEW ENDPOINT. Reading the patient's own list costs one call the portal
   already makes elsewhere and adds no surface to a patient-facing route.
3. NO ID OR NO ROW MEANS NO CLAIM. It renders what happened, what to do, and the
   clinic telephones via the existing ClinicPhones component - PG9's standard for
   a dead end, and no new component was invented.
4. THE DEPENDENT SPEC IS INVERTED IN THE SAME PR, which this card required.

=== THE SPEC WAS PINNING THE DEFECT IN PLACE, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING ===
portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts navigated to the screen directly and asserted
"Pedido recebido" was VISIBLE. Its own comment explained why: "The pending screen
is reachable directly and is what the flow lands on after a submit. Asserting it
here rather than driving a full booking keeps this test independent of slot
availability." THE COMMENT WAS CORRECT ABOUT THE TEST AND WAS DESCRIBING A
PRODUCT DEFECT. Fixing the product would have broken the test, and the test would
have looked like the thing that was wrong.
It is now two tests:
  THE NEGATIVE - arriving with no id produces NO success message, and arriving
    with a FABRICATED id produces no success message either. The second arm is
    the one that matters: an implementation that merely checked the id was
    PRESENT would satisfy the first and still confirm any booking anyone
    invented.
  THE POSITIVE - a REAL booking is driven end to end and still says "Pedido
    recebido", not "Marcacao recebida", with the slot not promised and reception
    named as who decides. It is now LOAD-BEARING: with the screen failing closed,
    every negative assertion is satisfied by a page that says "not found"
    unconditionally, including for a patient who really did book.

=== THE HELPER SPLITS SKIP FROM DEFECT, WHICH IS THE LOOP 7 LESSON ===
bookFirstAvailable returns false ONLY when the seeded calendar offers no slot -
a legitimate skip, because it depends on the run day. EVERY OTHER FAILURE THROWS:
no services, the date/time step never reached, no picker trigger, the picker not
opening, no Continuar control. LOOP 7's first helper returned null for four
different conditions and the caller skipped on all of them alike, so a broken
flow silently became a skipped test inside a green run.

=== A RACE THAT IS NOT ONE, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ===
The obvious objection is that a patient who just booked might arrive before the
row is readable. bookAppointment RETURNS the created appointment before the
redirect happens (booking/actions.ts:29-30), so the row is committed by then, and
this is a fresh server request reading committed data through the same primary
with no read replica in the path. Written into the page's header because the
failure mode would be ugly - a patient who booked being told we cannot find their
request - and because IF A REPLICA IS EVER INTRODUCED, this page is one of the
places that breaks. Better revisited then than hedged with a retry now.

=== COPY, AND IT CARRIES NO COMMITMENT ===
Two new strings in both locales: booking.pending_unverified_title / _body.
  pt: "Nao encontramos este pedido" / "Nao conseguimos confirmar este pedido de
      marcacao. Se acabou de o fazer, veja as suas consultas. Caso contrario,
      contacte a clinica."
NO fee, NO cancellation term, NO consent, NO retention, NO promise about response
time or outcome. Operational error text under the same delegated authority as the
seven PG9 strings, and listed for the clinic team in HANDOVER-STATE.md section 5c.
"contacte a clinica" is not new wording - it is already committed in otp_refused
and booking.no_slots.

Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, unit green including portal 155, build 4/4.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-12. CARDED REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE ROW COMMITS, because the defect is
in the SCREEN'S CONTRACT and not in any one booking.

=== THE FACT, AND IT IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THIS REPO ===
`/portal/booking/pending` renders "Pedido recebido" for anyone who navigates to
it. It takes no id, reads no row and verifies nothing.
apps/web/e2e/portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts:195-199 states it outright and
RELIES on it: "The pending screen is reachable directly and is what the flow
lands on after a submit. Asserting it here rather than driving a full booking
keeps this test independent of slot availability."
That comment is correct about the test and is describing a product defect.

=== WHAT A PATIENT CAN THEREFORE SEE ===
  - press BACK after leaving the screen, and be told again that a request was
    received;
  - REFRESH after a submit that FAILED, and be told it succeeded;
  - open a STALE LINK or a bookmark, and be told a booking they never made was
    received.
In every case the clinic learns nothing, because nothing was written. The patient
believes they have a pedido; reception has no row; the appointment does not
happen and nobody finds out until the patient does not arrive.

=== IT IS THE FOUR-INSTANCE PATTERN, AT THE PATIENT ===
PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md section 1.3: a verdict path where an unhandled case falls
back to the benign-looking outcome. HERE THE VERDICT IS "your booking was
received" AND THE FALLBACK IS SHOWING IT ANYWAY. The four instances already
recorded - string | null, the skip, the swallowed catch, ?? e.kind - were all in
this project's INSTRUMENTS. THIS ONE IS IN THE PRODUCT, FACING A PATIENT, which
is why it is high rather than medium.

=== THE FIX, when it is taken ===
The screen must be about a SPECIFIC pedido and must fail closed:
  1. carry the appointment id - /portal/booking/pending?id=... or a server-side
     redirect that puts it in the route;
  2. READ IT, through the patient's own scoped path (store.listOwn / getOwn is
     RLS self-scoped, so a wrong id returns nothing rather than someone else's
     row);
  3. if there is no id or no row, DO NOT SAY "recebido". Show the patient what
     actually happened and what to do - the clinic's telephone is the honest
     fallback, and EmptyState/ErrorState already exist for it.
  4. UPDATE portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts:192-209, which currently depends
     on the screen being reachable without a booking. That test must drive a real
     booking or assert the NEW fail-closed behaviour; leaving it as-is would pin
     the defect in place.

=== A TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT ===
Navigate to /portal/booking/pending WITHOUT booking and assert the success copy
is ABSENT. That is one assertion, it fails today, and it is the negative arm the
existing spec inverted into a convenience.

=== WHAT THIS CARD DOES NOT CLAIM ===
It does not claim a row failed to commit in any observed case. Whether the PG8
e2e's booking committed is a SEPARATE question, probed by the patient's own
appointments list. IF THAT COMES BACK FALSE, this card stops being a
robustness issue and becomes the reporting half of a live defect - a patient told
their booking was received when it was not - and the two are fixed together.

cards.title: RESOLVED: the row DOES cross. All three 'no row' readings came from the same non-waiting probe - isVisible({timeout}) ignores its timeout in playwright-core 1.60.0 - so a render race was read as a missing appointment. No product defect. The instrument is fixed

evidence.ref:
RUN 31649767622, shard 3, DIRECTION A, SAME COMMIT AND SAME SEED ON BOTH ATTEMPTS:
  attempt 1  [W13-07] A: agenda shows the row on the booked day: 443ms
             [W13-07] A: visible to RECEPTION on 2026-08-17? false
  attempt 2  [W13-07] A: agenda shows the row on the booked day: 1683ms
             [W13-07] A: visible to RECEPTION on 2026-08-17? true
             [W13-07] A: the crossing landed on 2026-08-17, the day it booked
Playwright reported the test as FLAKY, not failed: "1 failed, 1 flaky, 70 passed"
- the one failure in that shard was PG9's axe contrast red, a different test.

THE CAUSE, from the installed dependency rather than from reasoning. Every probe
in sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts used locator.isVisible({ timeout: N }). In
node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@1.60.0/.../types.d.ts:14491 that option is:
  "@deprecated This option is ignored. locator.isVisible() does not wait for the
   element to become visible and returns immediately."
So a probe written to wait 15 seconds answered in zero. Attempt 1 asked 443ms
after goto and got the pre-paint DOM; attempt 2 was slower and found the row.
.catch(() => false) then made a race indistinguishable from a real absence.

THE THREE SURFACES WERE NOT INDEPENDENT. Reception, owner and the patient's own
list were three calls to the same non-waiting probe. Three readings of one broken
instrument are one reading.

FIXED in this PR: becameVisible() uses waitFor({state:'visible'}) and narrows the
rejection - a TimeoutError is the negative answer, any other error is re-thrown.
Five call sites converted, two of them optional-element probes that were racing
the first paint and reporting the failure one step later under the wrong name.

cards.notes:
=== 2026-08-13: RESOLVED, AND IT WAS THE INSTRUMENT. ===

The one line that was supposed to settle this card - log page.url() after the
submit - was never needed. The run answered it more directly: the SAME commit,
against the SAME seed, reported the row absent on attempt 1 and present on
attempt 2, on the day it booked. A booking that does not commit does not appear
on a retry.

THE TENSION THIS CARD RECORDED IS RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE SUBMIT PATH. The card
said: "Either the row exists and THREE surfaces are wrong, or the row does not
exist and the submit path did not behave as written." The first is true, and the
three surfaces were wrong in the SAME way because they were the same probe. The
code read that said the submit path was correct was correct.

WHAT THIS COST, RECORDED BECAUSE THE COST IS THE LESSON: PG8 held open, an
incident card raised as possibly patient-facing, a session spent ruling out
tenant mismatch and PL-09 location scope by code read, and a diagnostic block
added, then removed for making the suite slow enough to be cancelled. All of it
downstream of one deprecated option.

IT IS INSTANCE FIVE OF SECTION 1.3, and the first found in an e2e probe rather
than in a guard or a fallback. The shape is identical: an unknown case (the page
has not painted yet) mapped onto a known, harmless-looking one (the element is
not there), and the system carried on reporting something reasonable.

CRITERION F GAINS A LINE FROM THIS. A guard proves a test RAN; the assertion
proves it tested the right SUBJECT; and now: THE PROBE MUST BE PROVEN TO WAIT.
An immediate probe with a timeout argument reads exactly like a waiting one at
the call site, and it is the call site that gets reviewed.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This does not close PG8. Direction A must still produce a
green AT ATTEMPT 1 with the waiting probe in place, and that run is what the gate
turns on. It does close the question of whether a patient can be shown a success
for a booking that does not exist ON THIS EVIDENCE - they cannot, and the earlier
withdrawal of that premise by strategy was right.

SEC-pending-screen-asserts-nothing IS UNAFFECTED AND STAYS HIGH. That card is
about the screen's CONTRACT - it says "Pedido recebido" to anyone who navigates
to it, with no id and no row read - and that is true whether or not any given
booking committed.

--- original card below, unedited ---

=== 2026-08-12, LATER: TENANT RULED OUT BY CODE READ, AND STRATEGY'S PREMISE
    CORRECTED ON THIS CARD SO IT IS NOT CARRIED FORWARD. ===

CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE THIS CARD WAS RAISED UNDER. Strategy told the owner
there was a live possibility that the portal shows a patient success for a
booking that does not exist. THE CODE AS WRITTEN DOES NOT SUPPORT THAT, and
strategy has withdrawn it. apps/portal/app/portal/booking/actions.ts:29-30
redirects to the pending screen ONLY after the API returns an appointment, and
:32-58 returns a rejection with pt-PT copy WITHOUT redirecting. On the real path a
failure keeps the patient on step 5. This card must not be cited as evidence of a
patient-facing defect; it is an unexplained test result with two possible causes.

TENANT MISMATCH IS RULED OUT FOR THE WRITE. Checked before spending a run:
  PORTAL_TENANT_ID is read in exactly ONE place repo-wide -
    apps/portal/lib/auth/otp.ts:54, the OTP LOGIN path. Nothing else reads it.
  bookAppointment (apps/portal/lib/api/client.ts:260-272) sends NO tenantId. The
    API derives the tenant from the patient's authenticated session.
  That is the SAME session the patient's own appointment list reads under, so a
    tenant mismatch cannot make the row invisible to the patient who created it.
It could in principle explain the two STAFF surfaces. It cannot explain the
patient's own list, and that is the probe that was verified sound.

A REAL GAP FOUND WHILE CHECKING, WORTH ITS OWN LINE: the CI step at
.github/workflows/e2e.yml:250 writes ONLY NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL to
apps/portal/.env.local. IT NEVER WRITES PORTAL_TENANT_ID. That does not affect
booking, and it WOULD break the OTP login path - which the suite never exercises
because it signs in through the trusted-device door instead. So a real
misconfiguration is invisible to the suite by construction. Not this failure's
cause; carded here because it is the kind of thing that surfaces later as a
mystery.

=== THE MEASUREMENT IS PENDING AT THE END OF THIS SESSION ===
The spec now logs, immediately after the submit click:
  [W13-07] SUBMIT: url = ...
  [W13-07] SUBMIT: has ?id= = <bool>
  [W13-07] SUBMIT: error banner = ...
Run 31645009941 shard 3 did not finish inside the session. READ THOSE THREE LINES
FIRST when it does; they settle the question without any further reasoning.

AND ONE HONEST OBSERVATION ABOUT MY OWN DIAGNOSTICS: that run's shard 3 exceeded
25 minutes against a normal 4-5. The owner-login block added for the location
check carries a 30s waitForURL and runs on EVERY attempt including both retries.
DIAGNOSTIC CODE ADDED TO SETTLE ONE QUESTION HAS MADE THE SUITE SLOW ENOUGH TO BE
ITS OWN PROBLEM, and it should be removed once the question is answered rather
than left in place.

--- original card below ---

RAISED 2026-08-12 FROM THE CANDIDATE-A PROBE. HALTED FOR THE OWNER PER THE
DISPATCH, BECAUSE IF IT IS WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE IT IS PATIENT-FACING. IT IS NOT YET
ESTABLISHED, AND THIS CARD SAYS SO RATHER THAN ALARMING ON AN INFERENCE.

=== THE EVIDENCE FOR "NO ROW". THREE INDEPENDENT SURFACES. ===
Run 31643956952, shard 3, after a booking the portal reported as received:
  visible to RECEPTION on 2026-08-17?                     false
  visible to OWNER (null location scope) on 2026-08-17?   false
  does the row exist, per the PATIENT'S OWN LIST?         false

AND THE PATIENT-LIST PROBE WAS VERIFIED SOUND BEFORE BEING BELIEVED, because a
negative from an unverified locator is what cost this gate two days:
  store.listOwn (store.ts:217-235) has NO STATUS FILTER; RLS scopes it to the
    patient's own rows, so a pending pedido IS returned.
  isUpcoming (appointments/status.ts) is TRUE for a scheduled row in the future,
    so 2026-08-17 lands in the upcoming list rather than being hidden.
  AppointmentsView.tsx:18 renders the time via toLocaleTimeString pt-PT,
    2-digit hour and minute, hour12 false, Europe/Lisbon -> "09:00", which is
    exactly what the probe matches.
So the probe would have found the row if it were there.

=== THE EVIDENCE AGAINST, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT YET AN INCIDENT ===
THE SUBMIT PATH READS AS CORRECT. apps/portal/app/portal/booking/actions.ts:
  :29-30  const appointment = await bookAppointment(input)
          redirect to /portal/booking/pending?id=<appointment.id>
  :32-58  on ApiError it RETURNS A REJECTION with pt-PT copy and does NOT
          redirect - no_therapist, 409 slot taken, 401 to login, and a generic
          "Nao foi possivel enviar a marcacao".
So on the REAL path the pending screen is reached only after the API returned an
appointment WITH AN ID, and a failure keeps the patient on step 5 with an error.
THAT CONTRADICTS "a patient was shown success for a booking that does not exist" -
on this code, they could not have been.

=== THE TENSION, STATED PLAINLY ===
Either the row exists and THREE surfaces are wrong, or the row does not exist and
the submit path did not behave as written. Both cannot be true. I am not guessing
which, and the dispatch's premise - that a patient sees a confirmation for a
booking that does not exist - IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY THIS EVIDENCE.

=== THE ONE LINE THAT SETTLES IT, the same move that settled the booking day and
    the location scope ===
LOG page.url() IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE SUBMIT.
  contains "?id="  -> the API returned an appointment, so a row WAS created, all
                      three probes are wrong in the same way, and this is a TEST
                      problem. Most likely candidate: the row's rendered time
                      differs from the slot label (timezone or format).
  no "?id="        -> the redirect never happened, "Pedido recebido" matched for
                      another reason, and the submit really did fail. THEN it is
                      an incident, and SEC-pending-screen-asserts-nothing is its
                      reporting half.
ONE RUN. Do not fix anything before it.

=== WHY IT IS CARDED AS AN INCIDENT ANYWAY ===
The possibility is serious enough to sit on the board rather than be buried in a
gate note, and the probe result is real evidence even if its interpretation is
open. If it resolves to a test problem, this card closes carrying that finding -
worth having, because three surfaces agreeing wrongly would itself be a
criterion-F lesson.

cards.title: An entire authentication path has ZERO e2e coverage: PORTAL_TENANT_ID is never written to the portal's CI env, and every spec signs in through the trusted-device door, so a real misconfiguration on the OTP login path is invisible to the suite by construction

evidence.ref:
FIXED 2026-08-13. Spec: apps/web/e2e/portal-otp-login.spec.ts.

BOTH FACTS THE CARD NAMED ARE ADDRESSED:
  1. e2e.yml now writes PORTAL_TENANT_ID beside NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, value
     TENANT_A - the id fixtures.ts:8 already pinned.
  2. A spec drives the REAL OTP path: phone -> issued code -> session ->
     dashboard, with no storageState, so it starts with nothing.

THE CARD'S STEP 2 SAID TO READ THE CODE FROM THE SHIPPED TEST SINK. THAT IS NOT
POSSIBLE AND THE CARD WAS WRONG ABOUT IT. createOtpTestSink holds codes in the
API PROCESS'S MEMORY (otp-transport.ts:82-95, deliberately not a singleton), and
Playwright is a different process. There is no in-process handle to read.

WHAT WORKS INSTEAD, WITH NO PRODUCTION CHANGE AND NO BACK DOOR: verifyCode has to
check the code against something, and that something is a row in
patient_otp_codes holding sha256(sha256(e164) + ':' + code). Both hashes are
unsalted and deterministic BY DOCUMENTED DESIGN (otp.ts: the phone hash "is a
confirmation oracle rather than a secret"). A test with the LOCAL service-role
key inverts the 6-digit space in 305ms worst case, measured. Shipped code only,
no test-only endpoint, nothing added to the login path LOOP 3 cleaned.

NOT A SECURITY FINDING. A 6-digit code has a 10^6 space by definition; the hash
was never the protection. The protection is the table being service-role only
(0056), the 5-attempt cap and the 5-minute expiry, all three stated in otp.ts.
Anyone able to read that table already has the patient row.

A SECOND SEEDED PATIENT WAS REQUIRED, AND THE REASON IS A REAL CONSTRAINT.
resolvePatientByProvenPhone (patient-linkage.ts:73) demands auth_user_id IS NULL,
and ensurePortalPatient sets Maria's so the trusted-device path can use her. She
is PERMANENTLY INELIGIBLE for a first OTP login. PATIENT_OTP_LOGIN_A
(...a305, +351 916 000 005) is never linked to an auth user; the verify route
issues a trusted device and mints a session and writes no auth_user_id, so the
fixture stays eligible and the spec is re-runnable in CI and locally alike.

ONE TEST, BOTH ARMS, ONE ISSUED CODE, AND THAT IS A BUDGET DECISION WITH A
REASON. RULES.otpRequest is 3/hour per phone (limiter.ts:184) and Playwright
retries twice, so one request per attempt leaves headroom for all three; two
would hit the ceiling on the second retry and report otp_rate_limited, which
reads as a broken login rather than a spec budgeting badly. The same live code is
REFUSED wrong and ACCEPTED right, so the pair cannot both be satisfied by a
verify route that says yes to everything - the failure a positive-only login test
would miss. The wrong guess spends one of five permitted attempts and leaves the
code live, which is what MAX_ATTEMPTS is for.

FOUR THINGS THE SPEC ASSERTS BEYOND "IT LOGS IN":
  the screen is still Decision D's - no password field anywhere;
  the refusal DISCLOSES NOTHING - no "wrong code", "does not exist", "not
    registered" or "expired" reaches the page, so the portal does not rebuild the
    patient-list oracle the API's single 401 exists to prevent;
  the session SURVIVES A RELOAD, which is what separates a session from a
    redirect;
  the dashboard RENDERS, not just redirects.

REGISTERED IN THE SKIP GUARD. .github/scripts/assert-e2e-executed.mjs now lists
this test as HARD_REQUIRED. A silent skip would return this path to exactly the
state the card describes, and the guard exists because that already happened once
to PG8.

THE TRUSTED-DEVICE SPECS STAY. They cover the returning patient, the path most
patients take daily. This adds the FIRST login beside them, per the card's step 3.

=== AND ITS FIRST RUN FOUND A LAUNCH-BLOCKING DEFECT ===
SEC-otp-linkage-exact-phone-match. resolvePatientByProvenPhone compares the
proven E.164 against the RAW free-text patients.phone with eq(), and nothing
normalizes that column on write, so a patient stored as "+351 912 345 678"
cannot log in at all. The OTP fixture is therefore stored as bare E.164 - NOT
realistic data, said loudly in the seed and in fixtures.ts - so this spec proves
THE LOGIN PATH rather than proving the clinic can use it. The defect is pinned
by apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.db.test.ts against real rows and HALTED for
the owner, because every fix needs a migration.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-12 WHILE RULING OUT A TENANT HYPOTHESIS. It is more valuable than the
answer it was found next to.

=== THE TWO FACTS, EACH HARMLESS ALONE ===
1. .github/workflows/e2e.yml:250 writes ONLY NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL to
   apps/portal/.env.local. IT NEVER WRITES PORTAL_TENANT_ID.
2. apps/portal/lib/auth/otp.ts:54-57 reads PORTAL_TENANT_ID and THROWS when it is
   absent - deliberately, loudly, per PG7's no-silent-degradation posture. The
   caller turns that into the `unavailable` screen.

TOGETHER THEY MEAN THE PORTAL'S OTP LOGIN CANNOT WORK IN CI. And no test notices,
because fixtures.ts:212-235 signs every portal spec in through the TRUSTED-DEVICE
door instead: the seed writes a device row and the setup presents the cookie.
That choice is itself well-reasoned - the OTP code lives in a transport that is
off in CI, and a back door in the login path is what LOOP 3 existed to remove -
but its consequence was never stated.

=== SO AN ENTIRE AUTHENTICATION PATH HAS NO E2E COVERAGE ===
Decision D's PRIMARY patient login - phone, code, session - is exercised by unit
tests and by the owner's deployed-screen checks, and by NO e2e. A regression in
it would pass every shard.

=== IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS THE 36 SKIPPABLE SUITES, AND WORSE IN ONE WAY ===
ACC-skippable-suites-unguarded counts tests that FAIL TO PROVE - they exist and
can silently not run. THIS IS A PATH NO TEST CAN REACH. There is nothing to
un-skip. The coverage is not disabled; it was never possible in this
configuration.

=== THE FIX, and it is small ===
1. WRITE PORTAL_TENANT_ID in the e2e workflow beside NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. The
   seed already knows the tenant - TENANT_A, fixtures.ts:8. One line.
2. THEN a spec can exercise the real OTP path end to end, because the OTP
   transport has a TEST SINK (otp-transport.ts createOtpTestSink) that captures
   codes in-process. Reading the code from the sink is NOT a back door in the
   login path - the sink is shipped, flag-gated production code and is what runs
   whenever OTP_LIVE_SEND is off.
3. KEEP the trusted-device specs. They cover the returning-patient path, which is
   the one most patients take daily. This adds the FIRST-login path beside them.

=== WHY HIGH ===
PG1 - AUTH - passed on the owner's deployed-screen observation, which is the
right evidence under WF-03 and is a POINT-IN-TIME check. Nothing in CI defends it
between now and launch. A gate closed on an observation with no automated guard
behind it is exactly the shape this board keeps finding.

cards.title: Six portal i18n keys are referenced by zero files - 403, 500 and offline - so an audit counts them as coverage and they imply screens that do not exist

evidence.ref:
RULED AND EXECUTED 2026-08-20. Owner ruling on Q-PORTAL-DEAD-I18N-1: the card's split recommendation, applied.

DELETED, 35 keys from BOTH locales: the 33 `auth` strings and `errors.403_title` / `errors.403_body`.

THE 33 auth STRINGS WERE THE WORST OF THE 163 and were the reason the ruling was worth asking for. Portal login is phone-and-code under Decision D; those strings described an email-and-password screen THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, including 'Recuperar palavra-passe'. Anyone auditing whether the portal has password recovery found the copy for it and concluded it did.

errors.403_* DELETED rather than wired: Decision D leaves a portal patient no route that can 403, and the body offered NO retry, NO navigation and NO telephone - being dead was the only thing stopping it shipping as a dead end.

errors.500_* WIRED UP, and it closed a real gap rather than merely spending a key. apps/portal/app/global-error.tsx did not exist. Every ROUTE had an error.tsx with pt-PT copy and the clinic's telephone; the ROOT had nothing, so a crash in the root layout, in a provider, or before a route boundary mounts fell past all of them to Next's framework default: an UNSTYLED ENGLISH PAGE, on a patient-facing product that is pt-PT only.

TWO DECISIONS IN THAT BOUNDARY, both because it replaces the root layout when it fires. It renders its own <html lang> from the same htmlLang() the layout uses, so a screen reader is not handed English markup describing Portuguese text. And it inlines its styles and the two telephone numbers rather than importing ClinicPhones: a boundary that catches 'the app failed to render' must not depend on more of the app rendering, and one that needs the stylesheet is one that renders unstyled exactly when it is needed.

errors.offline_* KEPT AND DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, which departs from the card's recommendation and is flagged rather than buried. `navigator.onLine` reports TRUE on a router with no internet, so a banner built on it would tell a working patient they are offline - section 1.3's shape, in the product rather than in an instrument. Detecting it honestly means distinguishing a NETWORK failure from an HTTP failure inside the portal's api client, which is its own piece of work. Carded as LE-portal-offline-state-unwired, and the two keys stay DECLARED_DEAD with that reason in the guard.

THE RATCHET IS LOWERED, 163 -> 126, and RE-MEASURED rather than subtracted. 163 - 33 - 2 (403) - 2 (500, now live) = 126, and the scan confirms 126. Lowering it when keys are removed is the point; raising it is how a ratchet becomes a rubber stamp.

THE REMAINING 126 ARE LEFT, per the card: mostly forward copy for screens that are planned rather than retired, decided as those screens land. They cannot grow silently.

Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck, test, build. pnpm test:scripts green with the lowered ceiling.

The ruling took the card's split recommendation. One departure, flagged rather
