TRUE on a router with no internet and a banner built on it would tell a working
patient they are offline. That is section 1.3 in the product. Carded.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

=== SPLIT 2026-08-20. THE COUNT IS RATCHETED; THE DELETION IS OWED. ===

READ THE EVIDENCE REF FIRST: THIS CARD SAYS SIX AND IT IS AT LEAST 163.
The six were found while answering one question about a 403 and were never the
class. The biggest group is `auth` at 33 - the password and magic-link login
Decision D retired - which is a far better example of this card's own point
than the error pages are.

BLOCKED ON IVAN, home_lane moved to in_flight so it lands in his column. The
question is at docs/QUESTIONS.md > Q-PORTAL-DEAD-I18N-1, with a recommendation
SPLIT by group rather than one answer for all 163.

NOTHING WAS DELETED AND NOTHING WAS WIRED UP. All 163 are still there and the
trap is still live. What changed is that it cannot get worse silently.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

FOUND 2026-08-12 WHILE ANSWERING "can a patient reach a 403". CARDED, NOT FIXED, ON
INSTRUCTION.

THE SIX, each referenced by ZERO files in apps/portal:
  errors.403_title      errors.403_body
  errors.500_title      errors.500_body
  errors.offline_title  errors.offline_body

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not tidiness: A DEAD KEY READS AS COVERAGE. Anyone
auditing "does the portal handle a 403 well" finds a pt-PT string, a sensible
sentence, and concludes the case is handled. It is not handled - it is
UNREACHABLE, which is a different and better fact, but nothing on the surface
says so. The keys imply screens that do not exist.

403 IS ALSO THE WORST-WRITTEN OF THEM, which compounds it: "Não tem permissão
para ver esta página" offers NO ACTION AT ALL - no retry, no navigation, no
telephone. If anyone ever wires it up as-is, they ship a dead end. The string
being dead is currently the only thing preventing that.

WHY IT WAS NOT DELETED THIS SESSION: deleting product strings is a change with no
benefit to the gate and some risk - a future 403 page would need them back, and
the en/pt files must stay in step. The decision belongs with whoever owns the
portal's error surface, not with a terminal closing a gate.

THE OPTIONS, for whoever takes it:
  a. DELETE all six from both locales. Cleanest. A future 403 page writes fresh
     copy, which it would need anyway since the current 403 body is unusable.
  b. KEEP and wire up a real 500/offline boundary. Defensible for 500 and
     offline, which ARE reachable states of a browser even if no route renders
     them today. NOT defensible for 403 under Decision D.
  c. KEEP and annotate. Impossible in JSON without a convention this repo does
     not have.
RECOMMENDED: (a) for 403, (b) for 500 and offline - they are different cases and
lumping them is why they are all still here.

cards.title: v2-gold-700 as label text on v2-gold-100 is 3.94:1, below the AA floor, on the admin page badge and the accent icon circle - found by the same measurement that reddened PG9, and NOT fixed there because it is staff-facing

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build. packages/ui contrast-aa.test.ts 7 assertions, all pass.

THE CARD IS A FALSE ALARM, AND THE MEASUREMENTS ARE BELOW SO NOBODY RE-OPENS IT WITHOUT THEM. It claims `text-v2-gold-700` on `bg-v2-gold-100` is 'a real AA failure on a rendered staff screen'. NOTHING RENDERED FAILS, for two independent reasons, both re-derived from main at a79efd3:

  1. THAT PAIRING ONLY EVER LANDS ON AN ICON. Both call sites - apps/web/app/admin/page.tsx and packages/ui/src/components/v2-accent.ts - put it on an `aria-hidden="true"` circle wrapping a lucide icon, with NO TEXT INSIDE IT. Read at admin/page.tsx:58-63. That is a GRAPHICAL OBJECT under SC 1.4.11 (3:1), and a decorative aria-hidden one at that. Measured 3.99:1: it clears.

  2. THE ONE GENUINE TEXT USE IS ON A DIFFERENT SURFACE. apps/web/lib/scheduling/therapist-color.ts renders the patient name in the therapist's hue inside `.glass-card`, which is rgba(255,255,255,0.72) over v2-bg - composited #FDFDFE. gold-700 there is 4.73:1, and the worst hue in the whole palette is green-700 at 4.62:1. Every one clears.

THE CARD'S NUMBERS ARE ALSO SLIGHTLY WRONG, corrected here rather than repeated: gold-700 on gold-100 is 3.99:1 and not 3.94:1; v2-gold-800 is #6F5028 and not #6F4F26; gold-800 is 7.36:1 on white and 6.61:1 on surface-muted, not 7.44 and 6.68. None of it changes the answer and all of it was recomputed rather than trusted.

THE PROPOSED FIX WAS THEREFORE NOT APPLIED, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Moving the two icon circles to gold-800 would darken a staff screen visibly for no accessibility gain, because 3.99:1 already clears the floor that applies to them. Moving THERAPIST_COLORS to gold-800 would fix a failure that does not occur on the surface it renders on, would change the agenda's gold hue visibly, and would leave green-700 (4.22:1 on surface-muted) and accent-2-700 (4.34:1) untouched - fixing one of three is the half-measure that reads as done.

WHAT SHIPPED IS WHAT THE CARD ACTUALLY ASKED FOR, in its own words: 'the gold USAGE is not yet covered - covering it means walking call sites rather than tokens, and that is this card's work.' Two new arms in packages/ui/src/contrast-aa.test.ts, plus a third pinning the instrument.

ARM 3: every entry of V2_ACCENT_TINT clears the 3:1 graphical floor on its own tint, parsed out of v2-accent.ts rather than restated. Five pairs asserted, and the count is asserted first.

ARM 4: every therapist hue clears 4.5:1 as TEXT on the COMPOSITED glass surface. THE COMPOSITE IS THE PIECE NOBODY HAD DONE. Every earlier measurement in this repo compared a label against an OPAQUE token; the surface the agenda actually renders names on is TRANSLUCENT. Checking against v2-bg under-reports the contrast and checking against white over-reports it. The composite is computed from the tokens, so retuning either re-runs it, and BOTH opacities are checked - 0.72 for .glass-card and 0.92 for section 4.4's no-backdrop fallback, because a browser without backdrop-filter gets the second and a guard that only checked the one it remembered would be right about half the renderings.

WALKING THE CALL SITES FOUND A SECOND PALETTE THE CARD DID NOT MENTION. therapist-color.ts carries the 7 deterministic THERAPIST_COLORS and, separately, 23 distinct stored-colour hues behind paletteColorByKey - forest, chartreuse, olive, cyan, navy, violet, magenta, pink, orange, mustard, red, brick, wine, brown, gray, ink. A guard written to 'the therapist palette' from memory would have checked SEVEN OF TWENTY-THREE and reported a clean sweep. All 23 are checked and all 23 clear.

ARM 5 pins the composite itself: alpha 1 returns the overlay, alpha 0 returns the backdrop, and 0.72 white over #F7F8FA is #FDFDFE. Without it a `composite` that ignored alpha would silently check every hue against pure white, which is the most generous surface there is.

FIVE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each restored from the git index, baseline 7/7 green after:
  an icon set to text-v2-gold-100 -> arm 3 red at '1.00:1, below the 3:1 floor'.
  a palette hue set to text-v2-gold-100 -> arm 4 red, naming the surface.
  the composite made to ignore alpha -> arm 5 red.
  the accent map's entry SHAPE changed so the regex stops matching -> arm 3 red at 'parsed to no pairs ... this guard is checking nothing'. The first version of this control only removed the TYPE ANNOTATION and did NOT redden, because the regex reads the entries rather than the declaration - so the control was re-aimed at the thing it was meant to break.
  the palette shrunk to 3 entries -> arm 4 red at 'too few text tokens'.

THE RESIDUAL, RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED, because it is real and no call site reaches it: gold-700 (4.31:1), accent-2-700 (4.34:1) and green-700 (4.22:1) are all below 4.5:1 on `surface-muted`. NO CURRENT CALL SITE PUTS ANY OF THEM THERE. Arm 1 already refuses to let any be re-annotated as AA label text; arms 3 and 4 now refuse to let a call site drift onto a surface where they fail. If a fourth surface is ever introduced under a label, that is what to re-run.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. No colour changed and no screen changed; what changed is that three claims about colours are now computed on every commit.
