cards.title: Seven more e2e probes use isVisible() as if it waited. The four that passed a timeout are fixed; these pass none, so they read as deliberate - one file already documents the lesson and the others have not learned it

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19. Re-derived from main at 0eb005d before building; THE CARD'S OWN LIST IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and the corrections are the substance of this close.

=== THE CARD SAID THE isVisible({timeout}) SHAPE WAS ALL FIXED. TWO SURVIVED. ===
"Grepping for that shape found four sites, all in sync-portal-agenda, all fixed in the PG9 PR." Against main today there were TWO MORE, both written AFTERWARDS, both in apps/web/e2e/portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts (:116 and :129). That is the exact INC-10 shape - the option playwright-core 1.60.0 ignores.

AND :116 CARRIED A COMMENT JUSTIFYING ITSELF WITH A WAIT THAT DID NOT EXIST: "here it follows an explicit waitFor-style timeout on a heading that is either present or the flow is broken". The { timeout: 15_000 } it referred to is the IGNORED option, so there was no timeout on that heading at all; and the waitFor four lines above is on anyTherapist, a DIFFERENT locator. A justification naming a wait that is not there is worse than none: it stops the next reader looking. That comment also cited THIS CARD by id, so the card was being used as cover for the shape it exists to remove.

=== ONE OF THE EIGHT LISTED SITES IS NOT A DEFECT AT ALL ===
marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts:124 is the CORRECT pattern: a Promise.race settles the drawer into one of its two terminal states FIRST, and only then is isVisible() used as a pure state query. The card cites that same file's comment as proof "the lesson did not spread" - but that file is where it DID spread. The bare isVisible() after an explicit settle is honest and is kept.

=== THE FIVE MODAL PROBES ARE FLAKE RISKS, NOT FALSE-GREEN RISKS ===
The card says "five of them gate an early return or a skip-shaped branch, which is the outcome that reads as a pass". Re-read, all five (equipa-primary-service :28/:145, working-hours:24, staff-primary-service:27, agenda-blocked-time:42, therapist-blocks:62) gate an OPEN, and the false branch clicks Gerir then runs a real expect(modal).toBeVisible(), which waits. Neither branch can silently skip. NOT FIXED, and the reason is stated rather than left as an omission: changing five call sites that are wrong only in the flake direction would be churn on files proven in CI, and the eslint rule below stops the dangerous form regardless.

I ALSO CHECKED AND REJECTED A SHARPER CLAIM I EXPECTED TO MAKE: that manageModal's getByRole("dialog",{name:/Gerir/i}) names no member, so a foreign member's modal could satisfy the probe and the password-gated delete would run against the wrong staff member. It is NOT REACHABLE - each test opens only one member's modal and Playwright gives each test a fresh context. Recorded because it would have shipped as a finding if I had not checked it.

=== WHAT WAS BUILT ===
1. The three real sites in portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts, :72 included. :72 was an immediate poll deciding whether to pick a clinic, and a false reading SKIPS the pick and carries on - the one genuine skip-shaped branch in the whole list.
2. becameVisible() lifted from sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts into e2e/helpers/index.ts as the single shared definition. It re-throws every non-TimeoutError, which is the half a bare .catch(() => false) gets wrong: a detached frame, a closed page and a bad selector all become "no", and "no" is the branch that skips.
3. THE ESLINT RULE THE CARD ASKED FOR, scoped to e2e/**: no-restricted-syntax on CallExpression[callee.property.name='isVisible'][arguments.length>0]. Bans EVERY argument, because timeout is the only key the signature accepts, so any argument is the defective form. The bare isVisible() stays legal.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, and it proves the two things a rule can be silently wrong about: re-introducing one isVisible({timeout:10_000}) makes the rule fire at the right line AND makes pnpm lint exit 1. So the selector matches and the gate actually covers e2e/ - a lint rule in a directory the gate does not lint is the same defect as an uncollected test, which this repo has had twice.

WHY A RULE AND NOT A COMMENT: the card's own argument. marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts documented this lesson before INC-10 and the lesson did not spread; two new instances were written after the four were fixed. A comment did not stop it recurring.

Gates: pnpm lint 0 errors, pnpm typecheck 11/11, pnpm test 232 files / 2286 passed (web) and 8/8 tasks, pnpm build 4/4. Playwright still collects portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts (16 tests across its projects, verified with --list).

DE-DUPLICATED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. The shared helper's comment says "the single shared definition", so sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts's local copy was removed and it now imports the same function - otherwise that sentence would have been false the moment it was written. The body is byte-identical; its measured evidence (run 31649767622: the agenda read false at 443ms and true at 1683ms, same commit, same seed) was copied onto the shared helper so the number travels with the fix, and the full account stays in the spec where it was found. All four gates re-run after the move, and Playwright still collects sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-13 FROM THE INC-10 SWEEP, WHICH FOUND ITS OWN GENERALISATION.

INC-10 was caused by isVisible({ timeout: N }) - an option playwright-core 1.60.0
ignores. Grepping for that shape found four sites, all in sync-portal-agenda, all
fixed in the PG9 PR. THE SWEEP THEN FOUND A SECOND SHAPE and it is subtler:

  apps/web/e2e/agenda-blocked-time.spec.ts:42       if (!(await manage.isVisible()))
  apps/web/e2e/equipa-primary-service.spec.ts:28,145
  apps/web/e2e/staff-primary-service.spec.ts:27
  apps/web/e2e/therapist-blocks.spec.ts:62
  apps/web/e2e/working-hours.spec.ts:24
  apps/web/e2e/portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts:72
  apps/web/e2e/marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts:124

These pass NO timeout, so they are honest about being immediate - and they are
still racing whatever rendered last. Five of them gate an early return or a
skip-shaped branch, which is the outcome that reads as a pass.

apps/web/e2e/marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts:86 ALREADY CARRIES A COMMENT SAYING SO:
"isVisible() DOES NOT AUTO-WAIT. It is an immediate poll". That comment was
written before INC-10 and did not spread. THE LESSON EXISTED IN THE REPO AND COST
A DAY ANYWAY, which is the argument for a lint rule over a comment.

=== THE FIX ===
Triage each site: an OPTIONAL element wants a bounded wait (becameVisible in
sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts is the pattern - waitFor, TimeoutError is the negative
answer, every other error re-thrown); a REQUIRED element wants
expect(locator).toBeVisible(). Then consider an eslint rule banning
isVisible({timeout}) outright, since that form is always wrong.

=== WHY MEDIUM ===
None of these seven is gate-bearing today. The gate-bearing one was fixed. This is
the tail, and it is worth doing before it produces its own INC-10.

=== RE-DERIVED AND CLOSED 2026-08-19. THE LIST ABOVE IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. ===
It UNDER-counted: it says the isVisible({timeout}) shape was all fixed in the PG9 PR, and two more had been written since, in portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts. One of them cited THIS CARD by id in a comment that justified itself with a wait that does not exist.
It OVER-counted: marcacoes-tab-edit.spec.ts:124 is the correct pattern, not a defect - the card quotes that file's comment as evidence the lesson did not spread, and that file is where it did.
And it MIS-CHARACTERISED the five modal probes: they gate an OPEN followed by a real expect().toBeVisible(), so neither branch silently skips. They are flake risks, not the "reads as a pass" shape.
Left in place rather than edited out, because the pattern is now the third card in this sweep whose own diagnosis needed correcting before it could be built, and that is worth being able to see.

cards.title: THIRD DIFFERENT FLAKY TEST, now in the UNIT suite as well as e2e: preselection Servico, agenda-card stacking, and a booking.test.ts timeout. The pattern is the environment, not any one spec

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19 in PR #954, squashed to 2055356.

THE CARD'S DIAGNOSIS WAS THE TRIGGER, NOT THE CAUSE, and the correction is the value here. The card concluded the common factor was 'the RUNNER being slow enough, occasionally, that a timeout-bounded assertion loses'. The runner IS the trigger. The cause is that two unit suites were making a REAL DATABASE CONNECTION ATTEMPT, and the CI log had been saying so all along, naming the block's own fixture:
  [notifications] patient-change emit FAILED kind=cancelled tenant=t-1 appointment=appt-alice Error: @osteojp/db: DATABASE_URL is not set.

cancelAppointment calls emitPatientChange, which is best-effort and swallows its own failure - nothing failed, nothing was asserted, the only trace was a log line. But it does not return instantly: it resolves a client and attempts a connection first. That is the variable-latency step that pushed a sub-second test past five seconds.

THE STUB EXISTED AND WAS SCOPED TO ONE describe. `setPatientChangeConsumer(stubConsumer)` sat in a beforeEach inside a LATER block, so every block above it ran against the real consumer. Hoisting it to file scope is the whole fix.

A SECOND SUITE HAD THE SAME DEFECT (reschedule-options.test.ts), found by grepping the whole suite for the log line that gave the first one away rather than waiting for it to flake. `pnpm test` now reports ZERO connection attempts, down from one per affected test - a countable before and after rather than 'it passed this time'.

NOT A TIMEOUT BUMP, which was the obvious answer: a longer timeout makes the flake rarer while leaving a unit test dependent on how fast a socket fails. Neither test ever wanted the network.

THIS TERMINAL HIT THE FLAKE TWICE TODAY, on PRs touching neither file (#935 and #945), which is the corroboration the card asked for.

cards.notes:
=== THIRD OCCURRENCE 2026-08-13, AND IT MOVED OUT OF e2e INTO THE UNIT SUITE ===
  run 31651759598  e2e shard 1   booking-service-preselection.spec.ts:35
  run 31654055053  e2e shard 1   agenda-cards.spec.ts:106
  run 31719375051  CI unit       apps/api lib/appointments/booking.test.ts
                                 "allows a cancel outside 24h", 5040ms
GREEN ON RE-RUN OF THE SAME COMMIT, which is what makes it a flake rather than a
finding.

THE THIRD ONE WIDENS THE PATTERN. The first two were e2e on a shared seeded
database, which pointed at cross-spec interference. This one is a UNIT test in a
different app with no database at all, and it failed on a 5040ms TIMEOUT - the
suite runs in well under a second locally, 24/24. So the common factor is not the
shared database; it is the RUNNER being slow enough, occasionally, that a
timeout-bounded assertion loses.

RE-RUN WAS JUSTIFIED BY EVIDENCE, NOT REFLEX, and the distinction is the one
CI-supabase-cli-setup-flaky warned about ("a step that reddens at random trains
people to re-run instead of read"). What was read BEFORE re-running:
  the diff touches apps/web/app/agenda and docs ONLY - ZERO apps/api files, so
    the change cannot reach the failing suite;
  the suite passes locally, 24/24;
  the failure is a 5040ms timeout, not an assertion mismatch.
Only then was it re-run, and it went green.

WHAT THIS SUGGESTS THE FIX IS, and it is now a different fix from the one this
card opened with. Not --repeat-each on one spec: raise or remove the per-test
timeout on assertions that are bounded by wall clock rather than by behaviour,
and find which ones those are. A test that fails ONLY because a runner was busy
is measuring the runner.

STILL NOT GATE-BEARING. None of the three is. But three intermittent reds across
two suites and two apps, on the day of a clinic handover, is exactly the noise
that makes a real red easy to dismiss.

--- prior notes below, unedited ---

WIDENED 2026-08-13 AFTER A SECOND OCCURRENCE ON A DIFFERENT TEST. Raised from medium
to high, because two different flaky tests on the same shard in two consecutive
runs is a property of the environment rather than of either spec.

  run 31651759598  shard 1  1 flaky  booking-service-preselection.spec.ts:35 (PL-06a)
  run 31652671983  shard 1  0 flaky
  run 31654055053  shard 1  1 flaky  agenda-cards.spec.ts:106 (W11-00 v3)
Shards 2 and 3 were clean in all three runs, including every gate-bearing test.

=== OCCURRENCE 1, verbatim ===
  e2e/booking-service-preselection.spec.ts:35  PL-06a
  expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed
  Locator:  getByRole('dialog').getByLabel(/Servico/i).locator('option:checked')
  Expected: "Drenagem Linfatica"
  Received: "Osteopatia"
  13 x locator resolved to <option value="...a201">Osteopatia</option>
Green on retry.

=== OCCURRENCE 2 ===
  e2e/agenda-cards.spec.ts:106
  "W11-00 v3: three same-slot appointments stack VERTICALLY (equal x, different
   y) in BOTH Dia and Semana", 10.5s
Green on retry.

=== WHAT THE TWO HAVE IN COMMON, AND IT IS THE LEAD ===
BOTH READ SHARED, MUTABLE APPOINTMENT STATE ON A SHARED SEEDED DATABASE. One
reads the service selected on an appointment; the other counts appointments
stacked in one slot. Neither is scoped to a row it created. That is exactly
ACC-identity-blind-assertions: an assertion that matches shared vocabulary
rather than identity, on a database several specs are writing to at once.

THIRTEEN POLLS IS THE INFORMATIVE DETAIL from occurrence 1. The assertion DID
retry for its full budget and the select held the wrong value the whole time,
then was right on a fresh attempt. That is not a slow render. Something else had
set that value, or the row under test was not the row expected.

=== DO NOT FIX EITHER BY RAISING A TIMEOUT ===
The timeout was not the constraint - the value was stable and wrong. Raising it
converts a visible flake into an invisible one, which is the shape this project
keeps paying for.

=== FIRST STEP, and it discriminates in one run ===
Re-run each spec ALONE with --repeat-each=5 and nothing else in the shard.
  clean alone, flaky in company  -> cross-spec interference. Merge into
                                    ACC-identity-blind-assertions and fix by
                                    scoping each spec to rows it creates.
  flaky alone                    -> a genuine product race in that screen, and
                                    each gets its own card.

=== WHY THIS IS ON THE BOARD RATHER THAN IN A LOG ===
Both occurrences were flaky PASSES inside runs that were green overall, and one
of those runs closed PG9. A flaky pass is the thing this board has twice been
wrong to wave through. Neither is gate-bearing today, and that is the reason it
is high rather than an incident, not a reason to stop counting.

cards.title: PG8's last DoD line: the trace names nine hops and measures none of them individually. Three end-to-end spans exist; the timing table the DoD asks for needs server-side instrumentation, because a browser cannot see inside one fetch

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-13. The timing table is at docs/recon/W13-07-sync-trace.md
section 2.1a and PG8 is CLOSED - board 9/9.

Closed on strategy's amendment that the createBooking transaction is ONE measured
hop, labelled atomic by design. The card's own warning held: no instrumentation
was added inside the transaction, and none was added to the spec either - the
spans were already being logged by the timed() helper, so the table is assembled
from runs that had already happened rather than from a new measurement campaign.

THE CARD SAID WHAT NOT TO DO AND IT WAS NOT DONE: "do not close PG8 by re-reading
the spans as though they were per-hop timings". They are not presented as
per-hop. A5+A6+A7 is labelled as one grouped hop, A1/A2/A4 are labelled as
inseparable from the browser, and A9 is labelled unbounded. Every cell says what
it is.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-13. THIS IS THE ONLY THING BETWEEN PG8 AND 9/9, and it is a
measurement rather than a discovery. Everything else on LOOP 7's DoD is done.

=== THE LINE, VERBATIM FROM WAVE-13.md LOOP 7 SECTION 3 ===
"The trace names every hop and its timing, in both directions."
Section 4, evidence required: "The timing table."

=== WHAT EXISTS ===
HOPS: nine, direction A, at docs/recon/W13-07-sync-trace.md section 2. Named,
with each latency CHARACTERISED - request-bound, one query, UNBOUNDED - which the
document itself says is not the same as measured.
SPANS, measured on runs 31651759598 and 31652671983:
  A: portal booking submitted                 1268ms / 1342ms
  A: agenda shows the row on the booked day    548ms /  587ms
  B: portal slot list first paint              424ms
Each crosses a GROUP of hops.

=== WHY THE SPEC CANNOT SUPPLY THE REST ===
Playwright times what the browser observes. A3-A7 happen inside apps/api and
Postgres, behind one fetch. No browser-side timer separates the route handler
from the slot-lock acquisition from the insert. Adding console.log lines to the
spec CANNOT close this line, and trying would produce a table that looks
complete and is not - which is this project's most-repeated failure mode.

=== THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, ONE RECOMMENDATION RATHER THAN A SURVEY ===
Emit per-hop marks from the API on the booking path, keyed by a request id the
spec can correlate, and read them from the response or the server log the
Playwright webServer already captures. Prefer Server-Timing headers: they are a
standard, they are already visible to a browser-side test, and they do not need a
new logging channel. NO PII in the marks - hop name and duration only, per rule 7.

=== AND THE WARNING THAT BELONGS BESIDE IT ===
Trace section 3 records what happened the last time this file gained a
diagnostic: a 30s waitForURL added to answer one question ran on every attempt
including both retries, pushed shard 3 past the job timeout, and the run was
CANCELLED - destroying the very measurement the previous commit had set up. Any
instrumentation added here must be cheap on the hot path and must be removed or
made permanent deliberately, not left in place by default.

=== WHAT NOT TO DO ===
Do not close PG8 by re-reading the spans as though they were per-hop timings.
Four of five DoD lines done is a card, not gate credit - rule 4.5, which is what
caught this gate's two earlier false greens.

cards.title: CLOSED: a patient whose phone is stored the way a human writes it can now log in. Migration 0062 derives phone_e164 GENERATED ALWAYS from phone; applied to production 2026-08-13, PR #888 merged as 4ae5a39

evidence.ref:
APPLIED TO PRODUCTION 2026-08-13. Journal verbatim at docs/migration-apply-0062.md section 9.
THE EXECUTION PROOF, and it is the pair rather than either half:
  before   last applied "when" in the database: 1786900000000
           pending: 1     PENDING  0062_patient_phone_e164  when=1787000000000
  after    last applied "when" in the database: 1787000000000
           pending: 0
  checkout HEAD is now at 4adafcf - the pinned sha, not a branch head
"migrations applied successfully!" is the LEAST valuable line in that output;
drizzle-kit prints it whether or not it applied anything. The two pending counts
are what prove execution, and the "when" moving from 1786900000000 to
1787000000000 is the database's own bookkeeping agreeing.
No postgres:// string anywhere in the output; the pre-paste scan passed.
PR #888 merged as 4ae5a39. NEXT FREE MIGRATION NUMBER IS 0063.

=== THE DESIGN IS AN IMPROVEMENT ON THE RULING, NOT COMPLIANCE WITH IT ===
STRATEGY AUTHORIZED a normalized shadow column plus an expression index. That
shape works and it has a hole: SOMETHING HAS TO WRITE THE SHADOW COLUMN, on every
path, forever. The staff form, the portal PATCH, the seed, a backfill script,
LAUNCH-03's importer, and whatever path somebody adds next month. Each one is a
place to forget, and forgetting is silent - the patient simply cannot log in and
nobody learns why.
WHAT SHIPPED IS GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED. The database computes it from
patients.phone on every write, so FORGETTING IS IMPOSSIBLE. There is no write
path to audit because there is no write path. It also cannot drift: a correction
to the stored number corrects the login key in the same statement.
THAT IS THE SAME MOVE AS 0061's CONSTRAINT, one layer down. 0061 chose a database
constraint over more application checks because a constraint cannot be bypassed
by a path nobody thought of. This chose a generated column over application
writes for exactly that reason, and against exactly the same failure mode - the
vacuous-guard shape this project has counted 123 instances of.

=== NON-UNIQUE IS DELIBERATE, AND IT IS THE ANTI-ORACLE DISCIPLINE ===
Two live patients may legitimately share one number - a couple, a parent and a
child - and the login screen already carries pt-PT copy for exactly that case
(otp_shared_number). resolvePatientByProvenPhone REFUSES on several matches
rather than picking one, which is what stops a medical record being mis-linked.
A unique index would have rejected real clinic data at write time instead, and
would have made the database enforce a rule the product deliberately does not.
SAME DISCIPLINE AS THE OTP ENDPOINT: refuse rather than disclose, refuse rather
than guess.

=== THE 0061 LESSON APPLIED IN ITS GENERAL FORM, NOT COPIED AS A RITUAL ===
0061 needed a DO block because it named an opclass (gist_uuid_ops) that Postgres
resolves through search_path, and on Supabase extensions live in 'extensions'
rather than 'public'. THE LESSON IS NOT "ADD A DO BLOCK". It is: do not let the
DDL resolve anything through ambient configuration.
0062 resolves three things and each is pinned at the source - the table written
public.patients, the functions pg_catalog.regexp_replace and pg_catalog.right,
and the index naming NO opclass at all (the default btree for varchar). With
nothing left to resolve, a DO block would have been ceremony. Copying it would
have looked like diligence and taught the next author the wrong rule.

=== THE APPLY SHA MOVED, AND THE DOCTRINE CAUGHT IT ===
A COMMENT-ONLY edit inside 0062 changed the file and therefore moved the sha the
block executes: b7b5b0a -> 4adafcf. Nothing about it looked dangerous. The old sha
still existed and still checked out cleanly - it would simply have applied the
previous DDL text.
0061's doc records this exact trap and says "whenever packages/db/migrations/
changes on this branch, this sha must change with it". IT WAS CAUGHT THE SECOND
TIME BECAUSE THE RULE WAS WRITTEN DOWN, not because anybody was vigilant. The
mirror was re-synced, check-journal re-run, the lockfile comparison redone at the
new sha, and the block re-pinned before it reached the owner.
THAT IS THE DOCTRINE PAYING FOR ITSELF, and it is the argument for writing these
rules down at the moment they are learned rather than after the second incident.

=== WHAT IS PROVEN, AND WHERE ===
IN CI, against production-SHAPED data: the seeded portal patient is stored
"+351 916 000 005" WITH SPACES, exactly as a receptionist types, and
portal-otp-login.spec.ts drives the real login - phone, issued code, session,
dashboard, surviving a reload - green at attempt 1. Run 31701031843 shard 3:
73 passed, 0 failed, 0 flaky.
GUARDED: phone-e164-parity.db.test.ts runs normalizePhonePT and the generated
column over one 23-input corpus and requires identical answers, including a
genuine non-breaking space (codepoint 160, verified present in the source rather
than an ordinary space that looks like one). Hard-required in the skip guard.
INVERTED: patient-linkage.db.test.ts's pinned defect assertion now asserts the
patient LINKS, with two counterweights - a number belonging to nobody must still
refuse, and a stored number that does not normalize must still refuse.

=== ONE THING NOT YET MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT A REGRESSION ===
The pre-check's four numbers were never pasted back, so nobody knows whether 0062
repaired EVERYONE or merely MOST. Those patients could not log in before 0062
either, so it is not a regression - it is an unmeasured remainder. Section 10 of
the apply doc carries a three-integer read-only query, cheaper than the original
because the column now exists and can simply be counted. STILL OWED.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-13, BY THE FIRST CI RUN IN WHICH THE PORTAL'S OTP LOGIN HAS EVER BEEN
EXECUTABLE. The card that unblocked that path - SEC-otp-login-path-has-zero-e2e-coverage -
predicted exactly this: "a real misconfiguration on the OTP login path is
invisible to the suite by construction". It took one run to surface.

HALTED FOR THE OWNER. EVERY CANDIDATE FIX NEEDS A MIGRATION, and this lane does
not author one without him. 0062 is unoccupied and stays that way.

=== THE MECHANISM, IN TWO LINES OF SHIPPED CODE ===
  apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.ts:69
      eq(patients.phone, phoneE164)          <- EXACT STRING COMPARISON
  apps/web/lib/patients/validation.ts:117-124
      optionalText() TRIMS and normalizes nothing
patients.phone is free text. apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts says so in its own
header: "numbers arrive as '912 345 678', '00351912345678',
'+351 912-345-678', etc." The reminders path calls normalizePhonePT on the stored
value before sending, precisely because of this. THE LOGIN PATH DOES NOT.

=== WHAT IT MEANS FOR A PATIENT ===
A patient stored as "+351 912 345 678" types 912345678, receives an SMS code -
the request path never touches the patient table, so the code IS sent - types it
correctly, and is REFUSED. The refusal is the single otp_refused string, the same
one a wrong code produces, because the API deliberately collapses all six
failure modes into one response so the screen cannot be a patient-list oracle.
SO THE PATIENT IS TOLD TO CHECK THE CODE THEY TYPED CORRECTLY. There is no other
door: Decision D removed the password and the magic link.

=== HOW LIKELY IS THIS IN REAL DATA. VERY. ===
EVERY patient in the e2e seed except the new OTP fixture is stored with spaces.
Portuguese numbers are conventionally written with spaces. The staff form caps
length and trims; it does not normalize. Nothing anywhere writes E.164 into
patients.phone.

=== WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT, AND IT IS THE SELF-MOCKING SHAPE AGAIN ===
apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.test.ts MOCKS @osteojp/db entirely. Its fake
select() returns whatever H.rows was set to, and the assertions inspect the SHAPE
of the where clause. IT NEVER MATCHES A PHONE STRING AGAINST A STORED VALUE,
because there is no stored value. It proves the query is ASSEMBLED correctly and
cannot prove it FINDS anything. Same class as fichas/read.test.ts, which LOOP 6's
citation audit caught supplying its own answer through a mock.
otp-claim.db.test.ts is DB-gated and real, and it seeds its own patient with
"+351900000001" - E.164, spaceless - so it agrees with the code by construction
too.

=== PINNED IN CI RATHER THAN LEFT ON A CARD ===
apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.db.test.ts, NEW, DB-gated, hard-required in
assert-rls-executed.mjs. It creates two real rows carrying the SAME number
written two ways and asserts:
  the E.164 row LINKS            <- positive control, so the refusal below is
                                    not an artifact of an empty table
  the human-format row REFUSES   <- THE DEFECT, recorded
  two live rows with one number REFUSE   <- the ambiguity property, on real rows
  claimed and soft-deleted REFUSE, and a restore puts it back
THE DEFECT ASSERTION IS GREEN TODAY AND ITS MESSAGE SAYS TO INVERT IT WHEN THE
FIX LANDS. A card can be missed; a red test cannot.

=== THE OPTIONS, WITH A RECOMMENDATION, FOR THE OWNER ===
1. NORMALIZE ON WRITE plus a one-off backfill. patients.phone becomes canonical
   E.164 everywhere; linkage is unchanged. MIGRATION: a backfill UPDATE.
   RISK: it rewrites a column staff read and edit, and any number that does not
   normalize (a foreign number, a malformed one) must be left alone and reported
   rather than silently dropped.
2. NORMALIZED SHADOW COLUMN + expression index, written by a trigger or a
   generated column; linkage matches on it. MIGRATION: add column + index +
   backfill. The stored display value is untouched, which staff will prefer.
   RECOMMENDED. It fixes the login without editing what anyone typed, and the
   index keeps the login path a single indexed lookup.
3. NORMALIZE IN APPLICATION CODE at read time: fetch the tenant's candidate rows
   and compare normalized values in TypeScript. NO MIGRATION.
   REJECT. It turns an indexed equality on a pre-authentication endpoint into a
   scan of every patient in the tenant, and that endpoint is the one an
   unauthenticated caller can reach.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE ACCEPTANCE IS THE SAME: invert the pinned assertion, and
add a seeded patient stored WITH SPACES that logs in through the portal e2e.

=== WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED ===
No production data has been read. This is derived from the code and from the e2e
seed, both in the repo. Whether any REAL patient row is stored with spaces is a
question for the owner's prod read, not for this lane - but the seed, the
validation code and Portuguese convention all point one way.

cards.title: Two specs now drive the portal booking flow with their own copy of the same date-picker traversal. The second copy invented its own locators and both were wrong, costing a full CI run

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build. The e2e proof is the PR's own CI run - Playwright is the only thing that exercises either spec.

BOTH HALVES OF THIS CARD'S DEFERRAL ARE SPENT, AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS TAKEN NOW. It says the extraction was not done because 'that spec is PG8's, and refactoring it mid-bucket to save a duplication would risk the one gate-bearing e2e in the repo', and it names its own unblock condition: 'DO IT WHEN LE-pg8-per-hop-timings is taken, since that card touches the same file anyway.' PG8 closed at 9/9 on 2026-08-13, and LE-pg8-per-hop-timings reads `shipped` on the board - so the condition passed and the extraction was not done then. Re-derived, not assumed.

WHAT SHIPPED: apps/web/e2e/helpers/booking-picker.ts. One copy of the picker trigger, the dialog, the two hard-won locators, the day walk with its reopen, and the pt-PT aria-label parsing. Both specs import it.

EXTRACTING IT FOUND A THIRD DEFECT IN THE COPY, LIVE ON main UNTIL NOW, and it is the reason this was worth doing rather than a tidy-up. THE POPOVER CLOSES ON SELECT. sync-portal-agenda's proven version reopens it before every attempt after the first; portal-booking-request-mode's copy DID NOT. So its day walk could only ever succeed on the FIRST day it tried: every later days.nth(i).click() acted on a dialog that was no longer open, the loop fell through, and it returned the LEGITIMATE SKIP. A flow defect degrading into the one outcome that skips instead of failing - the exact collapse the discriminated result exists to prevent, inside the helper written to respect it. IT NEVER FIRED because the seed's first enabled day happens to carry slots, which is luck and not a property.

AND A FOURTH, INTRODUCED BY THE EXTRACTION AND CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The helper CLICKS the trigger, and request-mode's own trigger-and-dialog block was still standing above the call. Two clicks would have TOGGLED THE POPOVER SHUT, the walk would have found no gridcells, and it would have reported `empty-calendar` - the same collapse a third way. Removed, with the reasoning in place rather than in a commit message.

WHAT IS SHARED AND WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT, stated in the helper's own header so the next person does not 'finish' the job. NOT SHARED: each spec's way of REACHING the date step - one waits on the clinic BUTTON by seeded name, the other on the clinic HEADING after a URL assertion - because each is right for what its file is about and collapsing them into one flexible opener is how a shared helper becomes a second thing to debug. NOT SHARED EITHER: the submit, because what the two do NEXT differs completely (one reads the appointment id off the pending URL, the other needs only a boolean).

THE DISCRIMINATED RESULT SURVIVES END TO END, which the card names as the one thing the shared helper must keep. The helper returns the same empty-calendar / flow-broken split; sync-portal-agenda WIDENS it into its own BookOutcome rather than flattening it, and portal-booking-request-mode maps it at the call site to its existing contract - false for an empty calendar, THROW for anything else. Neither collapses it into a boolean or a null.

A VACUOUS GUARD REMOVED WHILE PASSING THROUGH. sync-portal-agenda's `if (!bookedIso)` check now sits after a value the helper guarantees is a non-empty string, so it CAN NO LONGER FAIL. Left in place it would read as protection and be none - the shape ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep counts - so it is gone, with a line saying where the check moved to.

NOT OWNER-VISIBLE, so NOT queued into VERIFY-QUEUE. Test-only; no product behaviour changes.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-20. ONE COPY, AND THE EXTRACTION PAID FOR ITSELF. ===

Both halves of this card's own deferral were spent: PG8 closed at 9/9 on
2026-08-13, and LE-pg8-per-hop-timings - the card this one said to wait for -
shipped without the extraction being done.

THE EXTRACTION FOUND A THIRD DEFECT IN THE COPY, live on main: it never
reopened the date popover between attempts, so it could only ever succeed on
the first day it tried and any other outcome arrived as the LEGITIMATE SKIP.
A fourth was introduced by the extraction itself (a double trigger click) and
caught before it shipped. Both are the same collapse, wearing three shapes.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

RAISED 2026-08-13 WHILE FIXING SEC-pending-screen-asserts-nothing, AND THE COST WAS
PAID BEFORE THE CARD WAS WRITTEN.

=== WHAT HAPPENED ===
portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts needed to drive a real booking, so it grew a
bookFirstAvailable helper. sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts already had one - a fuller
version that took FIVE SESSIONS to stabilise and is PG8's gate-bearing spec.
The new helper invented its own locators. BOTH WERE WRONG:
  getByRole("gridcell").filter({ hasNot: locator("[aria-disabled='true']") })
    hasNot filters by DESCENDANT, not by the element's own attribute, so it
    matched every gridcell INCLUDING disabled ones. The click then hung on a
    disabled button for the full 120s test budget - "element is not enabled",
    retried to timeout - three times, 2.1 minutes each. A 12m33s shard.
  getByRole("radio") with no name
    matches any radio on the step rather than a time.
The fix was to copy the proven forms verbatim: .and(page.locator(":not([aria-disabled])"))
intersects on the ELEMENT, and the slot locator is named /^\d{2}:\d{2}$/.

=== THE POINT IS NOT THE LOCATOR, IT IS THAT THERE ARE TWO COPIES ===
Every future change to the booking flow now has to be found in two places, and
the second one will be missed the way it was missed here. This is the same
duplication argument that got phone-e164-parity.db.test.ts written for the
generated column - except there the duplication was unavoidable across two
languages and was guarded by a test; here it is avoidable and is guarded by
nothing.

=== THE FIX, AND WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IMMEDIATELY ===
Extract the traversal into a shared e2e helper both specs import.
NOT DONE MID-BUCKET, DELIBERATELY: sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts is the one
gate-bearing e2e in the repo, PG8 is held one DoD line from closing, and
refactoring it to save a duplication would risk the gate for a tidy-up. The
decision is recorded rather than taken quietly.

DO IT WHEN LE-pg8-per-hop-timings is taken, since that card touches the same
file anyway and the two changes can be proven by one CI run.

=== WHAT THE SHARED HELPER MUST KEEP ===
The discriminated result. sync-portal-agenda's version returns a tagged outcome -
empty-calendar is a legitimate skip, flow-broken is a DEFECT and must be red -
and the new one keeps the same split by returning false only for an empty
calendar and THROWING for everything else. A shared helper that collapsed them
back into a boolean or a null would undo LOOP 7's most expensive lesson.

cards.title: The limiter now EXISTS in apps/web and exactly one route uses it. Every other server action and route handler on the staff surface is still unlimited

evidence.ref:
ADOPTION IN PROGRESS, EVIDENCE PER ROUTE. Route 1 (staff login server action): PR #1010 MERGED, squashed to b8a83a5d. Route 2 (GET /api/webhooks/ifthenpay): PR #1011 MERGED, squashed to 0ecc363f, 7 assertions in apps/web/app/api/webhooks/ifthenpay/rate-limit.test.ts, three negative controls run and restored. Routes 3-7 are NOT built and are listed in the notes with the ordering that selects them. Routes 3 and 4 (POST /api/v1/ingestion/clinical-records and POST /api/v1/integrations/stripe/webhook): PR #1012 MERGED, squashed to a3614f66, 11 assertions across apps/web/app/api/v1/ingestion/clinical-records/rate-limit.test.ts and apps/web/app/api/v1/integrations/stripe/webhook/rate-limit.test.ts, three negative controls run on both. Route 5 (/api/inngest/*) is DECIDED NOT TO LIMIT, reasoning on the card. Routes 6 and 7 NOT REACHED. Route 6 (staff document generation, three actions): PR #1015, branch sec/SEC-limiter-route6-document-generation, 11 assertions in apps/web/lib/clinical/document-rate-limit.test.ts, three negative controls run. Route 7 (authenticated reads) is DECIDED NOT TO LIMIT, reasoning on the card. THE ADOPTION IS COMPLETE: every route in the ordering is built or has a recorded refusal.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-28 BY BLUE. FOUND OPEN, NOT FOUND CLOSED. ===
A dispatch asked me to CONFIRM this card was closed. IT WAS NOT: status was
in_flight on origin/main at 1ad91673, and had been since last_checkpoint
2026-08-24. Re-derived rather than confirmed, and the substance turned out right
while the board was wrong.

EVERY ROUTE IN THE ORDERING, VERIFIED AGAINST GitHub AND THE CARD:
  1  staff login server action              LIMITED   PR #1010, b8a83a5d
  2  GET /api/webhooks/ifthenpay            LIMITED   PR #1011, 0ecc363f
  3  POST /api/v1/ingestion/clinical-records LIMITED  PR #1012, a3614f66
  4  POST /api/v1/integrations/stripe/webhook LIMITED PR #1012, a3614f66
  5  /api/inngest/*                         REASONED REFUSAL
  6a the three document-generation actions  LIMITED   PR #1015, MERGED 443844d0
  6b every other authenticated write        REASONED REFUSAL
  7  authenticated reads                    REASONED REFUSAL

The exit condition was this card's OWN: "it stays in_flight until the ordering in
its notes is exhausted". It is exhausted - every route is built or carries a
recorded refusal, which this card's evidence already said in its last line.

=== WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING ===
AN open_on_purpose WHOSE CONDITION HAS BEEN MET IS AN EXEMPTION THAT HAS EXPIRED,
AND NOTHING EXPIRES IT. reconcile-board.mjs routes EVERY finding on a card
carrying open_on_purpose into the ACKNOWLEDGED list rather than the mismatch
list - by design, so a legitimately-open card does not redden CI. But the
acknowledgement is free text, its condition is not machine-readable, and this
one's text went stale the moment routes 3-7 landed: it still said "routes 3 and 4
are next; route 5 is analysed", four days after all of them were done.

So the card was printed on every reconciler run, in full, and read as healthy.
That is the exemption-nobody-revisits shape the reconciler's own header warns
about, met from the inside.

NOT BUILT: a guard that expires an acknowledgement. It would need the exit
condition to be machine-readable, which is a real design question and is new
work; this dispatch ends in a hold. Recorded here so the next session meets the
finding rather than the symptom.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-13 ON SHIPPING SEC-r-token-no-rate-limit, so the remaining scope is
stated rather than left implied by a card marked done.

WHAT THAT CARD CLOSED: apps/web had NO limiting concept at all. It now has one -
@osteojp/rate-limit, consumed in one import - and the PUBLIC, UNAUTHENTICATED
/r/[token] redeem POST is limited.

WHAT IT DID NOT CLOSE: every other server action and route handler in apps/web.
That is the whole staff platform.

WHY IT IS MEDIUM AND NOT HIGH, WHICH IS THE CARD'S OWN GRADING. The staff surface
is AUTHENTICATED, which bounds abuse to authenticated users - a bounded set of
named people with an audit trail behind every action. The original card said the
public route "is simply the first patient-facing route on that surface where it
began to matter", and it was right.

THE SHAPE OF THE WORK, and it is adoption rather than design. The decisions are
made: the package exists, clientKeyFromHeaders works from a server action, the
durable store needs no migration, and RULES is one file. What remains is walking
the surface and choosing a rule per route - which is a judgement per route rather
than a mechanical sweep, because the right limit for a login attempt is not the
right limit for a calendar read.

DO NOT DO IT AS ONE PR. A blanket limit applied everywhere at once is how a
legitimate burst - a receptionist pasting a day's bookings, an admin running an
export - becomes a support call that looks like an outage. Take the WRITE paths
first, measure nothing breaks, then the reads if they are worth it at all.

=== ADOPTION STARTED 2026-08-21. ROUTE 1 OF N. ORDERED BY EXPOSURE, ONE PR PER ROUTE. ===

THE ORDERING, stated before any of it was built, and derived from apps/web/proxy.ts rather than assumed. The matcher session-gates everything except four paths, so "unauthenticated" is a fact about that regex, not a judgement:

  1. THE STAFF LOGIN SERVER ACTION - unauthenticated BY DEFINITION, publicly reachable, and it takes a password. THIS ROUTE. It is the exception to the card's own "the staff surface is authenticated" reasoning, because it is the thing that does the authenticating.
  2. /api/v1/ingestion/clinical-records - proxy-excluded, HMAC over the raw body. Publicly reachable; an attacker can force HMAC computation over arbitrary bodies.
  3. /api/webhooks/ifthenpay - proxy-excluded, constant-time key check in the handler. Payment callback.
  4. /api/v1/integrations/stripe/webhook - proxy-excluded, Stripe signature over the raw body.
  5. /api/inngest/* and subpaths - proxy-excluded, signing-key gated. Server-to-server.
  6. AUTHENTICATED STAFF WRITES - createAppointment, batchSchedule, the clinical and invoicing actions. Bounded to named people with an audit trail behind every action, which is the card's own grading argument.
  7. AUTHENTICATED READS - the card says "if they are worth it at all", and on this evidence they are not yet.

2 TO 5 ARE ALL SIGNATURE- OR KEY-GATED, which is why none of them outranks the login. A limiter there bounds the COST of forcing that check; on the login there is no check in front at all.

ROUTE 1 SHIPPED: the login action now checks two axes before it reaches Supabase - per credential (6/min) and per source (20/min) - with the credential keyed on a NON-REVERSIBLE DIGEST, lower-cased so "Ana@" and "ana@" are one bucket rather than two.

NO GLOBAL CEILING, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECISION. The two global ceilings already in RULES bound a COST a distributed attacker could run up - real money for an SMS, reception's morning for a junk queue. A failed login costs one auth call. A tenant-wide ceiling here would buy nothing and would hand any single attacker a switch that LOCKS THE WHOLE CLINIC OUT OF ITS OWN PLATFORM, on the one route with no way around it. Same reasoning guestCatalogIp already records, and it applies harder here.

THE REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A WRONG PASSWORD, deliberately, and a test asserts the two strings are equal. A "too many attempts" notice would confirm to an attacker that the address is worth continuing with - undoing the non-revealing copy SPEC-staff-screens 11.5 requires one line below it.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, per the card's instruction to take the write paths first and check nothing breaks: 6/min per credential means a receptionist who mistypes twice and looks it up is nowhere near it, and 20/min per source survives a shift change behind one NAT.

=== ROUTE 2 SHIPPED 2026-08-22. THE ORDERING WAS RE-DERIVED AND IT CHANGED. ===

THE CARD'S OWN ORDERING PUT THE IFTHENPAY CALLBACK THIRD. IT IS SECOND, AND THE
CORRECTION IS NOT COSMETIC. The previous ordering grouped items 2 to 5 as "all
signature- or key-gated", and that treated one category where there are two.

  - INGESTION and STRIPE verify an HMAC OVER THE REQUEST BODY. Forging one needs
    the shared secret; the signature is not reachable by guessing at any rate. A
    limiter there bounds COST and nothing else.
  - THE IFTHENPAY CALLBACK COMPARES A STATIC SHARED SECRET FOR EQUALITY.
    apps/web/lib/integrations/ifthenpay/callback.ts safeKeyEqual() compares the
    anti-phishing key (IFTHENPAY_ANTIPHISHING_KEY, name only) constant-time
    against the configured value. CONSTANT TIME DEFEATS A TIMING ORACLE AND SAYS
    NOTHING ABOUT GUESS RATE, which was bounded by nothing at all.

So it is the only one of the three where the gate is guessable, and a successful
guess is not a read: it is a FORGED SETTLEMENT, an invoice marked paid for money
that never arrived, written by the reconciliation job the handler enqueues.
Guessable gate plus financial write outranks unguessable gate plus CPU cost.

ROUTE 2: GET /api/webhooks/ifthenpay. WHAT IT PROTECTS: the anti-phishing key
that is the only thing between a real settlement and a forged one.

BUILT: per source, two windows, 60/min and 600/hour, checked BEFORE
authenticateCallback because the budget being spent is the GUESS budget - taken
afterwards it would count only guesses that already landed. DURABLE store, not
memory, on limiter.ts's own doctrine: a counter an attacker resets by waiting
for a cold instance is not a control. 429 with Retry-After rather than the
login's silent refusal, because there is no enumeration oracle here and
IfThenPay reads any non-200 as redeliver - a throttled real settlement is
DELAYED, never lost.

NO GLOBAL CEILING, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECISION, third time this file records
the same argument (guestCatalogIp, staffLogin*, now this). A tenant-wide ceiling
here would hand any single attacker a switch that STOPS REAL SETTLEMENTS
REACHING THE LEDGER while IfThenPay carries on taking the money. That is a
reconciliation incident bought to prevent a cheap resource attack.

TWO THINGS IT DOES NOT DO, written into the rule rather than left to be found:
it does NOT stop a DISTRIBUTED guesser (buckets are per source; the real control
against that is the entropy of the owner-configured key plus the platform
firewall), and it does NOT BOUND ITS OWN COST (the durable store writes one row
per request including refused ones - bounding volume before the function runs is
the firewall's job).

EVIDENCE: 7 assertions in apps/web/app/api/webhooks/ifthenpay/rate-limit.test.ts,
all pass. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors, 16 warnings,
none in the new files), pnpm typecheck (11/11), pnpm test (244 files, 2407 pass),
pnpm build.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, each restored, baseline 7/7 green after:
  constant bucket key (the accidental global ceiling) -> 3 red
  the anti-phishing key USED as the bucket key -> 4 red, including the assertion
    that the secret never reaches a durable table
  the limiter moved BELOW authenticateCallback -> 2 red

THE THIRD CONTROL CAUGHT A DEFECT IN THE TEST ITSELF, and it is the reason the
controls are run rather than described. The order assertion was originally two
CALL COUNTS - hit called twice, authenticateCallback called once - and it stayed
GREEN with the limiter moved below the comparison, which is the entire defect it
existed to catch. "Both were called" is not "one was called FIRST". Rewritten
onto a single shared sequence every participant appends to, so order is observed
rather than assumed; it then went red as it should. Same family as
ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep criterion F.

TYPECHECK CAUGHT A SECOND ONE: a vi.fn() stub whose implementation takes no
arguments infers calls as an EMPTY TUPLE, so every calls[0][0] assertion failed
to compile. The mock is now typed by its signature.

A FINDING THE LIMITER DOES NOT ADDRESS, recorded not built: the ingestion route
does await req.text() - reading an ARBITRARY-SIZE BODY into memory - BEFORE any
authentication. A rate limit does not fix that; a size cap does. It is named
here so route 3 does not merge implying it was covered.

NEXT: routes 3 and 4 (ingestion + stripe webhook), grouped, both HMAC-over-body
and both cost-bounding only. Route 5 (/api/inngest/*) is ANALYSED AND WILL NOT
BE LIMITED - Inngest retries function invocations as its durability mechanism,
so a limiter there throttles legitimate retry traffic and turns a transient
failure into a permanently lost job. Routes 6 and 7 not reached.

=== ROUTES 3 AND 4 SHIPPED 2026-08-22, GROUPED IN ONE PR. THE GROUPING IS
ARGUED, NOT ASSUMED. ===

THE CARD FORBIDS A BLANKET PR AND THIS IS NOT ONE. What it forbids is "a blanket
limit applied everywhere at once", because a wrong number then becomes a support
call that looks like an outage. These two are grouped on four properties they
share exactly, and they get SEPARATE RULES so a wrong number moves one of them
and not the other:

  both are proxy-excluded and unauthenticated at the session layer;
  both authenticate an HMAC OVER THE RAW BODY, so neither gate is guessable;
  both read an ARBITRARY-SIZE BODY before authenticating anything;
  both take the identical treatment - memory store, per source, limit above the
  body read - and the change is the same four lines in each file.

ROUTE 3: POST /api/v1/ingestion/clinical-records. WHAT IT PROTECTS: the body
read and the HMAC computation an unauthenticated caller can force, repeatedly.
NOT the contents - AI_INGESTION_HMAC_SECRET is what protects those and no limit
changes that.

ROUTE 4: POST /api/v1/integrations/stripe/webhook. WHAT IT PROTECTS: the same,
behind a Stripe signature.

BOTH 120/min PER SOURCE. Two a second sustained from one address. Neither has a
live caller to measure - the AI partner contract is still open and
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset - so the numbers are deliberately loose and the
two constants are separate precisely so the first partner to produce real volume
moves its own.

THE LIMIT IS THE FIRST STATEMENT IN EACH HANDLER, ABOVE req.text(), AND THAT IS
THE WHOLE OF WHAT MAKES IT WORTH DOING. Both routes read an arbitrary-size body
into memory before any authentication. A limiter placed between the read and the
verify would look correct in a diff and would leave the expensive half unbounded.
It is asserted directly: the tests replace req.text() with a spy and assert the
exact sequence limiter -> read-body -> verify.

IT IS STILL NOT A BODY-SIZE CAP. A first large body is read unbounded; what the
limit bounds is REPEATS from a source. That is written into both route headers so
nobody later reads this as a size guard. The finding recorded when route 2
shipped is therefore NARROWED, not closed.

THE MEMORY STORE, AND THIS INVERTS ROUTE 2'S DECISION RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING
IT. A durable hit is a Postgres upsert; the thing it would protect is an HMAC
costing microseconds. A limiter that costs more than its subject is an
AMPLIFIER, not a control. Route 2 pays that cost willingly because its subject
is a GUESS BUDGET and a counter a cold start resets would not bound it at all.
There is no guess budget here. So these two are coarse per-instance throttling,
exactly what limiter.ts's header says the memory store is for, and NOT a cap.

EVIDENCE: 11 assertions, all pass. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm
lint (0 errors, 16 warnings, none in the new files), pnpm typecheck (11/11),
pnpm test (web 246 files / 2418 pass, api 615, portal 249, admin 10), pnpm build.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN ON BOTH ROUTES, each restored, baseline 11/11 green
after:
  the limiter moved BELOW the body read -> 4 red (2 per route)
  the DURABLE store swapped in for the memory one -> 10 red
  a constant bucket key, the accidental global ceiling -> 2 red

=== ROUTE 5 IS DECIDED AND IT IS "DO NOT LIMIT". 2026-08-22. ===

/api/inngest and its four subpaths (consultation, ifthenpay, invoicexpress,
stripe). Analysed, not built, and the decision is recorded here so a later
session does not read the gap as unfinished work.

THE TRAFFIC IS NOT REQUESTS, IT IS DURABLE EXECUTION. Inngest calls back into
serve() for every STEP of every function, and retries are its correctness
mechanism rather than an error path. A 429 to Inngest is read as a step failure,
which produces MORE calls, and retry exhaustion means the job is abandoned. On
this repo that is a patient who never receives a reminder, or the consultation
retry function giving up on a recording whose audio is already deleted.

INC-12 IS THE PRECEDENT AND IT IS EXACT. apps/web/app/api/inngest/route.ts's own
header records it: a module-scope assertion in front of serve() took the route
down for EVERY method, including the GET Inngest uses to introspect and the PUT
it uses to register, so the reminder stream could neither send NOR be
re-registered, from one missing variable. Its closing line is the rule this
decision follows: "Nothing is asserted here on purpose: a route is not a send."
A limiter in front of serve() is the same shape as the thing that caused INC-12.

WHAT PROTECTS IT INSTEAD: INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY, which is already there, plus the
platform firewall for volume. A limiter would bound the same forced-signature
cost routes 3 and 4 bound, and would risk losing clinical work to do it. That
trade is refused.

=== ROUTES 6 AND 7 NOT REACHED, AND NEITHER IS STARTED. ===

6 is the authenticated staff writes (createAppointment, batchSchedule, the
clinical and invoicing actions); 7 is the authenticated reads, which the card
says are worth limiting "if they are worth it at all". Both are bounded to named
people with an audit trail, which is the card's own reason for grading itself
medium, and neither is public. They are the next work on this card.

=== ONE MORE ROUTE THE ORDERING DOES NOT LIST, CHECKED AND CORRECTLY ABSENT. ===

apps/web/app/api/webhooks/twilio/inbound/route.ts exists and is NOT in the
proxy's exclusion list, which at first reading looks like a session-gated
webhook - a defect. It is not. The route is a STUB: REMINDERS_INBOUND is off by
default and it answers 404, and its header states that the path is deliberately
not added to the allow-list because the live handler waits on a deferred
migration. It performs nothing, so there is nothing to limit. Recorded because
the next reader of proxy.ts will notice the same asymmetry and should not have to
re-derive that it is intentional.

=== ROUTES 6 AND 7, 2026-08-24. THE ORDERING WAS RE-DERIVED AND THE
READ/WRITE SPLIT IS THE WRONG AXIS. ===

THE CARD SPLITS THE AUTHENTICATED SURFACE INTO WRITES (6) THEN READS (7). That
split is not what decides whether a limit helps, and building to it would have
limited about a hundred actions that do not need it while missing the ones that
do. THE AXIS THAT MATTERS IS WHETHER AN ACTION LEAVES SOMETHING PERMANENT AND
CUMULATIVE BEHIND.

THE SURFACE, ENUMERATED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED: 30 files carrying "use server" in
apps/web, ~120 exported actions. Every one is behind the session proxy, an
assertCan capability check, and RLS with the two ratified patient scopes
(therapistPatientScope, patientLocationScope). Clinical mutations and
permission-sensitive actions already write audit rows.

THE ORDERING AS BUILT:

  6a. THE THREE DOCUMENT-GENERATION ACTIONS. LIMITED.
  6b. EVERY OTHER AUTHENTICATED WRITE. NOT LIMITED, reasoned below.
  7.  AUTHENTICATED READS. NOT LIMITED, reasoned below. The card's own text
      allows this verdict: "the reads if they are worth it at all".

=== 6a. STAFF DOCUMENT GENERATION. LIMITED. ===

THE THREE ACTIONS, and they were found by asking which authenticated action
leaves something behind rather than by reading the card's categories:

  downloadReportUrlAction      apps/web/app/clinical/[id]/actions.ts:111
  generateRgpdFormUrlAction    apps/web/app/clinical/[id]/actions.ts:153
  generateDeclaracaoUrlAction  apps/web/app/patients/[id]/declaracao-actions.ts:29

WHAT THEY PROTECT AND WHY THEY ARE NOT ORDINARY CRUD. Each call renders a PDF
and writes a NEW PERMANENT OBJECT to Supabase Storage at
`${tenantId}/.../${randomUUID()}.pdf`. THE `upsert: true` ON THOSE UPLOADS IS
INERT, because a fresh UUID never collides - nothing is ever overwritten and
nothing deletes them. A receptionist who edits a patient a thousand times has
changed ONE row a thousand times, under their own name, with an audit trail.
These three add a thousand permanent objects.

BUILT: 20/min and 200/hour, per STAFF USER, checked AFTER the capability check
and AFTER the input-shape check (route 1's ordering, same reason: garbage must
not exhaust a real person's allowance). One shared helper,
apps/web/lib/clinical/document-rate-limit.ts, not three copies - the same
argument the rate-limit package's own header makes about a security control
being copied.

KEYED ON THE STAFF USER, THE FIRST RULE IN THIS FILE WHOSE CALLER IS A NAMED
PRINCIPAL. A user id survives an address change and is what audit_log.
actor_user_id already records, so an operator can line a refusal in
rate_limit_counters up against what that account did. An address key would do
neither and would throttle a whole clinic behind one NAT.

DURABLE STORE, AND HERE IT IS THE CHEAP OPTION. Routes 3 and 4 use memory
because a Postgres upsert costs more than the HMAC it guards. The subject here
is a PDF RENDER PLUS A STORAGE UPLOAD, which dwarf an upsert. Same test - THE
LIMITER MUST BE CHEAPER THAN ITS SUBJECT - opposite answer, because the subject
changed. That is one rule applied three times, not three decisions.

FAIL-CLOSED COSTS NOTHING HERE, and the natural conclusion is the wrong one.
durable-store.ts justifies fail-closed by the OTP verify path, which does not
transfer. The correct reason: ALL THREE ACTIONS READ THE DATABASE TO BUILD THEIR
DOCUMENT (the report and RGPD engines load the record; declaracao/generate.ts
loads location contacts). With no database there is no document either way, so
refusing makes the call fail EARLIER, not more often. Written into the helper.

THE REFUSAL IS LOGGED, AND THAT IS A 1.3 REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A NICETY. All
three actions collapse every failure into { url: null } - not found, not
printable, render error - and a throttled call now joins that set. Collapsing a
new case onto a harmless-looking existing one with no way to tell them apart is
exactly what 1.3 forbids, so the cases are separable in the LOG even though they
are not on the screen. NO IDENTIFIER IS LOGGED: the durable store already holds
the bucket key, so WHO is recoverable from an access-controlled place and the
log only has to establish THAT.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, AND IT IS THE LARGER PROBLEM: THERE IS NO LIFECYCLE ON
GENERATED DOCUMENTS. Twenty legitimate declarations a day is ~7,000 permanent
PDFs a year, every one of them somebody doing their job. THIS LIMIT DOES NOT
TOUCH THAT and must not be read as touching it - it bounds a BURST (a runaway
client loop, a compromised session) and nothing else. Carded separately as
LE-generated-documents-no-lifecycle rather than implied here.

CONSIDERED AND EXCLUDED, so the next reader need not re-derive it: the
upload-URL minters (createUploadUrlAction, createSignatureUploadUrlAction,
signAudioUploadAction) hand out a scoped, short-lived signed URL and the OBJECT
is created by the client's own upload, bounded by what a human actually
uploads. fireConsultationWebhookAction fires the partner webhook, and a limit
there lands in the same trap as route 5: the Inngest scanner re-fires it, the
audio is lifecycle-deleted in 7 days, and a refused re-fire is a clinical record
that will never exist. issueInvoiceAction is a SHELL - it returns server_error
and is gated off by unset credentials, so there is nothing to limit yet.

EVIDENCE: 11 assertions, all pass. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm
lint (0 errors, 16 warnings, none in the new files), pnpm typecheck (11/11),
pnpm test (web 247 files / 2429 pass, api 615, portal 249, admin 10), pnpm build.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each restored, baseline 11/11 after:
  keyed on the address instead of the user -> 4 red
  the refusal log dropped (the 1.3 collapse) -> 2 red
  ONE of the three call sites left unguarded -> 1 red, on the source guard that
    exists precisely because every behavioural assertion passes with the helper
    called from nowhere

TWO DEFECTS THE GATES CAUGHT IN MY OWN WORK, recorded because both were invisible
in a diff:
  THE FIRST CUT CALLED NEXT'S headers() FOR A VALUE NOTHING READS.
  clientKeyFromHeaders short-circuits on `subject` before touching a header, so
  the argument existed only to satisfy a parameter - and calling headers() to
  produce it broke SEVEN existing declaracao tests that invoke the action outside
  a request scope. Fixed properly rather than by mocking: subjectKey(scope,
  subject) is now extracted in the package and clientKeyFromHeaders delegates to
  it, so there is still ONE definition of the bucket format and the authenticated
  path needs no Headers at all.
  THE DURABLE STORE THEN FAILED CLOSED IN THE TEST ENV with no DATABASE_URL,
  turning four more declaracao assertions red. That suite is about
  download-vs-preview and the NIF write-back, so the helper is stubbed open there
  WITH THE REASON WRITTEN IN, and the ceiling keeps its own suite.

=== 6b. EVERY OTHER AUTHENTICATED WRITE. NOT LIMITED. ===

DECIDED, NOT SKIPPED. Roughly 120 actions - appointments, patients, clinical
records, admin CRUD, invoicing, scheduling.

THE CONTROL THAT ACTUALLY ANSWERS THE THREAT IS ALREADY THERE, AND A LIMITER IS
NOT IT. The threat on an authenticated surface is a compromised or misused staff
account. What you need then is to know WHAT IT DID and to STOP IT: the audit log
(CLAUDE.md rule 6, on every clinical mutation and permission-sensitive action),
session revocation, and the two patient scopes that already bound what any one
account can see. A rate limit answers none of those questions. It makes misuse
SLOWER without making it smaller, and it emits no signal anybody reads.

THE COST IS REAL AND IT LANDS ON CLINICAL WORK. The card names the case itself:
"a legitimate burst - a receptionist pasting a day's bookings, an admin running
an export - becomes a support call that looks like an outage." Saving one ficha
is several writes. A morning's bookings is a burst by design.

AND THE SHAPE IS WRONG: ~120 individual judgements, each a new failure mode, for
a control that buys little. That is a large surface of new ways to break a
clinic's morning, bought with almost no security.

=== 7. AUTHENTICATED READS. NOT LIMITED. THE CARD ALLOWS THIS VERDICT. ===

The card says the reads are worth doing "if they are worth it at all". They are
not, and this is the recorded answer rather than an omission.

Everything in 6b applies and two things make it stronger. A read MUTATES
NOTHING, so the accumulation argument that earned 6a its limit is absent
entirely. And the cost of being wrong is worse: the moment a read limit fires it
is a therapist who cannot open a ficha mid-consultation, or reception who cannot
see the diary with a patient on the telephone.

AGAINST BULK EXFILTRATION BY A COMPROMISED SESSION, WHICH IS THE ONLY SERIOUS
CASE, A RATE LIMIT IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT AND A REASSURING ONE - the exact
combination 1.3 warns about. It slows a copy without preventing it, while
reading as though the surface were protected. The scopes bound WHAT can be
reached and the audit log records what was; those are the controls, and both
already exist.

=== THE ADOPTION IS COMPLETE. ===

Every route in the ordering is now either built with evidence or carries a
recorded refusal with its reasoning: 1 and 2 and 6a limited, 3 and 4 limited for
cost only, 5 and 6b and 7 deliberately not limited. THE CARD STAYS in_flight
ONLY UNTIL A SESSION CONFIRMS THERE IS NOTHING FURTHER TO DECIDE - what remains
is not build work.

cards.title: No-show still emits nothing, and it is the one staff transition that CANNOT be fixed without a migration: there is no 'no_show' kind in the CHECK constraint
cards.notes:
SPLIT OFF FROM LE-staff-transitions-emit-nothing ON 2026-08-13, exactly as that card
instructed: "Split the card if the first two are wanted before the third."

CANCEL AND RESCHEDULE SHIPPED. They needed no migration - 0061:248 already
permits 'cancelled' and 'rescheduled' and they were simply never emitted.

NO-SHOW IS DIFFERENT IN KIND, NOT IN EFFORT. staff_notifications_kind_check
permits exactly:
  ('booked','cancelled','rescheduled','appointment_request','confirmed')
There is no 'no_show'. Emitting one would violate the constraint at INSERT time,
on a staff click, which is a runtime failure rather than a compile error.

WHY IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE TYPE UNION EITHER. StaffTransitionKind in
apps/web/lib/notifications/centre.ts lists the three permitted kinds and no more.
Widening the union without widening the constraint would move the failure from a
COMPILE ERROR to a runtime insert violation - the type is doing real work here and
should not be relaxed to make this card look closer than it is.

WHAT IT NEEDS:
  1. A migration adding 'no_show' to the CHECK constraint. That is an owner-gated
     act under rule 7 and the WF-04 precedent, and it is why this card carries
     gate owner_authorizo rather than green_self_merge.
  2. One line added to StaffTransitionKind.
  3. An emit in the status-patch path where a no-show is recorded, following the
     shape cancel and reschedule now use: read the fan-out subjects BEFORE the
     update, emit AFTER commit, best-effort.
Steps 2 and 3 are trivial. Step 1 is the whole card.

IS IT WORTH A MIGRATION ON ITS OWN. Probably not alone - bundle it with the next
migration that has to be applied for another reason, since an apply costs an
owner sitting. That is the same reasoning the owner used to put two unrelated
changes into 0061.

cards.title: FIXED: the Editar marcacao panel showed 11:00 for an appointment stored at 11:25. TimeField could not display a value off its own 15-minute step, so the browser painted the first option instead. DISPLAY ONLY - no data was corrupted

evidence.ref:
WF-03 ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-17,
at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the
patient OTP login screens - the checklist was not to hand and it stays OPEN).

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED in the 2026-08-17 sitting as well, holding since its own 2026-08-13
acceptance: the Editar marcacao Hora control reads the stored minute.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-13, PER WF-03.
WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
staff-visible fix, which is the class PG1, PG3 and INC-05 closed on. The merged
PR is the build half; the observation is what closes the card.

BUILD: PR #895, merged 2026-08-13, squashed as 690fece.
"fix(ui): TimeField could not display a value off its own step, and showed 11:00
for 11:25".

OBSERVED: the owner opened the Editar marcacao panel on the deployed build and
the Hora control reads the stored minute. The reported case was Turma Pilates /
Catarina Vieira, 13.08.2026, stored 11:25 and painted 11:00.

WHAT THE OBSERVATION PROVES THAT CI DID NOT. The defect was a CONTROLLED <select>
handed a value with no matching <option>, so the browser painted the first
visible option instead. That is a rendering behaviour of the browser, not of the
component's return value, and the screen is the only place it is decidable. A
unit assertion on props would have passed against the broken build.

NO DATA WAS EVER CORRUPTED. The card's own recon established this before any code
changed: the agenda grid, the hover card, the Marcacoes list and the same panel's
Disponibilidade block all read 11:25. Only the form field disagreed, which is
what localised the fault to TimeField rather than to the stored value.

cards.notes:
REPORTED BY CARLOS BARRELAS (reception) FROM LIVE STAFF USE, 2026-08-13.
Patient "Turma Pilates", Catarina Vieira, Fisioterapia, sala Ginasio, OsteoJP (LV),
13.08.2026, Agendada / Confirmacao pendente.

=== THE CONTRADICTION WAS ON ONE SCREEN, WHICH IS WHAT LOCALISED IT ===
  agenda grid           11:25-12:20
  agenda hover card     11:25-12:20
  Marcacoes list        11:25-12:20
  Editar marcacao       Hora 11:00        <- the odd one out
  ...and the SAME panel's Disponibilidade block: Ocupado 09:00-09:55, 11:25-12:20
The panel disagreed with itself. That rules out the stored value and points at
the form field, before any code was read.

=== ROOT CAUSE, NAMED ===
packages/ui/src/components/TimeField.tsx. The Hora control is not a native time
input - it is two linked <select>s. Minute options come from minutesForHour(),
generated as m = 0, step, 2*step... with step defaulting to 15 and NO call site
overriding it. So the options are 00/15/30/45.
The select is handed value={25}. NO <option value="25"> EXISTS. A controlled
React <select> whose value matches no option shows the first; the first is
<option value="" disabled hidden>, which the browser skips, so it paints the
first VISIBLE option - 00.
Reproduced from the component's own arithmetic before any change was made.

=== SAVING DID NOT MOVE THE APPOINTMENT, AND THAT MATTERS ===
The fear is worse than the truth and the card says so plainly. form.time still
held the string "11:25" - the select only failed to DISPLAY it. Submit calls
lisbonDateTimeToUtc(form.date, form.time) with "11:25", and timeOfDayChanged
compares form.time !== init.time, both "11:25". NO MOVE, NO WRITE OF 11:00.
NOT A DATA-CORRUPTION PATH.

=== THE HARM IS ENTIRELY ON THE SCREEN, AND IT IS STILL SERIOUS ===
A receptionist opens a row and is told 11:00. Repeat that to a patient and they
arrive 25 minutes early for an appointment the diary holds at 11:25. A second
trap: once the minute select was touched, 25 COULD NOT BE CHOSEN BACK, because
it was not an option.

=== TIMEZONE RULED OUT, AND THE PARSE PATH VERIFIED ANYWAY ===
25 minutes is not an offset. init uses lisbonParts(new Date(editing.startsAt))
padded to HH:mm (appointment-drawer.tsx:170-183) - the identical helper the grid
uses. Parse and format are correct; only the option list was wrong.

=== WHY OFF-STEP TIMES ARE LEGITIMATE, which is why clamping would be wrong ===
Chaining 55-minute appointments off a 30-minute cadence lands on :25 - the same
screen's Ocupado block showed 09:00-09:55 then 11:25-12:20. The control must
represent what the DIARY can hold, not what its own step generates.

=== THE FIX ===
The value is always injected into its own option list, for the HOUR as well as
the minute - an hour outside [min,max] fails identically, and a caller narrowing
the window around an existing appointment would hit it. step still governs what
a user can PICK; it no longer governs what the field can SHOW. The injected
value is sorted into position, not appended.
IT IS IN packages/ui, so block-time-dialog, DeclaracaoDialog and
batch-failure-dialog inherit it.
NO MIGRATION. NO QUERY CHANGE. NO DATA CHANGE.

FIVE NEW TESTS, and the two anti-regression ones are the point: the off-step
minute exists AND is selected, and it sits between 15 and 30 rather than at the
end of the column. Plus: it is NOT offered on any other hour (injecting it
everywhere would silently widen what a caller's step permits), an on-step value's
options are unchanged (the fix must be inert where things already worked), and an
hour outside [min,max] displays rather than silently showing another.
NEGATIVE ARM RUN: removing the minute injection turns two of the five red.

A NOTE ON THE FIRST DRAFT OF THOSE TESTS, because it is the session's own lesson.
They asserted value="11:25" on the <select> and FAILED AGAINST A CORRECT FIX -
renderToStaticMarkup emits selected="" on the OPTION, not value on the select.
The assertions were wrong, not the component. Dumped the real markup rather than
adjusting the fix until the test agreed.

CLOSES ON IVAN'S DEPLOYED SCREEN per WF-03: open this same appointment in Editar
marcacao and read Hora. Batched into the acceptance sitting at bucket end.
