=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-13, PER WF-03.
WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
staff-visible fix, which is the class PG1, PG3 and INC-05 closed on. The merged
PR is the build half; the observation is what closes the card.

BUILD: PR #896, merged 2026-08-13, squashed as 6154acf.
"fix(web): staff cannot book into a location they are not assigned to".

OBSERVED: the owner confirmed on the deployed build that a staff member cannot
create an appointment at a clinic outside their Equipa assignment, and that the
owner account is still unrestricted.

THE SERVER REFUSAL IS WHAT SHIPPED, NOT A RESTRICTED DROPDOWN. A UI-only lock
repeats the INC-08 root cause: the Estado Select offered every status with no
server check and reception reached an illegal transition in one click. A
restricted dropdown is defeated by a stale tab, a second window, or any request
that did not come from the form. All four write paths refuse.

PL-09 WAS NOT THE BUG. It is the only reason anyone noticed. The read path was
scoped and the write path was scoped by nothing, so an LV-only receptionist
created appointments at CB that he could then never see. The recon that found
this HALTED at the read path and reported "no defect here" rather than inventing
a cause, and the owner's own observation supplied the missing step.

CARRIED FORWARD, AND IT IS ON THE HANDOVER: a staff account with NO location
assignment is deliberately unrestricted, so that nobody is locked out of the
application on their first day. That means the scoping only protects a staffer
once Equipa has assigned them a clinic. ASSIGNING A LOCATION IS A MANDATORY
ONBOARDING STEP, stated in the leading section of docs/board/HANDOVER-STATE.md
because a clinic-team reader needs it and will not read the engineering detail.

cards.notes:
RAISED AND FIXED 2026-08-13 FROM CARLOS BARRELAS'S REPORT, VIA A RECON THAT
HALTED RATHER THAN GUESSED.

=== THE RECON THAT FOUND IT, because the route matters ===
Carlos reported JP's appointments missing from his agenda. The READ path was
investigated first and found CORRECT: every predicate on listAppointments was
checked and THERE IS NO ROLE FILTER - PL-06b is intact, is_bookable only. The
recon HALTED there and reported, rather than inventing a substitute cause.
The owner's observation settled it: the appointments existed, ALL AT OsteoJP (CB),
created by a staffer assigned to LV ONLY. PL-09 hid them correctly.
NOT A DEFECT ON THE READ PATH. Closed with that finding.

=== THE ACTUAL DEFECT, WHICH PL-09 MADE VISIBLE ===
The read was scoped and the write was scoped by NOTHING. An LV-only receptionist
selected CB in Nova marcacao and created appointments at CB he could then never
see. STAFF WERE BOOKING BLIND into locations outside their assignment. PL-09 was
not the bug; it is the only reason anyone noticed.

=== THE SERVER REFUSAL IS THE DELIVERABLE. THE FORM IS THE COURTESY. ===
A UI-only lock is the INC-08 root cause repeated: the Estado Select offered every
status with no server check and reception reached an illegal transition in one
click. A restricted dropdown is defeated by a stale tab, a second window, or any
request that did not come from the form.

FOUR WRITE PATHS GUARDED, and the fourth was found by a test rather than by
reading:
  createAppointment           refuses before runScoped
  batchScheduleAppointments   refuses before batchSchedule()
  rescheduleAppointment       refuses on the DESTINATION location
  cloneAppointment            refuses on the SOURCE's location
updateAppointment is EXEMPT STRUCTURALLY - UpdateAppointmentPatch carries
serviceId, room, status and notes and no locationId, so it cannot move an
appointment between clinics. There is an assertion that reddens if a location is
ever added to that patch.

CLONE WAS THE INTERESTING ONE. It names no location - it INHERITS the source
appointment's - so it did not look like a location-carrying path. It is. Its
guard is INSIDE the transaction because the location is not known until the
source row is read, which is the one honest exception to "refuse at the door".
And it does NOT rely on the actor being unable to find the id: they cannot see CB
appointments on a PL-09-scoped agenda, but "they cannot find it" is the read
scope doing the write scope's job, which is the exact confusion this card ends.

=== HOW CLONE WAS FOUND, and it is the session's own lesson again ===
The ordering assertion - "the guard runs BEFORE persistence" - failed with
"batchScheduleAppointments does not reach the database?". Investigating showed
batch delegates to batchSchedule() rather than calling runScoped, AND that the
runScoped I had been matching belonged to cloneAppointment, a path I had not
checked at all. A MIS-WRITTEN ASSERTION FOUND A REAL GAP.

=== ONE SOURCE OF LOCATION TRUTH, WHICH THE DISPATCH REQUIRED ===
bookingLocationScope and viewerLocationScope both call resolveViewerLocationIds.
Neither has its own query. Two sources drift silently and the drift would be
invisible until somebody booked into a clinic they cannot see - exactly how this
was found. Same reasoning as the rate-limit extraction on #892.

WHY TWO FUNCTIONS RATHER THAN ONE. viewerLocationScope returns null for a
THERAPIST, correctly: their reads are bounded by own-data rules, so location is
the wrong axis. The owner ruled that therapists, like reception and admin, may
only BOOK into assigned locations. Reusing the read scope would have left the gap
open one role over. PL-09 IS NOT WEAKENED ANYWHERE - it is untouched.

=== THE FORM, WITH NO NEW UI CODE ===
options.bookableLocations is a NEW field beside options.locations, not a filter
applied to it - locations feeds the agenda TOOLBAR, a read concern, and narrowing
it would change what a therapist can VIEW. The drawer reads the new one, and
PL-14's existing single-location branch then delivers the ruled behaviour for
free: exactly one assigned renders a locked read-only line, several render a
restricted dropdown, owner unrestricted.
The type change forced every construction site to declare the field - the
compiler catching drift, which is why it is a required field rather than optional.

=== A DECISION THE RULING DID NOT COVER, FLAGGED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ===
A staff member with NO assignment falls back to UNRESTRICTED, mirroring PL-09's
own documented fallback so the two cannot disagree: nobody is locked out
mid-onboarding and the restriction takes effect the moment Equipa assigns a
location. Refusing every booking from an unassigned staffer closes a hole nobody
has hit and opens a hard lockout that reads as a broken application on someone's
first day. The reported defect is closed either way - Carlos WAS assigned.

=== THE GUARD FAILS CLOSED, DELIBERATELY ===
Three existing suites went red with "tx.select is not a function" because the
guard adds a read their fakes did not expect. THE GUARD WAS NOT MADE RESILIENT.
It is an authorisation check: if the assignment source throws, the action fails
rather than proceeding. That is the OPPOSITE of the staff-transition fan-out,
where a notification read was made non-fatal - there the verdict was untouched;
here the check IS the verdict. The three fakes were updated instead, each
returning no rows (= unrestricted) so they keep testing what they were written
for.

THIRTEEN TESTS. Required arms all present: an LV-only actor is refused at CB, an
owner succeeds anywhere (asserted as null scope specifically, not merely
"permits both" - null is what tells callers there is nothing to check, and a
list that happened to contain both would diverge the moment a third clinic
opened), a two-location actor succeeds at both, a therapist IS scoped, and the
predicate has no third answer.
NEGATIVE ARM RUN AND OBSERVED: removing createAppointment's guard reddens the
suite.

NO MIGRATION. staff_locations is 0038 and already carries the data. 0063 UNTOUCHED.

MICROCOPY, delegated on the standing conditions, no commitment language:
  appointment.locationNotAssigned
  pt: "Nao pode marcar nesta localizacao. So pode marcar nas localizacoes que lhe
       estao atribuidas. Se precisar de acesso a outra, contacte a administracao."
  en: "You cannot book at this location. You can only book at the locations
       assigned to you. If you need access to another, contact administration."
Its own error code rather than 'forbidden', for the same reason
illegal_transition has one: "Nao tem permissao para esta acao" would send
reception looking for a missing capability that is not the problem - they HAVE
appointments:write, they simply do not work at that clinic.

CLOSES ON IVAN'S DEPLOYED SCREEN per WF-03, batched into the acceptance sitting:
open Nova marcacao as Carlos and confirm Localizacao offers LV only and is locked.

at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED: the agenda hour row grows to fit the appointments that start inside
it; nothing is clipped.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-13, PER WF-03.
WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
staff-visible fix, which is the class PG1, PG3 and INC-05 closed on. The merged
PR is the build half; the observation is what closes the card.

BUILD: PR #897, merged 2026-08-13, squashed as a4c9a7d.
"feat(agenda): the hour row grows to fit the appointments that start in it".

OBSERVED: the owner confirmed on the deployed build that an hour holding several
appointments now grows to fit them, Fisiozero style, and that the 30-minute slot
grid underneath is unchanged.

THIS WAS THE BUCKET'S RISKIEST ITEM AND IT WAS TIMEBOXED FOR THAT REASON. The
grid is absolutely positioned on a linear scale that SEVEN readers consume: the
gutter hour labels, the 30-minute slot buttons, the blocked bands, the start
groups, the group band cap, the now-line and the day height. Variable hour
heights replaces the coordinate system under every one of them.

IT LANDED ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ON OPTIMISM. The declared stop condition was:
if click targets, blocked bands, now-line and gutter labels are not all provably
intact at the first honest checkpoint, PARK IT. The checkpoint was the existing
suite, and all 26 pre-existing pins in agenda-grid.test.tsx pass unchanged,
including the one that matters most, that the :30 slot is still clickable,
focusable and labelled.

NOTHING WAS EVER HIDDEN, which is worth recording because the report read like a
data-loss report. PL-01 capped each start-group to its hour band and SCROLLED the
overflow deliberately, so no name was truncated. The cost was that a receptionist
had to scroll inside a 96px cell to read one.

cards.notes:
REPORTED FROM RECEPTION. Several appointments in one hour cropped, crowded the
hover target, and off-hour starts sat mid-row.

=== WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, WHICH IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE ===
Nothing was hidden. PL-01 capped each start-group to its hour band and SCROLLED
the overflow, deliberately, so no name was ever truncated. The problem was that
the scale was LINEAR - ((min - start) / 30) * 48 - so an hour was exactly 96px
whether it held one appointment or eight, and a receptionist had to scroll inside
a 96px cell to read a name.

=== THIS WAS THE BUCKET'S RISKIEST ITEM AND IT WAS TIMEBOXED FOR THAT REASON ===
The grid is absolutely positioned on that linear scale, and SEVEN things consume
it: the gutter hour labels, the 30-minute slot buttons, the blocked bands, the
start groups, the group band cap, the now-line, and the day height. Variable hour
heights means replacing the coordinate system every one of those reads.
THE STOP CONDITION WAS: if click targets, blocked bands, now-line and gutter
labels are not all provably intact at the first honest checkpoint, PARK IT.
THE CHECKPOINT WAS THE EXISTING SUITE. All 26 pre-existing pins in
agenda-grid.test.tsx pass unchanged, including the one that matters most - the
:30 slot is still clickable, focusable and labelled. It landed rather than
parked, on evidence rather than on optimism.

=== THE DESIGN ===
minToPx is now CUMULATIVE over per-hour heights instead of linear. An hour is its
96px base, or taller when a day needs the room: lines * 20px + padding.
WITHIN an hour the mapping stays PROPORTIONAL, so a :30 start sits exactly
halfway down its hour however tall that hour is, and 11:25 lands 25/60 of the way
down. That is what keeps vertical position encoding TIME rather than merely
ordering - and 11:25 is a real reachable time, as STAFF-01 established.

HOUR HEIGHTS ARE UNIFORM ACROSS EVERY DAY COLUMN, computed from the BUSIEST day
in view. This is the detail that makes the week view work: per-column heights
would put Monday's 10:00 at a different y than Tuesday's, and the gutter - drawn
ONCE, beside all of them - would agree with neither. Asserted both ways round, so
the function is order-independent.

=== WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE ===
NO COLLAPSE TO HOUR GRANULARITY. daySlots() still yields a slot every 30 minutes,
each is still its own focusable button with its own aria-label and click, and a
slot inside a blocked span is still DISABLED rather than merely covered. A
half-hour slot is now half of its (possibly taller) hour. Collapsing would have
looked like a tidy follow-up and would have SILENTLY HALVED THE BOOKABLE START
TIMES.
The hover card is unchanged. Status iconography and colour semantics are
unchanged. No query, no data change.

=== THE TWO PLACES THIS COULD HAVE GONE WRONG QUIETLY ===
THE GUTTER. If the labels kept the old scale they would drift off their rules the
moment an hour expanded - the clock would LIE rather than merely look untidy.
Same mapper, asserted by the existing hour-rule pins.
THE BLOCKED BANDS. BlockedBand closed over the module-level minToPx; it now takes
the mapper as a prop. A band on the old scale would drift off the slots it covers
- and the band is the VISUAL half of a fact whose ENFORCEMENT half is the
disabled slot underneath. They must agree or the screen says one thing and the
keyboard does another.

SIX NEW TESTS, and the first is the one that matters most: at base heights the
mapper is EXACTLY the old linear scale - 08:00 -> 0, 09:00 -> 96, 09:30 -> 144,
day 1152px. The fix must be inert on a quiet day or it is a redesign dressed as a
bug fix. Then: only the busy hour grows, the worst day wins per hour and the
function is order-independent, a :30 start stays halfway, an off-hour start lands
where the clock says, and the rendered column is genuinely taller end to end.
NEGATIVE ARM RUN: reverting the hour to a fixed height turns two of the six red.

CLOSES ON IVAN'S DEPLOYED SCREEN per WF-03, batched into the acceptance sitting:
open a day with several appointments in one hour and confirm every name is
readable without scrolling inside the cell.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-13, PER WF-03.
WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
staff-visible fix, which is the class PG1, PG3 and INC-05 closed on. The merged
PR is the build half; the observation is what closes the card.

BUILD: PR #898, merged 2026-08-13, squashed as a756928.
"fix(marcacoes): the patient name is never truncated".

OBSERVED: the owner confirmed on the deployed build that the Marcacoes row is now
two lines, identity then attributes, that the full patient name renders, and that
no field was dropped from the row.

'break-words', NOT 'truncate'. The patient span carried 'truncate', which is a
PROMISE THAT SOMETHING WILL BE CUT, and on a crowded single-line row the name is
what lost. A name too long for the line now WRAPS, which is the only behaviour
that guarantees it is fully readable whatever it is.

WHY NOT SIMPLY DROP 'truncate', since that is the one-line change a reader will
ask about: on a single-line row a long name shoves the service, location and
therapist along, every row wraps to a different height, and the list stops being
scannable. The implicit columns were the only thing holding it together. Giving
IDENTITY its own line lets the name be any length without moving anything else.

TIME STAYS ON THE NAME'S LINE. Time and name are what reception scans; splitting
them would have cost more than the change bought.

cards.notes:
REPORTED FROM RECEPTION: the list rendered "Abilio J...".

=== THE CAUSE ===
The row was ONE flex line - time, patient, service, location, therapist,
created-by, conflict, status, hover, Notas, Abrir - and every field competed for
its width. The patient span carried the class 'truncate', which is a PROMISE THAT
SOMETHING WILL BE CUT, and on a crowded row the name is what lost.

=== THE LAYOUT, WHICH WAS DELEGATED, SO HERE IS THE REASONING ===
TWO LINES:
  line 1  IDENTITY   time, estado glyph, recurrence, FULL patient name, hover,
                     conflict marker, status badge, Notas, Abrir
  line 2  ATTRIBUTES service chip, location, therapist, created-by
                     (indented under the time column on wide screens)

WHY NOT SIMPLY DROP 'truncate'. On a single-line row that makes a long name shove
the service, location and therapist along, so every row wraps to a different
height and the list stops being scannable - the implicit columns were the only
thing holding it together. Giving IDENTITY its own line means the name can be any
length without moving anything else.

'break-words', NOT 'truncate'. A name too long for the line WRAPS rather than
being cut, which is the only behaviour that guarantees it is fully readable
whatever it is.

TIME STAYS ON THE NAME'S LINE. Time and name are what reception scans; splitting
them would have cost more than the change bought. Asserted.

NOTHING WAS DROPPED, which the dispatch required explicitly. Every field is still
on the row. The four that moved to line 2 were ALREADY secondary - they were
already rendered at text-xs in text-v2-text-secondary - so the visual hierarchy
did not change, it was made explicit.

NO QUERY, NO DATA CHANGE. Layout only.

=== NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH THE AGENDA GRID ===
agenda-grid.tsx has shortPatientName, which keeps first + last and DROPS THE
MIDDLE NAMES on the grid face, with the full name preserved in the hover. That is
DELIBERATE and tested (W11-00 v3) - the grid face is a dense column where a full
name cannot fit at all. THIS CARD IS THE LIST, a different surface with a full
row to spend. The two were not conflated and the grid was not touched.

THREE TESTS: the name renders in full AND the element carries no 'truncate' (a
text-only assertion would pass on a name that happens to fit while the defect
stayed); no field was dropped, asserted field by field rather than by count so a
future removal is NAMED; and the time is still on the first line.
NEGATIVE ARM RUN: putting 'truncate' back turns the first one red.

open Marcacoes and confirm a long patient name reads in full.

cards.title: FIXED: /horarios rendered a black "Application error" page for a located receptionist, in front of the clinic team. The roster KEEPS a therapist with no clinic assigned and the schedule gate REFUSES that same therapist, so one unassigned colleague took the whole page down. Equipa had it too, for a located admin

evidence.ref:
WF-03 ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-17,
at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the
patient OTP login screens - the checklist was not to hand and it stays OPEN).

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED: /horarios renders for a located viewer. The black "Application error"
page is gone.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 213 files / 2059 passed, build 4/4.

TWO PINS, AND THEY PIN DIFFERENT THINGS.
  apps/web/app/horarios/horarios-roster-scope.test.ts - 6 tests, FOUR of them
    negative arms. Pins the data-layer property: building a LIST must yield a
    per-member answer, so no member can lose every other member.
  apps/web/e2e/horarios-renders-per-role.spec.ts - loads /horarios as admin,
    reception, therapist AND owner. Fails on the BROWSER-level symptom (the
    Next.js fallback text plus any uncaught pageerror), which is the only place
    a post-flush server throw is observable at all. A unit test cannot see it:
    the response is a 200 and the page dies afterwards.

ROOT CAUSE - TWO PREDICATES THAT DISAGREE ON EXACTLY ONE CASE:
  filterRosterByViewerScope (scheduling/therapist-location-filter.ts:74) KEEPS a
    therapist with NO location assignment. Deliberate: "dropping them would
    silently hide a real colleague behind a data-entry gap rather than isolate
    anything."
  assertTargetInScheduleScope (admin/schedule-scope.ts:56) THROWS not_found on
    that same therapist. Also deliberate: a located actor manages only their own
    location's staff.
Both are right alone. horarios/page.tsx:70-76 and admin/staff/page.tsx:113-120
ran them in SERIES - render the roster, then assert once per member inside a
Promise.all - so one refusal rejected the whole batch, the server component threw
after the shell had flushed, and the browser painted "Application error: a
client-side exception has occurred".

ROLE-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT REACHED THE PRESENTATION.
viewerLocationScope returns null for owner, therapist and unassigned staff, so
ONLY a located reception/admin ever reached the gate. Every account this was
demoed with was unscoped.

THE FIX IS A SHAPE CHANGE, NOT A WEAKENING. A throw is the right shape for a
single target - a write must refuse - and the wrong shape for building a list.

ONE query. listTimeOffBlocksForRoster() returns a discriminated
{manageable:true,blocks} | {manageable:false}, so "no absences" and "not yours to
manage" CANNOT collapse into each other. assertTargetInScheduleScope is UNCHANGED
and still runs on every time-off read and write; a negative arm proves it still
refuses the same member.

identically for a LOCATED ADMIN. Found by asking who else calls the same loader.

showHours - showHours says the member HAS no schedule, scheduleManageable says
the VIEWER cannot see it, and collapsing them would tell an admin a therapist has
no working hours when the truth is they cannot be seen from here.

N+1 REMOVED AS A SIDE EFFECT: one query per therapist became two for the whole

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a

OBSERVED: "Ver marcacao" in Notificacoes opens the appointment it names.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 215 files passed, build 4/4.
Pins: lib/scheduling/deep-link-window.test.ts (9 tests, including an invariant
asserted over every case) and 6 new render tests in
app/marcacoes/marcacoes-view.test.tsx.

RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE, BEFORE THE LIST QUERY, for two reasons that both matter.
The appointment may fall outside the default week, so ITS date is what decides
the range; and getAppointment is tenant- and RLS-scoped, so an id the viewer may
not see returns null on the server instead of being probed for on the client.

THE WINDOW ARITHMETIC IS A PURE FUNCTION WITH ITS OWN SUITE, and it was split out
because every wrong answer here FAILS SILENTLY: the page renders a perfectly
normal list that simply does not contain the row the notification promised, and
reception reads that as "the appointment is gone". Three interacting rules -
widen to reach the target, never narrow the range the user asked for, never
exceed the 92-day ceiling - with an invariant test asserting over every case that
a resolved target is inside the returned window.

THE CEILING CASE IS THE ONE WORTH READING. A link eight months out, clamped
forward from `from`, returns a valid-looking window that PROVABLY CANNOT contain
the target. It anchors on the target's own day instead.

FOUR STATES, KEPT DISTINCT: no link followed; link resolved and row present
(drawer opens, row highlighted and scrolled to); link resolved but row filtered
out by a client-side filter (drawer STILL opens - it is what the notification
promised and does not depend on the row being on screen - only the scroll is
skipped); link resolved to nothing (a plain pt-PT line, with the list still
rendered underneath).

TWO REAL BUGS CAUGHT BY THE TESTS RATHER THAN BY REVIEW:
  1. GlassCard destructures a fixed prop list and SILENTLY DROPS unknown props,
     so data-appointment-id on it would have reached neither the DOM nor the
     querySelector looking for it. The scroll would have silently never worked.
     The anchor moved to a plain wrapper.
  2. The first implementation used an effect plus a "handled" latch. Lint
     rejected the synchronous setState, correctly: deriving the initial modal
     state in the useState initialiser needs no latch, no effect, and cannot
     re-open a drawer the user just closed.

THE AGENDA-HIGHLIGHT VERSION WAS NOT BUILT, per the dispatch. What it would
additionally take is in the report and on this card's notes.

cards.title: A therapist can now block their OWN schedule, and only their own. The restriction is a SCOPE, not a capability: the server refuses a block whose target is not the acting therapist, and the Terapeuta selector is pinned to them

evidence.ref:
WF-03 ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-17,
at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the
patient OTP login screens - the checklist was not to hand and it stays OPEN).

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED: THERAPIST SELF-SCOPE on the deployed build. A therapist blocks their
own schedule and only their own; the Terapeuta control shows their own name as
text rather than a selector.

THIS IS THE ONE WHERE THE SCREEN COULD NOT HAVE BEEN THE PROOF ON ITS OWN, and
the card says why: the dangerous half was never the grant, it was
resolveScheduleScope returning null - "unrestricted" - for three different
reasons at once. The screen confirms the scope reaches the user correctly; the
server refusal is what the discriminated union and its 11 tests pin.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 215 files passed, build 4/4.
Pins: lib/admin/therapist-self-schedule.test.ts (11 tests, 5 negative arms) and the
rewritten e2e/horarios.spec.ts therapist arm.

THE DANGEROUS HALF WAS NOT THE GRANT. `resolveScheduleScope` returned `null` -
"unrestricted" - for the owner, an unassigned staffer AND a therapist alike,
because a therapist held no schedule capability so the value was never reachable
for them. THREE DIFFERENT REASONS COLLAPSED ONTO ONE VALUE. Granting
schedule:manage under that shape would have handed every therapist the entire
clinic's schedule, with no line of code looking wrong anywhere.

SO THE SCOPE BECAME A DISCRIMINATED UNION: {kind:"all"} | {kind:"locations"} |
{kind:"self"}. TypeScript then named every site that had to change - nine of them
across availability.ts and time-off.ts - instead of leaving them to be
remembered. A caller can no longer express the rule incorrectly; it can only fail
to call the assert at all, which is a visible omission rather than a subtly wrong
predicate. Same argument migration 0059 made for is_unconfirmed_pedido.

THE REFUSAL IS IDENTITY, NOT A QUERY: the self branch needs no database round
trip, and a test feeds it a permissive tx that would answer "yes" to anything, so
a permissive database cannot buy a therapist a colleague's schedule.

`forbidden`, NOT `not_found`. The location branch uses not_found deliberately, so
a located receptionist never learns another clinic's roster exists. A therapist
already knows their colleagues exist, so concealment would buy nothing and cost
them a comprehensible message. A new AdminErrorCode rather than a reused one.

UI LOCK IS A COURTESY, NOT THE ENFORCEMENT. The Terapeuta control renders as TEXT
rather than a disabled <select>: a disabled control reads as "a choice you cannot
make right now", and for a therapist there is no choice to make. INC-08 is the
precedent for why the server refusal is the deliverable.

THREE EXISTING TESTS ASSERTED THE OLD RULE AND WERE CHANGED DELIBERATELY, each
with the reason written at the assertion: permission-matrix (therapist now holds
schedule:manage, and the guard was re-pointed at what the grant must NOT have
carried), block-capability (the agenda control is now SHOWN - that is the
feature), and time-off-batch. THE LAST ONE IS THE INTERESTING ONE: it asserted a
therapist is refused by assertCan, which is no longer true and CANNOT BE MADE
TRUE BY ANY ROLE - owner, admin, reception and therapist all hold schedule:manage
now, so the capability gate is vacuous at the role level. It was rewritten to
prove the batch write goes through the TARGET assert with the requested target
and inserts nothing on refusal.

NAV DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: see LE-therapist-horarios-nav.

cards.notes:

cards.title: Therapists whose pattern is not weekly can now be scheduled up to 3 months ahead. JP alternates Castelo Branco and Linda-a-Velha week by week. NO MIGRATION: valid_from/valid_until already existed and every consumer already honoured them

evidence.ref:
WF-03 ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-17,
at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the
patient OTP login screens - the checklist was not to hand and it stays OPEN).

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED: an alternating-week pattern saved clean and the screen answered
"Semanas alternadas definidas." The CB/LV flip was then verified ACROSS THE WEEK
BOUNDARY - the day the pattern changes clinic - in BOTH consumers: the staff
agenda and the portal slot engine. That pairing is the acceptance that mattered.
The card's own build note says the two consumers read the dated rows through
different code (day-availability-core.ts isWithinValidity, and store.ts's SQL
predicate), and a vitest suite importing buildDay says nothing about a SQL
predicate. Only the deployed screens show both agreeing on the same week.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 216 files passed, build 4/4.

THE FINDING THAT DECIDED THE DESIGN, RE-DERIVED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN
ASSUMED: availability_templates ALREADY carries valid_from / valid_until, and
EVERY consumer already honours them. Verified at both, in both languages:
  day-availability-core.ts:83   isWithinValidity  (staff availability)
  store.ts:211-212              SQL predicate     (the portal booking guard)
So layer 2 is layer-1 rows carrying dates. No migration, no consumer change,
0063 stays frozen for ITEM 6.

WRITE-TIME INVARIANT, NOT READ-TIME PRECEDENCE, per the ruling. Read-time
"most specific wins" would have put the rule in FOUR places, two of them SQL -
the drift that produced the S1 incident and forced 0059 to collapse three copies
of a predicate into one function. The writer instead emits rows that CANNOT
double-cover, so the union every consumer already computes is automatically
correct and there is nothing to disambiguate.

THE INVARIANT IS NOT "AT MOST ONE ROW", and getting that wrong would have
deleted W13-A: two rows per (user, weekday) at the SAME location is a legal
split shift. The rule is: for any (weekday, date) covered more than once, all
covering rows must share a location AND not overlap in time.

ONE ROW PER (WEEKDAY, DATE), validFrom === validUntil === the date. Two offset
series cannot produce the same day, so the invariant holds by construction. A
row per WEEK would have been fewer rows and would have needed boundary
arithmetic to be right; a row per day needs nothing to be right.

LAYER 1 IS CARVED, NEVER DELETED (Q-W5-4): the weekly row is bounded to the day
before the pattern and an identical row RESUMES the day after, so the therapist
is not left without a schedule once the horizon ends. Both directions pinned.

generateLoteSchedule REUSED VERBATIM, called twice with a one-week offset. That
is the whole of the alternation, and it means "every 2 weeks" has one definition
across Agendar lote, Bloquear lote and this.

=== THE TWO DoD TESTS THE RULING NAMED ===
1. NO-DOUBLE-COVERAGE INVARIANT - apps/web/lib/scheduling/alternating-weeks.test.ts,
   13 tests. Includes a COUNTERWEIGHT that removes the carve and asserts the
   checker goes red with BOTH violation kinds, so an empty result can never be
   confused with a checker that returns nothing.
2. CB ONE WEEK, LV THE NEXT, AT EVERY CONSUMER. Asserted through buildDay - the
   REAL staff engine - not through the planner's own output, which would only
   prove the planner agrees with itself. Strongest arm walks EVERY working day
   of the 13-week horizon and requires exactly one clinic on each, with a
   checked-count assertion (65) so a vacuous pass is impossible.
   THE SQL CONSUMER IS A SEPARATE FILE AGAINST A LIVE DATABASE:
   packages/db/tests/alternating-weeks-portal.db.test.ts, 8 assertions, because
   a vitest suite importing buildDay says NOTHING about a SQL predicate. It runs
   the real store.ts shape and includes a negative control that the fixture
   seeded, a Monday outside the pattern refused at both clinics, and a
   wrong-time-of-day refusal so the predicate cannot be answering on date alone.

ADVISORY, NEVER DESTRUCTIVE: appointments inside the window are REPORTED after
the save (PL-11 + Q-W5-4), listed on screen rather than toasted, because a toast
disappears and these are appointments somebody must move.

AWAITING WF-03: Ivan's deployed-screen acceptance before this card closes.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-14. Migration 0063 authorized by strategy for guest_booking_requests
ONLY. PR #907, all checks green on its own sha, held at the apply gate.

SCOPE OF THAT PR, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD: the TABLE ONLY. The guest flow -
public route, rate limiting, the 5-step form, the reception queue - is NOT built
and is the next commit. The migration was opened first because apply-before-merge
gates everything downstream anyway.

WHY A NEW TABLE AND NOT A PROVISIONAL PATIENT ROW. appointments.patient_id and
staff_notifications.patient_id are both NOT NULL, so the existing pedido path
cannot represent someone who does not exist yet without inventing them. Doing so
would (a) write a CLINICAL record from an anonymous HTTP request and (b) be
auto-linking under another name, which R-GUEST forbids - creating a new patient
for someone who may BE an existing patient is the same mistake with a duplicate
attached.

NO ANON RLS POLICY, IN EITHER DIRECTION. The insert runs from apps/api under the
SERVICE ROLE, the seam the durable rate-limit store already uses (0056). An anon
INSERT policy would have left a writable, internet-reachable policy on a tenant
table permanently, guarded only by whatever WITH CHECK survives future edits.
NO DELETE POLICY either: a declined request is a STATUS, not a deletion.
Rule 3 binds the caller - tenant_id is NOT NULL so a service-role insert that
forgets it fails loudly.

JOURNAL RECONCILED: "63 .sql files match 63 journal entries in order, when
strictly increasing, and the supabase mirror matches by CONTENT." Number derived
at authoring (main ended at 0062), when = 1787100000000 on the SYNTHETIC series,
never Date.now() - INC-07 was a Date.now() value landing below its predecessor.

APPLY BLOCK DRAFTED under the standing doctrine, opening NOT VALIDATED, sent to
strategy and NOT to Ivan. Pre-check must read pending: 1, post-check pending: 0,
plus check-migration-tables.mjs guest_booking_requests as the receipt - valid
here because the table is genuinely new, unlike 0059 where the object already
existed and existence proved nothing.

- public route, rate limiting, the form, the reception queue - is NOT built") is

that already existed, with no migration.

evidence flagged - "the APPLY is not committed anywhere ... 0063 HAS NONE" - is

cards.title: GATE CLOSED: guest and patient phone normalisation are proven to agree, against a live database. The copy in 0063 is now safe, and the possible-existing-patient flag is proven to actually match

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. packages/db/tests/guest-phone-parity.db.test.ts, 5 assertions,
DB-gated so it runs against a live migrated database in the DB Tests job.

WHY THIS WAS HELD AS A SHIPPING GATE AND NOT LOGGED AS A NICETY. Reception's
"this may be somebody you already have" flag is a JOIN between
guest_booking_requests.phone_e164 and patients.phone_e164. If the two expressions
ever normalise differently the join returns NOTHING - and NOTHING IS THE BENIGN
ANSWER. No error, no log, no screen reporting anything odd: a returning patient
is silently treated as new and the clinic acquires a duplicate record for
somebody it already knows. Vacuous guard, on a verdict path, exactly the family
rehydrate section 1.3 is about.

THE CORPUS IS DELIBERATELY THE SAME SHAPE AS ITS SIBLING
(apps/api/lib/auth/phone-e164-parity.db.test.ts), including the traps that file
found worth pinning: the over-long number, the NON-BREAKING SPACE, the geographic
prefix, the foreign number. A parity test with an EASIER corpus than its sibling
would pass while the sibling failed, which is worse than having no test at all.

FIVE ASSERTIONS, AND THREE OF THEM ARE COUNTERWEIGHTS:
  1. the corpus covers BOTH outcomes - without this, uniformly-NULL columns
     would pass every parity check
  2. every input derives the same value in BOTH tables, read back from the
     database rather than computed in JavaScript or asserted from a migration's
     text
  3. THE FLAG ITSELF MATCHES: a patient stored "+351 912 000 111" and a guest who
     typed "912000111" join. Parity is the mechanism; this is the outcome it
     exists for
  4. NEGATIVE: a guest matching nobody is not flagged - a join that matched
     everything would pass (3) and be worse than useless
  5. NEGATIVE: two NULL normalisations do not match each other. NULL = NULL is
     not true in SQL, and without this every guest who typed a foreign number
     would match every patient who did

STILL THE RIGHT END STATE: one SQL function used by both columns. Not built,
because it means rewriting a generated column on 'patients', a table holding live
clinical data - its own migration with its own apply. Until then THIS TEST IS
WHAT MAKES THE COPY SAFE, which is why it gates the flow rather than following
it.

cards.notes:
RAISED BY GUEST-01 2026-08-14, DELIBERATELY AND NOT DISCOVERED LATER.

guest_booking_requests.phone_e164 carries patients.phone_e164's GENERATED ALWAYS
expression VERBATIM. That is what reception's possible-existing-patient flag
matches on: guest.phone_e164 = patients.phone_e164.

WHY THE DUPLICATION IS DANGEROUS IN THIS PARTICULAR PLACE. If the two ever
normalise differently, the flag silently stops matching - and A MISS LOOKS
EXACTLY LIKE A GENUINE NO-MATCH. Nothing errors, no screen reports anything odd,
and the outcome is a guest being treated as a new person when they are an
existing patient. That is the vacuous-guard shape this project has counted 123
instances of, sitting on a verdict path.

WHAT IS REQUIRED BEFORE THE GUEST FLOW SHIPS: a DB-gated parity test running one
corpus through BOTH generated columns and requiring identical answers, modelled
on phone-e164-parity.db.test.ts which already does this for SQL-vs-JS. Hard-
required in the skip guard, not optional.

THE RIGHT END STATE IS ONE SQL FUNCTION used by both columns, and it was NOT
built in 0063 for two stated reasons: 0063 is authorized for the new table only,
and rewriting patients.phone_e164 is a generated-column rewrite on a table
holding live clinical data. That is a separate migration with its own apply, and
inventing it inside an authorized-for-one-table migration would have been exactly
the scope creep the migration doctrine exists to prevent.

cards.title: Reception can SEE guest booking requests, each marked new client or possible existing patient. Its own section, separate from the pedido queue, because confirming one CREATES a patient and an appointment rather than changing a state

evidence.ref:
WF-03 ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER ON THE DEPLOYED PRODUCTION BUILD, 2026-08-17,
at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the
patient OTP login screens - the checklist was not to hand and it stays OPEN).

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED: a guest request rendered in reception's queue carrying
"Preferencia: 21/08/2026, tarde", with the "Novo cliente" mark on the row.

BOTH HALVES ARE THE ACCEPTANCE, not one. The MARK is what the ruling required -
a guest is visibly not an ordinary appointment. The LABEL is GUEST-04's honest
window format: "Preferencia", never "Data", and a PERIOD rather than an invented
time. An earlier build rendered "20/08/2026, 09:00" for somebody who had only
ever said "manha", which reads as a chosen slot in the place a chosen slot
appears. The deployed row now says what the person actually asked for.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test suite green, build 4/4.
6 render assertions in app/notificacoes/guest-requests-queue.test.tsx.

A SEPARATE SECTION, NOT A SECOND KIND OF ROW IN THE PEDIDO QUEUE. A pedido is an
existing patient's appointment changing state; the row already exists and
confirming it is an UPDATE. A guest request has no patient, no appointment and no
notification behind it, and confirming one CREATES both. One list would have put
two different actions behind one word.

THE FLAG IS A COUNT AND NEVER A LINK, on 0062's precedent:
resolvePatientByProvenPhone REFUSES when several patients share a number rather
than picking one, because mis-linking a medical record is the worst outcome
available. Zero matches renders "Novo cliente"; one renders "Podera ja ser
paciente"; several says so explicitly, because picking is not obvious. Exactly
ONE mark per row, asserted - rendering both would leave reception to work out
which applies, rendering neither reads as an ordinary appointment.

THE MATCH IS COUNTED IN THE SAME QUERY as a correlated subquery, so the flag and
the row come from ONE snapshot. Two round trips could report a match for a
patient created between them, or miss one deleted between them.

LOCATION-SCOPED like every other reception read (PL-09), via inArray rather than
a hand-built IN list - these ids come from the database so interpolating them is
not exploitable today, but a parameterised predicate cannot BECOME exploitable
when somebody later feeds this function a request value.

A REAL BUG CAUGHT BY THE TEST, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY: the row's
data-testid was on GlassCard, which destructures a fixed prop list and SILENTLY
DROPS anything else - so it reached neither the DOM nor the querySelector looking
for it. Identical to the Marcacoes row defect in STAFF-07. Moved to the <li> and
the reason is now written at the call site so a third occurrence does not need a
test to find it.

DEFERRED, NOT FORGOTTEN: the CONVERT action. The queue displays only, because
building interactivity before the action exists is scaffolding with nothing
behind it. Nothing can create a row yet either - the public form is not built -
so there is no live gap.

AWAITING WF-03, batched into the next acceptance sitting per WF-16.

evidence.ref:

at origin/main 464435b, in the batched acceptance sitting WF-16 requires.

THE SITTING, AS A NUMBER: 15 checks, 14 PASS, 0 STOP, 1 SKIPPED (W13-03, the
patient OTP login screens - the checklist was not to hand and it stays OPEN).

WF-03 makes the owner's observation on a deployed screen the evidence for a
patient- or staff-visible loop, and the merged PR is only the build half. What
follows is the observation; the build evidence this card already carried is
preserved verbatim below it.

OBSERVED: the public form at /marcacao submits, and what it produced downstream
carried the correct honest window format - a date and a period, never a time the
form never offered. Option A on the deployed build: no availability shown, no
slot implied.

=== BUILD EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM ===
SHIPPED 2026-08-14. Gates from the repo root: lint 0 errors (13 pre-existing
warnings, none new), typecheck 11/11, test 2120 passed / 20 skipped, build 4/4.
131 assertions added across six suites.

WHAT THE RULING CHANGED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE SHAPE. The halt this dispatch
answered was that all three reads the form needed - catalog, therapists, slots -
are authenticated and 401 for a guest. Option A exposes ONE of them and drops the
other two from the product, so the form collects a PREFERENCE and reception
resolves the slot at confirm (R-GUEST-1).

  - ONE new unauthenticated read: GET /api/v1/booking/guest/catalog. id + name
    for services and locations, nothing else - no price, no duration, no internal
    flag - behind the same four predicates as the authenticated catalog
    (tenant, active, not internal_only, patient_bookable). Rate limited per IP on
    the durable store, 30/min and 200/hour. NO GLOBAL CEILING, deliberately: a
    ceiling on a read of published data protects nothing and hands one attacker a
    switch that takes the public form off the air. RULES.guestCatalogIp carries
    the argument, and a test asserts no global key is ever spent.
  - MN-27 and MN-28 added to the exposure matrix: booking/therapists and
    booking/slots STAY AUTHENTICATED, by ruling. Enforced by their absence from
    PRE_AUTH in patient-surface.test.ts, which is the repo-wide scan - so exposing
    either means editing an allowlist entry with a name on it.
  - THE WRITE ENDPOINT NO LONGER ACCEPTS A SLOT. startsAt/endsAt are refused;
    preferredDate + preferredPeriod are required. practitionerId is refused and
    written NULL. An exact timestamp from a public form would be UNSOURCED -
    nothing public could have offered it - and reception would read it as a time
    the person was shown.
  - NO MIGRATION. 0063's timestamptz pair is reinterpreted at the write layer by
    encodeGuestPreferredWindow (@osteojp/db), Lisbon wall clock, manhã 09-13 and
    tarde 13-19 from the clinic's published hours. 0064 was not needed and was
    not authored.

THE READ SIDE WAS WRONG UNTIL THIS COMMIT AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE REPORTED IT.
Reception's queue rendered stamp(requestedStartsAt) - "20/08/2026 09:00" - in the
same format the pedido queue uses for a real appointment. Under Option A that is
a false statement about a clinical event: reception would ring somebody to
confirm nine o'clock when they only ever said "manhã". Now decoded through a
DISCRIMINATED UNION and labelled "Preferência"; a window that encodes no period
renders as the timestamp it is rather than being absorbed into a period nobody
stated (PORTAL-REHYDRATE §1.3).

A REAL DEFECT THE NEW TESTS CAUGHT, in the catalog route: the location list was
passed straight through from the SELECT instead of being mapped, so the
projection depended entirely on the select clause. Adding a column for a future
feature would have shipped it to the internet with no line in the diff looking
wrong. Mapped explicitly, both key sets pinned.

A SECOND ONE THE BUILD CAUGHT: /marcacao prerendered as ○ STATIC, which would
have baked a build-time "could not load the services" screen into the deployed
artefact. Typecheck and the unit suites were green through it; only
the next-build route table showed it. Now force-dynamic.

FORM: four steps (clinic, service, when, details), one <form>, one server action,
every prior answer carried as hidden fields so it works without JavaScript and
the server validates each step. Six fields and no more, asserted as a closed set.
No NIF (PL-20), nothing clinical. RGPD verbatim from clinical.consent.rgpd.label
and .body - resolved on the server, never copied into the screen, with a test
that fails if anybody pastes the paragraph in. The acknowledgement is required in
the markup AND checked on the server, because an attribute is a hint to a
browser.

THE CONFIRMATION IS A STATE, NOT A URL. SEC-pending-screen-asserts-nothing one
flow over: there is no address anybody can visit to be told their request
arrived. A guest has no id to verify against, and giving them one would put a
lookup surface on a public form.

THE LINK EXISTS AND IS NOT PUBLISHED. /marcacao is reachable so the owner can
walk it for WF-03; nothing links to it. It does not go public until JP's
confirmation copy lands (GUEST-05) and WF-03 passes.

ONE MESSAGE INSTEAD OF TWO, AND IT IS NOT A LOSS. The copies ended differently ("the patient login" / "the guest booking form"), and that clause is ALREADY in the log: both callers funnel the throw through their own logUnavailable, which prefixes [auth] otp/request or [guest] submit. The surface is recorded by the thing whose job that is; the message says the part only it can say, which is WHICH VARIABLE IS MISSING.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THE MERGE COULD HAVE COST ARE PINNED, two of them invisible in a diff and both failing in the direction that looks fine - apps/portal/lib/tenant.test.ts:
  CALL-TIME, NOT MODULE SCOPE. The suite imports the module with the variable DELETED and nothing throws; reading it then does. That is the property protecting `next build`, which imports modules to collect page data (the W13-03a defect). "Simplify to a constant" is the obvious tidy-up and it is the bug.
  NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES (rule 7): the message contains PORTAL_TENANT_ID and not the value.
  IT THROWS AT ALL, including on a set-but-EMPTY string - the state a `value !== undefined` check would pass and which would send an empty tenant to the API, rendering a misconfiguration as a service outage.
Plus the source guard the card is actually about: exactly one file reads the variable, and the other two import it. Two copies is the number at which a third gets written without anybody noticing; this is what notices.

a boot).

patient-facing path, and the rate-limiter extraction established that a
gate-bearing path is not touched to save an import line. Consolidating would have
put a PG1 file in a commit about a public form.

written without anybody noticing, and the failure mode is not cosmetic: one

cards.title: A convert that is abandoned before the booking leaves a patient with no appointment and no queue row chasing it
cards.notes:
OPENED BY GUEST-06, WHICH CREATED IT KNOWINGLY. Stated on the card rather than
discovered later.

THE SEQUENCE: reception presses convert, the patient is created and the request
moves to confirmed and leaves the queue, the agenda opens prefilled - and then
the phone rings and the drawer is closed. The person now exists as a patient with
no appointment, and nothing is tracking that they asked for one.

WHY IT WAS BUILT THIS WAY. The alternative is to hold the request pending until
an appointment exists, which means threading the request id through the whole
staff booking path so createAppointment can close it. That is a change to the one
code path every appointment in the product goes through, to serve a case that has
a manual recovery.

THE RECOVERY THAT EXISTS TODAY: the patient row is created, audited, and findable
in Pacientes, and "Nova marcacao" from their profile (W6-03) resumes exactly the
flow that was abandoned. Nothing is lost. Nothing chases it either.

RECOMMENDED FIX, when it is worth doing: do not move the status on convert. Move
it when converted_appointment_id is written, and have the queue show a converted-
but-unbooked request in a distinct state rather than removing it. That keeps
0063's two columns meaning what they say and needs no migration.

cards.title: guest_booking_requests has NO GRANT to authenticated - the only table in the migration set without one, and reception's guest queue reads as that role

evidence.ref:

osteojp-prod-apply worktree at 69770f5:

VERDICT: fine. The script's own three-way verdict, not an interpretation of it.

WHAT THE OUTPUT SHOWED, recorded in full because the surprise is in the detail:
  public.guest_booking_requests   RLS enabled: true
  authenticated: SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE
  service_role:  all privileges
  control table public.staff_notifications: 0055's explicit grants present

SO PRODUCTION HAS MORE THAN THE MIGRATION EVER GRANTED, not less. The table
picked up Supabase's DEFAULT PRIVILEGES at creation time, which is why
/notificacoes has worked since 0063 was applied on 2026-08-15 and why the owner
saw a guest request rendered in that queue on 2026-08-17.

THE INCIDENT HYPOTHESIS IS DEAD. Reception's queue was never down, not for a
minute, and the "broken" arm of this card's own verdict table never applied.

WHAT REMAINS IS A CI-AND-REPRODUCIBILITY DEFECT, which is a real defect and is
carded as GUEST-07-migration-0065-guest-acl: the committed migration set does
not reproduce production. A fresh database built from packages/db/migrations
gets a table authenticated cannot read, which is exactly what CI proved on #917.

=== CI EVIDENCE, PRESERVED VERBATIM FROM WHEN THIS WAS OPENED ===
FOUND 2026-08-17 by the DB-gated check on PR #917, which is the first time
CI has ever executed a real query against this table - every prior suite mocked
the database, so nothing could have caught it before.

  PostgresError: permission denied for table guest_booking_requests
  code 42501, at lib/scheduling/guest-convert.ts:170

SWEPT, NOT ASSUMED. Every CREATE TABLE in packages/db/migrations after 0003 was
checked for a GRANT in its own migration. guest_booking_requests (0063) is the
ONLY one without. 0055 grants SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE, 0056 and 0058 likewise, and
0055's comment states the rule: these tables do NOT inherit 0003's blanket grant.

cards.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-17 AS A CI-AND-REPRODUCIBILITY DEFECT, NOT AN INCIDENT. The
owner's production read settled it; the verdict and the full grant list are on
this card's evidence.

=== THE NEW FINDING, WHICH THE SAME OUTPUT PRODUCED AND NOBODY WAS LOOKING FOR ===
authenticated is OVER-PRIVILEGED on guest_booking_requests. It holds DELETE,
INSERT, REFERENCES, TRIGGER and TRUNCATE in addition to the SELECT and UPDATE the
feature needs. Nothing granted those deliberately - Supabase's default privileges
did, at CREATE TABLE time.

NOT AN INCIDENT EITHER, AND THE REASON MATTERS. RLS is enabled on the table and
it is the live guard: a privilege with no policy behind it grants no row. So the
exposure is bounded by 0063's policies, not by this ACL.

IT STILL GETS FIXED, because the committed migration and production should say
the same thing, and because a future policy change would be reasoned about
against an ACL nobody chose. That is GUEST-07-migration-0065-guest-acl, whose
scope was AMENDED by this finding from "add the missing grants" to "normalise the
ACL": grant SELECT and UPDATE, revoke the other five.

APPENDED TO END-legal-sweep FOR THE CYBERSECURITY REP: Supabase default
privileges grant broadly at table creation, tenant-wide, and that configuration
should be reviewed rather than worked around one table at a time.

=== THE DEPARTED-COLLABORATOR EVENT, recorded here so the next reader meets it ===
The sm33xy auto-update-branch activity on #917 is explained and closed. Full
record on GUEST-06-queue-convert-action, which is where a reader asking "why is
#917 a draft" will look. Access has been removed by the owner; the wider vendor
sweep is appended to END-legal-sweep.

--- the card as it stood while open, unedited below ---

TWO THINGS ARE TRUE AND ONLY ONE IS CERTAIN.

CERTAIN: the committed migration set is wrong, CI proves it, and GUEST-06 cannot
work without a GRANT. That is a one-line migration and it is HELD - 0064 is in
flight on the consultation PR and rule 8 allows one repo-wide.

UNRESOLVED: whether PRODUCTION is affected. withTenantContext sets role
authenticated, so if prod's ACL matches the migration, /notificacoes throws for
every staff member and has since 0063 was applied on 2026-08-15. The owner
observed that queue WORKING on 2026-08-17. Both cannot be true.

DO NOT RESOLVE THIS BY REASONING. Run the committed read-only script:
  set -a; . ~/osteojp-secrets/new-prod.env; set +a
  node packages/db/scripts/check-guest-requests-grant.mjs
It prints one of three verdicts: fine / partial (SELECT but no UPDATE) / broken.

WHAT THE ANSWER CHANGES:
  - "fine"    -> this is a CI-and-correctness defect. The GRANT migration is
                 still required so the schema is reproducible, but nothing is
                 burning and it can wait for 0064 to clear.
  - "partial" -> the queue works, the convert would fail at the update. Same
                 migration, still not an incident.
  - "broken"  -> reception's notifications page is down and has been for two
                 days. That is a production incident and it outranks everything
                 else on this board.

THE MIGRATION, WHEN AUTHORIZED, IS:
  GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON public.guest_booking_requests TO authenticated;
SELECT for the queue read, UPDATE for the convert marking a request handled.
NOT INSERT: the public form writes under the service role by 0063's deliberate
design, and granting authenticated an INSERT would create a second write path
into a table whose whole point is that only one exists. NOT DELETE.
The number is taken at BUILD time from whatever is free, never reserved here.

  schedule.searchLabel        "Procurar terapeuta pelo nome"
  schedule.searchNoMatch      "Nenhum terapeuta corresponde a esta procura."
(EN counterparts in the same commit.)

THE LABEL AND THE PLACEHOLDER SAY DIFFERENT THINGS ON PURPOSE. The placeholder is
short because it sits inside the field and disappears the moment somebody types.
The aria-label is the fuller sentence, because a screen reader user gets it
INSTEAD of the visual context rather than alongside it.

THE COUNT IS ALWAYS RENDERED, not only while filtering - "7" unfiltered, "2/7"
filtered. A number that appears and disappears is a second thing to notice; one
that is always there is read once and then trusted.

cards.notes:
UNBLOCKED AND AUTHORED 2026-08-18. The 0064 slot cleared when the owner applied
that migration and #916 merged as 267fce9, so rule 8 no longer holds this back.

=== THE PRE-AUTHORING VERIFICATION Q7 REQUIRED, DONE BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN ===
The ruling said: confirm by code read that no authenticated path relies on any
privilege being revoked, and HALT if one does. Every reference to the table in
the repository was enumerated and classified:

  apps/web/lib/scheduling/guest-requests.ts   authenticated (runScoped)  SELECT x2
  guest-convert.ts on #917 (unmerged)         authenticated (runScoped)  UPDATE x1
  apps/api/.../booking/guest/route.ts         SERVICE ROLE               INSERT x1
  packages/db/tests/guest-phone-parity.db     privileged connection      DELETE (teardown)
  portal/proxy.ts, portal/lib/guest/api.ts,
  packages/db/src/guest-preferred-window.ts   comments only, no operation

THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE BEEN A HALT WAS THE TEST TEARDOWN, and it is not one:
rls-harness connect() returns a raw client on the privileged URL and that suite
never enters the role helper, so its DELETE does not run as authenticated.
Checked rather than assumed, because "nothing uses it" is the claim the whole
migration rests on.

The service-role INSERT was confirmed the same way: the guest route uses the base
client and calls withTenantContext ZERO times. That is what makes revoking INSERT
from authenticated safe rather than merely plausible.

NO FK POINTS AT THE TABLE, so REFERENCES grants a capability nobody asked for,
and nothing creates triggers at runtime.

=== WHAT 0065 IS ===
packages/db/migrations/0065_guest_requests_acl.sql, journal idx 64,
when 1787300000000. NO schema change: no column, no index, no policy, no data.

  GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON public.guest_booking_requests TO authenticated;
  REVOKE INSERT, DELETE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE ... FROM authenticated;
  REVOKE ALL ON public.guest_booking_requests FROM patient;

The patient revoke follows 0055's precedent for staff_notifications: a guest
request carries another person's phone number and stated preference, the patient
role matches no policy here anyway, and the table gate refuses before RLS is even
consulted - two independent reasons for one denial, which is what PG6 asks for.

RLS IS UNTOUCHED. Not one policy changes. Production's extra privileges were
bounded by 0063's policies the whole time, which is why none of this was ever an
exposure and why INC-11 closed as a reproducibility defect.

=== STATE: AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED ===
Rule 7: the apply block is drafted, goes to strategy, then to Ivan, and the PR
merges only after he pastes the journal back. The draft was delivered to strategy
in the session report, opening with the verbatim NOT VALIDATED line, and was NOT
sent to the owner.

WHAT UNBLOCKS WHEN THIS LANDS: #917 comes out of draft and its DB-gated check
runs against a table CI can actually read.

--- prior notes below, unedited ---

DO NOT AUTHOR YET. Standing rule 8: ONE migration in flight across the whole
repo, and 0064 is CYAN's on the open consultation PR. This card exists so the
work is ready the day that slot clears, not so it can be started early. Rule 7
also forbids reserving a number in advance - 0065 is written here as the number
that is free TODAY and it is re-checked at build time, never assumed.

=== THE SCOPE, AMENDED 2026-08-17 BY WHAT THE PRODUCTION READ FOUND ===
It was "add the missing grants". It is now "normalise the ACL", because the
production read that closed INC-11 showed the problem is not too few privileges,
it is the wrong ones in both directions:

  GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON public.guest_booking_requests TO authenticated;
  REVOKE INSERT, DELETE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE
    ON public.guest_booking_requests FROM authenticated;

WHY EACH HALF.
  SELECT   - reception's queue reads this table, and withTenantContext runs every
             staff read as authenticated (packages/db/src/client.ts:121).
  UPDATE   - the convert marks a request handled.
  NOT INSERT - the public form writes under the SERVICE ROLE by 0063's deliberate
             design. The whole point of that table is that exactly one write path
             reaches it; granting authenticated an INSERT would create a second.
  NOT DELETE, NOT TRUNCATE - guest requests are never deleted. They are the
             record that somebody asked for an appointment.
  NOT REFERENCES, NOT TRIGGER - nothing in the application needs either, and they
             arrived from Supabase's default privileges rather than a decision.

WHY IT IS WORTH A MIGRATION AT ALL, GIVEN NOTHING IS BROKEN. Production already
has the privileges the feature needs, so this fixes no live behaviour. It fixes
REPRODUCIBILITY: a database built from packages/db/migrations today produces a
table authenticated cannot read, which is what CI proved on #917 and what any new
environment would inherit. And it makes least privilege true in the committed
schema rather than accidental in one project's dashboard.

RLS IS THE LIVE GUARD AND STAYS THE LIVE GUARD. This changes no policy. A
privilege with no policy behind it still grants no row; the ACL is the second
lock, not the first.

=== BEFORE AUTHORING, VERIFY BY CODE READ, AND HALT IF IT FAILS ===
Confirm NO authenticated path relies on any revoked privilege - in particular
that nothing inserts into or deletes from guest_booking_requests outside the
service-role form handler. If one does, STOP and report rather than revoking a
privilege something uses. Grep the write paths, do not reason from this note.

=== THEN THE ORDINARY MIGRATION CHOREOGRAPHY, RULE 7 ===
Author, open the PR, draft the apply block starting with the verbatim
NOT VALIDATED line (rule 9 of the work protocol), strategy validates it, Ivan
applies from the osteojp-prod-apply worktree with git checkout origin/<branch>
DETACHED, pastes the journal back, and only then does the PR merge.

WHAT UNBLOCKS WHEN THIS LANDS: #917 (GUEST-06) comes out of draft, its DB-gated
check runs against a table CI can actually read, and it merges on green.

cards.title: A third schedule entry mode: a day-by-day grid for a therapist whose dates follow no pattern at all. Same rows as layer 2, same carve, but it REFUSES on a collision with dated rows and names the dates rather than writing over them

evidence.ref:
ACCEPTANCE OBSERVED BY THE OWNER, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-18. His words, verbatim, covering items 2 to 6: "Item 2 to Item 6 all pass successfully, everything acts as described and expected." The script's described states carried the load-bearing specifics, which is why a bare "pass" closes these cards rather than leaving them unobserved: the expected screen was written out per item before the sitting, so agreeing with it is a positive reading and not an absence of complaint.

OBSERVED FOR THIS CARD: on a therapist card at /horarios, the day-by-day grid. A window was picked, dates set at different clinics, saved, and the panel RE-OPENED with exactly those dates back. The round trip is the check; a grid that renders correctly but does not persist would pass a screenshot and fail a clinic.

BUILD HALF, unchanged: PR #922, squashed to 5643acc, shipped with SCHED-05 in one PR because the fix and this mode are the same seam. Gates at merge: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 2164 passed across 222 files, build 4/4, plus the CI e2e set and the DB-gated suite green.

cards.notes:
RATIFIED IN FULL 2026-08-17. BUILD AUTHORIZED. No migration, no dependency on
INC-11 or #917.

=== WHAT IT IS, AND WHY A THIRD MODE RATHER THAN A SETTING ON AN EXISTING ONE ===
Mode 1 is the weekly schedule (layer 1): a recurring week, the default, unbounded.
Mode 2 is SCHED-01's alternating weeks: a generated PATTERN over a window.
Mode 3 is this: a WINDOW OF DATES WITH NO PATTERN. The therapist works these
specific days at these specific clinics, and no rule generates them.

It cannot be a setting on mode 2 because mode 2's whole correctness argument is
that a generator produces the rows - "two offset series cannot produce the same
day, so the invariant holds by construction". Hand-entered dates have no
generator, so they need the invariant CHECKED rather than guaranteed, and they
need a different answer when they collide with what is already there.

=== THE ROW MODEL IS UNCHANGED, WHICH IS WHY THERE IS NO MIGRATION ===
One availability_templates row per date, valid_from === valid_until === the date.
Verified in the shipped code, not assumed: alternating-weeks.ts writes exactly
that shape, and both consumers already honour the columns -
day-availability-core.ts through isWithinValidity, and the portal booking guard
as a SQL predicate at apps/api/lib/appointments/store.ts.

=== THE FOUR DECISIONS THE OWNER RATIFIED ===
1. REFUSE ON COLLISION WITH ALREADY-DATED ROWS, AND NAME THE DATES. Not "some
   dates conflict" - the actual dates, on screen, so the person can look at them.
2. THE ESCAPE IS OPT-IN AND IT IS A SECOND CONFIRMED ACTION. "Substituir esta
   janela" is never the default arm and never happens as a side effect of saving.
   The refusal comes first; replacing is a separate decision taken after reading
   which dates are in the way.
3. REPLACING DEACTIVATES. is_active = false on the superseded rows. It NEVER
   inverts a validity range and it never deletes. is_active already exists on the
   table (packages/db/src/schema.ts:851), so this needs no migration either, and
   the existing read path already filters on it.
4. THE CARVE AGAINST LAYER 1 IS UNCHANGED. The weekly row is bounded to the day
   before the window and an identical row resumes the day after, exactly as
   planAlternatingWeeks does today. Q-W5-4 stands: scheduling data is carved,
   never destroyed.

=== IT SHIPS WITH THE SCHED-05 FIX BECAUSE THE SEAM IS SHARED ===
SCHED-05 is the re-run range-inversion defect in mode 2's carve. The fix and this
build touch the same planner: "refuse on collision with dated rows, replace only
by explicit deactivation" is the same rule both modes need. Shipping them apart
would mean either a shared planner with no consumer, or this mode built on top of
a carve already known to invert. One PR.

=== PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT AFFECTS HOW MUCH TO TRUST THIS CARD ===
The delivered design document from the session that proposed this is NOT in the
repo and was not recoverable - not on the board, not in docs/, not in the bodies
of #918, #919 or #920. What is written above is RECONSTRUCTED from two sources
that are in the repo or in the ratification itself: the four ruled decisions, and
SCHED-01's recorded recon plus the shipped code it describes. The load-bearing
parts are therefore ruled or verifiable. The grid's interaction detail and its
microcopy are NOT recovered and are authored fresh under the standing microcopy
delegation, listed verbatim on this card when built.

=== TWO CALLS MADE DURING THE BUILD, STATED BECAUSE NEITHER WAS RULED ===

1. AN EMPTY WINDOW IS REFUSED rather than written as "works no days". The two are
   indistinguishable in the payload, one of them is a mis-click, and the
   deliberate version already has its own tool: blocked time removes availability
   without disturbing the schedule that resumes afterwards.

2. THE WINDOW GOVERNS ALL SEVEN WEEKDAYS, not only the ones with entries. The
   alternative silently conflates "I turned this day off" with "I did not touch
   this day": a Tuesday left unticked would keep its ordinary weekly row, so the
   grid would say not-working while the agenda kept offering slots. That is the
   1.3 collapse exactly, so the exhaustive reading is the safe one - and the
   panel renders every date in the window so the reading is visible rather than
   implied.

Both are reversible without touching the row model if the owner wants the other
behaviour; neither changes what is written for a day that IS set.

cards.title: Re-running the alternating-week pattern over a window it already covers INVERTS the dated rows' validity ranges and leaves them behind: valid_from after valid_until, dead, invisible and never cleaned up

evidence.ref:
ACCEPTANCE OBSERVED BY THE OWNER, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-18. His words, verbatim, covering items 2 to 6: "Item 2 to Item 6 all pass successfully, everything acts as described and expected." The script's described states carried the load-bearing specifics, which is why a bare "pass" closes these cards rather than leaving them unobserved: the expected screen was written out per item before the sitting, so agreeing with it is a positive reading and not an absence of complaint.

OBSERVED FOR THIS CARD, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE PASS. Saving the SAME window a second time was REFUSED, and the refusal NAMED THE DATES - weekday plus dd/mm - with "Substituir esta janela" present as the explicit way through. A second save that succeeded silently would have been the failure, because it is the silent overwrite this card exists to remove; a refusal that did not name the dates would have been half the fix, since the person cannot judge an overwrite they cannot see.

BUILD HALF, unchanged: PR #922, squashed to 5643acc, alongside SCHED-04. The carve moved into lib/scheduling/schedule-window.ts and refuses rather than inverting the ranges. Gates at merge: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 2164 passed across 222 files, build 4/4, plus the CI e2e set and the DB-gated suite green.

cards.notes:
CARD AUTHORIZED 2026-08-17. Fixed as part of the SCHED-04 build - same seam.

=== THE DEFECT, TRACED IN THE SHIPPED CODE RATHER THAN REPORTED ===
apps/web/lib/scheduling/alternating-weeks.ts, planAlternatingWeeks, the carve loop
at lines 116-141. It carves EVERY existing active row on a pattern weekday. On the
first run the only such rows are layer-1 weekly rows, and the carve is correct.

On a SECOND run over the same window, the existing rows now include the DATED rows
the first run created (valid_from === valid_until === that date). For each one:
  - line 120  row.validUntil < startDate     false, the date is inside the window
  - line 121  row.validFrom  > endDate       false, same reason
  - so it is carved: validUntil := the day before the NEW window starts
  - line 130  row.validUntil <= endDate      true, so resume is null
The row keeps its own valid_from - a date INSIDE the window - and is given a
valid_until BEFORE it. valid_from > valid_until. The row is dead, no resume row is
written, and nothing deletes it.

=== WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING ===
An inverted row is INERT AT READ TIME. isWithinValidity (availability.ts:51)
refuses any date before valid_from and any date after valid_until, and when
from > until no date satisfies both. So the schedule LOOKS right on every screen.

And the write-time invariant does not see it either: validityIntersects
(schedule-coverage.ts) computes aFrom <= bTo && bFrom <= aTo, which is false for
an inverted range against anything. So coverageViolations silently EXCLUDES the
rows it can no longer reason about, and the save succeeds reporting no violation.

That is PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 exactly: a case nobody handled maps onto the benign
one, and the system carries on reporting something reasonable. The rows
accumulate on every re-run, and the "no double coverage" guarantee is computed
over a set that quietly excludes them.

=== SEVERITY, HONESTLY BOUNDED ===
Not an incident. Nothing patient-facing is wrong: an inert row offers no slot and
blocks none. The cost is junk rows that grow per re-run and a coverage invariant
whose input set is not what it appears to be.

WORTH CHECKING ONCE, NOT ASSUMED: whether production carries any inverted rows
already, which would mean the pattern was applied twice over one window since
SCHED-01 shipped on 2026-08-14. That is a read-only query for the owner to run in
his own shell if wanted - never from this terminal - and it is not a precondition
for the fix.

=== THE FIX, WHICH IS THE SCHED-04 RULE APPLIED TO MODE 2 ===
The carve stops treating a dated row as a weekly row to be bounded. A dated row
inside the window is a COLLISION: refuse and name the dates, or, on the explicit
opt-in second action, supersede it by is_active = false. Bounds are never written
backwards. Layer-1 rows carve exactly as they do now.

=== DEFINITION OF DONE ===
A test that RE-RUNS the pattern over an already-dated window and asserts, on the
projected rows, that NO row has valid_from > valid_until and that no dead row
survives - with a counterweight that fails if the assertion is vacuous, per the
criterion-F rule that a guard proves a test ran and only the assertion proves it
tested the right subject.

unauthenticated WRITE path on the whole patient-facing surface - shipped with
GUEST-04 (#912) and was never added.

=== THE DEFECT IS NOT THE MISSING ROW. IT IS WHY NOBODY NOTICED. ===
Section 1.1's route list CANNOT go stale: patient-surface.test.ts enumerates
apps/api/app/api/v1 from the filesystem and fails until the matrix names every
route. Add a route, CI reddens.

Section 1.2 was a hand-typed list of five with nothing holding it to anything. So
the two halves of the same document had completely different failure modes, and
the unpinned half is the one that broke - six days, unnoticed, on the surface the
document exists to enumerate.

A server action is also the harder of the two to notice by eye: no registration,
no filename convention that forces it, reachable through a POST the framework
generates. Exactly the thing to enumerate rather than remember.

=== THE FIX ===
patient-surface.test.ts now enumerates every file under apps/portal/app whose
FIRST directive is "use server" - by the directive, not by the filename, because
that is what actually makes a file a server action - and fails until section 1.2
names it. Carried as MN-29. Section 1.2's paths are written out in full rather
than abbreviated so the assertion is exact; an abbreviation reads better and
cannot be checked.

NEGATIVE ARM RUN, NOT ASSUMED: a probe server action was added at
apps/portal/app/negative-arm-probe/actions.ts, the suite went red naming that
exact path, the probe was removed and the suite returned to 53/53 with a clean
git status.

=== ONE THING DELIBERATELY LEFT UNPINNED, stated rather than skipped ===
Section 1.3, the token surface, is one page in apps/web. Enumerating every page
under apps/web/app would sweep in the entire staff platform - hundreds of routes
that are not patient-facing - and a test that must be carefully scoped to stay
useful is a test somebody will scope wrongly later. If apps/web ever grows a
second patient-facing surface, pin it then with a list narrow enough to mean
something. Recorded in section 1.5 so the omission is a decision rather than a
gap.
