cards.title: INCIDENT: a missing REMINDERS_LINK_SECRET with REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND armed threw at MODULE EVALUATION and took down /admin/staff and the entire /api/inngest route - two surfaces that send nothing

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-18 in PR #934, squashed to eeb9662. Every required check green.

IT SHIPS ON THE MERGE RATHER THAN ON A SITTING, and that is a property of the fix rather than an exemption. WF-03 holds a card open when the owner must SEE something; the owner-visible result here is the ABSENCE of an outage, which is not a screenshot. /admin/staff and /api/inngest answering is the whole observation, and both were already up before this merged - the owner restored them by setting the flag back to false.

WHAT PROVES IT INSTEAD, and it is a pair rather than a single check:
  Importing the adapters with REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND armed and REMINDERS_LINK_SECRET absent - the exact production state of 2026-08-18 - does NOT throw.
  Sending in that state DOES throw, naming the missing variable.
Either half alone is a bug: the first without the second is a guard that was deleted, the second without the first is the outage. Both live in apps/web/lib/reminders/invite-boot-env.test.ts and packages/notify/src/gate.test.ts.

NEGATIVE ARM RUN BEFORE THE PR: restoring assertNotificationEnv at module scope in clients.ts fails exactly the three "loads while armed and incomplete" cases and nothing else. A test file that only ever passed would have proven nothing about the file having changed.

Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 8/8 tasks, build 4/4.

cards.notes:
WHAT HAPPENED, 2026-08-18. The owner set REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND=true on production. REMINDERS_LINK_SECRET was not set. `assertNotificationEnv` ran at MODULE SCOPE in three files, threw NotificationEnvError while the module graph was still being built, and every importer failed with it:
  /admin/staff returned an error page. It imports the invite chain (lib/admin/staff.ts -> lib/invites/email.ts -> lib/reminders/clients.ts).
  /api/inngest stopped answering entirely - GET (introspection), POST (invocation) and PUT (registration). So the reminder stream could neither send NOR be re-registered, from one missing variable.

THE ENVIRONMENT HALF IS ALREADY RESOLVED AND WAS NOT THIS TERMINAL'S. The owner armed the flag himself, set it back to false, redeployed, and /admin/staff renders again. NO COMMITTED-SOURCE ARMING EXISTS - the question "did something in the repo turn this on" is answered NO, and no hunt is owed. Recorded here because a future reader will ask it again.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS PROPORTION, NOT THE CHECK. The property being asserted is "this stream cannot send". The blast radius was "anything that transitively imports the adapters". Those two sets have no relationship to each other and the second is very much larger. The check was right and its POSITION was wrong.

THE FIX: the assertion moved into createNotifier().dispatch, the one place in the platform that actually sends. Armed-but-incomplete config now fails THE SEND with the SAME NotificationEnvError and the SAME full list of missing names. No behaviour change on a valid config.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and it is the load-bearing decision. It was NOT downgraded to a `missing_provider_config` suppression. That reason is the SAME line a healthy sandbox deploy writes, so a broken deploy would have become indistinguishable from a safe one in the Vercel logs - the exact silent degradation #763 and #778 removed from these paths. The assertion therefore sits BEFORE `transportConfigured`, which returns rather than throws. One line later and the fix would have been the old bug.

TWO THINGS THAT KEEP IT FROM BEING SILENTLY UNDONE:
  `envFlags` is REQUIRED on NotifierOptions. An app that forgets the guard is a TYPE ERROR at the one place a notifier is constructed, not a hole that announces itself nowhere.
  The deploy-time SIGNAL survives as `warnNotificationEnv`: the same list, logged loudly once per process, names only. It decides nothing and nothing reads it - PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 - so deleting it would cost the early warning and make nothing sendable.

THREE TEST FILES WERE ASSERTING A STATE THAT COULD NOT REACH PRODUCTION, and that is worth its own line. `armed with no keys -> missing_provider_config` was true of the code and false of every deployment, because the boot check crashed such a deploy before it could dispatch anything. The branch was unreachable while armed. Those cases now assert the throw, each carrying why it changed rather than being quietly rewritten.

CONSEQUENCE THE OWNER SHOULD KNOW, stated rather than buried: the env requirement is the APP's and not the channel's, exactly as the boot check's was. An incomplete deploy fails every send in the armed streams, not only the channel whose variable is missing. That is the same set of deploys that previously failed to boot at all, so it is strictly less severe than what it replaces.

LAUNCH-01 CARRIES THE PROCEDURAL HALF: set every variable the stream needs, redeploy, confirm the app is up, and only then arm the flag. The code no longer punishes the wrong order with an outage; it still punishes it with a stream where every send throws.

NO SCREEN OF ITS OWN. This is proven by test and by /admin/staff and /api/inngest continuing to answer. The owner-visible consequence is the absence of an outage, which is not a screenshot.

cards.title: DEFECT ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION: a therapist opened /notificacoes and saw the ENTIRE tenant's guest queue - strangers' names, phone numbers and convert buttons - because the gate was appointments:read, which every role holds

evidence.ref:
OWNER OBSERVATION ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-18 (second sitting of the day). Four items run, two PASS, one PASS with a fixture reading, one DEFECT. The defect is item 2 and it belongs to a card of its own (SEC-02-temp-password-no-forced-rotation); it does not touch any of the cards closed here.

ITEM 4 PASS, AND BOTH ARMS WERE RUN, which is the whole reason this card stayed open on green CI. THERAPIST 2 opened /notificacoes and saw NO guest section - absent, not empty. Reception opened the same page and still sees the rows and the convert buttons.

THE SECOND ARM IS NOT CEREMONY. A fix that removed the section for everybody would have satisfied the first observation completely and broken the front desk, and nothing on the therapist's screen could tell those two outcomes apart. That is why the sitting script asked for both.

THE ACCOUNT USED IS THE ONE THIS NEEDED: ZZ TESTE THERAPIST 2, created 2026-08-18 with NO location assigned. A therapist assigned to nothing is the strictest available reading of the ruling - there is no location scope that could have been doing the hiding, so the refusal is the capability and nothing else.

BUILD HALF, unchanged: PR #935 MERGED, squashed to bfe2b33, every required check green. `guest_requests:read` held by owner, admin and reception; the list, the count and both convert actions all assert it; notificacoes/page.tsx skips the fetch entirely so nothing reaches the RSC payload. 12 assertions in guest-queue-access.test.ts plus a named case in permission-matrix.test.ts, and the negative arm (reverting the gate to appointments:read) fails exactly the three therapist cases.

cards.notes:
OBSERVED BY THE OWNER ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION, 2026-08-18. chris@dlvlogistics.com, role Terapeuta, assigned to LV and CB, opened /notificacoes and saw the full "Pedidos de novos clientes" section: guest names, phone numbers and convert buttons, INCLUDING requests submitted by Rodica. Server-side per INC-08.

OWNER RULING, 2026-08-18, verbatim in substance: the guest queue is visible ONLY to owner, admin and reception. Reception and admin see only requests for their assigned locations, mirroring PL-09. Owner sees all locations. THE THERAPIST GETS NO SECTION, NO DATA, NOTHING TO HIDE CLIENT-SIDE - THE SERVER MUST NOT RETURN THE ROWS.

=== WHY IT SHIPPED, AND IT IS TWO CORRECT-LOOKING LINES MEETING ===
Neither line is wrong on its own, which is why this survived review.
  1. THE GATE WAS `appointments:read`, which EVERY role holds, because every role works the calendar. The capability check therefore PASSED for a therapist while gating nothing - it read as a real check and was not one.
  2. `viewerLocationScope` RETURNS null FOR A THERAPIST, and null means UNRESTRICTED. That is correct for the agenda, where a therapist is bounded by their own-data rules rather than by location. Here it handed the one role with no location scope the WIDEST POSSIBLE READ.
Together they turn "a therapist may read appointments" into "a therapist may read every stranger's phone number in the tenant".

=== THE FIX ===
A new `guest_requests:read` capability, held by owner, admin and reception. A guest request is NOT an appointment - no patient, no appointment row, no practitioner - so there is no therapist-shaped subset of this queue to hand out. The location scope needed no change and is now correct by construction: owner all, located reception/admin their own clinic, unassigned unrestricted per the STAFF-02 and PL-09 fallback.

IT THROWS RATHER THAN RETURNING AN EMPTY ARRAY, which is the decision worth recording. `[]` is a VALID ANSWER every caller renders as "no requests today", indistinguishable from a genuinely quiet queue - the exact collapse PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 names. A throw cannot be mistaken for data.

THE PAGE SKIPS THE FETCH rather than filtering the render, so no stranger's contact details reach the RSC payload of a page a therapist opens. The section is ABSENT rather than empty: an empty heading would still tell a therapist that a queue exists, what it is called, and that they are being kept out of it.

=== A SECOND, UNCALLED LEAK FIXED IN THE SAME PR ===
`countPendingGuestRequests` had NEITHER the gate NOR the location scope, and it HAS NO CALLER. It was fixed precisely because it has none: it is the obvious next thing somebody wires to the notifications badge, and a count reads as harmless because it returns no names. It is not harmless - it answers "how many strangers has this clinic collected contact details for". The missing location scope would also have made the badge disagree with the list it describes.

=== THE PEDIDO QUEUE WAS CHECKED AND DOES NOT HAVE THIS DEFECT ===
Asked for explicitly in the dispatch, so the answer is recorded rather than left implied. `listPendingRequests` reads `staff_notifications`, and migration 0055's `staff_notifications_own_select` policy pins every read to `recipient_user_id = auth.uid()` AT THE DATABASE. `resolveRecipients` (apps/api/lib/notifications/centre.ts) addresses exactly two sets: users with the RECEPTION role slug, and the explicitly named assigned practitioners. So a therapist sees only pedidos addressed to THEM, which is what ACC-therapist-queue-unobserved item 26a already verified on a screen.

ONE THING FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: the pedido queue is not LOCATION-scoped for reception - every reception user receives every pedido. That is D4's design (JP, 2026-08-11), which makes it a per-recipient inbox on the reasoning that a patient-initiated change concerns all of reception, and it is not a PL-09 violation. Reported, not touched, per the dispatch's "fix only the guest queue unless the pedido queue violates an existing ruling too".

=== THE GENERAL LESSON, which is about a COMMENT ===
notificacoes/page.tsx carried a paragraph explaining why the route needs no capability gate: RLS confines every row to the recipient, so "the rule is not which role, it is which person". That was TRUE of the page when written. GUEST-04 then added a section fed by a TENANT-WIDE table with no recipient column, and the stated reason for having no role gate silently became false for one section while remaining quoted in place. A justification for an ABSENT check has to be re-read every time the thing it justifies grows. The comment is corrected rather than deleted.

OWNER-OBSERVABLE: on the next sitting, a therapist at /notificacoes must see NO "Pedidos de novos clientes" section at all, while reception still sees and works theirs.

cards.title: FEATURE: the complex scheduling page /horarios had no sidebar entry on the owner account - the one nav entry was hidden from exactly the two roles holding every other capability

evidence.ref:
OWNER OBSERVATION ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-18 (second sitting of the day). Four items run, two PASS, one PASS with a fixture reading, one DEFECT. The defect is item 2 and it belongs to a card of its own (SEC-02-temp-password-no-forced-rotation); it does not touch any of the cards closed here.

ITEM 1 PASS. The owner sidebar shows Horarios BETWEEN Estatisticas and Administracao, and it opens the COMPLEX scheduling page rather than the simple horarios layer inside Administracao. Both halves of the ruling observed: the position and the destination.

=== THE SIDEBAR POSITION QUESTION IS ANSWERED: OPTION A, CONFIRMED 2026-08-18. ===
This PR moved the single /horarios entry to the end of the nav list, so for THERAPIST and RECEPTION - who see neither Estatisticas nor Administracao - Horarios became their LAST sidebar item instead of sitting after Marcacoes. That consequence was reported at merge rather than left to be discovered, with the one-line restore offered.

THE OWNER RULED OPTION A: the current production state STANDS. No change is made and none is pending. Recorded here rather than left silent because 'nobody objected' and 'the owner ruled' are different facts, and a future reader finding therapist Horarios at the bottom must be able to tell that it was decided rather than overlooked.

BUILD HALF, unchanged: PR #937 MERGED, squashed to afd6702, every required check green including all three E2E shards. `hideIfCapability` removed along with the mechanism itself, position asserted BY INDEX, and the role list now DERIVED from `can(role, "schedule:read")` so it cannot go stale a fourth time.

cards.notes:
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-18. The owner sidebar showed Inicio, Agenda, Pacientes, Marcacoes, Faturacao, Revisao Consulta, Estatisticas, Administracao - and no Horarios. Add the entry BETWEEN Estatisticas and Administracao, linking to /horarios, FOR EVERY ROLE THAT MAY ACCESS THE PAGE. Code-read which roles those are and match the nav to the access; DO NOT WIDEN ACCESS. The therapist sidebar already shows Horarios, leave it. The simple horarios layer inside Administracao stays untouched.

=== WHAT THE CODE-READ FOUND ===
`schedule:read` is held by ALL FOUR roles: owner (all capabilities), admin and reception (PL-09 Phase 5), therapist (ITEM 3, owner ruling 2026-08-14). `horarios/page.tsx` redirects anyone without it. So all four could already OPEN the page and two of them could not FIND it.

THE CAUSE WAS ONE PROPERTY ON THE NAV ENTRY: `hideIfCapability: "settings:read"`. Owner and admin hold `settings:read`, so the single entry pointing at /horarios was hidden from exactly the two roles that hold everything else.

THE REASONING BEHIND IT EXPIRED RATHER THAN BEING WRONG, and that distinction is the point. It read: owner and admin manage schedules inside Equipa (/admin/staff), so a second entry would be a duplicate surface for the same job. TRUE WHEN WRITTEN. Since then /horarios became the COMPLEX scheduling page - SCHED-03's roster search, SCHED-04's day-by-day grid, SCHED-05's overwrite refusal, all shipped 2026-08-17 - and Equipa's horarios layer is the simple one. They stopped being the same surface and nothing re-read the comment that said they were.

NO ACCESS WAS WIDENED. Not a capability changed, not a route guard touched. The nav now matches the access that already existed. The simple layer inside Administracao is untouched, as ruled.

=== THE COST, SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN DISCOVERED ===
ONE DESTINATION GETS ONE ENTRY IN ONE ORDERED LIST, so moving it to sit between Estatisticas and Administracao moves it for EVERY role. Therapist and reception see neither of those two items, so Horarios is now their LAST sidebar item instead of sitting after Marcacoes. The entry itself is untouched for them - same href, same label, same capability - which is what "the therapist sidebar already shows Horarios, leave it" protects.

THE ALTERNATIVE WAS REJECTED ON ITS SHAPE: a SECOND entry pinned to the old slot for those roles would put one destination in two nav rows kept apart by inverse conditions. That is the arrangement that drifts, and it is a near relative of the property being removed here.

=== `hideIfCapability` IS REMOVED, and it is not an unrelated tidy-up ===
Its only ever user was the line this card fixes. An unused "hide this from a MORE privileged role" hook is not inert: it is the shape of this bug, sitting in the type, ready to be reached for again. A nav entry should be gated by whether the role may USE the page, which `capability` already answers. If a surface ever genuinely needs hiding from a superset role, the mechanism comes back in a commit WITH its caller.

=== THE ASSERTION IS NOW DERIVED, SO IT CANNOT GO STALE A FOURTH TIME ===
The nav test's role list has been rewritten three times by three rulings: `["reception"]` (PL-09 Phase 5), `["therapist", "reception"]` (RULING A), all four (this card). It now asserts that the entry appears for exactly the roles holding `schedule:read` - the same capability the route redirects on - so granting the capability to a fifth role carries the nav with it, and widening the nav without the capability fails. Position is asserted separately BY INDEX, because "the entry exists" and "the entry is where he asked for it" are different claims and only the second was ruled on.

OWNER-OBSERVABLE: the owner sidebar must show Horarios between Estatisticas and Administracao, and it must open the complex scheduling page.

cards.title: A reusable, project-neutral template of this board schema, so the same system can run another project without inheriting OsteoJP content

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-18 in PR #936, squashed to 712481b. Owner add-on request: he will reuse this board system on other projects, driven by other chats and terminals.

WHAT IT IS: docs/board/BOARD-TEMPLATE.json, the schema with every project fact removed - one example card carrying every field including the optional open_on_purpose, nine placeholder gate conditions, the exact seven-lane set. docs/board/BOARD-TEMPLATE.README.md sits beside it saying it is the clean template and must never carry project content; BOARD-SPEC.md gained a paragraph pointing at both.

THE PLACEHOLDERS ARE TYPED, NOT PROSE, and that was the one real decision. Every enum value, lane id and date in it is a REAL VALID VALUE rather than the words describing it, so the template passes its own validator; the what-belongs-here guidance lives in the free-text title/notes/source_note fields. A template that cannot be validated teaches nothing and hides its own mistakes.

IT IS INERT HERE AND THAT IS DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. It is not registered in board-config.mjs, so render-board.mjs refuses it, and validate-board.mjs reports EXACTLY ONE violation against it - the BOARD_NAMES allowlist. That single line is simultaneously the proof it is not a live board and the only change a new project must make. Verified by running the validator against a scratch copy with the name allowlisted: BOARD VALID, 0/9 gates, 1 card.

TWO CONSTANTS A NEW PROJECT EDITS: BOARD_NAMES and LAUNCH_GATE_DENOMINATOR in validate-board.mjs (plus the matching DEFAULT_DENOMINATOR and a config entry in board-config.mjs). Both are hardcoded in the shipped scripts and neither is discoverable from the JSON alone, which is why the README names them.

No change to portal-board.json or prelaunch-board.json.

cards.notes:
COMPANION FILES A NEW PROJECT NEEDS for the board to be load-bearing rather than decorative, recorded here because the template alone is just a document: validate-board.mjs (is it WELL-FORMED), reconcile-board.mjs (is it TRUE - checks cards against merged PRs and against the gate's own state, exits 2 if it cannot ask), render-board.mjs plus board-config.mjs and board-app.js (the artifact and its interactive client), BOARD-SPEC.md (the governing spec), a rehydrate doc on the PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md pattern (the single most valuable file - it is what makes a stateless terminal useful), and CI wiring that runs the validator and the reconciler INSIDE an already-required job rather than as a new one, since a new job is a new check name and would not be in the required set.

BUILD ORDER: validator, then the rehydrate doc, then renderer and config, then reconciler, then CI. A board without the reconciler still works; a board without the rehydrate doc gets re-derived from chat history every session, which is the failure the whole system exists to prevent.

cards.title: DEFECT ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION: the invite flow issues a temporary password and first login does NOT force a rotation - the temporary credential logs straight in and stays valid indefinitely

evidence.ref:
OWNER OBSERVATION ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION, 2026-08-19. Five steps run on the disposable fixture chris+rotationtest@dlvlogistics.com. His words, verbatim: "all works as expected".

ALL FOUR ARMS OF THE RULING OBSERVED, and they are listed separately because a single "it works" over four distinct properties is worth nothing later if nobody wrote down which four:
  1. The temporary-password session reached ONLY O meu perfil.
  2. THE /agenda DEEP LINK WAS REFUSED. This is the arm a client-side redirect would have failed, and it is why the guard was put in AppShell server-side rather than in a login redirect.
  3. After setting the new password the platform opened, WITH NO BOUNCE-BACK. This is the arm that proves the rejected JWT design was rejected correctly: a token is stale until it refreshes, so under that design the freshly-rotated staffer would have been sent back to the screen they had just completed. It is the one property no CI test could have shown.
  4. The OLD temporary password was refused at sign-in.

BUILD HALF, unchanged: migration 0066 applied to production 2026-08-18 from 1d75c1c (receipt: docs/migration-apply-0066.md, pending 1 -> 0, `when` 1787300000000 -> 1787300100000, column verified via information_schema as boolean/not null/default false). PR #943 merged, squashed to 810a52d, all 12 checks green at the pinned head.

THE FIXTURE IS NOT YET DELETED AND ITS REMOVAL IS AN OWNER ACTION - see LE-staff-delete-leaves-auth-user, opened from what the deletion attempt found. It does not hold this card open: the fixture is a test account on a plus-tagged address whose password only the owner knows, and the property this card asserts was observed.

cards.notes:
OBSERVED BY THE OWNER, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-18, item 2. He signed in as ZZ TESTE THERAPIST 2 using the temporary password the Convidar dialog issued. IT LOGGED STRAIGHT IN. No set-password screen, no prompt, no interstitial - the session opened on the platform and the temporary password remained a valid, indefinite credential.

OWNER RULING, 2026-08-18: A SESSION ENTERING ON A TEMPORARY PASSWORD MUST BE FORCED TO SET A NEW ONE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE.

=== WHY THIS IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A MISSING NICETY ===
A temporary password is issued through a channel nobody treats as secret. Today it is READ OFF A DIALOG by whoever clicked Convidar and then relayed - spoken, messaged, pasted. That is acceptable ONLY while the credential's life ends at first use. Without forced rotation the relay channel becomes the account's permanent password, and every person who ever saw it retains access to a clinical system.

IT IS WORSE UNDER R9, WHICH IS THE CURRENT STATE. INVITES_LIVE_SEND is off, so NO invite email is sent and the temporary password is the ONLY way any invited staff member gets in. The hand-off path is not a fallback today; it is the whole onboarding flow. Every staff member onboarded before this is fixed holds a password that somebody else chose and read.

=== THE EXPOSED FIXTURE CREDENTIAL, RECORDED AS BURNED ===
THERAPIST 2's temporary password is treated as BURNED. The owner is rotating it manually, 2026-08-18, and FIXTURES.md carries the same note.

PRECISION ABOUT THIS TERMINAL, because standing rule 3 requires it and the distinction matters if anyone audits later: THE VALUE NEVER ENTERED THIS TERMINAL'S CONTEXT. The dispatch that reported the account's creation quoted the dialog's copy with the value elided ('Palavra-passe temporaria...'). This card records the owner's ruling that it is burned; it does not record a value seen here, and no rotation is owed on this terminal's account.

=== SCOPE, so the fix does not quietly become an auth rewrite ===
IN: the platform must know a password is temporary, and must refuse to serve anything except the set-password screen until it has been replaced. The forcing has to be SERVER-SIDE and it has to hold on EVERY route, not just the one the login redirect happens to land on - a client-side redirect is a suggestion, and a staff member who deep-links to /pacientes must be caught the same way.

OUT, unless recon proves otherwise: password strength policy, expiry of the temporary credential after N hours, and the invite email itself. Each is defensible and none is what was ruled. If the fix cannot be built without one of them, that is a premise mismatch - halt and say so rather than widening.

RECON REQUIRED BEFORE ANY DESIGN, and it is the first real question: does the platform currently RECORD that a password is temporary at all? If it does not, the fix needs a persisted marker and that may mean a migration - in which case rule 7 applies (author, owner applies, apply BEFORE merge) and rule 8 means it is the only migration in flight. Do not assume a column exists; read the schema.

OWNER-OBSERVABLE WHEN DONE: invite a fresh test account, sign in with the temporary password, and be REFUSED entry to everything until a new password is set. Then confirm the old temporary password no longer works.

=== RECON DONE 2026-08-18. THE ANSWER FORKS, AND THE FORK CHANGES WHO MERGES. BLOCKED ON IVAN FOR ONE DECISION. ===

THE CARD'S OWN FIRST QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Nothing in the platform records that a password is temporary.
  apps/web/lib/admin/staff.ts:183 mints `randomBytes(18).toString("base64url")` and passes it straight to provisionStaffUser.
  apps/web/lib/auth/provision.ts:72 calls admin.auth.admin.createUser with exactly three fields - email, password, email_confirm - and no metadata.
  The public.users insert that follows writes id, tenant_id, role_id, email and full_name. There is no password-state column.
  custom_access_token_hook (migration 0010, re-owned by 0060) stamps tenant_id, user_role and patient_id. Nothing about credentials.
So the fix needs a NEW persisted marker. That was the condition this card already named as the one that would pull in rule 7.

=== TWO DESIGNS. BOTH WORK. THEY DIFFER IN WHO MERGES, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT AN ENGINEERING PREFERENCE. ===

DESIGN B - a flag on the Supabase auth user (app_metadata).
  NO MIGRATION, so the dispatched `self-merge on green` holds.
  THE PROBLEM IS THAT IT CANNOT BE VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION. It rests on app_metadata arriving inside the token getClaims() returns. That is widely true of Supabase and it is still a REMEMBERED FACT, which rule 4 forbids building on. Docker is not running on this machine, so no local stack can answer it, and nothing in the repo's DB-gated suite signs in through GoTrue to inspect a real access token - those tests talk to Postgres directly. Proving it would mean building that sign-in harness first.
  IF THE ASSUMPTION IS WRONG THE GUARD READS TRUE AND DOES NOTHING. A claim that never arrives is a flag that is never set, and a forced-rotation check that never fires looks identical to one that passed. PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 names exactly this: on a verdict path an unhandled case must FAIL, not fall back. This one would fall back to `not temporary`.

DESIGN C - a column on public.users, read server-side per request.
  FULLY VERIFIABLE by the DB-gated suite that already exists, with no new harness.
  NEEDS MIGRATION 0066, so rule 7 applies - author here, IVAN APPLIES, apply BEFORE merge - and rule 8 makes it the only migration in flight. THE DISPATCHED `self-merge on green` CANNOT HOLD FOR IT.

=== ONE PROPERTY THAT SEPARATES THEM, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT MIGRATIONS ===
A JWT IS MINTED AT SIGN-IN AND STAYS STALE UNTIL IT REFRESHES. Under design B the flag lives in the token, so the moment the staffer SETS their new password their current token still says `must set password` - and the guard keeps redirecting them to the screen they just completed. That is a loop, and escaping it means forcing a token refresh at exactly the right moment. Design C reads the current row on each request and is never stale, so the loop cannot exist.

THAT IS WHY ENGINEERING RECOMMENDS DESIGN C despite it costing a migration and an owner touchpoint. The cheaper design is cheaper only until the first person tries to use it.

=== WHAT IS NEEDED FROM IVAN: ONE ANSWER ===
Approve DESIGN C and accept that this card becomes owner_merge with a migration to apply, OR direct DESIGN B and accept an unverified claim shape plus the refresh problem.

NOTHING WAS BUILT. This is recon, not a failed attempt - the failure ceiling is untouched and no code was written on either design. The card is blocked rather than halted because one answer unblocks it immediately.

THE DEFECT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL LIVE while this waits: with INVITES_LIVE_SEND off, the temporary password is the whole onboarding path, and every staff member onboarded before the fix holds a credential somebody else chose and read.

=== 2026-08-18: RULED OPTION C. BUILT. AWAITING THE 0066 APPLY. ===

THE EXPOSED CREDENTIAL IS DEAD. The owner logged in as THERAPIST 2 and set a new password through O meu perfil on 2026-08-18. The temporary credential that reached chat no longer opens anything. Recorded as the owner reported it; the value never entered this terminal's context, so nothing is owed here.

THE RULING, and the deciding argument is recorded as the OWNER'S rather than engineering's: under design B the flag rides in the JWT, and a token is stale until it refreshes - so a staffer who has JUST rotated still presents a token demanding rotation. B LOOPS THE EXACT PERSON THE FIX EXISTS TO HELP. Design C reads the live row per request and cannot.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
  Migration 0066 - `users.must_set_password boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, a COMMENT, and a partial index on (tenant_id) WHERE must_set_password. Additive; no policy, no grant, no existing row changed. Journal idx 65, `when` 1787300100000. Receipt skeleton at docs/migration-apply-0066.md with §5 DELIBERATELY EMPTY until the owner pastes the transcript.
  apps/web/lib/auth/password-rotation.ts - `requiresPasswordRotation` reads the live row, RLS-scoped, filtered to the caller's own id.
  provision.ts sets the marker at invite, in the one function that mints a staff auth user with a caller-supplied password, so a second invite path added later INHERITS it rather than having to remember it.
  perfil/actions.ts clears it AFTER the provider accepts the new password, never before - clearing first would free the account on a change that then failed, leaving the temporary password working with nothing left to ask.
  AppShell enforces the redirect; /perfil is the single exempt section.

IT IS A VERDICT PATH AND IT THROWS. `requiresPasswordRotation` refuses to answer when it finds no staff row, rather than returning false. The tempting one-liner `rows[0]?.mustSetPassword ?? false` maps FOUR distinct failures - no row, an RLS refusal, a query error, an unmigrated schema - onto "this password is fine", on the path where being wrong GRANTS ACCESS. PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3. The negative arm proves it: substituting that one-liner fails exactly the two throw tests and nothing else.

PRE-EXISTING STAFF: THE MARKER IS false AND THEY ARE NOT PROMPTED. This is a decision, not a default nobody thought about. There is NO PREDICATE that selects only the still-exposed accounts - GoTrue owns the credential and exposes no password-last-changed fact to this database - so the only available arms were "nobody" or "everybody". Forcing everybody is defensible on the merits and it is an OPERATIONAL EVENT landing on a working clinic at a moment nobody picked, which is the owner's to time rather than a schema default. Carded as LE-force-rotation-existing-staff.

WHY NOT THE PROXY, since that is the first question a reader has: proxy.ts runs in the middleware runtime and this check needs the database. The driver is postgres.js, which is Node-only. AppShell is the next-widest choke point - eleven layouts render it, so one check covers every authenticated section.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than discovered later: a SERVER ACTION or route handler invoked directly renders no shell and does not pass the gate. Those paths carry their own capability checks and reaching one requires first loading a page this gate refuses. Closing that gap is its own card if the owner wants it.

GATE IS NOW owner_merge, NOT green_self_merge. Rule 7: the migration is applied by the owner BEFORE this PR merges. The dispatched `self-merge on green` cannot hold for a card carrying a migration, and that was reported before anything was built rather than discovered at merge time.

Gates all four green at authoring: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test 8/8 tasks, build 4/4.

=== 2026-08-18: APPLIED AND MERGED. WHAT REMAINS IS ONE OBSERVATION. ===

THE MINIMAL OBSERVATION, and it needs NO real hire. The owner invites nobody today, so the check runs on a DISPOSABLE FIXTURE:
  1. /admin/staff -> Convidar. Any role, any name; use a plus-tagged address on the owner's own domain so it is unmistakably a fixture, e.g.
     chris+rotationtest@dlvlogistics.com. Copy the temporary password the dialog issues.
  2. Sign out. Sign in as that account with the temporary password.
     EXPECTED: the platform refuses to show anything except O meu perfil. Try /agenda or /pacientes directly in the address bar - the deep link must be refused too, not merely the landing page. That is the half a client-side redirect would fail.
  3. Set a new password on that screen.
     EXPECTED: the rest of the platform opens immediately, and it does NOT send you back to the profile screen. That return trip is the exact loop the rejected JWT design would have produced, so it is worth one deliberate look.
  4. Sign out and sign in with the OLD temporary password.
     EXPECTED: refused.
  5. Delete the fixture account.

WHY A FIXTURE RATHER THAN WAITING FOR A REAL INVITE: the guard should be proven before the next real staff member meets it, not by them. And the first real invite is a poor test subject - if it fails, it fails in front of somebody's first day.

ONE THING THE SITTING WILL NOT PROVE, stated so its absence is not read as a pass: existing staff are unaffected by design, so nothing about them is visible in this check. That population is LE-force-rotation-existing-staff.

=== 2026-08-19: OBSERVED AND CLOSED. AND THE CLEAN-UP FOUND A DEFECT. ===

The sitting passed on all four arms (evidence above). What did not go to plan is the fifth step - deleting the fixture - and it produced a real finding rather than a chore. Carded as LE-staff-delete-leaves-auth-user.

THIS TERMINAL DELETED NOTHING AND WILL NOT. A staff row and an auth user in production are a production write and a data deletion: standing rules 1, 2 and 12. The route is on that card for the owner to run.

cards.title: OWNER-TIMED: force a password rotation on every staff account onboarded BEFORE SEC-02, because each also received a password an admin chose and could read
cards.notes:
SPLIT OUT OF SEC-02 DELIBERATELY. Migration 0066 defaults `must_set_password` to false, so the fix closes the hole going FORWARD and disturbs nobody already working.

THE EXPOSURE FOR EXISTING STAFF IS REAL AND UNCHANGED. Every one of them was onboarded through the same hand-off: an admin read a temporary password off a screen and relayed it. Under R9 that was the only path.

WHY IT IS NOT A MIGRATION. There is NO PREDICATE that selects only the accounts still holding their handed-over password. GoTrue owns the credential and exposes no password-last-changed fact to this database, so the arms are `nobody` or `everybody` and nothing narrower exists. Choosing `everybody` inside a schema change would land a forced rotation on a working clinic at whatever minute the migration ran.

SO IT IS AN OWNER-TIMED ACTION: a single UPDATE the owner runs when it suits the clinic, after telling the team it is coming. One statement, and it is trivially reversible by the same statement with the boolean flipped - which is worth knowing before running it, because the failure mode is annoyance rather than damage.

The partial index 0066 creates exists for exactly this - it makes "who is still pending" answerable and therefore reversible.
