cards.title: Deleting a staff member removes the users row but NOT the Supabase auth user, so the address stays permanently taken and cannot be re-invited - and the delete refuses outright once the account has any audit activity

evidence.ref:
RECLAIM SHIPPED 2026-08-28 BY BLUE. FINDING 2 of this card is fixed; FINDING 1
is untouched and remains correct.

=== WHAT IS LEFT BEHIND, IN WHICH SYSTEM, AND THE PRODUCT PATH THAT HITS IT ===
LEFT BEHIND: one row in `auth.users` (GoTrue), holding the email address.
NOT left behind: nothing in `public`. deleteStaffMember removes
therapist_services, availability_templates, time_off and the `users` row, and
there is no createSupabaseAdminClient in that file at all.
THE PATH: inviteStaff -> provisionStaffUser -> admin.auth.admin.createUser.
The tenant-scoped pre-check reads `public.users`, which is now empty, so the
invite proceeds; createUser then fails on the surviving auth row and the invite
dies as `auth_email_taken`. Permanently, with no path in the product to clear it.

=== THE SHAPE: RECLAIM ON RE-INVITE, NOT A SECOND DELETE ===
Making the delete remove the auth user is a delete that must succeed in TWO
SYSTEMS WITH NO TRANSACTION. A half-success leaves either a live credential with
no staff row or a staff row with no login - and a two-system write with no way to
make both true is the shape that produced this defect. Reclaiming moves the work
to the re-invite, where a person is present, the intent is explicit, and one
system is touched at a time.

=== THE CANDIDATE SET IS CLOSED, AND THAT IS THE SECURITY ARGUMENT ===
THE OBVIOUS PREDICATE WAS REJECTED, and rejecting it is the most important
decision on this card. "An auth user holds this email and no `public.users` row
references it, therefore it is an orphan" is open at both ends:

  A PORTAL PATIENT HAS AN AUTH USER AND NO `users` ROW. schema.ts says it on the
  column: "A patient is a DISTINCT principal from a staff `users` row: there is
  no users row for a patient." So every patient with a portal login would be
  reclaimable. An admin could invite staff using a patient's address, have the
  password reset onto that identity, insert a staff row keyed to it, and take
  over the patient's portal login - locking the patient out of their own
  clinical record. A SEVERE ESCALATION CREATED BY THE FIX.

  AND THE SET IS OPEN: any future table linking an auth identity re-opens it
  silently, and the failure is invisible until somebody cannot sign in.

SO THE SET IS BUILT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: only an identity THIS TENANT
CREATED AS STAFF AND THEN DELETED. That set is enumerable without guessing,
because deleteStaffMember writes an audit row that SURVIVES the delete -
action "staff.delete", entityType "user", entityId = the auth id - and audit
rows are never removed, which is why the delete refuses an account with activity
in the first place. A patient's id is never in that set; another tenant's live
user is never in it; a future auth-linked table cannot put anything in it.

Two further in-tenant checks, neither redundant with the audit row: a live
`users` row at that id means it was re-created since (attachAuthLogin keys a
login to an existing row), and `patients.auth_user_id` means a patient has since
claimed it. And the ADDRESS MUST STILL MATCH on the auth side, which is what
stops a recycled id being taken - the audit row supplies a candidate, GoTrue
supplies the binding.

=== NO MIGRATION WAS NEEDED, AND TWO ALTERNATIVES WOULD HAVE NEEDED ONE ===
Shipped using only what exists: audit_log, entity_id, action, and GoTrue
getUserById. The two rejected routes are recorded below under THE QUESTION.

=== ROLLBACK: A RECLAIMED IDENTITY IS NEVER DELETED ON FAILURE ===
provisionStaffUser's existing rollback deletes the auth user when the users
insert fails. That is right for a FRESH MINT and wrong for a reclaim: the
identity existed before the call, it was already orphaned, and deleting it would
destroy a row this function did not create - turning a failed invite into the
irreversible deletion this whole card is about. The password stays changed,
which harms nobody: there is no staff row at either end, so nothing can sign in
with either password, and the next invite reclaims it again.

=== ACCEPTANCE: THE REAL FUNCTION, REAL POSTGRES, REAL AUDIT ROWS ===
apps/web/lib/auth/reclaim.db.test.ts, hard-required in assert-rls-executed.mjs.
9 tests, green locally against a live Supabase Postgres. The audit rows are
written through `writeAudit`, THE SAME PRODUCTION HELPER deleteStaffMember calls,
not hand-shaped inserts.
  finds the deleted identity when the address still matches; matches
  case-insensitively and trimmed; REFUSES a patient's login holding the same
  address; REFUSES a patient's login when no staff deletion matches at all;
  REFUSES an id re-created as a live users row; REFUSES an identity that now
  holds a different address; REFUSES one already gone from auth; does NOT see
  another tenant's deletion, with that tenant's own successful reclaim as the
  positive control; returns null on an empty address.

NEGATIVE ARM PROVEN BY SUBSTITUTION: swapping the closed set for the naive
"no users row therefore an orphan" predicate reddened
"REFUSES a patient's login when NO staff deletion matches at all" -
`AssertionError: expected '9522bfeb-...' to be null`, the patient's auth id
returned where null was required. Restoring it returned 9/9.

AND IT NAMED WHICH TEST HAS THE TEETH: the OTHER patient test still passed under
the naive predicate, because the staff candidate happened to sort first. A single
"a patient is refused" test would have been green against the escalation. The
decoy-removed variant is the one that proves it.

=== WHAT IS NOT PROVEN WITHOUT A SCREEN, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED ===
GoTrue is injected, not real: db-tests.yml captures DATABASE_URL and
deliberately NOT the Supabase URL or service-role key - its own comment says so -
so no DB-gated suite can call admin.auth.admin.*. deleteStaffMember cannot be
driven end to end for the same reason: it re-authenticates the actor's password
against GoTrue first. The end-to-end loop - delete, re-invite the same address,
sign in - is Ivan's, and it is what closes this card.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-28 ON IVAN'S SIX-STEP RUN, ON THE DEPLOYED BUILD. ===
HIS RESULT, QUOTED: "confirmed. The invite, delete, re-invite with the same
address and sign-in all succeeded on the deployed build."

STEPS 4 AND 5 ARE THE PROVING ARMS AND THEY PROVED DIFFERENT THINGS:
  4  THE RE-INVITE OF THE SAME ADDRESS SUCCEEDED. Before this card that was
     refused permanently, with no path in the product to clear it - the orphaned
     auth identity held the address forever and the one case the delete exists
     for, a mistyped or wrong-role invite, was exactly the case it broke. This
     arm proves the identity was FOUND and reclaimed.
  5  THE SIGN-IN SUCCEEDED with the password issued by that re-invite. This arm
     proves the reclaimed identity was made USABLE. It is a separate arm because
     a build that passed 4 and failed 5 would look like a success on the Equipa
     screen and lock the invited person out - the row created, the password not
     reset, nobody able to get in. Worse than the refusal it replaced, because it
     looks like it worked.

Steps 1, 2, 3 and 6 are setup and cleanup and can fail for ordinary reasons that
say nothing about this card. They did not.

THIS IS THE HALF NO TEST COULD REACH. reclaim.db.test.ts proves the SELECTION
against real Postgres, including the refusal that keeps a portal patient's
identity out of the candidate set. GoTrue was injected there because db-tests.yml
captures DATABASE_URL and deliberately not the Supabase URL or service-role key,
and deleteStaffMember re-authenticates the actor's password against GoTrue before
it will delete anything. The end-to-end loop was therefore always going to be a
person on a screen, and it has now been run.

FINDING 1 OF THIS CARD REMAINS CORRECT AND UNTOUCHED: the delete still refuses an
account with any audit activity, and DEACTIVATE is still the designed path for an
account with history.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-19 while working out how to delete the SEC-02 test fixture. Both halves were read from the source rather than tried against production, which no terminal may touch.

=== FINDING 1: THE DELETE WILL REFUSE THIS FIXTURE, AND PROBABLY MOST REAL ONES ===
deleteStaffMember (apps/web/lib/admin/staff.ts) carries a linked-records guard that refuses when the user has ANY appointment, clinical record, note, analytics event OR AUDIT ROW - counted as auditLog.actorUserId = the target.

THE SEC-02 SITTING ITSELF CREATED SUCH A ROW. Step 3 was the fixture changing its own password, and changeOwnPasswordAction writes an audit entry with actorUserId = the fixture. So the account is now `has_activity` and Equipa will refuse to delete it.

THAT GUARD IS CORRECT AND IS NOT THE DEFECT. Its own comment states the intent: an established therapist is never destroyed, only an activity-free account such as a mistyped invite. Audit rows must not vanish because somebody deleted the actor. The designed alternative is DEACTIVATE, and deactivation genuinely neutralises the account at the app layer: custom_access_token_hook selects the staff branch `WHERE u.id = ... AND u.is_active = true`, so an inactive user gets no tenant_id and no user_role claim, getRequestContext() returns null, and every route fails closed to /login.

=== FINDING 2: THE DEFECT. DELETE LEAVES THE AUTH USER BEHIND. ===
deleteStaffMember removes therapist_services, availability_templates, time_off and the public.users row. It NEVER calls admin.auth.admin.deleteUser - there is no createSupabaseAdminClient in the file at all. The auth.users row survives the delete.

THE USER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT THE SCARY ONE, AND IT IS WORSE THAN IT SOUNDS. The orphan cannot USE the platform - no staff row means no claims, and the app fails closed. What it can do is HOLD THE ADDRESS FOREVER. inviteStaff pre-checks public.users, which is now empty, so it proceeds; createUser then fails on the surviving auth user and the invite dies as `auth_email_taken`. Delete a mistyped invite, correct the typo, re-invite the same person - REFUSED, permanently, with no path in the product to clear it.

THE ONE CASE THE DELETE IS FOR - a mistyped invite - IS EXACTLY THE CASE IT BREAKS. That is why this is worth fixing rather than documenting.

NOT DIAGNOSED FURTHER, and the next session should not assume: whether provisionStaffUser's own rollback path (it deletes the auth user when the users insert fails) is the right shape to reuse here, and what should happen if the auth deletion fails after the row is gone. A delete that half-succeeds is worse than one that refuses.

=== THE SEC-02 FIXTURE: THE OWNER'S ROUTE, AND IT IS HIS TO RUN ===
A staff row and an auth user in production are a production write and a data deletion. Standing rules 1, 2 and 12: this terminal logs it and blocks, and never executes it.
  STEP A, in the product: Administracao > Equipa > the fixture > deactivate. Expect DELETE to be refused with `has_activity` per finding 1; deactivate is the designed path for an account with history and it closes the app-layer door immediately.
  STEP B, in the Supabase dashboard: Authentication > Users > chris+rotationtest@dlvlogistics.com > delete. THIS is the step that actually retires the credential, and nothing in the product performs it today - which is finding 2.
  Doing B without A leaves a staff row whose login is gone; doing A without B leaves a live credential. Both, in that order.

URGENCY, honestly: LOW. The fixture is a plus-tagged address on the owner's own domain, its password is known only to him, and with the staff row deactivated it cannot reach anything. It is untidy rather than dangerous. The DEFECT behind it is the part worth scheduling.

=== THE QUESTION, AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS NOT NEEDED IN THE END ===
BLUE, 2026-08-28, under the standing constraint that this terminal authors no
migration: migration files are PURPLE's lane and the migration head belongs to
the import.

THE FIX SHIPPED WITHOUT ONE. Two routes that were considered would each have
needed a migration, and both are recorded so a future session meets the decision
instead of making it again.

ROUTE A, REJECTED - a table recording deleted staff identities BY ADDRESS, so a
re-invite could look the address up directly. The statement would have been:

  CREATE TABLE public.staff_auth_orphans (
    id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    tenant_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    auth_user_id uuid NOT NULL,
    email       citext NOT NULL,
    deleted_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (tenant_id, auth_user_id)
  );

NOT NEEDED, and it is worse than what shipped even if it were free: it stores an
EMAIL ADDRESS, which is PII, in a new table purely to make a lookup convenient -
against rule 7's direction of travel, and against the reason audit metadata is
PII-free today. The audit log already holds the id, and GoTrue already holds the
address; joining them at the moment of need costs one read per candidate and
stores nothing new.

ROUTE B, REJECTED - read auth.users directly to find the identity by address:

  GRANT SELECT ON auth.users TO service_role;

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, against a live Supabase Postgres:
  as postgres     : select count(*) from auth.users -> 11
  as service_role : ERROR: permission denied for table users
                    HINT: Grant the required privileges ... GRANT SELECT ON
                    auth.users TO service_role;
So the app's own role cannot read auth.users without that grant. Rejected twice
over: it is a migration, and it widens service_role's reach over the auth schema
permanently to save one bounded loop.

NEITHER IS PROPOSED. They are here so the next reader knows both were weighed and
why the shipped shape needs neither.

=== THE STEPS IVAN RUNS ON SCREEN. GoTrue CANNOT BE DRIVEN FROM CI. ===
db-tests.yml captures DATABASE_URL and deliberately NOT the Supabase URL or the
service-role key - its own comment says so - so no DB-gated suite can call
admin.auth.admin.*. deleteStaffMember cannot be driven end to end for the same
reason: it re-authenticates the actor's password against GoTrue before it will
delete anything. Everything that can be proven without a screen is proven; this
is what is left, and it is five steps in Administracao > Equipa.

USE A THROWAWAY ADDRESS ON A DOMAIN YOU CONTROL - a plus-tag on your own is
ideal. It becomes a real Supabase auth identity and it is deleted at the end.

  1. INVITE the throwaway address as a therapist. Note the temporary password.
     RIGHT: the invite succeeds and the person appears in Equipa.
     WRONG: any refusal at all - that is a different defect and this test cannot
            start.

  2. DELETE that staff member. It has no activity yet, so the has_activity guard
     does not fire.
     RIGHT: it is removed from Equipa.
     WRONG: refused with has_activity. If that happens the account did something
            between steps 1 and 2; start again with a fresh address.

  3. INVITE THE SAME ADDRESS AGAIN, as any role. Note the new temporary password.

  4. *** PROVING ARM. *** The invite must SUCCEED.
     RIGHT: it succeeds and the person is back in Equipa.
     WRONG: it fails saying the email is already registered. That is the defect
            unfixed - the orphaned auth identity was not reclaimed - and it is
            exactly what happened before this card. Stop and report that.

  5. *** PROVING ARM. *** SIGN IN as that address with the password from step 3,
     in a private window.
     RIGHT: sign-in succeeds and lands on the change-password screen (SEC-02:
            the account is marked mustSetPassword).
     WRONG: the password from step 3 is rejected. That means the row was created
            but the RECLAIMED IDENTITY'S PASSWORD WAS NOT RESET, so the account
            exists and nobody can get into it - a worse state than the refusal
            it replaced, because it looks like it worked.

  6. DELETE it again, to leave nothing behind. Expect the same has_activity guard
     if you completed a password change in step 5; if so, DEACTIVATE instead,
     which is the designed path for an account with history.

STEPS 4 AND 5 ARE THE PROVING ARMS AND THEY PROVE DIFFERENT THINGS. Step 4 proves
the identity was FOUND and reclaimed; step 5 proves it was made USABLE. A build
that passed 4 and failed 5 would look like a success on the Equipa screen and
lock the invited person out - which is why the sign-in is a step and not an
afterthought.

STEPS 1, 2, 3 AND 6 ARE SETUP AND CLEANUP. They can fail for ordinary reasons
that say nothing about this card.

cards.title: Three payment/invoicing sandbox suites are deliberately skipped pending vendor credentials, and nothing will remind anyone to un-skip them when the keys arrive
cards.notes:
SPLIT OUT OF ACC-skippable-suites-unguarded when that card closed 2026-08-19. It is the one residual the RECON-02 guard cannot cover, and it is a MEMORY problem rather than a guard problem.

THE THREE SUITES, each a bare `describe.skip` with its reason written beside it:
  apps/web/lib/integrations/ifthenpay/inngest/functions.test.ts - sandbox happy-path, pending the owner-provisioned IfThenPay sandbox keys (clinic PT entity).
  apps/web/lib/integrations/invoicexpress/inngest/functions.test.ts - pending the InvoiceXpress sandbox key AND the VAT-23% sign-off (#107).
  apps/web/lib/integrations/stripe/inngest/functions.test.ts - pending the Stripe secret key AND the same VAT sign-off.

THEY ARE CORRECTLY SKIPPED AND MUST STAY SO. Each is the only test in its file that would touch a live vendor sandbox, and each carries the standing instruction: do NOT un-skip without the keys in env, the rule is do not hit the live sandbox. Un-skipping early does not fail loudly - it sends real requests to a payment provider.

WHY NO GUARD CAN HELP, which is the whole reason this is a card. A check would have to redden on "skipped AND the credentials now exist", and the credentials are an env fact in a deployment this repo cannot read. Keying on the skip alone would redden three suites that are correct today, every run, forever - the fastest way to get a guard switched off.

SO THE TRIGGER IS AN EVENT, NOT A CHECK: the moment any of those vendor credentials is provisioned, un-skip that suite and run it once. Whoever provisions the key is the person who knows; this card exists so the knowledge is written down somewhere that is not three separate file comments.

LOW PRIORITY BECAUSE NOTHING IS AT RISK TODAY. No payment integration is live, so an unrun sandbox test protects nothing yet. It becomes real the day invoicing or payments are switched on, and on that day this is a prerequisite rather than a nicety.

cards.title: Guest portal: the clinic phones render as an unattributed strip of four numbers, and the service list ignores which clinic the visitor picked

evidence.ref:
OWNER OBSERVATION ON DEPLOYED PRODUCTION, WF-03 SITTING 2026-08-19, at main sha d69270a. Four items queued by the to-do sweep, THREE OBSERVED, ONE NOT RUN. Items 1, 2 and 3 PASS. Item 4 (the AI-02 unmapped-keys banner) was NOT observed and is recorded as NOT RUN rather than as a pass - no record with unmapped keys exists yet, so there was nothing to look at. AI-02 stays open on its own card.

ITEM 1 PASS. /marcacao step 1 shows the four numbers GROUPED UNDER THEIR CLINIC'S NAME, and the owner confirmed the blocks match what osteojp.pt/contactos publishes. That external cross-check is worth more than the internal one this card shipped with: the test proves the component renders lib/clinics.ts, and the sitting proves lib/clinics.ts agrees with the number a patient would otherwise find on the public site. Neither half proves the other.

ITEM 2 PASS. The guest service list DIFFERS BY CLINIC and each list matches what Administracao > Servicos shows as "Oferecido aqui" for that clinic. The offered-only-where-priced rule (W8-01a) now reaches the public form.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE THE CARD WARNED ABOUT IS NOW OWNED BY A PERSON. The sitting's item 2 said in as many words that a service with no active price row at a clinic will be ABSENT from the public form, that no terminal can read production data to check the grid is complete, and that the fix for anything missing is a price row rather than a code change. RODICA CONFIRMED THE PRICE GRID AND OWNS IT GOING FORWARD. That is the half no test on this board could ever have supplied - the code is correct about what the config MEANS, and only a person can say whether the config is TRUE.

BUILD HALF, unchanged: PR #950 MERGED, squashed to 7426254, every required check green. Part 1 groups the numbers under clinics.phone_label and leaves the shared ClinicPhones component alone, because on the login screen and the seven error boundaries the surface has no identity and narrowing it would leak which clinic a patient belongs to. Part 2 derives locationIds from active service_location_prices rows in apps/api/app/api/v1/booking/guest/catalog/route.ts; six assertions including the location_id ceiling, the inactive-clinic case and the priced-nowhere case, and the negative arm (restoring the old predicate) fails three. The UI filter in GuestBookingForm was already correct and untouched - the defect was entirely in what the API put in the field it was filtering on.

cards.notes:
TWO OWNER RULINGS, 2026-08-19, both on /marcacao.

=== PART 1: THE PHONE NUMBERS. Ruled: structured contact information. ===
The four clinic numbers rendered as a bare wrapped row of green links attributed to nobody. A visitor who wants to ring Castelo Branco could not tell which two of the four reach it - so the affordance that exists precisely for somebody giving up on the form was unusable at that moment.

WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM, as asked, and the halt condition did NOT trigger: they are HARDCODED STATIC DATA in apps/portal/lib/clinics.ts, not per-clinic database rows. CLINIC_CONTACTS pairs each clinic with its own numbers - Linda-a-Velha 969 472 111 / 214 191 988, Castelo Branco 969 877 553 / 272 328 221 - so EVERY number is attributable from data and nothing had to be guessed. Source of record is osteojp.pt/contactos; the values are static and change on redeploy. The strip existed because the page used ALL_CLINIC_PHONES, a deliberate FLATTENING of that structure which drops the attribution.

NO NEW COPY WAS AUTHORED. The heading is clinics.phone_label ("Telefone" / "Phone"), which already existed; the clinic names and the numbers are both data. Structuring data already on the screen is presentation, not copy - the same reasoning ClinicPhones records for itself.

THE SHARED ClinicPhones COMPONENT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED. It renders the flat list on the login screen and on seven error boundaries, where the surface has no identity to attach numbers to and where narrowing would leak which clinic a patient belongs to. /marcacao had its OWN inline copy of the strip, so the fix is local: one screen changed, not eight.

=== PART 2: SERVICES FILTERED BY CLINIC. Ruled: only what that clinic offers. ===
THE UI FILTER WAS ALREADY CORRECT. GuestBookingForm computes `servicesHere` = services whose locationIds include the chosen clinic. The defect was entirely in what the API put IN locationIds, so the filter was passing everything.

THE DISCREPANCY, REPORTED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY PICKING - and it is a THREE-way disagreement, not two:
  1. Administracao > Servicos derives "Oferecido aqui" from OFFERED-ONLY-WHERE-PRICED (W8-01a): a service is offered at a location IFF an active service_location_prices row exists there. The admin page iterates ALL active locations and ignores services.location_id entirely.
  2. The GUEST CATALOG derived it from services.location_id, null meaning "all locations". That column SCOPES a service to a clinic; it says nothing about whether the clinic offers it. Turning a service off at one clinic in Servicos writes a price row and never touches it, so the two diverge on the first such action - exactly as observed with Drenagem Linfatica.
  3. The STAFF booking read (lib/scheduling/data.ts) filters services by `isActive` ALONE, with no location predicate at all. Staff still see every active service at every clinic. NOT CHANGED HERE - the ruling was about the guest flow, and changing what reception can book is a different decision with a different blast radius. Worth the owner knowing it is now the odd one out.

THERE IS NO SEPARATE "OFFERED" FLAG TO DISAGREE WITH THE PRICE FIELDS. Offered IS the existence of an active price row; is_active on that row is the switch and price_cents is the value. Single-sourced, so the "flag vs price" disagreement the dispatch guarded against does not exist. The disagreement that DOES exist is the one above, and the ruling names the admin config as the authority, which resolves it.

THE IMPLEMENTATION INTERSECTS TWO THINGS RATHER THAN REPLACING ONE WITH THE OTHER, and that is the one judgement call worth reading. services.location_id is kept as a CEILING: a service scoped to one clinic cannot surface at another whatever a stray price row says, while the price grid decides where it is actually offered. Neither field alone is right - the scope ignores what the clinic configured, and the grid alone would let a clinic-specific service appear where it was never meant to. Pinned by its own test.

NO NEW PUBLIC SURFACE (MN-27, MN-28 unchanged). The response keeps exactly the keys it had; locationIds already existed. What changed is which locations land in it. A price row's EXISTENCE is read, its VALUE never leaves the route, and a test asserts the payload matches no price-shaped string.

THE OPERATIONAL RISK, STATED BECAUSE NO TEST CAN COVER IT: the public catalog is now only as complete as the price grid. A service with no active price row anywhere will not appear on the public form at all. That is CONSISTENT with what the admin screen already says about such a service - "Nao oferecido aqui" at every clinic - but it is a live, patient-visible consequence of production data this terminal cannot read. It is the first thing to check at the sitting.

cards.title: Staff booking reads services by isActive alone, with no location predicate - the odd one out beside the guest catalog and Administracao > Servicos. RECON ONLY, no code change

evidence.ref:
CLOSED BY-DESIGN 2026-08-19. IVAN RULING, OPTION B: staff booking stays UNRESTRICTED. It offers every active service at every clinic, with no location predicate and no pricing predicate. NO CODE CHANGE.

WHAT THIS SETTLES, stated so the divergence is never re-opened as a bug: apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts:291-293 reads services on services.isActive alone, while the guest catalog (apps/api/app/api/v1/booking/guest/catalog/route.ts:142-149) and the "Oferecido aqui" badge (apps/web/lib/admin/services.ts:318-323) both derive from active service_location_prices rows. THE THREE READERS ARE NOW INTENTIONALLY DIFFERENT, not accidentally so.

THE REASONING THE RULING RESTS ON, recorded because the next reader will find the asymmetry and assume it is a defect: reception books exceptions. A price row is a BILLING fact, and letting it govern what staff MAY BOOK would mean an unpriced service becomes unbookable at the front desk - which is a worse failure than an inconsistency between two screens, because it blocks real clinical work over a config gap.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is accepted rather than unnoticed: after GUEST-08 the same configuration produces two different answers on two screens. A service unpriced at a clinic is ABSENT from the public form and PRESENT on reception's. That is now by design.

THE RECON THIS CARD ASKED FOR IS NOT PERFORMED, deliberately. The card scoped a consumer enumeration, a numbered blast radius and an options paper, all of which existed only to inform this decision. The decision is made, so the recon has no consumer. The pack asymmetry noted while carding it (servicePacks carries locationId in the same query, services does not) is left unexamined and is NOT covered by this ruling - if it ever matters it needs its own card.

cards.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-19, DERIVED FROM MAIN AT d69270a RATHER THAN FROM A REPORT. Every line below was read out of the committed files named, this session.

=== THE THREE READERS, AND THE ONE THAT DISAGREES ===
apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts:291-293, inside fetchStableAgendaRef, the reference data behind the STAFF booking form:
    .from(services).where(eq(services.isActive, true)).orderBy(asc(services.name))
ONE predicate. isActive. NO location predicate of any kind.

apps/api/app/api/v1/booking/guest/catalog/route.ts:142-149, the PUBLIC guest catalog, as of GUEST-08 (#950, 7426254): locationIds are derived from ACTIVE service_location_prices rows. Offered-only-where-priced.

apps/web/lib/admin/services.ts:318-323, the "Oferecido aqui" badge on Administracao > Servicos: the same active service_location_prices rows.

TWO OF THE THREE AGREE, AND THE STAFF FORM IS THE THIRD. The rule the clinic configures in Servicos, and that a patient now meets on /marcacao, does not reach the screen reception books on.

=== WHY THIS IS A CARD AND NOT A FIX ===
IT IS NOT SELF-EVIDENTLY A DEFECT, and that is the point. There is a real reading in which staff SHOULD see every active service regardless of clinic: reception books exceptions, a therapist may deliver something unpriced at that site, and a price row is a BILLING fact that may or may not be intended to govern what staff may book. The guest form and the staff form have different audiences and could legitimately have different rules. GUEST-08 did not decide this question, and nothing on the board has.

WHAT MAKES IT WORTH RECORDING ANYWAY: after GUEST-08 the divergence became OBSERVABLE. A service unpriced at Castelo Branco is now absent from the public form and present on reception's - so the same configuration produces two different answers on two screens, and no copy on either explains why. If that is intended it should be written down; if it is not, it is a defect with a blast radius nobody has measured.

=== SCOPE OF THIS CARD: READ-ONLY RECON. NO CODE CHANGE. ===
Deliverable is a written finding, and the decision is routed AFTERWARDS, not taken here.
  1. Enumerate every consumer of fetchStableAgendaRef's serviceRows and say what each does with the list - the booking form, the filters, anything else. A filter that includes inactive services on purpose (marcacoes-view.tsx already documents doing exactly that) is not the same consumer as a create form.
  2. State the blast radius in numbers, not adjectives: how many screens, which roles, and whether the same query also feeds a WRITE path. A read that only draws a dropdown is a different risk from one that decides what may be created.
  3. Note the pack asymmetry found while carding this: in the SAME query, servicePacks carries locationId (W8-01c) and services does not. Whether packs are actually filtered by it downstream is unread and belongs in the finding.
  4. Write the options with their consequences - leave as is and document the divergence; filter staff by the same service_location_prices rule; filter only the create path and leave the filters whole; add an explicit per-service flag distinct from price. Recommend one. DO NOT IMPLEMENT.
  5. The product question - may reception book a service that is not priced at that clinic - is OWNER-CONFIRMABLE and is not answered by this card or by any terminal. Standing rule 15.

CLOSES ON: the finding committed under docs/recon/, with the consumer enumeration and the numbered blast radius, and the product question logged for the owner. Not on a code change.

cards.title: Criterion F, the population that actually passes falsely: toBeVisible/toContainText on a non-identity locator over the shared seeded database. Never swept

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19. Enumeration at docs/recon/ACC-visibility-assertions-unswept.md, fix in apps/web/e2e/scheduling.spec.ts.

494 ASSERTIONS -> 57 UPPER BOUND -> ONE REAL CASE. toBeVisible, toBeHidden, toContainText and toHaveText across 60 spec files in apps/web/e2e. The card demanded the honest number with its method and forbade reporting an alarming upper bound as the finding: 57 is the bound, ONE is the finding.

EVERY ASSERTION IS ACCOUNTED FOR AND THE EQUALITY IS ASSERTED. The classifier is comment-stripped, multi-line aware, resolves one level of variable indirection, and its buckets SUM TO 494. Without that check the residue could hide in a parsing gap and the headline would be an artefact of the regex rather than a fact about the suite - which is exactly the mistake the previous card's triage made when it scanned E2E specs against themselves.

THE BUCKETS: 46 absence assertions (the SAFE direction - contamination makes these FAIL); 48 identity-bearing locators; 203 chrome/testid/label, where no database row can conjure a button or a dialog; 32 scoped to a container the test opened; 91 text literals on a DETAIL page showing ONE subject; 17 with no route resolved, unclassified and NOT cleared; 57 unscoped text literals on a LIST page.

THE 57 READ INDIVIDUALLY: ~11 are TOASTS, which the test's own action raises and no row can; ~14 are static page chrome and stat LABELS; ~24 are scoped through a local helper the classifier could not follow; ~7 are parser artefacts, reported rather than silently dropped.

THE ONE REAL CASE, scheduling.spec.ts:412. page.getByText("Sem nota").first() on /marcacoes for one day. THE DAY IS NOT EXCLUSIVE: "a newly created appointment persists as scheduled / pendente (W3-01)" books MARIA on the same RUN_DAY_BASE + 13, so the list holds two rows and .first() was choosing between them.

IT WAS SAFE FOR A REASON THAT LIVES OUTSIDE THE ASSERTION, which is the finding rather than the fix. marcacoes-view.tsx:306 gates the chip on status === "completed" && !appt.hasNote, and maria's stays scheduled. The assertion depended on a render rule in ANOTHER FILE rather than on anything it stated. Widen that rule and .first() matches maria's row while ana's status update has silently failed - the compensating error, where our own write fails, a foreign row satisfies the check, and the suite reports a pass.

THE FIX uses the repo's own idiom, page.locator(".glass-card", { hasText }), PROVEN ON THIS EXACT ROUTE by agenda-hover.spec.ts:49-51 and notes-unification.spec.ts:60-61, both green in CI - chosen rather than invented. PLUS A NEGATIVE ARM asserting maria's row does NOT carry the chip, which states the per-row rule the test was borrowing. The render condition was read at the render site before the arm was written, not inferred from a unit test about a different component.

NOT COVERED, said rather than implied: apps/portal/e2e and apps/api were not swept - this is apps/web/e2e only, where the shared seeded database and the cross-spec contamination risk live. The 17 unresolved-route assertions are unclassified, not cleared.

Gates: pnpm lint 0 errors, pnpm typecheck 11/11. Playwright still collects scheduling.spec.ts (43 tests across its projects, verified with --list). E2E cannot run locally; the suite runs in CI on this PR.

=== THE FIRST VERSION OF THE FIX WAS WRONG, AND CI CAUGHT IT VIA THE NEGATIVE ARM ===
Run 32321417051, shard 3, job 96284206608. It used page.locator(".glass-card", { hasText }), copied from agenda-hover.spec.ts and notes-unification.spec.ts, which do use that selector on this route. BUT ON THIS PAGE .glass-card IS ALSO THE OUTER GlassPanel WRAPPING THE WHOLE LIST - marcacoes-view.tsx:521 says so in as many words. Filtering it by a patient name matched THE PANEL, which contains every row. The scoped locator was the whole list wearing one row's name.

THE POSITIVE ASSERTION STILL PASSED, because ana's chip sits inside that panel. A locator that scoped NOTHING looked exactly like a fix and would have shipped as one. THE NEGATIVE ARM IS THE ONLY REASON ANYONE KNOWS: maria's row reported the chip too, because it was the same element.

TWO LESSONS, and the second generalises. VERIFYING THAT A SELECTOR IS USED ON A ROUTE IS NOT VERIFYING THAT IT IDENTIFIES WHAT YOU THINK - the precedent was real and my reading of it was wrong, because those specs use .glass-card to reach something row-unique INSIDE the match, which tolerates the match being the panel. And A SCOPING CHANGE NEEDS A NEGATIVE ARM OR IT CANNOT TELL REAL SCOPING FROM FAKE SCOPING: the positive assertion is satisfied either way, which makes it the wrong instrument for checking its own premise.

CORRECTED to [data-appointment-id], the actual row wrapper at marcacoes-view.tsx:208, read at the render site rather than inferred from another spec's usage.

cards.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-19 OUT OF ACC-identity-blind-assertions, which is closed. Full reasoning in docs/recon/ACC-identity-blind-assertions.md section 4.

=== WHY THE FIRST SWEEP LOOKED AT THE WRONG POPULATION ===
ACC-identity-blind-assertions swept 170 toHaveCount(N) assertions. It was a good sweep and it produced the rule this card inherits. But toHaveCount was chosen because it is GREPPABLE, not because it is where the risk concentrates, and the two are not the same thing.

AN EXACT COUNT SELF-CORRECTS. A row another spec created usually pushes toHaveCount(1) to 2 and the assertion FAILS - loud, and harmless. It can only pass falsely through a COMPENSATING ERROR: your own write silently fails at the same moment a foreign row is present. Real, and rare - one instance found across the whole 170 (therapist-blocks.spec.ts, fixed).

THE POPULATION THAT PASSES FALSELY AS ITS ORDINARY BEHAVIOUR IS UNSWEPT:
  await expect(page.getByText("Bloqueio pontual")).toBeVisible();
  await expect(list).toContainText("Confirmada");
These pass on ANY matching row - yours, another spec's, or the seed's - and fail only when NOTHING matches. CONTAMINATION MAKES THEM MORE LIKELY TO PASS, not less. That is the exact inverse of the direction the first card's absence-assertion argument relies on, so that argument does not transfer to this population and must not be reused on it.

=== SCOPE ===
  1. Enumerate toBeVisible, toBeHidden, toContainText and toHaveText across apps/web/e2e, and split by whether the LOCATOR carries identity (a run-unique name, a RUN_DAY_BASE-derived date, a randomUUID fixture) or only shared vocabulary (a status label, a service name, a type badge, a time).
  2. THE SPLIT THAT MATTERS IS NOT PRESENCE-VERSUS-ABSENCE HERE. toBeHidden and toHaveCount(0) are the safe direction for counts; for visibility the safe direction is different, because an absence assertion on a shared locator FAILS when another spec's row is present, which is a flake rather than a false proof. Say which direction each case is wrong in rather than reusing the count taxonomy.
  3. Report the honest number with its method, exactly as the first card did, and DO NOT report an alarming upper bound as if it were the finding.
  4. Fix only cases where a foreign row can satisfy the assertion IN PLACE OF the subject. Leave the rest carded.

=== THE RULE THIS INHERITS, unchanged and worth restating in full ===
When writing an assertion against the shared seeded database, ask: COULD A ROW THIS TEST DID NOT CREATE SATISFY IT? If yes, add identity - a patient name, a run-unique id, a RUN_DAY_BASE-derived date. Never a time, a status, a service name, a date or a bare count alone.

WORKED EXAMPLE ALREADY IN THE REPO, and it is the shape to copy: therapist-blocks.spec.ts now filters the list row by its own run-scoped date and asserts the badge INSIDE that row. The row proves the block is ours; the badge proves it is the mode we asked for. One assertion answering one question each, instead of one count answering neither.

CLOSES ON: the enumeration committed under docs/recon/ with its method stated, every fixed case carrying a negative arm, and every unfixed case carrying the reason it is safe.

cards.title: Network-dependent setup steps have no timeout of their own, so a hang is killed by the JOB ceiling with no cause printed. Four occurrences, two causes, two shards killed in one day

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-19, and the card as first written was too narrow. It argued from ONE occurrence and named the Supabase retry as the problem. Measuring properly changed both the diagnosis and the fix.

=== THE MEASUREMENT, 23 REAL SHARD RUNS (docs-only skip runs excluded) ===
  median 7.6 min, fastest 6.7, and 17 of the 23 sit between 6.7 and 8.5.
  outliers: 11.1, 11.2, 11.6, 14.0, 17.8, 24.2.
THE TESTS ARE NOT SLOW. Playwright itself takes 241-290s across shards. Every
outlier is SETUP, and the job ceiling was 25 minutes against a surviving maximum
of 24.2 - FORTY-EIGHT SECONDS OF MARGIN.

=== THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG BY GENERALISING FROM ONE SAMPLE ===
I sampled the 24.2-minute outlier, found the Supabase retry, and reported that
every long run was Supabase. The very next kill was a DIFFERENT STEP. Recorded
because the error is the interesting part: one sample and a plausible mechanism
read exactly like a diagnosis.

=== FOUR OCCURRENCES, TWO STEPS, AND THE SECOND STEP IS THE ONE NOBODY HAD SEEN ===
  1+2. supabase/setup-cli, release-CDN 503 and a port collision - already carded and fixed.
  3. Start Supabase hung ~22 min on its FIRST attempt (run 32263942836 job 96103690200). The retry then SUCCEEDED, Playwright started at 14:51:02Z, and the ceiling expired 0.7s later.
  4. Install Playwright Chromium hung on apt (runs 32269074242 jobs 96120745688 and 96129595818, TWICE IN A ROW on the same shard). Both stopped dead on the identical line:
       Get:5 https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble-security InRelease [126 kB]
     then 24 minutes of total silence. Note the host: the surrounding lines fetch from azure.archive.ubuntu.com, the runner's local mirror, and Get:4/Get:5 go to archive.ubuntu.com instead. The non-mirror host is what hangs.

=== THE REAL GENERALISATION, WHICH IS BROADER THAN THE CARD'S TITLE WAS ===
SEVERAL SETUP STEPS DEPEND ON EXTERNAL NETWORKS AND NONE HAD A TIMEOUT OF ITS
OWN. The job ceiling was the only backstop, and because a hang emits NO ERROR,
it surfaced as a bare "The operation was canceled" with the cause twenty-four
minutes earlier in the log. Both kills on 2026-08-19 were read as regressions in
the change under test before the log was opened - once by the terminal that
wrote this card.

=== WHAT WAS BUILT ===
1. PER-STEP timeout-minutes on every network-dependent step, each derived from
   measured healthy durations rather than guessed: install deps 10m (normal 11-12s),
   Playwright install 16m (normal 12s / 47s / 282s), Supabase CLI 6m (3s),
   Supabase start 12m (77-93s), migrations 8m (30-31s).
2. AN INNER 'timeout' ON EACH ATTEMPT, which is the load-bearing part. A step
   killed by timeout-minutes is DEAD and cannot retry itself; only an inner
   timeout hands control back so a retry is possible at all. 420s per Playwright
   attempt (1.5x the slowest healthy 282s), 300s per supabase start attempt (3x
   the normal 93s).
3. THE PLAYWRIGHT INSTALL NOW RETRIES ONCE, matching the Supabase house style:
   loud ::warning:: when a retry rescues the run so it stays visible in the
   checks UI, ::error:: naming infrastructure when both attempts fail, plus apt
   lock-holder and browser-cache diagnostics between the attempts.
4. THE JOB CEILING 25 -> 35, and ONLY safe because of 1 and 2. A single hung step
   now fails at its own budget of at most 16 minutes, leaving 19 for a run that
   normally needs 7. Two independent hangs would still reach the ceiling, which
   has never been observed and keeps the backstop able to fire.

=== A DEFECT IN THE FIX ITSELF, FOUND BY TESTING IT RATHER THAN READING IT ===
The retry first captured the exit code as 'if install_browsers; then exit 0; fi'
followed by 'rc=$?'. In bash '$?' after 'fi' is the status of the IF STATEMENT,
which is 0 when no branch ran - so EVERY failure would have reported "exited 0
(not a timeout)". One line collapsing four outcomes onto the harmless-looking
one, in the diagnostic whose whole job is to tell them apart. Section 1.3, inside
the fix for a section 1.3 problem. Verified in a shell, then rewritten to capture
directly.

BEHAVIOURAL PROOF, four cases against the script extracted from the committed
YAML with the install stubbed: timeout-then-success exits 0 with the timeout
warning; timeout-then-timeout exits 1 naming exit 124; hardfail(7)-then-success
exits 0 and correctly says "exited 7 (not a timeout)"; clean success exits 0
silently. The third case is the one the bug would have destroyed.

Gates: the workflow YAML parses, and both edited shell bodies pass bash -n.

=== THE FIRST PUSH OF THIS FIX FAILED ON CI, AND THE FAILURE IS THE BEST EVIDENCE IN THE CARD ===
Run 32277423282. THE TIMEOUT WORKED: shard 1 hung on the same apt line at
16:43:37 and was cut off at 16:50:03 with exit 124 - seven minutes instead of
twenty-four, and shard 3 passed clean in 6m49s. THE RETRY DID NOT RUN.

WHY: GitHub executes `run:` blocks as `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`,
and the script's own `set -uo pipefail` does NOT remove that injected `-e`. The
bare `install_browsers` call aborted the step the instant it returned non-zero,
so the retry below it was unreachable. Shards 1 and 2 both died this way.

THIS IS THE SECOND WRONG FORM IN THE SAME FIVE LINES, and the pair is worth
keeping because each looks obviously correct and fails in a different direction:
  `if cmd; then exit 0; fi` then `rc=$?`   ->  rc is ALWAYS 0 ($? is the IF
      statement's status), so every failure reports "exited 0 (not a timeout)".
  `cmd` then `rc=$?`                        ->  under the injected -e the script
      never reaches the retry at all.
  `rc=0; cmd || rc=$?`                      ->  correct on both counts. Shipped.

THE SUPABASE STEP BESIDE IT SURVIVES THE SAME -e ONLY BY ACCIDENT OF POSITION:
its call sits inside an `if` CONDITION, where the shell suppresses -e. That is a
property of where it sits, not of how it was written, which is exactly why
copying its shape into a different position broke.

THE REAL LESSON IS ABOUT THE TEST, NOT THE SCRIPT. The first harness ran the
extracted script under a plain `bash` with no flags and passed all four cases -
against a script CI then killed. A harness that does not reproduce the runner's
shell flags is not testing the thing that runs. The harness now invokes
`bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`, verbatim.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, re-run correctly after a first attempt silently regressed zero
call sites and produced a meaningless pass: with both call sites reverted to the
bare form, timeout-then-success exits 124 and emits ZERO warnings - reproducing
the CI failure exactly. With the shipped form it exits 0 and emits the retry
warning. Five cases pass under the faithful harness, including hard-fail-then-
hard-fail correctly reporting "exited 7" rather than a timeout.

THE SUPABASE STEP'S CONTROL FLOW WAS VERIFIED SEPARATELY under the same flags
(if-condition then a final bare command): retry-succeeds exits 0 with one
warning, both-fail exits 1 with one warning, first-succeeds exits 0 silently. Its
flow is unchanged by this card - only `timeout 300` was added around each
invocation.

=== THE SECOND CI RUN PROVED THE -e FIX AND EXPOSED THE NEXT LAYER ===
Run 32278665484. The retry RAN this time (its diagnostics printed and the step
reported "Two attempts failed"), so the -e correction is confirmed on the runner
rather than only in a harness. It then failed for a new reason:

    E: Could not get lock /var/lib/apt/lists/lock. It is held by process 2427 (apt-get)

`timeout` signals the DIRECT child, which is pnpm. `--with-deps` runs apt-get
through sudo, and THAT GRANDCHILD SURVIVES the kill still holding the lock. The
first attempt was cut at exactly 420s and the retry died two seconds later. So a
retry after a timeout was guaranteed to fail, every time, until the orphan was
reaped. Fixed with --kill-after=30s plus a wait-then-TERM-then-KILL reap that
prefers waiting, because killing a package manager is a last resort.

=== AND THE DIAGNOSTIC I ADDED TO CATCH THIS LIED ABOUT IT ===
It printed the lsof header AND "(no apt locks held)" at 17:02:45, two seconds
before apt reported the lock WAS held by pid 2427. `lsof` exits non-zero when ANY
named file is merely unlocked, so `|| echo "(no apt locks held)"` fired on a
PARTIAL SUCCESS and asserted the opposite of the truth. One line mapping "lsof
could not examine everything" onto "there is nothing to examine" - in the
diagnostic whose entire job was to tell those apart. THIRD instance of section
1.3 inside this one fix. The fallback is gone: it now prints what lsof found and
an empty result means empty.

SIX CASES PASS under the faithful harness: timeout with apt clear, timeout with
an orphaned apt-get and the retry succeeding, timeout with an orphan and the
retry failing, hardfail-then-success, hardfail-then-hardfail, and clean success.

A HARNESS DEFECT WAS ALSO FOUND AND FIXED: BSD sed has no \s, so the stubbing
substitutions silently matched NOTHING and the real sudo and sleep ran. The
harness now stubs with shell FUNCTIONS, which cannot silently fail to apply.

cards.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-19 FROM A LIVE OCCURRENCE ON PR #957, timings read out of the job log rather than inferred.

=== THE OCCURRENCE, WITH ITS NUMBERS ===
Run 32263942836, E2E shard (3), job 96103690200.
  14:25:43Z  job starts
  14:48:51Z  "Start Supabase (lean stack)" emits its own retry warning, verbatim: "This run hit CI-supabase-cli-setup-flaky. The diagnostics below name the cause; do not dismiss them as noise."
  14:51:02Z  the retry has SUCCEEDED and Playwright starts
  14:51:02.97Z  "##[error]The operation was canceled."
  14:51:06Z  job ends. 25m23s elapsed against .github/workflows/e2e.yml timeout-minutes: 25.
ZERO TESTS RAN. Shards 1 and 2 on the same run passed in 8m19s and 7m33s.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT JUST ANOTHER INSTANCE OF CI-supabase-cli-setup-flaky ===
That card is SHIPPED, and correctly: its stated fix was to retry both Supabase steps and announce the retry rather than hide it. THE RETRY DID ITS JOB HERE. It fired, it printed its diagnostics, and it succeeded.

THE MITIGATION SUCCEEDED AND THE JOB FAILED ANYWAY, because the 25-minute budget was sized for the path where the flake does not happen. A retry that takes 23 minutes cannot fit inside a 25-minute job that also has to run a 4-minute suite. So the mitigation is only effective when the flake is CHEAP, and it is structurally unable to help in the case it was written for. Nothing on the shipped card says this, and nobody would find it by reading either the card or the workflow - it only shows up in the arithmetic of one real run.

=== WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A RE-RUN ===
It reproduces the exact habit that card names as the real cost: "a step that reddens at random trains people to re-run instead, which is exactly the reflex that lets a genuine red be dismissed." A red shard whose log says the retry SUCCEEDED is worse than one that says it failed, because the obvious reading - "the flake is handled, so this red is about my change" - is wrong. That is what happened here: the 25-minute duration against a 7-11 minute baseline was initially read as a regression in the change under test, and only the log settled it.

=== OPTIONS, none taken here ===
  1. RAISE timeout-minutes on the shard job so a retried Supabase start still leaves room for the suite. Cheapest, and the number should be derived from a measured worst-case start plus the slowest observed shard, not guessed.
  2. MOVE the Supabase start behind its own step budget so a slow start fails FAST and loudly as a start failure, rather than silently eating the suite's time and surfacing as a cancel with no test output.
  3. FAIL THE JOB EXPLICITLY when the retry path is taken and less than the slowest observed shard duration remains, with a message naming this card. Turns a confusing cancel into a stated cause.
Recommend 2 plus 3: raising the ceiling alone hides the signal and makes every future occurrence cost more wall-clock before it says anything.

CLOSES ON: a shard that hits the Supabase retry path and reports the cause in a form a reader cannot mistake for a failure of the change under test - proven by a log line, not by the absence of the problem.

cards.title: The E2E workflow argues its 35-minute ceiling is safe BECAUSE of per-step budgets, and the one step that actually overruns has none - so a bad runner destroys its own evidence
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while shepherding PR #1031. NOT ACTED ON: the fix is one line in
.github/workflows/e2e.yml but it changes CI for EVERY pull request, which is
outside the card that found it. Owner's call, with a recommended default below.

WHAT HAPPENED. E2E shard 1 on run 32857988428 ran 35m17s and died on the job
ceiling with a bare "The operation was canceled". It was NOT hung: four tests
were TIMING OUT at the 120s test timeout (playwright.config.ts:50) and retrying
twice each, which is where the 35 minutes went.

  admin-packs.spec.ts:13    2.1m x 3 attempts   (4.2s in the run 9 minutes earlier)
  admin-packs.spec.ts:65    2.1m x 3            (3.5s)
  admin-packs.spec.ts:110   2.1m x 3            (3.0s)
  agenda-blocked-time:93    4.0m x 3            (13.1s)

THE SAME 78 TESTS PASSED ON THE SAME BRANCH NINE MINUTES EARLIER (run 32857043721,
77 passed 1 flaky in 5.1m), and the re-run passed in 7m36s. A test that normally
finishes in 3 seconds taking over 120 is a degraded runner, not an assertion.

=========================================================================
THE DEFECT IS NOT THE SLOW RUNNER. IT IS THAT THE CANCELLATION DESTROYED THE
EVIDENCE, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT THE FILE CLAIMS IT FIXED.
=========================================================================
e2e.yml:88-107 argues the ceiling was raised 25 -> 35 and is "only safe to raise
BECAUSE of the per-step budgets below", and that "a single hung step now fails at
its own budget, at most 16 minutes". It then names the precise failure it is
preventing: "a hung step emits no error, so the job ends on a bare 'The operation
was canceled' with the real cause twenty minutes earlier in the log".

THAT IS WORD FOR WORD WHAT HAPPENED, because the budgets went on five SETUP steps
and not on the test step:
  10  Install dependencies
  16  Install Playwright Chromium
  12  Start Supabase (lean stack)
   8  Apply migrations + base seed
   5  Upload Playwright report
   -  Run Playwright E2E   <-- the step that overran

THE COST IS NOT WALL CLOCK, IT IS THE REPORT. Playwright prints its failure
summary at the END of a run, and step 21 (Upload Playwright report) never
executed - so there was no summary, no trace and no artifact. The cause had to be
reconstructed from a DIFFERENT run's log. LE-osteojp-e2e-debugging-doctrine says
read the Playwright artifact FIRST; this configuration can delete it.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: timeout-minutes: 16 on the Playwright step, matching the
Chromium install budget and the file's own "at most 16 minutes" claim. The
measured median shard is 7.6 minutes and the tests take 4-5, so 16 is more than
double the worst healthy case, and it leaves 19 of the 35 for everything else -
which is the arithmetic e2e.yml:103-105 already states as the design.

WHAT IT WOULD NOT FIX, said plainly: the shard would still fail. It would fail 19
minutes sooner, with its report uploaded and its reason named.

RELATED, AND ALREADY CARDED: CI-shard-timeout-budget-defeats-flaky-retry, and
CI-supabase-cli-setup-flaky - the earlier run's log emitted warnings naming BOTH,
so that runner was already unhealthy before Playwright started.

=== SHIPPED 2026-08-25, PR #1033. ===
The one-line fix, ratified by the owner in the Friday-freeze dispatch. e2e.yml now carries the budget its own header claimed it had since 2026-08-19.

evidence.ref:
MERGED as PR #1033, squashed to d59425ac. Owner-ratified. All four required checks ran for real - Lint+typecheck+test 3m54s, DB-gated 2m41s, three full E2E shards (8m15s/7m51s/6m16s), spec drift 12s - and zero non-success check runs on the head SHA.

timeout-minutes: 16 on the Run Playwright E2E step. It does NOT make a bad shard pass; it makes it fail 19 minutes sooner WITH its report uploaded. The budget buys evidence, not green.

cards.title: WATCH ITEM: portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts:342 retried once on the merging run of #959, where two prior shard-3 runs had zero flaky. Observation only, no code change
cards.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-19. OBSERVATION ONLY. NOTHING IS DIAGNOSED HERE AND NOTHING IS FIXED. This card exists so a second occurrence arrives already half-diagnosed instead of costing an afternoon - the same posture as LE-e2e-nif-edit-404, which was opened on exactly this basis.

=== THE OCCURRENCE ===
Run 32281005018, E2E shard (3), job 96159521871, on the merging run of PR #959.
  ✓ 36 [chromium] portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts:342:5
     "request-mode: a REAL pedido still says PEDIDO, never a finished booking" (retry #1) (1.6s)
Playwright's summary: 1 flaky, 73 passed (5.4m).

=== NOTHING WAS SKIPPED, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ===
1 flaky + 73 passed = 74, which is the SAME TOTAL as both prior shard-3 runs. Playwright counts flaky separately from passed, so the drop from "74 passed" to "73 passed" is accounting and not a lost test. This was verified before the merge, because a test count that falls by one is exactly the shape of the skip-guard defect this repo has had twice.

=== THE COMPARISON, AND ITS LIMIT ===
Two prior shard-3 runs on effectively the same spec code both reported "74 passed (4.0m)" with ZERO flaky:
  job 96112495496 (PR #957 rerun) and job 96156108869 (PR #960).
TWO RUNS IS NOT A SAMPLE. It is not sufficient to call this pre-existing, and it is not sufficient to call it new. Saying so is the point of the card.

=== WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE DISMISSED AS UNRELATED ===
The test traverses code edited in that very PR. bookFirstAvailable() calls openServiceStep(), which contains the :72 change, and the run continues through the :116 and :129 changes.

=== AND WHY THE CHANGE IS THE UNLIKELY CAUSE ===
Every one of those three edits replaced an IMMEDIATE POLL with a BOUNDED WAIT. The old :116 in particular would throw "never reached the date/time step" on an early poll; the new one waits up to 15s for the same element. That makes the traversal MORE deterministic, not less. A change in that direction producing a new flake would be surprising and would itself be the finding.

=== THE HONEST ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS ===
This is the most timing-sensitive test in the suite: it books a real slot end to end against the seeded calendar, and it carries test.skip(!booked) precisely because a slot is not guaranteed. Load on the runner, or slot contention with another spec, is at least as plausible as anything in the diff.

=== WHAT TO DO, AND IT IS NOT AN INVESTIGATION ===
IF IT FLAKES AGAIN ON ANY FUTURE RUN, APPEND THE OCCURRENCE HERE: run id, job id, shard, the retry line, and the run's flaky/passed totals. Do not open a second card and do not start diagnosing on occurrence two - accumulate first. A third occurrence with three recorded data points is worth a session; one is worth a note.

DO NOT "FIX" IT BY ADDING A TIMEOUT OR A RETRY. This project's e2e doctrine is that a retry can change the input and that one green run proves nothing that can race. If the cause is real, padding it hides it.

CLOSES ON: either a second occurrence that turns this into a real investigation with its own card, or a deliberate decision that enough clean runs have passed to call it noise - stated with the number of runs, not with a feeling.

cards.title: Fixtures, beyond the one invariant a constraint now enforces: could production ever contain what this seed block builds

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. docs/recon/ACC-fixture-forbidden-state-sweep.md, derived from origin/main at 53ae1bd. ZERO FORBIDDEN STATES FOUND IN FIXTURES, against the invariants the schema names and that a fixture is capable of expressing.

THE INVARIANT LIST CAME FROM THE SCHEMA, as the card instructed: 86 ADD CONSTRAINT, 81 CHECK, 7 unique indexes, 4 triggers in packages/db/migrations. The named ones are the EXCLUDE constraint appointments_no_double_confirmed, the two window CHECKs, the attempt_count range, the two status enums, two UNIQUE rules, and four triggers.

THE SPLIT THAT DECIDES WHAT A FIXTURE CAN EVEN VIOLATE, and it was not obvious going in: A FIXTURE IS A STATE, NOT A TRANSITION. None of the four triggers is reachable by a fixture - clinical-record immutability, both append-only rules and patient-number assignment all constrain WHAT MAY HAPPEN TO A ROW, not WHAT A ROW MAY LOOK LIKE. No seed block can express "this locked record was later edited"; that is a sequence, and the trigger refuses the second step. So most of the schema's enforcement is about transitions, and the fixture question is far narrower than the constraint count suggests.

THE SCAN: 441 test files, comments stripped. 48 start/end literal pairs examined within object literals -> ZERO inverted or zero-length windows. Zero fire_status values outside the CHECK. Zero negative attempt_count. Zero fixtures constructing two coexisting confirmed appointments on one practitioner at one window.

THE PARENT CARD'S "SIX FILES BUILD TWO OR MORE CONFIRMED APPOINTMENTS" WAS COUNTING MENTIONS, NOT ROWS. Read individually: estado-server-enforcement and audit-override-trace pass "confirmed" as an ARGUMENT to updateAppointment, a transition against ONE row; agenda-grid renders single-element arrays, and its three at lines 328-332 are three separate renders; actions.status-event has one base fixture plus an update call; pedido-confirm's two occurrences are an ASSERTION and an AUDIT PAYLOAD FIELD, not fixtures at all; and double-booked-surface is the legitimate one, building the state on purpose to prove the constraint's refusal reaches the agenda as pt-PT. FIFTH INSTANCE of the same lesson after categories A, B, C and the first fixture pass: a shape-match counts the APPEARANCE OF A STRING, not the thing the string sometimes indicates.

A DEFECT IN THE SCAN ITSELF, CAUGHT BY ITS OWN GUARD. The first run reported 0 test files scanned and therefore 0 violations - a clean-looking result - because a cd into packages/db/migrations had persisted from an earlier command and find apps packages matched nothing. A find that matches nothing exits 0, and a scan over zero files finds zero problems. It was caught because the scan ASSERTS ITS OWN FILE COUNT before reporting. That assertion exists because of LEARNINGS.md sections 4 and 5, and this is the FIRST time the guard was already in place before the mistake happened rather than added after it.

NOT COVERED, said rather than implied: the 81 CHECK constraints were not exhaustively enumerated - only the NAMED ones are greppable, and anonymous inline CHECKs are unlisted; uniqueness violations across separate fixture objects were not scanned, which consultations_recording_unique and quick_notes_tenant_user_uq would need; and only invariants a fixture can express AS STATE were in scope.

cards.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-19 out of ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep, which is closed. Full reasoning in docs/recon/ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep-counts.md, section FIXTURES.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT COVERED BY THE SWEEP THAT SPAWNED IT ===
That sweep counted ASSERTIONS. Its worst single instance was in a SETUP: appointment-note-present-capture.test.ts seeded TWO CONFIRMED APPOINTMENTS on one therapist at one identical window - the exact state the system exists to prevent - and every assertion in the suite passed against it, for months. IT WAS FOUND BY 0061's EXCLUDE CONSTRAINT ON ITS FIRST CI RUN, not by a review and not by any of the 385 test files. A sweep scoped to expect() calls walks straight past it.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY ANSWERED, so this card does not re-walk it ===
For THAT invariant the class is closed and does not depend on vigilance: the fixture is fixed, 0061's GiST EXCLUDE constraint on public.appointments is real, and packages/db/tests/no-double-confirmed.test.ts tests the constraint itself. Any DB-BACKED fixture attempting the state now fails at insert.

=== WHAT REMAINS ===
  1. THE IN-MEMORY SURFACE. 40 test files mention a confirmed status; 10 are DB-backed and 30 are in-memory, where nothing is inserted so no constraint can catch anything. Six of the 30 build two or more confirmed appointment objects.
  2. THE INVARIANT SET ITSELF IS NOT ENUMERATED. "No two confirmed appointments on one therapist at one window" is one invariant. The others - whatever they are - have not been listed, and listing them is most of this card's work. Start from the constraints and triggers the schema already carries, because those are invariants somebody has already decided are real.

=== THE CRITERION, and it is what stops this becoming a bulk rewrite ===
A FIXTURE THAT CONSTRUCTS A FORBIDDEN STATE IS A DEFECT ONLY WHEN THE TEST IS NOT ABOUT THAT STATE. Where the forbidden state is the subject, building it is CORRECT, and refusing to build it would leave the refusal path untested. The worked example is double-booked-surface.test.ts, which builds the double-booked state on purpose to prove the constraint's refusal reaches the agenda as pt-PT rather than as a raw Postgres 500. estado-server-enforcement, audit-override-trace, agenda-grid, actions.status-event and pedido-confirm are the other five and are UNREAD.

DO NOT BULK-FIX and do not report an alarming count. The parent card's whole result was that 123 suspects became one real defect, because a shape-match cannot tell DOING the suspicious thing from being ABOUT it.

CLOSES ON: the invariant list committed under docs/recon/, each in-memory fixture that violates one either fixed or justified in a comment naming what it is about, and the honest number stated with its method.

cards.title: The board reconciler makes 80 sequential gh API calls with no retry, and one transient read reddens a REQUIRED check

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED 2026-08-20. A bounded retry on NON-404 failures in docs/board/reconcile-board.mjs, with five tests in reconcile-board.test.mjs.

THE 404 RULE IS UNTOUCHED, and that was the constraint the fix had to respect. A 404 is an ANSWER - the PR does not exist - and anything else is a failure to ASK, which must never be reported as an answer. A retry changes only how hard we try to ask; it does not turn an unasked question into a satisfied one. SO A 404 BREAKS OUT OF THE RETRY LOOP IMMEDIATELY rather than being retried, because retrying a definite answer would be as wrong as accepting a non-answer. There is a test asserting the 404 path makes exactly ONE call.

A RESCUED READ IS ANNOUNCED with ::warning::, matching the e2e workflow's Supabase and Playwright steps. A silent retry makes a flake un-measurable, which is how the Supabase one reached three occurrences before anyone counted them.

TESTABLE BY DESIGN. fetchPrStates now takes an injectable reader and pause, so the failure is INJECTED rather than waited for - the card's own closing condition, "proven by a test or by an injected failure, not by the absence of the problem". The pause is stubbed to a no-op in tests: the retry's correctness is in WHAT it retries, not how long it waits.

FIVE TESTS: a transient failure that recovers returns the real state after 3 calls; THE EXACT OCCURRENCE - one bad read out of three PRs no longer fails the run; a 404 is an answer and is NOT retried (exactly one call); a persistent failure still THROWS after 3 attempts; and a negative control.

NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN AND IT IS DECISIVE: setting ATTEMPTS back to 1 - the pre-fix behaviour - fails 3 of the new tests (36 pass, 3 fail). Restored, all 39 pass. The 404 test and the persistent-failure control pass under BOTH, which is correct: neither depends on retrying, and that discrimination is what shows the other three fail for the right reason.

THE LIVE RECONCILER STILL EXITS 0 against the real board, so the refactor survives roughly 80 real gh calls rather than only the injected ones.

STRUCTURAL ALTERNATIVE NOT TAKEN, recorded so it is not re-proposed as an oversight: the card suggested one paginated query instead of ~80 round trips. It is the better long-term shape - fewer calls is fewer chances to fail, and faster - but it changes the query shape and adds pagination edge cases, where the retry is minimal and directly addresses the observed failure. Left for whoever finds the round trips slow enough to matter.

cards.notes:
OPENED 2026-08-19 FROM A LIVE OCCURRENCE, not from a code read.

=== THE OCCURRENCE ===
PR #965, run 32318873585, job 96276819988, step "Reconcile the board against merged PRs":
    CANNOT VERIFY: gh could not read PR #764: unexpected end of JSON input
    [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 2.
"Lint + typecheck + test" - a REQUIRED check - went red on a PR whose content was fine. RE-RUNNING THE SAME COMMIT PASSED, which is the definition of transient.

=== THE RECONCILER'S DESIGN IS RIGHT AND IS NOT WHAT NEEDS CHANGING ===
docs/board/reconcile-board.mjs:324-350 throws rather than returning a partial map, with the comment "a half-answered question about which work has shipped is worse than none", and it distinguishes a 404 (an ANSWER: the PR does not exist) from any other failure (a failure to ASK, which must not be reported as an answer). THAT DISTINCTION IS EXACTLY THE SECTION 1.3 DISCIPLINE and must survive any fix. Exit 2 means "could not ask" and is correct here.

=== THE GAP ===
It makes ONE gh api call PER CITED PR, sequentially, over roughly 80 PRs, WITH NO RETRY. "unexpected end of JSON input" is a truncated or empty response - a transient network failure, not a 404 - so a single bad read out of eighty reddens the gate. This is the same class as CI-shard-timeout-budget-defeats-flaky-retry, shipped earlier today: a network-dependent step in a required check with no resilience.

=== THE FIX, NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE ===
A bounded retry on NON-404 failures only, preserving the 404-is-an-answer rule untouched, and announcing a rescued read with ::warning:: the way the e2e workflow's Supabase and Playwright steps already do - so a run that needed rescuing stays VISIBLE rather than reading as clean. A silent retry would make this flake un-measurable, which is how the Supabase one reached three occurrences before anyone counted them.
CONSIDER ALSO the cheaper structural fix: one paginated query for all PR states instead of eighty round trips. Fewer calls is fewer chances to fail, and it is faster.

CLOSES ON: a transient non-404 gh failure being retried and reported, proven by a test or by an injected failure - not by the absence of the problem.

cards.title: Manual time entry books outside the therapist's disponibilidade - the check existed and its verdict was discarded

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN ON DEPLOYED SCREENS 2026-08-21, VERIFY item 4, ALL THREE ARMS. Arm 1: a manual time outside the therapist's hours is REFUSED and the message NAMES the hours that day. Arm 2: picking a slot from the disponibilidade panel still saves normally, so the fix did not stop the clinic booking. Arm 3: a therapist with NO hours configured is still bookable at any hour, so availability stays opt-in and nobody became unbookable. AND THE OVERRIDE CANNOT REACH THE REFUSAL - 'Guardar mesmo assim' does not save an out-of-hours time. Merged #992.

cards.notes:
=== BUILT 2026-08-20. THE CHECK EXISTED; ITS VERDICT WAS BEING DISCARDED. ===

Status is in_flight rather than shipped because WF-03 applies: the refusal is
a message reception reads. VERIFY-QUEUE item 4, with BOTH arms - the refusal,
and the ordinary picker path still saving normally.

ONE THING FLAGGED FOR IVAN AND DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED HERE: there is now no
way to book a genuine one-off exception outside a therapist's hours. The
override cannot reach this refusal, on purpose. If the clinic needs late
bookings the answer is to extend the disponibilidade; if it needs a real
exception path, that is a product question and this card does not answer it.

--- prior notes below, unchanged ---

DISPATCHED 2026-08-20 as part 3 of the Rodica batch. NEEDS NO SCHEMA, so it is NOT blocked on migration 0067 and shipped while that PR waits at its apply gate.

THE DEFECT, as reported: the manual time field books outside the therapist's schedule. Catarina ends at 13:00 and a manual entry books 17:00.

PL-11 IS CHANGED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-20: availability becomes ENFORCED at write time for staff manual time entry, where it was advisory on that path. Recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-21 ON THE OWNER'S SCREENS, ALL THREE ARMS. ===

OBSERVED: the refusal names the hours (arm 1); picking from the panel still saves (arm 2); a therapist with no hours configured stays bookable (arm 3). AND THE OVERRIDE CANNOT REACH IT - confirmed, which is the arm the card cared most about: an override that reinstated the exact defect would have been a bypass wearing a button.

ARMS 2 AND 3 ARE WHY THIS IS CLOSED RATHER THAN HALF-CLOSED. A fix that refused everything would have passed arm 1 perfectly and stopped the clinic booking; a fix that refused therapists with no configured hours would have made them unbookable. Both were checked and both are fine.

cards.title: errors.offline_* is kept and unwired: navigator.onLine reports TRUE on a router with no internet, so the obvious implementation would tell a working patient they are offline
cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-20 while executing the Q-PORTAL-DEAD-I18N-1 ruling. The ruling said to WIRE UP 500 and offline. 500 is wired (apps/portal/app/global-error.tsx). OFFLINE IS NOT, and this card is why.

THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION IS WRONG. `navigator.onLine` answers 'is there a network interface', not 'can I reach the server'. It reports TRUE on a router with no internet, on a captive portal, and on a VPN that is up but not routing. A banner built on it tells a patient whose portal is working perfectly that they are offline - an unhandled case wearing the face of a known one, which is section 1.3 exactly, and in the PRODUCT rather than in an instrument.

IT ALSO FAILS THE OTHER WAY, which is the half that makes the naive version worse than nothing: a phone that has lost signal mid-request often still reports onLine TRUE for several seconds, so the banner is absent exactly when it would have been useful.

WHAT AN HONEST VERSION LOOKS LIKE: distinguish a NETWORK failure from an HTTP failure in apps/portal/lib/api/client.ts. A fetch that REJECTS (TypeError) never reached the server; a fetch that RESOLVES with 5xx did. Only the first is 'offline', and it is a fact rather than a guess. That is a change to the api client's error contract and to every caller that reads it, which is why it is its own card.

AUTHORED 2026-08-20 ON OWNER AUTHORISATION. Slot 0067 confirmed free from packages/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json: 66 entries, idx 0-65, highest tag 0066_users_must_set_password.

ONE MIGRATION FOR FOUR NEEDS, by the same ruling. Rule 8 allows one in flight repo-wide and the batch needs all four; they are unrelated in subject and identical in risk profile - additive columns with defaults, two new tables, and one data backfill that is an arithmetic identity.

1. appointments.origin. Q-PEDIDO-EMIT-1 ruling A. is_unconfirmed_pedido stops joining staff_notifications, so a failed best-effort notification emit can no longer make a patient's request indistinguishable from a staff booking while it blocks its slot.
2. appointments.pack_instance_id. A pacote session becomes a real appointment row instead of a counter decrement.
3. patient_pack_instances.legacy_consumed. What makes 'existing balances preserved exactly' an identity rather than a hope.
4. patient_followup_postponements and patient_followup_contacts. The recuperacao surface's two durable facts.

THE APPLY BLOCK IS A DRAFT AND HAS NOT BEEN SENT TO IVAN. docs/migration-apply-0067.md opens with the mandatory NOT VALIDATED line. Path is draft -> strategy -> Ivan, per section 4.9.

=== RULED 2026-08-20: THE §4.9 CONFLICT IS SETTLED. ===

PORTAL-REHYDRATE §4.9 says an executor never sends an apply block to Ivan directly, in any form, in any turn. Report bodies are read on Ivan's screen before they reach strategy, so printing a draft block in one and obeying §4.9 literally cannot both hold. It was named rather than resolved by the terminal, and strategy ruled it.

THE RULING: a DRAFT may transit Ivan's screen inside a report body, and only with the NOT VALIDATED line first. IVAN RUNS ONLY BLOCKS ISSUED BY STRATEGY AND MARKED VALIDATED. The rule was never about which pixels a draft crosses; it is about which artefact is executable, and the executable one is the one strategy stamped.

§4.9 ITSELF IS AMENDED IN THE FIRST PR AFTER #991 MERGES. It is not amended now because main is frozen at 9f196b6 while 0067 is pinned: any merge to main voids the pin. Carded as LE-portal-rehydrate-4-9-amendment.

=== APPLY BLOCK REJECTED BY STRATEGY 2026-08-20, FIVE DEFECTS, ALL FIXED. ===

set -a and a tilde env path (both banned; set -a errors in zsh), the mandatory check-pending-migrations.mjs pre-check and post-check missing entirely, no git status --short / git cat-file pre-flight, no teardown, and pnpm --filter @osteojp/db db:migrate - which is not merely non-canonical but BROKEN: db:migrate is defined in the ROOT package.json, not in @osteojp/db, so that command would have failed at the top of a production sitting.

EVERY ONE OF THE FIVE WAS ALREADY FIXED ONCE, at 0065. docs/migration-apply-0065.md §0 records the same four-defect rejection and names the cause: the block was built from the shape of the previous apply document instead of from docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, which is the committed source. This draft did it again. The runbook is now cited in section 4 by name, and the correction is recorded here rather than only in a chat turn, because a lesson that lives in a dispatch is one forgotten paste from not existing.

=== APPLIED 2026-08-20. ONE STOP CONDITION FIRED AND THE DOCUMENT WAS WRONG, NOT THE DATABASE. ===

V5 expected still_reads_notifications FALSE and production returned TRUE. TRUE is correct: the committed function is a DISJUNCTION (a.origin = 'patient_portal' OR the staff_notifications row exists), so pg_get_functiondef MUST contain both strings. An apply returning FALSE would have meant the migration did not run.

HOW THE EXPECTATION WENT STALE, from this branch's own history: 208e753 authored the migration with the function keyed on origin ALONE and authored the V5 expectation to match. 2642c35 then changed the function to a disjunction, because pedido-does-not-block.db.test.ts went red on five assertions, and it did NOT touch the apply document. Five later commits edited that document, including a full rebuild from the runbook after a five-defect rejection, and none revisited V5.

THE LESSON: a verification query whose expectation is not regenerated when the migration changes produces a FALSE STOP. Same class as the stale-sha defect and worse in effect - a stale sha stops an apply that should have run, a stale expectation stops an apply that DID run correctly, at the moment of least tolerance for ambiguity: mid sitting, credentials live. Carded as LE-apply-block-expectation-drift.
