cards.notes:
DISPATCHED 2026-08-20. BLOCKED ON MIGRATION 0067 BEING APPLIED - it needs patient_followup_postponements and patient_followup_contacts, which RB-00 carries.

SELECTION, as ruled: a completed attendance from the first day of the PREVIOUS month until 7 days ago, AND no future appointment, AND not currently postponed.

SHOWS: last attendance date, associated therapist, available contacts.

ACTIONS ARE ALL CLIENT-SIDE DEEP LINKS opening on the receptionist device - wa.me with a prefilled editable message, an sms: link, a mailto: with prefilled subject and body. NO SERVER-SIDE SENDING, no Twilio, no Resend, R9 live-send flags untouched. The server records only that a human pressed a link.

ADIAR: postpone N weeks, removes the patient until that date, stored server-side, REVERSIBLE, and the reversal is recorded rather than erasing the row - visible who and when on both halves.

ACCESS: owner, admin, reception. Location-scoped per PL-09. THERAPISTS SEE NOTHING. No new public surface.

COPY: pt-PT templates are DRAFTED and EDITABLE before send. Marked for Ivan's copy review at the sitting rather than treated as approved.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-20: migration 0067 is APPLIED TO PRODUCTION and #991 merged. Receipt at docs/migration-apply-0067.md section 10. Main is no longer frozen.

=== BUILT 2026-08-20. WHAT SHIPPED, AND THE FOUR DECISIONS INSIDE IT. ===

1. A NEW CAPABILITY, followup:read, NOT patients:read. Owner, admin, reception; a therapist gets nothing and cannot reach the route. The obvious host was patients:read, which every role holds - so the gate would have passed for a therapist while reading as a real check. That is SEC-01 exactly, one card earlier, on the section directly above this one on /notificacoes. Three layers enforce it and they are not one check written three times: the nav hides the entry, the route redirects, and listFollowupCandidates THROWS rather than returning an empty list, because an empty list is a valid answer a future caller would render as "nobody to call".

2. THE SELECTION PREDICATE LIVES IN packages/db AND IS SHARED WITH ITS OWN TEST. Its two readers are the staff query and the DB-gated test that proves it against real Postgres. Writing it inline and re-typing it in the test is the drift shape LE-apply-block-expectation-drift was carded for on this same day - a proof written against one version of a rule, never regenerated, going GREEN while asserting the old rule. guest-preferred-window.ts sits beside it for the same stated reason.

3. THE WINDOW IS THE PATIENT'S MOST RECENT ATTENDANCE, not "some attendance". Read the loose way, a patient seen in July AND again three days ago qualifies, and reception rings somebody they saw on Monday. Both ends of the ruling then do their work: 7 days means not-seen-recently, the first of the previous month means still-a-live-relationship. Boundaries are computed in Europe/Lisbon with the offset re-derived AT THE WINDOW START, because a window opening in March and closing in April spans a DST change and one shared offset moves the boundary by an hour. Seven unit tests pin January, DST, the last day of a month, and the Lisbon-versus-UTC wall date - the last of which caught a wrong EXPECTATION of mine, not wrong code.

4. A CANCELLED FUTURE APPOINTMENT IS NOT A BOOKING. It is precisely the patient this list exists to catch: they dropped out and nobody noticed. Counting it as a booking would hide the patient who most needs the call, silently, because the row still exists and still looks like an appointment. Asserted in both directions in the DB test.

NOTHING SENDS ANYTHING. Every action is a client-side deep link opening on the receptionist's own device - wa.me, sms:, mailto: - with an editable prefilled message. No Twilio, no Resend, R9 flags untouched. The server records only that a human pressed a link, and the screen says so in Portuguese: the mark reads "contactado", never "enviado", because a tick is the most over-read symbol on a screen like this.

A LANDLINE GETS NO WhatsApp AND NO SMS BUTTON, reusing isSmsCapablePT rather than a second copy, and the screen NAMES the absence instead of just omitting the buttons - "no button" and "this patient cannot be reached that way" are different facts and only the second tells reception to ask for a mobile.

NAV PLACEMENT WAS FORCED BY A COMMITTED RULING. The entry first went between Estatisticas and Administracao and broke nav-items.test.ts, which asserts NAV-01's position BY INDEX because "position was the ruling, not an incidental". Moved beside Marcacoes, which is also where it belongs: a reception queue about bookings that do not exist yet. The three per-role list assertions were updated because a new page legitimately changes them; the therapist list is UNCHANGED and now carries an explicit not-to-contain for this route.

STILL OPEN: the owner's eyes on the deployed page and on the pt-PT copy.

CI CAUGHT A SELF-CONTRADICTION IN MY OWN SUITE, 2026-08-20, AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT. The whole-predicate test expected [QUALIFIES] alone, on the description "eight patients differ in one respect each, and none may appear". That sentence was FALSE about three of the eight, and the per-clause tests in the same file already said so - they assert toContain for exactly those three. Three fixtures are POSITIVE controls, not negative ones: a cancelled future appointment is not a booking, an expired postponement is a pause and not a deletion, and a revoked one has to actually bring the patient back. Each proves a clause does not OVER-exclude, which is the direction that fails silently: an over-strict predicate renders an empty list, and an empty list reads as good news on a screen whose empty state says "nobody to contact". The headline now asserts both directions by name.

=== OWNER RULING 2026-08-21: THE TEMPLATE COPY ROUTES TO RODICA ONLY. ===

The pt-PT recovery message is NOT for general review. It goes to Rodica, and only AFTER the /recuperacao crash is fixed and Ivan has made his own edit at the re-sitting. Sequence is part of the ruling: fix, Ivan edits, then Rodica.

WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN JUST DONE: the card and the queue both say "the copy is a draft and it is yours to change", which invited the wrong reviewer at the wrong time. This is the routing.

THE CARD STAYS in_flight. Its steps were never run - the page crashed on arrival - so nothing about RB-01 has been observed.

=== THE noPhone COPY FIX IS OBSERVED AND CLOSED. THE CARD STAYS in_flight.
2026-08-24. ===

OBSERVED BY IVAN ON THE DEPLOYED /recuperacao SCREEN, 2026-08-22: the false
duplicate under the buttons is GONE, and the inline field renders "Sem numero
registado" correctly.

THAT SETTLES THE DEFECT #1009 FIXED AND NOTHING ELSE ON THIS CARD.

A BOOKKEEPING GAP THIS CLOSES, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY PATCHED.
INC-12-recuperacao-server-render's notes end with "carded and fixed separately:
See RB-01." NO SUCH RECORD EXISTED ON RB-01 until this line. The fix shipped in
#1009 with its reasoning in the commit message and INC-12's evidence, and the
card it pointed at never received it - so a reader following the cross-reference
found nothing, and the owner's observation of it had no card to land on. It
lands here, which is what makes INC-12's sentence true.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, restated because "a duplicate" understates it:
followup.noPhone rendered TWICE on a row with no phone - once as the field's
value and once under the buttons. The second was keyed on "cannot be messaged",
which is TWO different rows: no phone at all, and a LANDLINE. ON A LANDLINE ROW
THE FIELD SHOWED THE REAL NUMBER AND THE LINE UNDERNEATH SAID "Sem numero
registado". Not redundant. FALSE. The field keeps the empty case because that IS
the field; the line under the buttons now carries only the case the field cannot
express - a good number this screen cannot use, which is the one that tells

=== STEPS B C D E F REMAIN UNPROVEN. DO NOT CLOSE THIS CARD. ===

OWNER, 2026-08-22: his list holds ONE PATIENT AND THAT PATIENT HAS NO PHONE. So
five things on this card have never been exercised on a screen:

  B  the mobile row
  C  the prefilled message
  D  the contact mark
  E  Adiar
  F  the therapist lockout

EVERY ONE OF THEM NEEDS A ROW THE LIST DOES NOT CURRENTLY CONTAIN. This is the
same shape INC-12 recorded and it is worth stating twice: the empty and
near-empty page renders correctly throughout, which is exactly why a defect on
the populated path survives observation. A no-phone row proves the no-phone
branch and nothing else - it cannot reach the WhatsApp or SMS buttons, cannot
carry a prefilled message, and offers no path to the mark.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THEM OBSERVABLE, stated so the next sitting is not scheduled
against the same blocker: a patient in the qualifying window WITH A MOBILE. That
is a fact about the clinic's data, not about the build, and no terminal may read
production to find out when one appears. Until one does, these five steps are

THE TEMPLATE COPY ROUTING IS UNCHANGED by this observation: fix, Ivan edits,
then Rodica. Ivan has not yet made his edit, because the message cannot be seen
without a mobile row either.

=== THE FIXTURE EXISTS AND B TO F WERE RUN, 2026-08-22. THE CARD IS NOT CLOSED.
    THE PER-STEP OBSERVATIONS ARE NOT IN HAND. ===

THE BLOCKER RECORDED ABOVE IS LIFTED. "A patient in the qualifying window WITH A
MOBILE" was the stated condition and Ivan built one: ZZ TESTE Portal, with a
mobile set, a future marcacao cancelled, and a qualifying completed consultation
present. That shape is exactly what the card said was needed - the cancelled
future appointment is the clause this list exists to catch, and the DB test
asserts it in both directions.

IVAN RESTORED THE PATIENT'S ORIGINAL TELEFONE AFTERWARDS. Recorded so a later
reader does not mistake the test row for clinic data, and so nobody "corrects"
a number back to the fixture value. The row was a fixture for one sitting; it is
not a patient of this clinic and its phone is not a contact.

HE CONFIRMED STEPS B THROUGH F ON DEPLOYED SCREENS. That is the owner's report
and it is recorded as given.

WHY THE CARD STAYS in_flight ANYWAY, AND IT IS THE DISPATCH'S OWN CONDITION.
The instruction was explicit: fill Observed lines PER STEP, B through F
separately, NEVER AS ONE BLANKET LINE - and "do not close without them in hand".
What is in hand is one blanket confirmation covering five steps. Splitting that
sentence into five sentences would produce five blanket lines wearing per-step
labels, which is the same claim with more punctuation and reads afterwards as
five observations that never happened.

THIS BOARD HAS PAID FOR EXACTLY THAT ONCE. PG1 passed for seven days on four
observations of which one had not been made: the second half of one test was run
in the belief it was the next one, and the record was written as though both had
passed. The cost was not the product - nothing was wrong with it - it was that
the record could not be trusted. A card closed on a reconstructed step list is
that failure with the reconstruction done deliberately.

WHAT IS NEEDED, one line each, and each naming what was SEEN rather than that it
passed:
  B  THE MOBILE ROW - the row rendered with the number, and WhatsApp and SMS
     offered beside Email rather than the no-phone line.
  C  THE PREFILLED MESSAGE - which channel was opened, and that the message
     arrived already written, with the FIRST NAME and the last-consultation date

  D  THE CONTACT MARK - the mark appearing after the link was opened, reading

  F  THE THERAPIST LOCKOUT, AND IT IS THE SECURITY ARM SO IT NEEDS BOTH HALVES

NOTHING ABOUT THE BUILD IS IN QUESTION. This is a records gap, not a defect, and
the five steps are believed to pass. The card closes the moment the five lines
arrive.

=== THE TEMPLATE IS ROUTED TO RODICA, 2026-08-24. NO EDITS WERE SUPPLIED. ===

The 2026-08-21 ruling sequences this: fix, Ivan edits, then Rodica. The fix
shipped (#1009) and the mobile row now exists, so the message is finally visible
on a screen.

IVAN SUPPLIED NO EDITS WITH THIS DISPATCH, so the template goes to Rodica
VERBATIM as committed. Recorded rather than left implicit: "no edits" and "edits
not yet received" are different states, and the ruling's sequence is satisfied
either way only if the first is what happened. If edits arrive later they are
applied and Rodica reviews the edited text, not this one.

WHAT SHE REVIEWS, and it is one body across three channels rather than three
messages. followup.messageTemplate is the whole of it; only email adds a subject
(followup.messageSubject, "OsteoJP"). The substitutions are {name} -> the
patient's FIRST NAME only, and {date} -> the last consultation date as
DD/MM/YYYY in Europe/Lisbon.

NO CLINICAL CONTENT AT ALL - not the service, not the therapist's speciality, not
a reason - because a WhatsApp preview appears on a lock screen other people can
see; and the message is A DRAFT that opens in the receptionist's own WhatsApp,
Messages or mail client and can be changed word by word before sending, which is
what makes a templated message acceptable for a clinical relationship at all.
Nothing is sent by the platform.

=== OWNER OBSERVATIONS, 2026-08-27. RECORDED AS GIVEN. RB-01 DID NOT CLOSE. ===

Ivan sat with the page. FIVE OF THE SIX STEPS DID NOT PRODUCE A CLOSING
OBSERVATION, and the card stays in_flight. Recorded per step, in his words,
without interpretation:

  B  CONFIRMED. The mobile row shows the number and offers WhatsApp, SMS and
     Email beside it.
  C  PARTIAL. WhatsApp OPENED. THE PREFILLED CONTENT WAS NOT VERIFIED. This is
     the step the whole template review hangs off - `followup.messageTemplate`,

     being asked about. An unverified prefill means the body has still never

2026-08-27. It is no longer the acceptance criterion: the owner ruled the same

completed consultation was theirs. So F must be RE-WRITTEN before the next

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE RE-RUN. B is the only step with a durable confirmation,
and it is re-run anyway: the sitting is one pass, and a step observed on an
earlier deployment is not evidence about the one in front of him. Steps B through

=== IVAN'S SITTING, 2026-08-28. OBSERVED PER STEP, QUOTED, NEVER AS ONE LINE. ===
B  "CONFIRMED. One row shows a mobile number with WhatsApp, SMS and Email beside it."
C  "CONFIRMED. WhatsApp opened with the message already drafted, read on screen: 'Bom dia ZZ, fala a OsteoJP. Notamos que ja nao a/o vemos desde 19/08/2026 e queriamos saber como esta. Se quiser marcar uma consulta, e so responder a esta mensagem.' SMS and Email carried the same body. First name substituted, date as DD/MM/YYYY, nothing clinical."

E  "CONFIRMED. Adiar 4 semanas moved the patient to Adiados with a return date; Trazer de volta returned them."
F1 "CONFIRMED. Recuperacao present in the therapist sidebar with the orange phone icon."
F2 "CONFIRMED. The therapist sees their own patients."
F3 "CONFIRMED. Another therapist's patient is ABSENT from the list."
F4 "CONFIRMED. Reception still sees the full list."
G  "CONFIRMED ABSENT for admin", which is SR-02 working as ruled.
H  "CONFIRMED. Icons distinct and coloured."
I  "CONFIRMED. Active row clearly legible."  Ivan's words on H and I: "well built and very clear."

FIVE OF SIX CONFIRMED. RB-01 STAYS in_flight ON STEP D ALONE, and the re-run is
STEP D ONLY. B, C and E were observed on the deployed screen and are recorded
above in his words; re-running them would be re-asking a question already
answered about this build.

WHY D IS NOT A SMALL REMAINDER. The contact mark is the only durable record on
this page that a patient was reached. Without it the list cannot answer the one
question reception opens it to ask - HAS ANYBODY RUNG THIS PERSON - so two
receptionists ring the same patient while the one nobody rang stays quiet. That
is the failure this page exists to prevent, arriving through the page itself.

The defect is carded as LE-followup-contact-mark-never-recorded, which carries
the diagnosis to the line and the fix. RB-01 closes when Ivan sees a mark appear.

STEP C ALSO CLEARED THE TEMPLATE PRECONDITION. The 2026-08-21 ruling sequences
the review as fix, then Ivan, then Rodica, and required the body to be confirmed
on a real screen first. It now has been, verbatim, above. The template is routed
to Rodica with the compound-first-name note recorded below.

=== {name} IS THE FIRST TOKEN, NOT THE FIRST NAME. FOR RODICA. ===
apps/web/app/recuperacao/deep-links.ts:55 resolves {name} as
`patientName.trim().split(/\s+/)[0]` - the first WHITESPACE-DELIMITED TOKEN of
the stored full name. Observed as "ZZ" on the fixture, which is correct for that
row and hides the case that is not.

A COMPOUND FIRST NAME RENDERS ONLY ITS FIRST WORD. "Maria Joao Silva" is
greeted as "Bom dia Maria". In Portugal that is common rather than exotic, so it
will happen, and it is not a defect the code can fix on its own: nothing in the
record distinguishes a second given name from a first surname.

BEHAVIOUR IS NOT CHANGED. It is recorded, and it goes to Rodica with the
template, because whether "Bom dia Maria" is acceptable for a patient called
Maria Joao is a question about how the clinic speaks to people - hers, not
engineering's. If she wants the full first-name field, that is a data question
(which part of the name is given) before it is a code one.


=== THE ACCENTS WERE ALREADY THERE. 2026-08-28, BLUE. NOTHING WAS CORRECTED. ===
A dispatch reported that the body observed on screen "carries no Portuguese
accents" and asked for the screen to be corrected before the copy went to
Rodica. IT WAS NOT NEEDED, and the finding is recorded rather than acted on.

THE COMMITTED LITERAL, verbatim:
  Bom dia {name}, fala a OsteoJP. Notámos que já não a/o vemos desde {date} e
  queríamos saber como está. Se quiser marcar uma consulta, é só responder a
  esta mensagem.

Seven accented characters: á á ã í á é ó (Notámos, já, não, queríamos, está,
é, só).

RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, in four ways:
  1. `git log -S'Notámos'` finds the accented form in #998, the commit that
     CREATED the feature. `git log -S'Notamos que ja'` finds NOTHING - the
     unaccented form has never existed in that file.
  2. `getStrings` is a dictionary lookup and nothing else.
  3. `followupMessage` is two `.replace()` calls.
  4. The three link builders `encodeURIComponent`, which round-trips byte for
     byte; asserted end to end in deep-links.test.ts.
There is no normalizer, no NFD and no transliteration anywhere on the path.

SO THE OBSERVATION WAS A TRANSCRIPTION, not a screen. Recorded without blame:
typing a quoted sentence without diacritics is the ordinary thing to do at a
keyboard, and the standing rule is what caught it - re-derive an owner-reported
fact from the live system before building on it. Building the "fix" would have
been a no-op commit against a defect that did not exist, and it would have put a
false correction in the record.

WHAT WAS BUILT INSTEAD, because the dispatch's real value survives its premise:
a test that pins each accented WORD and the exact seven-character accent set,
plus NFC normalisation and the end-to-end encode round trip. Negative arm proven
by stripping one accent at authoring time: three assertions reddened
("contains Notámos", the seven-character set, and the end-to-end arm), and
passed again when restored. Accents are the easiest thing in a dictionary to
lose silently, and losing them produces a message that is merely a bit wrong -
which nobody reports.

=== THE SMS COST OF THE ACCENTS, WHICH IS REAL AND IS ACCEPTED ===
á, ã, í and ó are NOT representable in GSM-7. (é is.) So the body forces UCS-2:
70 characters per single segment and 67 per concatenated segment, against
GSM-7's 160 and 153.

For the representative case - name "Maria", date "19/08/2026", 168 characters:
  as shipped, accented   : UCS-2, 168 units, 67 per segment -> 3 SEGMENTS
  if accents were stripped: GSM-7, 168 units, 153 per segment -> 2 SEGMENTS

ONE EXTRA SEGMENT, AND IT COSTS NOTHING TODAY: nothing on this page is sent by
the platform. The deep link opens the receptionist's own Messages app on her own
plan, so the segment count is hers and not a Twilio line item. It would become a
real cost only if this body were ever reused by REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND, which is a
different template and a different card.

CORRECT PORTUGUESE WINS OVER A SEGMENT. Written down so a future cost-reduction
sweep meets the decision instead of making it again.

=== THE EMAIL CHANNEL HAS NO e2e ARM, AND THAT IS A LIMIT OF THE HARNESS ===
`mailto:` CANNOT BE INTERCEPTED BY PLAYWRIGHT - `page.route` and
`context.route` handle http(s) only. The first version of the write e2e clicked
Email and tried to neutralise the handoff that way; the pattern matched nothing,
the click produced no request the test could see, and the test failed for a
reason unrelated to its subject.

So the deployed arm exercises WHATSAPP, whose `https://wa.me/...` is routable.
PER-CHANNEL WRITE COVERAGE LIVES IN
`apps/web/lib/followup/record-contact.db.test.ts`, which drives the production
function directly for whatsapp, sms and email against real Postgres and reads
the rows back - including that a second channel is a second row.

STATED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED. "The e2e only clicks WhatsApp" looks like an
oversight and is a constraint; the coverage it appears to be missing exists one
layer down, where it can actually be asserted.

=== THE NAME-TOKEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED. OWNER, 2026-08-28. SETTLED. ===
This card recorded, for Rodica, that {name} resolves to the FIRST
WHITESPACE-DELIMITED TOKEN of the stored name - so a patient registered as
"Maria Joao Silva" is greeted "Bom dia Maria" - and asked whether that was
acceptable.

IT IS. The owner accepted the behaviour: treating a patient registered as Maria
Joao as Maria is acceptable.

SO THE BEHAVIOUR STANDS AND IS NOT A DEFECT. deep-links.ts is unchanged, the
template is unchanged, and this is recorded as ruling SR-09 so it is not
re-raised. A future session finding "only the first word of a compound given
name is used" has found a decision, not a bug.

AND THE ORDER OF THE QUESTION IS RECORDED WITH IT, because it is the part that
would otherwise be re-derived wrongly: if the clinic ever does want the full
given name, that is a DATA question - which part of what is stored is the given
name - before it is a template question. Nothing in the record distinguishes a
second given name from a first surname, so no change to the template can decide
it.

cards.title: A Pacote of N books N appointments instead of one, the balance derives from linked rows, and `consumir` goes

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN ON DEPLOYED SCREENS 2026-08-21, steps G-J all confirmed. G: a patient who already held a pacote read EXACTLY the number it read before - the observation this card turned on, and the one the migration could only prove arithmetically. H: the Consumir and Restaurar buttons are gone from the patient profile and the line explaining where sessions are counted from is present. I: booking a pacote session showed the balance before saving and the number went down by one after. J: cancelling that marcacao returned the session. Merged #999, squashed 325c2e6.

cards.notes:
DISPATCHED 2026-08-20. BLOCKED ON MIGRATION 0067 BEING APPLIED - it needs appointments.pack_instance_id and patient_pack_instances.legacy_consumed.

THE DEFECT: selecting a Pacote in Nova marcacao books ONE appointment, and `consumir` in the patient profile burns a session with NO appointment row - no who, no when, no slot. The balance is a counter nothing can reconcile against the diary.

LEGACY STATE, DERIVED FROM main BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED, which the dispatch required: service_packs is the pack TYPE; patient_pack_instances is one patient's purchase with sessions_total and a monotonic sessions_remaining; bookPackSessionTx registers-or-decrements that counter inside createAppointment's tx; the profile's consumir/restore adjusts it with an audit row and no appointment. THERE IS NO LINK COLUMN AT ALL - the appointment records the pack's BASE SERVICE as its serviceId and nothing else.

IT DOES MAP CLEANLY, SO THIS DID NOT HALT, and the reasoning is on the migration: a pure derive-from-linked-rows model would count ZERO for every existing instance and silently RESTORE every session already used - fabricating SESSIONS, the mirror of fabricating appointment rows. legacy_consumed records what is known (how many, not which) and the backfill is an identity, so every existing balance is preserved exactly and nothing is invented.

sessions_remaining IS FROZEN, not dropped: it is the only evidence the backfill can ever be checked against. A guard asserts no application code writes it.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-20: migration 0067 is APPLIED TO PRODUCTION and #991 merged. Receipt at docs/migration-apply-0067.md section 10. Main is no longer frozen.

=== BUILT 2026-08-20. WHAT SHIPPED. ===

THE BALANCE IS DERIVED: sessions_total - legacy_consumed - linked appointments that are not cancelled. The formula and both subtracted terms live in packages/db/src/pack-balance.ts, shared by the staff query, the booking guard and the DB-gated test - the same one-definition rule RB-01 followed, for the same reason LE-apply-block-expectation-drift was carded.

CONSUMIR AND RESTAURAR ARE DELETED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED, and the reasoning is the best part of this card: they existed for the under-24h / no-show rule, and a no-show is now an appointment with status no_show, which the formula counts by itself. The rule survives as a consequence of the data instead of a button somebody must remember - and it can no longer be applied to a patient with NO appointment at all, which is what made the old counter unreconcilable. THE SERVER ACTION WENT WITH THE BUTTON: removing the UI alone would have left a "use server" function callable by anything that can POST, still writing a balance nothing can reconcile.

A PACOTE MAY NOW BOOK N APPOINTMENTS. W8-01c rejected pacote + repeticao with the reason "rather than silently draining N". This card inverts that reasoning exactly: draining N is the feature, and it is no longer silent because every occurrence carries pack_instance_id. The refusal MOVED rather than disappearing - a batch larger than the balance is refused inside the transaction, by name (pack_insufficient), not truncated. Truncation would look like success and leave reception to find the missing appointments in the diary.

A LATENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE LIFTING THE GUARD: the recurrence CHILDREN inherited common.serviceId, so a pacote recurrence would have recorded the WRONG SERVICE on every occurrence after the first. The old refusal hid it. With the refusal lifted it would have shipped.

SESSIONS_REMAINING IS FROZEN AND THE GUARD THE SCHEMA PROMISED NOW EXISTS. packages/db/src/schema.ts named scripts/pack-sessions-remaining-is-frozen.test.mjs by path and the file did not exist - a comment pointing at a guard that is not there, which is the shape section 4.11 was committed to end. It now exists, runs in the required check, and has three arms: no application code names the column, the one allowed writer only INSERTs it, and the schema comment still names this file by path so the pointer cannot go stale silently. The two DB tests that ASSERT the backfill identity are allow-listed with the reason - a test asserting the frozen value is the opposite of drift, and forbidding it would delete the guard's own justification.

instances-core.ts WAS DELETED ENTIRELY. Its three functions all computed a value to write into sessions_remaining. The arithmetic did not move, it ceased to exist.

STILL OPEN: the owner on a real pacote, and Q-RB-02-1 (form pre-fill), which is a clinical decision about INTERVAL rather than a technical one - guessing weekly does not produce an error, it produces ten real appointments at the wrong cadence.

PROCESS SLIP, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST TWO CI ROUNDS AND WAS ENTIRELY MINE. I ran the full gate set, then added two files (pack-derived-balance.db.test.ts and the e2e edit), and did not re-run everything before pushing. CI found both: a TS18048 on a destructured row, and booking-packs.spec.ts asserting the Consumir/Restaurar buttons this card deletes. Neither was a surprising defect; both were caught by gates I had already run once and treated as still valid. THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: the gates prove the tree they ran against, not the branch. A file added after them is unproven, and "I ran the gates" is a statement about a moment.

THE FROZEN-COLUMN GUARD CAUGHT ITS FIRST FILE WITHIN MINUTES OF BEING WRITTEN - my own pack-derived-balance.db.test.ts, which seeds a realistic pre-0067 instance. Allow-listed with that reason. It is the clearest evidence available that the guard is not decorative.

E2E: booking-packs.spec.ts steps 1-4 SURVIVED UNCHANGED across a complete replacement of the mechanism - book once and 9/10, book twice and 8/10 read the same under a counter and under a derived balance. That is the strongest evidence available that existing balances read the same. Steps 5-6 became an assertion that the manual controls are ABSENT, on the row rather than the page so it cannot pass because the profile failed to render. The cancelled-returns-the-session arm is deliberately NOT driven through the UI: it needs a disclosure, a cancel drawer and a confirmation on a spec already carrying two twelve-second saves, and this project has two open cards on that class of flake. It is proven against real Postgres through the same predicate the application ships.

A REAL BUG, FOUND BY AN E2E SCREENSHOT, AND IT FAILED SILENTLY. The count subquery interpolated the Drizzle column: sql`... WHERE a.pack_instance_id = ${patientPackInstances.id}`. Drizzle rendered that as a.pack_instance_id = "id" - the BARE column name - and inside FROM appointments a the unqualified "id" resolves to a.id. So the predicate read a.pack_instance_id = a.id, which is never true. IT DID NOT ERROR: it returned 0 for every instance, so every pacote read as untouched and the agenda banner showed 10/10 after a booking. A wrong answer wearing the face of a valid one, section 1.3, in a query.

WHAT DID NOT CATCH IT, and this is the part worth keeping: the DB-gated test asserted the PREDICATE STRINGS against real Postgres and passed, because the strings were never the broken part. The broken part was how Drizzle rendered a correlation, and no test looked at generated SQL. That is LE-apply-block-expectation-drift in miniature INSIDE A SINGLE CARD - a proof that is about something adjacent to the thing that ships.

THREE THINGS CHANGED SO IT CANNOT RECUR: the caller now NAMES the outer column (packLinkedCountSql), pack-balance.test.ts PINS the generated SQL in both directions including an explicit assertion against the broken form, and the DB-gated test now IMPORTS the same function the application uses instead of writing its own copy of the subquery.

WHAT ACTUALLY FOUND IT: reading the Playwright artifact rather than reasoning. The screenshot said 10/10, which is a fact; I had talked myself through three wrong hypotheses before looking at it. The doctrine on OsteoJP-e2e-debugging is right - read the artifact FIRST.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-21, SELF-REPORTED BEFORE THE SITTING. THE HEADLINE HALF OF THIS CARD IS NOT DONE. ===

I reported "a pacote may now book N appointments" as delivered. IT IS NOT REACHABLE BY ANY USER, and I should have checked which code path the UI uses before claiming it.

WHAT I ACTUALLY CHANGED: the pacote+recurrence refusal inside createAppointment, on its `recurrence` parameter. THREE FACTS, each re-derived from main on 2026-08-21, make that unreachable:
  1. appointment-drawer.tsx line 678 sends `recurrence: null` - and it is the ONLY caller in the repository that passes the field at all. The recurrence branch of createAppointment has no live caller.
  2. The drawer's visible multi-booking control is AGENDAR LOTE, not recurrence. Its own comment says so: "Agendar lote (W2-10) - replaces the V1 recorrente control."
  3. The lote block is gated `{!editing && !form.packId && (` - HIDDEN whenever a pacote is selected - and `batchScheduleAppointments` takes no packId at all (zero occurrences in batch.ts).

So the guard I lifted was on a path nobody reaches, and the children-serviceId defect I found while lifting it is real but sits on that same unreachable path.

WHAT IS GENUINELY DELIVERED AND REACHABLE, unchanged by this correction: the derived balance, the link written on every single booking, consumir/restaurar deleted, sessions_remaining frozen with its guard, and the pack_insufficient refusal in the case that IS reachable - booking against a pacote with nothing left.

HOW IT HAPPENED, because the mechanism matters more than the instance: I read createAppointment, found a pack+recurrence guard whose comment described exactly the behaviour this card inverts, and lifted it. The comment was true when written and the code was live once. I never asked WHO CALLS THIS. Re-deriving the card's premises from main is a rule this project has paid for seven times, and I applied it to the SCHEMA and not to the CALL GRAPH.

THE REMAINING WORK IS CARDED AS RB-02b. It is not a small edit: it needs batchScheduleAppointments to accept and link a pacote, the lote gate to open for pacotes, and the balance refusal to move to the batch path.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-21 ON THE OWNER'S SCREENS. ===

OBSERVED: steps G-J confirmed by Ivan on app.osteojp.pt. An existing pacote read exactly the number it read before (G); Consumir and Restaurar are gone and the derived-sessions line is present (H); booking showed the balance and decremented it by one (I); cancelling returned the session (J).

G IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND IT PASSED. The production apply proved the balance identity arithmetically - V3 returned zero rows wrong - but "every existing balance is preserved exactly" only became a fact about the CLINIC when the owner opened a real patient and read the same number. It is now both.

cards.title: Make 'a Pacote of N books N appointments' actually reachable: teach Agendar lote about pacotes

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN ON THE DEPLOYED DRAWER, 2026-08-22. STEPS T AND M TO Q ALL PASS, ALL AS SPECIFIED. OBSERVED: the count box appears WITHOUT a patient selected; it TIGHTENS on patient selection; rows 2..N are empty; an incomplete list is REFUSED; three booked with the balance down by three; over-booking is REFUSED BY NAME; a busy slot books the free one and LISTS the busy one, with the balance down by one. BUILD HALF: five gates green 2026-08-21, packBatchIsOverbooked 5 cases + 5 labelled source guards.

cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-21 FROM MY OWN FALSE CLAIM. RB-02 reported this as delivered; it is not reachable by any user. The full account is on RB-02.

THE PREMISE, RE-DERIVED FROM main ON 2026-08-21 - check it again before building, because that is exactly what went wrong last time:
  - apps/web/app/agenda/appointment-drawer.tsx:678 sends `recurrence: null`, and it is the ONLY caller passing the field. createAppointment's recurrence branch has no live caller.
  - The visible multi-booking control is AGENDAR LOTE (W2-10), which its own comment says replaced the recorrente control.
  - The lote block is gated `{!editing && !form.packId && (` - hidden for pacotes since W8-01c.
  - apps/web/lib/scheduling/batch.ts contains ZERO occurrences of packId.

THE WORK, and it is three pieces rather than one edit:
  1. batchScheduleAppointments accepts a packId, resolves the instance ONCE via bookPackSessionTx, and writes pack_instance_id on every row it inserts - the same shape createAppointment already has.
  2. The balance refusal moves to the batch path: refuse by name when the batch is larger than the instance's available balance, inside the transaction, and REFUSE rather than truncate. Booking eight of the ten asked for looks like success and leaves reception to find the missing two in the diary.
  3. The lote gate opens for pacotes, and the serviceId forcing that createAppointment does must happen on the batch path too - otherwise every lote row records the pacote's chosen service rather than its base service.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE AND MUST NOT BE REDONE: the derived balance, the link on single bookings, the frozen-column guard, and packLinkedCountSql. This card is the reachability, not the model.

Q-RB-02-1 IS ABOUT THIS CARD, NOT ABOUT RB-02, and its text was corrected on 2026-08-21 for the same reason: it described reception setting a repeat count they cannot see. The INTERVAL question it asks stays open and stays clinical.

=== BUILT 2026-08-21 TO THE DISPATCHED SPEC. ===

THE CALL GRAPH WAS RE-DERIVED FIRST, which is the whole reason this card exists. batchScheduleAppointments has exactly two callers, both in appointment-drawer.tsx (the lote submit at 648 and rebookSlot at 793); createAppointment has one. Confirmed before a line was written.

WHAT SHIPPED:
- packId lives on BatchExplicitInput ONLY, never on BatchRecurrenceInput. The owner ruling "no interval control and no weekday recurrence for the pacote path" is therefore enforced BY TYPE: a caller has nowhere to put a rule alongside a pacote. A test asserts the two type bodies stay that way.
- The drawer reveals a pacote batch section when a Pacote is chosen: a COUNT pre-filled to the balance, capped at it, editable downwards, and then N date/time pickers. No weekday picker, no every-N-weeks, no generator, no end-mode. Row 1 is seeded from the form's own slot; ROWS 2..N START EMPTY, because seeding them would imply a spacing and the spacing is the clinic's decision (Q-RB-02-1). An empty row is REFUSED at submit rather than defaulted - defaulting it would book a real appointment at a time nobody chose.
- The engine resolves the pacote INSIDE the transaction via bookPackSessionTx, checks the cap, forces the base service onto every row, and writes pack_instance_id on every row. No new counter, no new query: the balance stays derived and the consumption is still the link itself, so a rolled-back batch spends nothing with no compensating update.
- Over-booking throws PackBatchRefused and the action maps it to the existing pack_insufficient code. CAUGHT BY TYPE rather than by message, so a reworded message cannot silently downgrade a named refusal into a generic one. It refuses, it never truncates.
- Partial booking is unchanged and still works: the engine books every free slot and reports each busy one, which is also how RB-03's disponibilidade enforcement reaches this path - classifyBatchSlots requires a slot to fit inside a FREE interval, and free is working-hours-minus-booked, so an out-of-hours slot cannot be booked here either.

ONE STRUCTURAL POINT WORTH RECORDING: a pacote batch now ALWAYS opens the transaction, even when nothing is bookable. The pre-existing early skip (toBook.length > 0) would otherwise swallow the over-booking refusal, because asking for five sessions from a pacote with three is an error whether or not the five slots are free.

WHAT THE NEW TESTS DO AND DO NOT PROVE, said on the tests themselves rather than left to be assumed: packBatchIsOverbooked is a pure decision and is proven outright. pack-batch-links.test.ts is a SOURCE GUARD over batch.ts - it proves the lines that write the link and force the service have not been deleted or renamed, which is the failure a later refactor of the insert would produce. It does not prove the column is written; that is proven one layer down by pack-derived-balance.db.test.ts against real Postgres through the production function.

STILL OPEN: the owner on the deployed drawer, and Q-RB-02-1, which is now exactly what it says it is - whether to pre-fill a count on a control that EXISTS. The count IS pre-filled as built; the interval question is moot because there is no interval control, by ruling.

=== SPEC APPROVED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-21, WITH A BINDING EXTENSION. ===

The dispatched spec is ratified as built: count pre-filled, capped, editable down, no interval, no weekday, every slot hand-picked, partial allowed, over-booking refused by name.

THE EXTENSION, verbatim in substance: selecting a pacote of N reveals N slot pickers in BOTH cases - a pacote the patient already HOLDS and one being ASSIGNED now. PACOTES ARE BOOKED IN ADVANCE, NEVER CONSUMED ONE APPOINTMENT AT A TIME. Count pre-filled to N, or to sessions remaining for a held instance.

=== DEFECT FOUND AT THE SITTING 2026-08-21: STEP L FAILED. CAUSE ESTABLISHED, THEN FIXED. ===

Ivan selected NESA 10 sessoes in Nova marcacao and saw no count box and no extra rows.

CAUSE 2a IS RULED OUT WITH EVIDENCE, not assumed: the GitHub deployment record for Production - osteojp-platform shows sha 42234617 (this card's own merge) deployed 2026-08-21T11:23:03Z, state success. RB-02b WAS live.

CAUSE 2b CONFIRMED, to the line: the block was gated {!editing && selectedPack && form.patientId && ...} and his Paciente field was empty. The pacote Select is not gated on a patient, so a pacote was selectable while the box that responds to it was not rendered - the screen offered the input and hid the consequence.

FIXED by dropping form.patientId from the gate. The ceiling then has two sources arriving at different times: the pacote's own sessionCount immediately, and a held instance's remaining balance once a patient is chosen. THE COUNT CAN THEREFORE TIGHTEN AFTER A PATIENT IS PICKED, and the visible list is DERIVED from the ceiling rather than synchronised to it - a useEffect calling setPackRows was written first and the lint rule refused it, correctly, as a cascading render.

THE ASSIGN-NOW PATH NEEDED NO NEW TRANSACTION WORK, verified rather than assumed: bookPackSessionTx registers the instance INSIDE the booking transaction when none exists, so the instance and its N appointments commit or roll back together. "A batch that half creates an instance" was never reachable. Pinned by a test rather than left as a claim.

=== CLOSED ON OBSERVATION 2026-08-22. STEPS T AND M TO Q, ALL AS SPECIFIED. ===

OBSERVED, step by step:
  the count box appears WITHOUT a patient selected;
  it TIGHTENS when a patient is selected;
  rows 2..N are empty;
  an incomplete list is REFUSED;
  three booked, with the balance down by three;
  over-booking is REFUSED BY NAME;
  a busy slot books the free one and LISTS the busy one, with the balance down
  by one.

THE PARTIAL-SUCCESS ARM IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED AND IT PASSED. "Books the free
one and lists the busy one, balance down by one" is the case where a batch
booking can silently lie in either direction - decrementing for a slot it did
not take, or taking a slot without decrementing. The observation names both
halves in one sentence: which slot was booked, and what the balance did. Either
alone would have been consistent with the wrong behaviour.

REFUSED BY NAME, NOT MERELY REFUSED. An over-booking that is refused without
saying WHO tells reception nothing they can act on with a patient in front of
them. The card asked for the name and the screen gave it.

THE COUNT BOX BEFORE A PATIENT IS SELECTED, AND TIGHTENING AFTER, is two
observations rather than one, and the second is the one a screen can fake: a box
that never changes looks identical to a box that is always right when the
starting figure happens to match. Both were seen.

BUILD EVIDENCE AND ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE ARE RECORDED SEPARATELY, per
PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.4: the merge was the build half and this sitting is the
evidence half.

cards.title: Port check-migration-functions.test.ts off the abandoned W13-04a branch onto main, then retire the branch

evidence.ref: PORTED 2026-08-21 onto a fresh branch off main. W13-04a tip sha at port time: c321fbf791081620849d78bf2cb743caffe20741, re-read rather than trusted. Four files ported byte-identically (verified by git hash-object against the branch blobs): packages/db/tests/check-migration-functions.test.ts, packages/db/scripts/check-migration-functions.d.mts, the stripSqlComments + IS_CLI upgrade to packages/db/scripts/check-migration-functions.mjs, and section 9 of docs/migration-apply-0059.md. Five gates green from the repo root; the ported test is 10 passing assertions in the ordinary pnpm test, not the DB-gated job.

cards.notes:
RULED 2026-08-20. PICK ORDER: DIRECTLY AFTER RB-02, which is why it carries RB-02's number with a suffix rather than a new one.

THE PREMISE IS DERIVED, NOT INHERITED, and both halves were checked against the live refs on 2026-08-20: packages/db/tests/check-migration-functions.test.ts EXISTS on origin/portal/W13-04a-availability-exclusion (tip c321fbf791081620849d78bf2cb743caffe20741, dated 2026-08-07, 3 commits ahead of main, tip NOT an ancestor of main) and does NOT exist on origin/main. Verified with git ls-tree -r --name-only on both refs, not from a card note.

PORT IT ONTO A FRESH BRANCH OFF main. Do not resurrect W13-04a, do not merge it, do not rebase it. The file is the deliverable; the branch is not.

THE PR OPENS AFTER #991 MERGES, NOT BEFORE, and the reason is mechanical rather than a matter of tidiness. main is frozen at 9f196b6 while migration 0067 is pinned for the apply, and this repository's branch protection has strict: true - every PR must be up to date with main to merge. Any merge to main before #991 lands forces another rebase of the 0067 branch, which changes its head, which voids the pinned sha. The apply block's own stop condition is that the applied sha must equal the merged sha.

AFTER THE PORT PR MERGES, TWO CLOSING STEPS, in this order: re-read the tip sha of origin/portal/W13-04a-availability-exclusion and RECORD IT ON THIS CARD (c321fbf791081620849d78bf2cb743caffe20741 as read on 2026-08-20, re-read rather than trusted at the time); then DELETE the branch. Deleting a remote branch whose content is preserved on main loses nothing, which is the condition PORTAL-REHYDRATE section 7.0 sets for retiring a tree or a branch. Recording the sha first is what makes the deletion reversible: a deleted branch is recoverable from its sha and unfindable without it.

WHAT THIS CARD DOES NOT DECIDE: whether the other two commits on W13-04a carry anything worth keeping. Read them when you port; if they do, that is a separate card and the branch is not deleted until it is resolved.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-20: migration 0067 is APPLIED TO PRODUCTION and #991 merged. Receipt at docs/migration-apply-0067.md section 10. Main is no longer frozen.

=== PORTED 2026-08-21. THE CARD SAID ONE FILE; IT IS FOUR, AND THREE OF THEM ARE NOT OPTIONAL. ===

THE TEST CANNOT STAND ALONE, which the card could not have known and which reading the branch answered in one diff. check-migration-functions.test.ts imports { stripSqlComments } from ../scripts/check-migration-functions.mjs. Main's copy of that script has no such export AND reads process.argv at module scope, so importing it from a test would print the usage message and process.exit(2) at import time. Commit c321fbf added BOTH halves together: the stripSqlComments export plus an IS_CLI guard so the module can be imported without running as a CLI. Porting the test without the script would not have been a weaker port, it would have been a broken one.

WHAT THE OTHER TWO COMMITS CARRY, read at port time as the card requires:
  566c4b6 - migration 0059 itself, its supabase mirror, the journal entry, store.ts and day-availability.ts changes, pedido-does-not-block.db.test.ts, and the first version of the checker. ALL OF IT IS ON MAIN OR SUPERSEDED ON MAIN. cards.title: Read-only recon: did the content of fix/portal-dashboard-getsession ever land on main?

evidence.ref: READ-ONLY RECON COMPLETE 2026-08-21. Branch origin/fix/portal-dashboard-getsession, tip 1f5326f9df0c36dbfa47a5bfd405c5f7160a0d06, 9 commits, 4 files differing from main. VERDICT PER FILE: 1 LANDED, 3 OBSOLETE, 0 UNLANDED. Nothing was changed, nothing merged, nothing deleted - the branch is untouched and still on the remote. Full per-file account in the card notes.

cards.notes:
RULED 2026-08-20. READ-ONLY, AND THE SCOPE IS THE POINT: inspect commits and diffs, report the finding on this card, CHANGE NOTHING, MERGE NOTHING, DELETE NOTHING. Low priority.

DERIVED 2026-08-20 FROM THE LIVE REFS: origin/fix/portal-dashboard-getsession exists, tip 1f5326f9df0c36dbfa47a5bfd405c5f7160a0d06, dated 2026-06-17, 9 commits ahead of origin/main, and the tip is NOT an ancestor of main.

ANCESTRY IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A CARD RATHER THAN A ONE-LINER. Every merge in this repository is a SQUASH, which rewrites the sha, so 'not an ancestor of main' is the expected reading for a branch whose content landed months ago and for a branch that was abandoned - it cannot tell the two apart. The question is about CONTENT, and only a per-file diff against main answers it.

METHOD: git diff origin/main...origin/fix/portal-dashboard-getsession, file by file; for each file that still differs, read the change and establish whether the same change is present on main under a different sha, or whether main has since moved past it in a way that makes the branch's version obsolete. Three verdicts are possible and they are not the same: LANDED (content on main), OBSOLETE (superseded by different work), UNLANDED (a real change nobody has). Say which, per file. A single overall verdict on a 9-commit branch would be the conflation section 1.3 warns about.

OUTPUT IS A FINDING WRITTEN ON THIS CARD, in those terms, with the shas that support it. WHETHER TO DELETE THE BRANCH IS THE OWNER'S DECISION AND IS OUT OF SCOPE HERE - the recon exists so that decision has evidence under it, which is exactly what it does not have today.

=== RECON COMPLETE 2026-08-21. READ-ONLY. NOTHING CHANGED, NOTHING DELETED. ===

Branch tip 1f5326f9df0c36dbfa47a5bfd405c5f7160a0d06 (2026-06-17), 9 commits, 4 files differing from main. THE ANCESTRY TEST REMAINS USELESS AND THE PER-FILE DIFF ANSWERED IT, exactly as the card predicted.

VERDICT PER FILE. One LANDED, three OBSOLETE, ZERO UNLANDED.

1. apps/api/lib/supabase/middleware.ts - LANDED.
   The substantive change IS on main: await supabase.auth.getSession() replacing getUser(), identical call. Only the comment prose differs, and main's is a tightened rewrite of the same reasoning about patient JWTs carrying role='patient' and the auth server answering 403. This is the fix the branch is named after and it is in production.

2. apps/portal/app/portal/dashboard/page.tsx - OBSOLETE, AND DELIBERATELY REVERSED.
   The branch wraps getMyAppointments() in try { } catch { /* non-fatal - show empty state rather than error boundary */ }. MAIN REMOVED EXACTLY THAT, on purpose, with a comment saying why: the swallow "left the list EMPTY and the page rendered 'Nao tem consultas agendadas' - telling a patient with a real appointment tomorrow that they have none". Main now uses Promise.all so a failure reaches error.tsx. The branch also adds a user_metadata.first_name fallback that main deleted with the same swallow it served. RESTORING ANY OF THIS WOULD REINTRODUCE A FIXED DEFECT.

3. apps/portal/app/portal/dashboard/error.tsx - OBSOLETE.
   Same component, and main is a strict superset: i18n keys instead of hardcoded pt-PT strings, plus <ClinicPhones /> in the description so a patient who cannot load the page gets a number to ring.

4. apps/portal/app/portal/account/page.tsx - OBSOLETE, same family as 2.
   The branch does getSession() then try/catch degrade to auth-user name and email. LE-portal-supabase-residue removed precisely that on 2026-08-07, and main carries the reasoning: the fallback "could never fire" because Decision D routes every patient through OTP and WF-07 refuses to link a patient row that already has an auth user, so the branch was structurally unreachable - and the try/catch was "the same class of lie the dashboard told about appointments".

THE FINDING IN ONE LINE: the branch's one real fix is on main, and its other three files are the pre-fix versions of code this project has since deliberately hardened. THERE IS NOTHING ON IT THAT MAIN WANTS.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, because this card is read-only: the branch is untouched and still on the remote. WHETHER TO DELETE IT IS THE OWNER'S DECISION AND IS OUT OF THIS CARD'S SCOPE. The recon exists so that decision has evidence under it, and the evidence says deletion loses nothing - but the tip sha above should be recorded wherever that decision is taken, as RB-02a did for W13-04a.
