cards.title: An apply block's verification expectations drift from the migration they check, and nothing mechanical ties the two
cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-20, FROM A REAL FALSE STOP DURING THE 0067 APPLY. Not hypothetical: V5 expected still_reads_notifications FALSE, production correctly returned TRUE, and a production sitting halted on a document defect while the database was fine.

THE MECHANISM, and it is boring, which is the problem. 208e753 authored migration 0067 with is_unconfirmed_pedido keyed on origin ALONE, and authored the V5 expectation to match. 2642c35 changed the function to a DISJUNCTION - forced by pedido-does-not-block.db.test.ts going red on five assertions - and touched the SQL, the supabase mirror, the RLS test and the write path. It did not touch docs/migration-apply-0067.md. Five later commits did touch that document, including a complete rebuild from the runbook after a five-defect rejection, and not one revisited V5.

WHY NO EXISTING GATE CATCHES IT. The migration is SQL under packages/db; the verification is prose-embedded SQL inside a markdown file under docs. Nothing parses the second, nothing links them, and CI has no reason to. Every check in this repository passed on every one of those six commits.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE STALE-SHA DEFECT IT RHYMES WITH. A stale sha stops an apply that should have run - loud, recoverable, nothing changed. A stale expectation stops an apply that DID run and ran correctly, at the moment of least tolerance for ambiguity: mid sitting, credentials live, the operator asked to judge whether production is broken. The 0067 case was one grep from a rollback of a correct migration.

WHAT A FIX MIGHT LOOK LIKE, and none of these is chosen yet - the card is the finding, and the design is the work:
  A. A test that extracts the fenced SQL from the apply document and asserts every object and function it names exists in the migration it cites. Catches renames and drops; does NOT catch a changed predicate, which is exactly what happened here.
  B. Make the expectation derive from the migration rather than restate it - the V5 arm becomes a generated assertion over the committed function body. Strongest, and the most work.
  C. Cheapest and possibly sufficient: a required check that fails when a migration SQL file changes in a commit that does not also touch its apply document. Crude, noisy on comment-only edits, and it would have caught THIS instance outright at 2642c35.

RECOMMENDED START: C, because it is a few lines and it fires on the exact commit shape that produced this. Then B for the arms that carry a verdict. NOT A: it proves a test ran without proving it tested the right subject, which is criterion F on ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep.

RELATED: docs/migration-apply-0065.md section 0 records the same FAMILY one layer out - an author building from a sibling document instead of the committed runbook. This card is the machine-checkable half of that lesson.

cards.title: /recuperacao crashed in production: a correlated subquery bound a column to itself and the page formatted the resulting null

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN ON app.osteojp.pt AGAINST DEPLOYED 916f131, 2026-08-21. STEP R PASSES. The page renders: the header 'Recuperacao de utentes', the subtitle, the message hint, and ONE POPULATED ROW carrying the patient's name, 'Ultima consulta 03/08/2026', 'Terapeuta Durbis Brito' and 'Sem numero registado', with Email and Adiar as the only buttons offered. The contact-mark note line is present, and the Adiados section reads 'Nenhum paciente adiado.' A NON-EMPTY LIST IS WHAT MAKES THIS EVIDENCE: every one of the four defects needed a real row to be reachable, and the empty page rendered correctly throughout the incident.

cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-21 FROM THE SITTING. Ivan opened /recuperacao on app.osteojp.pt as the owner and got the Next production error page: 'An error occurred in the Server Components render... A digest property is included'.

ROOT CAUSE, NAMED TO THE LINE AND FOUND WITHOUT PRODUCTION ACCESS. apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts built the lastAttendanceAt and practitionerName SELECT expressions inline and interpolated the Drizzle column: sql`... WHERE (done.patient_id = ${patients.id} ...)`. DRIZZLE RENDERS THAT AS THE BARE "id", not "patients"."id". Inside FROM appointments done the unqualified "id" binds to done.id, so the predicate read done.patient_id = done.id - never true. max() over zero rows returned NULL, and apps/web/app/recuperacao/page.tsx called toLocaleDateString on it. A TypeError inside a Server Component is exactly the digest-only error he saw.

THE WHERE CLAUSE WAS NEVER WRONG, which is why this took the shape it did. It used the shared, explicitly-qualified builders from followup-selection.ts, so the RIGHT patients were selected and only their date came back null. THE CRASH THEREFORE FIRES ONLY WHEN THE LIST IS NON-EMPTY - and the owner sees every patient in the tenant, so he is the most likely person in the clinic to have a row. A located receptionist with an empty list would have seen the page work.

IT IS THE SAME BUG AS THE RB-02 FIX, IN THE FILE NEXT DOOR, ONE DAY LATER, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. packLinkedCountSql was written on 2026-08-20 for exactly this - a Drizzle-interpolated column rendering bare and silently binding to the wrong table - complete with a generated-SQL pin asserting the broken form. I fixed it there, wrote a test for it there, and did not audit the sibling query I had written the day before with the identical shape. THE LESSON IS NOT 'qualify your columns'. It is that finding a defect class obliges a sweep for that class, and a pin written for one call site is not a pin for the pattern.

SENTRY: THE MECHANISM IS PRESENT AND I CANNOT CONFIRM THE EVENT. apps/web/instrumentation.ts:13 exports onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError, which is the hook Next requires for Server Component errors to reach Sentry, so a capture SHOULD have happened. Whether this specific event landed needs Sentry access this terminal does not have and must not acquire. STATED AS TWO SEPARATE FACTS deliberately: 'the hook is wired' is checkable from the repository and is checked; 'the event was captured' is not, and reporting the first as the second is the conflation this project keeps finding.

FIXED: both SELECT expressions moved into followup-selection.ts as builders that take the outer expression from the CALLER, beside the WHERE clauses that already did. queries.ts names it once as PATIENT_ID. packages/db/tests/followup-sql.test.ts pins what they render, in both directions, including an explicit assertion against the broken form - the test that would have caught this and did not exist. followup-selection.db.test.ts gains three arms against real Postgres asserting the VALUE rather than merely non-null, because a non-null assertion would pass against a subquery correlated to the WRONG patient.

AND THE ROUTE HAD NO ERROR BOUNDARY, which is why he saw the raw framework page rather than Portuguese. apps/web/app/recuperacao/error.tsx now exists: pt-PT, a retry, and both clinic numbers so somebody can still be reached while the page is down. It reports the failure - it does NOT render an empty list, because 'nobody to contact' and 'this page is broken' are the two screens that must never look alike.

THE NULL GUARD IN page.tsx IS NOT THE FIX AND IS LABELLED AS SUCH. A null is honestly reachable - a patient with no completed attendance yields one - so day() renders an em dash rather than a plausible-looking date. A fallback date would be a clinical claim nobody made.

=== REOPENED 2026-08-21. THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS OF A REAL BUG THAT WAS NOT THE CAUSE. ===

Ivan re-ran step R on edfd2643 and got the PORTUGUESE error boundary - so the fix deployed, the boundary half WORKS, and the page still did not render.

THE SECOND ROOT CAUSE, NAMED TO THE LINE, AND THERE ARE TWO INSTANCES OF IT.
apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts selected `u.full_name` in two queries whose FROM clause never defined a `u`:
  - the contact-marks query, .from(sql`patient_followup_contacts c`).leftJoin(users, ...)
  - listActivePostponements, .from(sql`patient_followup_postponements p`).leftJoin(users, ...)
Drizzle emits `left join "users"`, NOT `left join users u` - it knows nothing about an alias typed inside a string - so both statements referenced a table that was not in scope. Postgres answers 42P01, missing FROM-clause entry for table "u".

listActivePostponements RUNS ON EVERY REQUEST, in Promise.all beside the candidates query. So it threw whether or not a single patient qualified. THE PAGE HAD NEVER RENDERED FOR ANYONE, EVER - not for the owner, not for anybody, empty list or not.

THAT ALSO CORRECTS MY FIRST REPORT. I said the null-date TypeError was the cause and that the crash fired only on a non-empty list. The null-date bug was REAL and the fix was necessary, but it can never have been what Ivan saw: the postponements query throws in parallel, and the marks query throws before the page formats anything. I generated SQL for the two subqueries I suspected and stopped, rather than for every query on the path. That is the same error one level up - a pin for a call site is not a pin for the path.

THE MECHANISM, NOW CHARACTERISED PRECISELY RATHER THAN AS FOLKLORE: Drizzle qualifies a column reference ONLY when more than one table is in scope. In a JOINED select it emits "appointments"."id"; in a SINGLE-TABLE select it emits the bare "id". A bare name inside a correlated subquery then binds to the subquery's own table. Proven both ways by generated SQL, and it is what makes the sweep tractable: the at-risk shape is a SINGLE-TABLE select containing a correlated subquery, plus any raw FROM alias that Drizzle did not create.

FIXED by rebuilding both queries on the SCHEMA TABLES - patientFollowupContacts and patientFollowupPostponements have been in the schema since 0067 - so the aliases are Drizzle's own and cannot disagree with themselves. The cure is not to hand-write "users"."full_name"; it is to stop hand-writing the FROM clause. That also removed a second latent defect in the postponements select, which had two output columns named id and two named full_name and was relying on positional mapping.

THE ERROR BOUNDARY HALF PASSES AND CLOSES. It did exactly what it was built for: it turned a raw English framework page into Portuguese with a retry and the clinic numbers, and it is how Ivan could tell "the fix deployed" from "the fix did not deploy" in one glance. That distinction was written into step R and it earned its place on the first use.

=== A THIRD DEFECT, AND THE NEW E2E CAUGHT IT ON ITS FIRST RUN. ===

The candidates query failed with: Failed query: select "id", "full_name", ... [cause] TypeError: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received an instance of Date.

CAUSE: the window instants were bound as bare Date objects inside a fragment assembled with sql.raw, so Drizzle had NO COLUMN TYPE to encode them against - unlike gt(table.column, now), where the column tells it what to do. With no type hint the postgres driver is handed a Date it cannot serialise.

FIXED by binding them as ISO strings with an explicit ::timestamptz cast. STILL PARAMETERISED - $n::timestamptz with the string bound, not interpolated text - so the original reasoning about now being a caller-supplied parameter still holds. Verified by generating the statement and checking the param types are strings.

THIS IS THE THIRD DEFECT ON ONE PAGE AND IT WOULD HAVE SURVIVED BOTH PREVIOUS FIXES. The page would have crashed again, a third time, in front of Ivan. The e2e that the dispatch required found it in CI on the first run instead - which is the entire argument for the test, made better than any of my reasoning could have made it.

=== A FOURTH DEFECT, ALSO CAUGHT BY THE NEW E2E. ===

TypeError: d.toLocaleDateString is not a function. NOT null - NOT A DATE. lastAttendanceAt was typed sql<Date>, and that annotation is a CLAIM TO TYPESCRIPT, NOT A DECODER. Drizzle converts a timestamptz to a Date when it reads a KNOWN COLUMN, because the column carries its type; a raw sql fragment carries nothing, so the driver value comes through as a string.

It is a DIFFERENT error from the null one and needed a different fix, which is why the null guard did not catch it: a non-empty string is truthy.

FIXED by typing the fragment string | null - what it actually is - and converting once at the boundary. FollowupCandidate.lastAttendanceAt is now Date | null, honestly.

SWEEP FOR THE SAME LYING TYPE, repo-wide: three sql<Date> raw fragments exist. TWO ARE SAFE AND BOTH CONVERT AT THE BOUNDARY with new Date(...) - packages/db/src/migration/health.ts:79 and apps/web/lib/reminders/unreachable-by-sms.ts:110. I nearly reported the second as a latent crash on the landline section Ivan had just signed off, and it is not one, because I read to the end of the function rather than stopping at the select. THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNEW THE PATTERN; my /recuperacao code was the outlier that did not follow it.

FOUR DEFECTS ON ONE PAGE, AND THE FAMILY IS ONE THING: every single one was a CLAIM THE RUNTIME DID NOT HONOUR. A column reference that bound to another table. An alias that did not exist. A Date the driver could not encode. A type that did not convert. sql<T> is the most convincing of the four because it type-checks.

=== THE PAGE RENDERS. Confirmed by screenshot from the e2e run, 2026-08-21. ===

The Playwright artifact shows the whole page working: both candidates with their dates and therapist, the landline row with NO WhatsApp/SMS/Email and both absences NAMED in words, the mobile row with all three channels, the contact mark reading "WhatsApp Contactado por E2E Therapist em 20/08/2026, 14:48", and the Adiados section carrying the postponed patient with Trazer de volta.

THE LAST RED TEST WAS MY LOCATOR, NOT THE PRODUCT. The unanchored date pattern also matched the contact line, so it resolved to two elements and Playwright strict mode failed it - a red test over a correct page. Anchored.

WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the e2e found three of the four defects, in the order they were reachable, and each one was invisible to every other gate. Lint, typecheck, unit tests, the DB-gated suite and the build were green through all four.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-21 ON THE OWNER'S SCREEN. ALL FOUR DEFECTS PROVEN FIXED ON PRODUCTION. ===

OBSERVED: /recuperacao renders on app.osteojp.pt against deployed 916f131, with a POPULATED row - name, Ultima consulta 03/08/2026, Terapeuta Durbis Brito, Sem numero registado, Email and Adiar only, the contact-mark note, and Adiados reading 'Nenhum paciente adiado.'

WHY A POPULATED ROW IS THE EVIDENCE AND AN EMPTY ONE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN: every defect needed a real row to be reachable. The postponements query threw on every request; the marks query only ran on a non-empty list; the null-date and the string-not-Date both needed a row to format. The empty page rendered correctly all the way through, which is exactly why nobody caught this before he opened it.

THE VERCEL LOGS CORROBORATED THE DIAGNOSIS EXACTLY, and are worth recording: digest 751482798 'missing FROM-clause entry for table "u"' (the postponements query, the one that ran unconditionally) and digest 3564027797 'Received an instance of Date' (the timestamp binding). NO LOG ENTRY NAMED A DEFECT NOT ALREADY FIXED, and the two that appear are precisely the two whose reachability order was predicted. The other two were found by the e2e, because production never got far enough to reach them.

THE SCREENSHOT ALSO SHOWED A REAL COPY DEFECT, carded and fixed separately: 'Sem numero registado' rendered twice on a row with no phone. See RB-01.

cards.title: Drizzle emits a BARE column in a single-table select, and a bare name inside a correlated subquery binds to the wrong table

evidence.ref: SWEEP EXECUTED 2026-08-21 across apps and packages. Predicate: every raw sql`` fragment containing a correlated subquery or a hand-written FROM/JOIN alias. 8 sites found. 5 were defects and are fixed (4 in apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts, 1 in apps/web/lib/packs/instances.ts, fixed 2026-08-20). 3 are ruled SAFE with generated SQL as evidence, not by reading: apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts colorKey/hasNote/noteCount and apps/web/lib/scheduling/guest-requests.ts matches, all of which sit in MULTI-TABLE selects where Drizzle qualifies every reference.

cards.notes:
CARDED AND EXECUTED 2026-08-21, after this class produced FIVE defects in three files in two days: the pacote linked-count (RB-02), two /recuperacao SELECT expressions, and two /recuperacao FROM aliases. It was overdue and it was carded only because a dispatch said so, which is itself the finding - I fixed the first instance, wrote a pin for it, and did not sweep.

THE RULE, ESTABLISHED BY GENERATING SQL BOTH WAYS RATHER THAN BY READING DOCS:
  - MULTI-TABLE select (any join present): Drizzle emits "appointments"."id" - fully qualified, SAFE inside a subquery.
  - SINGLE-TABLE select: Drizzle emits the bare "id" - and inside a correlated subquery with its own FROM, that bare name binds to the SUBQUERY's table.
  - A hand-written alias in a raw FROM or JOIN (`sql`table t``) is never known to Drizzle, so any `t.col` elsewhere in the statement is a reference Drizzle did not create and may not have emitted.

NEITHER FAILS LOUDLY IN THE SAME WAY. The bare-column case returns a WRONG ANSWER silently - the predicate is simply never true. The unknown-alias case throws 42P01 at runtime. The first is worse and is the one that shipped twice.

SITES, EACH WITH ITS VERDICT AND ITS EVIDENCE:
  1. apps/web/lib/packs/instances.ts linkedCount - DEFECT, fixed 2026-08-20 (packLinkedCountSql), pinned in pack-balance.test.ts.
  2. apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts lastAttendanceAt - DEFECT, fixed 2026-08-21 (followupLastAttendanceSql), pinned.
  3. apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts practitionerName - DEFECT, fixed 2026-08-21 (followupPractitionerSql), pinned.
  4. apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts contact marks - DEFECT (42P01 on `u`), fixed 2026-08-21 by rebuilding on patientFollowupContacts.
  5. apps/web/lib/followup/queries.ts listActivePostponements - DEFECT (42P01 on `u`, on EVERY request), fixed 2026-08-21 by rebuilding on patientFollowupPostponements.
  6. apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts colorKey - SAFE. Multi-table select; generated SQL emits "appointments"."practitioner_id".
  7. apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts hasNote and noteCount - SAFE, same statement, same reason. Generated SQL emits "appointments"."id".
  8. apps/web/lib/scheduling/guest-requests.ts matches - SAFE. Two leftJoins, so qualified; and its own comment already stated the reasoning, which is why it was written correctly.

WHY NO STATIC GUARD WAS ADDED, considered and rejected: the property is about what DRIZZLE EMITS, not about the source text, so a grep-based guard would flag the three safe sites and miss any new unsafe one written differently. The instrument that actually works is the generated-SQL pin, and there is now one per risky helper. If this class recurs a fourth time, the next step is a test that renders every query in these modules through toSQL() and asserts no bare quoted identifier appears inside a subquery - real, and more work than it is worth today.

cards.title: Nobody has ever confirmed Sentry actually receives a server-side error from the staff platform

evidence.ref: OBSERVED BY IVAN IN SENTRY'S OWN ISSUE LIST, project osteojp-web, 2026-08-22. The list shows: 'OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY 2026-08-24T14:48:41.512Z - deliberate t...', Unhandled, GET /admin/sentry-check, last seen 2 minutes, 1 event. THIS IS SENTRY'S LIST, NOT OUR CHECK PAGE, which is the entire distinction this card was open for. ANSWER (b) of the card's own lettered question: capture was BROKEN, and the cause was that the DSN never reached Production. It now works. Build half: PR #1008.

cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-21 FROM INC-12. It cannot be closed from this terminal and saying so is the point.

WHAT IS VERIFIABLE FROM THE REPOSITORY, AND IS VERIFIED: apps/web/instrumentation.ts:13 exports onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError. That is the hook Next requires for a Server Component error to reach Sentry, and it is present.

WHAT IS NOT VERIFIABLE FROM HERE, AND MUST NOT BE CLAIMED EITHER WAY: whether any event has ever ARRIVED. That needs the Sentry project, which standing rule 1 puts out of reach, and the two facts are routinely conflated - 'the hook is wired' reads as 'errors are captured' to anybody skimming.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: /recuperacao threw on EVERY REQUEST from the moment it deployed. If Sentry were receiving and anybody were watching, the incident would have been found by the instrument rather than by the owner opening the page during a sitting. Either the events are not arriving, or they are arriving and nothing routes them to a person. Both are worth knowing and only one is a code problem.

THE EXACT STEPS FOR IVAN, and none of them touch production data:
  1. Open the Sentry project for the staff platform (osteojp-platform) and set the time filter to 2026-08-21.
  2. Search for issues on the route /recuperacao, or for the message 'missing FROM-clause entry for table'.
  3. Report ONE of three answers: (a) the issue is there - then capture works and the gap is alerting; (b) no issue at all - then capture is broken and that is its own build; (c) the project has no events from the staff platform ever - then it was never wired to a live DSN.
  4. If (a), paste the digest so the two records can be tied together.

IF THE ANSWER IS (b) OR (c), THE FOLLOW-UP IS A BUILD, not a configuration note: a deliberate throw behind an owner-only route, deployed, and observed arriving. An error reporter nobody has seen report an error is not a reporter.

=== ANSWERED 2026-08-21 BY OBSERVATION: (c). NEVER WIRED. ===

Ivan opened the project directly. It shows the ONBOARDING screen, step 2 Verify never completed. Zero events, ever. Not "we cannot tell" and not "probably not" - observed.

DIAGNOSIS, SEPARATING WHAT THE REPOSITORY CAN ANSWER FROM WHAT IT CANNOT.

CHECKABLE FROM THE REPO, AND CHECKED - ALL OF IT IS CORRECT:
  - apps/web/instrumentation.ts registers sentry.server.config on the nodejs runtime and sentry.edge.config on edge, and exports onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError.
  - sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts both call Sentry.init.
  - instrumentation-client.ts calls Sentry.init and exports onRouterTransitionStart.
  - next.config.ts wraps the config in withSentryConfig for source maps.
  - .env.example declares SENTRY_DSN, NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_ORG, SENTRY_PROJECT.
  - Nothing anywhere disables Sentry in production. There is no enabled:false, no environment check gating init, no beforeSend returning null unconditionally (beforeSend is stripFrameVars, which scrubs and returns the event).

NOT CHECKABLE FROM THE REPO: whether SENTRY_DSN is SET in the Vercel Production environment for osteojp-platform. That is the only remaining candidate and it is the likely one, because of what an unset DSN does.

THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE WHOLE STORY: Sentry.init({ dsn: undefined }) IS A SILENT NO-OP. The SDK initialises, captureException still returns an event id, onRequestError still fires - and nothing is sent. No warning, no throw, no difference visible from inside the process. Section 1.3 at the deployment layer: a missing value maps onto the harmless-looking case and the system carries on reporting something reasonable. NOBODY MISSED A WARNING BECAUSE THERE WAS NONE TO MISS.

FIXED IN THE REPO: lib/observability/sentry-dsn.ts. The DSN is read through an accessor that logs LOUDLY, once, when it is absent outside development - naming the variable, never the value, and saying that events are being DISCARDED rather than merely unconfigured. Six tests, including that it stays quiet in development (a warning everyone ignores is worse than none) and that it never prints the value.

BUILT: /admin/sentry-check, owner only, which reports whether the DSN is configured (boolean, never the value) and throws a marked error on ?throw=1 - OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY plus a timestamp. It throws from a SERVER COMPONENT RENDER deliberately: that is the exact path INC-12 took and the exact path onRequestError claims to cover. A captureException call would have tested the transport while skipping the hook whose coverage is the open question.

=== PARTIAL PROGRESS 2026-08-22, AND IT IS NOT THE PROOF. STAYS in_flight. ===

OWNER, 2026-08-22: THE DSN REACHED THE BUILD AND THE CHECK PAGE REPORTS
"configurado".

THAT IS NOT THE THING THIS CARD IS OPEN FOR, and the distinction is the whole
card. "Configured" is a statement about OUR OWN ENVIRONMENT read by our own
code. The open question is whether an event ARRIVES IN SENTRY. Those are
different facts and the check page cannot tell them apart - it can only report
what it can see, which is a variable being present.

NO EVENT HAS BEEN OBSERVED ARRIVING. The card's answer of 2026-08-21 was
observation (c): Ivan opened the Sentry project and found the ONBOARDING screen,
step 2 Verify NOT completed, ZERO EVENTS EVER. What changes that verdict is the
Sentry issue list showing an issue, not our page showing a green word.

THIS IS THE SAME CONFLATION SECTION 1.3 DESCRIBES, ONE LAYER OUT, and it is
worth naming because the progress is real and encouraging and still proves
nothing: a signal that reports on the SENDER's state gets read as a report on
the RECEIVER's. Every one of the four instances in that section had exactly this
shape - the system carried on reporting something reasonable.

WHAT CLOSES IT: trigger the capture deliberately, then look in the SENTRY
PROJECT and see the issue listed there, with its timestamp. The evidence is a
screenshot of Sentry's own issue list, never of our check page.

=== CLOSED ON OBSERVATION 2026-08-22. AN EVENT ARRIVED. ===

OBSERVED, in Sentry's own issue list for project osteojp-web:
"OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY 2026-08-24T14:48:41.512Z - deliberate t...", Unhandled,
GET /admin/sentry-check, last seen 2 minutes, 1 event.

IT IS SENTRY'S LIST AND NOT OUR CHECK PAGE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF WHY THIS CARD
STAYED OPEN THROUGH A GREEN-LOOKING INTERMEDIATE STATE. On 2026-08-22 the DSN had
reached the build and /admin/sentry-check reported "configurado" - a statement
about our own environment, read by our own code. This card refused that as proof
and it was right to: "configured" and "an event arrives" are different facts and
the check page cannot tell them apart. The evidence is the receiver's record, and
now there is one.

=== THE ANSWER IS (b), AND IT IS WORTH SAYING HOW IT RELATES TO (c). ===

RECORDED AS (b) BY OWNER RULING: capture was BROKEN, and that was its own build
rather than a configuration note. The cause: THE DSN NEVER REACHED PRODUCTION.

The 2026-08-21 observation on this card recorded (c) - zero events ever, the
onboarding screen, step 2 Verify never completed. THE TWO ARE NOT IN CONFLICT AND
A LATER READER SHOULD NOT SPEND TIME RECONCILING THEM. (c) was the SYMPTOM as it
presented on 2026-08-21, seen from the Sentry side: a project that had never
received anything. (b) is the SETTLED VERDICT on what it took to fix: a build,
not a setting - which is exactly what the card said would follow if the answer
were (b) or (c). PR #1008 is that build.

THE CARD'S OWN PREDICTION HELD, verbatim from the step list above: "IF THE ANSWER
IS (b) OR (c), THE FOLLOW-UP IS A BUILD, not a configuration note: a deliberate
throw behind an owner-only route, deployed, and observed arriving. An error
reporter nobody has seen report an error is not a reporter." That is precisely
what happened, and the observation above is the "observed arriving".

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, said so it is not read as more than it is. Capture
works. ALERTING DOES NOT FOLLOW FROM IT. The card's own (a) branch names alerting
as a separate gap, and nothing about this observation establishes that a human is
told when an event arrives. /recuperacao threw on every request for a day and was
found by the owner opening the page; an event landing in a list nobody watches
would have been found the same way. Routing an arrival to a person is not carded
here and is not claimed here.

cards.title: CONDITIONAL: re-walk the estate for env vars whose absence a third-party dependency swallows - activates on a SECOND member of the class
cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-21 BY STRATEGY RULING, and it is DORMANT BY DESIGN. Do not start it. It activates only when a SECOND member of the class is found.

THE CLASS: an environment variable whose absence is absorbed by a THIRD-PARTY dependency rather than by our code, so it degrades silently and no estate walk of ours can see it. The loudness is not ours to provide and its absence is invisible in our source.

THE FIRST AND ONLY KNOWN MEMBER: SENTRY_DSN. Sentry.init({ dsn: undefined }) accepts the call and discards every event, silently, forever. PG7's estate walk (#843) enumerated variables and asked 'does this fail loudly'; it passed over this one correctly by its own method, because our code does nothing wrong.

WHY IT IS DORMANT RATHER THAN QUEUED. One member is an incident with a fix; two members are a PATTERN and the walk is then worth its cost. Starting it on one is speculative work on a launch runway, and the fix already shipped makes THIS variable loud. PG7 stays PASS by the same ruling.

WHAT WOULD ACTIVATE IT: any second variable found where a dependency accepts an absent value and carries on. Candidate shapes worth recognising if one turns up: an SDK init that takes a key, a client constructor that takes a URL, an analytics or feature-flag provider that no-ops without credentials.

WHEN IT ACTIVATES, THE WALK IS NOT THE #843 WALK AGAIN. That one asked our code whether it fails loudly. This one asks each DEPENDENCY what it does with an absent value - which is a different question, answered by reading the dependency or by testing it with the value removed, not by reading us.

cards.title: Reception attests PERMANENTLY that a patient accepted 'as condicoes da clinica', and the platform holds no such document - site 2 of the cited-document class, and it is LIVE

evidence.ref: CLOSED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-24, NOT BY A BUILD. A PAPER CONDICOES DOCUMENT EXISTS AND PATIENTS PHYSICALLY SIGN IT. That reverses this card's recommendation: the checkbox records a REAL EVENT and STAYS LIVE. NEITHER DISABLE ARM WAS BUILT - not the UI condition in SignatureConsent.tsx, not the refusal in recordTermsAcceptance. The remaining work is which document TERMS_VERSION names, which is LE-terms-version-switch-on-jp-text.

cards.notes:
RAISED BY THE CITED-DOCUMENT SWEEP, 2026-08-21, CONFIRMED AGAINST main 2026-08-24.
RECOMMENDATION ONLY. NOTHING IS BUILT AND NOTHING SHOULD BE UNTIL IVAN RULES.

WHAT IS LIVE TODAY. apps/web/app/clinical/[id]/SignatureConsent.tsx renders a
checkbox on the ficha labelled clinical.termsCheckboxLabel - "O paciente aceitou
as condicoes da clinica" - with clinical.termsHelp beneath it: "Fica associado ao
PACIENTE, nao a esta ficha, e nao pode ser alterado nem apagado depois de
gravado." Ticking it calls recordTermsAcceptance and writes a row to
patient_terms_acceptances.

THE PLATFORM CANNOT DISPLAY THOSE CONDITIONS TO ANYONE. Not to the patient, not
to the receptionist ticking the box, not to whoever later disputes it.
schema.ts:1908 is explicit and it is a design decision rather than an oversight:
"termsVersion is the document's identity, never its text."

IT IS THE SAME DOCUMENT AS PACKET ITEM 5.2, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS ONE FINDING AND
NOT TWO. The two differ in urgency in the direction nobody would guess: THE FEE
LINE IS OFF AND THE CHECKBOX IS ON. The item that is not a launch blocker is the
one already collecting attestations.

=========================================================================
THE WORST PART IS NOT "WE CANNOT DISPLAY IT". IT IS RETROACTIVE ATTACHMENT.
=========================================================================
Rows written today carry termsVersion = "2026-08"
(terms-acceptance.ts:40, hardcoded). JP is being sent two DRAFTS this week. When
he returns one, the natural thing to call it is the month it was settled - and
if that is "2026-08", EVERY ROW CAPTURED BEFORE THE TEXT EXISTED SILENTLY
BECOMES A CLAIM THAT THE PATIENT ACCEPTED THAT SPECIFIC TEXT. Text nobody had
written when the box was ticked.

THE RECORD WOULD LOOK PERFECT AND BE FALSE, AND IT CANNOT BE CORRECTED.
Migration 0058 REVOKEs UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE at the table and defines no UPDATE
or DELETE policy, so the database refuses both regardless of what application
code asks. terms-acceptance.ts says so in its own header: "A legal record that
application code can rewrite is not a legal record." That property is right, and
it is exactly what makes a wrong row permanent.

THIS IS PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 ON A LEGAL RECORD: an unknown case (accepted
WHAT?) mapped onto a known-looking one (accepted "2026-08"), with the system
carrying on reporting something entirely reasonable.

=========================================================================
THE RECOMMENDATION, IN TWO PARTS. THE FIRST IS FREE AND URGENT.
=========================================================================
PART 1 - TELL JP NOW: WHATEVER HE RETURNS MUST NOT BE VERSIONED "2026-08".
Any other label - a date, "v1", anything - and the collapse above cannot
happen: rows captured before the text existed keep pointing at a version that
never had text, which is TRUE and stays visibly true. This costs nothing, needs
no code change, and it is the single highest-value sentence in this card. It
should go with the drafts, while he still has them open.

PART 2 - DISABLE THE CHECKBOX until a terms version with text exists.
RECOMMENDED, WITH ONE CONDITION THAT COULD REVERSE IT.

  THE COST OF DISABLING IS NEAR ZERO TODAY, and that is derived rather than
  assumed. The ONLY downstream consumer of an acceptance is the fee gate:
  apps/web/lib/reminders/data.ts:106 joins patient_terms_acceptances on
  TERMS_VERSION, and lib/reminders/fee-notice.ts is the gate. THE FEE LINE IS
  OFF (owner ruling A: it stays off until the terms document exists). The ficha
  also DISPLAYS an existing acceptance as read-only context, which is a read and
  is unaffected. Nothing else reads it - verified by grep across apps/ and
  packages/ for recordTermsAcceptance, getLatestTermsAcceptance and
  hasAcceptedTerms.

  So today the checkbox feeds one consumer that is switched off. Disabling it
  removes nothing anybody uses and stops the ledger growing rows that cannot be
  interpreted.

  THE CONDITION THAT WOULD REVERSE THIS, AND IT IS THE ONE FACT NO TERMINAL CAN
  DERIVE: DOES THE CLINIC ALREADY HAVE A PAPER CONDITIONS DOCUMENT THAT PATIENTS
  PHYSICALLY SIGN? If it does, the checkbox is recording a REAL WORLD EVENT and
  "the platform cannot display it" is beside the point - the document exists, it
  is simply not in the platform. In that case the box should STAY, and the fix
  is instead to make TERMS_VERSION identify THAT paper document rather than an
  unwritten one.

  The evidence points the other way but does not settle it:
  terms-acceptance.ts's own header records "JP confirmed no existing signed
  document contains the fee rule". That is a statement about the FEE RULE, not
  about whether any conditions document exists at all. IVAN OR JP MUST ANSWER
  IT; it is not inferable from the repository and guessing it is exactly what
  standing rule 15 forbids.

  A RISK OF DISABLING, STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED: a control switched off
  "temporarily" is a control nobody re-enables. If part 2 is taken, the
  re-enable belongs on the same card as installing the returned terms text, not
  on a memory.

WHAT IS NOT RECOMMENDED, AND WHY, SO THE OPTION IS CLOSED RATHER THAN
FORGOTTEN: changing TERMS_VERSION to a string that NAMES the absence (something
like "no-text-yet"). It looks honest and it is worse: it puts a value into a
legal ledger whose only purpose is to be resolvable to a document, and it would
still be a row saying a patient accepted something. The choice is capture an
identity that will resolve, or capture nothing.

NO MIGRATION IS INVOLVED IN EITHER PART. Part 1 is a sentence to JP. Part 2 is a
UI condition in SignatureConsent.tsx and a refusal in recordTermsAcceptance -
the belt and the braces, because a disabled control that the server still honours
is not disabled. 0058 is untouched either way.

BLOCKED ON IVAN. Two questions, in order: does a paper conditions document
exist; and if not, disable the checkbox until JP's text arrives.

=== OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: A PAPER DOCUMENT EXISTS. THE RECOMMENDATION IS
REVERSED AND THE CHECKBOX STAYS LIVE. ===

THE CONDITION THIS CARD NAMED AS DECISIVE IS THE ONE THAT HELD. The card said,
verbatim: "IF THE CLINIC ALREADY HAS A PAPER CONDITIONS DOCUMENT THAT PATIENTS
PHYSICALLY SIGN... the checkbox is recording a REAL WORLD EVENT and 'the platform
cannot display it' is beside the point - the document exists, it is simply not in
the platform. In that case the box should STAY."

IT DOES. Patients physically sign a paper conditions document. So a receptionist
ticking that box is attesting to something that actually happened in front of
them, which is exactly what the control was built to record.

NEITHER ARM WAS BUILT, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF HAVING ASKED. No UI condition in
SignatureConsent.tsx, no refusal in recordTermsAcceptance. Had this been built on
the recommendation before the answer arrived, reception would have lost a control
that was working correctly, and the acceptances it captured in the meantime would
simply not exist - unrecoverable, because the event is a signature on paper that
nobody would have gone back to log.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WAS NEVER THE CHECKBOX. It was WHICH DOCUMENT the
recorded label names. TERMS_VERSION says "2026-08", a label with no document
behind it, while the thing patients are signing is a real paper document. The
mechanism is right, the identity it records is wrong, and that is a one-constant
fix carded as LE-terms-version-switch-on-jp-text.

I RECOMMENDED THE OPPOSITE AND THE REASONING THAT LED THERE WAS SOUND ON THE
FACTS I HAD. The card derived that the only downstream consumer is the fee gate
and that the fee line is off, so disabling looked nearly free. THAT ANALYSIS WAS
CORRECT AND IRRELEVANT: it measured the cost inside the platform and the event
being recorded is outside it. The fact that decided the question was never going
to be in the repository, which is why it was asked rather than assumed - and it
is the reason standing rule 15 exists.

PART 1 OF THE RECOMMENDATION STANDS AND HAS BEEN ACTED ON: the returned document
is labelled "condicoes-v1-2026" and not "2026-08". That was the free, urgent half
and it is now both an owner ruling and a machine guard
(LE-terms-version-label-collision-guard).

cards.title: Every printed declaration, report and RGPD form leaves a PERMANENT PDF in Storage that nothing ever deletes
cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-24 WHILE BUILDING ROUTE 6 OF SEC-web-surface-limiter-adoption, and
carded separately so the limiter is not read as having addressed it. IT HAS NOT.

THE MECHANISM, re-derived from main. Three actions render a PDF and upload it:

  downloadReportUrlAction      ${tenantId}/reports/${id}/${randomUUID()}.pdf
  generateRgpdFormUrlAction    ${tenantId}/rgpd-forms/${id}/${randomUUID()}.pdf
  generateDeclaracaoUrlAction  ${tenantId}/declaracoes/${patientId}/${randomUUID()}.pdf

Each returns a 60-SECOND signed URL. THE OBJECT IS PERMANENT. The `upsert: true`
on all three uploads looks like it would overwrite and CANNOT: a fresh
`randomUUID()` never collides, so every single print creates a new object.

SO THE STORED ARTEFACT OUTLIVES ITS OWN URL BY FOREVER. The signed link dies in
a minute; the PDF stays in ATTACHMENTS_BUCKET until somebody deletes it, and
nothing does.

THE SCALE IS ORDINARY WORK, NOT ABUSE, WHICH IS WHY THE RATE LIMIT IS THE WRONG
INSTRUMENT FOR IT. Route 6 bounds a BURST at 20/min per user. A receptionist
printing twenty declarations a day, every working day, is nowhere near that
ceiling and still leaves roughly SEVEN THOUSAND permanent PDFs a year. The limit
does not slow that down by one document.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DISK. These are CLINICAL AND FISCAL DOCUMENTS - a report
carries the patient's record, a declaracao carries their name and attendance, an
RGPD form carries their identity. CLAUDE.md's retention rule and LAUNCH-02's
ruling D (generic wording, "pelo periodo legalmente exigido para registos
clinicos", no year fixed) both bear on how long a copy may sit in object
storage. A pile of undated regenerated duplicates is not obviously covered by a
retention position written about RECORDS.

NOT BUILT AND NOT DECIDED. Three shapes, and the choice is the owner's because
it touches clinical data retention, which CLAUDE.md lists as owner-confirmable:

  (a) A STORAGE LIFECYCLE RULE on the generated prefixes - reports/, rgpd-forms/,
      declaracoes/. Cheapest, needs no code, and it is a Supabase console action
      the owner takes. Deletes copies that are already re-generable on demand.
  (b) DELETE AFTER SIGNING. The object exists only to be handed a 60s URL, so it
      could be removed once that URL is issued or shortly after. Correct in
      principle, and it makes a re-download a re-render.
  (c) STOP STORING THEM AT ALL and stream the bytes. Biggest change, and it
      conflicts with the existing decision that bytes are never proxied through
      Next - which is why the upload exists in the first place.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) FIRST, because it is reversible, needs no deploy, and stops
the growth today; then (b) as the real fix if the volume warrants it. (c) is
recorded so it is not re-invented, not because it is advised.

NO MIGRATION. NO PROD ACCESS FROM ANY TERMINAL - the retention window and the
lifecycle rule are both owner actions, and no terminal may read the bucket to
count what is already there. HOW MANY OBJECTS EXIST TODAY IS UNKNOWN and is
stated as unknown rather than estimated.

=== OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: OPTION (a), ROUTED TO JP, DOES NOT BLOCK LAUNCH. ===

(a) IS ACCEPTED AS THE RECOMMENDATION: a storage lifecycle rule on the generated
prefixes - reports/, rgpd-forms/, declaracoes/. It needs no code and no deploy,
and the documents are re-generable on demand, which is what makes deleting old
copies safe rather than lossy.

IT ROUTES TO JP AS CLINICAL RETENTION, travelling with packet items 5.1, 5.2 and
5.3. That is the right bundle: it is the same class of question - how long a
document about a patient may be kept - asked of the same person. Splitting it out
is how one of the four gets forgotten.

IT DOES NOT BLOCK LAUNCH, and the reason is worth stating rather than left as an
assurance. Nothing about the accumulation degrades over the launch window: the
growth rate is a few documents a day, the copies are not exposed to anybody (the
signed URL that reaches a browser dies in sixty seconds), and the fix is a console
setting that can be applied at any point without a deployment or a code change.
A retention position taken carefully next month protects exactly the same
documents as one taken hastily this week.

NOTHING IS BUILT. No lifecycle rule is written by any terminal - it is a console
action and standing rule 2 puts it out of reach - and no cleanup code is added.
The number of objects that exist today remains UNKNOWN and is not estimated: no
terminal may read production storage.

cards.title: A terms label may never gain text after acceptances were recorded without it - the machine half of 'do not call it 2026-08'

evidence.ref: PR #1017 MERGED, squashed to 0d03e430. 6 assertions in apps/web/lib/clinical/terms-version-ledger.test.ts, all pass; the ledger itself is TEXTLESS_TERMS_VERSIONS and TEXTED_TERMS_VERSIONS in apps/web/lib/clinical/terms-acceptance.ts. Three negative controls run and restored, baseline 6/6 after: "2026-08" added to TEXTED (the hazard) -> 3 red; emptying TEXTLESS to force a pass (the evasion) -> 2 red; TERMS_VERSION pointed at an untracked label -> 2 red. Four gates green from the repo root: pnpm lint (0 errors), pnpm typecheck (11/11), pnpm test (web 2435 pass), pnpm build. NO OWNER OBSERVATION IS OWED: this is a build-time check with no screen, so CI is the whole of its evidence.

cards.notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: the terms document must not be labelled "2026-08", and
Ivan is telling JP. THIS CARD IS THE OTHER HALF, because a human instruction is
forgotten and this particular one is UNCORRECTABLE when it is.

THE HAZARD, precisely. Acceptances have been recorded under "2026-08" since
apps/web/lib/clinical/terms-acceptance.ts:40 was written, and NO DOCUMENT TEXT
HAS EVER EXISTED FOR IT - schema.ts:1908 is explicit that termsVersion is the
document's identity, never its text. If JP's returned document carries that
label, every row captured before the text existed instantly becomes a claim that
the patient accepted THAT TEXT. The record would look perfect and be false.

AND IT COULD NOT BE PUT RIGHT. Migration 0058 REVOKEs UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE at
the table and defines no UPDATE or DELETE policy, so the database refuses both
regardless of what application code asks. terms-acceptance.ts says why in its own
header: "A legal record that application code can rewrite is not a legal record."
That property is correct. It is also exactly what makes a wrong row permanent.

=========================================================================
THE OBVIOUS GUARD WOULD NEVER FIRE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN PROBLEM.
=========================================================================
The dispatch asked for a guard that fails if TERMS_VERSION is ever set to a value
matching an already-used label. BUILT AS ASKED IT WOULD DO NOTHING FOR THE CASE
THAT MATTERS: "2026-08" IS ALREADY THE VALUE. A document arriving under that name
requires NO CODE CHANGE AT ALL - no constant moves, no diff to review, a green
build - and the collision lands in complete silence.

A guard on the constant watches the wrong event. THE EVENT THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS
IS SOMEBODY DECLARING THAT A LABEL NOW HAS TEXT, and that is what this watches.

WHAT SHIPPED. Two committed lists beside TERMS_VERSION:
  TEXTLESS_TERMS_VERSIONS  labels under which acceptances were recorded while NO
                           text existed. Append-only. ["2026-08"] today.
  TEXTED_TERMS_VERSIONS    labels whose document text is fixed. EMPTY today, and
                           the emptiness is the state of the world rather than an
                           unfinished list: JP has two drafts and has returned
                           neither.
THE GUARD IS THAT THEY NEVER INTERSECT. Adding "2026-08" to TEXTED turns the
build red with the reasoning in the assertion message: RELABEL THE DOCUMENT, do
not edit the lists.

HOW IT IS USED WHEN JP ANSWERS, written on the constant so nobody has to find
this card:
  a label OTHER than a text-less one -> add it to TEXTED, point TERMS_VERSION at
    it. "2026-08" stays text-less forever, which is TRUE and stays visibly true.
  the label "2026-08" -> the build fails. That is the intended outcome and the
    answer is to relabel the document.

IT NEEDS NO PRODUCTION READ, DELIBERATELY. The authoritative set of used labels
is the distinct values in patient_terms_acceptances.terms_version, and no
terminal may read production to find them. A COMMITTED LEDGER IS DERIVABLE,
REVIEWABLE AND CI-ENFORCEABLE WITHOUT ONE. It is a claim about history that a
human maintains, and the alternative - a check that can only run against prod -
would be a guard that never runs in CI at all.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, said rather than left to be assumed: that the ledger is
COMPLETE. If acceptances were ever recorded under some label this file does not
list, nothing here would know. Today that cannot have happened - TERMS_VERSION
has held exactly one value since 0058 was applied, and recordTermsAcceptance
defaults to it - but the ledger is an assertion about the past and its accuracy
is maintained by hand.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT CAUGHT THE EVASION. Every other
assertion is of the form "these two lists do not overlap", and TWO EMPTY LISTS
SATISFY ALL OF THEM PERFECTLY while recording nothing whatsoever. So one
assertion states the current state of the world affirmatively - "2026-08" is in
TEXTLESS and TERMS_VERSION is "2026-08". The negative control that empties
TEXTLESS to force the collision through reddens exactly that one. Same family as
ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep criterion F: a guard proves a test RAN; only the
assertion proves it tested the right SUBJECT.

CHANGING TERMS_VERSION NOW REQUIRES DECLARING THE NEW LABEL, and that friction is
the feature rather than a side effect. The third negative control demonstrates it:
pointing the constant at an untracked label fails until somebody says which kind
of label it is. A label in neither list is untracked, and untracked is how one
slips into TEXTED later without anybody noticing what it was.

RELATED, AND STILL BLOCKED ON IVAN: LE-ficha-terms-checkbox-no-document. This
card removes the silence from the LABEL hazard. It does NOT stop the checkbox
recording new text-less acceptances, which is that card's question and needs the
owner's answer on whether a paper conditions document exists. Neither arm of it
was built.

cards.title: Point TERMS_VERSION at condicoes-v1-2026 when JP's text lands - one constant, no migration, and the old rows stay permanent either way
cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-24 ON OWNER RULING C. The ficha checkbox STAYS LIVE - a paper
conditions document exists and patients physically sign it - so what needs
changing is not the control but WHICH DOCUMENT the recorded label names.

THE CHANGE, and it is one line: apps/web/lib/clinical/terms-acceptance.ts:40,
TERMS_VERSION from "2026-08" to "condicoes-v1-2026".

WHEN: THE MOMENT JP'S TEXT LANDS. Not before. "condicoes-v1-2026" is already in
TEXTED_TERMS_VERSIONS as the incoming label, and the ledger suite asserts by name
that TERMS_VERSION has NOT yet moved - so a session that moves it early turns the
build red rather than quietly starting to record acceptances against a document
nobody can produce. That assertion is the trigger for this card, not a nuisance:
it goes red exactly when this card should be doing its work.

=========================================================================
THE MIGRATION CONSEQUENCE, STATED IN FULL. THERE IS NO MIGRATION.
=========================================================================
TERMS_VERSION is an application constant, not schema. Nothing in 0058 changes and
no migration is authored, which also means this card does not reactivate the
one-migration-in-flight rule.

WHAT HAPPENS TO THE EXISTING ROWS: NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME.
Every acceptance recorded so far keeps terms_version = "2026-08". They are not
rewritten, not backfilled, and not deleted.

THEY GO ON POINTING AT A LABEL THAT NEVER HAD TEXT, AND THAT STAYS VISIBLY TRUE.
This is the good ending rather than a residue to tidy: those patients accepted the
clinic's conditions on paper, and the platform recorded THAT AN ACCEPTANCE
HAPPENED under a label whose document identity was never fixed. Leaving the label
alone keeps the record honest about exactly how much it knows. Rewriting them to
"condicoes-v1-2026" would be the retroactive attachment this whole family of
cards exists to prevent - it would assert that those patients accepted JP's
version 1 text, which nobody can show they saw.

0058 MAKES THEM PERMANENT EITHER WAY, so the choice is not really open. The
migration REVOKEs UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE at the table and defines no UPDATE or
DELETE policy: the database refuses a rewrite regardless of what any code asks.
A backfill is not merely inadvisable here, it is not executable. That property is
deliberate - terms-acceptance.ts's header: "A legal record that application code
can rewrite is not a legal record."

WHAT THE FICHA WILL SHOW AFTER THE SWITCH, so nobody reads it as a defect: a
patient who accepted before the switch renders "Aceitacao registada em <date>
(2026-08)"; one who accepts after renders "(condicoes-v1-2026)". TWO LABELS
VISIBLE ON THE SAME SCREEN IS CORRECT and is precisely why 0058 is a table with
history rather than three columns on patients - "what did this patient agree to
in March" has to stay answerable after the terms move on.

THE FEE GATE FOLLOWS THE CONSTANT AND THAT IS A REAL CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING.
apps/web/lib/reminders/data.ts:106 joins patient_terms_acceptances on
TERMS_VERSION. After the switch, a patient whose only acceptance is under
"2026-08" NO LONGER SATISFIES THE FEE GATE and the fee line will not render for
them until they accept the new version. THAT IS RIGHT: the fee line cites "os
termos aceites na marcacao", and for those patients the terms accepted were a
document whose text was never fixed. It does mean the switch quietly resets the
population the fee line can reach - which matters only when the fee line is armed,
and it is off.

WHOSE MOVE: JP'S. Blocked on him for the text. When it lands this is
green_self_merge, one constant, the ledger suite, and the two assertions above
flipping to their post-switch form.

cards.title: The Fisiozero source adapter and the delivery sanity checker - the amostra structure is confirmed, so the seam can finally be implemented

evidence.ref: PR #1025. packages/db/src/migration/sources/fisiozero.ts + packages/db/tests/fisiozero-adapter.test.ts (33 assertions), and scripts/import/check-delivery.mjs + scripts/import/check-delivery.test.mjs (14 assertions). Four negative controls run and restored: emitting a patient with no resolvable clinic -> 1 red; treating escala_eva 0 as absent -> 1 red; parsing naive local times as UTC -> 4 red; dropping the orphaned-zip-entry direction -> 1 red. Gates green from the repo root. CLOSED 2026-08-24: the card was held open ONLY because primaryLocationKey and patientNumber reached no column. #1028 connects both plus health_insurance_numbers in upsert.ts, so the stated condition - "until they are [written] or until the owner rules they should not be" - is met. The adapter also now normalises telefone and sexo at the boundary per docs/migration-notes.md.

cards.notes:
THE SEAM IS IMPLEMENTED. packages/db/src/migration/source.ts has carried
"interface only, deliberately UNIMPLEMENTED... No implementation, scraping, or
field mapping may be written before that sample exists" since Phase 5. The
amostra was probed blind, the owner pasted the sanitized structure, and that
precondition is now met.

STAGING, VALIDATE AND UPSERT ARE UNTOUCHED. The adapter emits the existing
intermediate shapes and nothing else in the pipeline changed.

=========================================================================
MACHINE-CHECKABLE ACCEPTANCE. Every line runs from the repo root.
=========================================================================
  A1  pnpm --filter @osteojp/db exec vitest run tests/fisiozero-adapter.test.ts
      -> 33 passed, 0 failed.
  A2  node --test scripts/import/check-delivery.test.mjs -> 14 passed, 0 failed.
  A3  node --test scripts/import/probe-amostra.test.mjs -> 7 passed (the probe
      this build was authored from, unchanged).
  A4  pnpm typecheck -> 11/11 packages.
  A5  pnpm lint -> 0 errors.
  A6  pnpm build -> 4/4.
  A7  pnpm test -> the db suite includes tests/fisiozero-adapter.test.ts and is
      NOT DB-gated: it runs on every PR with no DATABASE_URL.
  A8  the test "NOTHING maps to confirmed" asserts no ESTADO_MAP value is
      "confirmed".

=========================================================================
THE REQUIREMENTS, AND WHERE EACH IS PROVEN
=========================================================================
1. SYNTHETIC IDS. appointmentSourceId = sha256(id_paciente|inicio|terapeuta),
   episodeSourceId = sha256(id_paciente|data_avaliacao|specialty), both 128 bits
   of hex. Nothing reads a clock, a counter or a row index, so a re-run is
   byte-identical and the staging ledger's idempotency holds. Two rows that
   collide are COLLAPSED and COUNTED rather than silently deduplicated
   (checks.duplicateSyntheticAppointmentIds).

2. TIMEZONE. naiveLocalToIso does a ROUND-TRIP check rather than offset
   arithmetic: a candidate instant is correct only if formatting it back in
   Europe/Lisbon reproduces the wall time we started from. That is what makes
   both DST edges fall out rather than needing to be special-cased. THE MARCH
   GAP IS REFUSED - 01:30 on the jump day is not a moment, and converting it
   invents one - and THE OCTOBER FOLD IS RESOLVED TO THE EARLIER INSTANT AND
   FLAGGED, because either answer is a guess and a silent pick is
   indistinguishable from a certainty. A decade of history crosses those edges
   about twenty times.

   A DEFECT IN MY FIRST IMPLEMENTATION, CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TEST AND WORTH
   RECORDING: ambiguity detection probed offsets only around the naive instant,
   which in the autumn fold already sits PAST the transition - so the
   pre-transition offset was never sampled, one of the two valid instants was
   invisible, and an ambiguous time reported as certain. The probe now brackets
   the day (-24h, 0, +24h) so both offsets in play are always seen.

3. ESTADO AS DATA. ESTADO_MAP is a frozen object, so a vendor confirming one
   more value is an edit to data rather than a change to a branch. NOTHING maps
   to confirmed, and a test pins it: confirmation in this platform means a
   patient answered a reminder WE sent, and no vendor row can evidence that -
   asserting it would fabricate a patient's action. The "marcada" case is
   conditional: a booking still marked marcada whose start is in the PAST is a
   row nobody ever closed out, not a future appointment, and importing it as
   scheduled would put a decade of dead bookings into reception's diary. Those
   route to to_review. Unknown values route there too, carrying the VALUE.

4. RESOLVERS INJECTED. terapeuta, tipo_servico and location all arrive as maps.
   LOCATION IS A PARAMETER WITH TWO SHAPES AND NEITHER IS HARDCODED, per the
   card: a per-clinic export carries the clinic in the FILENAME and a combined
   one carries it in a column. Choosing now and being wrong means re-deriving
   every patient's location after import.

5. primaryLocationKey IS MANDATORY AND ENFORCED AT COMPILE TIME. It is a
   REQUIRED field on MigrationPatient, so no adapter can emit a patient without
   one; a row whose clinic cannot be resolved routes to to_review. Making it
   required cost four fixture sites and four assertions in
   migration-batch-validation.test.ts, all updated - a smaller price than an
   invariant that holds only by convention. It is a KEY and not an id because
   every cross-reference in types.ts is a key: the adapter cannot know a uuid
   the platform assigned.

6. numero_paciente carries as patientNumber, and the PRE-IMPORT UNIQUENESS
   CHECK is checks.patientNumberDuplicates, reported as a COUNT with a warning.
   THE COUNT AND NOT THE VALUES: a patient number identifies a patient.

7. data_criacao IS NOT READ ANYWHERE. It is an export timestamp, not a
   registration date, and a test asserts the value does not reach the emitted
   patient by any route including notes.

8. SPECIALTY FIELDS FOLD UNDER THEIR OWN NAMES, empty omitted. Renaming them
   into a house vocabulary would be a clinical judgement - queixas and motivos
   are not obviously the same field - and this adapter is not entitled to make
   one. escala_eva IS INCLUDED WHENEVER THE CELL HOLDS A NUMBER, ZERO INCLUDED:
   "no pain" and "not asked" are different facts and a falsy check conflates
   them. Both directions asserted.

9. ATTACHMENTS from documentos.csv AND from FICHEIRO on pacientes and episode
   files, deduplicated by filename, with documentos.csv winning because it is
   the only source carrying the mime type and the original name. storagePath is
   the tenant-prefixed destination. THE BYTE COPY IS NOT THIS CARD.

10. BLIND. Neither suite reads a delivery file, and neither can: the adapter
    takes CSV TEXT rather than paths, so packages/db has no fs access on this
    path at all. Every fixture is generated inside the test file.

=========================================================================
THE DELIVERY CHECKER
=========================================================================
scripts/import/check-delivery.mjs, run by Ivan. Exit 0 accept, 1 reject, 2 no
directory. Checks UTF-8, expected headers per file, id_paciente uniqueness,
referential integrity from every referencing file, documentos.ficheiro
uniqueness, the estado vocabulary, and ZIP correspondence in BOTH DIRECTIONS
when a zip is supplied.

BOTH DIRECTIONS BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT FAULTS. A referenced file absent from
the archive is a BROKEN RECORD - a patient's document is gone. An archived file
nothing references is an ORPHAN, and it may be the document of a patient the
export DROPPED, which row counts alone would never reveal.

EXTRA COLUMNS ARE A NOTE, NOT A FAILURE: the caderno lets the vendor choose the
extraction method, so more data than asked for is not a non-conformance.
Missing columns are.

WITHOUT --zip IT SAYS SO. "correspondence NOT checked" is printed, because
silence on that line would read as checked-and-fine.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, printed on the accept path so the acceptance is not
over-read: it checks STRUCTURE and REFERENCES. It cannot check that the contents
are correct or complete against the clinic's own records.

=========================================================================
TWO PREMISE MISMATCHES AGAINST THE DISPATCH, BOTH RESOLVED IN THE ONLY
DIRECTION AVAILABLE
=========================================================================
The dispatch requires primary_location_id and patient_number on every emitted
patient, and forbids touching upsert internals. MigrationPatient carried NEITHER
FIELD, and upsert.ts's importPatient maps ten columns and writes neither.

So each requirement splits in two. The ADAPTER half is complete: both values are
derived, primaryLocationKey is compile-time mandatory, and the uniqueness check
runs. The PIPELINE half cannot be done from here without editing upsert.ts,
which was forbidden.

Both fields are therefore CARRIED AND NOT PERSISTED - said in the type
definition itself in capitals, in this card, and in
LE-migration-patient-fields-not-persisted. A field that reaches no column is the
half-connected wire section 1.3 describes, and the only thing worse than the gap
is the gap being quiet.

patient_number carries a second problem that is a decision rather than a
mapping: the column is integer NOT NULL filled BY A TRIGGER under the
tenant-unique constraint patients_tenant_number_uq. Vendor numbers and
trigger-assigned numbers are two numbering schemes for one column, and which one
owns it is the owner's call.


=== CLOSED 2026-08-24. THE HOLD CONDITION WAS MET, NOT WAIVED. ===

This card carried open_on_purpose for one reason: two fields the adapter derived
correctly were written nowhere, and closing would have reported the adapter as
delivering data that reached no column. #1028 persists primaryLocationKey,
patientNumber and health_insurance_numbers in upsert.ts and removes the capitals
warning from types.ts, so the wire is connected and the reason is gone.

THE SAME PR ALSO CLOSED THE DEFECT THIS CARD SHIPPED WITH: telefone and sexo were
passed through verbatim against two committed instructions, found by re-reading
migration-notes.md rather than trusting this card. Both normalise at the boundary
now, and normalizePhonePT has a single home so the instruction to reuse it is
literally followable.

cards.title: The adapter derives primaryLocationKey and patientNumber correctly and upsert.ts writes neither - a field that reaches no column
cards.notes:
RAISED 2026-08-24 WHILE BUILDING MIG-01, and carded rather than fixed because
the dispatch that built the adapter explicitly forbade touching upsert.ts.

THE STATE. MigrationPatient now carries primaryLocationKey (required) and
patientNumber (optional). The Fisiozero adapter populates both. upsert.ts's
importPatient builds a ten-key values object - fullName, dateOfBirth, sex, nif,
email, phone, address, postalCode, city, notes - AND NEITHER FIELD IS IN IT. The
values are derived, validated, staged in raw, and then dropped at the last step.

WHY IT IS HIGH RATHER THAN MEDIUM. Not because the fields are missed - the
platform has run without them - but because THE ADAPTER NOW LOOKS LIKE IT
DELIVERS THEM. A reader of the adapter, its tests and its card would conclude
that an imported patient lands with a primary location. It does not. That is
PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3 with the unknown case mapped onto the reassuring one, and
the only reason it is not already a defect is that nobody has run the import.

primaryLocationKey IS THE STRAIGHTFORWARD HALF. patients.primary_location_id is
nullable and unreferenced by importPatient; adding it to the values object and
resolving the key through resolvers.locationIdByKey is the same shape the
function already uses for locationKeys. IT MATTERS BECAUSE PL-09 MAKES AN
UNPLACED PATIENT LOOSER, NOT TIGHTER: patientLocationScope falls back to
unrestricted, so 8,000 imported patients with a null primary location would be
visible more widely than the clinic would expect, quietly.

patientNumber IS NOT A MAPPING AND MUST NOT BE TREATED AS ONE. The column is
integer NOT NULL, DEFAULT null as a type-level marker, FILLED BY A TRIGGER,
under the tenant-unique constraint patients_tenant_number_uq. Writing vendor
numbers into it means:
  - the trigger's assignment scheme and the vendor's numbering must not collide,
    and across 8,000-10,000 rows they certainly would unless the import takes
    the column over completely;
  - the adapter has already reported that numero_paciente is NOT guaranteed
    unique in the delivery (checks.patientNumberDuplicates), while the
    constraint is tenant-unique, so some deliveries cannot be carried at all;
  - MAX(patient_number) lookups feed the assignment path, so importing high
    vendor numbers moves where new patients start.

THREE OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
  (a) let the trigger assign and keep the vendor number in notes or elsewhere,
      losing the platform-visible continuity the clinic may expect;
  (b) take the column over for imported rows and reseed the assignment above the
      imported maximum;
  (c) add a separate legacy_patient_number column, which needs a migration and
      is the only option that keeps both numbers true at once.
RECOMMENDED: (c), because it is the only one where neither number has to lie,
and because a clinic that has quoted patient numbers to patients for a decade
will keep quoting them. IT NEEDS A MIGRATION, so it is owner-gated and nothing
is authored here.

BLOCKED ON NOBODY, GATED ON THE OWNER. (a) and (b) are code-only and could ship
tomorrow; (c) is a migration and is his to authorise.

=== PART 1 EXECUTED, PART 2 HALTED. 2026-08-24. ===

THE RULING MATCHES CARDED OPTION (b) in intent - "take the column over for
imported rows and reseed the assignment above the imported maximum" - and the
first half is done. THE SECOND HALF IS UNBUILDABLE AND THAT IS THE FINDING.

PERSISTENCE IS CONNECTED. upsert.ts importPatient now writes
primary_location_id, patient_number and health_insurance_numbers alongside the
ten columns it already mapped, and the capitals warning is gone from types.ts
because the wire is no longer half-connected.

TWO THINGS THE DISPATCH NAMED THAT THE SCHEMA DOES NOT HAVE:
  `seguro_saude` and `numero_apolice` ARE NOT TWO SCALAR COLUMNS. PL-23
  (migration 0051) models insurance as health_insurance_numbers, a jsonb
  `{insurer, number}[]`, NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]' with a CHECK keeping it an array,
  because "a patient may hold more than one (ADSE plus a private insurer is
  ordinary in PT)". The caderno specifies both vendor columns as semicolon
  separated IN MATCHING ORDER, so the adapter ZIPS them. A mismatched count
  routes the row to to_review rather than mispairing an insurer with the wrong
  policy number, which is worse than recording neither.

  OMITTING patient_number IS NOT THE SAME AS PASSING null. The column is
  `integer NOT NULL DEFAULT sql\`null\``, a type-level marker letting a caller
  leave it out so the trigger fills it. So a patient with no vendor number must
  have the KEY ABSENT. Written as a conditional spread rather than `?? null`,
  and a negative control that changes it to `?? null` fails TYPECHECK - drizzle's
  own types refuse the null before Postgres ever would.

=========================================================================
NO MIGRATION WAS AUTHORED. THERE IS NO COUNTER OR SEQUENCE TO SEED.
=========================================================================
The ruling asks the import migration to "seed the per-tenant counter/sequence
above max imported numero_paciente to kill collisions under
patients_tenant_number_uq".

THAT MECHANISM DOES NOT EXIST IN THIS DATABASE. public.assign_patient_number
(0029, redefined SECURITY DEFINER in 0047) computes
  COALESCE(MAX(patient_number) WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id, 0) + 1
LIVE on every insert, under a per-tenant advisory lock. There is no sequence, no
counter table and no stored high-water mark. IT IS SELF-SEEDING BY
CONSTRUCTION: import a patient numbered 9,999 and the next trigger-assigned
number is 10,000, with nothing to configure. 0029's own comment already says the
other half - "Explicit values skip this path entirely (keep original numbers)".

So the migration would have been a NO-OP against production, and this project has
paid three times for migrations that were no-ops without anybody noticing (0038-
0041, 0049, 0058). Authoring one to satisfy the shape of an instruction would
have put a fourth through the apply runbook for nothing.

PROVEN RATHER THAN ARGUED: packages/db/tests/patient-number-collision.db.test.ts,
six DB-gated assertions against real Postgres in the required check - an explicit
9,999 is preserved; the next assigned number is 10,000 with nothing seeded;
assignment continues for later patients; a LOWER vendor number imported after a
higher one survives and does not drag the counter backwards; and numbering is
per tenant so one clinic's import cannot move another's.

THE COLLISION THAT IS REAL, and no migration fixes it either: a vendor number
that duplicates a number ALREADY HELD by an existing patient in the same tenant.
Those rows exist and hold those numbers now; seeding a counter would not move
them. The sixth assertion pins that this case genuinely fails on
patients_tenant_number_uq, and the adapter already reports it BEFORE any import
as checks.patientNumberDuplicates. IF THE CLINIC HAS REAL PATIENTS TODAY WHOSE
TRIGGER-ASSIGNED NUMBERS OVERLAP EDUARDO'S RANGE, that is a data reconciliation
for the owner and it is the one thing here that could still stop an import.

MIGRATION DISCIPLINE, for the record: the next free number IS 0068, derived from
the committed journal (67 entries, idx 0-66, last tag
0067_followup_packs_and_provenance). It stays free. The pre-check
packages/db/scripts/check-pending-migrations.mjs was NOT RUN by this terminal:
it opens a READ ONLY transaction against PRODUCTION and standing rule 1 forbids
a terminal pointing anything at prod. It is an owner step, and there is nothing
for it to check because nothing is pending.

cards.title: The attachment byte-copy job - resumable, streaming, and it never overwrites an object it cannot vouch for

evidence.ref: REHEARSED 2026-08-26 at main 76dd93a2 against non-prod djflfnnjvkbwnsgqwawj. Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-26.md section 5.2. The Supabase REST calls HAVE now run against a live bucket: uploaded 22, skipped 0, conflicts 0, failures 0, bytes 1413, exit 0 - and the objects were READ BACK from the bucket under <tenantId>/migration/fisiozero/, count 22, equal to `uploaded`. The re-run proved resume and skip: uploaded 0, skipped 22, exit 0. Three defects the mocks could not have found were fixed to get there (PRs #1041, #1042). CLOSE CONDITION IS THE OBJECT COUNT, ruled 2026-08-27: a terminal has no browser, and the REST read asks the same question of the same API the upload used.

cards.notes:
=== CLOSED 2026-08-27 BY THE EXECUTED REHEARSAL. Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-26.md, §5.2. ===

CARDED AND BUILT 2026-08-24. docs/migration-notes.md section 3 has specified this
job since Phase 5: "The importer expects attachments to already be in Supabase
Storage (storagePath is NOT NULL). Ivan needs to build a separate job."

MACHINE-CHECKABLE ACCEPTANCE:
  A1  node --test scripts/import/copy-attachments.test.mjs -> 10 passed, 0 failed.
  A2  grep -c "require(" scripts/import/copy-attachments.mjs -> 0 (pure ESM).
  A3  pnpm test:scripts includes it -> the whole scripts suite green.
  A4  the leak assertion: no /ZZV\d{3}/ token appears in any conflict or
      failure entry, asserted directly.

WHAT IT DOES. Streams each file from a directory OR a ZIP, hashes it, checks the
target, uploads through the Supabase Storage REST API, and appends one JSONL
checkpoint line per file. Concurrency is a fixed worker pool.

NEVER BUFFERS A WHOLE FILE. The delivery may be tens of gigabytes. Each file is
read TWICE - once to hash, once to upload - and two passes over local disk is the
price of knowing the digest BEFORE the bytes leave the machine, which is what
makes the collision check mean anything at all.

THE CHECKPOINT IS NOT TRUSTED ON ITS OWN, and this is the property most worth
having. It records what we BELIEVE we did; storage.exists records what is
actually there. A resume that skipped on the checkpoint alone would skip an
entire bucket that had been emptied between runs, on the strength of a file
sitting on this laptop. A negative control that removes the verification turns
one test red.

AN OCCUPIED TARGET IS NEVER OVERWRITTEN. Three cases and all three refuse:
digest differs from what we uploaded, digest changed since we uploaded, and
target exists with NO record of our having put it there. The last is the one
that matters most - an object of unknown origin may be a live clinical document,
and this job has no business deciding otherwise.

A MAPPED FILE ABSENT FROM THE DELIVERY IS A FAILURE, NOT A SKIP. The importer
would otherwise write an attachment row pointing at nothing, and storage_path
being NOT NULL makes exactly that look healthy.

NO FILENAME IS EVER PRINTED, INCLUDING ON FAILURE. The card said "no filenames
except conflict/failure entries" and then, in the same breath, "print sha256 and
checkpoint line number instead of the name". THE SECOND INSTRUCTION IS THE
OPERATIVE ONE and this implements it: attachment filenames may carry patient
names, and a failure summary is precisely the output somebody pastes into a
chat. Every conflict and failure is identified by CHECKPOINT LINE NUMBER and
sha256, both of which Ivan can resolve locally and neither of which is personal
data.

CREDENTIALS BY ENV NAME ONLY - SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are
read into a header and never returned, logged or included in any error this
module raises.

WHAT IS UNVERIFIED, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: THE SUPABASE REST CALLS
HAVE NEVER RUN AGAINST A LIVE BUCKET. Standing rule 2 forbids a terminal making
cloud writes, so every test drives a MOCK client and the endpoint shapes are
authored from the documented API. Ivan's first run is the proof, and it should be
a handful of files before it is tens of gigabytes.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN AND RESTORED, 10/10 after: overwriting an occupied
target instead of conflicting -> 1 red; trusting the checkpoint over the bucket
-> 1 red; (the third is on the runner card).

DEPENDS ON: MIG-01 for the mapping file, which is the adapter's attachment
output (filename -> tenant-prefixed storage_path).


=== THE CLOSE PATH IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN, 2026-08-25. MIG-04. ===

docs/import/REHEARSAL.md section 5 is the run that closes this card: emit the
attachment mapping, copy the bytes into a NON-PROD bucket, confirm the objects
in the dashboard, then re-run to prove skip-on-resume.

ONE REASON IT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN RUN BEFORE TODAY, and it was not a missing
runbook. copy-attachments.mjs requires --mapping <mapping.json>, this card
describes it as the adapter's attachment output, and NO COMMITTED SCRIPT EMITTED
ONE. packages/db/scripts/rehearsal-import.ts --emit-attachment-mapping does now.

STAYS OPEN. The REST calls still have never touched a live bucket. The card
closes on Ivan's pasted section 5 transcript - the five counts on the first run,
the five on the second with uploaded=0, and the dashboard confirmation - not on
the runbook existing.

cards.title: The import runner - dependency order, an incomplete mapping refused before staging, and attachments gated on their bytes existing

The runner HAS now met a database: IMPORTED patient 1000, clinical_episode 44, appointment 891, clinical_record 44, attachment 22; failed 0; referential integrity OK; patient number fidelity OK over 882 vendor numbers; exit 0. cards.notes:

runner since Phase 5: "importRecords is a library function; it needs a caller."

MACHINE-CHECKABLE ACCEPTANCE:
  B1  node --test scripts/import/run-import.test.mjs -> 14 passed, 0 failed.
  B2  the ordering assertion feeds records in REVERSE and asserts the runner
      imports in ENTITY_ORDER regardless.
  B3  the never-delete assertion inspects every method the injected pipeline
