  B4  pnpm test:scripts includes it.

THE PIPELINE IS INJECTED, and that is forced by the repo rather than chosen:
packages/db ships RAW TYPESCRIPT with no build step (package.json main is
./index.ts), so a plain .mjs script cannot import it under bare node. Injection
also makes every refusal testable with no database, and it is what makes the
never-delete rule PROVABLE rather than merely asserted - the fake pipeline
records every call and a test greps them.

=========================================================================
THE CONFIRMATION PHRASE AND THE EXIT CODES ARE DEFINED HERE. THEY WERE NOT
FOUND, AND THAT IS A HALT WORTH RECORDING.
=========================================================================
The dispatch says "--apply plus the explicit confirmation phrase per standing
rules" and "exit codes per standing rules". NO SUCH RULES ARE COMMITTED. A search
of CLAUDE.md, docs/ and .claude/ returns the general doctrine ("done is a number,
a file, or an exit code"), the Twilio proof's own exit table, and ship.md's - and
nothing defining an import confirmation phrase or an import exit code table.

This is the shape PORTAL-REHYDRATE 4.11 exists to end: a rule carried between
dispatches in prose that a stateless terminal cannot derive. So the file DEFINES
both and says it is defining rather than transcribing:
  CONFIRM_PHRASE = "IMPORT FISIOZERO INTO PRODUCTION"
  EXIT = { OK: 0, FAILED: 1, BAD_INVOCATION: 2 }
IF THE OWNER HAS A DIFFERENT PHRASE IN MIND, THAT LINE IS WHERE IT CHANGES.

THREE MODES. --dry-run touches no pipeline at all (asserted: zero calls), so it
runs before any credential exists. --preview (the default) stages and validates
and writes NO target table. --apply requires the exact phrase.

AN INCOMPLETE MAPPING HARD-FAILS BEFORE ANYTHING IS STAGED, and the reasoning is
the whole point: a partial mapping DOES NOT CRASH. An unmapped terapeuta routes
its appointments to to_review, so the run would quietly import a fraction of the
diary and report success over the rest. Finding that afterwards means
reconciling thousands of rows by hand.

THE REFUSAL NAMES THE KEYS WITH COUNTS - "Dra Quem" 412 rows - because a refusal
that names nothing cannot be acted on, and counts tell Ivan which are typos and
which are a real therapist whose entire diary would have been skipped. Values are
operational metadata and ruled safe.

A DEFECT IN MY FIRST CUT, CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT AND WORTH RECORDING: the runner
re-derived the unmapped names from the to_review rows, which carry the REASON and
not the VALUE. The list came out EMPTY - a refusal that named nothing, which is
worse than no refusal because it looks like diligence. MIG-01's adapter now
tallies unmappedTerapeuta and unmappedTipoServico by value with counts, and the
runner reads those.

ATTACHMENTS ARE LAST AND ARE GATED ON THEIR BYTES EXISTING. attachments.
storage_path is NOT NULL, so a row pointing at a missing object is written
happily and looks entirely healthy. The precondition reads the byte-copy job's
checkpoint and refuses the WHOLE RUN if any attachment has no uploaded entry -
including one whose upload ended in a conflict.

NOTHING IS EVER DELETED FROM migration_staging_rows. The ledger is both the audit
trail and the idempotency key: a run that deletes from it makes the next run
re-import everything it already did. The runner exposes no delete capability to
inject in the first place, and the test asserts both.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN AND RESTORED, 14/14 after: importing in the adapter's
emitted order instead of ENTITY_ORDER -> 1 red; warning instead of hard-failing on
an incomplete mapping -> 3 red; skipping the attachment-object precondition -> 1
red.

DEPENDS ON: MIG-01 (the adapter it consumes) and the byte-copy job above (the
checkpoint it reads).

=== VENDOR ANSWERS LANDED 2026-08-25. THREE ITEMS, NO MIGRATION. ===

FOUR ANSWERS RECORDED, because each one changed or confirmed a decision that had
been made without them:
  1. TWO EXPORTS, ONE PER CLINIC. So a run uses location kind:"fixed" and the
     clinic comes from which delivery it is - not from a column. The adapter
     already supported both shapes and hardcoded neither, which is exactly the
     reason it was written that way.
  2. data_criacao IS THE GENUINE REGISTRATION DATE, except a legacy batch
     carrying import-day dates.
  3. ONLY Fisioterapia AND Osteopatia exist.
  4. ZIP NAMES MATCH THE CSV REFERENCES EXACTLY - the delivery checker's
     both-directions correspondence check should therefore come back clean, and
     a mismatch is now a real finding rather than an expected quirk.

ITEM 1 - REGISTRATION DATE. THE EARLIER RULING IS REVERSED, AND THE REASONING
BEHIND IT WAS SOUND ON THE FACTS THEN HELD. `data_criacao` was left unread
because it was believed to be an EXPORT timestamp; the vendor says otherwise, so
MigrationPatient now carries `registeredAt` and upsert.ts persists it into
patients.created_at - the same conditional-spread shape importClinicalRecord
already uses for recordedAt, and for the same reason: created_at is NOT NULL
DEFAULT now(), so a patient with no source date must have the KEY ABSENT. Passing
null would be rejected; passing new Date() would stamp import day onto a patient
the clinic has had for a decade.

NO HEURISTIC DETECTS THE LEGACY BATCH, BY INSTRUCTION, AND THE INSTRUCTION IS
RIGHT. A rule guessing which dates are "wrong" from their shape would silently
rewrite genuine registrations that happen to fall on the same day. A wrong date
nobody can audit is worse than an honest one the clinic knows about.

AN UNPARSEABLE data_criacao DOES NOT SINK THE PATIENT, unlike a bad appointment
instant. A registration date is PROVENANCE: losing the whole patient over it
would cost far more than letting created_at take its default. Counted as
checks.unparseableRegistrationDates so the number is visible rather than
absorbed.

ITEM 2 - MAPPING CONFIG TEMPLATE. scripts/import/mapping-config.template.json,
committed. The FILLED file is mapping-config.local.json and is gitignored;
git check-ignore resolves both it and any nested copy to
.gitignore:68 **/mapping-config.local.json, and the template itself is proven NOT
ignored.

THE DISPATCH'S PREMISE ABOUT THE RUNNER WAS WRONG AND THAT IS THE FINDING HERE.
It says "Runner already hard-fails on placeholders per MIG-03". IT DID NOT.
checkMappingCoverage checked that the maps EXISTED and that location.kind was one
of two strings - a config filled entirely with 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
passed every check, staged the whole delivery, and would have failed at IMPORT
time on a foreign key, halfway through, with rows already written.

A PLACEHOLDER IS WORSE THAN A MISSING KEY. A missing key routes its rows to
to_review and the run stays honest; a placeholder uuid is a confident answer that
is false. findPlaceholders now refuses the run on any placeholder uuid or
PENDING_OWNER_RULING, naming the slot, before anything is staged. The committed
template is asserted to be refused AS-IS.

TO_NORMALIZE IS HANDLED DIFFERENTLY AND NOT AS FATAL, because
appointments.service_id is NULLABLE and an unmapped type already imports without
a service. But it CANNOT be passed through either: upsert.ts:320 throws
unresolved("serviceKey") for a key with no resolver entry, so handing
"TO_NORMALIZE" to the adapter would turn an undecided catalogue label into a
mid-import crash. It is stripped, and the removal is logged.

A VACUOUS TEST OF MY OWN, CAUGHT BY ITS NEGATIVE CONTROL. stripToNormalize had a
passing unit test while NOTHING PROVED runImport CALLED IT - the control that
passed TO_NORMALIZE straight through left all 23 assertions green. The function
working and the function being used are different facts. runImport now returns
`effectiveConfig` on every path and the test asserts the STRIPPED config is what
was used; the same control now fails.

ITEM 3 - IMPORT-DAY OVERLAP CHECK. scripts/import/preflight-patient-numbers.sql.
One read-only SELECT, no writes, no temp tables, four aggregates per tenant and
no patient value of any kind, so its output is safe to paste back in full. IVAN
RUNS IT in the Supabase SQL editor; no terminal may (rule 1), which is why it is
a committed .sql file rather than a script that opens a connection.

WHAT IT IS FOR, restated on the file itself: the trigger side is already safe -
assign_patient_number is MAX+1 computed live, so importing 9,999 moves the next
number to 10,000 with nothing to seed. The unsafe side is the clinic's EXISTING
patients, who already hold numbers. A vendor number colliding with one of those
is REJECTED by patients_tenant_number_uq, no migration fixes it, and it has to be
decided before the run rather than discovered during it.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-27 BY THE EXECUTED REHEARSAL. Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-26.md, the whole transcript. ===

CARDED AND BUILT 2026-08-25. The rehearsal that closes MIG-02 and MIG-03.

=========================================================================
THE DISPATCH'S PREMISE WAS WRONG IN TWO PLACES, AND FINDING OUT WHY IS
MOST OF WHAT THIS CARD DID.
=========================================================================
It asks for a runbook whose steps 6 and 7 are "Runner --preview" and "Runner
--apply". NEITHER COMMAND EXISTED. Two wires were missing, and a runbook whose
central steps cannot be typed would have been the exact artefact PORTAL-REHYDRATE
section 1.3 warns about: something that reports a harmless-looking state over an
unknown one.

WIRE 1 - THE RUNNER HAD NO ENTRYPOINT. scripts/import/run-import.mjs main()
refuses EVERY invocation with BAD_INVOCATION and prints the instruction nobody
had followed: "Import runImport() from a tsx entrypoint and pass
{ adapterResult, config, pipeline }". MIG-03's own open_on_purpose says so
plainly - "binding the real one needs a tsx entrypoint". So the runner has never
met a database because there was no way for it to.

WIRE 2 - NOTHING EMITTED THE ATTACHMENT MAPPING. copy-attachments.mjs has always
required --mapping <mapping.json>, MIG-02 describes it as "the adapter's
attachment output (filename -> tenant-prefixed storage_path)", and NO COMMITTED
SCRIPT PRODUCED ONE. The bytes could not be copied, so the runner's attachment
precondition could never be satisfied, so --apply could never reach step 6 of
its own flow.

BOTH ARE BUILT HERE, in packages/db/scripts/rehearsal-import.ts, because a
rehearsal runbook that cannot be executed is not a deliverable. NO ORCHESTRATION
MOVED: order, the mapping refusal, the confirmation phrase, the attachment
precondition and the exit codes all stay in run-import.mjs where 25 assertions
and four negative controls hold them. The entrypoint does four things - guard the
target, read the delivery, build the resolvers, open the transaction.

=========================================================================
MACHINE-CHECKABLE ACCEPTANCE. Every line runs from the repo root.
=========================================================================
  C1  node --test scripts/import/rehearsal-runbook.test.mjs -> 19 passed. This
      IS the card's stated acceptance, made checkable: the runbook exists, the
      guard command is present, and the counts are stated literally.
  C2  pnpm --filter @osteojp/db exec vitest run tests/rehearsal-import.test.ts
      -> 24 passed, 0 failed.
  C3  node --test scripts/import/run-import.test.mjs -> 25 passed (was 23).
  C4  pnpm test:scripts -> 208 passed (was 187).
  C5  the no-prod-ref assertion: NO command block in REHEARSAL.md contains
      either blocklisted ref, asserted against the refs READ FROM
      seed-guard.ts rather than from a copy in the test.
  C6  gates from the root: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, test (db 365
      passed), build 4/4.

=========================================================================
THE GUARD IS A SCRIPT, NOT A GREP, AND THAT WAS A CHOICE THE DISPATCH LEFT OPEN
=========================================================================
It offered "reuse seed-guard's check if invocable standalone, else a one-line
grep guard". seed-guard.ts is NOT invocable standalone - its entry point
resolveSeedDatabaseUrl also demands SEED_DEV_CONFIRM and is wired into the
seeds - so packages/db/scripts/assert-not-prod.ts MAKES it invocable rather than
duplicating the blocklist into a shell pattern.

THE COPY IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM A GREP GUARD WOULD HAVE CREATED. A grep carries
its own copy of the refs, and a copy of a blocklist goes stale silently - which
is precisely SEC-seed-guard-prod-blocklist, where the list sat EMPTY for months
with a comment as its only enforcement. A test asserts the guard file contains
no ref literal of its own.

IT CHECKS MORE THAN THE SEED GUARD DOES, AND THE EXTRA ARM IS THE ONE THAT
MATTERS. resolveSeedDatabaseUrl reads DATABASE_URL only. A rehearsal also holds
SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, and the byte copy writes through the
Storage REST API using those. A shell whose DATABASE_URL points at a scratch
project while SUPABASE_URL still points at production PASSES a database-only
guard and then uploads patient documents into the live bucket. parseProjectRef
returns null for https://<ref>.supabase.co, so that arm is a substring test,
which cannot under-match. Its negative control turns 1 test red.

AN EMPTY ENVIRONMENT IS A REFUSAL, NOT A PASS. Section 1.3's one-line
convenience: a guard that passes when it examined nothing reports the harmless
case over an unknown one. Nothing set means the env file was not sourced, and
that is the finding.

=========================================================================
THREE DEFECTS FOUND WHILE WIRING, ALL IN COMMITTED CODE, ALL FIXED HERE
=========================================================================
1. THE TEMPLATE COULD NOT PRODUCE A RUNNABLE CONFIG.
   adaptFisiozeroDelivery() REQUIRES tenantId - it builds the storage prefix
   <tenantId>/migration/fisiozero/<file> from it - and every pipeline call is
   tenant-scoped. mapping-config.template.json had NO SUCH SLOT. A config filled
   exactly as the template asked was not sufficient to run anything. The slot is
   added, shipping as a placeholder.

2. findPlaceholders NEVER SCANNED THE CONFIG ROOT, so the slot just added had no
   placeholder check at all. It scanned three nested maps. tenantId is the worst
   possible one to miss: an all-zero tenant uuid does NOT trip a foreign key -
   it writes the entire delivery into a tenant that does not exist, under RLS
   policies that then hide every row, and the run reports success. The scan now
   covers the root and location.locationKeyByValue. Negative control: removed
   -> 1 red.

3. batch_id IS A uuid COLUMN, NOT FREE TEXT (schema.ts:1493). My first cut
   defaulted it to "rehearsal-fisiozero", which Postgres rejects at INSERT -
   halfway through a staging run, after the connection is open. Caught while
   reading the schema rather than in Ivan's sitting. It is now a FIXED uuid
   constant, and fixed matters as much as uuid: reconciliation is scoped by
   batch id, so a fresh id per run would give the second --apply an EMPTY batch
   to reconcile - which reports zero of everything and looks EXACTLY like the
   clean no-op section 7.3 exists to prove.

=========================================================================
A DEFECT IN THE PIPELINE WIRING, CAUGHT BY READING upsert.ts RATHER THAN BY A
TEST, AND IT WOULD HAVE FAILED EVERY ROW
=========================================================================
My first livePipeline computed validation counts and returned them WITHOUT
marking the ledger. upsert.ts reads migration_staging_rows.status and refuses
any row still `pending` with "import attempted before validation" - it does not
re-derive validity. That preview would have been clean and the --apply would
have failed EVERY RECORD. This is exactly the class of failure the rehearsal
exists to find, found one layer earlier.

ONLY `pending` ROWS ARE MARKED, and that is the idempotency re-run: on the second
--apply every row is already `imported`, and markValidated THROWS unless the row
is pending - so marking blindly would turn section 7.3 into a crash instead of
the no-op it is meant to demonstrate.

ONE TRANSACTION PER PHASE, NOT ONE PER RUN. The ledger is both the audit trail
and the idempotency key: a single transaction wrapping stage + import would roll
the LEDGER back alongside a failed import, so a re-run would have no record the
first attempt happened and would repeat all of it.

withTenantContext AND NOT getDbAdmin(). The admin handle bypasses RLS. Running as
an authenticated principal means migration_staging_rows' tenant-isolation
policies apply to every statement, so the rehearsal proves the POLICIES too and
not merely that the SQL is well formed.

=========================================================================
THE COUNTS ARE STATED LITERALLY, AND TWO OF THEM ARE NOT WHAT THE DISPATCH SAID
=========================================================================
The dispatch gives 1000 patients, 1000 marcacoes, 44 episodios, 22 documentos.
Those four are stated verbatim in the runbook. THE ADAPTER DOES NOT EMIT THEM
ONE-TO-ONE, and a runbook that implied it would have Ivan reporting correct
numbers as surprises:

  clinical_episode = 44 AND clinical_record = 44 - THE SAME ROWS TWICE. The
  caderno's instruction for a vendor with no episode concept is one episode per
  clinical record, closed, and the adapter emits both from each episodios row
  with the same sourceId. The runbook asserts they must be EQUAL.

  attachment IS NOT 22. documentos.csv contributes 22, and the FICHEIRO column
  on pacientes.csv and on each Episodios_*.csv contributes more, deduplicated by
  filename with documentos.csv winning. The number is whatever
  --emit-attachment-mapping reports, and the runbook gives the formula and a
  floor (never below 22) rather than a figure it cannot know.

  to_review FROM THE ESTADO TABLE IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. After a clean
  check-delivery run, unknown_estado is necessarily 0 - the checker exits
  non-zero on any estado outside {realizada, falta, marcada}. So the estado-driven
  to_review is marcada_in_the_past, which for a historical sample is the whole
  marcada count from check-delivery's own `estado seen:` line. That line is why
  section 3 tells Ivan to write it down.

THE FOUR COUNTS ARE THE DISPATCH'S, AND NOTHING COMMITTED CORROBORATES THEM.
Said plainly rather than presented as verified: no probe output for the amostra
is in the repository, so these numbers are transcribed from the dispatch and
section 2 of the runbook is where they get checked against reality for the first
time. If they disagree, section 2 is a halt and not an adjustment.

=========================================================================
THE CLEANUP PERMISSION, BOTH HALVES, BECAUSE HALF OF IT IS DANGEROUS
=========================================================================
Deleting from migration_staging_rows is permitted ONLY on a non-prod rehearsal
target and NEVER on production, and the runbook says both in the same sentence.
On production that delete destroys the record of what was imported, on a
one-shot extraction that cannot be repeated.

MIG-03's invariant is UNCHANGED and is not weakened by this: the runner exposes
no delete capability to inject and a test asserts it. What section 8 describes is
an operator resetting a scratch project by hand, in a transaction, children
before parents, behind a re-assertion of the guard - because the SQL editor has
no guard of its own. Four assertions cover it, including the delete ORDER.

=========================================================================
WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RUN FROM THIS TERMINAL, AND WHAT WAS NOT
=========================================================================
RUN: both no-database modes, end to end, against a SYNTHETIC delivery generated
in the scratch directory by this terminal - never the amostra. --dry-run reports
2 patients, 1 episode, 2 appointments, 1 record, 3 attachments from a fixture
with 2 pacientes rows, 1 episodios row and 1 documentos row - which is the
attachment arithmetic above, demonstrated. --emit-attachment-mapping writes 3
entries. check-delivery.mjs accepts the fixture, exit 0. The guard refuses a prod
DATABASE_URL and a prod SUPABASE_URL, and passes a non-prod pair. The committed
template is refused as-is with config."tenantId" named among the placeholders.

NOT RUN, AND IT CANNOT BE FROM HERE: anything touching a Supabase project or the
amostra. That is the card's open_on_purpose and it is the whole point.

A HAZARD FOUND BY RUNNING RATHER THAN BY READING, and written into the runbook:
`pnpm --filter @osteojp/db exec` sets the working directory to packages/db, so a
repo-relative --config path resolves under packages/db/ and the script reports
"config unreadable" with exit 2. Every path in the runbook is absolute and
section 0.3 says why.

NINE NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN AND RESTORED:
  root placeholder scan removed                    -> 1 red
  location key passed through instead of resolved  -> 1 red
  BOM strip dropped on delivery read               -> 1 red
  SUPABASE_URL substring arm removed from guard    -> 1 red
  literal "44 episodios" removed from the runbook  -> 1 red
  guard script renamed in the runbook command      -> 3 red
  prod ref planted in a runbook command block      -> 1 red
  "NEVER permitted on production" softened         -> 1 red
  cleanup delete order reversed                    -> 1 red

NO MIGRATION. NO WF-03 ITEM: there is no screen. The deliverable is a document
and two scripts Ivan runs in his own shell.

cards.notes:
CARDED AND BUILT 2026-08-25, the Friday-freeze dispatch. Three items, three
owner rulings, and two of the three premises did not survive verification.

=========================================================================
ITEM 3a. THE GUARD WAS EMBEDDED, SO prod-import.ts WAS GENUINELY NEEDED.
=========================================================================
VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: rehearsal-import.ts imported PROD_REFS/parseProjectRef
directly and refused a blocklisted ref at line 493 - the guard was IN the
entrypoint, not merely a runbook step. So the rehearsal entrypoint literally
cannot reach production, and a second entrypoint was the only way.

BUT THE DISPATCH'S "IDENTICAL FLOW" WAS DELIVERED BY EXTRACTION, NOT BY COPY.
Copying 567 lines is the literal reading and it is the wrong one. This
repository has already paid for a copy once: SEC-seed-guard-prod-blocklist was a
duplicated blocklist that sat EMPTY for months while a comment claimed it was
enforced. A copied IMPORT FLOW would be worse - a fix landing on the rehearsal
path and not on the production one would be discovered on the single night the
clinic cannot repeat the extraction.

So packages/db/scripts/import-core.ts holds the whole flow ONCE, and the two
entrypoints are gates and nothing else. Four assertions enforce it, including a
line ceiling and a per-step check that neither entrypoint re-implements
adaptFisiozeroDelivery, runImport, readDelivery, livePipeline or
attachmentMapping.

THE PHRASE IS READ FROM STDIN, AND THAT IS A DECISION WITH A REASON. CLAUDE.md
says "typed by Ivan once per window". --confirm lands in shell history, in
scrollback and in `ps` output - and once it is in history the next run is an
up-arrow, which is exactly the deliberation the phrase exists to force. An env
var lands in the env FILE and is inherited by every child process. Stdin leaves
it nowhere. It is never echoed, and the expected value is NOT printed on
failure: printing it turns a refusal into a copy-paste prompt.

--confirm IS REJECTED RATHER THAN IGNORED on this entrypoint, so an operator
carrying the rehearsal's habit is told instead of silently running with a phrase
the gate never read.

TWO GATES, ONE PHRASE. The target gate is this file; the WRITE gate is still
run-import.mjs comparing its own CONFIRM_PHRASE. A test pins the two constants
equal - if they diverge, the target gate would accept a phrase the write gate
then rejects, and the operator would be refused after typing it correctly.

=========================================================================
ITEM 3b. seed-guard DOES NOT BLOCK THE IMPORT PATH, AND THE MECHANISM IS
SCOPING BY IMPORT, NOT BY CONFIGURATION.
=========================================================================
There is nothing to fix. The exact mechanism, traced:

  PROD_REFS is a plain DATA export. It blocks nothing by itself.
  resolveSeedDatabaseUrl() is the ENFORCING function - it exits the process -
  and it is imported by EXACTLY the eight seed scripts under packages/db/seed/
  (dev-reference, patients-dev, appointments-dev, availability-dev,
  episodes-dev, working-hours-real, location-cleanup, plus load-env's comment).
  NOTHING in the import path imports it.

  The import path touches PROD_REFS in exactly two places, both of which are
  entrypoint gates rather than library behaviour: assert-not-prod.ts (the
  standalone rehearsal guard) and rehearsal-import.ts. prod-import.ts imports
  parseProjectRef ONLY, to PRINT the ref - a test asserts it never calls
  PROD_REFS.includes.

  copy-attachments.mjs imports seed-guard NOT AT ALL - grep -c returns 0. The
  byte copy has no prod guard of any kind and never did.

THAT LAST ONE IS REPORTED AS A FINDING RATHER THAN FIXED. It is CORRECT for the
production run, which must reach the live bucket. It also means there is no
accidental-prod protection on the byte copy: a stale SUPABASE_URL uploads patient
documents to production with nothing to stop it. assert-not-prod.ts already
checks SUPABASE_URL for exactly this reason, which is why PROD-RUN.md and
REHEARSAL.md both put the guard BEFORE the byte copy. Carding a guard inside
copy-attachments is the owner's call, not this card's.

=========================================================================
OWNER RULING B: THE MAPPING TABLE ON MAIN DID *NOT* REFLECT IT. NOW IT DOES.
=========================================================================
The dispatch said "verify the mapping table on main already reflects it, fix if
not". IT DID NOT. mapEstado returned { ok: false, reason: "marcada_in_the_past" }
and the row went to toReview. Ruling B says cancelled.

`cancelled` IS A REAL appointment_status (schema.ts:42-48), checked before
relying on it - a status outside that enum is rejected by validate.ts before
anything is staged.

THE COUNT IS WHAT KEEPS THE RULING AUDITABLE. checks.pastMarcadaCancelled plus a
warning line on every run, because a ruling that silently changes what a decade
of rows MEAN is a ruling nobody can check afterwards. Demonstrated live against a
synthetic fixture: two past-dated marcada rows now report appointment=2,
to_review=0 and the warning names the count; before the change they were
to_review=2, appointment=0.

FIVE PLACES ENCODED THE OLD RULE and all five moved together: the adapter, its
tests, the mapping-config template's _estado reference block, REHEARSAL.md's
estado table and derivation, and the runbook guard that asserted the OLD reason
string appears in REHEARSAL.md.

=========================================================================
ITEM 2. THE ADMIN UI CANNOT DO IT. THAT IS WHY IT IS SQL.
=========================================================================
THE SCHEMA QUESTION, ANSWERED FROM THE DDL RATHER THAN FROM A COMMENT:

  CAN A STAFF ROW EXIST WITH NO AUTH USER? YES. public.users has EXACTLY TWO
  foreign keys - users_tenant_id_tenants_id_fk and users_role_id_roles_id_fk.
  There is NO FK from users.id to auth.users.id.

  MIGRATION 0018's COMMENT SAYING OTHERWISE IS WRONG. 0018_quick_notes.sql:15
  reads "users.id is 1:1 with auth.users.id (enforced by FK)". No such
  constraint was ever created. The 1:1 is a CONVENTION the app upholds by always
  minting both together. A test now pins the FK's ABSENCE, so if a migration ever
  adds it these accounts become un-creatable and the test says so first.

  WHAT EXCLUDES THEM, each traced to the query that reads it:
    is_bookable = false  THE SCHEDULING ONE. therapist-bookable.ts is a
                         one-line predicate (`return row.isBookable`) and the
                         Terapeuta dropdown AND the agenda's therapist filter
                         read the SAME list (data.ts:311).
    role_id = NULL       Every role-keyed query INNER JOINs roles, so a null
                         drops the row from all of them with no flag to forget.
    is_active = false    Removes them from the agenda reference query
                         (data.ts:277) and the staff notification fan-out.
    login                No auth.users row = no credential exists. Stronger than
                         any flag: it is the absence of a thing rather than a
                         check something might skip.
    disponibilidade      Needs no flag. Availability is rows in
                         availability_templates keyed by user_id; they get none.

  THE HISTORY STILL RENDERS, and this is the part that would have bitten. The
  agenda's appointment query joins innerJoin(users, ...) WITH NO is_active
  PREDICATE (data.ts:180), so a decade of imported rows renders normally with
  the practitioner's name. The only thing lost is the ability to FILTER the
  agenda to these two, because the filter list is the bookable list. Their rows
  appear under "Todos os terapeutas" - the intended trade.

WHY THE UI CANNOT: its ONLY creation path is inviteStaff (staff.ts:154) ->
provisionStaffUser (provision.ts:46) -> admin.auth.admin.createUser at
provision.ts:72, called BEFORE the users insert. Every account the UI can create
has a login and a password. activateStaffLogin is the opposite operation - it
gives a login to a row that already exists. So a UI-created account would be a
real credential for a clinic and a treatment method, which is the exact thing
ruling A forbids.

DELIVERED AS (b): scripts/import/legacy-staff-accounts.sql. Preview SELECT with
literal expected counts, then a transactional INSERT expecting `INSERT 0 2`,
then a verify SELECT expecting EXACTLY 2 ROWS with has_auth_user FALSE.

.invalid ADDRESSES, RFC 2606, chosen deliberately: users.email is NOT NULL and
unique per tenant so a value is required, and .invalid can never resolve
anywhere. clinica@osteojp.pt could one day BE a real mailbox.

FIXED LITERAL UUIDS, not gen_random_uuid(): they must be pasted into
mapping-config.local.json, and generating them means hand-copying two uuids
under time pressure where a mistype is a foreign-key failure MID-IMPORT.

THE ACCENT IS LOAD-BEARING. "Clínica OsteoJP" carries an í and the mapping
matches the vendor string EXACTLY; a test forbids the unaccented variant.

cards.notes:
CARDED AND BUILT 2026-08-25. Two guards, no migrations.

=========================================================================
GUARD 1. THE BYTE COPY HAD NO PRODUCTION GATE AT ALL, AND THAT WAS THE
FINDING THIS CARD EXISTS TO CLOSE.
=========================================================================
Reported on MIG-05 and ruled on here. Every other step of the import was
guarded - rehearsal-import refuses a blocklisted ref, prod-import demands the
phrase, assert-not-prod checks the whole shell - and copy-attachments.mjs
imported seed-guard NOT AT ALL. The one file that could put patient documents
into the live clinic bucket was the one file that would not stop you.

THE RUNBOOKS MITIGATED IT BY ORDERING. Both put assert-not-prod before the byte
copy. AN ORDERING CONVENTION IS NOT A GUARD: it protects the operator who
follows the runbook, which is not the operator who needs protecting.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN. A non-prod target is COMPLETELY unaffected - no
prompt, nothing to type - because the rehearsal is run repeatedly and a prompt on
it would be trained away within a day. A prod target cannot move a byte without
the phrase, typed on stdin. Asserted both directions.

EXIT 2 AND NOT 1, per the dispatch and defensible on its own: a missing phrase is
not a data failure. The delivery is fine and nothing was attempted. It is a
wrong INVOCATION, which is what 2 means in CLAUDE.md's ratified table - and it
keeps 1 meaning exactly one thing here, conflicts or failures during a run that
actually happened.

=========================================================================
THE BLOCKLIST IS READ AT RUNTIME, NOT COPIED, AND THAT NEEDED A NEW FILE
=========================================================================
The dispatch said "reuse the seed-guard list, do not duplicate it".
copy-attachments.mjs runs under BARE NODE - deliberately, it has no build step
and no tsx dependency - and bare node cannot import a .ts file. So the choice was
duplicate two refs into the .mjs, or read the declaration at runtime.

DUPLICATING IS THE FAILURE THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY HAD.
SEC-seed-guard-prod-blocklist was a blocklist that sat EMPTY for months while a
comment claimed it was enforced. scripts/import/prod-refs.mjs reads the real
declaration on every run, and a test asserts NEITHER new file contains a ref
literal.

IT THROWS RATHER THAN RETURNING [], AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. A parser that
cannot find the list has two options and only one is safe: returning an empty
array makes every includes() false, so the guard passes EVERYTHING and reports
nothing - the same silent-empty failure, reintroduced through a regex that
stopped matching. Section 1.3 exactly. Three arms tested: empty, missing, and
unreadable, all throw; the CLI turns each into exit 2.

IT PARSES THE DECLARATION, NOT THE WHOLE FILE. A whole-file scan for 20-character
tokens would also match the refs named in the surrounding COMMENTS - which happen
to be the same two today - so an emptied declaration would still look populated.
A test pins that: a fixture with the refs in comments and an empty array THROWS.

TWO ARMS ON THE URL MATCH. parseProjectRef reads the two POSTGRES forms and
returns null for https://<ref>.supabase.co, which is precisely the Storage
endpoint shape this job writes to. The parse handles that; a substring test
catches a custom domain, a pooler string pasted into the wrong variable, or a
port suffix. Substring CANNOT under-match, and the asymmetry is deliberate: a
false positive costs one confused operator, a false negative uploads patient
documents into the live clinic.

=========================================================================
GUARD 2. THE COLLISION FALLBACK, AND WHY THE DEFAULT DOES NOT MOVE
=========================================================================
WITHOUT THE FLAG NOTHING CHANGES. A colliding vendor number still rejects under
patients_tenant_number_uq, and a test asserts the existing numbers are not even
READ in that mode. Rejecting is the right default: silently renumbering a patient
the clinic identifies BY THAT NUMBER is a data change nobody asked for.

THE MECHANISM IS OMITTING THE KEY, NOT RENUMBERING. upsert.ts spreads
patientNumber conditionally and 0029's assign_patient_number only fills the
column IF NEW.patient_number IS NULL. So deleting the key is the entire
implementation - there is no renumbering code. PASSING null WOULD BE REJECTED
because the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT sql`null`, and a negative control that
sets null instead of deleting turns 1 red.

THE CALLER'S RECORDS ARE NEVER MUTATED. The staged row keeps the vendor number in
`raw` - that is the audit trail, and it must still say what the vendor sent even
though the target row will not. A control that mutates in place turns 1 red.

READ ONCE, BEFORE ANY PATIENT IMPORTS. Re-reading per patient would be thousands
of round trips AND would see numbers this very run had just assigned - so a later
vendor number could collide with an earlier reassignment and be reassigned again
for no reason. Asserted with a call counter.

THE PAIR IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT THE COUNT. A count of reassignments is useless
to reception: the patient walks in quoting the OLD number and somebody has to map
it. The runner reads back what the trigger assigned - through the LEDGER's
imported_entity_id, the only link between a vendor sourceId and the row written -
and prints vendor -> assigned pairs.

NUMBERS ONLY. No name, no sourceId, no id. A pair of integers is not personal
data; a list of renamed patients would be. A control that adds the sourceId to
the pair turns 3 red.

TWO REFUSALS RATHER THAN TWO SILENCES, both section 1.3:
  - the flag passed to a pipeline that cannot read existing numbers REFUSES,
    because proceeding would import under the DEFAULT behaviour while the
    operator believes reassignment is on.
  - pairs that cannot be read back print a WARNING naming the count, because
    silence would read as "no collisions", which is the opposite of the truth.

=========================================================================
MACHINE-CHECKABLE ACCEPTANCE
=========================================================================
  E1  node --test copy-attachments-gate.test.mjs      -> 19 passed
  E2  node --test patient-number-reassign.test.mjs    -> 15 passed
  E3  node --test prod-run-runbook.test.mjs           -> 25 passed (was 18)
  E4  node --test copy-attachments.test.mjs           -> 10 passed, unchanged
  E5  node --test run-import.test.mjs                 -> 25 passed, unchanged
  E6  pnpm test:scripts -> 280 (was 239)
  E7  gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, db 386 passed, build 4/4
  E8  the FLAG-NAME assertion: the runbook and import-core.ts must name the
      same flag, because a typo in the runbook is a silently ignored flag and
      an import under the default behaviour.

FIFTEEN NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN AND RESTORED:
  gate accepts any phrase                        -> 4 red
  empty blocklist returns [] instead of throwing  -> 2 red
  substring arm dropped                           -> 1 red
  non-prod target prompted too                    -> 1 red
  seed-guard blocklist emptied for real           -> 10 red
  patientNumber set to null instead of deleted    -> 1 red
  non-colliding numbers reassigned too            -> 3 red
  caller's record mutated                         -> 1 red
  reassignment applied without the flag           -> 1 red
  missing pipeline method proceeds silently       -> 1 red
  sourceId added to the pair list                 -> 3 red
  flag renamed in code but not the runbook        -> 1 red
  reception/Monday handoff removed                -> 1 red
  byte-copy phrase removed from the runbook       -> 1 red
  contingency stops saying WHEN to use the flag   -> 1 red

RUN FROM THIS TERMINAL, against synthetic data only: prod URL + wrong phrase
refuses with exit 2 and leaves the checkpoint 0 bytes; prod URL + correct phrase
opens the gate; non-prod URL is never prompted; the flag is accepted by the real
prod-import entrypoint and appears in its usage line.

cards.notes:
CARDED AND BUILT 2026-08-25. Data-only, no migration, no DDL.

=========================================================================
THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH TOOK FIVE PARSERS, AND THE FIFTH IS THE ONE THAT
WOULD HAVE ABORTED THE TRANSACTION.
=========================================================================
The schema declares foreign keys in FIVE distinct DDL forms, and a parser that
handles only the common one silently misses whole tables. Each form was found by
noticing the previous parse had produced a number that could not be right:

  1. ALTER TABLE x ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY (c) REFERENCES "public"."p"
  2. CREATE TABLE ... CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY (c) REFERENCES ...
  3. CREATE TABLE ... "c" uuid ... REFERENCES "p"("id")      column-level, quoted
  4. CREATE TABLE ... c uuid ... REFERENCES public.p(id)     unquoted
  5. ALTER TABLE x ADD COLUMN c uuid ... REFERENCES public.p(id)

FORM 1 ALONE GAVE 13 TABLES. Adding form 3 found patient_trusted_devices and
patient_terms_acceptances (15). Adding form 4 found consultations,
patient_followup_contacts and patient_followup_postponements (18).

FORM 5 CHANGED THE ORDER RATHER THAN THE SET, AND THAT IS THE DANGEROUS KIND.
Migration 0067 adds `appointments.pack_instance_id -> patient_pack_instances(id)`
as an ADD COLUMN. Without it both tables sit at depth 1 with no ordering
constraint between them, appointments gets deleted after pack instances, and the
WHOLE TRANSACTION ABORTS on a foreign key - in the middle of a production window,
on the most destructive step in the migration.

FINAL: 117 edges, 18 tables with an FK path to patients, ONE cascading edge
(patient_trusted_devices). Every other edge is ON DELETE NO ACTION, so a missed
child ABORTS rather than orphans - the safe direction, and the reason the
transaction is trustworthy at all.

THE CASCADING TABLE IS STILL DELETED EXPLICITLY, per the dispatch, so its count
appears in STEP 1 instead of vanishing into a cascade nobody can audit.

=========================================================================
THREE TABLES CARRY A PATIENT ID WITH NO FOREIGN KEY. THOSE ARE THE ONES
THAT WOULD HAVE LEFT ORPHANS.
=========================================================================
They do NOT block the delete, which is exactly why they are dangerous: the
transaction succeeds and leaves rows pointing at patients that no longer exist.

  patient_audit_log.patient_id            nullable, no FK   -> DELETED
  staff_notifications.patient_id          NOT NULL, no FK   -> DELETED
  guest_booking_requests.converted_patient_id  nullable, no FK -> NULLED

patient_audit_log IS AN AUDIT LOG AND DELETING FROM ONE DESERVES A SENTENCE:
these rows attest to nothing that happened to a real person - they are training
artefacts - and leaving them means an audit log referencing ids that resolve to
nothing. staff_notifications.patient_id is NOT NULL so it cannot be nulled, and a
notification about a deleted patient renders as broken UI.

THE THIRD IS NULLED RATHER THAN DELETED, and the distinction is the scope of this
card. A guest booking request is NOT patient-rooted - it exists BEFORE any patient
does and merely points at one after conversion. Deleting it would exceed
"deletes only patient-rooted rows". The column is nullable by design, so nulling
removes the dangling pointer without destroying the request. A control that
deletes it instead turns 3 red.

=========================================================================
auth.users FINDING: PATIENTS HAVE NO SUPABASE AUTH ROWS. NO DASHBOARD STEP.
=========================================================================
Requirement 3 asked whether patient OTP login creates auth.users rows. IT DOES
NOT, and the answer is traceable rather than asserted:

  * migration 0010 header - the portal issues its OWN token with tenant_id,
    patient_id and role='patient', and creates "a dedicated, LOGIN-LESS Postgres
    role `patient`", declared NOLOGIN at 0010:60, "assumed via SET ROLE, never
    connected to directly".
  * client.ts PatientClaims carries patient_id and NOT `sub`. Staff claims carry
    `sub` so auth.uid() resolves; patient claims deliberately do not.
  * patient_otp_codes (0056) is keyed by phone_hash. NO patient_id, no auth
    linkage, rows expire on their own.
  * There is NO auth.admin.createUser, signUp or signInWithOtp anywhere in the
    API or portal source. The only createUser in the repo is provisionStaffUser,
    which is the STAFF invite path.

SO THERE IS NOTHING TO REMOVE FROM THE AUTH DASHBOARD, and PROD-RUN.md says so
rather than omitting the step - an omission reads as forgetfulness.

=========================================================================
STORAGE: THE ROW DELETE DOES NOT DELETE THE OBJECT
=========================================================================
STEP 1b lists storage_path BEFORE the delete, deliberately: afterwards the rows
naming those objects are gone and the paths are unrecoverable. Nothing in the
database reaches into Supabase Storage, so any object left behind is orphaned
forever. Expected count is likely 0 - training data rarely has uploads.

THE PATHS ARE PRINTED, which is the ONE place this script outputs anything other
than a number. A path cannot be deleted from the dashboard without knowing it,
and these are test patients, so the paths are not real patient data.

=========================================================================
MACHINE-CHECKABLE ACCEPTANCE
=========================================================================
  F1  node --test cleanup-test-patients.test.mjs -> 19 passed
  F2  node --test prod-run-runbook.test.mjs      -> 32 passed (was 25)
  F3  pnpm test:scripts -> 306 (was 280)
  F4  gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 11/11, db 386 passed, build 4/4
  F5  THE GRAPH ASSERTION, which is the one worth keeping: the test RE-DERIVES
      the FK closure from the migrations across all five DDL forms and fails if
      any patient-rooted table is not covered by the script. A future migration
      adding a child of patients turns it red before the window, not during.
  F6  the ORDER assertion: ten ordering pairs, including
      appointments-before-patient_pack_instances, the form-5 trap.

TEN NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN AND RESTORED:
  appointments deleted AFTER pack instances     -> 1 red
  staff_notifications delete dropped            -> 1 red
  guest_booking_requests deleted not nulled     -> 3 red
  a bare unscoped `delete from invoices;`       -> 1 red
  storage listing moved after the delete        -> 1 red
  migration_staging_rows deleted                -> 3 red
  migration_staging_rows updated                -> 1 red
  users deleted                                 -> 2 red
  the backup warning removed from the runbook   -> 1 red
  (and the cleanup step removed entirely)       -> covered by F2

TWO OF MY OWN CONTROLS WERE FAULTY AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH. The first attempts
at the migration_staging_rows and users controls injected their statement by
replacing the FIRST occurrence of "commit;" - which is inside a PROSE COMMENT
near the top of the file ("type rollback; instead of commit;"). The comment
filter stripped it, both controls passed, and a passing negative control is worse
than none: it certifies a guard that was never exercised. Re-run against the real
statement they turn 3 red and 2 red.

NOT RUN. Standing rule 12 makes data deletion owner-confirmable; standing rule 1
forbids a terminal touching production. Every assertion is static analysis of the
SQL against the committed schema. NOTHING here has been executed against any
database, and it must not be.

INSTRUCTION 1, migration-notes.md "2026-07-01 - Sex field normalization":
"When the Fisiozero CSV+ZIP source adapter is built, it must normalize sex to
canonical values (male/female/other). Map: F/feminino/Feminino/f -> female,
M/masculino/Masculino/m -> male. Fix at the migration boundary, not in
deriveFigSex."
WHAT THE ADAPTER DOES: fisiozero.ts passes row["sexo"] through verbatim, so an
"F" lands in patients.sex as "F".

INSTRUCTION 2, migration-notes.md "2026-07-07 - Phone field normalization":
"The future Fisiozero importer must ALSO normalize phones at the migration
boundary... convert '912 345 678' / '00351912345678' / '+351 912-345-678' to
canonical +3519xxxxxxxx before writing patients.phone, and surface (not silently
drop) rows that do not resolve to a valid PT format. Reuse normalizePhonePT
rather than re-deriving the rules."
WHAT THE ADAPTER DOES: passes row["telefone"] through verbatim.

WHY THE PHONE ONE IS THE SERIOUS HALF AND IS NOT A TIDINESS ITEM. THE PATIENT
PORTAL LOGS IN BY TELEPHONE NUMBER. LAUNCH-03's own card says the phone-format
check is the one that decides whether "most of the patient base cannot log in on
day one". Migration 0062 generates patients.phone_e164 from patients.phone, and
it normalises the four shapes it knows - so an un-normalised number does not
error, it derives NULL, and that patient simply cannot log in. Nobody finds out
from a log. That is the exact defect the note was written to prevent, and the
adapter shipped without it.

THE OBSTACLE IS REAL AND IS WHY THIS IS CARDED RATHER THAN PATCHED IN PASSING.
"Reuse normalizePhonePT rather than re-deriving the rules" CANNOT BE DONE AS
WRITTEN: normalizePhonePT lives in apps/web/lib/reminders/phone.ts and the
adapter lives in packages/db, which cannot import from an app.
packages/notify/src/sms-capability.ts records that the function is ALREADY
DUPLICATED across two apps with FIVE live call sites, guarded by a parity suite
written the day it was duplicated. A third copy inside packages/db would be the
third, and the parity suite would not cover it.

SO THERE IS A DESIGN DECISION HERE AND STANDING RULE 15 SAYS NOT TO GUESS IT:
  (a) MOVE normalizePhonePT into a shared package (packages/notify is the
      natural home - it already owns sms-capability, which depends on exactly
      this definition of a well-formed PT number) and have all call sites plus
      the adapter import it. Correct, and it touches five live call sites on
      gate-bearing paths including OTP.
  (b) INJECT a normalizer into the adapter, so packages/db stays pure and the
      caller supplies the app's own function. Smallest blast radius; the default
      would still have to be refuse-or-passthrough, and a passthrough default is
      how this defect happens again.
  (c) A THIRD COPY in packages/db with a parity test against the other two.
      Explicitly what sms-capability.ts's header argues against.
RECOMMENDED: (a). The note itself says reuse rather than re-derive, and (a) is
the only option that makes that literally true. It is the largest change and it
belongs in its own card with its own gates rather than riding along here.

SEX NORMALISATION HAS NO SUCH OBSTACLE and is a pure function of a string. It
could ship immediately; it is bundled here only so the two notes are answered
together rather than one being closed and the other forgotten.

NOT BUILT IN THIS SESSION, DELIBERATELY. The dispatch scoped two cards and
neither is this; patching the adapter in passing would have been unrequested
scope on a gate-bearing path, and (a) needs an owner decision. RECORDED THE DAY
IT WAS FOUND so it is not discovered by an import that leaves 8,000 patients
unable to log in.

=== EXECUTED 2026-08-24. OWNER RULING: PACKAGE-LEVEL SINGLE SOURCE. ===

THE RULING MATCHES CARDED OPTION (a) - "MOVE normalizePhonePT into a shared
package (packages/notify is the natural home)" - and (a) is what was executed.

WHAT MOVED. apps/web/lib/reminders/phone.ts -> packages/notify/src/phone.ts,
exported from the package index. apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts DELETED. Ten
import sites re-pointed to @osteojp/notify. packages/db gained a workspace
dependency on @osteojp/notify, which is what finally made
docs/migration-notes.md's literal instruction - "reuse normalizePhonePT rather
than re-deriving the rules" - possible to obey at all.

ZERO COPIES REMAIN IN apps/. Proven mechanically rather than by grep-and-hope:
packages/notify/src/phone-single-source.test.ts runs `git grep -l` for a
definition and asserts the result is exactly ["packages/notify/src/phone.ts"].

THE PARITY TEST WAS DELETED AND REPLACED, NOT SIMPLY DROPPED.
apps/web/lib/reminders/phone-parity.test.ts imported one copy across the app
boundary to compare it against the other. It was answering the right question
with the wrong instrument: it could only ever prove the two copies IT KNEW ABOUT
agreed, and the third copy - the one the adapter would have needed - would have
been invisible to it. The guard now asks "is there more than one" instead of "do
the copies agree", which is the property that actually protects the OTP login,
the reminder dispatch, the guest booking and the import.

THE TWO COPIES WERE BYTE-IDENTICAL IN CODE and differed only in their header
comments, so nothing had to be reconciled and no behaviour changed. The parity
suite had never caught anything; it existed because the NEXT edit was the risk.

PHONE NORMALISATION IN THE ADAPTER, first-valid-wins across semicolons, with
every further number preserved into `notes` as "Outros contactos: ...". Nothing
is discarded - a second number is often the only way to reach an elderly
patient, and migration-notes.md's own words are "surface (not silently drop)".

THE DAY-ONE LOGIN COUNT is checks.unresolvablePhones, surfaced by the runner
preview as a COUNT and never as numbers. LAUNCH-03 names this as the check that
decides whether most of the patient base can log in: the portal authenticates BY
TELEPHONE, 0062 derives phone_e164 and yields NULL for a shape it does not
recognise, and that patient then cannot get in with nothing in any log to say
so. The runner also states the healthy case affirmatively, because silence there
would read as "not checked".

SEX NORMALISATION per the 2026-07-01 note, F/feminino -> female and
M/masculino -> male, with an unrecognised value routed to to_review. patients.sex
is varchar(16) and NOT an enum, so the database would have accepted a raw "F"
without a word - which is exactly why the note says to fix it at the boundary.

ONE CITATION IN THE DISPATCH DOES NOT HOLD, and it changed nothing because the
dispatch was specific enough on its own. It attributes the multi-phone rule to
docs/migration-notes.md ("re-read the note and follow it exactly where it is
more specific than this dispatch"). RE-READ: that file's only phone content is
the 2026-07-07 normalisation instruction and it says NOTHING about multiple
numbers. The semicolon-separated-principal-first rule is the CADERNO v1.1's, and
v1.1 is a .docx that no test can read - recorded on LAUNCH-03a. So the rule
followed is the dispatch's own.

EVIDENCE: 42 assertions in the adapter suite (9 new), 80 in packages/notify
(3 new in the single-source guard), 16 in the runner suite (2 new). Three
negative controls run and restored: a second copy re-introduced under apps/ -> 2
red; the adapter passing telefone through verbatim again -> 4 red; (the third is
on the patient-fields card).

cards.title: Batch the import writes - 1.7 rows/s is hours on the real delivery, and the rehearsal measured it
cards.notes:
=== SHIPPED 2026-08-27. PR #1048 at 5ebbacf3, rehearsed on that SHA. Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-27.md. ===

WHAT LANDED, against the four ruled defaults:
  A1  One SELECT per parent per entity group (preloadRefs), paged at 1000 ids.
      No per-row resolver SELECT remains; requireImportedRef is gone.
  A2  Chunks of 200 in ledger order, one savepoint each: one multi-row INSERT,
      one bulk UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...) of the ledger (markImportedMany).
      The row uuid is generated in JS BEFORE the INSERT rather than by the
      column default, so the staging-row-to-target-row pairing is a fact
      rather than an inference about RETURNING order - which Postgres does
      not promise and which nothing in the result would reveal if it stopped
      being true. RETURNING id is then a CHECK on the pairing.
  A3  A failing chunk rolls back to its savepoint and is re-imported one row
      at a time through the existing path, so the bad row gets its own
      sqlstate and constraint and the other 199 land. Ledger semantics,
      markFailed, sanitizeImportError, reconciliation and exit codes
      unchanged.
  A4  Unnumbered patients are never chunked, and the split is by PREDICATE
      rather than by input order, so B5 holds however the caller sorted.
  A5  Idempotency unchanged - imported rows are skipped before chunking.

THE NUMBER THAT IS NOT 100x, AND WHY IT IS RIGHT. patient went 8.0x where
appointment went 148.9x, because 118 of the 1000 patients carry no vendor
numero_paciente and those deliberately stay one statement per row: 0029's
assign_patient_number reads COALESCE(MAX,0)+1 PER STATEMENT, so a chunk of
unnumbered rows would have every row compute the same number and all but one
would be refused. ~59s of the patient phase's 71.2s is those 118 rows, and
the alternative is a faster import that renumbers patients the clinic
identifies by number.

WHAT IS NOW THE LARGER HALF, AND IS NOT THIS CARD. The --apply command took
401s total: 78.3s of import and ~5m20s of adapter, staging and validation.
stageRows and markValidated still run per row. Not in scope here, not a
defect, and the thing worth measuring next on the real delivery.

--- prior notes below, unedited ---

THE NUMBER, MEASURED RATHER THAN FEARED. The 2026-08-26 rehearsal imported 2001
rows in 19m30s at 1.7 rows/s, per-entity:

  IMPORTED  patient             1000   571.8s   1.7 rows/s
  IMPORTED  clinical_episode      44    26.1s   1.7 rows/s
  IMPORTED  appointment          891   506.1s   1.8 rows/s
  IMPORTED  clinical_record       44    32.2s   1.4 rows/s
  IMPORTED  attachment            22    13.4s   1.6 rows/s

Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-26.md section 7.1.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT A MICRO-OPTIMISATION. The real delivery is
8,000-10,000 patients plus a decade of appointments and clinical records. At this
rate that is HOURS, on the one night the clinic has already retired the old system
and the vendor contract does not permit a second extraction. The rate is flat across
entities, which is the signature of ROUND-TRIP LATENCY rather than of any query:
importOne opens its own savepoint and issues several statements per row, against a
pooler in Frankfurt.

=== DEFAULTS, ALREADY RULED. Build to these; do not re-derive them. ===

1. CHUNKED MULTI-ROW INSERTS PER ENTITY, one savepoint per CHUNK rather than per
   row. That is where the round trips go.
2. PER-ROW FALLBACK WHEN A CHUNK FAILS. Non-negotiable, and it is the whole reason
   this is not a one-line change: a chunk that fails must not take 99 good rows with
   it. Re-run the failed chunk row by row so the ledger records WHICH row failed and
   WHY, exactly as it does today. A batch import that reports 'chunk 7 failed' is
   worse than the slow one it replaced.
3. THE B5 ORDERING IS PRESERVED. Within the patient group, rows carrying a vendor
   numero_paciente import FIRST (run-import.mjs orderForImport). The 2026-08-26
   rehearsal lost 12 patients to collisions the import MANUFACTURED by ordering:
   0029's assign_patient_number fills a NULL with MAX+1, so an unnumbered row
   imported early takes a low number and a later row whose vendor number IS that
   value is rejected. Chunking must not reorder within a group.
4. LEDGER SEMANTICS UNCHANGED. Every row still transitions pending -> validated ->
   imported with its own imported_entity_id; an `imported` row is still skipped with
   zero writes; recovery is still re-stage plus re-validate. The idempotency proof
   (section 7.3: IMPORTED 0 on every entity, SKIPPED 2001) must still hold
   byte-for-byte, and it is the first thing to check after the change.

=== ACCEPTANCE, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT ===
Section 7.1 re-run on the SAME amostra completes in UNDER 3 MINUTES with the
IDENTICAL counts - 1000/44/891/44/22, failed 0, referential integrity OK, patient
number fidelity OK over 882, exit 0 - and the transcript is committed under
docs/import/evidence/. Identical counts is half the acceptance: a faster import that
moves one number is not this card.

NOT A MIGRATION. This touches packages/db/src/migration/upsert.ts and the runner;
no schema change, no migration number.

cards.title: drizzle-kit migrate exits 1 against the rehearsal project with nothing on stdout or stderr
cards.deferred: DEFERRED POST-GO-LIVE by owner ruling 2026-08-27. Not cancelled and not dismissed: a migration tool that fails silently is exactly the class of defect this project keeps logging under PORTAL-REHYDRATE 1.3. What changed is WHEN, not WHETHER. It is deferred because it blocks nothing - check-pending-migrations.mjs answers the question drizzle-kit was being asked, exits 0, and says how it knows - and because diagnosing a tool that prints nothing is open-ended work that go-live does not have room for. Excluded from the self-merge sweep until go-live.
cards.notes:
OBSERVED during the 2026-08-26 rehearsal setup against non-prod
djflfnnjvkbwnsgqwawj. `pnpm --filter @osteojp/db exec drizzle-kit migrate` exited 1
with NO output on stdout or stderr - no error, no stack, no journal line, nothing to
read.

WHY IT DID NOT STOP THE REHEARSAL. The schema was already fully applied, which
check-pending-migrations.mjs proved directly and loudly:

  last applied "when" in the database: 1787300200000
  journal entries on disk:             67
  pending:                             0
  OK: the pending set is exactly what was expected.
  exit=0

So the rehearsal proceeded on the checker's answer rather than the tool's silence,
and every count downstream was measured against the schema the pipeline expects.

WHY IT IS STILL A DEFECT WORTH A CARD. A silent exit 1 is indistinguishable from a
silent exit 1 that mattered. The next person to run it against a project that is NOT
current gets the same nothing, and REHEARSAL.md section 1.1 lists that command first
for a project being created fresh - where the checker's 0 would not save them.

FIRST THINGS TO TRY, so nobody re-derives them: the session pooler on 5432 rather
than 6543 (advisory locks - section 1.2 already documents this trap for the env
file), drizzle.config.ts's DATABASE_URL_DIRECT fallback, and running drizzle-kit
directly rather than through `pnpm --filter exec`, which swallows output on some
failure paths (section 0.35 documents the reverse case, the bare `undefined`).

BLOCKED ON GO-LIVE. Nothing before go-live needs it: production's schema is applied
by the prod-migrate workflow, and PROD-RUN.md section 2.3 applies no migrations at
all.

cards.title: E2E shard 2 intermittently 404s /clinical/new while another shard serves it on the same commit
cards.deferred: DEFERRED POST-GO-LIVE by owner ruling 2026-08-27. Not cancelled: an intermittently red required check is a real cost and it will eventually be paid by somebody who believes it. What changed is WHEN. Deferred because the failure is not in product code, a re-run clears it, and chasing an intermittent CI environment fault is open-ended. cards.notes:
OBSERVED on PR #1046, 2026-08-27. Every test in
apps/web/e2e/ficha-signature-consent.spec.ts timed out at 120s. The Playwright
artifact's page snapshot is a NEXT.JS 404 on /clinical/new:

  Error: locator.click: Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded.
  Call log: - waiting for getByRole('combobox', { name: /Paciente/i })
  Page snapshot: heading "404" / "This page could not be found."

THE DIFF WAS AN IMPORT-TOOLING DIFF - a SQL file, two runbooks, packages/db/src/
migration and its tests. It touches no apps/web file and no route.

WHAT RULES OUT THE DIFF, and it is one fact rather than an argument: SHARD 1 OF THE
SAME RUN, ON THE SAME COMMIT, EXERCISED /clinical/new SUCCESSFULLY - clinical.spec.ts,
10 tests green, including the Modelo picker test that navigates there. One runner's
web dev server 404ed a route another runner served from the identical build.
The same spec had passed in shard 2 on the parent commit (PR #1045) in 11.6s.

THE SECOND-ORDER FAILURE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIRST. The job then hit the
16-minute budget, so Playwright never wrote e2e-results.json, so the
assert-e2e-executed gate exited 2 with 'could not read apps/web/e2e-results.json'.
A timeout therefore reports as a MISSING-EVIDENCE failure rather than as a timeout,
and the real cause is only in the artifact. Whoever picks this up: read the
artifact FIRST (docs/board LEARNINGS - the Playwright artifact names the cause and
'passes locally, red on CI' is a race until proven otherwise).

RESOLVED FOR THAT PR by `gh run rerun --failed`: green in 7m56s, all four required
checks pass, merged as 76dd93a2.

LIKELY DIRECTIONS, unverified: a Turbopack dev-server route that had not compiled
when the first request arrived, or the request reaching the wrong port (the shard
starts three Next servers - web, api on 3002, portal on 3001, and the portal has no
/clinical/new). A shard that waits for a real readiness signal on the WEB server
rather than on the first 200 would be the cheapest fix if that is the cause.

BLOCKED ON GO-LIVE.

cards.title: Batch the staging and validation writes - the import is 78s inside an apply that takes 401s, and the other five minutes is the ledger marked one row at a time

evidence.ref: SHIPPED as PR #1050, squashed to 6909bf0c, then REHEARSED on that SHA against non-prod djflfnnjvkbwnsgqwawj. Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-27b.md. ACCEPTANCE WAS A MEASUREMENT AND IT IS MET: the WHOLE apply command - adapter, stage, validate, import, reconcile - completed in 84s against 401s on 2026-08-27 and ~19m30s on 2026-08-26, with the IDENTICAL counts: 1000/44/891/44/22, failed 0, referential integrity OK, patient number fidelity OK over 882, exit 0. Phase breakdown, now PRINTED rather than inferred: stage 2.9s (693.6 rows/s), validate 1.9s (1049.8 rows/s), import 76.0s. Section 7.3 unchanged: IMPORTED 0 on every entity, SKIPPED 2001, exit 0, in 10s. Section 8 reset completed, both triggers 'O', every count back to 0. Four DB-gated tests ran live in CI: a 501-row batch stages to the identical ledger chunked and in one statement; re-staging resets a failed row and leaves an imported row alone; a mixed chunk of 500 marks exactly one row failed with its detail and 499 validated; the bulk guard refuses the whole chunk when one row is not in the expected status.

cards.notes:
=== SHIPPED 2026-08-27. PR #1050 at 6909bf0c, rehearsed on that SHA. Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-27b.md. ===

THE FIRST GUESS WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED IT. stageRows was
ALREADY one multi-row INSERT per entity - staging was never the cost. All
~5m17s removed from the command was the VALIDATE phase, which marked 2001
ledger rows one at a time. The new STAGED/VALIDATED timing lines exist so the
next person does not have to find that by subtraction, which is how it was
found this time.

WHAT THE stageRows CHUNKING ACTUALLY BOUGHT is a failure the amostra cannot
reach. Six bound parameters per row against Postgres' 65535-parameter ceiling
means one whole-entity INSERT stops working at ~10,900 rows. The delivery is
8,000-10,000 patients plus a decade of appointments, so it would have fired
FIRST on import night, on the biggest entity, with the old system retired.
A 1000-row rehearsal is structurally unable to find that class of defect.

THE CONTROL THAT SAYS NOTHING ELSE MOVED: the import phase is 76.0s against
78.3s on 2026-08-27 - run-to-run noise. MIG-09 did not touch it and the
numbers say so.

WHAT IS NOW THE REMAINING COST, and it is ruled to stay: patient is 69.0s of
the 76.0s import, and ~59s of that is the 118 unnumbered patients that must
stay one statement per row so 0029's trigger assigns each a distinct number.

--- prior notes below, unedited ---

THE NUMBER, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. MIG-08 took the import phase from
19m10s to 78.3s. The 2026-08-27 apply still took 401s end to end, so ~5m20s is
everything BEFORE the import - and it had to be found by subtraction, because
nothing in the transcript said where it went.
Evidence: docs/import/evidence/REHEARSAL-2026-08-27.md.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY GOES, and the first guess was wrong. `stageRows` was ALREADY
one multi-row INSERT for the whole entity - staging was never the cost. The
cost is the VALIDATE phase: import-core's validate loop calls markValidated or
markFailed PER ROW, which is 2001 round trips to a pooler in Frankfurt.

AND STAGING CARRIES A LATENT FAILURE THAT THE AMOSTRA CANNOT REACH. Every
column of every row is a bound parameter, six per row here, and Postgres
refuses more than 65535 in one statement. One whole-entity INSERT therefore
stops working at about 10,900 rows - and this delivery is 8,000-10,000 patients
plus a decade of appointments. It would fail FIRST on the night the extraction
cannot be repeated, on the biggest entity, with the old system already retired.
That is the shape of defect a 1000-row rehearsal is structurally unable to find.

=== DEFAULTS, ALREADY RULED. Build to these; do not re-derive them. ===
1. stageRows: multi-row INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE in chunks of 500,
   semantics unchanged - a non-imported row resets to pending with its raw
   replaced and error_detail cleared; an imported row is untouched. Every
   value a bound parameter.
2. markValidated and markFailed at validate time: one UPDATE ... FROM
   (VALUES ...) per chunk, guarded on the expected transition and throwing on
   count mismatch, with per-row fallback on throw exactly as MIG-08 does.
3. Adapter and validation LOGIC untouched. Import phase untouched.
4. The apply summary prints STAGING and VALIDATION elapsed seconds and rows/s
   beside the existing import lines - so the next person does not have to
   subtract.

=== ACCEPTANCE, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT ===
The full rehearsal --apply command on the amostra completes in UNDER 2 MINUTES
TOTAL - not the import phase, the whole command - with the IDENTICAL counts:
1000/44/891/44/22, failed 0, referential integrity OK, patient number fidelity
OK over 882, exit 0; section 7.3 still IMPORTED 0 / SKIPPED 2001. Transcript
committed under docs/import/evidence/.

NOT A MIGRATION. packages/db/src/migration/staging.ts, import-core.ts and the
runner; no schema change, no migration number.

cards.title: A therapist who was the SECOND clinician on a dual-therapist session does not get that patient on /recuperacao - a known and accepted cost, dormant until the clinic reports one
cards.deferred: DORMANT BY STRATEGY RULING SR-04, 2026-08-27. Build no alternative. The scope stays primary-practitioner-only and this card ACTIVATES ONLY on a real report from the clinic - a therapist saying a patient they treated is missing from their list, traced to a dual-therapist session where they were the secondary. Not a hypothetical, not a code review, and not a self-merge sweep item until that report arrives.
cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-27 BY STRATEGY RULING SR-04, at the moment the cost was created, rather than left to be discovered by whoever felt it.

=== THE COST, STATED PLAINLY ===
The owner ruling of 2026-08-27 gives a therapist /recuperacao scoped to the patients whose MOST RECENT COMPLETED CONSULTATION WAS THEIRS. `followupOwnPatientClause` in packages/db/src/followup-selection.ts implements that by reading `done.practitioner_id` - the PRIMARY practitioner - and nothing else.

A dual-therapist appointment carries a second clinician in `appointments.practitioner_2_id`. If that session is the patient's most recent completed one, only the PRIMARY therapist gets the patient on their list. The secondary does not, even though they were in the room.

=== WHY IT WAS BUILT THIS WAY, SO NOBODY RE-ARGUES IT ===
packages/db/src/schema.ts is explicit on the column: the secondary is "de-emphasized LINKED DISPLAY data" and "PRIMARY-ONLY SEMANTICS everywhere - availability, the Servico/Localizacao auto-selects, analytics money attribution, the AI-recording primary pair + idempotency key, and the Estado/lifecycle axes ALL stay on the primary pair." `followupPractitionerSql`, which renders the practitioner NAME on this same page, reads the primary for the same reason. Scoping on the primary keeps this page consistent with every other axis; the alternative makes it the exception.

=== THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS TWO CHANGES AND NOT ONE ===
The scope clause and the displayed practitioner are the SAME SUBQUERY SHAPE - same completed set, same `ORDER BY done.starts_at DESC LIMIT 1` - so the row the scope admits is by construction the row whose clinician the page names. That is a property worth more than the line it costs.

Scoping on `practitioner_id OR practitioner_2_id` while the screen still names only the primary would show a therapist a patient whose visible clinician is somebody ELSE. That reads as a bug on the screen even though the scope is doing what was asked. SO IF THIS IS EVER BUILT, THE DISPLAY COLUMN MOVES IN THE SAME COMMIT - either naming both clinicians, or naming the one who matches the viewer.

=== WHAT WOULD CHANGE, IF IT IS EVER ACTIVATED ===
  1. `followupOwnPatientClause` - the subquery selects a pair rather than one id, or the comparison becomes an IN over both columns of the same LIMIT 1 row.
  2. `followupPractitionerSql` - the display column, in the same commit, per the paragraph above.
  3. `apps/web/lib/followup/scope.ts` - nothing, and that is the point: the mutation guard imports the clause rather than restating it, so it follows automatically. Verified by apps/web/lib/followup/scope.test.ts.
  4. `packages/db/tests/followup-selection.db.test.ts` - a fourth fixture, a patient whose most recent completed session was dual, asserted from BOTH therapists' seats.

=== WHAT ACTIVATES IT ===
A real report from the clinic, per SR-04. The affected services are the dual-participant ones - Massagem 4 Maos and Sessao Familia. Whether a secondary therapist ever wants that patient on their list is a question about how the clinic actually works, and nobody has asked it.

=== WHAT IS NOT AT RISK MEANWHILE ===
Nothing is disclosed that should not be, and nothing is lost: the patient is on the PRIMARY therapist's list and on reception's, and the front desk is who rings them. The cost is a therapist not seeing a patient they might have wanted to see, which is a smaller failure than the opposite and is the correct direction for a screen that is every patient's telephone number.
