cards.title: Pressing a channel on /recuperacao never records the contact mark: the write was fire-and-forget on a click that also navigates, and every failure was swallowed

evidence.ref:
FOUND BY IVAN ON THE DEPLOYED SCREEN 2026-08-28, RB-01 step D, after a
GENUINE BROWSER RELOAD: "pressing WhatsApp on a row opens WhatsApp, and no
'Contactado por ... em ...' line ever appears under that patient".

=== FACT 1. A WRITE WAS ATTEMPTED. THE FEATURE WAS BUILT. ===
followup-list.tsx:98-108 `mark()` called the `recordFollowupContact` server
action with the patient id and the channel. So the acceptance line did not pass
on nothing; it passed on a write that was issued and not guaranteed.

=== FACT 2. THE WRITE WAS NOT GUARANTEED TO SURVIVE THE CLICK, AND THE CODE
     SAID SO IN ITS OWN COMMENT. ===
"THE RECORD IS FIRE-AND-FORGET AND THE NAVIGATION IS NOT BLOCKED ON IT." The
handler returned immediately and the anchor's default action proceeded -
`https://wa.me/...` into a new window, `sms:` and `mailto:` handed to an
external application - while the Server Action POST was still only SCHEDULED
inside `startTransition`. A Server Action is dispatched by React's transport,
which has no way to say "this request must outlive the document". Whether it
survived was the browser's decision.

THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON THAT ISOLATES IT, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE ON
THIS CARD: `postponeFollowup` is the same shape in the same file - same
"use server" module, same requireRequestContext, same assertCan, same
followupLocationScope, same runScoped, same assertFollowupPatientInScope, same
insert, same revalidatePath. It is invoked from a BUTTON, with no navigation.
IVAN OBSERVED STEP E WORKING in the same sitting: Adiar moved the patient and
Trazer de volta returned them. So session, capability, scope guard, RLS grants,
insert and revalidate are all proven good BY OBSERVATION. The only differing
factor between the action that worked and the one that did not is the concurrent
navigation.

=== FACT 3. THE READ PATH RUNS AND REACHES THE ROW. ===
queries.ts selects patient_followup_contacts left-joined to users for the
candidate ids; page.tsx maps it to FollowupRow.contacts; followup-list.tsx:239
renders it. Proven live, and greenly, by the e2e "a recorded contact renders with
who and when" - see the section on that test below.

=== FACT 4. THE WRITE WAS NOT REFUSED, AND A REFUSAL WOULD HAVE BEEN INVISIBLE. ===
0067 grants SELECT, INSERT on patient_followup_contacts TO authenticated, with
patient_followup_contacts_insert_own_tenant WITH CHECK (tenant_id =
jwt_tenant_id()). The capability is followup:read, which reception and admin
hold. The scope guard resolves to the patient-id clause alone for an unlocated
reception user, and step E proves that same guard passing for the same user on
the same patient minutes earlier. So refusal is NOT the cause here.

IT WOULD HAVE BEEN UNKNOWABLE IF IT WERE. followup-list.tsx:102-106 caught every
rejection into an empty block, under a comment that reads well and is false in
the case that mattered: "there is nothing useful to tell the user". There is. A
mark that was never recorded is INDISTINGUISHABLE ON SCREEN from a patient
nobody has contacted - a new failure case wearing the face of a harmless known
one, on the exact row a receptionist reads to decide whether to ring somebody.

=== THE FIX ===
1. lib/followup/record-contact.ts - ONE definition of the write (capability,
   channel, scope, insert). The transport changed; the rule did not.
2. app/api/followup/contact/route.ts - a route handler, because
   `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })` is SPECIFIED to outlive the document that
   issued it and a Server Action call cannot carry that flag. CLAUDE.md prefers
   server actions "when possible"; this is the case where that clause fails, and
   the handler's header says so.
3. followup-list.tsx - the fetch is issued synchronously in the click handler,
   NOT scheduled in a transition. The anchor keeps its real href: middle click,
   long press and a JavaScript failure still reach WhatsApp, and the navigation
   is still never blocked on the write.
4. A failure is LOUD: role="alert" on the row, above the contact history, with
   401 given its OWN message because "sign in again" and "try again" are
   different instructions. Not collapsed onto one.

=== THE TEST THAT CLAIMED TO COVER THIS, AND WHY IT WAS GREEN ===
apps/web/e2e/recuperacao.spec.ts, "a recorded contact renders with who and when
(the contacts query)". It has passed since RB-01 shipped.

IT PROVES THE READ. The row it renders is inserted by seed-e2e.mjs THROUGH THE
SERVICE-ROLE CLIENT, so it arrives by a route no user takes. Its own comment is
honest about its purpose - it exists to execute the contacts query against real
rows - but its NAME describes the visible outcome, and a green test named after
the outcome is read as the outcome working.

THAT IS CRITERION F ON ACC-vacuous-guard-sweep, and the same spec confessed the
identical class one test earlier: "MY OWN E2E ASSERTED THE WRONG STRING ON THE
LANDLINE ROW AND PASSED, because the text was present - for the wrong reason."
The class was found, named, and not swept - in the file holding it.

THE WRITE PATH HAD NO TEST AT ALL. That is the answer that matters more than the
fix.

=== WHAT NOW COVERS IT ===
lib/followup/record-contact.db.test.ts - against a REAL Postgres, through the
  PRODUCTION FUNCTION, reading the row back out: the row is written; who and
  when are asserted as VALUES; a second channel is a SECOND ROW and so is the
  same channel twice (0067 grants no UPDATE, and three attempts is a different
  fact from one); an unknown channel is refused and writes nothing; a therapist
  is refused on another therapist's patient and ACCEPTED on their own.
  Hard-required in assert-rls-executed.mjs so a silent skip reddens.
app/recuperacao/contact-mark.test.tsx - keepalive is present, the transport is
  not a server action, no preventDefault, no empty catch, every catch reports,
  401 is its own branch, and the alert renders ABOVE the history.
e2e/recuperacao.spec.ts - the deployed arm, ASSERTING THE ROW AND NOT THE LABEL:
  the seeded patient already shows a "Contactado ..." line, so the contact lines
  are COUNTED and must go up by one and name the channel pressed. Plus a refused
  write that must surface an alert and must NOT add a line.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-28 ON THE DEPLOYED BUILD. BOTH PRs OBSERVED TOGETHER. ===
PR #1063 (squashed 4ded75d0) made the write survive the navigation and made a
failure loud on the row. PR #1068 (squashed e5627d2e) closed strategy ruling
SR-06 by capturing every failure branch on the SERVER, because the alert is
unreachable on the two channels whose anchors carry no target and navigate the
current document.

IVAN, ON THE DEPLOYED BUILD, 2026-08-28, STEP D RE-RUN. HIS RESULT, QUOTED:
"steps 5, 6 and 7 all showed the expected result. The contact mark records on
open, a second channel is a second line, and the same channel twice is two
lines."

THE THREE ARMS, EACH ONE A DISTINCT CLAIM:
  5  THE MARK RECORDS ON OPEN. The defect, gone. Pressing a channel now leaves a
     "Contactado por <name> em <date>" line under that patient, and it is still
     there after a reload - which is how the defect was found and the only check
     that cannot pass on optimistic client state.
  6  A SECOND CHANNEL IS A SECOND LINE. The append-only property on screen:
     0067 grants no UPDATE, so contacting by SMS after WhatsApp adds a row rather
     than replacing one.
  7  THE SAME CHANNEL TWICE IS TWO LINES. The arm that distinguishes an append
     from an upsert keyed on (patient, channel). Three attempts to reach somebody
     is a different fact from one attempt, and only the history tells them apart.

THE OBSERVATION PROVES THE #1063 HALF DIRECTLY. The #1068 half is proven by
construction and by test rather than by this sitting, and that is stated rather
than implied: a server-side capture is invisible on a screen BY DESIGN - it
exists precisely for the case where there is no screen left to look at. What
Ivan's re-run establishes is that the success path works; route.test.ts
establishes that no failure path is silent, with the negative arm reddening 9 of
10 when the capture is removed.

cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-28 BY BLUE, from Ivan's RB-01 step D.

DIAGNOSED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN, in the order the dispatch set, and the
four facts are in the evidence field above rather than repeated here.

THE ONE-LINE VERSION: the mark was written by a click that also navigated, over
a transport that cannot be told to outlive the page, with every failure caught
into an empty block. Two independent reasons it could produce nothing, and no
way for anyone to find out which.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED. The navigation is still not blocked on the
write, because a failed audit row must never cost the patient their phone call.
The anchor still has a real href. The mark still means "somebody opened the
contact", never "a message was sent", and the two new failure strings are
checked by test for not saying "enviado".

cards.title: Migration 0068 - appointments.patient_2_id has no index, and it is the Recuperacao defect

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED AND APPLIED TO PRODUCTION, PR #1073, under SR-11 apply-before-merge.

APPLIED FROM THE PROD-APPLY WORKTREE, DETACHED ON THE BRANCH (94f3e28e), never on main. That is the 0049 failure mode, checked rather than assumed.

TARGET VERIFIED BEFORE ANYTHING RAN: SUPABASE_URL host dfotoodqvmjhbdcxyaxf.supabase.co; DATABASE_URL_DIRECT the session pooler on :5432; DB user postgres.dfotoodqvmjhbdcxyaxf. CLAUDE.md:110 names dfotoodqvmjhbdcxyaxf as the PRODUCTION project.

PRE-CHECK (read-only, mandatory): last applied when=1787300200000, 68 journal entries on disk, pending 1 - 0068 with when=1787300300000. OK.

MIGRATE printed "migrations applied successfully". THAT MESSAGE IS NOT EVIDENCE: 0049 and 0058 both printed it while changing nothing. Verified independently by asking the database instead:
  last applied when=1787300300000, pending 0   (journal 67 -> 68)
  appointments_patient_2_idx present: YES
  CREATE INDEX appointments_patient_2_idx ON public.appointments USING btree (patient_2_id) WHERE (patient_2_id IS NOT NULL)
  drizzle.__drizzle_migrations: 68 rows

THE VERIFICATION EXPLAIN FROM THE REPORT, RUN ON PRODUCTION: Bitmap Heap Scan under a BitmapOr of appointments_patient_idx AND appointments_patient_2_idx. Execution Time 0.108 ms. Not a Seq Scan.

THE RECUPERACAO QUERY, ON PRODUCTION:
  BEFORE-equivalent (planner forced to the shape the missing index forced, inside a READ-ONLY transaction; an approximation, labelled as one, and no index was dropped on production)  127,169.728 ms
  AFTER, cold   227.163 ms
  AFTER, warm   170.734 ms
188 rows returned. The lab estimate was 17.9 s; production hardware under a pooler is seven times worse, which is why Sentry saw statement timeouts rather than a slow page.

RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT CHANGES NOTHING BUT SOMEBODY WILL NOTICE: production has dual=0 today - zero appointments carry patient_2_id - so the partial index is empty, 8 kB, one page. The fix still works, and the production EXPLAIN above PROVES that rather than arguing it. The defect was never about how much data sits in the column: with NO index on patient_2_id the OR cannot be answered by index at all and Postgres must seq-scan. An empty index the planner can probe is enough to build the BitmapOr. When dual-therapist sessions start being booked the index is already there and already correct.

Per SR-11, migration authorship froze again the moment this merged.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (index).

CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION. Sentry reported statement timeouts on /recuperacao and /estatisticas/indicadores two hours before this card was written, which is the exact defect docs/audit/PHASE-2-PERF.md measured.

THE DEFECT. `appointments.patient_2_id` was added by migration 0032_secondary_participants.sql:30 with a foreign key at :32 and NO INDEX. Every clause behind /recuperacao filters on `(patient_id = X OR patient_2_id = X)`. An OR whose second arm has no index cannot be answered by a BitmapOr, so Postgres sequentially scans all 41,000 appointments, once per patient row, 13,881 times per page load.

EIGHT CALL SITES, NOT ONE. Five application expressions in packages/db/src/followup-selection.ts (:63 :80 :96 :198 :214) and three RLS helper functions across migrations 0045 and 0047. The shape was correct every time; nobody checked whether the database could answer it.

MEASURED AT PRODUCTION SCALE (8,400 patients / 41,000 appointments / 1,640 dual-patient / 35,720 completed), stock postgres:16, schema and index set transcribed from this repo's own migrations:
  /recuperacao, real window     17,962.890 ms  ->  190.940 ms
  same on a 90-21 day window    14,449.862 ms  ->  ~178 ms over three runs
  patients_select RLS helper     1,077.421 ms  ->   36.255 ms
The plan flips from `Seq Scan on appointments` to `Bitmap Heap Scan` under a BitmapOr.

PARTIAL, AND THAT IS MEASURED TOO. Only 1,640 of 41,000 rows carry a secondary patient. The partial index is 32 kB against 632 kB for the full one, gives an identical plan and identical timings, and costs nothing on the 96% of inserts that leave the column NULL. `patient_2_id = <non-null uuid>` implies NOT NULL, so the planner can always use it.

AUTHORSHIP. Migration authoring transferred to BLUE for 0068 ONLY, ruling SR-11. Apply-before-merge doctrine binds: applied to production from the prod-apply worktree BEFORE the PR merges, proof is pasted journal output and a production EXPLAIN ANALYZE, never self-assertion. After 0068 merges, migration authorship freezes again until strategy releases it.

Full account: docs/audit/PHASE-2-PERF.md, Task 0.

cards.title: Loading boundaries - /recuperacao, /patients and /estatisticas had no loading.tsx

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED, PR #1074. loading.tsx on /recuperacao and /estatisticas, skeleton shells built from the packages/ui Skeleton and SkeletonTable primitives and sized to each page's real layout.

/estatisticas covers /estatisticas/indicadores too - a loading.tsx applies to its segment and everything nested under it that does not declare its own - which is the route Sentry reported OSTEOJP-WEB-4 on.

/patients IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THIS CARD LEAVES BEHIND. One was added and shard 2 went red on patients.spec.ts:288 and isolation-therapist.spec.ts:44, both "expected 404, received 200". A segment-level loading.tsx wraps the whole /patients subtree INCLUDING /patients/[id] in a Suspense boundary, so [id]'s notFound() 404 is committed as a streamed 200 before the page body runs. Both failing tests are ISOLATION guardrails, so the regression was security-relevant and not cosmetic.

THE CODEBASE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THIS DOWN, at apps/web/app/patients/page.tsx, and the file that comment warns against is exactly what I added. The comment now carries this run as evidence rather than as a warning, and /patients streams through its own LOCAL Suspense, which is the correct shape for a route with a dynamic child.

The 0068 PR's three shards were green, which is what ruled the migration out and pointed here.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (three files, no schema, no query change).

apps/web had only THREE loading.tsx files (agenda, dashboard, marcacoes) and only three files using Suspense. Eleven top-level sections with a page.tsx had no loading boundary, and /recuperacao - the slowest route in the application - was one of them.

WHAT IT COSTS. With no boundary there is no streamed shell: the router holds the current screen and paints nothing until the whole RSC response arrives. An 18-second query then presents as a frozen application rather than a loading one, which is most of what the owner actually experienced when he reported "other sections become unclickable".

THIS CARD COVERS THE THREE BUILT TODAY. The remaining eight sections are PERF-02b.

cards.title: .env.example is missing OTP_LIVE_SEND, the INVITES pair, and 27 other names the code reads

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED as PR #1094, squashed to 5cb1b0b3, all eight checks SUCCESS. .env.example named 27; the code reads 71; 44 were undocumented.

THE CARD SAID 30 AND A DISPATCH SAID FIVE, and both are the same artefact at different widths: a scan sees only the read styles it covers. process.env.NAME is found by any grep; env.NAME through an injected EnvSource is not, which this card ALREADY RECORDED for OTP_LIVE_SEND; and a name held in a CONSTANT defeats both - REMINDERS_REPLY_CAPABLE is declared as REPLY_CAPABLE_FLAG (reply-capability.ts:56) and read through it.

MY OWN FIRST SCAN COVERED TWO STYLES AND REPORTED REMINDERS_REPLY_CAPABLE AS NOT EXISTING ANYWHERE. It does. Recorded because it is the defect the file is being fixed for, reproduced by the person fixing it.

NAMES ONLY, asserted: every added line ends in '=' and the diff is checked for it.

THE TEST IS THE POINT. scripts/env-example-covers-the-code.test.mjs runs in test:scripts, in the REQUIRED job, and compares against all three read styles. Removing OTP_LIVE_SEND reddens it; it also asserts one variable per read style so an extractor that stops matching reddens instead of passing quietly. This file was hand-fixed once and drifted again.

A4_DISABLE_LOCK and PORTAL_BASE_URL get NO line and are named in the file, so the omission is a decision.

test:scripts 475 (was 472), lint 0.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (a template file; no runtime effect).

.env.example names 27 variables. The code reads 65. Three of the missing ones gate whether messages leave the platform:

  OTP_LIVE_SEND       gates ALL patient login OTP SMS
  INVITES_LIVE_SEND   gates the staff-invite email

  REMINDERS_INBOUND   gates the inbound-reply capability

Full list of the 30 missing names: docs/audit/PHASE-1-AUDIT.md, Task 2.

cards.title: apps/portal declares @sentry/nextjs and wires no Sentry at all

cards.title: OSTEOJP-WEB-4 - the indicadores query groups every appointment by patient with no date bound

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED, PR #1076. dayBounds returned start:null when the URL carried no "from", and null means NO DATE PREDICATE AT ALL. Ten aggregates then ran over every appointment and invoice ever recorded, four of them grouping by patient, at 8,400 patients and 41,429 appointments, on every load of the landing view. Bounded to twelve months; an explicit "from" always wins.

THE SCREEN IS NOT ALLOWED TO LIE ABOUT THE WINDOW. The page resolves the same default into the filters it hands the view, so the period picker renders the dates actually being queried. A page reporting all-time while querying twelve months would be the silent-degradation shape this codebase keeps cataloguing, and worse than the timeout it fixed. The floor is applied independently inside getKpiReports as defence in depth.

COLUMNS WERE ALREADY NARROW: every select in kpi-queries.ts names its fields and the widest read is three patient columns for demographics. The defect was the missing bound alone, and saying so is more useful than a cosmetic edit.

THE MATERIALIZED-VIEW ESCALATION WAS RULED IN ADVANCE AND IS NOT NEEDED. It applied only if the query still could not answer inside the statement timeout after 0068 and the bound. It answers.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (a date bound and column narrowing).

CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION by Sentry: statement timeout on /estatisticas/indicadores, alongside the /recuperacao timeout, two hours before this card was written.

The query groups every appointment by patient with no date bound. At 41,000 appointments over 8,400 patients that is the whole table, every load.

FIX AS INSTRUCTED: bound to the last 12 months and narrow the selected columns.

ESCALATION PATH, RULED IN ADVANCE so it is not a judgement call at 2am: if after the 0068 index AND the date bound it still cannot answer inside the production statement timeout at real scale, a materialized view is carded POST-LAUNCH rather than built today.

Source: docs/audit/PHASE-2-PERF.md, and Sentry OSTEOJP-WEB-4.

cards.title: /admin/sentry-check can be triggered anonymously in production

evidence.ref:
RESOLVED WITH EVIDENCE, PR #1076. THE PREMISE WAS ALREADY SATISFIED, and no second gate was built to look busy.

/admin/sentry-check on current main: redirects an unauthenticated visitor to /login; redirects any non-owner role to /; both checks sit BEFORE the throw; throws only on ?throw=1 so a bookmark or refresh cannot manufacture noise; reports whether the DSN is set and never its value.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING IS COVERAGE. The route had ZERO tests, so nothing stood between a future edit and an anonymously-triggerable error generator in production - on the page that produced OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY, the evidence HANDOVER-STATE.md records as clearing the last hard block on arming sends. An error channel outsiders can flood is one that can be made useless exactly when it is needed.

Five assertions now pin all of it, including that the role check sits BEFORE the throw: an ordering swap would raise the event and then redirect.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (an auth gate on one route).

The route that raises a deliberate test error into Sentry is not behind the admin auth gate, so anyone who knows the path can fire events into the project's issue stream from production.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY. This is the route that produced OSTEOJP-SENTRY-VERIFY, the evidence HANDOVER-STATE.md records as clearing "the last hard block on arming sends". An error channel that anonymous callers can flood is an error channel that can be made useless exactly when it is needed - the launch day it was built for.

FIX: gate behind the EXISTING admin auth. No new mechanism.

Source: this dispatch, Task 4 item two.

cards.title: Browser-extension frames produce Sentry events - executors/200.js and friends

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED, PR #1076. denyUrls for the extension URL schemes, plus a beforeSend calling isForeignFrameEvent - and the second is the half that does the work, because an extension injected as a plain script (executors/200.js, the observed example) has an ordinary https URL that denyUrls cannot see.

THE RULE: everything this app ships to a browser is served from /_next/, so an event that has frames and none of them under /_next/ is not about our code.

IT FAILS OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is the whole design. No exception values, no stacktrace, no frames, or any frame of ours anywhere in the stack: all KEPT. It asks "is ANY frame ours" rather than "is the TOP frame theirs", so an extension wrapping one of our callbacks does not cost us the event. Losing noise costs an unread issue; losing a real error costs the channel, silently.

CLIENT CONFIG ONLY. A server frame is never extension code, so the same rule on the server or edge could only ever lose a real error. 9 tests, most of them asserting that something is KEPT.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (a client-config filter).

Injected browser-extension code running in a staff member's tab raises exceptions that Sentry attributes to our application. executors/200.js is the observed example. None of it is our code and none of it is actionable, and on launch day it is noise sitting on top of the one channel that is supposed to tell us something is wrong.

FIX: a filter on the apps/web Sentry CLIENT config excluding frames whose path is not under /_next/. The exact filter is stated in the dispatch report.

DELIBERATELY CLIENT-ONLY. The server and edge configs are untouched: a server frame is never extension code, and a path filter there would be a way to lose a real error.

Source: this dispatch, Task 4 item one.

cards.title: INC-13 - E352, a use server module exporting a non-async value, on POST /recuperacao

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED, PR #1075. THE DEFECT WAS LIVE ON MAIN. It did not die with the #1063 rebuild, and it is the verification that established that rather than an assumption in either direction.

ENUMERATED, as the dispatch required. The only module in the recuperacao feature whose FIRST STATEMENT is the use-server directive is apps/web/lib/followup/actions.ts:
  POSTPONE_WEEKS              const array   NON-ASYNC VALUE - this is E352
  PostponeWeeks               type          erased before the directive means anything, harmless
  postponeFollowup            async fn      valid
  revokeFollowupPostponement  async fn      valid

NOT server-action modules, and saying so matters because both look like suspects: lib/followup/scope.ts and lib/followup/record-contact.ts open with an import of the server-only package, and the use-server string in scope.ts sits inside a comment on line 19. server-only and use server are different mechanisms.

FIX: the const, its type and its guard moved to the plain module lib/followup/postpone-weeks.ts. actions.ts now exports async functions and nothing else.

IT ALSO CLOSED A DUPLICATE: followup-list.tsx carried its own [2, 4, 8, 12], a second copy of a closed set whose entire purpose is to be closed. Both sides import the one definition now, so the screen cannot offer a length the server rejects.

PROOF THE ACTIONS LOAD: 4 tests, including a static guard that fails on any future non-async export from any use-server module in the feature, with a vacuity check so it cannot pass by scanning nothing, and which tests the FIRST STATEMENT rather than a substring.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH SAFE (verification first; a file move only if the defect is still live).

Sentry OSTEOJP-WEB-2, error E352: "a use server file exporting a non-async value", fired on POST /recuperacao. Last seen three days ago on releases dae2f9e5 and 068a83e8.

WHY THIS IS A VERIFICATION AND NOT AUTOMATICALLY A FIX. Both named releases are OLDER than #1063, which rebuilt that surface. The defect may have died with the rebuild. Asserting either way without looking is the failure this project keeps cataloguing.

METHOD, as instructed: enumerate every export of every "use server" module in the recuperacao feature against CURRENT main and state each one's kind in plain text. If a non-async export remains, move it to a plain module and prove the actions still load. If none remains, the defect died with the rebuild and this card resolves with that evidence.

Source: this dispatch, Task 3.

cards.title: The /patients list becomes a structured data table with server-side filtering and a stat strip

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED, PR #1077. Seven columns through the packages/ui Table; server-side filtering, ordering, paging and the four statistics; every filter a URL search param; EmptyState for both the empty and zero-result cases; a server component with exactly two client pieces, and they are the two that must be - the filter bar owns controlled inputs, the Table takes onSortChange.

THE NIF SEARCH NORMALISES BOTH SIDES. parseSearch already strips the typed side to digits; the STORED value may itself carry spaces or dots, and nif ILIKE '123456789%' then matches nothing at all. Phone uses the STORED phone_digits generated column from 0015. NIF has no such column and one cannot be added today, because migration authorship freezes after 0068 per SR-11, so it uses a per-row regexp_replace bounded to one tenant's role-scoped set beside an ILIKE that already scans. A nif_digits column mirroring 0015 is carded POST-LAUNCH as UX-01b rather than smuggled in.

Last visit and next appointment are correlated subqueries carrying the (patient_id OR patient_2_id) shape, in the SELECT list so they run only for the rows a page returns. They were safe to write ONLY because 0068 indexed that shape, which is why this task was sequenced after it.

"IN THE RECOVERY WINDOW" REUSES THE RECUPERACAO PREDICATE ITSELF - followupLastAttendanceClause and followupNoFutureBookingClause from @osteojp/db, the exact clauses that page selects on - so the number cannot drift from the page it summarises.

Sorting by name uses patients_tenant_name_idx directly. Sorting by last visit orders on the correlated subquery, NULLS LAST in both directions: a patient never seen is not the oldest visit, and floating them to the top of an ascending sort would bury the answer.

THE ROLE SCOPE IS UNCHANGED. therapistPatientScope and patientLocationScope are the same helpers the previous list used, ANDed in the same order. A redesign that quietly widened who can see a row would be a security change dressed as a table. The location SELECT narrows within the viewer's own scope and can never widen it.

cards.notes:
TAG: PRE-LAUNCH. OWNER REQUEST, SHAPE DECIDED. Built exactly as specified; no options were returned to the owner.

THE SHAPE, as ruled:
  - packages/ui Table, Input, Select, StatusChip. Columns: patient number, full name, NIF, phone, primary location, last visit date, next appointment date.
  - Server-side filtering and the EXISTING pagination. Never client-side filtering over the full set - at 8,400 rows that would ship the whole table to the browser.
  - Filter bar: one free-text search matching name, NIF, phone and patient number TOGETHER; one location select; one has-upcoming-appointment toggle.
  - Every filter is a URL search param, so views are shareable and the back button works.
  - A compact stat strip of four server-computed numbers on indexed queries: total patients, seen this month, with an upcoming booking, in the recovery window.
  - Server component throughout; client only where an input demands it.
  - Sorting by name and by last visit, on the existing indexes.
  - Empty and zero-result states use the ui EmptyState.
  - Density tight. It is a working tool for 8,400 rows, not a brochure.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG:
  1. NIF search MUST match with and without spaces.
  2. Last visit and next appointment come from indexed lookups. If they need the same (patient_id OR patient_2_id) shape, that is now indexed by 0068 - which is why this task is sequenced after it.

cards.title: patients.nif has no digits-only generated column, so NIF search pays a per-row regexp_replace
cards.deferred: DEFERRED POST-LAUNCH 2026-08-30. It is a migration file, and migration authorship froze again the moment 0068 merged (SR-11). It cannot be picked up without strategy releasing it, and the current cost is bounded rather than pathological.
cards.notes:
TAG: POST-LAUNCH.

UX-01's free-text search matches NIF with and without spaces, which means normalising BOTH sides: parseSearch strips the typed side to digits, and the STORED value may itself carry spaces or dots.

phone already has the right shape - migration 0015 added a STORED generated column phone_digits, precisely because "phone search called regexp_replace() per-row at query time" in its own words. nif never got the same treatment.

So lib/patients/list-queries.ts carries:
  regexp_replace(coalesce(nif, ''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') like $1

THE COST IS BOUNDED AND IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: it runs over one tenant's role- and location-scoped patient set, on a table of 8,400 rows, beside an ILIKE on full_name that already scans. It is not the 0068 shape - there is no per-row subquery and no join.

THE FIX IS A MIRROR OF 0015: add nif_digits GENERATED ALWAYS AS (regexp_replace(coalesce(nif, ''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')) STORED, index it, and change the one call site. Small, mechanical, and NOT eve-of-launch work on a frozen lane.

cards.title: INC-14 / OSTEOJP-WEB-8 - a logged-out staff request rendered a 500 instead of the login screen

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1079, launch day, under SR-12.

THE DEFECT. lib/auth/context.ts threw a bare Error("UNAUTHENTICATED") when no session existed. In a Server Component render that is an unhandled 500, so a logged-out person opening /clinical/[id] or /clinical/new got a server error page. ONE shared guard, 121 call sites across apps/web reach it.

THE FIX IS NOT "REDIRECT ON EVERY FAILURE". getRequestContext() returned null for a logged-out visitor AND for an unreachable Auth service, and the guard threw the same bare Error for both. Redirecting for everything would have fixed the 500 and introduced a worse bug: a Supabase outage presenting as everybody quietly logged out, with nothing on the error channel.

THREE OUTCOMES, each with the response it deserves:
  ok           proceed
  anonymous    no session / expired / a verified token we cannot use -> redirect /login, NOT reported
  unavailable  Auth unreachable -> Sentry captureException, then RETHROW. Never a redirect.

The discriminator is the ERROR CLASS - AuthRetryableFetchError for transport, isAuthError for a refusal - not a message substring that breaks on an SDK reword.

SEVEN PAGES UNWRAPPED: agenda, marcacoes, estatisticas, estatisticas/painel, estatisticas/indicadores, reminders/review, patients/new. Each had a bare catch{} that already called redirect("/login"), so each LOOKED correct - and each would have swallowed the guard's NEXT_REDIRECT and converted a real outage into a silent login bounce.

I COMMITTED THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL DOWN AND THE BUILD CAUGHT IT: the classifying catch swallowed DynamicServerError, what cookies() throws under static generation, and pnpm build failed prerendering /clinical/new and /admin/services. isNextControlFlow() now rethrows DYNAMIC_SERVER_USAGE, NEXT_NOT_FOUND and NEXT_REDIRECT. Written up in the file, because the shape is easy to reintroduce and hard to see.

A NARROWING, RECORDED: the first version also moved lib/scheduling/actions.ts and appointment-read-actions.ts to getRequestContext(), which needed the auth mock edited in nine test files - and the DB-gated CI job, which the local suite does NOT include because those suites self-skip without DATABASE_URL, then failed a tenth I had not found. Chasing it across 31 mock factories produced two TypeScript errors. On launch day that was the wrong trade, so both modules went back to origin/main and the diff there is COMMENT-ONLY. They keep the behaviour their tests already assert; an outage reaching them is still captured by the guard before it throws.

TESTS: 19. Each outcome asserted separately, including that an outage does NOT redirect and a plain logout does NOT report. A static guard fails on any future call site inside a try or a .catch, with a vacuity check, an ANNOTATED exemption mechanism, and a pin that there are exactly two exemptions.

cards.notes:
Sentry OSTEOJP-WEB-8. Both of today's issues fired on the vercel.app host - see INC-15, which removes that surface.

apps/api is deliberately unchanged: requirePatientPrincipal throws for route handlers that answer with a status code, which is correct there and wrong here. No API route in apps/web calls this guard, checked.

cards.title: INC-15 / OSTEOJP-WEB-7 - the vercel.app host carried no auth cookie, and every request on it looked logged out

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1080, launch day, under SR-12. RESOLVED-BY-THIS.

Both of today's Sentry issues fired on osteojp-platform.vercel.app. That host serves the same production deployment, so pages render - but the Supabase auth cookie is scoped to app.osteojp.pt, so NOTHING carries a session there. Every protected route is a logged-out request, which is how the INC-14 guard defect, one a signed-in user would never meet, filled the error channel on launch day.

IT ALSO ENDS THE SERVER-ACTION DEPLOY SKEW ON THAT HOST. A .vercel.app project domain follows the newest production deployment while a tab left open on it holds action ids from the deployment it loaded. Redirecting the host away removes the surface those errors live on rather than papering over each one.

THE EXACT CONDITION - redirect if and only if all four hold:
  process.env.VERCEL_ENV === "production"
  a Host header is present and non-blank
  its hostname, lowercased with any :port stripped, is NOT localhost | 127.0.0.1 | ::1 | [::1] | *.localhost
  and is NOT app.osteojp.pt
Target: same pathname, same query, https, app.osteojp.pt, port cleared.

308 AND NOT 301: a permanent redirect that PRESERVES METHOD AND BODY. A 301 turns a POST into a GET, silently discarding a form submission instead of moving it.

IT RUNS FIRST in proxy(), before the session work and before the flight-request short circuit, because a flight request on the wrong host is precisely the deploy-skew case.

VERCEL_ENV IS THE GATE, NOT A URL PATTERN. Vercel sets it to "preview" for previews and leaves it unset locally, so previews and laptops are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION. A regex over .vercel.app hostnames would have to keep up with Vercel's URL format.

IT FAILS OPEN IN ONE DIRECTION. A canonical-host redirect that fires when it should not is a site nobody can reach. Not-production, no Host header, blank, localhost, already canonical: all serve the request.

Matcher-excluded paths are untouched, so no signature-verified webhook can be redirected.

TESTS: 15, and most assert that NOTHING happens - the failure directions are not symmetric.

cards.notes:
Sentry OSTEOJP-WEB-7, carded resolved-by-this per dispatch.

OWNER FOLLOW-UP, and it is not code: the vercel.app host now 308s to app.osteojp.pt permanently. Browsers cache a 308. If the canonical domain ever changes, that cache is a real obstacle and the redirect must be changed BEFORE the domain moves, not after.

cards.title: E2E shard 3 went red on every open PR because the booking picker could not cross a month boundary

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1081, launch day. A BLOCKER ON main, NOT CAUSED BY EITHER OF TODAY'S FIXES.

Shard 3 failed identically on both open PRs - portal-booking-request-mode.spec.ts:333 and sync-portal-agenda.spec.ts:264 - and neither PR touches booking, the portal, the seed or the picker. One changes apps/web/lib/auth plus seven pages; the other adds a middleware host redirect that is provably inert in CI because VERCEL_ENV is unset there. IDENTICAL FAILURES ON BOTH IS WHAT RULED THEM OUT.

THE CAUSE IS A DATE. seed-e2e.mjs seeds therapistLocOne at LOCATION_A for weekday 1 ONLY - Monday 09:00-13:00. The picker opens on the CURRENT month. Run the suite on a Monday afternoon and the only Monday left in the month is today, already past, so the month view offers nothing and the helper concluded empty-calendar. 2026-08-31 is a Monday; the runs were at ~16:30 UTC.

THE CALENDAR WAS NEVER EMPTY - the next selectable Monday was one month click away. The helper simply could not cross a month boundary. It now pages forward, bounded to two clicks, before concluding anything.

TEST HELPER ONLY. No product code, no seed change, no assertion weakened. The seed was deliberately NOT widened: the CI-is-a-failure-not-a-skip guard depends on that condition, and widening would have made this pass by removing the property other tests rely on.

Confirmed by the fix itself: shard 3 went green on the very next run.

cards.notes: A SECOND, SEPARATE INFRASTRUCTURE OBSERVATION FROM THE SAME DAY, recorded because it will recur and should not be diagnosed from scratch: after this fix, shard 3 failed once more on #1080 with FOUR different spec files and several 2.1-minute timeouts, on an 18m48s run against a usual 7-9m. A re-run of the same commit passed in 7m36s. That is runner degradation, not a code defect, and it is the shape CI-shard-timeout-budget-defeats-flaky-retry already describes.

cards.title: NO reminder could be dispatched in production: the pedido gate keyed on a column every appointment carries

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1083 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. THE 24h SMS AND THE 48h EMAIL WERE BOTH DEAD, INDEPENDENTLY, AND THEY COMPOUNDED.

24h SMS: dispatchReminder's pedido gate was confirmation_state = 'pending'. That column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' (0024) and the staff create path leaves it UNSET ON PURPOSE so the default applies - actions.ts says exactly that. Every appointment in the system is born pending, so the gate refused every one of them.

48h EMAIL: patients.reminder_email_enabled is DEFAULT false (0019, JP's product decision), so the email channel was off for every patient who had not opted in. Nobody had.

THE LOOP THAT MADE IT UNRECOVERABLE: the ONLY writer that ever cleared 'pending' was redeem.ts, reached by clicking the confirm link IN THE 48h EMAIL - the message the other half of the defect prevented. The pipeline could not reach its own unlock.

WHY THE SUITE WAS GREEN. pedido-not-remindable.test.ts had the correct negative arm and NAMED it - "a gate that skipped every scheduled row would silently kill reminders for ordinary staff-booked appointments" - then spelled that arm confirmationState: null. Null is what rows PREDATING 0024 carry; nothing the product writes today is null. The arm guarded a state production no longer produces.

THE FIX: the gate keys on origin = 'patient_portal' while still scheduled, which is the DATABASE's own definition (public.is_unconfirmed_pedido, 0059/0067). 0067's header states the property that makes it safe: "a staff booking has neither marker". R10's reasoning is untouched; it was implemented against the wrong column.

Every negative arm in that suite now uses the values the product actually writes, and the new arm - an ordinary staff booking, pending, MUST dispatch - is the one whose absence cost the launch its reminders.

cards.notes: A NEGATIVE ARM IS ONLY WORTH ITS FIXTURE. Recorded as a shape because it recurs: the test named the right property and proved it against a state the product stopped producing at migration 0024. The 48h half of the defect is NOT closed by this card - it is a JP product decision, Q-W14-01.

cards.title: 48h is email only and 24h is SMS only, enforced server-side instead of resting on a fan-out detail

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1083 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. Owner ruling 2026-08-31.

IT WAS ALREADY TRUE AND IT WAS NOT ENFORCED. REMINDER_OFFSETS carries one channel per offset and the scheduler fans out that one, so the pair was always right AS LONG AS the scheduler was the only caller. Nothing refused a wrong (offset, channel) pair, and the tenant config can switch both channels on independently.

TWO PLACES HOLD IT NOW. planReminderChannels cannot produce a twin whatever the toggles say; dispatchReminder refuses a mismatched pair outright with its own outcome reason, channel_not_for_offset - so a stale queued run from before a routing change cannot deliver a 48h SMS.

ROUTING FIRST, PREFERENCE SECOND, and the order is the design. Routing decides WHICH channel an offset may use; the preference decides whether that channel may be used at all for this patient. A patient who disabled SMS gets NO 24h message - not an email in its place. A suppressed channel is a suppressed message, never a message on the other channel.

cards.notes: The 48h send is skipped without error when the patient has no email: outcome {dispatched:false, reason:'channels_off'}, which is a non-error skip the caller already handles. What this card does NOT fix is REACH - see Q-W14-01.

cards.title: Decision A: the booking confirmation is scoped to portal patient bookings by appointments.origin

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1083 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. Owner decision A, 2026-08-31.

THE PREDICATE: appointments.origin = 'patient_portal' - the authorship the system already records (0067) and the same column is_unconfirmed_pedido keys on. NOT created_by IS NULL: 0067's header records that appointments-created-by-provenance.test.ts proves 7/7 against live Postgres that 0049's WITH CHECK is a DISJUNCTION, so a STAFF principal may insert a null creator. Absence of a creator is not evidence of a patient (SR-08).

ENFORCED IN THE DISPATCH, not at the three enqueue sites, so a fourth call site inherits the rule instead of having to remember it.

A SECOND GATE SHIPPED WITH IT AND IT IS THE REASON THE CARD IS NOT SIMPLY 'DONE': the confirmation also refuses an unaccepted pedido. JP ruled 2026-08-06 that all twelve bookable services are request-mode with ZERO auto-confirmed, so every portal booking IS a pedido - and the approved body opens "A sua marcacao esta confirmada". Sending it at request time tells the patient the clinic accepted something it has not seen.

cards.notes: CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: with both gates, the confirmation currently sends for NOTHING. Staff bookings are out of scope by decision A; portal bookings are pedidos. Resolution is Q-W14-02 - recommendation is to send it when reception ACCEPTS, which needs the accept path to emit appointment/scheduled (card W14-confirmation-on-accept).

cards.title: The Twilio inbound webhook is wired to the classifier, with four guard rails and a signature check

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1083 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31.

SIGNATURE: HMAC-SHA1 over the configured URL plus key-sorted POST params, constant-time compare. The URL comes from REMINDERS_INBOUND_BASE_URL, NEVER request.url or x-forwarded-* - trusting those on an open route lets a forger choose the string their own signature was computed over. Proven by a DIFFERENTIAL test against Twilio's own SDK, not a constant copied out of a doc.

TENANT from REMINDERS_INBOUND_TENANT_ID, never the payload. There is no Twilio-number-to-tenant table and authoring one is frozen (SR-11).

GUARD RAILS, all four proven against real Postgres (inbound-reply.db.test.ts, hard-required in assert-rls-executed.mjs): status must be scheduled; the reply must land between the 24h reminder's send instant and the appointment start, with the window DERIVED from REMINDER_OFFSETS; exactly one live patient must carry the number (limit(2) not limit(1) - WF-07's refusal applied here); the stored-phone predicate matches exactly the four forms normalizePhonePT accepts, not a nine-digit suffix.

THE CONFIRM CAN LOSE TO THE DATABASE. appointments_no_double_confirmed (0061) is an EXCLUDE constraint and two scheduled rows on one window stay legal, so a SIM can ask for a second confirmed row it forbids. 23P01 rolls the transaction back, the appointment stays scheduled, the audit row is written in its own transaction, and reception gets the thing that resolves it.

AUDIT: every status change writes audit_log with metadata.source = "patient-sms-reply" and actor_user_id null (a patient has no users row). NOT patient_audit_log - its auth_means is under a DB CHECK admitting only signed_token and otp_session, and widening it is a migration.

cards.notes: ARMED BY NOBODY HERE. REMINDERS_INBOUND stays off, REMINDERS_INBOUND_TENANT_ID and REMINDERS_INBOUND_BASE_URL are unset, and the sender is still alphanumeric so no reply can physically arrive (Q-W14-04). The reception review QUEUE is the one part that could not be finished: it needs sms_inbound_events and migration authorship is frozen (Q-W14-05). recordForReview is called and is a no-op until that table exists.

cards.title: A Messaging Service SID was being passed as Twilio's From parameter

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1083 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31.

clients.ts sent every message as messages.create({ to, from, body }) with from = TWILIO_SMS_FROM ?? TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID. From takes a phone number, an alphanumeric sender id or a short code; routing through a Messaging Service is a DIFFERENT parameter.

docs/qa/twilio-proof.md asserted the old behaviour "(which Twilio accepts)". That claim was never exercised: the 2026-07-11 delivery proof ran with TWILIO_SMS_FROM set, so the fallback branch has NEVER sent a message. It was untested, not proven.

It now resolves to MessagingServiceSid when the value matches MG + 32 hex. NOTHING CHANGES for the current production config (TWILIO_SMS_FROM=OsteoJP), which twilio-proof.test.ts pins.

cards.notes: This is the arm the E.164 migration in Q-W14-04 will land on: routing the interactive SMS through a Messaging Service that owns a two-way number is the recommended shape, and it could not have worked before this fix.

cards.title: JP: three new reply-acknowledgement bodies, plus whether the 24h SMS may say 'Responda SIM'

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1087 (BLUE), merged 2026-09-01. JP APPROVED ALL FOUR ITEMS on 2026-09-01, verbally to the owner (WF-18 A and B).

The three acknowledgements are approved EXACTLY AS WRITTEN - not a word changed between shipping `approved: false` on 2026-08-31 and being approved. The registry records JP and the date on their own constant, not the shared 2026-08-03 one, so the nine bodies he approved that day are not silently re-dated.

The 24h SMS now carries "Responda SIM para confirmar ou NAO para cancelar". The four approved lines are byte-identical and asserted as such; the keywords are DERIVED from INBOUND_KEYWORDS, so the words the reminder tells a patient to send cannot drift from the words the classifier recognises.

RENDERED: 143 chars, GSM-7, ONE segment on the worst-case fixture.

cards.notes:
THE REPLY LINE IS CAPABILITY-GATED (same-day correction, 2026-09-01). It appends ONLY when the configured outbound sender can receive a reply: TWILIO_SMS_FROM is an E.164 number, or a messaging service is configured AND REMINDERS_REPLY_CAPABLE is exactly "true" (the sender pool cannot be inspected from here, so it is declared rather than guessed). With an alphanumeric sender - production today - the 24h body renders WITHOUT the line and without advertising the reply window.

THE APPROVAL COVERS BOTH RENDERINGS, mechanically rather than generously: the gated body is BYTE-IDENTICAL to JP's 2026-08-03 approval and a STRICT PREFIX of the 2026-09-01 amendment, so there is no rendering under this id that nobody has approved. templates.test.ts asserts the prefix property in both locales.

THE LINE ARMS ITSELF the moment the sender becomes replyable - plus, if messaging-service routing is used, the flag is set. The answer is computed PER SEND, not captured at module load, so no code change and no deploy beyond the one the env change already needs.

THE FEE-SEGMENT COST FROM MY EARLIER REPORT IS NOW CONDITIONAL, not permanent: with the gate off the fee-bearing body is 153 chars and fits with 7 to spare, exactly as before. Armed, the two lines together overflow and renderSms throws rather than splitting. See LE-fee-line-no-longer-fits-one-segment.

cards.title: JP: reminder_email_enabled defaults to false by JP's own decision, so the 48h email reaches nobody

evidence.ref:
APPLIED TO PRODUCTION 2026-09-01 under SR-15, apply-before-merge. Migration 0070.

TARGET REF VERIFIED FIRST in the prod-apply worktree, detached on the feature branch.

JOURNAL PROOF: drizzle.__drizzle_migrations held 69 rows before and 70 after.

READ BACK FROM PRODUCTION, not asserted:
  reminder_email_enabled default   false -> true
  patients total                   8,404
  with a registered email          1,930
  without an email                 6,474
  ROWS CHANGED BY THE BACKFILL     1,930
  ROWS LEFT UNTOUCHED              6,474
  patients with an email still off 0
  reminder_sms_enabled default     unchanged (true)

This reverses 0019's DEFAULT false - JP's own 2026-08-03-era decision - which made the 48h reminder reach NOBODY for the entire life of the pipeline, because the offset routes to email only and no patient had ever switched the flag on.

cards.notes: THE BACKFILL COULD NOT PRESERVE AN OPT-OUT and does not pretend to: `false` is the stored value for both 'opted out' and 'never chose', the portal PATCH writes no audit row, and SR-08 forbids building a set from an absence. Anyone who had deliberately switched email off is now switched on. JP ruled knowing that; the portal toggle is the mitigation. The provenance gap itself is carded as LE-reminder-pref-has-no-provenance.

cards.title: Ivan: the production sender is alphanumeric, so no patient reply can physically arrive
cards.notes: TWILIO_SMS_FROM=OsteoJP - the PT alphanumeric sender approved 2026-06-11 and confirmed on the handset in the 2026-07-11 delivery proof. Alphanumeric sender IDs are ONE-WAY. Task 4 is inert until this changes, whatever the code does. Console actions: provision a PT mobile long code; add it to the Messaging Service that already holds the OsteoJP alphanumeric sender; point that service's inbound webhook at https://app.osteojp.pt/api/webhooks/twilio/inbound; then either set TWILIO_SMS_FROM to the E.164 number or clear it and set TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID. Recommendation inside it: move the confirmation and follow-up SMS to the same sender too, so a patient sees ONE identity from the clinic. Q-W14-04.

cards.title: The reception review queue needs sms_inbound_events, and migration authorship is frozen

evidence.ref:
APPLIED TO PRODUCTION 2026-08-31 under SR-17 (dispatched as SR-14), apply-before-merge.

TARGET REF VERIFIED FIRST, in the prod-apply worktree, detached on the feature branch - never main, which is the failure mode where drizzle-kit silently no-ops against a tree that does not carry the file.

JOURNAL PROOF: drizzle.__drizzle_migrations held 68 rows before and 69 after; `to_regclass('public.sms_inbound_events')` was null before and resolves after.

OBJECT PROOF read back from production: RLS enabled; three policies (staff_select, staff_update, staff_insert); six constraints including the classification CHECK, the resolution CHECK and the resolved-pair CHECK; four indexes including the partial queue index and the tenant-scoped provider-sid unique index; grants authenticated = INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE with NO DELETE and NO TRUNCATE, and the `patient` role holding NO GRANT AT ALL.

Zero rows in the new table, as expected: the webhook that fills it is not armed.

cards.notes: SR-17 (dispatched as SR-14) froze migration authorship again on merge. Q-W14-01's reminder_email_enabled default flip is a DIFFERENT migration and is still blocked - it needs a JP product decision AND a further strategy release, and this ruling released one number.

cards.title: Emit appointment/scheduled when reception ACCEPTS a pedido, so the confirmation is true when it arrives

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1085 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. Owner ruling WF-17: the confirmation sends at ACCEPTANCE, never at request time. confirmAppointmentRequest emits appointment/scheduled post-commit with the accepted appointment as its single target, so confirmationEligible is true by construction and the confirmation fires exactly once.

At that moment the status is `confirmed`, so dispatchConfirmation's two gates - origin = patient_portal, and not an unaccepted pedido - both pass, and the body JP approved on 2026-08-03 is TRUE when it arrives. No new copy and no new approval.

cards.notes: Proven against the real event flow, not against a mock of it: the real enqueue helper, the real trigger filter, the real fan-out computation and the real dispatch gates, with only inngest.send faked because it is the one call that leaves the process.

cards.title: apps/api emits NO Inngest event on a portal booking, so a portal appointment gets no reminders either

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1085 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. CLOSED BY THE SAME LINE as the confirmation, and it was the wider half.

apps/api has no inngest dependency and store.createBooking emits nothing, so a portal-booked appointment received NO 48h email and NO 24h SMS - not before acceptance, and not after it either, because nothing had ever enqueued them. The three staff paths in lib/scheduling/actions.ts were the only emitters in the repo.

FIXED WHERE THE APPOINTMENT BECOMES REAL, not where it is requested. Emitting from apps/api would have needed the Inngest client there, an INNGEST_EVENT_KEY in the portal project's environment, and a second place that knows the reminder contract - and under WF-17 it would still have been the wrong moment.

cards.notes: The proof carries a SOURCE-LEVEL arm asserting apps/api still emits nothing, because an absence cannot be observed by calling something. If a future change makes the portal emit at booking time, that arm goes red rather than the defect shipping.

cards.title: The reception reply queue is built and worked: migration 0069, RLS, its own capability, and three buttons that do what they say

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1085 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. THE PAGE IS /reminders/review, behind REMINDERS_INBOUND.

WHY A SECOND TABLE WHEN audit_log ALREADY RECEIVES EVERY REPLY. Two reasons, either sufficient: audit_log is contractually ids-and-instants only (CLAUDE.md rule 7) so it may not hold the message BODY, and it is append-only by RLS so a row cannot be marked done. A queue that cannot be resolved is a list that grows forever. The audit row STAYS and is still written for every reply.

THE SENDER'S NUMBER IS HASHED. A queue row does not need a dialable number - it carries patient_id whenever the sender matched - and an UNMATCHED number is the one piece of PII the clinic has no relationship to.

THE CAPABILITY CHANGED AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE REVIEW. The page shipped gated on `appointments:read`, which EVERY role holds - the exact mistake `guest_requests:read` exists because of, where a therapist saw the whole tenant's guest queue on deployed production. It now has `sms_replies:read` and `sms_replies:resolve`, two rather than one because seeing a queue and moving a real appointment from it are different acts. 0069's policies carry the same role set, so the application check is the first gate and not the only one.

PROVEN: 16 RLS isolation assertions (cross-tenant both directions, THERAPIST refused, patient role refused at the TABLE gate before RLS is consulted, redelivery refused by the unique index, the resolved-pair CHECK, no DELETE for anyone) plus 13 store tests against real Postgres. Both hard-required in assert-rls-executed.mjs.

cards.notes: THE THREE BUTTONS NOW ACT. "Marcar como confirmada" moves the matched appointment rather than filing the reply. Reception has NO time window - a person reading the message IS the authority the automatic window defers to - but the DATA guard stays: only a scheduled appointment may move, and a confirm that would create a second confirmed overlap loses to 0061 and writes NOTHING, leaving the item in the queue.

cards.title: Reception accepting a pedido now emits the scheduling event, so the confirmation and both reminders finally fire for portal patients

evidence.ref: SHIPPED #1085 (BLUE), merged 2026-08-31. Owner ruling WF-17. One call in confirmAppointmentRequest's post-commit block closes both W14-confirmation-on-accept and W14-portal-bookings-emit-no-reminder-events.

cards.notes: Sequenced exactly as the earlier card said it should be: the accept path is in apps/web and turned out to be the better single emit point for BOTH the confirmation and the reminders.

cards.title: The reply line and the fee line cannot share one segment: armed together they overflow
cards.notes:
NARROWED BY THE 2026-09-01 CAPABILITY GATE, not closed. The conflict was reported as permanent; it is conditional.

TODAY (alphanumeric sender, reply line gated OFF): the 24h body is 99 chars and the fee-bearing body is 153 - ONE segment, 7 to spare, exactly the budget that existed before WF-18 B.

ARMED (E.164 sender or a declared messaging service): the body is 148, leaving 12, and the fee line is 53. Together they exceed 160 and renderSms THROWS rather than splitting - assertSmsCompliant runs after both appends, which is what makes that guarantee real.

NOTHING IS AT RISK ON EITHER PATH. Three gates on the fee line are all shut: REMINDERS_FEE_NOTICE_ENABLED unarmed, reminder.24h.sms.fee_notice approved:false, counsel unsigned.

IT BECOMES A DECISION THE DAY BOTH LAND. If the Portuguese number arrives AND counsel signs, variant B needs a fee line of 12 characters or fewer - which no usable wording fits - or acceptance of a two-segment 24h SMS for patients who accepted the terms. A JP-and-counsel choice, NOT one this lane may take by trimming approved copy. fee-notice.test.ts pins both arms so the day it matters is not the day it is discovered.

cards.title: A patient reminder preference records no provenance, so an opt-out is indistinguishable from a never-chose
cards.notes:
SURFACED BY 0070 AND NOT CLOSED BY IT. `reminder_email_enabled` and `reminder_sms_enabled` are bare booleans; the portal profile PATCH (apps/api/lib/patient/profile.ts) writes no audit row. So `false` means BOTH 'this patient opted out' and 'this patient never opened the screen', and nothing can tell them apart.

WHAT IT ALREADY COST: 0070's backfill re-enabled email for every patient with an address INCLUDING anyone who had deliberately switched it off. There was no predicate that could have spared them - SR-08 is explicit that a set must be built from positive provenance, and there is none. JP ruled the reversal knowing this.

IT REMAINS TRUE AFTER 0070. A patient who switches email off tomorrow leaves the column at false with the same ambiguity, so a future default change would face the identical problem. The fix is a provenance record on the preference change - an audit row, or a `chosen_at` column - and it is a migration plus a portal change, so it needs a strategy release. Not urgent while no further default change is planned; recorded so the next one does not rediscover it.

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED #1089 (BLUE), merged 2026-09-01.

THE DEFECT. WF-18 B added "Responda SIM para confirmar ou NAO para cancelar" to the 24h SMS on the same day. The live sender is `OsteoJP`, a PT ALPHANUMERIC SENDER ID, which is ONE-WAY: a handset shown one disables the reply field or fails the send.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN NEVER ASKING, which is the reason it was fixed the same day rather than carded. The failure is SILENT AT THE PATIENT'S END. Someone who types SIM believes they confirmed; the agenda still reads `agendada`; reception rings them and they are certain they already answered. Asking and not hearing damages trust in a way that not asking does not.

THE FIX ADAPTS THE MESSAGE TO THE SENDER rather than waiting for the sender - the Portuguese number is delayed on Twilio inventory and the clinic is sending reminders today.

MEASURED, BOTH STATES, through the production render path:
  GATE OFF (today):  94 chars, GSM-7, 1 segment, byte-identical to JP 2026-08-03
  GATE ON:          143 chars, GSM-7, 1 segment, the 2026-09-01 amendment
  the off body is a STRICT PREFIX of the on body, asserted in both locales

41 tests: the capability matrix in both directions, exact-string flag semantics, the refusal of a flag override on a visible alphanumeric sender, and a dispatch-level arm proving the gate is actually CONSULTED where the message is built - a gate nobody asks is this same defect one layer out.

cards.title: The 24h SMS told patients to reply SIM while the sender was an alphanumeric id that cannot receive one
cards.notes:
THE CLASSIFIER, WEBHOOK AND REVIEW QUEUE ARE UNTOUCHED, deliberately. An unprompted reply - someone who knows to answer, or a message that reaches a number we later own - is still classified, still moves the appointment under the same guard rails, and still lands in reception's queue. The gate changed what the clinic SAYS, not what it HEARS.

IT ALSO CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER REPORT: I recorded the fee-segment cost as permanent. With the gate it is conditional, and today's budget is unchanged from before WF-18 B.

cards.title: The board says the client-data import has not run; migration 0068 and the PERF-01 card say production carries 8,400 patients and 41,429 appointments

evidence.ref:
CLOSED BY SR-17 (dispatched as SR-14), 2026-09-01, RESOLVED AGAINST THE SECOND COLUMN: the import ran. Owner-confirmed go-live plus a production dashboard reporting a 153.3 MB database, relayed as text because standing rule 1 means no terminal may read it.

This is the EIGHTH card class of false status recorded on this board (PORTAL-REHYDRATE §2 item 2a counts seven to 2026-08-20), and it is a shape the reconciler cannot see: `node docs/board/reconcile-board.mjs docs/board/portal-board.json` exits 0 with no mismatches on this exact contradiction, because its stale-card rule keys on the PRs a card CITES and its gate-claim rule on the gate a card CLAIMS. A card whose PROSE is falsified by another file's prose triggers neither.

WHAT RESOLVES IT: two counts from production, run by Ivan. Nothing else. The exact statement is in the report.

cards.title: The /patients stat strip runs six correlated appointment subqueries per patient over the whole scoped set, on every page load

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED as PR #1093, squashed to 3e0f3780. All eight checks SUCCESS on a code diff, so the DB-gated job and all three E2E shards ran for real.

THE STAT STRIP IS ONE PASS. It unnests appointments over BOTH participant columns once, aggregates per patient, and joins. Production scale, warm, three runs: 171.630 / 173.828 / 195.401 ms -> 38.406 / 38.651 / 38.986 ms. FOUR AND A HALF TIMES, not the fifteen the PERF-01 prototype measured - and the difference is the point: the prototype ALSO folded patientLocationScope into the aggregate, which is a rewrite of a security predicate and was deliberately not shipped. 4.5x is what the safe half buys, measured rather than inherited.

THE ISOLATION SUITE DID NOT EXIST AND NOW DOES. apps/web/lib/patients/list-queries.db.test.ts, 23 tests, real database, through the production functions, RLS enforced. Every expectation is fixed BY CONSTRUCTION from the fixture, because comparing old against new proves they AGREE and cannot prove both are wrong.

SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS BEFORE THE REWRITE WAS WRITTEN: patient_2_id arm 8/23 red, primary_location_id arm 8/23 red, activePatientsOnly in stats 5/23 red, in the page 5/23 red, no-future-booking clause 3/23 red, roleScope->undefined GREEN. Four re-run red against the rewritten code, two of them aimed at its own new failure modes.

TWO THINGS THE CONTROLS FOUND, BOTH IN MY OWN WORK. (1) The no-future-booking control stayed green because no patient in the fixture had BOTH a last visit in the window and a future booking, so that clause had no assertion; a patient was added that exists solely for it. (2) roleScope->undefined stays green and it is CORRECT that it does: RLS 0047 is the CEILING, so the app layer can only narrow below it. The suite therefore proves the app layer never narrows wrongly and says nothing about it narrowing at all - so patientLocationScope is pinned SEPARATELY through the BYPASSRLS handle, which is the only proof of its own it has ever had.

ONE PROPERTY LOST AND REPLACED. The old version BOUND followupLastAttendanceClause and followupNoFutureBookingClause so its number could not drift from /recuperacao. The aggregate cannot bind them - they ARE the per-row scan it removes - so a drift test counts the window BOTH ways on the same fixture and asserts they agree.

THE MEMO. resolveViewerLocationIds ran once per caller in its own transaction: three times per /patients render, five or six on the agenda; React cache() was used nowhere in apps/web. Six transactions per load became four, nineteen statements thirteen. Keyed on the three primitives of RequestContext, never the object. THE LOCAL 2% IS NOT THE BENEFIT and is not quoted as one: the harness has no network latency, so it cannot measure pooler round trips. The COUNT is exact.

THIRTY CONCURRENT SESSIONS, POOL MAX UNCHANGED AT 2, three paired runs:
  /patients p50 1579/1861/1712 -> 592/742/655   p95 1751/2370/2044 -> 667/1005/755
  agenda    p50 1781/1933/1710 -> 696/852/714   p95 2722/3617/3137 -> 1050/1388/1180
  create    p50 1361/1645/1513 -> 541/697/569
  wall      6402/7840/6982 ms  -> 2479/3142/2666 ms
~2.6x, consistent across pairs. The BEFORE figures exceed PERF-01's 1330/1569/1136 because the box now also runs the local Supabase stack; the within-run ratio is the trustworthy number and the drift is stated rather than hidden.

No migration, no index, no RLS policy edit, no console change, no pool change.

cards.notes:
BLOCKED BY THE STOP CONDITION ON INC-16, NOT BY THE WORK. The dispatch halts on "any Phase 1 finding that contradicts the board" and orders no further action; the rewrite is measured, equivalence-proven and deliberately unbuilt.

THE REWRITE IS SECURITY-RELEVANT AND MUST NOT BE MERGED ON THE LAB NUMBER ALONE. It reimplements patientLocationScope's predicate inside the aggregate, and lib/patients/scope.ts says in its own words that "a redesign that quietly widened who can see a row would be a security change dressed as a table". Shipping it needs the DB-gated isolation suites green, not just the equivalence check above.

SEPARATE AND SMALLER: memoising resolveViewerLocationIds per request (React cache()) removes 270 of 780 transactions and 810 of 2418 statements at 30 sessions. It moved p50 by only ~2% on the LOCAL harness because a local staff_locations read is 0.083 ms; its real value is on production, where each removed statement is a round trip across the transaction pooler and each removed transaction is a connection acquisition against a 2-slot pool. THE HARNESS CANNOT SIZE THAT because it has no network latency, and this card says so rather than quoting the local 2% as the answer.

NOT MEASURED, BECAUSE STANDING RULE 1 FORBIDS IT: Sentry route timings, pg_stat_statements, the pooler's own connection limit, and Vercel function duration. The dispatch asked for all four. The read-only scripts and the exact console click paths are in the report.

cards.title: scripts/perf-seed-loadtest.mjs would seed 2,000 patients into the LIVE clinic: its safety abort names the retired Supabase project, not the current one

evidence.ref:
SHIPPED as PR #1092, squashed to ca970a9a. Every required check SUCCESS on a CODE diff, so the DB-gated suite and all three E2E shards ran for real rather than taking the docs-only skip path.

THE GUARD IS NOW POSITIVE. packages/db/seed/local-target.ts admits a target only by affirmatively recognising an allowed local host, with exact equality on a PARSED host - never includes(), which is an allowlist carrying the blocklist's disease. Wired into resolveSeedDatabaseUrl (all seven dev-data seeds) and into scripts/perf-seed-loadtest.mjs via scripts/local-target.mjs, which reads the host list from the TypeScript declaration at runtime rather than copying it.

THE DEFECT WAS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ARGUED. With assertLocalTarget removed as a negative control the seeder reaches the production pooler and returns 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres"'. A fake password in the fixture is the only thing that stopped it writing.

SR-08, BOTH ARMS. Every refusal case is driven through the predicate it replaced and asserted to have PASSED there: an unlisted production-shaped ref, 127.0.0.1.attacker.example.com, a local address sitting only in the password, and an unparseable URL. Three negative controls run and restored: exact-equality -> includes turns 2 red, unparseable -> allowed turns 1 red, guard removed from the seeder turns 2 red.

THE DRIVER IMPORT MOVED BEHIND THE GUARD. It previously used an absolute path into another developer's home directory, so a module-not-found was doing the work everyone believed the guard was doing, and an abort for the wrong reason is not an abort.

Gates by exit code: db:check-journal 0, lint 0 (0 errors), typecheck 0 (11/11), test 0 (8/8), test:scripts 0 (472, was 460), build 0 (4/4).

cards.notes:
FOUND WHILE LOOKING FOR A LOAD-TEST HARNESS FOR THIS JOB, which is exactly how it would be found in anger.

scripts/perf-seed-loadtest.mjs:23 reads `if (DB_URL.includes("jaxmkwoxjcgzkwxgbayx"))`. That ref is the RETIRED old production project. packages/db/seed/seed-guard.ts:31 is the canonical list and holds BOTH: `export const PROD_REFS: string[] = ["dfotoodqvmjhbdcxyaxf", "jaxmkwoxjcgzkwxgbayx"]`, with dfotoodqvmjhbdcxyaxf commented on line 24 as "PRODUCTION (Central EU / Frankfurt), the live clinic".

SO THE GUARD PASSES ON PRODUCTION. Pointed at the current DATABASE_URL the script does not abort; it inserts 2,000 patients and 20,000 appointments (N_PAT/N_APT at :53-54) into the live clinic, with `ssl: "require", max: 4`.

TWO THINGS MAKE IT WORSE, not better. Its filename and header advertise it as THE perf harness, so a terminal or a person asked to load-test reaches for it first. And its header says "SAFETY: Aborts if DATABASE_URL_DIRECT/DATABASE_URL contains the PROD ref" - a claim that is now false, which is the §1.3 shape exactly: a guard that reports something reasonable while checking the wrong thing.

It is also already dead as written: line 16 imports postgres from `/Users/sm33xy/Projects/OsteoJP/node_modules/...`, an absolute path on somebody else's machine. That is what stops it TODAY, and it is not a safety property - one `pnpm add` away from being the only thing that was.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND IS NOT AUTHORED HERE, because this dispatch's stop condition halts before Phase 2: import PROD_REFS from packages/db/seed/seed-guard.ts and refuse on any member, the way scripts/import/prod-refs.mjs and packages/db/scripts/assert-not-prod.ts already do; and fix the import path. Alternatively delete the script - this job's own harness (a disposable postgres:16 container pinned to 127.0.0.1) replaces it and never holds a credential at all.

SHIPPED, WITH ONE GAP LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE AND CARDED SEPARATELY. seed/form-templates.ts and seed/roles.ts are NOT gated: they are configuration seeds the owner runs against production deliberately, so a local-only gate would break a documented workflow. They carry no target guard at all today - see SEC-config-seeds-have-no-target-guard.

cards.title: The reconciler cannot see a card falsified by another committed file's prose - the fourth staleness shape
cards.notes:
CARDED UNDER SR-16, DESIGN ONLY. The ruling says card the design and do not build it, and this card deliberately stops at the design.

THE SHAPE. `reconcile-board.mjs` runs two rules. The stale-card rule keys on the PRs a card CITES; the gate-claim rule on the gate a card CLAIMS. Both read the card's own fields. A card whose PROSE is falsified by ANOTHER committed file's prose touches neither, so the reconciler exits 0 and reports no mismatch - which it did, on INC-16, on the exact contradiction that halted PERF-01.

IT IS THE FOURTH SHAPE, and the header of `reconcile-board.mjs` already names three: a card citing a merged PR while open; a card claiming a gate the gate does not hold; and a card written BEFORE the work and never touched after, which cites nothing and claims nothing. The fourth is different from the third: the third is silent because the card says nothing checkable, the fourth is loud in the WRONG FILE. Five cards said the import had not run while a merged migration header, a shipped card's production EXPLAIN and a merged audit all said it had.

WHY A FIFTH RULE IS THE OBVIOUS FIX AND PROBABLY THE WRONG ONE. The tempting rule is a cross-file assertion scan: extract factual claims from card prose, extract them from docs and migration headers, diff. That is natural-language contradiction detection over 246 cards and a repository of prose, and its failure mode is the one this project keeps cataloguing - it would be WRONG QUIETLY, reporting a clean board because its extractor stopped matching, which is exactly how PROD_REFS sat empty for months behind a working-looking comment.

THREE CANDIDATES, NARROWEST FIRST, EACH MECHANICAL:

  A. PIN THE FACTS THAT MULTIPLE FILES ASSERT. The collision was over row counts and go-live state. If those live in ONE committed place that both the board and the docs read, they cannot disagree - the same argument `getPatientListStats` makes for reusing the recuperacao predicate rather than restating it. Narrow, mechanical, and it only covers facts somebody thought to name.

  B. MAKE THE MIGRATION HEADER A CITATION. 0068's header asserted a production state in prose. If a migration that asserts one names the card that owns it, the reconciler can check that card's status the way it already checks PR citations. Reuses an existing rule instead of inventing a fourth.

  C. ACCEPT THE GAP AND MOVE THE GUARD TO THE BOOT REPORT. PORTAL-REHYDRATE already carries the only thing that catches the third shape - re-derive every card from main before building it. The fourth may be the same class, in which case the honest fix is a documented boot step, not a rule that looks mechanical and is not.

RECOMMENDATION: B, then A for the specific counts. C is the fallback and must be chosen deliberately rather than by failing to build A or B.

DO NOT BUILD ANY OF THEM without a ruling on which. A wrong rule here is worse than no rule, because a green reconciler is read as a true board.

cards.title: seed/form-templates.ts and seed/roles.ts take DATABASE_URL and write, with no target guard of any kind
cards.notes:
FOUND WHILE SHIPPING PERF-08 (#1092), AND LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN CLOSED BY BREAKING A WORKFLOW.

Both read `process.env.DATABASE_URL`, check only that it is SET, and open a client: form-templates.ts:308-328, roles.ts:122-142. Neither calls `resolveSeedDatabaseUrl`, neither consults PROD_REFS, and neither now calls `assertLocalTarget`. There is no blocklist, no allowlist and no confirmation step between a stale shell and a write.

THEY ARE NOT DEV-DATA SEEDS AND THAT IS WHY THEY WERE NOT GATED. They are CONFIGURATION seeds - the form-template catalogue and the permission roles - and the owner runs `seed:form-templates` against production on purpose, under a phrase, as the v5 template seed. A local-only gate would have broken a documented owner workflow, so PERF-08 excluded them and said so on the card and in the code.

WHAT THE RIGHT GUARD LOOKS LIKE, AND IT IS NOT THE LOCAL-ONLY ONE. These need an explicit PRODUCTION CONFIRMATION rather than a refusal: the operator names the target, the way `SEED_DEV_CONFIRM` does, so that reaching production is a typed decision instead of whatever the shell happened to hold. The byte-copy phrase gate in the import lane is the existing worked example.

GATE owner_authorizo, because the fix changes how the owner runs a production step and he is the one who runs it. It is not a self-merge card.

THE RISK IS REAL BUT BOUNDED, stated so nobody reads this as bigger than it is: both are idempotent upserts of configuration, keyed on (key, version) and on role name. The damage from a wrong target is a config row in the wrong database, not patient data - unlike the load-test seeder PERF-08 closed, which inserted 2,000 patients.
